articles.title: ThreatsDay: Critical Firewall Flaws, Banking Trojans Rented, Weaponized PDF, Token Theft + 26 More Stories
articles.text:
Some attacks take real skill. Others just need someone to leave a door open. This week has both. Exposed passwords, old bugs still getting exploited, and trusted software doing things it shouldn't.
There's a strange mix of clever tricks and careless mistakes. Hackers are borrowing trust from familiar apps, websites, and AI tools. Some are using AI to speed things up. Others are leaving their own attack files exposed. Not exactly careful work.
Different stories, familiar weak spots. Here's what showed up this week.
The threats change every week. Subscribe, and we’ll alert you when each new ThreatsDay Bulletin is out.
- 
  
  PHP2Shell attacks persist WordPress security company Wordefence said it's not aware of any WordPress site compromised through PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) as of October 28, 2026. "We continue to see PHP2Shell-related requests across the more than 5 million sites we protect," it said. "Those requests show ongoing scanning and exploitation attempts; they do not show whether an attempt succeeded. Our site-cleaning and incident response teams have not handled a WordPress compromise attributed to these vulnerabilities."
- 
  
  40,573 secrets exposed Hudson Rock's investigation into the FortiBleed credential harvesting campaign has uncovered 975 newly identified domains and 40,573 exposed secrets, including 37,076 local-user records and 1,576 Active Directory LDAP bind records. The data comes from newly obtained 1,703 FortiGate source files associated with 1,689 host identifiers. "The configuration material dates to around February 2026, earlier than the likely May/June material examined in the first investigation," Hudson Rock said. The latest discovery has been codenamed FortiBleed 2.0.
- 
  
  Institutional DNS hijacked Threat actors have used domain shadowing to place illegal gambling content beneath legitimate school and government domains in two unrelated operations. "In both cases, an unauthorized party appears to have gained access to DNS administration and created records that the original domain owners may not have noticed," Infoblox said. "Because the resulting hostnames sat within established institutional namespaces, they provided especially useful infrastructure for search-engine optimization (SEO) and traffic acquisition." One cluster, linked to a threat actor called Hidden Hawk, has been found to add individual CNAME records that mapped institutional hostnames to gambling pages hosted largely on Cloudflare Pages. The second campaign exploiting an Indian government domain "delegated entire subzones to third-party authoritative nameservers and used a wildcard, allowing many hostnames to be managed outside the victim's DNS environment." Put differently, the unauthorized DNS access creates new institutional hostnames, which resolve to infrastructure serving illegal gambling doorway pages. The pages also leverage the established reputation of school and government namespaces to ensure that the malicious URLs show up prominently in search engine results.
- 
  
  AI banking credential warning Bank of America is reminding customers not to share banking credentials with AI agents. In an email blast to customers titled "Protecting your finances in the AI World," the financial institution urged customers to never share their username and password with another person or an outside service, "including an AI-enabled tool or agent that offers to act on your behalf."
- 
  
  Android tightens contact access Google has announced that an upcoming Android release will no longer be able to directly write to contacts with the WRITE_CONTACTS permission. "Instead, you can use the standard contact intents (ACTION_INSERT, ACTION_EDIT, and ACTION_INSERT_OR_EDIT)," Google said. "Currently, if your app needs to save even one contact, you might be requesting WRITE_CONTACTS. But that permission grants broad access, allowing an app to make widespread changes to contacts across the device in the background, even without user interaction. Most apps don’t need such broad permission."
- 
  
  26,400 live credentials exposed A scan of 7.25 million public repositories on Gitee, China's largest indigenous Git hosting platform, has uncovered 26,400 unique verified-live credentials, including an active organization-admin credential for a major enterprise AI platform and thousands of live cloud provider access keys, independent security researcher Ben Zimmermann said.
- 
  
  Critical Fortinet fixes released Fortinet has released a "coordinated set of security updates for FortiOS, FortiManager, and FortiAnalyzer" to address critical and high-severity flaws that were flagged using an AI-assisted vulnerability discovery approach. Details of the issues are being kept under wraps until November 10, 2026. With Fortinet devices becoming a favorite target for attackers, it's essential that users move quickly to apply the fixes.
- 
  
  Zero-permission token theft Details have emerged about a now-patched flaw in Microsoft Authenticator (CVE-2026-80097 aka AuthMask) that could be exploited by installing and running a malicious application on an affected Android device and convincing the user to complete an authentication flow in the app by claiming to be a trusted app and getting the corresponding tokens. The flaw could be exploited to take over work accounts without requiring additional permissions. "Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to obtain authentication tokens and access resources as the affected user," Microsoft said. According to Enclave, "an unprivileged Android app with zero permissions could impersonate any installed Microsoft first-party app and have the Microsoft Authenticator broker hand it that app's tokens. The setup is a device with Authenticator installed and one work account signed into it."
- 
  
  32 fake AI bots hunt secrets Attackers are disguising themselves as AI agents to steal credentials. Cequence said it has tracked a single actor running AI agent impersonation at scale by posing as about 32 different AI bots, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity, while searching for passwords, API keys, and cloud credentials. "The malicious scanner runs from a major cloud provider and rotates through about 32 AI bot identities, spanning crawlers and assistants from OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Perplexity, and others," Will Glazier said. "It ignores web pages and requests files that commonly store secrets, including .env configuration files, cloud credential files, private SSH keys, and server environment data, working from a list of roughly 90 file paths. Each address sends a short burst of 50 to 190 requests in about eight seconds and then moves on. The scanner works through targets one at a time, around the clock, and first sends random nonsense paths to find websites that answer every request, a common scanning technique. It hit organizations in financial services, retail, telecommunications, energy, and software, and stayed active from at least late September through late October."
- 
  
  China-linked network intrusion The U.S. Embassy in Fiji has revealed that hackers linked to China broke into a regional organization based in Suva between July and August 2026. "Hackers with links to China maintained access to the organization's network over several days," it said. The embassy did not name the threat actor. Nor did it disclose what data the attackers may have accessed.
- 
  
  Camera software weaponized Attackers have been breaking into enterprise networks via camera management software, according to new research from security firm Huntress, which observed multiple incidents in September and October 2026 and traced them back to a compromised application. Source code artifacts point to a Korean company selling analog and IP cameras and digital and network video recorders. The activity abuses the legitimate "WpcMon.exe" binary to sideload DLLs that establish outbound connections to a remote server. "This activity demonstrates how attackers can blend malicious code with trusted Windows components to evade detection," Huntress said.
- 
  
  68 GB government data breach In a major operational security blunder, an unknown threat actor stole 68 GB from a Philippine government agency, maintained a detailed log of the transfer, then left that log open on the internet at 13.163.205[.]35:80. "The copy finished in under 24 minutes on September 6, 2026," Hunt.io said. "The transfer log records 27 SQL Server backups whose filenames correspond to the case-management systems of a Philippine overseas-employment and migrant-worker administration. Beside the log sat the operator's toolkit, a rebranded GodPotato build, a PowerShell stager, two payloads and a full Impacket environment."
- 
  
  AI model data exfiltration concerns Canadian AI company Cohere has claimed that it caught Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model unsuccessfully attempting to send data to China from its evaluation sandbox as part of a prompt instructing the LLM to detect malicious file download and execution by monitoring for curl processes downloading bash scripts to /tmp followed by bash execution. "Asked to write a defensive detection rule, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ignored instructions and inventoried the machine it was running on and then tried to upload a probe file to an Alibaba Cloud storage bucket in Beijing," Cohere said. "We cannot answer whether this is deliberate or a leftover glitch from training." Cohere has also released a dataset containing the model trace and corresponding raw token IDs in connection with the behavior. "The exact output is not guaranteed all the time, and many trials may be required to reproduce the behavior," Cohere said, adding "there are similarly unexpected URLs that the model also tends to output, most containing aliyunc." However, the findings have also led to social media chatter that the company is resorting to geopolitical fearmongering and that they are an attempt to clamp down on open-weights models.
- 
  
  Post-quantum migration roadmap The U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has released guidelines that detail the timelines for transitioning away from quantum-vulnerable algorithms to quantum-resistant standards. "The report describes different use cases and says why one migration might take longer than another," said NIST mathematician Dustin Moody, who heads the PQC standardization project. "We understand there's not one strategy that fits all use cases, and we want to help people handle their migration while staying abreast of what's changing."
- 
  
  AI-powered ransomware operation exposed SOCRadar has uncovered the live workspace (i.e., open directory) of a threat actor tied to the n0n ransomware group, which exposed the operation's full workflow as of September 2026. The directory at 185.157.161[.]148 includes an AI coding agent configured with about 150 models to produce hundreds of attack scripts, with more than $7,216 in usage costs. "Entry points included a credential stuffing campaign against 305 FortiGate SSL-VPN devices, exposed AWS keys, weak RDP/WinRM credentials, and compromised hosting management portals," SOCRadar said. At least 23 organizations across 14 countries are said to have been identified in the workspace, including a U.S. sports retailer, a cloud provider, a teachers’ union, a Venezuelan ISP, an Argentine ministry and a pharmaceutical subsidiary.
- 
  
  Government AI access restricted The Swedish government has barred employees from accessing browser-based versions of ChatGPT or Claude on their work computers over security concerns relating to the processing of sensitive data. "Officials were concerned that entering sensitive information into these models without an agreement setting out how to protect and secure the data could lead to it being fed into the model and stored for training," Euro News reported.
- 
  
  42 repositories hijacked JFrog and SafeDep have uncovered a campaign in which threat actors hijacked third-party 42 GitHub repositories across 11 owners to deploy payload blobs large enough "to evade the GitHub search and API paths normally used to find this kind of compromise." JFrog said, "The repositories contain execution hooks for AI coding assistants and IDEs, plus 12.9 to 13.7 MB polymorphic wrappers that all decode to the same hidden CI-publisher payload." The activity is assessed to be related to a Miasma-family npm worm propagated under various packages ending with "testmetest." According to SafeDep, the worm "shares code with Miasma 'Phantom Gyp' from June 2026 and adds the token-revocation wiper from Mini Shai-Hulud. The malicious versions steal credentials, spread to other packages and repositories, and install a wiper that deletes the home directory when the victim revokes the stolen GitHub token." Unsuspecting developers who installed the packages had their data stolen and repositories compromised with malicious code to produce further malicious testmetest releases and run shellpanel workflows targeting cPanel systems through CVE-2026-41940, overlapping with a prior campaign detailed by Socket in July 2026.
- 
  
  Android banking malware-as-a-service A new Android malware operation called MR ROBOT is targeting customers of Indian banks and transforming banking fraud into a subscription business, with cybercriminals renting customized banking trojans to steal OTPs, card details, UPI PINs and credentials while secretly forwarding calls to bypass security checks. "It is not a single-actor campaign but a rented crimeware platform: a master operator leases access to affiliates, who use a Telegram bot ('APK Shield) and a web control panel (v7.0) to build personalized banking trojans on demand and distribute them through fake Play-Store-style pages and messaging-app lures," CloudSEK said. The kit impersonates around 36 lure apps, including banks, utility providers, and government services. One affiliate is estimated to have intercepted 5407 text messages from 153 infected devices.
- 
  
  MDM platforms abused for remote access Threat actors are abusing legitimate mobile device management (MDM) platforms, like Hexnode and Rippling, by using social engineering to enroll devices or install management agents, per Huntress. "Once established, MDM provides a trusted, privileged path for malicious activity, such as deploying rogue RMM tools and maintaining remote access," it said.
- 
  
  Critical Gotenberg RCE exploited Threat actors are exploiting CVE-2026-42589 (CVSS score: 9.8), a critical remote code execution flaw in Gotenberg, to deliver a Go-based reverse shell called "cache_base." The flaw was patched in May 2026. According to VulnCheck, the activity originated from a residential Japanese IP address in early October 2026. "The execution flow is straightforward: acquire a lock, collect host information, connect to C2, register the victim, and open a shell," VulnCheck said. Over the past 30 days, the vulnerability has recorded 1,358 exploitation events from 128 unique source IP addresses.
- 
  
  Discord discussions go public Discord has announced it will allow search engines to index discussions in Discoverable Servers and make them accessible on the web to users outside the platform without an account or invitation, starting mid-December 2026. "Discussions in Discoverable Servers will soon be easier to find when you search the web, so you can find the answer you're looking for and step straight into the conversation on Discord," it said. The changes apply only to Discoverable Servers and do not extend to private servers and direct messages.
- 
  
  800+ ransomware victims claimed The Gentlemen ransomware operation has claimed more than 800 victims across multiple regions and sectors, with most attacks targeting organizations in the U.S. and Europe. "The group supports multiple platforms, with ransomware variants targeting Windows, Linux, NAS, and BSD systems, allowing its affiliates to target a broad range of enterprise environments," Acronis said. "The group's operations include the use of EDR-killing tools. In a recent incident, a custom dropper was observed deploying vulnerable Safetica ProcessMonitorDriver [CVE-2025-70795] and Lenovo BootRepair.sys drivers to terminate security processes."
- 
  
  AI model loading RCE risk Pillar Security has disclosed an arbitrary-code-execution vulnerability in Unsloth's core model-loading path (CVE-2026-93348, CVSS score: 8.6). It has been fixed in unsloth_zoo 2026.8.14. "An attacker-controlled model configuration could cause Python code to execute during loading," researcher Ariel Fogel said. "The affected code ran inside the model-loading process, with access to whatever that process could read, modify, or authenticate to. In an AI development environment, that can include proprietary datasets, model artifacts, Hugging Face tokens, and cloud credentials. Exploitation required an affected loading path to process an attacker-controlled configuration."
- 
  
  Unauthenticated root-level RCE XBOW said it identified an unauthenticated, critical-severity remote code execution bug in a public web application belonging to the U.S. Election Assistance Commission (EAC). "The vulnerable application was a resource/logistics calculator, not a voting machine or voter registration system," XBOW researcher Ariel Walter Garcia said. "The flaw allowed an unauthenticated attacker to execute code as root inside the backend container, with access to locally protected resources and outbound network connectivity, a privileged foothold reachable via a crafted unauthenticated web request."
- 
  
  Session-hijacking RAT emerges A new remote access trojan called DarkCore comes with a dedicated browser that could let attackers access Gmail, WhatsApp, and MediaFire accounts using stolen sessions, while giving the impression that the activity is originating from the victim's own IP address. DarkCore was first advertised on cybercrime forums in August 2026. "The seller describes a browser that reuses those sessions to access work mailboxes, instant messaging apps, cloud storage and other services through the infected machine's IP address," BlackFog said. "The purpose is to make the access look like legitimate activity from the user."
- 
  
  AI-powered malware framework Cisco Talos has disclosed details of a new AI-integrated command-and-control (C2) framework called NIK C2. The implant features surveillance, theft, lateral movement, and evasion capabilities, including credential dumping, RDP session hijacking, process hollowing, and a C2-driven screen lock ransomware module. "NIK C2 contains a Windows implant, using which, an actor can dump credentials, stream the victim's keystrokes to collect the targeted victim's sensitive data, and instruct an integrated AI model to analyze the harvested data, all within the compromised session," Talos said. "In this framework, the actor has abused the OpenAI Chat Completions application programming interface (API), which is an HTTP endpoint that enables ChatGPT-style conversations programmatically. In addition to the features that enable theft, an actor can also deploy desktop screen-locking ransomware via the NIK C2 implant onto the victim machine, leading to a ransom demand in Bitcoin or USDT cryptocurrencies." Three different versions of the malware have been identified to date since August 12, 2026. Talos said NIK C2 alters adversary tradecraft by collapsing collection and exploitation into a single continuous session.
- 
  
  Malicious PDF delivers backdoor A phishing email using a FedEx tax invoice lure and containing a ZIP archive with a PDF has been observed triggering a multi-stage infection process to deliver a previously undocumented variant of the Sirius Backdoor. "The PDF abuses /OpenAction and /Launch objects to trigger an embedded Base64-encoded PowerShell command upon opening," Trellix said. "Execution relies on social engineering to trick the user into approving the PDF reader's security confirmation prompt. The PowerShell stager decrypts and reflectively loads a .NET assembly in memory. This loader performs process hollowing into legitimate Windows processes such as msbuild.exe, svchost.exe, etc., allowing the malware to operate under trusted process contexts." The final payload is SIRIUS, a Microsoft Visual C++ based backdoor with extended remote access capabilities.
- 
  
  AI reshapes ransomware economics A new analysis from Flare has revealed that threat actors are building a mixed AI toolkit, combining commercial models with local, open-weight, and jailbroken alternatives, as well as leaning on stolen AI credentials to shift costs to victims. "Where AI can help is with understanding systems, writing tools and troubleshooting. The threat actor still needs access, decisions and a way to obtain payment," Flare said. "If AI helps an affiliate write a working data-export script without hiring a specialist, the affiliate may avoid that specialist’s fee and the wait for their help. AI makes expertise cheaper to obtain only when the cost of using and checking its work is lower than the cost of the specialist help it replaces."
- 
  
  Emerging data-extortion threat A recently observed cyber-extortion actor named ScarlettGroup is publicly advertising alleged data compromises and uses negotiation deadlines and threatened disclosures to pressure targeted organizations. The group's dark web site listing includes victims from technology, education, government, and entertainment sectors. "ScarlettGroup demonstrates characteristics associated with financially motivated data-extortion operations, including public victim claims, deadline-based pressure, and underground forum activity," Foresiet said. "Its dedicated leak-site infrastructure and structured disclosure mechanism indicate an organized approach to promoting alleged compromises and exerting reputational pressure."
- 
  
  Infostealers evolve into RATs Following its disruption in June 2026 as part of Operation Endgame, StealC has returned four months later as Stadia. "This time it's not a stealer: it's a full remote access trojan," Varonis said. "The RAT's features include hidden desktop control, a live command shell, a file explorer, a process manager and an in-memory loader, with StealC's stealer welded on as one module among six. The actor behind Stadia is working hard to win back original StealC customers: every former StealC customer is offered a free month on the top ($900) tier." The development comes as Moonlock Lab revealed that the Icarus macOS stealer has similarly evolved from a smash-and-grab crypto and data stealer to a malware with remote-access capabilities. The new iteration is called ICMacOS. "The stealer is actively advertised on cybercrime forums by a Russian-speaking actor operating under the handle GlowComa, with feature updates regularly announced via Telegram," SOCRadar said. "GlowComa promotes ICMacOS alongside Icarus ClickFix, a companion panel designed to deliver payloads using malicious copy-and-paste terminal commands. The infection chain relies on initial dropper scripts to detect the host architecture and harvest administrator passwords using fake system dialogs before delivering the primary payload." Another macOS-focused stealer is Aokigahara, which goes beyond browsers, VPN clients, cryptocurrency wallets, FTP/SFTP clients, password managers, and email applications to also target AI applications and development tools. "The stealer collects authentication files, session data, and configuration files associated with Claude, ChatGPT Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, and other tools," Check Point said. "Stolen AI credentials could offer opportunities for monetization. Usable credentials or session tokens could enable unauthorized access to paid AI services or the resale of compromised accounts."
That's the week's mess. Some attacks were clever, some were painfully simple, and a few attackers made life easier for the people investigating them. The common problem? Too much trust in things nobody was watching closely.
AI is adding new tricks, but the old ones aren't going anywhere. Stolen credentials, weak access controls, and forgotten bugs still get plenty of work done. New tools, familiar mistakes.
The useful part is knowing where those mistakes keep showing up. That's usually where the next problem starts.

articles.title: Amazon baisse ses robots aspirateurs avant le Black Friday : 10 offres Roborock, Dreame et Ecovacs
articles.text:
Amazon a lancé ses Ventes Flash à quelques semaines du Black Friday, prévu le 27 novembre, et les aspirateurs robots y tiennent une belle place, avec une offre chez JoyBuy. Nous avons retenu 10 offres, des modèles d’entrée de gamme aux stations complètes, en distinguant les baisses prouvées des remises calculées sur un prix conseillé.
Les Ventes Flash Amazon reviennent à l’approche du Black Friday, et les robots aspirateurs laveurs sont parmi les produits les plus remisés. Les prix relevés le 28 octobre varient beaucoup, et l’affichage d’un gros pourcentage ne dit pas toujours si la baisse est réelle.
Cette sélection réunit 10 offres, presque toutes chez Amazon, une chez JoyBuy. Elle s’adresse aussi bien à ceux qui cherchent un petit robot d’appoint qu’à ceux qui veulent une station avec lavage automatique des serpillières. Pour chaque produit, nous indiquons ce que la remise vaut vraiment.
Les 10 offres sur les aspirateurs robots repérées par la rédaction
- ECOVACS T90 MAX PRO Aspirateur Robot à 519 € au lieu de 599 €
- eufy Robot Vacuum Omni E25 à 579 € au lieu de 899,99 €
- roborock Q7 L5+ Robot Aspirateur Laveur avec Station à 179,99 € au lieu de 389,99 €
- roborock Q10 S5+ Set Aspirateur Robot Laveur avec Station à 229,98 € au lieu de 439,99 €
- roborock Qrevo Edge 2 Aspirateur Robot Laveur à 549,99 € au lieu de 889,99 €
- roborock Qrevo 2 Pro Aspirateur Robot Laveur avec Station à 499,99 € au lieu de 689,99 €
- Lefant M330 Plus Robot Aspirateur Laveur 5000Pa Anti-Emmêlement Gris à 129,96 € au lieu de 299,99 €
- Lefant M213 Mini Robot Aspirateur Laveur de Sol à 99,99 € au lieu de 299,99 €
- Lefant M2 Robot Aspirateur Laveur 6000Pa avec Cartographie Laser à 109,96 € au lieu de 399,99 €
- 2 en 1 Robot Aspirateur Laveur Cartographie Jusqu'à 6000Pa Navigation à 129,99 € au lieu de 259,99 €
VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
Quelles offres sortent vraiment du lot ?
Dans cette liste, deux offres seulement s’appuient sur un prix moyen du marché relevé sur 90 jours : l’Ecovacs et l’eufy. Pour les autres, le pourcentage se calcule sur un prix conseillé ou un ancien prix Amazon, ce qui ne prouve pas une baisse réelle. Un -73 % impressionne, mais il pèse moins qu’une remise plus modeste mesurée face au marché. Le vendeur compte aussi : plusieurs offres viennent de boutiques officielles de marque sur Amazon.
- ECOVACS T90 MAX PRO : À 519 € au lieu de 599 €, la remise de -13 % paraît modeste, mais elle se mesure face à un prix moyen du marché de 629,89 € sur 90 jours. C’est l’une des deux baisses réellement documentées de la liste. Il est vendu par la boutique officielle ECOVACS sur Amazon, avec une offre annoncée jusqu’au 04/11.
- eufy Robot Vacuum Omni E25 : Proposé à 579 € chez JoyBuy contre 899,99 € avant, soit -36 %, il se situe sous un prix moyen du marché de 699,67 € sur 90 jours. La baisse est donc solide. Le prix vient d’Affilizz et date du 27/10 : vérifiez-le sur la page du marchand avant d’acheter.
- roborock Qrevo Edge 2 : À 549,99 € (-38 %), il est annoncé jusqu’au 08/11. Attention : ce prix n’est pas un plancher, car nous avions déjà relayé ce même modèle à 549,99 € le 6 octobre. La remise repose en outre sur un prix conseillé, pas sur un historique.
- roborock Qrevo 2 Pro : Il passe à 499,99 € au lieu de 689,99 € (-28 %), avec une station qui lave et sèche ses serpillières. Nous l’avons déjà relayé le 26 octobre sous les 500 € : le prix n’a donc rien d’inédit. La remise est la plus mesurée de la gamme roborock, mais elle reste calculée sur un prix conseillé.
- Lefant M2 : C’est la remise la plus forte de la liste, -73 %, à 109,96 € au lieu de 399,99 €. Elle est calculée sur un prix conseillé, sans preuve de baisse réelle : le chiffre est à relativiser. Il s’adresse à un petit budget qui veut une navigation laser, d’une marque moins établie que roborock ou Ecovacs.
- Robot aspirateur laveur Yigars 2 en 1 : À 129,99 € au lieu de 259,99 € (-50 %), il vise les petits budgets. Son offre était annoncée jusqu’au 28/10 à 23:59 : elle a peut-être pris fin, à vérifier sur la page. La remise repose sur un prix conseillé.
Acheter maintenant ou attendre le Black Friday ?
Sur les 10 offres, seules deux reposent sur un prix moyen du marché : l’Ecovacs T90 MAX PRO et l’eufy Omni E25. Les huit autres affichent des remises de -28 % à -73 % calculées sur un prix conseillé ou un ancien prix, qui peuvent surévaluer l’économie. Plusieurs modèles roborock ont déjà été relayés récemment à des prix proches, ce qui montre que ces tarifs ne sont pas inédits.
Le Black Friday tombe le 27 novembre, suivi du Cyber Monday le 30 novembre, mais rien ne garantit des prix plus bas sur ces modèles. Les offres Amazon de cette liste s’arrêtent entre le 01/11 et le 08/11, donc le choix se fait plus tôt. Pour vous repérer, notre comparatif des aspirateurs robots recommande le Dreame Aqua10 Ultra Roller Complete comme choix toutes catégories, et l’Ecovacs Deebot T90 Pro Omni, un autre modèle que celui de la liste, en milieu de gamme.
Ventes Flash Amazon : vos questions
Jusqu’à quand durent ces offres ?
Les offres Amazon de la liste sont annoncées jusqu’à des dates comprises entre le 01/11 et le 08/11, sauf une, annoncée jusqu’au 28/10 à 23:59. Le prix JoyBuy de l’eufy date du 27/10 et doit être revérifié.
Les prix barrés sont-ils fiables ?
Pas tous. Seuls l’Ecovacs T90 MAX PRO et l’eufy Omni E25 sont comparés à un prix moyen du marché sur 90 jours. Pour les autres, la remise se calcule sur un prix conseillé ou un ancien prix Amazon.
Faut-il attendre le Black Friday pour acheter un aspirateur robot ?
Le Black Friday est prévu le 27 novembre et le Cyber Monday le 30 novembre, mais rien ne garantit une baisse supplémentaire. Les remises de cette sélection sont celles relevées le 28 octobre.

articles.title: ATK Reveals Affordable RS8 Air HE and Neo Mechanical Aluminium Gaming Keyboards
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
ATK Reveals Affordable RS8 Air HE and Neo Mechanical Aluminium Gaming Keyboards
ATK, the brand behind several affordable high-performance gaming peripherals, has just announced the new RS8 series gaming keyboards in both mechanical and Hall effect flavors. The RS8 Air is a $99.98 Hall effect keyboard that will launch with a discount bringing the price down to $74.89, while the RS8 Neo is a more traditional mechanical keyboard that will have a starting MSRP of $84.98 but will launch at $59.98. Both keyboards have the same TKL layout, which is often considered as striking a good balance between productivity and gaming use cases, and both keyboards will also feature CNC-machined aluminium, gasket-mounted cases and translucent, frosted polycarbonate keycaps for the RGB backlighting to shine through. 
Being a Hall effect keyboard, the RS8 Air will feature 8 kHz polling in addition to typical HE features, like adjustable actuation, rapid trigger, SOCD, and DKS in addition to the classic key remapping and RGB customization. All of this will happen in ATK's Hub 3.0 software. It also has a hardware switch on the back of the keyboard for on-the-go profile switching without having to remember a keyboard combination or open the software. The RS8 Air will have an aluminium switch plate for a firm feel and accurate actuation detection, and it will have five layers of internal sound treatment to cut out reverberation and echoes that can be common in aluminium keyboards. The RS8 Air will be available in white or black with Lucid Blade or Ice Blade switches or in pink or Lake Green with Ice Blade switches for an extra $10.The ATK RS8 Neo, on the other hand, leans more into the typing feel and premium build quality aspects than the gaming-focussed Air. It still has the same design and TKL layout, but it swaps out the stiff gaskets and aluminium plate on the Air for a more flexible polycarbonate plate and softer gaskets. The RS8 Neo also has 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth connectivity as additional quality-of-life features, powered by a 12,000 mAh battery. Despite the wireless connectivity, the ATK RS8 Neo also has 8 kHz polling, SOCD, mod tap, and a "Plus Music Rhythm" mode that sets the RGB backlighting to react to music.The ATK RS8 Neo will be available in white, black or Lake Green with Ice Steed switches, in pink with Anya Max switches, or in a special Arctic Fox colorway that comes with Aurora Fox switches and swaps out the translucent PC keycaps for five-sided dye-sublimated keycaps.

articles.title: Lista de códigos ocultos de Netflix para ver series y películas de terror en Halloween 2026
articles.text:
Durante la época de Halloween 2026, algunas personas pueden optar por ver películas o series de terror en Netflix.
Los códigos secretos de Netflix permiten explorar subcategorías específicas dentro del catálogo de terror. Para utilizarlos, los usuarios pueden ingresar el código correspondiente y acceder a contenidos vinculados con ese tipo de historias.
La selección incluye producciones de monstruos, vampiros, zombis, asesinos en serie y relatos sobrenaturales, entre otras alternativas para Halloween.
Códigos secretos de Netflix para películas y series de terror
- Películas de terror de serie B – 8195
- Películas de criaturas – 6895
- Películas de terror de culto – 10944
- Películas de terror en aguas profundas – 45028
- Películas de terror extranjeras – 8654
- Películas cómicas de terror – 89585
- Películas de monstruos – 947
- Películas slasher y de asesinos en serie – 8646
- Películas de terror sobrenatural – 42023
- Películas de terror de adolescentes – 52147
- Películas de terror de vampiros – 75804
- Películas de terror de hombres lobo – 75930
- Películas de terror de zombis – 75405
Por qué no ver películas de terror en XuperTV
Durante Halloween de 2026, muchas personas buscan películas y series de terror para ver en casa, pero Xuper TV, antes llamada Magis TV, no es una alternativa recomendable.
La aplicación ofrece contenidos audiovisuales y deportes en vivo sin una suscripción mensual, aunque su instalación y uso pueden exponer a los usuarios a riesgos de seguridad y también a problemas legales.
ESET, compañía de ciberseguridad, analizó la APK de Magis TV y detectó permisos críticos e invasivos que no corresponden a una plataforma convencional de streaming.
La firma clasificó este tipo de servicios como aplicaciones potencialmente indeseables y advirtió que esas autorizaciones podrían ser utilizadas con fines maliciosos.
El principal problema es que las aplicaciones de streaming no oficiales suelen distribuirse fuera de Google Play Store y App Store.
Para instalarlas, los usuarios deben recurrir a sitios web alternativos que pueden evitar los controles de calidad y seguridad de las tiendas oficiales. Esa vía facilita la distribución de software malicioso.
David González Cuautle, investigador de ESET Latinoamérica, señaló que la habilitación excesiva de permisos especiales y críticos es una señal de riesgo.
Según explicó, estas aplicaciones pueden comprometer tanto el dispositivo como toda la red doméstica. Además, podrían servir como puerta de entrada para malware, incluidos spyware, troyanos y herramientas orientadas al robo de información personal.
El uso de Xuper TV también plantea un riesgo legal. ESET indicó que retransmitir contenidos sin los derechos correspondientes vulnera la propiedad intelectual y puede derivar en bloqueos de proveedores de internet o acciones judiciales.
La advertencia se extiende a los Set-Top Boxes, dispositivos que se conectan al televisor para acceder a aplicaciones y contenidos audiovisuales.
Si fueron modificados para instalar aplicaciones piratas, firmware no oficial o archivos descargados desde páginas externas, pueden transformarse en puertas de entrada para malware y spyware en el hogar.
Dónde ver películas y series de forma gratuita y segura
YouTube, Pluto TV, Prime Video, RTVE Play y Plex son cinco alternativas para ver películas y series gratis en Fire TV. YouTube ofrece videos, documentales, conciertos, contenido educativo y series web sin necesidad de pagar una suscripción para acceder a su catálogo abierto.
Pluto TV reúne canales en vivo, películas, series y programas como CSI Miami, The Walking Dead, Daredevil y Naruto. Una de sus ventajas es que permite acceder a los contenidos sin iniciar sesión.
Prime Video cuenta con una sección llamada “Free”, donde se pueden encontrar títulos gratuitos como Alvin y las ardillas 2, El justiciero y Sin rastro.
RTVE Play, la plataforma de Radio Televisión Española, ofrece series, películas, documentales, informativos y programas como MasterChef. Plex, por su parte, incluye publicidad y propone producciones como Medici, The Dick Van Dyke Show y Hot Ones.

articles.title: OpenMouse Launches Open-Source Customization for Logitech, Razer, Wooting, and SteelSeries Keyboards
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
OpenMouse Launches Open-Source Customization for Logitech, Razer, Wooting, and SteelSeries Keyboards
Not too long ago, the developers behind OpenMouse, the open-source, community-driven alternative mouse configuration suite, revealed that they were working on supporting keyboard customization alongside the myriad gaming mouse models the suite now supports. As per a recent announcement on the project's Discord server, the latest OpenMouse beta release has added support for a number of gaming keyboards from Logitech, Razer, SteelSeries, and Wooting. Initial support also appears to be in development for Wuque Studio and the Kochi Hummingbird 68. 
So far, actual feature support also appears to be limited, and the implementation is very much still in beta, with the app connecting correctly to a Wooting 80HE in a brief test but failing to load the proper keymap and failing to adjust the settings correctly. However, the planned feature set appears to be competitive with most proprietary keyboard customization tools, with HE features like adjustable actuation, rapid trigger, toggle key, mod tap, SOCD, and DKS, all present in addition to robust RGB customization and support for layers and profiles. What is notably absent is the ability to remap keys, however.OpenMouse also now allows users to install the Bridge app to create custom per-game profiles for compatible gaming mice, and it appears as though the same functionality will eventually be added for supported keyboards. It's not clear when keyboard support will leave the beta testing phase, but the development team has called on gamers to participate in the beta test.
Sources:
				OpenMouse on Discord, 				OpenMouse

articles.title: Linux Kernel TCP Flaw With 9.8 CVSS Score Affects Ubuntu, Red Hat and Other Distributions
articles.text:
A flaw in the Linux kernel's TCP code, tracked as CVE-2026-98432, affects Ubuntu, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), and other Linux distributions. The kernel's own CVE team rates it 9.8 out of 10 on the CVSS scale.
Anthropic said on October 27 that its AI model wrote an exploit that uses the flaw to let a remote attacker with no credentials run commands as root on Linux servers with a multipath TCP listener.
As of October 29, Ubuntu and RHEL have not released a fixed kernel. Red Hat, Amazon, Oracle, and SUSE score the flaw between 5.9 and 8.1, lower than the kernel team's 9.8.
The flaw is a race condition in the code that sets up new IPv4 TCP connections. It can make the kernel read memory it has already freed, a bug type known as a use-after-free.
The kernel fix credits Anthropic researcher Xinyang Ge with reporting the bug. Neither the CVE record nor the fix mentions multipath TCP (MPTCP). The link between that feature and this bug comes from Anthropic's post.
MPTCP lets one connection use several network paths at once. On Linux, an application must request MPTCP when it opens a socket.
Anthropic's post says the flaw "was patched upstream and backported to all maintained stable kernel branches." For distribution users, that fix arrives only in the vendor's kernel package. Debian, Oracle Linux, SUSE, and Amazon Linux have shipped fixed packages, at least for some of their kernels, but Ubuntu and RHEL have not.
Which Distributions Have a Fix
| Distribution | Vendor rating | Status as of October 29 | Fixed package or advisory | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, 24.04 LTS, 26.04 LTS and 26.10 | Priority High | Work in progress | None released | 
| Ubuntu 16.04, 18.04 and 20.04 | Priority High | Vulnerable | None released | 
| RHEL 8, 9 and 10, OpenShift 4 | Moderate, 5.9 (CVE page) Important, 8.1 ( advisory file) | Fix deferred | None released | 
| RHEL 7 | Not applicable | Not affected | Not needed | 
| Amazon Linux 2023, kernel6.18 package | Important, 7.0 | Fixed October 24 | kernel6.18-6.18.56-125.164.amzn2023 (ALAS2023-2026-3251) | 
| Amazon Linux 2023, kernel6.12 package | Important, 7.0 | Fixed October 29 in Amazon's advisory; Amazon's CVE page still says pending | kernel6.12-6.12.113-138.209.amzn2023 (ALAS2023-2026-3335) | 
| Amazon Linux 2 Amazon Linux 2023, kernel package | Important, 7.0 | Pending fix | None released | 
| Oracle Linux 7, 8, 9 and 10, UEK kernel | Important, 8.1 | Fixed October 16 | ELSA-2026-500397, ELSA-2026-500398, ELSA-2026-500399 | 
| Debian trixie (stable) | No score listed | Fixed October 16 | linux 6.12.113-1         (DSA-6568-1) | 
| Debian 12 (bookworm) | No score listed | Fixed October 17 and October 22 | linux 6.1.190-1         (DLA-4841-1) linux-6.12 6.12.113-1~deb12u1         (DLA-4850-1) | 
| SUSE Linux Micro 6.2, openSUSE Leap 16.0 | Important, 8.1 | Fixed | kernel-default 6.12.0-160000.40.1 or later | 
| SLES 15 SP4 to SP6 LTSS, SLES 16.0, SLE Micro 5.3 to 5.5 | Important, 8.1 | In testing | None released | 
| SLES 15 SP7 | Important, 8.1 | Affected, fix in progress | None released | 
Ubuntu also lists its cloud, FIPS, and real-time kernels as vulnerable or as work in progress. Red Hat says its fixes are "currently deferred to a future update." Neither Red Hat nor Ubuntu gives a release date.
How the Bug Works
The race happens during the TCP handshake. When a connection is completed, the kernel hands the IP options stored with the pending request to the new socket without copying them.
If that socket is destroyed while another CPU is still using the options to answer a resent connection request, the kernel reads freed memory.
IPv6 is not affected by this race because the kernel copies the options for IPv6 connections.
The bug was introduced in Linux 4.4. Kernel developers applied a fix on October 5, ten days before the CVE was published.
The fix makes the kernel wait until other CPUs finish reading the options before it frees them.
Why the Scores Differ
The kernel's CVE team added the 9.8 score to the CVE record on October 24, nine days after publishing the CVE.
Its score assumes an attacker who sends a TCP connection request carrying IPv4 Record Route or Timestamp options, then resends the request to try to win the race. The team rated attack complexity low, saying both sides of the race are "attacker-induced."
In that case, the team says, the bug could send nearby kernel memory back to the attacker, corrupt kernel memory, or crash the system.
As of October 28, the National Vulnerability Database (NVD) had not added its own score and showed the kernel team's 9.8. Ubuntu's page also shows that score.
Red Hat's CVE page rates the flaw Moderate, scoring it 5.9 because the race is hard to win. It says the most likely result is a kernel crash, with memory corruption possible in theory, and that "no confidentiality or integrity impact has been demonstrated."
Red Hat's machine-readable advisory file, updated on October 29, lists the impact as Important and scores the flaw 8.1, with high confidentiality and integrity impact. Red Hat's bug tracker changed the issue's severity from medium to high the same day. On that day, the CVE page showed Moderate and 5.9.
Oracle and SUSE also score the flaw 8.1, with the same CVSS vector as Red Hat's advisory file. Those scores match the kernel team's on every metric except attack complexity, which the vendors rate high and the kernel team rates low. Amazon scores it 7.0.
What Anthropic Says It Built
Anthropic described the Linux exploit in an October 27 post about flaws that its AI model, Claude, found and exploited. The Hacker News covered the post on October 28. Claude wrote the exploit after "initial prompting," Anthropic said.
The exploit works in two stages. First, the race makes the kernel send extra bytes back to the attacker. Once one of those replies contains a kernel address, the attacker can get around KASLR, the kernel's memory address randomization.
Second, the same bug overflows a buffer and overwrites a callback pointer with the address of a payload the attacker had already placed in kernel memory. When the kernel calls that pointer, the payload executes a shell command of the attacker's choice as root.
A lost race only fails that one connection attempt and does not crash the system, so an attacker can keep trying, the company said. In its test, leaking a kernel address took 48 minutes, and reaching command execution took 5 more minutes.
The post does not include the exploit code, the kernel version, or the configuration Anthropic tested.
Red Hat says a remote attacker who can reach an exposed TCP service could trigger the race. Anthropic's root exploit, however, targeted servers with a multipath TCP listener. The post does not say whether servers without one can be taken over the same way.
As of October 29, none of the vendor advisories, the CVE record, or Anthropic's post reports attacks using the flaw. It does not appear in a copy of CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog that Luxembourg's CIRCL last updated on October 28.
What to Do Now
Where your distribution has released a fixed kernel, install it. The table above lists the packages and advisories for Debian, Oracle Linux, SUSE and Amazon Linux.
If you build your own kernel, the fix is in Linux 5.10.272, 5.15.223, 6.1.190, 6.6.159, 6.12.113, 6.18.56, 7.2.10 and 7.3. The kernel's CVE team recommends updating to the latest stable kernel. It says the kernel community does not support cherry-picking individual fixes.
Ubuntu, RHEL and some Amazon Linux and SUSE releases have no fixed kernel to install yet. Red Hat says no available mitigation meets its standards for being easy to deploy, suitable for most installations and stable. None of the other vendor advisories lists one.
The advisories and Anthropic's post do not say whether turning off multipath TCP, or blocking incoming connection requests that carry IP options, would lower the risk.

articles.title: Google autorise l’installation d’apps Android en un seul clic depuis Chrome
articles.text:
Installer une application depuis une boutique alternative au Play Store ne demandera plus qu'une pression sur l'écran, sans fenêtre de confirmation, à partir du 1er décembre. Google réserve toutefois ce raccourci aux boutiques qui lui versent 10 000 dollars par an, et aux smartphones sous une version d'Android encore en bêta.
Aujourd'hui, une boutique d'applications tierce doit d'abord obtenir de vous l'autorisation d'installer des applications, puis vous faire valider chaque installation et chaque mise à jour. Dans son programme Registered App Stores, présenté en mars au moment de solder son conflit avec Epic Games, Google accorde d'office cette autorisation aux boutiques qu'il agrée, et vous recevez leurs mises à jour en arrière-plan, selon vos réglages habituels. La participation est facultative, et les boutiques non inscrites continueront de fonctionner sans changement. La France fait partie des pays concernés, mais pas les États-Unis.
Android 17 QPR2 nécessaire sur votre smartphone
Il faudra un téléphone sous Android 17 QPR2 ou une version plus récente pour installer une application d'une seule pression. La dernière version de cette mise à jour trimestrielle d'Android, sortie le 16 octobre, est toujours une bêta, et Google ne donne aucune date de sortie de la version finale. Si votre téléphone tourne sous une version antérieure, rien ne changera le 1er décembre, et vous continuerez de valider chaque installation.
Google se fonde sur le pays déclaré dans votre compte, et non sur votre position. Lors d'un séjour aux États-Unis ou dans un autre pays exclu du programme, vous gardez les installations en un geste et les mises à jour automatiques, alors qu'après un déménagement signalé sur votre compte, vous retrouvez les options prévues dans votre nouveau pays de résidence.
Vous donnerez toujours votre accord à chaque installation, simplement d'une seule pression au lieu de plusieurs écrans. Selon les règles du programme, les boutiques « ne doivent pas installer d'applications en silence sans le consentement de l'utilisateur ». Lors d'un téléchargement volumineux ou d'une installation en arrière-plan, elles doivent afficher une notification visible pendant toute l'opération, et laisser sur le téléphone une notification à fermer manuellement quand vous lancez une installation depuis un autre appareil.
En entreprise, les administrateurs informatiques peuvent bloquer l'installation de ces boutiques sur les appareils qu'ils gèrent. Google ne précise pas si les administrateurs peuvent aussi écarter une boutique installée auparavant.
Si vous désinstallez une boutique agréée, vous gardez ses applications sur votre téléphone, mais elles ne reçoivent plus de mises à jour automatiques. Réinstallée plus tard, la boutique reprend la main sur leurs mises à jour sans vous redemander votre accord, à condition qu'aucune autre boutique ne les ait mises à jour entre-temps.
Les obligations des boutiques agréées
Une boutique candidate doit appartenir à une organisation enregistrée auprès de Google, et non à un développeur individuel, et faire contrôler l'identité de son éditeur dans le cadre de la vérification des développeurs Android. Avant l'examen de sa candidature, elle paie à Google 10 000 dollars, à renouveler chaque année, puis dépose l'intégralité de son catalogue dans un espace de stockage fourni par Google, ainsi que chaque nouvelle application et chaque mise à jour, afin que Google analyse en continu ces fichiers à la recherche de logiciels malveillants.
Google laisse à chaque boutique la responsabilité de tout son catalogue et ne modère pas les contenus proposés. Si, sur trente jours, il repère des applications potentiellement dangereuses dans plus de 1 % des tentatives d'installation ou dans plus de 2 % du catalogue d'une boutique, il lui facture en revanche des frais supplémentaires pour analyser et nettoyer ce catalogue.
Une boutique agréée n'a pas non plus le droit de bloquer l'installation d'une concurrente ni de masquer les alertes de sécurité d'Android. En cas de manquement à l'une de ces règles, retard de paiement compris, Google peut retirer une boutique du programme jusqu'à la correction du problème, après un préavis. À partir du 1er juin 2027, chaque boutique devra en outre obtenir, puis renouveler tous les ans, la certification MASA de niveau AL2 délivrée par l'App Defense Alliance.
Avec l'Android Developer ID API, fournie par Google, les boutiques agréées peuvent vérifier si chaque application de leur catalogue vient d'un développeur vérifié, et Google leur recommande de bloquer l'installation des autres. Google applique ce contrôle d'identité depuis le 30 septembre sur les appareils certifiés du Brésil, d'Indonésie, de Singapour et de Thaïlande, pour les applications de sept boutiques, et prévoit de l'étendre au monde entier en 2027. L'entreprise n'explique toutefois ni la méthode d'analyse des applications soumises, ni le délai de contrôle d'une nouvelle version. Tel est Google.
- Grande diversité d’applications (+2,5 millions)
- Intégration avec les services Google
- Interface utilisateur intuitive
Registered App Stores est un programme d’agrément qui permet à certaines boutiques tierces de bénéficier d’autorisations système plus fluides sur Android. Concrètement, une boutique enregistrée peut obtenir l’autorisation d’installer des applications sans faire repasser l’utilisateur par plusieurs écrans de validation, et gérer les mises à jour en arrière-plan selon les réglages du téléphone. Ce n’est pas un remplacement du Play Store, mais un cadre où Android traite ces boutiques comme des sources “de confiance” sous conditions. Les boutiques non enregistrées restent utilisables, mais conservent les étapes de confirmation classiques. Le programme s’accompagne d’obligations (identité, dépôt des APK, contrôles) et d’une redevance annuelle.
QPR veut dire Quarterly Platform Release : ce sont des mises à jour trimestrielles d’Android qui ajoutent des fonctions au système, au-delà des correctifs de sécurité. « Android 17 QPR2 » désigne donc une branche précise d’Android 17 intégrant des changements au niveau de l’OS, notamment dans la gestion des installateurs, des confirmations et des droits accordés aux boutiques. La fonctionnalité “en une pression” dépend de ces modifications système, ce qui explique qu’elle soit limitée aux appareils ayant cette version (ou plus récente). Tant que la version finale n’est pas déployée sur les téléphones, les appareils restent sur le parcours de validation habituel.
MASA (Mobile Application Security Assessment) est un référentiel de sécurité promu par l’App Defense Alliance pour évaluer des pratiques et contrôles de sécurité autour des applications et des écosystèmes mobiles. Un niveau comme AL2 correspond à un palier d’exigences plus élevé qu’un simple contrôle automatisé, généralement orienté sur des preuves de processus, de gouvernance et de capacités de gestion des risques. Exiger MASA AL2 d’une boutique revient à imposer un standard externe, renouvelable, pour maintenir un certain niveau de confiance. Cela ne garantit pas “zéro malware”, mais renforce l’auditabilité et la responsabilité opérationnelle des acteurs.

articles.title: Ruidos extraños y pérdidas de agua: señales de que tu lavadora necesita mantenimiento
articles.text:
La lavadora soporta cientos de ciclos de lavado al año, pero ese uso constante termina por desgastar sus componentes internos. Reconocer a tiempo las señales de desgaste permite evitar averías mayores, reparaciones costosas y la necesidad de reemplazar el equipo antes de tiempo, además de garantizar que la ropa salga limpia.
La mayoría de las fallas en este electrodoméstico no ocurren de forma repentina: casi siempre existen alertas previas que anticipan un problema. Ignorarlas puede derivar en daños por agua o en averías que comprometen la seguridad del hogar. Saber identificar estos síntomas ayuda a prolongar la vida útil del aparato.
La acumulación de humedad genera malos olores
Los olores a moho o humedad dentro de la lavadora suelen originarse por residuos acumulados en la junta de la puerta, el dispensador de detergente o el tambor. Ventilar el equipo después de cada uso y limpiar la junta con un paño seco reduce la proliferación de hongos y bacterias. Realizar ciclos de limpieza con agua caliente una vez al mes también contribuye a eliminar olores persistentes.
La ropa sale sucia o con mal olor tras el lavado
Cuando las prendas salen con manchas, olor desagradable o sin la limpieza esperada, el problema puede estar en el agitador, el impulsor o en residuos acumulados en el tambor. Sobrecargar la lavadora o usar demasiado detergente reduce la eficacia del lavado. Limpiar el tambor con regularidad usando vinagre blanco o productos especiales, y evitar cargas excesivas, ayuda a mantener un rendimiento óptimo.
Las fugas de agua indican mangueras o sellos dañados
La presencia de charcos o humedad alrededor del equipo señala fugas que pueden originarse en mangueras agrietadas, sellos desgastados o conexiones mal ajustadas. Inspeccionar todas las conexiones junto con el sello de la puerta permite localizar el origen del problema. Sustituir las mangueras de goma por otras de acero inoxidable aumenta la durabilidad y previene futuros escapes. Si el origen de la fuga no se identifica, conviene recurrir a un servicio técnico.
El llenado o el drenaje de agua presentan fallas
Una lavadora que no se llena de manera correcta, que deja agua estancada o que tarda demasiado en drenar suele tener filtros obstruidos, válvulas defectuosas o mangueras dobladas. El primer paso consiste en revisar y limpiar el filtro de desagüe y las mangueras de suministro. Si el problema persiste, puede ser necesaria la intervención de un técnico para revisar la bomba o la válvula de entrada.
Los ruidos extraños durante el ciclo anticipan averías mayores
Zumbidos, rechinidos, golpeteos o chirridos no son normales en un equipo en buen estado. Estos sonidos pueden indicar rodamientos desgastados, varillas de suspensión rotas, una correa de transmisión defectuosa o bloqueos en la bomba de desagüe. Actuar con rapidez ante estos ruidos evita que una avería menor se convierta en un daño estructural más grave y costoso.
La vibración excesiva revela problemas de nivelación
Cuando la lavadora vibra de manera inusual, se desplaza sola o emite golpes fuertes durante el centrifugado, es probable que exista un problema de nivelación o de suspensión interna. Los amortiguadores o resortes desgastados, un tambor desbalanceado o una superficie desigual pueden explicar el fenómeno.
Ajustar las patas niveladoras suele corregir el inconveniente, pero si la vibración continúa, conviene solicitar una revisión profesional para evitar daños en el tambor o en el suelo.
No esperar a que la lavadora se detenga por completo resulta clave para evitar daños mayores y prolongar su vida útil. Atender los síntomas desde su aparición permite resolver las fallas de forma sencilla y económica. Ante cualquier señal de advertencia, la consulta con un profesional es la opción recomendada para mantener el equipo en condiciones óptimas de funcionamiento.

articles.title: FromSoftware Delays The Duskbloods to 2027 for Final Balancing
articles.text:
Friday, October 30th 2026
FromSoftware Delays The Duskbloods to 2027 for Final Balancing
FromSoftware has officially pushed The Duskbloods, its multiplayer action game made exclusively for the Nintendo Switch 2, out of 2026. In a post on the game's official X account, the studio said development is at the "final adjustment stage" and that the launch window now moves to 2027. There's no date or even a quarter attached to the new window, so it could land anywhere next year. FromSoftware also apologized to players who have been waiting for the game.
In a follow-up post, the studio said the August network test showed strong interest in the game's combat and strategic depth, and that the extra time will go toward final tweaks to game rules and balancing. That closed test ran from August 21 to 23 and got off to a rough start, as server issues forced FromSoftware to end the first session early. Interestingly, more players applied for it than for the Elden Ring Nightreign test, despite the game being tied to a single platform.Of course, the delay won't surprise many people. FromSoftware revealed The Duskbloods alongside the Switch 2 back in April 2025 with a 2026 target, and parent company Kadokawa kept that window in its financial reports while confirming no plans for other platforms. Directed by Hidetaka Miyazaki, the game drops up to eight players into PvPvE matches. With two months left in the year and no release date ever announced, a slip has looked likely for a while now. Hopefully, the extra time also helps FromSoftware sort out the server problems seen during the test.

articles.title: Fedora 45 Gets Official Launch Date After Bugs Caused Delays
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
Fedora 45 Gets Official Launch Date After Bugs Caused Delays
Fedora Linux 45 has been under development for some time, with the distribution having been delayed twice, the latest delay due to blocker bugs resulting in a no-go decision by the development team as recently as last week. Now, following a recent developer meeting, Fedora 45 has officially been given the stamp of approval for a November 3 release date, according to the public meeting minutes. 
Fedora 45 is a fairly tame update, coming from Fedora 44, although there are a number of notable updates to the included software and configuration, including an update to Gnome 51, support for new Qualcomm Snapdragon X Series laptops, and the implementation of the new DRM Panic front-end. The KDE versions of Fedora will now also fully adopt the KDE Plasma Login Manager, and they will feature a unified KDE out-of-the-box experience. For a full run-down of new features and changes in Fedora 45, check the Fedora 45 beta changelogs. Following the launch of Fedora 45, we will likely see Fedora spins and Fedora-based distros, like Bazzite and Nobara Linux also release a major version update to match.
