articles.title: Fake ChatGPT and Claude Apps Abuse Signed Executables to Deploy Crypto Miners
articles.text:
Threat actors are delivering malicious loaders and cryptocurrency miners under the guise of artificial intelligence (AI) desktop applications for Anthropic Claude and OpenAI ChatGPT as part of a campaign dubbed Yoba.
The activity involves creating fake GitHub projects that claim to be desktop applications like GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and Claude Opus, only to deliver a malware family called YobaLoader.
"The malware is placed next to legitimate, signed executables from OpenAI and Anthropic so it can be loaded indirectly, a technique commonly known as DLL sideloading, which is often used to bypass security protections," Check Point Research said in an analysis.
To add to the project's credibility, the attackers set up GitHub.io pages to describe the capabilities of the software. Although the GitHub projects' popularity is not manipulated using techniques like ghost networks, signs point to the use of SEO poisoning tactics to ensure that links to them are surfaced on top of search results on Google.
Some of the identified GitHub pages links are below -
- github[.]com/gpt-5-6/sol-free-desktop
- gpt-5-6.github[.]io
- github[.]com/gpt-5-6/gpt-5-6.github.io
- github[.]com/gpt-6-astra/gpt-6-astra.github.io
- gpt-6-astra[.]github[.]io
- github[.]com/opus-5-0/opus-5-0.github[.]io
- opus-5-0[.]github[.]io
"Each repository uses a different email address (edwardcarlsonmkym[@]outlook[.]com, daxschneiderdjuu[@]outlook[.]com, and rioprestonlfyx[@]outlook[.]com), and the uploader appears to operate in UTC+4, UTC-4, and UTC+3 respectively," Check Point said. "This inconsistency likely reflects a deliberate attempt to obscure the threat actor's true operational time zone."
Hosted within these repositories are ZIP archives that, among other files, contain two specific components -
- Setup.exe, a legitimate signed OpenAI Codex or Claude executable
- winmm.dll, a malicious DLL that's sideloaded by the executable
The DLL is a dropper codenamed YobaDropper, which implements checksum value checks by hashing the basename of its host executable and if it matches a hard-coded value "0xE6C2F326." In other words, the check requires it to be launched under "Setup.exe," and fails if the DLL is executed on its own inside a sandboxed environment.
Additional anti-analysis techniques and pre-checks include 200,000 iterations of "Sleep(5500)," which amounts to 12.73 days, and skipping machines whose keyboard layout corresponds to that of Russia, Belarus, Tajikistan, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan.
Another language ID excluded from the infection process is Tatar. Notably missing from the list is Ukraine, which used to be historically included in such checks.
YobaDropper, for its part, triggers a DLL sideloading chain of its own comprising "wmpdmc.exe" and "ampdui.dll," copying the former from its "system32" folder and placing it in a new directory named "WMProcess" created under "ProgramData."
The dropper then extracts and decrypts an embedded payload, and drops it into the same folder as "wmpdui.dll." It also establishes persistence by means of a scheduled task that launches the legitimate executable to load the malicious payload.
The second DLL is YobaLoader. It implements the same anti-sandbox technique as YobaDropper, requiring the malware to be run only by "wmpdmc.exe" by checking the hash against a hard-coded value ("0x552751E3"). The loader is responsible for three main tasks -
- Downloads an image from a Telegram channel ("t[.]me/yoba_fanclub").
- Uses the last 50 bytes as a seed to generate a domain based on three lists of dictionary words and an integer value in the range 0–999 using a domain generation algorithm (DGA). The end result is domain in the format "adjective-noun-verb-digit.dedyn[.]io."
- Queries Google's DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) API to obtain a Base64-encoded command from a DNS TXT record by passing the constructed domain as input.
- Decrypts the response to obtain the link to fetch the next-stage payload ("files.catbox[.]moe/z5zpy9.dat").
"By relying on a DoH service and common file-hosting platforms, the actor aims to bypass passive DNS monitoring and some gateway-based security protections, making their command-and-control traffic harder to distinguish from regular user activity," Check Point said.
The downloaded payload is then injected into "svchost.exe," resulting in the execution of an XMRig cryptocurrency miner.
Evidence indicates that the first GitHub repository was created around July 2026, although the malicious releases were not uploaded until the end of August. What's more, early versions of YobaLoader have been found to only exclude Russia from infection, while also incorporating extensive anti-debugging and anti-VM checks, which have since been removed in newer versions.
"The Yoba campaign shows how attackers can use trusted platforms and the current interest in AI tools to distribute malware in a way that looks believable and harmless at first glance," Check Point said. "By packaging their code together with well-known software names and hosting it on GitHub, they lower the chances that users or basic security checks will immediately flag the files as suspicious."

articles.title: Morocco's ABA Life secures $40 million investment from Admaius Capital Partners
articles.text: Morocco-based healthtech company ABA Life has signed a $40 million investment agreement with pan-African private equity firm Admaius Capital Partners, subject to customary closing conditions and approval from Morocco's Competition Council. Founded in 2021, ABA Life is the healthcare arm of ABA Technology, founded and chaired by Mohamed Benouda. The company develops and operates healthcare solutions combining artificial intelligence, medical technology, telemedicine, connected healthcare infrastructure and clinical services. ABA Life has developed an integrated, profitable business model, delivering healthcare programmes in partnership with public institutions and foundations to expand access to medical services. The investment will support the company's AI for Sovereign Health programme, including its Mediot AI platform and clinical intelligence solutions, alongside the expansion of its healthcare technologies and services and entry into international markets. Press release: ABA Life, the healthcare arm of ABA Technology, has announced the signing of an investment agreement with Admaius Capital Partners (“Admaius”) for $40 million, subject to customary closing conditions and to clearance by the Competition Council of the Kingdom of Morocco. The transaction marks a major milestone in ABA Life’s growth and in its ambition to build, from Morocco, a healthtech champion with international reach. Founded only five years ago, ABA Life has built an integrated and profitable model combining artificial intelligence, medical technology, telemedicine, connected health infrastructure and healthcare operations. Through large-scale programmes, notably in partnership with public institutions and foundations, the company has shown its ability to turn technological innovation into concrete solutions that widen access to care. “AI for Sovereign Health”: accelerating innovation and scale The investment will support a new phase of growth built around three priorities: accelerating the “AI for Sovereign Health” programme through Mediot AI and the development of clinical intelligence solutions; industrialising and deploying the Group’s healthcare technologies and services at scale; and accelerating expansion into international markets. Building on its technology capabilities and operational experience, ABA Life intends to create a next-generation HealthTech platform combining artificial intelligence, medical innovation and operational excellence, with the ambition of building, from Morocco, one of the Kingdom’s next technology unicorns. “In five years, we have shown that a profitable healthcare technology model, able to deploy at scale, can be built from Morocco. This funding marks the start of a new phase: acceleration and internationalisation. Our ambition is to make ABA Life a global healthtech reference and one of Morocco’s next unicorns. With AI for Sovereign Health, we want to develop a new generation of clinical intelligence in Morocco and take it to international markets,” said Mohamed Benouda, Founder and Chairman of ABA Technology. “From our very first discussions, we were impressed by what ABA Life has built: an integrated healthcare operator combining medical devices, connected infrastructure, care operations and proprietary technology developed in Morocco. We are pleased to support Mohamed Benouda and his teams in this new phase of growth and international expansion,” said Selim Ettriqui, Head of Morocco and West Africa at Admaius Capital Partners. “ABA Life has the qualities we look for in our investments: an ambitious entrepreneurial team, a proven business model, strong technology foundations and significant potential to scale. We are convinced of its ability to become an international healthtech reference and are pleased to support this ambition,” said Marlon Chigwende, Managing Partner at Admaius Capital Partners.

articles.title: Une fusée se dresse à nouveau sur le pas de tir français de Diamant, 51 ans après son dernier lancement
articles.text:
Le CNES a dressé une maquette grandeur nature de Callisto, son démonstrateur de fusée réutilisable, sur l’ancien pas de tir de Diamant au Centre spatial guyanais. Une première depuis 51 ans, qui donne le coup d’envoi des essais au sol.
Le lanceur réutilisable Callisto n'a pas encore décollé, mais le Centre national d'études spatiales (CNES) lui a déjà offert une adresse prestigieuse. Sa maquette se dresse depuis quelques heures sur le tout premier pas de tir orbital de Kourou, celui d'où partait la fusée Diamant. Pendant une semaine, ce double grandeur nature va échanger avec le radar et les installations de la base sans quitter le sol d'un centimètre. L'exercice peut sembler modeste, mais il prépare en réalité un moment que le CNES juge crucial pour ces échanges, à savoir le retour sur Terre.
Callisto, la fusée réutilisable du CNES, fait enfin ses premiers pas en Guyane
Avant d'accueillir le vrai Callisto, le Centre spatial guyanais s'entraîne avec une doublure. Construite par la PME française CIPAL, cette maquette dévoilé ce jeudi 29 octobre 2026 reprend à l'identique la taille du démonstrateur, soit 13 mètres de haut pour un mètre de diamètre. Elle ne volera pas, mais elle embarque six antennes positionnées exactement comme sur l'engin définitif. L'idée est de vérifier tout ce qui se passe autour de la fusée : les installations du pas de tir, la façon dont le véhicule et la base se raccordent et communiquent entre eux, ainsi que les procédures que suivront les équipes le jour J.
Pendant cette semaine d'essais, tout tourne autour des communications. Une fusée en vol dialogue en permanence avec le sol. Elle transmet en temps réel au centre de contrôle les mesures de ses capteurs et les images de ses caméras, tandis que les équipes peuvent lui envoyer des ordres via son ordinateur de bord et que le radar de la base suit sa trajectoire. Selon le CNES, la précision de ces échanges compte au décollage, mais plus encore à la redescente. Car Callisto ne finira pas sa course dans l'océan, puisque comme un Falcon 9 de SpaceX, il doit revenir se poser à la verticale, à ceci près que son moteur fonctionne à l'hydrogène et à l'oxygène liquides, quand la fusée américaine carbure au kérosène.
Plutôt que d'attendre que le lanceur soit terminé pour tester la base, le CNES a choisi de mener les deux chantiers de front. En repérant d'éventuels problèmes côté sol pendant que le véhicule est encore en développement, l'agence espère gagner du temps et limiter la facture. Aux côtés des équipes du CNES et du Centre spatial guyanais, plusieurs industriels sont mobilisés, avec CIPAL, MT Aerospace Guyane, TSO et Thales Alenia Space. Ces essais lancent ainsi la qualification, une longue série de tests chargée de prouver que tout fonctionne comme prévu, qui s'étalera jusqu'en 2027. Quant au véritable Callisto, celui qui volera, le CNES annonce son arrivée « dans la foulée », sans plus de précision.
Sur le pas de tir de Diamant, Callisto court après son calendrier
Pour les passionnés du spatial français, l'image a une saveur assez particulière. Car Diamant fut le premier lanceur de satellites tricolore. Oui, c'est lui qui, en 1965, a fait de la France la troisième puissance spatiale de l'histoire, depuis la base d'Hammaguir en Algérie. Transférée en Guyane, la fusée a décollé de ce pas de tir dès mars 1970, pour huit lancements au total. Le programme s'est arrêté en 1975, faute de budget, car à l'époque, la France avait choisi de miser sur le projet européen Ariane, et le site a fini en zone de stockage. Le revoilà réhabilité, avec une fusée de nouveau dressée à la verticale, dans une configuration que le CNES juge proche de celle de l'époque. On aperçoit bien aussi, sur les photos transmises par le CNES, les sorties des carneaux, c'est-à-dire les conduits d'évacuation des flammes.
Le projet Callisto, lancé par le CNES en 2017 avec les agences allemande (DLR) et japonaise (JAXA) de l'espace, cette dernière fournit d'ailleurs le moteur réutilisable à hydrogène, testé cet été sur un petit prototype au pays du Soleil levant. À l'origine, le démonstrateur devait voler dès 2020 ou 2021, avant que l'objectif ne glisse d'année en année… jusqu'à 2026. L'agence n'avance pas de nouvelle date, mais avec une qualification qui court jusqu'en 2027, ce calendrier-là semble lui aussi dépassé.
Ce petit démonstrateur n'a de toute façon pas vocation à devenir un lanceur opérationnel. Sa campagne de dix vols, dont l'objectif est un aller-retour jusqu'à environ 20 km d'altitude, servira surtout à chiffrer ce que coûterait un premier étage réutilisable européen. En Suède, Themis, développé par ArianeGroup pour l'ESA, attend toujours son premier saut, que l'agence n'est plus certaine de voir d'ici la fin de l'année. Alors oui, même s'il y a des signaux positifs, face à SpaceX, qui fait atterrir ses boosters depuis une dizaine d'années, l'Europe a encore du chemin à parcourir.

articles.title: US Air Force turns to AI to solve one of its most dangerous flight missions
articles.text:
The US Air Force wants to use AI to help with its mid-air refuelling problems
US Air Force wants AI to spot dangerous refuelling mistakes
- US Air Force wants AI to detect mistakes during aerial refuelling
- Tanker cameras would supply footage for automated analysis of refuelling operations
- AI would monitor aircraft speed, alignment, positioning, and approach velocity
The US Air Force is exploring using AI to identify mistakes during aerial refuelling operations and improve how crews receive performance feedback.
The proposed system would analyze footage captured by tanker aircraft cameras, identifying flight manoeuvres and operational errors that conventional assessments might overlook.
Military officials want the technology to provide detailed evaluations of refuelling exercises, reducing dependence on human judgement during one of aviation's most demanding procedures.
AI system will monitor aircraft movements and refuelling accuracy
The initiative focuses on developing software capable of examining interactions between tanker aircraft and approaching receivers throughout the complicated fuel transfer process.
Using computer vision and machine learning, the technology would examine aircraft movements and determine whether crews maintained appropriate separation and alignment.
It would also monitor the refuelling boom, comparing its movements against aircraft trajectories to identify potentially dangerous deviations during fuel delivery.
Measurements would include aircraft speed, relative positioning, approach velocity and alignment, allowing instructors to examine specific manoeuvres rather than relying on general observations.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The proposed software would automatically identify departures from expected flight conditions and generate performance information for instructors reviewing completed refuelling missions.
Currently, assessments depend substantially on instructor observations, crew evaluations and manually examining recorded footage, according to the military's research solicitation.
These methods can produce inconsistent judgements, particularly when instructors interpret the same manoeuvre differently or overlook brief errors during complicated operations.
Therefore, the software’s assessment will include graphical overlays, colour-coded performance maps and chronological displays identifying significant events during individual refuelling exercises.
The Air Force consequently wants automated measurements that could provide more consistent evaluations while helping personnel understand precisely where mistakes occurred.
The project falls under the Small Business Innovation Research programme, which invites companies to develop technological solutions addressing specific military requirements.
Interested developers have until November 25 2026 to submit applications outlining how their proposed systems could satisfy the service's operational and training requirements.
KC-46 tanker technology and future training applications
The initial development effort concentrates on the KC-46 Pegasus, a refuelling aircraft equipped with cameras supporting remotely controlled fuel transfer operations.
Its remote vision equipment allows boom operators to guide the refuelling apparatus using camera feeds and 3D displays instead of direct observation.
However, the aircraft's existing viewing technology has experienced persistent technical difficulties, although military officials expect most outstanding problems to be resolved soon.
Developers are expected to consider interactive review environments that allow pilots and instructors to examine manoeuvres from different perspectives.
The technology could eventually connect with flight simulators, virtual reality equipment and augmented reality training platforms already used for aviation instruction.
Military planners want an operational prototype suitable for integration with existing training arrangements for at least one category of receiving aircraft.
The solicitation also identifies potential applications beyond refuelling, including automated assessments of other aviation activities throughout the Department of Defense

articles.title: Vivillon regresa en Pokémon Legends: Z-A tras 10 años de espera
articles.text:
Vivillon Motivo Pokébola volverá a estar disponible por primera vez desde 2016. Los jugadores de Leyendas Pokémon: Z-A podrán obtener esta forma especial, que hasta ahora solo se había distribuido mediante eventos.
La campaña permitirá conseguir un Vivillon Motivo Pokébola si la comunidad mundial alcanza 660.000 puntos Vivillon al evolucionar Spewpa. Pokémon todavía no informó la fecha en la que se habilitará la distribución final de esta variante.
Los jugadores pueden recibir un Spewpa mediante la función Regalo misterioso. El plazo para reclamarlo vence el 18 de noviembre, y el Pokémon evoluciona al llegar al nivel 12.
Cómo es Vivillon
Vivillon es el Pokémon número 666 de la Pokédex y pertenece a los tipos Bicho y Volador. Es la evolución de Spewpa, que a su vez evoluciona desde Scatterbug.
La particularidad de Vivillon está en sus alas: puede presentar distintos motivos. El Spewpa distribuido en la campaña puede evolucionar de forma aleatoria en uno de 16 diseños disponibles, aunque quedan excluidos el Motivo Floral, el Motivo Marino, el Motivo Vergel y el especial Motivo Pokébola.
El Vivillon Motivo Pokébola se distingue por un diseño inspirado en la clásica Poké Ball. La forma solo había estado disponible mediante distribuciones especiales: la primera se realizó en París en 2014 y la última, en 2016.
En qué consiste Leyendas Pokémon: Z-A
Leyendas Pokémon: Z-A es una aventura de rol ambientada en Ciudad Luminalia, donde se desarrolla un plan de renovación urbana para convertir el lugar en un espacio compartido entre personas y Pokémon.
El juego modifica el sistema tradicional de la franquicia con combates en tiempo real: los Entrenadores y sus Pokémon pueden desplazarse durante las batallas, mientras que el alcance, el área de efecto y el tiempo de activación de los movimientos influyen en cada enfrentamiento.
La aventura también incluye los Juegos Z-A, una competición nocturna en la que los jugadores comienzan en el rango Z y deben ganar combates para avanzar hasta el rango A. Durante el día, pueden capturar Pokémon en las zonas salvajes, entrenar a su equipo y reunir objetos antes de volver a competir.
Pokémon UNITE se despide de Nintendo Switch y dispositivos moviles en 2027
Pokémon UNITE finalizará su servicio el 23 de marzo de 2027 en Nintendo Switch y dispositivos móviles, según The Pokémon Company. Desde esa fecha, los jugadores no podrán iniciar sesión ni participar en partidas, lo que pondrá fin a casi seis años de actividad del título de estrategia y acción en tiempo real.
El juego se estrenó en Nintendo Switch el 21 de julio de 2021 y luego llegó a dispositivos móviles.
Durante su funcionamiento, propuso partidas de cinco contra cinco en las que cada participante controlaba un Pokémon, lo hacía subir de nivel y buscaba sumar más puntos que el equipo rival antes de que terminara el límite de 10 minutos.
La compañía suspendió la venta de gemas Aeos el 27 de octubre de 2026. Sin embargo, los usuarios podrán gastar las que ya tengan en sus cuentas hasta el cierre definitivo.
Se interrumpieron las nuevas suscripciones y las renovaciones automáticas de UNITE Club, aunque quienes mantengan una membresía activa conservarán sus beneficios hasta el fin del período contratado.
Antes del cierre, Pokémon UNITE recibirá una actualización el 12 de noviembre de 2026.
El parche incluirá un evento especial y una función de Biblioteca, que permitirá consultar algunos registros y contenidos una vez que el servicio deje de estar disponible. Para acceder a esa herramienta después de marzo de 2027, los jugadores deberán descargar los datos necesarios antes de la fecha límite.
El calendario competitivo continuará hasta 2027. El torneo Pokémon UNITE Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo mantendrá sus eliminatorias, previstas para comenzar el 5 de diciembre de 2026.
De esta manera, el juego tendrá una última etapa de contenidos, recompensas y competencias antes de despedirse definitivamente de sus dos plataformas.

articles.title: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon Leads Benchmarks for Finding, Exploiting, and Patching Vulnerabilities
articles.text:
Google on Wednesday took the wraps off Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities.
"It shows significant gains across coding and agentic tasks as well as across key capabilities critical for cybersecurity defense, landing a firm lead in SEC-bench Pro (88.2%) for finding vulnerabilities, ExploitGym (54.8%) for exploitation, and CWE-bench (71.0%) for patching," Koray Kavukcuoglu, senior vice president of Google DeepMind and chief AI architect at Google, said.
On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index benchmark, Carbon leads with a score of 59, surpassing Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 (58), OpenAI GPT-6 Astra (57), GPT-6.1 Sol (55).
One of the core focus areas is cybersecurity, where the latest iteration reportedly delivers significant performance improvements across the board, including vulnerability detection, validation, and remediation. Carbon is also twice as likely to generate secure code versus Argon.
Google also emphasized that Carbon attempts to respond to complex or high-pressure tasks by seeking human input in the face of ambiguity rather than "guessing or forcing a path forward," as well as resisting every evaluated attack attempt at indirect prompt injection.
The debut of Gemini 4 Carbon comes less than a week after the tech giant unveiled Gemini 4 Argon. The release plan is similar to that of its predecessor, with the rollout currently limited to a subset of cyber defenders before expanding access to other trusted partners as part of its Fairwind Program.
Google also said it's actively engaged in the U.S. government's voluntary process for pre-release model testing.
The development comes as OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra, which it described as a fast, efficient model that "excels at communication and computer-based tasks."
"GPT‑6.1 Terra meets the Critical threshold in cybersecurity under our Preparedness Framework, and maintains the protections developed for GPT‑6 Astra," OpenAI said.
"GPT-6.1 Terra brings with it the alignment improvements of the GPT-6 series. According to our evaluations, GPT-6.1 Terra is more likely to stay within scope and honestly disclose limitations and potential blockers to the user compared to GPT-5.6 Terra. In our prompt-injection tests, GPT-6.1 Terra also showed strong resistance to malicious instructions designed to divert it from the user's task."
Earlier this week, rival Anthropic also disclosed that an unreleased, internal research model uncovered critical vulnerabilities in some of the world's most widely used software.
This included a one-click remote code execution in Google Chrome, a one-click exploit chain in Apple Safari that could be used to access a user's browsing history, cookies, and other sensitive data, an Android lock screen bypass, and a denial-of-service (DoS) flaw in the Windows HTTP.sys driver (CVE-2026-33096, CVSS score: 7.5). All the identified issues have been fixed by Google, Apple, and Microsoft.
"These attack chains demonstrate the model's ability to create sophisticated, multi-step exploits in both open-source and proprietary software," Anthropic said.
"These skills have historically been the domain of few specialist teams with expertise in these targets. Now, it’s something models can do with little human involvement, and then prove by producing a working exploit that anyone can run and verify."

articles.title: Egypt's Tanmiya Capital closes $130 million fund backed by EIB, IFC and EBRD
articles.text: Egypt-based private equity firm Tanmiya Capital Ventures (TCV) has announced the final close of its second fund at $130 million, exceeding its $120 million target, following a $37.5 million commitment from the European Investment Bank (EIB) through its development arm, EIB Global. The fund is backed by international and local institutional investors, including the Egyptian-American Enterprise Fund (EAEF), European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), International Finance Corporation (IFC) and Egypt's Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise Development Agency (MSMEDA). Founded in 2016, Tanmiya Capital Ventures focuses on growth equity and private equity investments in established mid-market Egyptian businesses. Fund II will target companies operating in healthcare, training, fintech, consumer goods, logistics and transport, providing capital and operational support to facilitate expansion. The fund is expected to build a portfolio of six to eight companies, supporting business growth, corporate governance improvements and job creation. At least 30% of its portfolio companies are expected to meet one or more of the EIB's gender equality financing criteria. Press release: The European Investment Bank (EIB), through its development arm EIB Global, invested $37.5 million in Tanmiya Capital Fund II to expand access to growth capital for established small and medium-sized companies in Egypt. The investment was announced today at a ceremony in Cairo attended by EIB Vice-President Gelsomina Vigliotti and Tanmiya Capital Ventures Managing Partners Ahmed El Guindy, Youssef Ahmed Ayoub and Mohamed Mohsen Mahgoub. The EIB commitment helped Tanmiya Capital Fund II reach a final close of $130 million, exceeding its $120 million target. The fund is supported by a diversified group of international and local investors, including the Egyptian-American Enterprise Fund (EAEF), the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), the International Finance Corporation (IFC), and Egypt’s Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise Development Agency (MSMEDA). Managed by the independent Egyptian investment firm Tanmiya Capital, the fund will invest in a diversified portfolio of established, high-growth companies in Egypt. It will focus on businesses seeking strategic capital to expand, professionalise their operations and strengthen their competitiveness, with investments expected across healthcare, training, financial technology, consumer goods, logistics and transport. The investment addresses the limited availability of long-term equity finance for small and medium-sized companies in Egypt. By combining capital with strategic and managerial support, the fund is expected to help portfolio companies scale up, improve governance and create jobs. At least 30% of portfolio companies are expected to meet one or more of the EIB’s criteria for financing that supports gender equality. “Egypt’s private sector has enormous potential to drive sustainable growth, create quality jobs and deepen economic ties with Europe. Our investment in Tanmiya Capital Fund II will provide ambitious local companies with the growth capital and expertise they need to expand. It also reflects the European Union’s commitment, through Global Gateway and the new Agenda for the Mediterranean, to supporting a more competitive, inclusive and resilient Egyptian economy,” said EIB Vice-President Gelsomina Vigliotti. “The successful closing of Tanmiya Capital Fund II above its target reflects strong investor confidence in our strategy and in the potential of Egypt’s private sector. The EIB’s commitment brings not only capital, but also valuable international expertise and a shared focus on sustainable growth, strong governance and long-term value creation. Together, we will support ambitious Egyptian companies as they scale up, become more competitive and expand their links with regional and European markets,” said Tanmiya Capital Managing Partner Ahmed El Guindy. “Our investment in Tanmiya Capital Ventures Fund II reflects IFC’s commitment to strengthening Egypt’s private sector by expanding access to the long-term growth capital businesses need to grow and create jobs," said Ary Naïm, IFC's Division Director for North Africa and the Horn of Africa. "By partnering with experienced local fund managers, we can help promising Egyptian companies, including family-owned businesses, strengthen their operations, become more competitive, and scale. This is an important part of our broader work to mobilize private investment and support sustainable, inclusive growth in Egypt.” “Our investment in Tanmiya Capital Fund II reinforces MSMEDA’s Fund of Funds program mandate, through which we partner with experienced private equity and venture capital managers and support emerging ones to crowd in private and international capital into promising Egyptian companies. We believe TCVII will channel much-needed growth capital and expertise to businesses with real potential to expand and create jobs, in line with the Egypt’s strategy to empower the private sector and Vision 2030,” said Mostafa Ismail Hassan, CEO of the Egypt’s Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise Development Agency (MSMEDA). “We are proud to continue our long-standing partnership with TCV, a team that has consistently demonstrated its ability to invest in and build growing businesses in Egypt. The fund’s oversubscribed close is a strong signal of investor confidence, and our commitment reflects our firm belief in the long-term fundamentals of the Egyptian economy and the central role of its private sector in driving growth and job creation,” said Yasmine Ghobrial, Chief Investment Officer of the Egyptian-American Enterprise Fund (EAEF). The operation follows a Team Europe approach and supports the EU-Africa Global Gateway Investment Package. It is also expected to strengthen commercial links between Egypt and Europe, as portfolio companies may source equipment, technology and services from European suppliers or develop partnerships with European businesses. At its target scale, the fund is expected to build a portfolio of six to eight companies and support thousands of jobs across Egypt. The EIB will also contribute its experience in environmental, social and governance standards and international private equity best practice through its participation in the fund’s advisory committee.

articles.title: Fusions-acquisitions et due diligence cyber : pourquoi le passif numérique d'une PME peut torpiller une opération
articles.text:
Quand vous vendez votre PME, l'acheteur vérifie vos comptes, mais aussi vos systèmes informatiques, avant de signer. Ce qu'il découvre peut faire baisser son offre ou repousser la vente de plusieurs mois.
Vous êtes sur le point de vendre votre structure. Votre repreneur, et c'est bien logique, ne vous la rachète pas les yeux fermés en vous faisant confiance. Il fait contrôler vos systèmes informatiques par une équipe technique, de la même manière que vos comptes par un expert-comptable.
C'est ce qu'on appelle la due diligence cyber dans le jargon des fusions-acquisitions. Selon Bpifrance Le Lab, 370 000 entreprises françaises changeront de mains d'ici 2030, et 40 % des dirigeants de PME ou d'ETI veulent céder leur activité dans les cinq prochaines années. Pour vous, ce contrôle peut peser sur le prix final ou sur les délais de la vente.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Vos systèmes informatiques sous contrôle
Selon le rapport d'activité 2025 de Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr, il y a eu plus de 500 000 personnes et entreprises accompagnées sur l'année. Les signalements de fuites de données ont progressé de 107 % par rapport à 2024, et les tentatives d'hameçonnage de 70 %. Normal dans ce cas que cela pousse le repreneur à contrôler vos systèmes avant de vous croire sur parole.
L'équipe technique mandatée par le repreneur cherche d'abord les failles non corrigées dans vos systèmes et vérifie si chaque incident passé a bien été déclaré à la CNIL. Elle chiffre ensuite ce qu'une fuite de vos données clients coûterait après la vente, pour ajuster son offre en conséquence.
Le baromètre 2025 de Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr, mené auprès de 588 entreprises de moins de 250 salariés, indique un incident de sécurité dans 16 % des cas au cours des douze derniers mois. Une PME sur quatre seulement a mis en place une procédure écrite de réponse à incident. Si vous n'avez pas cette procédure, un repreneur le verra dans les premières heures de son contrôle.
La garantie de prix et le risque numérique
Le règlement européen sur la protection des données vous oblige à notifier une violation de données personnelles à la CNIL dans un délai de 72 heures après sa découverte. Si vous avez subi une fuite sans jamais la déclarer, votre acheteur hérite de cette obligation non remplie et du risque d'une sanction pour un manquement commis avant la vente.
Un rançongiciel jamais totalement neutralisé pose un second problème. L'accès que l'attaquant a laissé ouvert peut resservir après la vente, même si vous avez payé une rançon ou restauré vos données au moment des faits.
Ces deux situations pèsent directement sur la garantie de passif que vous signez au moment de la cession. Cette clause protège l'acheteur si la réalité de votre entreprise diffère de ce que vous avez déclaré avant la signature, avec un délai de notification et un plafond fixés par contrat. Une partie du prix, généralement entre 5 et 10 %, est bloquée sur un compte séquestre pendant toute la durée de cette garantie. Dans l'encadré ci-dessous, vous pourrez en apprendre plus sur son fonctionnement précis.
Si vous vendez une très petite structure sans garantie de passif formalisée, l'acheteur compense l'absence de recours contractuel par une décote appliquée dès l'offre initiale. Il calcule cette décote à partir des failles identifiées pendant son contrôle.
Déclarer un incident avant la signature vous permet de négocier son impact sur le prix avant que la vente ne soit conclue. Si vous ne le déclarez pas et que l'acheteur le découvre après coup, il doit vous notifier dans un délai contractuel précis, souvent entre 30 et 60 jours, faute de quoi il perd son droit à indemnisation.
Le prix de cacher un incident
D'après le baromètre de Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr évoqué plus haut, une interruption d'activité touche 29 % des entreprises confrontées à un incident. Un vol de données en touche 22 %, et une perte financière directe 11 %. Pour vous, ces trois conséquences influencent le prix que l'acheteur est prêt à payer, qu'elles soient déclarées à l'avance ou découvertes après coup. Une interruption d'activité de plusieurs jours, par exemple, réduit le chiffre d'affaires que l'acheteur intègre dans son calcul de valorisation.
Une faille majeure détectée pendant le contrôle a aussi un effet sur les délais. La signature peut être reportée le temps qu'un prestataire corrige les points bloquants, ou les clauses de la garantie de passif rediscutées avant la vente.
Toujours selon Bpifrance Le Lab, environ 130 000 TPE et PME changeront de mains en France au cours des cinq prochaines années, au rythme actuel des cessions. Une PME qui prouve une bonne hygiène numérique inverse ce rapport de force et accélère sa vente.
Comment nettoyer votre posture 
de sécurité avant la vente pour négocier son prix au plus juste
Documentez votre politique de sécurité informatique avant de mandater un repreneur. L'ANSSI réunit treize mesures essentielles pour les TPE et les PME dans son guide de référence. Comme vous pourrez le lire plus bas dans notre décryptage sur les failles de sécurité liées aux arrivées et aux départs de salariés, la plupart des PME n'ont jamais formalisé leurs droits d'accès ni leurs procédures de départ. Le repreneur repère ces deux lacunes en quelques heures.
Testez vos sauvegardes hors ligne au moins une fois par trimestre et documentez chaque test par écrit. L'acheteur exige toujours une preuve écrite, jamais une simple déclaration orale sur ce point.
Dans notre décryptage sur les prérequis techniques que les assureurs cyber exigent de leurs clients, on vous détaillait les critères qu'ils vérifient. Pour un repreneur, ce sera quasiment la même chose. Activez donc une authentification forte sur vos messageries et vos accès cloud. Isolez vos sauvegardes du réseau principal et testez leur restauration. Mettez en place une supervision continue de vos systèmes et un plan de gestion des correctifs. Formez votre personnel par des campagnes régulières de simulation de phishing.
Téléchargez enfin la MalletteCyber Pro de Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr. Lancé en juin 2026 pour les structures de moins de 250 salariés, cet outil gratuit réunit un livret pratique et un jeu de cartes pour sensibiliser vos équipes sans budget dédié. Onze organisations professionnelles, dont la CCI France et le Medef, soutiennent cette initiative. Le kit est disponible sous licence ouverte et prêt à imprimer directement. Ces vérifications prennent du temps. Mieux vaut les engager plusieurs mois avant de contacter un repreneur, pas après avoir reçu une première offre.

articles.title: Anthropic sued over Elvis catalog — and the 274-song copyright battle shows the AI industry's 'fair use' excuses are getting old
articles.text:
Anthropic sued for allegedly using 274 Elvis Presley songs in AI training — and it's about time AI companies faced the music
The owners of Elvis's songs are taking Claude's developer to court
Elvis Presley has been dead for nearly 50 years, but apparently even the 'King of Rock and Roll' can't escape the AI industry's appetite for training data. The owners of 274 Elvis songs made famous by Presley have sued Anthropic, accusing the company behind Claude of using his music without permission to build its AI models, and are seeking tens of millions of dollars in damages.
Anthropic disputes the allegations and says it intends to defend the case. AI companies have long argued that training models on copyrighted works can qualify as fair use, an issue courts are still working through. There's an important legal difference between learning patterns from existing material and reproducing protected expression, but that distinction has become a remarkably convenient place for the AI industry to hide its enormous dependence on other people's creativity.
It's hard to sympathize with the companies on the receiving end of these sorts of lawsuits, even when the plaintiffs are not without resources of their own. Unfortunately, these disputes are becoming all too normal. AI-powered music is becoming more widespread, if not necessarily popular, and we've reached a point where discovering that an AI company allegedly used hundreds of copyrighted songs without permission barely qualifies as surprising news.
The only unusual part is that this time the person whose music is at the center of the dispute happens to be Elvis Presley.
A little less uncompensated song use
The lawsuit makes an accusation that goes beyond simply using copyrighted material for training. According to the complaint, Claude could generate material that closely resembled existing Elvis songs, even after Anthropic introduced safeguards intended to prevent infringement. Requests to recreate songs for modern audiences allegedly produced versions retaining recognizable elements of the originals.
An AI model learning about music isn't automatically infringing copyright, and copyright law doesn't give anyone ownership of an entire musical style. But if a commercial AI system reproduces protected lyrics or creates unauthorized adaptations, it's hard to see why the company behind it should get a special exemption simply because the copying happens through complicated software.
AI companies have been trying out various arguments in court, but a lot of it feels like an attempt to claim that AI development is so important that the usual rules should somehow bend around it. Training requires enormous amounts of information, and licensing everything would be expensive or inconvenient, but that's a standard headache for companies whose products rely on copyrighted material.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
TV shows and movies license music, whether an original track or just the right to record a new version for their project. No company is allowed to simply grab hold of copyrighted material simply because clearing it would slow down development. AI companies should have to take copyright seriously too, even if that makes their business models more expensive.
It's also particularly galling that songs people spent years creating and popularizing can become raw material for commercial technology without the rights holders having any meaningful say. Access to a work and permission to exploit it are separate questions, regardless of how sophisticated the software becomes. Ignoring those rules is why artists who passed away decades ago seem to produce new music whose earnings don't go to their estate.
AI music turns the volume up
Elvis is hardly the first musician to become part of this fight. Major music publishers have already sued Anthropic over allegations involving copyrighted lyrics, while AI music generator Suno has faced legal challenges from record labels. The Elvis lawsuit stands out because it focuses on the catalog associated with one of the most recognizable performers in history.
That fame might help draw attention to a problem that has affected considerably less powerful creators for years. Independent artists may struggle to establish whether their work was used to train a model. If someone with Elvis Presley's commercial legacy needs a federal lawsuit to challenge alleged unauthorized copying, ordinary musicians' prospects look bleak.
Of course, the companies controlling Elvis's catalog aren't struggling artists themselves, but that doesn't make the underlying complaint any less important. The principle shouldn't depend on whether the copyright owner is wealthy or famous.
I'm also not convinced that every AI company needs unrestricted access to practically everything ever written or recorded to produce useful technology. Claude is an impressive assistant, but its ability to answer questions doesn't suddenly make songwriters' copyright interests irrelevant. If AI developers want to build profitable products using creative works, they should be prepared to explain where that material came from and why they were entitled to use it.
The courts may decide in Anthropic's favor due to fair use, but even that ruling wouldn't automatically mean AI companies have permission to go wild on every song ever recorded. The best path forward won't be as simple as making it always allowed or illegal to use copyrighted material for AI training, but the companies building these systems shouldn't rely on their ambitions as a good enough reason to ignore rights holders.
The AI industry has become very good at explaining how much it needs human creativity, but it's time it became equally good at respecting the people responsible for it.

articles.title: Qué pasa si te roban la cuenta de ChatGPT y qué medidas tomar
articles.text:
Un viaje organizado, una consulta técnica, el análisis de una propuesta comercial, documentos de trabajo sensibles o una conversación incómoda que se quiere preparar antes de tenerla: todo eso queda almacenado en ChatGPT cada vez que un usuario lo utiliza. La compañía de ciberseguridad ESET Latinoamérica advierte que cada consulta o pedido incorpora información privada sobre intereses, hábitos, proyectos, relaciones y preocupaciones, un detalle que convierte a la cuenta en un blanco atractivo si cae en manos de un ciberdelincuente.
El riesgo no se limita a la simple lectura de conversaciones ajenas. Según el análisis de ESET, también depende de la información que se haya compartido, las funciones utilizadas dentro de la plataforma y los servicios externos que estén conectados a la cuenta.
Qué puede hacer un atacante con la cuenta vulnerada
El escenario más común es el acceso a información sensible. Si un cibercriminal vulnera una cuenta, puede leer todas las conversaciones, revisar documentos compartidos y acceder a cualquier otro dato disponible. Dependiendo de lo que se haya ingresado, pueden quedar expuestos datos personales, información laboral, estudios médicos o detalles de proyectos confidenciales.
Ese mismo contenido puede convertirse en insumo para ataques de ingeniería social más convincentes. Al conocer intereses, relaciones profesionales y personales del usuario, el atacante cuenta con elementos para diseñar estafas y engaños más creíbles y, por lo tanto, más peligrosos.
El problema también puede trascender al usuario original. Si se compartieron contratos, datos de clientes o documentos internos de una empresa, el incidente puede escalar y afectar a colegas, clientes o a la organización completa.
Las integraciones y permisos habilitados amplían el margen de daño. Por ejemplo, si la cuenta tiene conectada una función para enviar correos electrónicos, el atacante podría enviar mensajes haciéndose pasar por el usuario real, ya sea para engañar a un compañero de trabajo, solicitar información confidencial o distribuir un enlace fraudulento. Si además existe acceso a documentos laborales, el atacante podría consultar archivos con información sensible.
Cuando la cuenta tiene habilitadas funciones de pago, créditos de API o recursos facturables, el ciberdelincuente puede generar consumos no autorizados y provocar pérdidas económicas directas. En los casos más graves, el atacante puede modificar las configuraciones de seguridad y dificultar la recuperación del acceso, lo que deja al usuario sin sus conversaciones y herramientas mientras intenta contener el incidente.
Las tres formas más comunes en que se roba una cuenta
La firma de ciberseguridad detalla tres vías principales por las que una cuenta de ChatGPT termina en poder de un atacante. La primera es el phishing: un correo o mensaje que simula provenir de ChatGPT u OpenAI alerta sobre un supuesto problema de seguridad o la necesidad de verificar los datos, e incluye un enlace a una página falsa diseñada para robar el correo electrónico y la contraseña. Este engaño también puede llegar a través de redes sociales o anuncios fraudulentos.
La segunda vía es la reutilización de contraseñas. Usar la misma clave en ChatGPT, el correo electrónico y otras plataformas facilita el trabajo al atacante: si las credenciales de uno de esos servicios se filtran en una brecha de datos, pueden emplearse para iniciar sesión en otras cuentas mediante una técnica conocida como credential stuffing.
La tercera corresponde a dispositivos comprometidos o sesiones expuestas. Un equipo infectado con malware puede permitir el robo de información ingresada por el usuario o de credenciales almacenadas. También existen situaciones menos sofisticadas, como dejar una sesión abierta en una computadora compartida, usar un equipo ajeno sin cerrar la cuenta o perder un dispositivo desbloqueado, lo que permite a cualquiera acceder a la información disponible.
“Establecer qué tan grave puede ser que roben una cuenta de ChatGPT dependerá de la utilidad que se le dé, la información que se comparta, las funciones que se utilicen y los servicios conectados que se tengan a la cuenta”, explicó Mario Micucci, investigador de Seguridad Informática de ESET Latinoamérica.
Según el especialista, no enfrenta las mismas consecuencias quien usa la herramienta para consultas generales que quien comparte información de clientes y documentos internos de una empresa.
Los pasos a seguir ante un acceso no autorizado
ESET recomienda actuar con rapidez cuando se detecta o se sospecha de un ingreso no autorizado, dado que el objetivo no es solo recuperar el acceso, sino impedir que el atacante permanezca conectado.
El primer paso es cambiar la contraseña por una nueva, única y robusta. Si el acceso a la cuenta se realiza mediante Google o Microsoft, también debe modificarse esa credencial, ya que pudo quedar comprometida. El segundo paso consiste en cerrar todas las sesiones activas desde la configuración de seguridad de ChatGPT, lo que obliga a los dispositivos conectados a iniciar sesión nuevamente.
A continuación, conviene revisar la actividad de la cuenta en busca de acciones no reconocidas, como inicios de sesión, cambios de contraseña, modificaciones en los métodos de autenticación o conversaciones que no se recuerde haber generado.
El cuarto paso es activar la autenticación de doble factor, que agrega una verificación adicional al momento de iniciar sesión. ESET aclara que esta medida debe aplicarse después de cambiar la contraseña y cerrar las sesiones activas, ya que activarla no desconecta a quien ya haya ingresado previamente con la cuenta comprometida.
Por último, si se detectó actividad no autorizada, no es posible recuperar el acceso o persiste la sospecha de que la cuenta sigue comprometida, se recomienda contactar al equipo de soporte de OpenAI a través de su Centro de ayuda oficial.

articles.title: Bungie Ignites Rumors of "Destiny Classic" With Destiny 1 Re-Release Teaser
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
Bungie Ignites Rumors of "Destiny Classic" With Destiny 1 Re-Release Teaser
Following the disappointing launch of Marathon, which apparently came at the cost of development support for Destiny 2 and much of the team behind it, Bungie has officially dropped a hint of its next move in its plan to "return Destiny to its original promise," as promised in a prior studio update. In a recent Steam community update, Bungie's Josh Deane, the new general manager of Marathon, reiterates that Bungie is "not done with Destiny," going on to tease "Destiny Legacy," and stating that "the whole experience needs to be served to you all," which sounds an awful lot like a relaunch of the original Destiny, just judging by the description.
Destiny 'Legacy' [Expect a new February Progress bar] 
Our epic journey started over a decade ago, and the whole experience needs to be served to you all where you play today. Expect more information when we come back to you all early next year.
While a re-release of Destiny has gotten fans excited, Deane also provided an update on the re-release plans for Destiny 2, which is already in pre-production and is slated to enter production in February 2027. Deane estimates that the production phase will take around 12 months from then, so an early 2028 re-launch (unvaulting) for Destiny 2 is possible, officially restoring all the legacy content that was previously promised to be returned.
What are we starting with? In our "Next Chapter of Bungie" comms, we noted Campaigns, Destinations, and Raids specifically. What else is on the table? 
Josh: Our first pass for unvaulting, available to all players, focuses on getting our campaign slate whole again. We're specifically targeting the activity content of Campaigns, Strikes, and Raids from vaulted expansions. Menagerie holds a special place in our hearts (and we've seen years of community requests for a return), so it will be a part of this pass as well:
- Red War, Forsaken, Curse of Osiris, and Warmind campaigns
- Strikes from the above releases
- Raids, and Raid Lairs from the above releases
- Menagerie Activity with reprised rewards
Beyond this first pass, we're also investigating content that we're defining as stretch goals at unvaulting launch or after. For example, we know aspirational content like legacy Raids needs a deeper chase even if we may not able to address it upfront. As we get closer to unvaulting we'll be able to provide stronger insight into these areas:
- Free Roam Destinations (Public Events, Lost Sectors, Escalation Protocol, etc.)
- Seasonal Activities from Sundial (Season 9) to The Coil (Season 23)
- Raid and Raid Lair Weapon updates
- PvP Maps
Our final section currently does not have a path to update either for technical and/or strategic reasons. As we're looking to build the future of Destiny, we need to find balance. While we'd love to bring back some additional activities, or refresh things like our New Light experience, it could come at a cost for what we want to build for you in the future:
- Updated New Light Experience
- Seasonal Story Missions
- Gambit Map (Kell's Grave)
- Seasonal Hubs (e.g., Eliksni Quarter)
Source:
				Bungie on Steam

articles.title: Les militaires français peuvent assembler eux-mêmes ce détecteur de brouillage GPS maison
articles.text:
La Direction générale de l’armement a livré quinze détecteurs de brouillage GPS à des bases de l’Armée de l’air et de l’espace. Conçu en interne, le KJLab repère aussi les tentatives de leurrage sur quatre constellations satellites.
Le brouillage GPS, longtemps cantonné aux scénarios d'espionnage, fait désormais partie du quotidien des armées. La Direction générale de l'armement (DGA) s'organise pour le contrer, comme en témoigne la livraison à l'Armée de l'air et de l'espace d'une petite série de détecteurs conçus en interne. Quinze exemplaires du KJLab montent désormais la garde sur des bases aériennes, l'oreille tendue vers les satellites américains, européens, chinois et russes. Leur conception en quatre mois et leur fabrication dans un fablab interne tranchent, on peut dire, avec les longs programmes d’armement habituels.
La DGA se dote d'un détecteur fait maison contre le brouillage GPS
Le KJLab a pour mission de traquer deux menaces distinctes. On sait que les signaux des satellites de navigation, émis depuis environ 20 000 kilomètres d'altitude, arrivent au sol très affaiblis. Le brouillage en profite, puisqu'il les couvre d'un bruit radio bien plus puissant, si bien que le récepteur n'entend plus rien et perd sa position. Le leurrage, plus sournois, imite ces signaux pour transmettre de fausses coordonnées. Ici, l'appareil continue de fonctionner normalement, mais se croit tout simplement ailleurs. Dans les deux cas, un avion ou un drone peut perdre le nord, au sens le plus littéral du terme.
L'une de ses forces, c'est l'étendue de son écoute. Pour détecter le brouillage, le KJLab peut en même temps surveiller les quatre grandes constellations GNSS, l'acronyme qui désigne les systèmes de positionnement par satellite. Cela comprend le GPS américain, l'européen Galileo (qui va bientôt se renforcer de satellite de nouvelle génération), le chinois BeiDou et le russe GLONASS. Chacune de ces constellations émet sur plusieurs fréquences, comme une station de radio qui diffuserait sur plusieurs canaux. Sur la tablette durcie qui lui sert d'écran, une grille passe ces canaux en revue un à un, de L1 et L5 pour le GPS à G1 et G2 pour GLONASS, pour montrer d'un coup d'œil lequel est perturbé.
Le KJLab ne faut pas que constater les dégâts en direct. Il enregistre ses mesures sans limite de durée, ce qui permet de rejouer un incident après coup, pour en décortiquer le déroulé. L'opérateur humain garde aussi sous les yeux l'historique des 30 dernières minutes. Et côté réception, l'appareil se fie aux signaux GNSS civils, ceux ouverts à tous et que nos téléphones exploitent en partie.
Un détecteur appelé à évoluer avec les retours du terrain
Non, cet objet n'est pas issu d'un appel d'offres interminable, mais d'un projet d'innovation participative, une démarche qui permet aux personnels du ministère de porter eux-mêmes une idée jusqu'à sa réalisation. Le besoin, lui, a été validé par une équipe de militaires et la DGA. La livraison porte la signature du CeRGEN, le centre de la DGA chargé de fédérer les compétences en guerre électronique, l'art d’écouter, de perturber ou de protéger les ondes, et en guerre de la navigation (NAVWAR), qui vise précisément les signaux de positionnement.
Le KJLab, et c'est une petite performance, a été conçu en à peine quatre mois. Il a mobilisé plusieurs départements de DGA Maîtrise de l'information, le site breton de la DGA spécialisé dans la cyberdéfense et la guerre électronique, avec l'appui du correspondant innovation du centre, chargé d’accompagner ce type de projets.
Avant d'être livrés, les appareils ont été fiabilisés, autrement dit testés et consolidés pour tenir la route sur le terrain, puis fabriqués dans le tout nouveau fablab du site, un atelier où l'on conçoit et assemble soi-même les prototypes et petites séries. Le plus important peut-être, c'est que les militaires pourront, s'ils le souhaitent, monter eux-mêmes leurs détecteurs à partir de kits, comme un meuble livré en pièces détachées. Voilà qui devrait les aider à gagner en réactivité en fonction des besoins du terrain, mais aussi en autonomie et en résilience, puisque les unités peuvent s'équiper par leurs propres moyens.
Le KJLab, qui ressemble à une tablette de 10 pouces équipée d'une connectique USB-C, est en plus évolutif. Les choix de mise en œuvre, les essais sur le terrain et les exercices sont pensés main dans la main avec les forces, dont les retours d'expérience permettront au CeRGEN d'ajuster le produit si nécessaire. Une logique itérative presque digne d'une start-up, bienvenue à l'heure où le brouillage des signaux satellites est devenu monnaie courante dans plusieurs régions d'Europe.

articles.title: Nvidia’s new Vera Rubin chips are heading to Meta in a $3bn deal
articles.text:
Nvidia is set to work even closer with Meta's slightly creepy Muse AI models — and it's even investing $3bn in Meta to show its support
Nvidia commits billions to Meta’s share offering
- Nvidia reveals plans to invest $3 billion in Meta’s share offering
- Meta could raise $95 billion to finance its expanding AI infrastructure
- Nvidia hardware will support Meta’s next generation of artificial intelligence agents
Nvidia has revealed plans to invest $3 billion in Meta’s share offering while both companies increase cooperation on artificial intelligence systems designed to operate as personal agents.
The agreement will give Meta access to additional Nvidia computing technology as Facebook’s parent company develops its Muse models and associated artificial intelligence services.
It also includes discussions about agent supervision technologies, although the companies have not disclosed a timetable for implementing every proposed collaboration.
Nvidia hardware will power Meta’s next generation of AI agents
Meta expects to install more Nvidia equipment, including its forthcoming Vera Rubin platform and Vera central processors, to support training and execution of advanced agent systems.
The companies also intend to improve performance throughout the computing process, with particular attention to processing efficiency, system throughput and infrastructure operating expenses.
Networking equipment will form another part of Meta’s planned deployment, including Nvidia Spectrum-X technology and BlueField-4 components for handling communication between computing resources.
The companies are considering Nvidia’s OpenShell architecture for safer agent deployment, alongside Sentry technology intended to track agent activity and support data processing.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“AI agents represent a new computing paradigm — software that understands our goals, reasons, uses tools and gets work done on our behalf,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of Nvidia.
“This changes how we use computers, from operating applications to working with intelligent agents.”
Meta claims its Muse systems have achieved strong results in benchmark testing, while consumer downloads have climbed since their initial release.
“Muse is how we bring personal superintelligence to everyone. We’re excited to keep working with Nvidia to deliver the best personal agents and frontier models for billions of people,” said Mark Zuckerberg, founder and CEO of Meta.
However, the companies have not supplied specific download totals or independent comparisons that would establish how widely these models outperform competing products.
Meta’s multibillion-dollar fundraising supports its AI expansion
Nvidia’s investment comes as Meta prepares to raise substantial capital through share sales intended to finance its expanding artificial intelligence infrastructure.
Meta initially outlined a fundraising programme worth approximately $35 billion, comprising $22.5 billion in ordinary Class A shares and $12.5 billion in convertible depositary securities.
The company subsequently increased its ordinary share sale to $25 billion, with each Class A share offered at $625 and depositary securities priced at $50 per share.
Its broader fundraising plans could generate up to $95 billion through successive offerings, though the full amount is not guaranteed.
Nvidia’s proposed $3 billion contribution would make it a participant in Meta’s financing, linking its investment directly to a major customer’s infrastructure spending.
The companies have not disclosed how much additional Nvidia equipment Meta will purchase under the expanded partnership or when all planned deployments will occur.

articles.title: Webinar: How to Build AI Threat Readiness Into Your Security Operations
articles.text:
Security teams have spent years trying to detect threats faster. AI is changing the harder part: how much time defenders have left to act.
Advanced AI models can now help attackers discover vulnerabilities, generate exploit code, and move through weaknesses faster than traditional security processes were built to handle.
The challenge is no longer just finding another vulnerability or generating another alert. It is knowing which exposures matter, what an attacker can reach, and which issues need to be fixed first.
That is the focus of next week's webinar, How to Build AI Threat Readiness Across Your Security Operations, featuring an expert from Wiz. The session will show how security teams can improve visibility, prioritize real risk, and shorten the path from detection to remediation.
Most security teams already have plenty of data. They have vulnerability findings, cloud alerts, identity signals, application telemetry, and threat detections. The harder problem is connecting those signals quickly enough to answer the questions that drive action.
Is this vulnerability reachable? Does the exposed asset contain sensitive data? Can an attacker move from it to something more important? Who owns the affected system? What should be fixed first?
When those answers live across different tools and teams, investigations slow down. That delay matters more when attackers can automate parts of the discovery and exploitation process.
📅 Save Your Spot Today: Register for the Webinar Here.
The webinar focuses on two practical needs: broad visibility and faster action.
Security teams need enough context to understand risk across cloud infrastructure, code, identities, SaaS, AI services, and the software supply chain. They also need a way to identify exploitable paths, investigate suspicious activity, and deliver remediation to the right owner without having to rebuild the same context every time.
A Wiz expert will explain how organizations can use unified security context to separate urgent exposure from background noise, understand attack paths, and bring security agents into investigation and remediation workflows.
For SOC teams, that can mean less time spent manually assembling context. For vulnerability management, it means knowing which findings deserve immediate attention. For cloud and security engineering teams, it means connecting risk to the people and systems that can actually fix it.
The goal is not to automate every security decision. It is to remove delays caused by fragmented tools, repetitive investigation, and unclear ownership.
Attendees will leave with a framework for assessing whether their current security operations are ready for faster, AI-assisted attacks. The key questions are practical: Can you see enough of the environment to understand an attack path? Can you quickly determine whether a new issue affects something attackers can reach? Can you move a validated risk from detection to remediation fast enough?
AI is increasing the speed at which weaknesses can be found and used. Security teams need to respond with better context and less delay.

articles.title: Mapa descomunal, 210 GB de descarga y nueva policía: todo lo que se sabe de GTA 6
articles.text:
GTA 6 suma nuevas revelaciones a menos de un mes de su estreno. El mapa jugable combinará las extensiones de GTA 4, GTA 5 y Red Dead Redemption 2, el juego podría ocupar alrededor de 210 GB en PlayStation 5 y Rockstar Games prepara un sistema policial renovado con tácticas como bandas de clavos y perros.
A esto se sumaría un sistema meteorológico con consecuencias directas en la jugabilidad y hasta un filtro de gameplay oficial que terminó apareciendo en un episodio de South Park.
Con el lanzamiento fijado para el 19 de noviembre en PS5 y Xbox Series, la cantidad de información difundida en los últimos días permite anticipar varias de las mecánicas que definirán la experiencia en Vice City y el estado de Leonida.
El mapa de GTA 6: tamaño y comparación con otros juegos de Rockstar
La escala del mundo abierto es uno de los datos que más expectativa generó. Según la comparación ofrecida por Rockstar, la superficie jugable de GTA 6 equivaldría a combinar los mundos de GTA 4, GTA 5 y Red Dead Redemption 2 en un solo mapa.
Esa extensión no se limitará al exterior. El juego sumará muchos más interiores explorables respecto a entregas anteriores, lo que ampliaría las posibilidades de interacción dentro de edificios y espacios cerrados en Vice City.
El clima también tendrá un papel con consecuencias directas en la jugabilidad. Está previsto un sistema meteorológico que incluirá tormentas capaces de dificultar los vuelos y la navegación, un factor que obligaría a adaptar estrategias de desplazamiento según las condiciones del entorno.
A esto se suman los eventos emergentes filtrados, pensados para dar vida de forma dinámica tanto a Vice City como al resto del estado de Leonida, reforzando la sensación de un mundo en constante movimiento más allá de las misiones principales.
Peso de instalación: los 210 GB que preocupan en PS5
Otro de los datos más comentados tiene que ver con el almacenamiento necesario para instalar el juego. GTA 6 podría ocupar alrededor de 210 GB en PlayStation 5, una cifra que obligaría a buena parte de los jugadores a liberar espacio antes del estreno del 19 de noviembre de 2026.
El dato no fue confirmado ni por Rockstar Games ni por Take-Two Interactive. Procede de la cuenta PlayStation Size, que suele anticipar tamaños de instalación a partir de información disponible en la tienda digital de Sony.
El posible peso del juego pone otra vez el foco en el almacenamiento de las consolas de la generación actual. El lanzamiento será digital incluso para quienes compren una edición física en tiendas, ya que esas cajas incluirían un código de descarga y no un disco físico del juego.
Por ese motivo, contar con espacio libre suficiente se convierte en un requisito ineludible para poder instalar GTA 6 el día de su estreno, más allá del formato de compra elegido.
Nuevo sistema policial: bandas de clavos y perros contra los protagonistas
Entre las filtraciones recientes figura también el funcionamiento del renovado sistema policial de GTA 6. Las fuerzas de seguridad utilizarán tácticas como bandas de clavos y perros para detener a los protagonistas durante las persecuciones.
Esta mecánica se suma a los eventos emergentes del mapa y apunta a un comportamiento policial más elaborado que el visto en GTA 5, con recursos específicos pensados para frenar la huida de los jugadores en distintas situaciones de persecución.
Conducción más exigente: calles estrechas y mayor tráfico
Rockstar también introducirá cambios en el diseño vial de sus ciudades. GTA 6 tendrá carreteras más estrechas y tráfico más denso que GTA 5, según información compartida por Jason Schreier, periodista de Bloomberg, tras una conversación con Aaron Garbut, director artístico y codirector de Rockstar North.
La diferencia podría transformar la manera de recorrer Vice City. En GTA 5, las vías anchas permiten acelerar, cambiar de carril y adelantar con relativa facilidad. En la nueva entrega, los espacios reducidos y la mayor presencia de vehículos obligarían a calcular mejor cada maniobra.
Rockstar no detalló todavía cómo responderán los vehículos ni qué reglas seguirá la inteligencia artificial del tráfico. El efecto final sobre la conducción dependerá de la física de los coches, el comportamiento de los personajes controlados por el juego y la gestión de atascos y colisiones.
Gameplay filtrado en South Park
La aparición de gameplay oficial de GTA 6 en un episodio de South Park fue una de las novedades más comentadas. La escena, ambientada en una playa de Vice City, muestra al protagonista Jason interactuar con un personaje no jugable y su perro de una manera tan inesperada como escatológica.
En el fragmento, el dueño del animal recoge sus excrementos en una bolsa mientras camina por la playa. Jason se acerca, le arroja un objeto por la espalda y toma la bolsa para arrojársela al rostro, en una secuencia que destaca por el nivel de detalle de la animación.
Todavía no está claro si esta acción formará parte de las mecánicas generales disponibles en el juego completo o si corresponde a una situación específica diseñada para ese fragmento mostrado en la serie.
Por otra parte, la revista Edge tuvo acceso a 90 minutos de juego en las oficinas de Rockstar North y publicó 12 nuevas imágenes de GTA 6, material que se suma a las filtraciones sobre el mapa, el sistema policial y el clima difundidas en los últimos días.

articles.title: Windows 11 Pro Lifetime License Is Just $10 Through Nov 1
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
Windows 11 Pro Lifetime License Is Just $10 Through Nov 1
Microsoft Windows 11 Pro is available for $9.97 (MSRP $199) through Nov. 1, a saving of $189.03. The purchase provides a lifetime license for one PC, with no subscription or recurring fees. The license is non-transferable.
