articles.title: Elon Musk veut s'offrir tout un quartier à côté de ses data centers aux USA
articles.text:
D'immenses data centers sont installés par xAI (SpaceX) dans une localité du Mississippi. Un même endroit où Elon Musk veut dorénavant racheter plus de 400 habitations.
SpaceX est l'une des entreprises les plus importantes au monde dans le secteur de l'intelligence artificielle. Et elle le doit à l'absorption de xAI, qui bénéficie de plusieurs supercalculateurs gigantesques au niveau de Memphis, dans le Mississipi. Mais l'activité de ces derniers a tendance à incommoder le voisinage. Alors, du côté d'Elon Musk, on choisit une option radicale pour résoudre ce problème.
Elon Musk veut racheter les habitations à côté de ses data centers
Colonial Hill, c'est un quartier tranquille situé en bordure de Memphis qui n'aurait, dans des conditions normales, jamais vraiment fait parler de lui. Mais ces dernières années, les habitants de ce coin ont vu naître trois data centers gigantesques de SpaceX : Colossus 1, Colossu 2 et Macrohardrr. Autant d'installations qui sont alimentées par une centrale électrique installée à proximité.
Et cette activité ferait mal à l'environnement, avec notamment un bourdonnement continu qui s'entend dorénavant sur place. Les habitants ont donc commencé à se plaindre. Et selon The Guardian, afin de répondre à ces plaintes, Elon Musk a tout simplement décidé de racheter le quartier. Des agents immobiliers font ainsi actuellement du porte à porte dans le quartier, et proposent de racheter les maisons.
Une seule condition : ne pas se joindre à la plainte en cours
Un agent immobilier a ainsi déclaré que l'objectif était de racheter un ensemble de 418 maisons, avec 18 propriétaires qui auraient déjà dit oui à la proposition. Il faut dire que les locaux ont une véritable incitation à s'en aller, quand on lit les descriptions des nuisances sonores. « On dirait le bruit d'un moteur d'avion, mais c'est un bruit continu, c'est incroyablement fort » explique ainsi une résidente au Guardian, qui habite à un peu plus de trois kilomètres du complexe de xAI.
Mais si les habitants du quartier se disent qu'il vaut peut-être mieux finalement s'en aller, il faut aussi noter que le rachat de leur habitation est attaché à une condition. Ils ne doivent en effet pas se joindre à une plainte qui a été initiée par des voisins il y a quelques mois contre ces nuisances. Une façon simple pour Elon Musk de s'éviter des difficultés à l'avenir ?
Source : The Guardian

articles.title: Telegram Android Flaw Lets Attackers Run Code When Users Answer Voice Calls
articles.text:
A flaw in Telegram for Android could be chained with two other bugs to take full control of a victim's phone through a voice call, once the victim answered, according to security startup NebuSec.
The attacker needed only an ordinary Telegram account. Telegram fixed the flaw in version 12.10.4 of the app, released in late September, and NebuSec disclosed it on October 29.
Combined with an information-leak bug, the flaw gives the attacker an escape from the Telegram app to Android, NebuSec co-founder and chief executive Eten Zou told The Hacker News. Adding an Android root exploit then gives full control of the phone, including its messages, microphone and camera.
The flaw can be triggered in every version from 8.6.2 through 12.10.3, Zou said. Those versions came out between March 2022 and September 2026.
The company confirmed it in private voice calls on ARM64-based phones and has no evidence so far that it directly affects Telegram's iOS and desktop apps or group calls.
Anyone using Telegram for Android should make sure the app is on version 12.10.4 or later. The version number appears at the bottom of the app's Settings page. The flaw had no CVE identifier as of October 29.
The attack needs the victim to be called and to answer, Zou said, so setting Telegram's call privacy option to "Nobody" blocks it, and so does declining the call.
NebuSec has not seen the flaw used in real attacks, and believes no one else had realized it could be turned into remote code execution.
NebuSec reported the flaw to Telegram on September 26, after version 12.10.4 had shipped. Telegram acknowledged the report but did not believe the flaw could be turned into remote code execution, so no CVE was assigned and no bug bounty was paid, Zou said. The Hacker News has asked Telegram for comment.
During a Telegram call, the two apps send each other short messages to set up the call and report its state. One type, called MediaState, reports whether the microphone is muted, whether the camera is on, and how the video is rotated.
The flaw was in the code that reads MediaState messages. That code did not handle missing fields correctly and accessed memory it should not, according to NebuSec.
Telegram's published source code for version 12.10.3 contains a flaw that matches that description, a review by The Hacker News found. When a MediaState message included a rotation value, the code checked that value. It then read a different field, the video state, even if the message had no such field.
Version 12.10.4 reads the rotation value from the right field. The calling code that uses this message was switched on in version 8.6.2, the first version NebuSec names.
Telegram's Android, iOS, and desktop apps use one shared library, called tgcalls, for calls. A change labeled "Fix camera rotation" made the same correction in tgcalls on April 21, 2026.
Telegram's iOS source code included that change from version 12.7, released in May, and the desktop app's code from version 7.0.1, released in July. Telegram for Android received it in version 12.10.4 in September.
Whether the earlier code could be exploited in those apps has not been shown.
NebuSec's video shows two phones, one marked as the attacker and one as the victim. The victim accepts a Telegram call. About half a minute into the call, the victim's phone switches to its home screen, the app icons fall down the screen, and a "HACKED BY NEBUSEC" logo appears.
The video does not show which Telegram or Android version the victim's phone was running. No technical write-up of the flaw was on NebuSec's website as of October 29, so the attack chain, including the two other bugs, depends on the video and on what the company says.
NebuSec, a startup backed by Y Combinator, says its Code Security product, which runs on OpenAI's GPT-5.4 model, found the flaw. In July, the company described an Android exploit chain that started with a Firefox flaw and reached the kernel of an ARM64 device running Android 17.
Separately, the Zero Day Initiative (ZDI) published an advisory on October 15 about an unpatched flaw in rlottie, the library Telegram apps have used to draw animated stickers. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-111105 (CVSS score: 7.0), can let an attacker run code if a user opens a malicious file or page, ZDI said.
Telegram had told ZDI in March that checks on its servers mitigated the flaw, and in April asked ZDI for a full remote code execution chain.
Those checks could be bypassed, researcher Saifeldeen Aziz says in the abstract for his OffensiveCon talk in Tokyo. The research used AI-guided fuzzing, which feeds code with large amounts of broken or unexpected input, to find memory-corruption bugs in rlottie across Telegram's iOS, Android, and desktop apps. It then chained those bugs with flaws in how stickers are delivered and checked to run code on Telegram for iOS.
The Android app replaced rlottie with tlottie, a library written in Rust, between versions 12.8.1 in June and 12.10.0 in August, according to Telegram's published source code. The desktop app's code made the same switch in September, and the iOS code added tlottie in version 13.0 in October while still including rlottie.
(This article has been updated with answers from NebuSec chief executive Eten Zou on the attack chain, how users can block the attack, and how Telegram responded to NebuSec's report. The opening now says the flaw was chained with two other bugs. A sentence describing the sticker research has also been corrected.)

articles.title: Uber, Amazon e Instacart demandaron a Nueva York para frenar la ley que limita despedir repartidores
articles.text:
Uber, Amazon e Instacart presentaron una demanda federal contra la ciudad de Nueva York para bloquear una ley que prohíbe a las plataformas de reparto desactivar a un repartidor sin una causa justificada o una razón económica real. La norma entra en vigor en enero, según Bloomberg Law.
La demanda se presentó el 28 de octubre de 2026 en el tribunal federal del Distrito Sur de Nueva York, en Manhattan, con el número 1:26-cv-09455. El texto tiene 94 páginas y siete cargos, según Courthouse News Service. Los representan los estudios Sidley Austin y Gibson Dunn & Crutcher.
Las empresas sostienen que la ley viola la Primera y la Decimocuarta Enmienda de la Constitución de Estados Unidos, que protegen la libertad de expresión y el debido proceso, además de la cláusula de contratos. Argumentan que la ciudad reescribe los acuerdos que ya tienen con los repartidores.
En la demanda, las compañías afirman que las desactivaciones son “relativamente raras” y que casi siempre se vinculan con seguridad o fraude. Según su texto, la ley las obligaría a reabrir casos de repartidores que fueron dados de baja por esas razones.
Qué exige la ley y por qué la rechazan
La Ley Local 34 impide que un servicio de reparto desactive a un trabajador contratado salvo que demuestre una causa justificada, como una falta de conducta, o un motivo económico genuino. Obliga a avisar al repartidor antes de la baja, según PYMNTS.
Según Reuters, citada por PYMNTS, la demanda también cuestiona que algunas obligaciones alcancen decisiones de desactivación tomadas desde 2021. Las empresas planean pedir una medida cautelar, una orden judicial que suspenda la ley mientras avanza el caso.
Instacart publicó el 28 de octubre un texto con su postura. Dice que la ley demorará la eliminación de cuentas que representen riesgos de seguridad y que podría obligarla a divulgar información sensible sobre cómo detecta el fraude.
La empresa afirmó que la norma “hará más difícil” aplicar estándares contra conductas inseguras, acoso, robo y fraude. Sostuvo que envió más de 50 preguntas al Departamento de Protección del Consumidor y el Trabajador de la ciudad y que no recibió respuesta.
Instacart aseguró que, con o sin la ley, sus compradores reciben una explicación del motivo de la baja, una vía de apelación y una revisión humana de la decisión final.
El antecedente de Uber y Lyft
Las compañías comparan la ley con la Ley Local 52, que regula las desactivaciones de conductores de Uber y Lyft. El 21 de julio, el juez federal Gregory Woods la bloqueó con una medida cautelar y escribió que beneficia a una parte pequeña de los conductores, según Reuters.
Woods consideró que Uber y Lyft probablemente demostrarían que la ley afecta gravemente sus contratos. Esa norma debía entrar en vigor el 28 de julio. El fallo no la anuló de forma definitiva: el litigio sigue abierto.
Instacart describe la Ley Local 34 como “sustancialmente similar” a la Ley Local 52. Los representantes de la ciudad no respondieron de inmediato a la consulta de Courthouse News Service sobre la demanda.
DoorDash compra Instacart por USD 17.000 millones
DoorDash anunció la compra de Instacart por USD 17.000 millones, en una operación aprobada por ambos directorios que busca reforzar su posición frente a Walmart y Amazon en el delivery de supermercados en Estados Unidos.
La oferta, de USD 65 por acción, implica una prima del 26% y se financiará principalmente con efectivo, aunque los accionistas podrán elegir acciones o una combinación. La fusión sumará la red tecnológica y logística de DoorDash a las casi 100.000 tiendas de Instacart.
La compañía combinada ofrecerá 50.000 comercios adicionales, mientras Instacart cerrará Caper Cart en 2027, con costos estimados de hasta USD 80 millones.

articles.title: Hitscan Hyperlight X Launches: 35-37 g Wireless Gaming Mouse with SPDT Switches and Updated Internals
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
Hitscan Hyperlight X Launches: 35-37 g Wireless Gaming Mouse with SPDT Switches and Updated Internals
Hitscan has announced an update to its Hyperlight wireless gaming mouse from 2024, both reducing the weight of the symmetrical mouse and updating its internals in the name of faster clicks and lower response times. The Hitscan Hyperlight X will use the same shape as the original Hyperlight, but the Hyperlight X will allegedly weigh in at 35-37 g, depending on whether you're using full-size or dot skates. While Hitscan itself hasn't shared all that much about the new mouse, aside from its October 28 launch date, @jakeufps on X shared some information about the new hardware. 
[Editor's note: Our in-depth review of the original Hitscan Hyperlight is live]
While the Hyperlight X will allegedly have the same shape, it will feature new SPDT switches—nominally closed mechanical switches that send a click when the circuit is opened, effectively reducing the actuation distance and click latency substantially. The Hyperlight X will also launch with the PixArt PAW 3950 sensor, an update from the prior 3395, and a Nordic nRF54L15 MCU. It will also ship with an 8K receiver, enabling 8 kHz polling from the factory instead of requiring an additional accessory purchase. 
Update Oct 29th: Hitscan has updated the product page of the Hitscan X with official $109.99 pricing and a proper spec sheet.The Hyperlight X will also feature a 200 mAh battery, which is 50 mAh smaller than the outgoing Hyperlight, and it will be fully customizable in both a web driver and an optional downloadable app. 
The rest of the secret sauce all apparently lies in software and firmware optimizations, with the aforementioned reviewer citing "heavily optimized firmware," with further comments highlighting an implementation fixes made by XBAB Tech to essentially eliminate DPI downshift and smoothing.
Source:
				Hitscan on X			
	
	
	
		
	
		
2 Comments on Hitscan Hyperlight X Launches: 35-37 g Wireless Gaming Mouse with SPDT Switches and Updated Internals
COM (Common): The movable contact that switches between the other two terminals.
NC (Normally Closed): Connected to COM when the switch is not pressed.
NO (Normally Open): Connected to COM when the switch is pressed.
So the mouse can detect a click, when the switch is no longer connected to NC and before it is connected to NO.
This allegedly reduces latency, but can also, depending on switch design, firmware and wear, produce more double clicks.

articles.title: The Rise of the Threat Operator: How AI Will Redefine Security Operations and Careers
articles.text:
AI is beginning to take over much of the work that has traditionally defined the security analyst's job. Investigating alerts, collecting evidence, correlating activity across tools, and executing response actions are becoming tasks that AI systems can perform on their own. As these capabilities mature, security operations centers (SOCs) will see major changes in how work is organized, how decisions are made, and what is expected of the people responsible for defending organizations.
For security professionals, this is a chance to take on a much broader role. As AI assumes more of the operational workload, analysts can move beyond individual alerts and investigations to direct the defense across the entire security lifecycle. We call this emerging role the Threat Operator: an AI-native security professional who translates business risk into defensive priorities, directs AI-driven operations, and exercises judgment over the decisions and actions taken by those systems.
The impact reaches beyond day-to-day SOC work. It will change the skills organizations need, how security professionals develop expertise, and the career paths open to people entering the field.
From Individual Tasks to Overall Defense
The traditional SOC developed around specialized functions, each supported by its own tools and workflows. Threat intelligence teams study adversaries, detection engineers create rules, threat hunters search for activity that existing controls may have missed, analysts investigate alerts, and incident responders contain confirmed threats. These functions are closely related, yet the work often moves between teams through separate systems, tickets, and manual handoffs. AI is starting to tie these activities together. For example, intelligence about a new threat can lead to a hunting hypothesis, which can reveal a detection gap and produce a new detection. That detection may identify suspicious activity requiring investigation, followed by containment and further improvements to the organization's defenses. AI agents can coordinate and execute these workflows, carrying context and findings from one stage to the next.
That changes where security professionals add the most value. A Threat Operator works across the defensive lifecycle, setting priorities based on the organization's exposure, business operations, and threat landscape. They determine which risks deserve attention, what the defense should accomplish, how much autonomy AI should have, and when a decision requires human intervention. They are also responsible for judging whether the operation is actually improving security.
Consider a financial institution facing a newly identified threat targeting identity infrastructure. AI agents could assess the institution's exposure, hunt for relevant activity, identify gaps in existing detections, and recommend defensive actions. The Threat Operator would provide the institutional context needed to guide that work, including which systems support critical business processes, what constitutes unacceptable risk, and which actions require authorization.
The result is a gradual shift from human-in-the-loop to human-on-the-loop, with security professionals supervising and governing AI-driven operations. The level of autonomy will depend on the maturity of the technology, the consequences of particular actions, and the organization's tolerance for risk, but a human remains accountable throughout.
Rethinking How Security Professionals Gain Experience
Junior security analysts will feel some of the biggest effects. For decades, the SOC has provided an entry point into cybersecurity, with analysts developing their skills through alert triage, evidence collection, investigations, documentation, and escalation. Although much of this work is repetitive, it has also served as an apprenticeship. Over time, analysts learn how systems behave, how attackers operate, and how experienced practitioners distinguish genuine threats from benign activity. As AI absorbs more of these responsibilities, organizations will need to rethink how that experience is acquired. The traditional progression from handling simple alerts to managing complex investigations may become less relevant as AI takes on more sophisticated work. Without a deliberate approach to training, security teams may struggle to develop the experienced professionals they will need in the future.
AI can also open up a different path for professional development. Junior Threat Operators can gain supervised exposure to a much wider range of security activities, examining how intelligence informs hunting, how detections are developed, how investigations reach conclusions, and how response decisions affect the business. They can review the evidence behind AI-generated findings, challenge assumptions, identify missing context, and learn from the decisions made by more experienced colleagues. This only works if organizations invest in technical fundamentals and structured mentorship. Analysts still need to understand networks, operating systems, attacker techniques, and the security technologies underlying AI-driven workflows. Experienced practitioners will need to teach younger colleagues how to evaluate conclusions, recognize uncertainty, and exercise judgment when the available evidence is incomplete.
The Skills Needed
For the current generation of security analysts, technical proficiency has often been measured through familiarity with security tools and the ability to extract useful information from them. Query languages, detection logic, endpoint telemetry, and investigation techniques have been central to the profession. Those skills still matter. AI adds new demands on top of them: orchestration, governance, and interpreting automated decisions.
Threat Operators will need to translate business security risks into clear defensive objectives that AI systems can execute. They must understand the organization's architecture, critical assets, operational dependencies, and relevant adversaries, and know how to communicate that context to AI agents. Their work will involve evaluating hypotheses, validating evidence, setting escalation criteria, and determining whether an automated action has achieved its intended outcome.
For example, an AI system investigating a compromised server may recommend immediate isolation. That call could be technically sound. But the server may support a critical business process where disruption carries significant consequences. A Threat Operator must understand those dependencies and determine how the response should proceed, balancing containment requirements with operational risk. This need for defined oversight and accountability is also reflected in the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.
The role will combine four areas of expertise:
- Business security risk: Understanding organizational priorities, critical assets, and the consequences of security decisions.
- Threat and adversary understanding: Interpreting intelligence and anticipating how attackers may target the environment.
- Defensive operations: Understanding detection, hunting, investigation, and response across the security lifecycle.
- AI orchestration and judgment: Directing AI workflows, evaluating their conclusions, and governing automated actions.
Building a Career Path Around Defensive Outcomes
The Threat Operator role should become a career path with increasing levels of responsibility. Early-career operators can focus on validating evidence, reviewing AI conclusions, adding environmental context, and understanding how decisions connect across the defensive lifecycle. As they gain experience, they can begin translating business risks into defensive objectives, directing agent workflows, identifying coverage gaps, and determining when operations should escalate or act.
Senior Threat Operators will take responsibility for defining autonomy boundaries, governing consequential actions, evaluating the reliability of AI-driven decisions, and measuring whether security operations are reducing organizational risk. Professionals may enter this career path from investigations, threat intelligence, detection engineering, incident response, security architecture, or risk management, bringing different areas of expertise to a role that spans the entire defensive operation.
Security leaders should start building the training, governance, and progression frameworks needed to support these responsibilities. That includes establishing which decisions require human approval, how operators validate AI-generated evidence, how autonomy expands as systems demonstrate reliability, and how individual performance is evaluated. Measures such as the quality of defensive decisions, the closure of detection gaps, and improvements in threat coverage will matter more alongside traditional operational metrics.
This will happen at different speeds in different organizations. Security professionals will have more say in how their organizations defend themselves. The old SOC trained people to operate tools. The AI-native SOC has to train them to operate the defense.

Learn more about how Conifers helps security teams direct and govern AI-driven defense across the full SOC lifecycle.

articles.title: Infobae, Clarín y La Nación ya usan IA en sus redacciones: ninguno deja que la máquina decida qué se publica
articles.text:
El jueves 29 de octubre, tres de los principales medios argentinos discutieron en Media Party Buenos Aires cómo se incorpora la inteligencia artificial a una redacción sin perder la identidad del medio.
Participaron el director de Estrategia de IA y Operaciones Editoriales Regionales de Infobae Opy Morales, el director digital de Clarín Javier Kraviez y el secretario de Redacción de La Nación Gastón Roitberg. Moderó Guadalupe López, de Chequeado.
La primera barrera fue el miedo. “¿Esto me va a sacar el trabajo?” es, según Kraviez, la pregunta que aparece primero cuando llega una tecnología así. Clarín respondió con una capacitación de meses, no de días, junto a una consultora externa y su área de Big Data. No terminó.
En La Nación, el camino fue otro. No hay un departamento de IA sino un equipo con gente de distintas especialidades que trabaja con todas las áreas de la redacción.
El diario publicó su guía de uso interna para que otros medios la adapten. Para Roitberg, la etapa de adopción ya pasó: el desafío ahora es supervisar y auditar lo que hace la IA.
Infobae dejó de escribir manuales de IA
En Infobae, la IA está integrada a todo el proceso a través de ScribNews, la plataforma que el medio desarrolló hace tres años y que usan los periodistas de sus cinco redacciones, con el manual de estilo incorporado. Cada redactor elige qué herramienta usar en cada parte del trabajo.
En una noticia de último momento, el primer paso y el último botón antes de publicar son del periodista.
Hace un año, Morales decidió eliminar los manuales: un PDF, explicó, queda obsoleto en el momento en que se termina. En su lugar, la plataforma tiene un asistente que conoce todas sus funciones. Cada capacitación se graba y se carga en ese asistente, que los periodistas consultan cuantas veces quieran.
Los periodistas jóvenes trabajan tres meses sin IA antes de recibir acceso. “La IA no elige, siempre te da opciones”, dijo Morales. A su juicio, el problema más grande no es la tecnología sino el criterio, que hay que seguir formando.
Los tres coinciden en dónde está el valor del periodismo
Para Kraviez, la cuenta del negocio es simple: el suscriptor paga cuando encuentra algo relevante para su vida en una fuente en la que confía. La IA abarata la producción de contenidos, dijo, pero la relevancia y la confianza se construyen. Roitberg fue por el mismo lado: “Volumen y velocidad no implica calidad”.
Morales anticipó dónde va a crecer el uso de la IA: en el trabajo que se hace sobre información que ya está publicada en la web. Aun ahí, aclaró, el proceso termina con una persona que valida.
Lo que la máquina no puede hacer es salir a buscar la noticia. “La IA está llena de datos, de información, pero no tiene fuentes”, resumió Morales.
Kraviez advirtió que no se puede dejar la agenda pública en manos de un algoritmo. Roitberg propuso empezar cada proyecto por el problema que se quiere resolver, y no por la herramienta.
El panel fue parte de la XIV edición de Media Party, la conferencia internacional de periodismo y tecnología que se realiza del 29 al 31 de octubre en la Ciudad Cultural Konex de Buenos Aires. Su patrocinador principal es Google News Initiative, el programa de Google para medios.
La edición anterior convocó a más de 2.000 emprendedores, periodistas, programadores, diseñadores, tecnólogos y académicos de 30 países.
Entre los oradores de este año figuran el director de IA de Guardian News & Media, la empresa que edita The Guardian, Caspar Llewellyn Smith; la editora ejecutiva del Pulitzer Center Marina Walker Guevara, una de las responsables de la investigación de los Panama Papers, y la editora en jefe del diario ucraniano Ukrainska Pravda Sevgil Musaieva.

articles.title: Xbox Console Sales Fall 14% as Microsoft Points to Supply Shortages
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
Xbox Console Sales Fall 14% as Microsoft Points to Supply Shortages
Microsoft's gaming business shrank again in the first quarter of its 2027 fiscal year, which ended on September 30. Xbox revenue came in at $5.38 billion, down 2% from $5.51 billion a year ago, while Microsoft as a whole grew revenue by 19% to $92.3 billion. Content and services revenue fell 2%, and hardware dropped a bigger 14% on a lower volume of consoles sold. CFO Amy Hood said the overall Xbox decline was driven by third-party content and Xbox Game Pass, partly offset by growth in first-party games.
Microsoft Gaming CEO Asha Sharma, however, put a positive spin on the numbers in a post on X. She pointed out that the 2% decline is much smaller than the 10% drop a quarter earlier, and that margins improved. She also listed record results for Minecraft and World of Warcraft Forever, called Modern Warfare 4 Call of Duty's most acclaimed release in over a decade, and said PC platform revenue grew by double digits. As for hardware, Sharma claims console sales are being held back by supply, with demand currently outpacing the number of consoles available. She added that Xbox is working to get more units out to players, partly through an expanded refurbishment program.That supply argument is interesting, since Microsoft announced another round of console price hikes in June, which pushed the 1 TB Series X to $799.99 on August 1. US Xbox hardware unit sales then hit an all-time low through August, according to Circana. The refurbishment plan also seems to tie into Microsoft emailing inactive Xbox owners earlier this month, nudging them to trade their consoles in at Best Buy for up to $375, with traded-in units set to be resold at lower prices. Microsoft expects content and services to grow by mid-to-high single digits next quarter, while hardware is expected to decline again.

articles.title: 26,400 Valid Cloud and AI Credentials Found Exposed in Public Gitee Repositories
articles.text:
26,400 credentials that developers left in public code on Gitee, a Chinese code-hosting service, still worked when a researcher tested them. Anyone who copied one from that code could have used it.
Independent researcher Ben Zimmermann found them by scanning 7.25 million public Gitee repositories and reported the results on October 28. Most were keys for cloud and AI services, led by 9,473 Alibaba Cloud AccessKey pairs.
Zimmermann sent the vendors with the most exposed keys a list of their credentials, but he did not contact the developers who leaked them. When he published, he had not confirmed that any of the reported credentials had been revoked. So anyone who has pushed a key to a public Gitee repository cannot assume it has been revoked.
The scan ran for about a month, but Zimmermann did not provide the dates, so it is unclear how long ago the credentials were tested. He also did not say whether anyone else had used them.
He ran two secret scanners, TruffleHog and Kingfisher, over every repository. Both tried each credential against the service that issued it and kept only those that worked, he wrote.
The scanners read each repository's full commit history. A key that a developer later removed from the code could still be found and counted there.
The 26,400 figure counts each credential once, regardless of how many repositories it appeared in. By commit date, 12,242 of the credentials came from 2025, nearly half the total. Some dated to the late 2000s.
What Was Exposed
After the Alibaba Cloud keys, the largest groups were 3,805 YouTube API keys, 3,170 DeepSeek keys, 1,489 keys for Zhipu's BigModel AI platform, and 1,348 OpenAI keys. Smaller numbers were found for GitHub, AWS, Google Cloud and Google's Gemini.
One of the credentials was "an active organization-admin credential for a major enterprise AI platform," Zimmermann wrote. He did not name the platform or say what the credential could reach.
What a working key lets someone do depends on the service. OpenAI says that a compromised key allows another person to use the account's quota without the owner's consent. That can cause "data loss, unexpected charges," a used-up monthly quota, and interrupted API access.
A YouTube API key is a Google Cloud API key that identifies a project, Google says. Without API restrictions, such a key can be used with every API that accepts Google Cloud keys.
What to Do If You Committed Keys
Treat any key that has ever been in a public Gitee repository as exposed, and revoke it at the provider. Deleting a key from the code or rewriting the repository's history does not revoke it, as noted by TruffleHog's maker, Truffle Security.
- Alibaba Cloud: create a new AccessKey pair, switch your apps to it, then disable and delete the old pair. Check for unexpected charges and for resources created or deleted that you did not need, Alibaba Cloud's leak response plan says. ActionTrail shows the key's API calls for the last 90 days, but data operations in services such as OSS and SLS have to be checked in each service's own logs.
- Google and YouTube API keys: rotate the key, which creates a new key with the same restrictions, update your apps to use it, then delete the old key. Add API restrictions so the key works only with the APIs you need.
- OpenAI: rotate the key immediately from the API Keys page, as OpenAI advises, and set spend limits to help limit charges from a leaked key.
Two Scanners, Different Results
MongoDB makes Kingfisher, and Zimmermann's post was developed with its Kingfisher team.
In this scan, TruffleHog found 12,737 credentials that worked, and Kingfisher found 14,664, but only 1,001 were found by both. Each tool alone found about half of the total.
TruffleHog found almost all of the Alibaba Cloud keys. Kingfisher found all 1,489 BigModel keys, because TruffleHog has no detector for Zhipu's keys, Zimmermann wrote.
Teams that rely on a single scanner should verify its detectors against the services they use.
Gitee and Other Code Hosts
China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology chose Gitee in 2020 as the base for a national open-source code-hosting platform.
Gitee's public API is limited, and a 2021 attempt to study leaked credentials on the site gave up because of it.
Gitee's rate, 3.64 working credentials per 1,000 repositories scanned, is higher than the rates from earlier scans of GitLab (3.11) and Bitbucket (2.39). Those scans used only TruffleHog, Zimmermann wrote.
Based on TruffleHog's results alone, Gitee's rate is 1.76, but that count excludes services TruffleHog does not cover, such as Zhipu. So neither figure shows which platform leaks more.

articles.title: Las acciones de Intel cayeron cerca de 20% tras pronosticar ventas inferiores por la crisis de las PC
articles.text:
Las acciones de Intel cayeron entre 18% y más de 20% en las operaciones posteriores al cierre del jueves 29 de octubre de 2026, después de que la empresa pronosticara para el cuarto trimestre ingresos y ganancias inferiores a lo esperado, según Reuters. La compañía citó la debilidad del mercado de PC y una explosión en una fábrica de Israel.
Intel prevé ingresos de entre USD 15.000 y 16.000 millones en el cuarto trimestre. Los analistas consultados por LSEG esperaban USD 17.070 millones. La ganancia ajustada proyectada es de 25 centavos por acción, frente a los 43 centavos que anticipaba el mercado.
La cotización cerró la jornada regular en USD 92,07 y bajó a USD 75,88 en la sesión posterior, según Yahoo Finance. Es el nivel más bajo desde abril, según eThe Oregonian. Las acciones de Intel habían subido más de 100% en lo que va de 2026.
El tercer trimestre, terminado el 26 de septiembre, dejó ingresos de USD 16.510 millones, un 21% más que un año antes y en línea con lo previsto. La ganancia ajustada fue de 52 centavos por acción, por encima de los 40 centavos estimados.
Los chips para PC cayeron mientras los de centros de datos crecieron
Las ventas de la división de chips para computadoras bajaron 5%, a USD 8.100 millones, y quedaron por debajo de los USD 8.980 millones que esperaba el mercado. El negocio de centros de datos e IA, en cambio, subió 78%, a USD 7.300 millones, según CNBC.
El director financiero, David Zinsner, dijo: “Vemos que la desaceleración de las PC continuará al menos durante la primera mitad del próximo año”. Intel proyecta, según Quartz, que el mercado de PC caerá 12% en 2026 y otro 10% en 2027.
El director ejecutivo, Lip-Bu Tan, atribuyó parte del problema al precio de la memoria. “Los precios de la memoria subieron mucho. Mi predicción es que en 2027 será un problema muy grave para todos”, dijo a Bloomberg, según Quartz. La empresa tenía previsto subir 10% los precios de sus procesadores para PC en octubre.
La explosión en Israel costará USD 600 millones en ventas
Zinsner dijo a Reuters que la explosión de octubre en la planta de Kiryat Gat, en Israel, restará unos USD 300 millones a los ingresos del cuarto trimestre y unos 200 puntos básicos al margen bruto. Se espera un efecto similar en el primer trimestre, unos USD 600 millones en total. CNBC indicó que el accidente mató a dos trabajadores e hirió de gravedad a un tercero.
La fábrica estuvo parada dos semanas y fabrica sobre todo chips para centros de datos. Intel aún evalúa cuántas obleas, los discos de silicio donde se fabrican los chips, se pueden aprovechar. Zinsner indicó que la producción empezaría a recuperarse hacia el fin de esa semana.
Tan reconoció a Bloomberg, según Quartz, que no pueden cumplir con los pedidos de los clientes. La empresa dice que no logra producir suficientes procesadores Xeon, los de servidores, para una demanda que superó sus cálculos. The Oregonian advirtió que eso la expone a perder mercado frente a rivales.
Intel eleva su previsión de capital para 2026
Intel elevó a USD 20.000 millones su previsión de inversión de capital para 2026, desde los USD 18.000 millones de julio, y dijo que en 2027 el gasto aumentará de forma considerable. En agosto había reunido USD 23.000 millones con una oferta de acciones.
La caída arrastró a otras empresas en la sesión posterior: AMD bajó 4% y Broadcom 2%, según Reuters.
Un analista de Rosenblatt Securities atribuyó el movimiento al “contagio” del ánimo negativo, y Reuters recordó que esos movimientos suelen exagerarse fuera del horario regular. AMD presentará resultados la próxima semana y Nvidia lo hará a mediados de noviembre, según CNBC.

articles.title: Google et XREAL lancent les AURA : des lunettes XR avec Gemini, et une mauvaise nouvelle pour la France
articles.text:
Google et XREAL ouvrent les commandes des AURA, premières lunettes XR filaires sous Android XR, avec Gemini intégré. Prix de lancement : 1 099 dollars jusqu’à fin décembre, aux États-Unis, au Canada et en Corée du Sud. L’Europe reste pour l’instant sans prix ni date.
Les lunettes XR filaires sous Android XR quittent enfin le stade de la démo : les AURA sont commandables depuis le 28 octobre, avec Gemini pour assistant et un boîtier de calcul déporté relié par câble. Le catalogue annonce plus de 150 applications conçues pour la XR, en plus des applications Android classiques de Google Play, mais la disponibilité géographique ferme la porte à la France, du moins pour l’instant.
Moins de 95 grammes, mais un boîtier à garder sur soi
Selon Google, les lunettes pèsent moins de 95 grammes parce que le calcul se fait dans un boîtier de poche relié par câble. Celui-ci contient la batterie et la puce Snapdragon Reality Elite de Qualcomm, qui fait ses débuts avec les AURA. Les verres sont transparents, avec un champ de vision de 70 degrés : vous voyez votre environnement à travers, avec les fenêtres d’applications qui flottent dans l'espace.
Ce boîtier pèse tout de même 265 grammes, Il peut aussi servir de trackpad, et on peut y associer un clavier et une souris Bluetooth. Les lunettes reprennent par ailleurs trois caméras : deux latérales pour le suivi des mains, une centrale pour les photos et vidéos.
Lors de notre prise en main en septembre à l'IFA, nous avions vraiment apprécié ce premier contact avec les Xreal Aura.
Un écran de portable en mode Wired Mirroring, et Gemini qui surligne
Le mode Wired Mirroring affiche l’écran d’un ordinateur portable dans une fenêtre redimensionnable, via un câble USB-C compatible sortie vidéo. Aucun logiciel à installer, et l’affichage n’est visible que par le porteur : un document confidentiel dans un train ou un hôtel reste hors de vue des voisins. Les jeux d’une console portable ou d’un PC passent par la même voie.
Gemini peut analyser ce que vous regardez, dans la pièce comme sur vos écrans virtuels. Nouveauté du jour : en partageant sa vue, on peut lui demander de surligner l’élément sur lequel se concentrer, dans la pièce ou à l’écran. Côté divertissement, les verres peuvent être assombris pour isoler du décor et redeviennent transparents quand quelqu’un entre dans le champ.
1 099 dollars en promo, 1 279 ensuite, et l’Europe en rade
Le tarif de 1 099 dollars concerne le modèle de base (12 Go de RAM, 256 Go de stockage) jusqu’à la fin de l’année, Il devrait ensuite repasser à 1 279 dollars. De son coté, la version 16 Go et 512 Go est à 1 299 dollars au lieu de 1 499 jusqu’au 31 décembre.
L’Europe, elle, doit se contenter d’un « Founder Priority Pass » à 299 euros, un acompte sans prix final connu… XREAL évoquait une arrivée « peu après » dans les 27 pays de l’Union, France comprise, mais ni Google ni XREAL n’ont donné de date ou de prix pour le vieux continent.

articles.title: “Los fondos de los usuarios están seguros”: cofundador de Binance ante posible hackeo que congeló más de USD 3 mil millones
articles.text:
Changpeng Zhao, cofundador de Binance, afirmó que la mayor plataforma de intercambio de criptomonedas del mundo podría haber sufrido un ataque informático, aunque aseguró que los fondos de los usuarios permanecen protegidos. La alerta derivó en la congelación de más de 3.000 millones de dólares en activos por parte de los dos principales emisores de stablecoins.
“¡Los fondos de los usuarios están seguros! Sí parece un hackeo en Binance”, escribió Zhao en una publicación. El empresario agregó que ya no gestiona la plataforma Binance.com, pero que, en su calidad de accionista, espera que todos los fondos de los usuarios queden completamente cubiertos.
Tether y Circle congelaron sus activos en el exchange
Ante los informes sobre la posible vulnerabilidad, Tether y Circle Internet Group, los dos principales emisores de stablecoins, anunciaron de forma independiente el bloqueo de sus activos vinculados a Binance.
Paolo Ardoino, director ejecutivo de Tether, declaró en una publicación en la red social X que la empresa congeló más de 1.500 millones de dólares en stablecoins “debido a un posible ataque informático al exchange Binance”. Zhao precisó esa cifra en aproximadamente 971 millones de dólares en su propio mensaje.
Por su parte, Jeremy Allaire, director de Circle Internet Group Inc. (CRCL), confirmó la congelación de 800 millones de dólares de su criptomoneda ante “informes de una posible vulnerabilidad que involucra a Binance”. Zhao situó este monto en unos 823 millones de dólares.
El monto total congelado supera los 3.000 millones de dólares
Binance difundió una actualización en la que cuantificó el alcance de la medida.
“Binance ha confirmado un incidente de seguridad y los equipos están trabajando sin descanso para resolverlo. Los fondos de los usuarios permanecen seguros. Como medida de precaución, todos los depósitos y retiros están suspendidos temporalmente mientras los equipos de seguridad realizan verificaciones, aseguran la infraestructura de wallets y rastrean los activos afectados, con el estrecho apoyo de las fuerzas del orden y socios de la industria”, indicó.
“Los usuarios no asumirán el impacto financiero de este incidente. Binance cubrirá todas las pérdidas”, agrega el comunicado.
“Agradecemos a los socios que han actuado con rapidez para apoyar estos esfuerzos. Para mayor claridad, el total actual verificado de activos congelados es de US$3.000 millones. Esta cifra se actualizará a medida que se verifique más información. Solo compartiremos información confirmada y proporcionaremos nuevas actualizaciones a través de los canales oficiales de Binance”, finaliza la actualización.
Zhao, por su parte, agradeció en su mensaje “el congelamiento rápido” por parte de ambos emisores de stablecoins, en lo que describió como una respuesta coordinada ante la eventual brecha de seguridad en el exchange.
El último lanzamiento de Binance
Diez días antes de este incidente, Binance había lanzado Binance AI Pro, un agente de inteligencia artificial especializado en finanzas que convierte ideas de trading en estrategias automatizadas a través de una conversación en lenguaje cotidiano. La herramienta está disponible para los usuarios en el sitio web y la aplicación de Binance, sin necesidad de un registro por separado.
El sistema presenta cada estrategia como un flujo de trabajo visual, denominado Strategy Canvas, que permite inspeccionar y ajustar cada paso, y antes de cualquier operación real puede probarse mediante trading simulado con fondos virtuales.
El paso a operaciones reales requiere una revisión y aprobación por parte del usuario, y se ejecuta en una AI Strategy Account, una subcuenta virtual aislada de la cuenta principal que solo el propietario puede fondear mediante transferencia manual.
El agente no tiene capacidad para mover fondos por su cuenta, y las estrategias pueden pausarse, ajustarse o revocarse en cualquier momento. Binance AI Pro combina un modelo de lenguaje de gran tamaño con un entorno de agente específico para finanzas desarrollado por la compañía, que se nutre de datos de mercado propios y de fuentes de terceros seleccionadas.

articles.title: Cisco Patches Actively Exploited ASA and FTD VPN Flaw That Can Crash Firewalls
articles.text:
Cisco has released patches to address a high-severity security flaw in Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software that it said has been exploited in the wild.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-76418, is rated 8.6 on the CVSS scoring system. Successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.
According to Cisco, the issue is rooted in the Remote Access SSL VPN service of ASA and FTD software.
"This vulnerability is due to logic errors when secondary authentication is configured on a tunnel group," it said in a Wednesday advisory. "An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted request when connecting to the SSL remote access VPN. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the affected device to reload, resulting in a DoS condition."
The network equipment major said it became aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability in October 2026, but did not share any specifics as to when the attacks began, who is behind them, and the scale of the efforts.
Fixes for the flaw are available in the following versions -
- 
    Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software Release
    
  - 9.16 and earlier - Fixed in 9.16.4.104
  - 9.18 - Fixed in 9.18.4.96
  - 9.20 - Fixed in 9.20.4.50
  - 9.22 - Fixed in 9.22.3.200
  - 9.23 - Fixed in 9.23.1.48
  - 9.24 - Fixed in 9.24.1.27 and 9.24.10.1
- 
    Cisco Secure FTD Software Release
    
  - 7.0 and earlier - Fixed in 7.0.11
  - 7.2 - Fixed in 7.2.13
  - 7.4 - Fixed in 7.4.9
  - 7.6 - Fixed in 7.6.7
  - 7.7 - Fixed in 7.7.14
  - 10.0 - Fixed in 10.0.3
  - 10.1 - Fixed in 10.1.1
Cisco also noted that the vulnerability affects Cisco devices if the following conditions are met -
- They are running a vulnerable release of Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software or Cisco Secure FTD Software.
- The SSL remote access VPN login service is reachable.
- Secondary authentication is configured in the tunnel group scope.
"If tunnel-group-list enable is configured, check all tunnel groups, including the default tunnel group, DefaultWEBVPNGroup, for secondary-authentication-server-group," Cisco said.
"If tunnel-group-list enable is absent or has been removed using the no tunnel-group-list enable command, check the default tunnel group, DefaultWEBVPNGroup, for secondary-authentication-server-group because disabling the group list does not remove exposure when that default group uses secondary authentication."
As a temporary mitigation, the company is recommending that customers turn off the tunnel group list if DefaultWEBVPNGroup does not use secondary authentication, or disable secondary authentication on any user-configured tunnel group list or on the default tunnel group, DefaultWEBVPNGroup.
"On Cisco Secure FTD Software, review the deployed remote access VPN policy and the resulting device running configuration in Cisco Secure FMC Software or Cisco Secure FDM," Cisco said. "A successful VPN login is not required to reach the affected processing path."
The disclosure comes as Cisco revealed that a sophisticated advanced persistent threat (APT) actor tracked as UAT-11473 weaponized CVE-2026-20127, an authentication bypass vulnerability in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controller instances, to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to affected systems.
The activity, which has targeted space and satellite services, defense and aerospace technology, and policy research sectors, is assessed to share infrastructure overlaps with Volt Typhoon's Silent Train covert network.
"UAT-11473 then installed a custom malware framework we track as 'KeyDrift' consisting of multiple components [like PolyFlame and LittleFilch] geared towards collecting sensitive keying information, acting as backdoors and intermediate command-and-control (C2) hosts," Cisco Talos said.
"The framework is designed to provide long-term persistent access and automated exfiltration of sensitive keying material. KeyDrift operates inside SD-WAN control-plane processes and is capable of intercepting decrypted control traffic, extracting control-session metadata and data-plane keying material, and staging or transmitting the collected material using encrypted records."

articles.title: 'This is a training and trust problem, not an AI problem': Barely any workers are verifying information given to them by AI
articles.text:
'This is a training and trust problem, not an AI problem': Barely any workers are verifying information given to them by AI
Computer says “knock yourself out”
- Just 24% of employees verify the results of an AI-generated answer before proceeding
- A worrying 39% of employees have acted upon AI-generated responses that turned out to be inaccurate or unsuitable
- The research was conducted by Censuswide on behalf of learning company O’Reilly
AI chatbots are preferred to colleagues and managers for work-related matters, according to a survey of 2,000 UK workers, with under a quarter (24%) bothering to confirm the results or directions from an AI-generated solution.
Meanwhile, with over a third of employees revealing that guidance from an AI has resulted in inaccurate and incomplete answers (if they were even suitable in the first place), almost as many have received no AI training or guidance in the past year.
The research from O’Reilly Media raises some serious questions, not just about how AI is being used in the workplace, but what controls, oversight, and training accompany its use.
An AI training gap?
The use of AI in the workplace has had some interesting outcomes, but one that few will have predicted is the use of AI chatbots as a substitute for advice from colleagues.
O’Reilly’s survey has unlocked not just the concerning 24% bothering to verify AI-generated answers, but also the paltry 16% that are provided with AI training that relates to their role, and 35% say no AI guidance or training has been given at all.
Without the full context of individual workplaces to consult, it appears that AI has been introduced and teams simply left to get on with it, while training attempts to catch up.
"We're seeing a workforce that has fully embraced AI as a first port of call, but the safety net hasn't caught up with the speed of adoption," said Alexia Pedersen, SVP International at O'Reilly. "People are moving faster than their organizations' training and governance.”
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Pedersen describes that gap as a place where “mistakes happen.” But the obvious answer isn’t necessarily the right one. There is an alternative to putting the breaks on AI, she says. “The answer isn't to slow down AI adoption; it's to close the gap with the right training, verification habits, and trusted expertise to back it up."
Building a culture of verification
While the results of the survey raise questions about AI use, the statistics do point towards a challenge in the delivery of training, as well as trust in colleagues and organizational structures.
Pedersen observes, "This is a training and trust problem, not an AI problem." Some solutions will need to be found to ensure that AI training is as important as other work-based learning.
"Organizations that invest now in structured, role-specific AI training and in building a culture of verification rather than uncritical acceptance will be the ones who turn today's AI adoption into a genuine productivity advantage," Pedersen concludes.

Christian Cawley has extensive experience as a writer and editor in consumer electronics, IT and entertainment media. He has contributed to TechRadar since 2017 and has been published in Computer Weekly, Linux Format, ComputerActive, and other publications.
He currently heads up the team at smart home website Matter Alpha, and writes about retro gaming at Gaming Retro.

articles.title: À 1,99 €/mois la première année, Proton Mail facilite le départ de Gmail
articles.text:
Pour le Black Friday, Proton baisse fortement le prix de sa messagerie chiffrée : -60 % sur Proton Mail Plus et -50 % sur Proton Unlimited avec l’abonnement d’un an. Si vous hésitiez à quitter Gmail, c’est le moment.
Pour la plupart d’entre nous, Gmail est la boîte mail par défaut. Elle est gratuite, pratique, déjà installée sur le téléphone, et on n’y pense plus. Pourtant, elle contient une bonne partie de notre vie : factures, échanges avec la banque, documents administratifs, conversations privées, comptes en ligne. Tout cela est hébergé chez une entreprise dont le modèle économique repose sur la publicité.
Proton Mail propose l’inverse : une messagerie chiffrée, hébergée en Suisse, sans aucune publicité, financée uniquement par ses abonnés. Son principal frein était le prix. Jusqu’au 30 novembre, ce frein disparaît presque.
Gmail : gratuit, mais à quel prix ?
Gmail n’est pas gratuit, on le paie autrement. Google a bâti son modèle sur la publicité, et votre boîte mail en fait partie : des annonces s’affichent dans l’onglet Promotions, et vos usages enrichissent l’écosystème Google dans son ensemble. Avec l’arrivée de Gemini dans Gmail, l’IA lit désormais vos messages pour les résumer, proposer des réponses et faire des recherches dedans.
Il faut aussi tenir compte de la juridiction. Google est une entreprise américaine, soumise au Cloud Act, ce qui permet aux autorités des États-Unis de demander l’accès à des données même lorsqu’elles sont stockées en Europe. Pour une boîte mail qui contient vos papiers d’identité et vos relevés bancaires, ce n’est pas un détail.
Proton Mail : un modèle fondé sur la confidentialité
Proton a été fondé à Genève par des scientifiques passés par le CERN, avec une idée simple : vos e-mails ne regardent que vous. Les messages entre utilisateurs Proton sont chiffrés de bout en bout. Le reste de votre boîte est protégé par un chiffrement « zéro accès » : même Proton ne peut pas lire ce qui est stocké sur ses serveurs.
Le service repose sur le droit suisse, l’un des plus protecteurs au monde en matière de vie privée. Son code est open source, ce qui permet à n’importe quel expert de l’examiner. Surtout, Proton n’a pas besoin de vos données pour gagner de l’argent : ses revenus viennent uniquement des abonnements.
Cette approche n’empêche pas le confort. Proton Mail Plus comprend :
- 15 Go de stockage, partagés avec Proton Drive ;
- jusqu’à 10 adresses e-mail et 1 nom de domaine personnalisé ;
- 10 alias « hide-my-email », pour s’inscrire sur un site sans donner sa vraie adresse ;
- un calendrier chiffré, des dossiers et libellés illimités ;
- des applications iOS, Android et web, avec une assistance prioritaire.
Proton Mail Plus vs Gmail : le comparatif
|  | Proton Mail Plus | Gmail (gratuit) | 
| Chiffrement | Bout en bout + zéro accès | Chiffrement standard, Google peut accéder aux données | 
| Publicité | Aucune | Oui (onglet Promotions) | 
| Modèle économique | Abonnements | Publicité | 
| Juridiction | Suisse | États-Unis (Cloud Act) | 
| Alias pour masquer son adresse | 10 inclus | Non | 
| Domaine personnalisé | Oui | Non (via Google Workspace, payant) | 
| Prix Black Friday | 1,99 €/mois | Gratuit | 
Changer de boîte mail sans rien perdre
C’est souvent ce qui fait renoncer : « Je vais perdre mes mails et mes contacts. » En réalité, Proton a prévu le cas. L’outil Easy Switch importe en quelques clics vos e-mails, contacts et calendriers depuis Gmail. Vous pouvez ensuite activer une redirection automatique : tout ce qui arrive encore sur votre ancienne adresse est renvoyé vers Proton.
La transition se fait donc à votre rythme. Vous mettez à jour vos comptes en ligne au fil de l’eau, sans rien couper du jour au lendemain. Et si Proton ne vous convient pas, la garantie « satisfait ou remboursé » de 30 jours vous protège.
Black Friday : deux offres jusqu’au 30 novembre
Proton Mail Plus : -60 %. Au lieu de 4,99 € par mois, l’abonnement passe à 1,99 € par mois, soit 23,88 € pour la première année. Il est ensuite renouvelé à 47,88 € par an. Le Black Friday divise donc la facture par plus de deux. C’est la formule idéale pour remplacer Gmail au quotidien.
Proton Unlimited : -50 %. Pour ceux qui veulent quitter tout l’écosystème Google, Unlimited regroupe toute la suite Proton : Mail, Calendar, 500 Go de stockage sur Proton Drive, Proton Docs et Sheets pour travailler à plusieurs, le gestionnaire de mots de passe Proton Pass et Proton VPN. Au lieu de 12,99 € par mois, il passe à 6,49 € par mois, soit 77,88 € pour la première année, puis 119,88 € par an.

articles.title: Pulsar Teases Dual-Sensor Gaming Mouse with True Adjustable Sensor Position
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
Pulsar Teases Dual-Sensor Gaming Mouse with True Adjustable Sensor Position
Pulsar seems to be on a bit of a run in 2026, having already shown off a new X5 ergo gaming mouse and launched a new X2F CrazyLight fingertip mouse, but its latest announcement isn't an actual product launch, but rather a peek at what's to come for the brand. According to a new mini-documentary Pulsar published on its YouTube channel, it is working on a gaming mouse platform that would allow for dual sensors. 
In the mini-doc, Pulsar explains that "innovation at the mechanical level has reached a realm where humans can no longer keep up," likely referring to the ever-increasing DPI and polling rate increases that we have seen gaming mouse companies brag about. As such, it is developing the dual-sensor system to allow users to better tailor their mouse inputs to their individual needs and movement patterns. The system basically combines sensor data from both sensors and calculates movement based on a pre-determined offset that can be set in software by a user. This theoretically allows the sensor to be placed anywhere on the bottom of the mouse.This isn't the first time that a dual-sensor gaming mouse concept has been tested, with YouTuber and former Aimlabs CTO, Giovanni Laerte Frongia, aka bardOZ, having previously shown off a prototype of a dual-sensor setup and virtual sensor position. There have also been other gaming mice, like the Pwnage Vanta, that featured physical sensor movement to achieve a similar result, but Pulsar's engineering team says that this was tedious. The dual-sensor system also has the advantage of reducing sensor noise, since that sensor noise is unique to each unit, similar to CPU silicon quality. 
Similarly to how the new Corsair Sabre V3 Pro PureVector mice aim to optimize X and Y axis sensor DPI by having the user play AimLabs, the Pulsar implementation looks to be using mini-games to find an optimal virtual sensor position automatically, but it will likely also allow users to manually set virtual sensor position. It's unclear when Pulsar will launch a dual-sensor gaming mouse, and the team didn't specifically mention which mouse shape would lead the charge, but Pulsar's mice generally share internals across a specific generation, so it's entirely likely that we will see multiple dual-sensor mice from Pulsar when the system eventually makes it to market.

articles.title: GitHub Launches npm Firewall to Block Malicious Packages Before Installation
articles.text:
GitHub has announced that it's introducing a new package firewall as a preview to block installation of suspicious npm packages during installation time.
"The firewall inspects both metadata requests and package downloads for signs of malicious activity, acting as an install-time policy gate," GitHub said.
The feature, which currently supports only npm packages, is available in public preview for all GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers, including data-resident GitHub Enterprise Cloud.
According to the Microsoft subsidiary, the firewall is placed between endpoints or internal registries and the upstream package repositories so as to deter malware attacks that compromise systems when packages are installed.
This behavior can expose users to severe security risks, especially when artificial intelligence (AI) agents and CI runners automatically install dependencies to complete a task or build without their explicit permission.
The idea is that endpoints like coding agents and CI/CD hosts use the firewall for their requests instead of directly pointing to the public package registries. The firewall then checks package downloads against policy controls such as minimum package age and malware advisories, and blocks downloads that do not meet those policies.
To use the firewall, administrators are required to configure policy controls, such as the ones listed below -
- Block known malware by checking against the GitHub Advisory Database for active malware advisories
- Block packages based on the severity of vulnerabilities by checking the GitHub Advisory Database for flaws that affect the requested package version. The control defaults to "Critical only" as the severity level that blocks an installation, although users can choose "High or higher," "Medium or higher," or "Any severity."
- Block attestation downgrades by comparing attestations for the requested package version with those of earlier versions and stop the download if the requested version does not have an SLSA attestation.
- Block newly-introduced install scripts by checking whether the package recently added scripts that run using preinstall or postinstall hooks, which can be abused to steal sensitive data.
Block packages based on a cooldown period that prevents versions that are newer than the configured minimum age from being installed. The value can range from 1 to 365 days. The default value is 1 day. Users can disable it by setting it to 0.
Users who need access to a package that gets blocked erroneously by the firewall can submit an exception request, which can then be approved by enterprise administrators and security managers.
The development comes as Rust 1.100, which is scheduled for release on November 12, 2026, readies to add support for a configurable minimum publish age, allowing security scanners and maintainers time to flag and block malicious crate releases before they can be installed or used by users.
The value, defined via the "global-min-publish-age" option in "cargo/config.toml," allows users to specify a minimum publication age in days or weeks. If left unspecified, a seven-day waiting period is applied by default to skip releases published within that window.
Over the past year, similar waiting periods have been implemented across open-source ecosystems, including npm, Python, Microsoft Visual Studio Code, Ruby, Bun, pnpm, and Yarn, as a way to bolster software supply chain security by reducing the chance that a newly published, unreviewed version is immediately pulled into a build.
Cooldown periods help add friction and slow down attacks in which a bad actor publishes a poisoned version of a popular package after seizing control of a maintainer account, thereby preventing rapid spread through manual or automated installations.
"The tradeoff is that legitimate fixes have to wait, too, unless developers make an exception," Socket said. "Malicious code also doesn't magically become harmless with age. A release that escapes detection can simply outlast the cooldown. The value is in buying researchers, maintainers, and registries time to act before the next dependency update carries an attack further."

articles.title: “Une incrédulité mêlée d’excitation” : la découverte d’un nouveau monde au-delà de Pluton pourrait changer la carte de notre Système solaire
articles.text:
“Une incrédulité mêlée d’excitation” : la découverte d’un nouveau monde au-delà de Pluton pourrait changer la carte de notre Système solaire
Elle a échappé à tous les télescopes pendant des décennies, noyée dans la cohue d'étoiles de la Voie lactée. Un monde de glace qui pourrait mesurer jusqu’à 1 500 km se cachait au-delà de Pluton, perdu au milieu de millions d’étoiles. On l’avait même photographié en 2016, sans que personne le remarque. Celui qui l’a repéré a d’abord cru à une erreur. Si les astronomes confirment ce qu’il a vu, notre Système solaire comptera une sixième planète naine.
L'observatoire Vera C. Rubin, perché sur le Cerro Pachón, au Chili, a dévoilé le 27 octobre 2026 l'existence de 2026 ED138, un objet glacé situé à environ 46 unités astronomiques du Soleil, soit près de 6,9 milliards de kilomètres. Pluton orbite en moyenne à 40 unités. Avec un diamètre estimé entre 600 et 1 500 km, ce corps figure parmi les plus gros candidats au statut de planète naine jamais repérés au-delà de Neptune. S'il est confirmé, il deviendra le sixième membre reconnu par l'Union astronomique internationale.
Meet our Solar System's newest dwarf planet candidate: 2026 ED138!
Orbiting past Pluto, scientists found it in NSF–DOE Rubin Observatory data from earlier in 2026. Early analysis suggests it's 600–1500 km across, one of the largest found past Neptune!
🔗 https://t.co/wTOg898zBupic.twitter.com/hEgnk597rl
— NSF-DOE Rubin Observatory (@VRubinObs) October 27, 2026
Comment 2026 ED138 a été repéré dans les données de Rubin
Le soir du 13 octobre, Matthew Holman, astrophysicien au Center for Astrophysics Harvard & Smithsonian, passe au crible des images captées entre mars et juillet par le télescope Simonyi. Il utilise un algorithme conçu avec son collègue Kevin Napier, qui relie entre elles les détections d'un même point lumineux en mouvement d'une nuit à l'autre. Un objet attire son regard : son éclat, rapporté à sa distance, trahit une taille hors norme. Le chercheur soupçonne d'abord une erreur, la sienne ou celle de son code.
	
Ma première réaction a été une incrédulité mêlée d'excitation.
Mario Jurić, chercheur à l'Université de Washington et responsable scientifique du Système solaire pour Rubin, exhume alors vingt observations supplémentaires, jusqu'au 4 mars. Des clichés d'archives de la caméra DECam, elle aussi installée au Chili, prolongent la piste jusqu'en 2016. Plus de dix ans de trajectoire reconstitués.
Pourquoi si tard ? L'objet évolue près du plan de la Voie lactée, une région saturée de millions d'étoiles, selon la National Science Foundation. Les relevés précédents y avaient renoncé.
Une planète naine encore à confirmer
La fourchette de taille reste vertigineuse, car elle dépend de la capacité de sa surface à réfléchir la lumière, une valeur encore inconnue. À 600 km, ED138 serait plus petit que Cérès (environ 940 km). À 1 500 km, il dépasserait Makémaké. Pour décrocher le titre, il doit être assez massif pour que sa propre gravité l'ait arrondi. Seules des observations infrarouges permettront de trancher.
Son orbite, inclinée d'environ 25 degrés, suggère qu'il a été bousculé par Neptune dans un lointain passé. D'autres mondes comme Sedna, Quaoar ou Gonggong attendent d'ailleurs toujours leur reconnaissance officielle.
Rubin ne fait que commencer. Son grand relevé du ciel austral, lancé en juin 2026, doit durer dix ans, et l'observatoire avait déjà signalé plus de 11 000 astéroïdes inconnus en avril.
	
Rubin va photographier tout le ciel austral encore et encore pendant dix ans. Les autres objets cachés dans les zones délaissées par les relevés précédents sont désormais à notre portée.
