articles.title: Amazon cayó en bolsa por ventas previstas bajo lo esperado y un gasto en IA que consume su caja
articles.text:
Las acciones de Amazon cayeron más de 5% fuera del horario de operaciones el 29 de octubre de 2026, después de que la empresa informó ganancias y ventas trimestrales inferiores a lo previsto, una proyección de ingresos para fin de año algo menor a la esperada y un flujo de caja negativo por el gasto en inteligencia artificial.
En el tercer trimestre, que terminó el 30 de septiembre de 2026, las ventas netas subieron 12%, hasta USD 201.900 millones.
Los analistas consultados por LSEG esperaban USD 202.310 millones. La ganancia por acción fue de USD 1,89, frente a los USD 1,96 que preveía el mercado, según CNBC.
La ganancia neta bajó a USD 20.700 millones desde USD 21.200 millones un año antes. Amazon explicó que en 2025 había registrado ganancias antes de impuestos por USD 9.500 millones por su inversión en la empresa de IA Anthropic, un efecto que no se repitió.
La caída llegó tras una jornada ya negativa: la acción cerró con una baja de 4,25%, a USD 243,79, mientras el índice Nasdaq retrocedía 1,38%, según Motley Fool. Después del cierre, AP informó una baja de más de 5% y CNBC, de más de 7%.
USD 42.400 millones negativos en flujo de caja
El flujo de caja libre, el dinero que queda después de pagar las inversiones, fue negativo en USD 42.400 millones en los últimos 12 meses. Un año antes había sido positivo en USD 14.800 millones. Amazon atribuyó el cambio a las compras de equipos e infraestructura, que aumentaron USD 94.800 millones, sobre todo por la IA.
Es el segundo trimestre consecutivo con flujo negativo. En el anterior, el saldo había sido de USD 7.600 millones negativos, según CNBC. La empresa mantuvo su previsión de gasto de inversión para 2026 en unos USD 220.000 millones.
El director ejecutivo, Andy Jassy, dijo en la llamada con inversores que Amazon gastará “significativamente más” en 2027, según CNBC. También afirmó que la empresa ve “una línea de visión clara” hacia retornos financieros atractivos.
Otros gigantes tecnológicos mostraron cursos distintos. Microsoft redujo su previsión de gasto del año a USD 170.000 millones, desde USD 175.000 millones, y Alphabet mantuvo la suya entre USD 195.000 y USD 205.000 millones, según CNBC.
La nube acelera; la publicidad y el cierre de año decepcionan
Amazon Web Services, la división de computación en la nube, facturó USD 46.000 millones, 39% más que un año antes y su mayor ritmo de crecimiento en casi cinco años. Su ganancia operativa fue de USD 17.800 millones. Jassy proyectó crecimientos superiores a 40% en 2027 y 2028.
En la llamada, según GeekWire, Jassy dijo que la división tiene contratos por USD 578.000 millones en ingresos futuros, más del doble que un año antes. En el comunicado, el ejecutivo habló de que Amazon podría tener dos negocios de un billón de dólares en ingresos en los próximos cinco a 10 años.
Sus ingresos llegaron a USD 19.640 millones, frente a los USD 20.820 millones que esperaba el mercado, según StreetAccount. Amazon atribuyó parte de la diferencia al cambio de fecha del Prime Day, que este año cayó en el segundo trimestre. Sin ese efecto, el crecimiento de las ventas habría sido unos cuatro puntos porcentuales mayor.
Para el cuarto trimestre, que incluye las compras de fin de año, Amazon prevé ventas de entre USD 240.000 y USD 247.000 millones, un alza de 12% a 16%. El punto medio queda por debajo de los USD 244.500 millones que esperaba el mercado, según LSEG.
La ganancia operativa estimada para ese período es de entre USD 28.500 y USD 33.500 millones. La empresa prevé que los ingresos publicitarios crezcan por encima de 15% anual en esos meses.

articles.title: Attacker Tried to Exploit Alpine Linux’s GitLab via CVSS 10.0 Flaw Its Ruby Left Open
articles.text:
An attacker tried to exploit a critical GitLab vulnerability on the Alpine Linux project's own GitLab server a week after GitLab released a fix, Alpine Linux said on 28 October.
The flaw, CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS score: 10.0), can let an attacker run code on a GitLab server through a crafted regular expression in a CI configuration. Alpine found no evidence that the attack worked but cannot rule it out, so it rebuilt the server from scratch and reset every account's password.
GitLab's fix is a set of patches to the Ruby that GitLab ships in its own packages and container images. Alpine's GitLab image used standard Ruby, so upgrading the server to GitLab 19.3.6 on 22 October did not fix the flaw.
For anyone running GitLab on their own Ruby, built from source or in their own container image, "upgrading GitLab is not enough," Alpine said. Those servers also need Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12, 4.0.9 or later, and users of Alpine's alpinelinux/gitlab image need to pull 19.3.6 again.
The server gitlab.alpinelinux.org hosts aports, the repository from which Alpine's packages are built. Packages built from 20 to 24 October, and the 21 October releases, came from aports changes verified against records outside GitLab, according to Alpine.
Those releases include the minirootfs files that the official Alpine Docker images are built from. Alpine is extending the checks to 27 October, when it closed the server. The keys that sign its packages and releases have never been on the GitLab server.
How the Attack Unfolded
On 13 October, Alpine upgraded the server to GitLab 19.3.4 instead of 19.3.5, which it calls a mistake. The server was still on that version, without the 12 October fix, when a newly registered account began probing it on 20 October.
The account sent crafted CI configurations to the server on 20 and 21 October. They crashed GitLab worker processes 8 times, and the main attack on 21 October also caused 502 errors and caused CI jobs to fail.
In 4 of those crashes, the attacker got partway through the exploit and failed at the next step, according to Alpine. The attacker also downloaded Alpine's GitLab container image, which Alpine said: "suggests they were tuning the exploit to our exact build."
Alpine blocked the account on 23 October. The attacker came back on 25 and 26 October and tried to get back in, but those attempts failed, Alpine said.
On 26 October, Alpine found that the server was still vulnerable after its 22 October upgrade to 19.3.6. The next day, it closed GitLab to everyone except its developers and build servers and started rebuilding it.
The rebuild finished on 28 October. Alpine also replaced GitLab's secret keys, and the rebuilt server runs Ruby 3.3.13 or later, which has the fix. Alpine is testing it before reopening it to the public.
What Alpine Can and Cannot Rule Out
Alpine found no sign that the attacker's code ran on the server. Timing probes showed no delays;; there were no unexpected files, keys, hooks, or processes; and no private data was sent back to the attacker via any web or API request that Alpine can see.
It cannot be sure, though. "A successful exploit would leave no crash and no trace in the web logs," Alpine said. Some logs from the attack day are gone, including background job logs and the old container's filesystem, and neither Alpine nor its hosting provider logged outbound network connections.
Because the evidence needed to confirm code execution no longer exists, Alpine treated the server as compromised and rebuilt it to remove any foothold a successful exploit could have left.
If the attack succeeded, these could have been exposed:
- Email addresses, names, and IP addresses of all users
- Password hashes
- 2FA secrets, CI/CD variables and runner tokens
- Webhook, integration and push mirror credentials
- Personal access tokens, which are stored as hashes
- Private repositories, and confidential issues and merge requests
Beyond the password reset and the new secret keys, Alpine has not said whether runner tokens, CI/CD variables, access tokens or integration credentials stored on the server have been replaced.
To check its packages, Alpine confirmed that every aports change added from 20 to 22 October arrived through a recorded push by a known developer. It checked this against records it says the attacker could not reach: a developer's copy of the repository and all 45 build servers. Every package built from 20 to 24 October came from aports changes as published on git.alpinelinux.org.
Why the GitLab Upgrade Did Not Fix It
GitLab compiles the regular expressions in CI configurations with Ruby, and the bug behind CVE-2026-97229 is in Onigmo, the regular expression engine built into Ruby.
GitLab's 12 October release fixed it by patching the Ruby inside GitLab's Linux package and container images. Ruby's own fixed versions came out on 22 and 23 October.
A GitLab upgrade does not change a server's own Ruby, so a GitLab install on standard Ruby keeps the flaw until Ruby itself is updated to a fixed version, as Alpine found.
GitLab's fixed Linux packages and its official container images carry the patched Ruby. A self-compiled install, or a container image that installs Ruby separately as Alpine's did, does not get it.
As of 29 October, neither of GitLab's patch release posts for 12 and 21 October tells administrators of self-compiled installs to update Ruby. GitLab's self-compiled installation guide still lists Ruby 3.2 as its minimum version, and Ruby 3.2 reached end of life in April and will get no fix.
Which GitLab Servers Are Exposed
GitLab's advisory says that, "under certain conditions," the flaw could have allowed an unauthenticated user to run code on the server. GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already patched.
Rapid7 built a working exploit in a lab and published proof-of-concept code on 13 October. The exploit ran commands as GitLab's git user on an unpatched official GitLab 19.4.1 image, but the same input did not run on the patched 19.4.2 image.
That exploit needs write access first: the attacker must commit a malicious .gitlab-ci.yml file and a file path with UTF-8 characters to a branch of a public project. That requirement does not apply on servers where new users can register themselves and create projects.
In Rapid7's tested route, "only the final CI lint request is unauthenticated." GitLab's own detection notes also say the attacker must first create that file path through ordinary repository APIs. Rapid7 does not yet know how the attack in the original report to GitLab, which is still private, avoids the write step.
Alpine has not said how its attacker's CI configurations reached GitLab, or whether new accounts could create public projects on its server.
CVE-2026-97229 was not in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog as of the catalog's 28 October update.
What GitLab Administrators Should Do
GitLab's 21 October releases are the newest on each branch listed below, and they also fix CVE-2026-110264, a separate regex flaw.
| Branch | Fixes CVE-2026-97229, per GitLab's advisory | Newest release (21 October) | 
|---|---|---|
| 19.5 | Not listed as affected | 19.5.1 | 
| 19.4 | 19.4.2 | 19.4.3 | 
| 19.3 | 19.3.5 | 19.3.6 | 
| 19.2 | 19.2.8 | 19.2.9 | 
| 19.1, 19.0 and 18.11 | Not listed as affected | 19.1.9, 19.0.10 and 18.11.13 | 
Which release fixes a server depends on how GitLab is installed:
- GitLab's Linux package or official container images: upgrade to the newest release for your branch.
- Self-compiled installs, or images that install their own Ruby: upgrade GitLab and update Ruby to 3.3.13, 3.4.12, 4.0.9, or later. Ruby 3.2 will not receive the fix, so servers running 3.2 need to upgrade to one of those versions.
GitLab's advisory named 19.3.4 as the fixed version for the 19.3 branch when it was published on 12 October. It now names 19.3.5 and lists 19.3.4 as affected, so servers still on 19.3.4 should move to 19.3.6.
If a server cannot be upgraded right away, Rapid7 suggests restricting anonymous access to public projects, stopping untrusted users from creating or writing to public projects, or blocking the CI lint route. Those steps cover only Rapid7's exploit route and do not fix the vulnerable regular expression compiler, the company said.
GitLab has published six detection rules for exploitation attempts against self-managed servers, written in the Sigma format. Four of them, which GitLab marks as experimental, look for hostile patterns in CI regexp warnings and GraphQL ciLint requests, unusually long file paths with non-ASCII characters, and Ruby crash reports that point to Onigmo.
The guidance with those rules warns that a successful exploit can leave no crash, and it gives these further steps:
- Look for files owned by the git user in /tmp, unexpected child processes of Puma or Sidekiq, outbound connections, and changed crontabs or SSH keys for the git user.
- If there are signs of code execution, treat the server as compromised and rotate the secrets in gitlab-secrets.json, all CI/CD variables, all runner tokens and all access tokens.
- Limit who can create accounts and personal access tokens on the server.
What Alpine Users Should Do
Account holders will need to set a new password with "Forgot your password?" on the sign-in page when gitlab.alpinelinux.org reopens, Alpine said. It has also seen automated login attempts against its GitLab using passwords leaked from other sites, and anyone who used their gitlab.alpinelinux.org password elsewhere should change it there.
Users of the alpinelinux/gitlab image should pull alpinelinux/gitlab:19.3.6 again. The image published on 27 October contains Ruby 3.3.13, while any 19.3.6 image pulled before then, and every older tag, is vulnerable.
Alpine's own Ruby packages already have the fix: Ruby 3.4.12 on Alpine 3.22, 3.23, 3.24 and edge, and Ruby 3.3.13 on Alpine 3.21. Running apk upgrade installs it.
Ruby's maintainers say the bug matters only for programs that compile a regular expression from text an attacker controls, and that Ruby's Regexp.timeout setting does not protect against it.

articles.title: Microsoft donne un nouveau souffle au ray tracing avec DirectX, même sur les cartes graphiques actuelles
articles.text:
Microsoft vient de dévoiler ce qu’il présente comme la plus importante évolution du ray tracing dans DirectX depuis 2018. Au programme : des scènes plus détaillées, des calculs beaucoup plus efficaces et des gains de performances impressionnants en démonstration. Le tout sans nécessiter une nouvelle génération de cartes graphiques.
Le ray tracing permet aux jeux vidéo de reproduire plus fidèlement les reflets, les ombres et les effets de lumière. Mais cette technologie a un défaut bien connu des joueurs PC : elle demande énormément de puissance de calcul, surtout lorsque les décors sont complexes et que de nombreux objets bougent à l'écran.
Microsoft veut justement s’attaquer à ce problème. Avec une nouvelle version expérimentale de son DirectX 12 Agility SDK, l’entreprise introduit plusieurs technologies destinées à rendre le ray tracing moins gourmand.
Des décors plus complexes, sans tout recalculer
Pour comprendre cette évolution, il faut savoir qu’une carte graphique ne calcule pas les rayons lumineux au hasard. Elle utilise une sorte de carte simplifiée de la scène, appelée structure d’accélération, pour déterminer plus rapidement quels objets peuvent être touchés par la lumière. Le problème ? Quand les objets bougent ou que le décor change, une partie de cette structure doit être reconstruite. Une opération qui peut devenir particulièrement coûteuse et pour laquelle Microsoft propose deux solutions complémentaires.
La première, Clustered Geometry, permet de regrouper les éléments d’un décor en petits ensembles réutilisables. Plutôt que de recalculer toute la géométrie, le moteur graphique peut conserver une bonne partie du travail déjà effectué. La seconde, PTLAS, applique une logique similaire aux scènes animées : seules les parties modifiées doivent être mises à jour.
Résultat attendu : moins de calculs inutiles et davantage de ressources disponibles pour afficher des environnements détaillés avec des effets de lumière réalistes.
De 1,2 à 79 FPS : des résultats impressionnants, mais attention
Microsoft accompagne son annonce d’une démonstration technique particulièrement parlante. Sur une Radeon RX 9070, le passage à Clustered Geometry fait passer les performances de 1,2 à 79 images par seconde dans une scène de test. Le temps nécessaire à la construction des structures d’accélération chute également de 788 à 3,11 millisecondes, tandis que leur consommation mémoire diminue de près de 90 %.
Ces chiffres sont spectaculaires, mais ils doivent être replacés dans leur contexte. Il s’agit d’un cas de démonstration conçu pour mettre en évidence les avantages de cette nouvelle méthode, pas d'un gain que l’on retrouvera dans les jeux commerciaux. D’autant que cette optimisation peut nécessiter davantage de mémoire temporaire pendant certains calculs.
Bonne nouvelle, pas besoin de changer de carte graphique
Autre intérêt de cette évolution : elle ne repose pas sur de nouvelles unités matérielles. Les technologies présentées sont destinées aux GeForce RTX de NVIDIA, aux Radeon RX 9000 d’AMD et aux Intel Arc série B, ainsi qu’à certains GPU intégrés compatibles. Elles nécessiteront toutefois des pilotes adaptés et surtout une intégration par les développeurs.
Autrement dit, installer une mise à jour de DirectX ne fera pas soudainement grimper les FPS de vos jeux actuels. L’intérêt se situe plutôt du côté des futurs titres, dont les moteurs pourront exploiter ces outils pour afficher des scènes plus riches tout en maîtrisant le coût du ray tracing.
Microsoft pose ainsi les bases d’une évolution importante du rendu graphique sur PC. Reste désormais à voir comment les studios s’en empareront et quels bénéfices les joueurs constateront réellement.

articles.title: Halloween 2026 : les 10 meilleurs films d’horreur à voir sur Disney+
articles.text:
Halloween 2026 : les 10 meilleurs films d’horreur à voir sur Disney+
En quête du film idéal pour frissonner devant Disney+ ? Les Numériques vous propose sa sélection des dix meilleurs titres à voir sur la plateforme de streaming pour l'édition 2026 de Halloween.
C'est officiel : nous sommes en plein mois d'octobre, et dans la "spooky season" de Halloween ! Et entre une sculpture de citrouilles et une chasse aux friandises, rien de tel que de s'installer devant un film doucement terrifiant à voir sur Disney+.
La plateforme de streaming propose une belle sélection de longs-métrages pour se faire peur, mais encore faut-il savoir ce qui vaut le coup. C'est pour ça que Les Numériques a sélectionné pour vous 10 valeurs sûres et dix des meilleurs films à regarder pour frissonner à tous les âges.
Quels sont les meilleurs films à voir sur Disney+ pour Halloween ?
Casper
Un tout jeune fantôme, Casper, ronge son frein et s'ennuie à mourir en compagnie de ses oncles dans le manoir de Whipstaff. Quand une petite fille et son père viennent s'installer dans la maison hantée, il pense pouvoir enfin s'amuser...
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
La Colline a des yeux
Pour fêter leur anniversaire de mariage, Big Bob Carter et sa femme Ethel ont demandé à leur famille de partir avec eux en Californie. Mais en chemin, une route désertique va conduire les Carter vers le pire des cauchemars…
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
Traquée
Brynn Adams est une jeune femme talentueuse rejetée par sa communauté. Solitaire donc, mais toujours optimiste, elle trouve son réconfort entre les murs de la maison où elle a grandi. Une nuit, elle est réveillée par des bruits provenant d'intrus manifestement non humains. Commence alors un éprouvant face-à-face entre Brynn et une foule de créatures extraterrestres qui la mettent en péril imminent, mais l'obligent aussi à affronter son passé.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
Wedding Nightmare
La nuit de noces d’une jeune mariée, incarnée par Samara Weaving, tourne au cauchemar quand sa riche et excentrique belle-famille lui demande d’honorer une tradition qui va se révéler meurtrière, demandant à chacun de lutter pour sa survie.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
Hocus Pocus, les trois sorcières
Halloween 1993 : Pour gagner le coeur de sa bien-aimée, Max Dennison, va, par bravade, allumer la bougie fatidique qui a le pouvoir de faire renaître les trois soeurs Sanderson Winifred, Sarah et Mary, les trois plus célèbres sorcières de Salem.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
The Rocky Horror Picture Show
Cette comédie musicale déjantée commence par une nuit d'orage, quand la voiture de Janet et Brad, un couple coincé qui vient de se fiancer, tombe en panne. Obligés de se réfugier dans un mystérieux château, ils vont faire la rencontre de ses occupants pour le moins bizarres, qui se livrent à de bien étranges expériences.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
Alien : Romulus
Le film se concentre sur une équipe de jeunes colons de l'espace qui explore les profondeurs d'une station spatiale délabrée, ignorant les horreurs qui les attendent. C'est là qu'ils sont confrontés aux créatures les plus terrifiantes de l'univers : les Xenomorphes.
L'intégralité de la franchise Alien est également disponible sur Disney+.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
La Mouche
Seth Brundle, un jeune biologiste très doué, met au point une invention qui doit révolutionner le monde : la téléportation. Les essais sur un babouin sont peu convaincants et après des fuites dans la presse, il décide de se téléporter lui-même. Seulement il ne s'aperçoit pas qu'une mouche fait partie du voyage.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
Le Manoir hanté et les 999 fantômes
Agent immobilier accro du boulot, Jim Evers traîne sa famille jusqu'à une grande et glaciale demeure qu'il rêve de transformer en un somptueux immeuble en copropriété. Mais à son arrivée, la famille Evers découvre très vite qu'elle n'est pas seule dans la maison...
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
Le Village
Une petite communauté isolée vit dans la terrifiante certitude qu'une race de créatures mythiques peuple les bois entourant le village. Cette force maléfique est si menaçante que personne n'ose s'aventurer au-delà des dernières maisons, et encore moins pénétrer dans les bois... Le jeune Lucius Hunt, un garçon entêté, est cependant bien décidé à aller voir ce qui se cache par-delà des limites du village, et son audace menace de changer à jamais l'avenir de tous...

articles.title: Hackers Exploited Cisco SD-WAN Flaw to Plant Malware Built to Steal Encryption Keys
articles.text:
Hackers exploited a critical Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN flaw, fixed in February, to plant custom malware inside the systems that control an organization's SD-WAN network.
The malware, called KeyDrift, is designed to copy the keys that encrypt traffic between sites and store them for later use, Cisco Talos said on October 28. Talos calls the attacks historical but does not specify when they occurred or whether any keys were sent.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-20127 and has a CVSS score of 10.0. It allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass authentication and gain administrative privileges on these control systems. On a Controller, the attacker can log in as a high-privileged internal account that is not root.
When Cisco disclosed the flaw in February, Talos tracked its exploitation as UAT-8616, a cluster of activity it said went back to at least 2023.
In Cisco's traditional key exchange, each SD-WAN router periodically generates an AES key for its traffic and sends it to the Catalyst SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart). The Controller passes the keys on to other routers. A process on the Controller called vdaemon runs the encrypted control connections that carry these keys.
On a compromised Controller, a KeyDrift component called LittleFilch hooks into vdaemon and reads control messages after they are decrypted. For a preset list of edge routers, it pulls out their IP addresses and a 32-byte field. Talos assesses that field as the AES-256 key material that the Controller passes between routers.
LittleFilch encrypts what it collects with RSA and writes it to a file. It can then send that data over UDP to an address listed in a settings file, which it deletes after reading. Talos could not recover that settings file.
The group behind KeyDrift, which Talos tracks as UAT-11473, has targeted space and satellite services, defense and aerospace technology, and policy research.
The group's infrastructure "overlaps considerably" with Silent Train, Talos assesses with high confidence. Silent Train is the name Lumen's Black Lotus Labs uses for a network of hacked small-office, home-office, IoT and business devices.
Lumen says Volt Typhoon used the network to hide its activity. CISA, the NSA and the FBI said in 2024 that Volt Typhoon is a Chinese state-sponsored cyber group.
Talos links UAT-11473 to Volt Typhoon only through the infrastructure overlap. It does not say the two are the same group, or how UAT-11473 relates to UAT-8616, the cluster it reported in February.
Separately, Lumen said on October 28 that Volt Typhoon was exploiting CVE-2026-20127 by late 2025 and continued to exploit it after Cisco disclosed the flaw in February. Lumen does not tie that activity to KeyDrift.
KeyDrift primarily starts via modified runit scripts that Cisco SD-WAN devices use to launch their services, according to Talos. In one version, the script for the SSH service starts a loader script, conf_sshd, before the real SSH server. The conf_sshd script writes vdaemon's process IDs to a file, and a tool called rsshd injects KeyDrift's main module, PolyFlame, into each of those processes.
PolyFlame runs in memory inside vdaemon. It can act as a TinyShell-like backdoor that runs commands and reads and writes files, or as a relay that forwards commands between its command server and other machines. It is built to accept commands within SD-WAN control traffic, and the analyzed samples contained no hardcoded server address.
On a compromised Validator, formerly vBond, a fake aaamgr service under /etc/sv/aaamgr/ runs a packed loader, aaamgrd, that decrypts and runs PolyFlame. Cisco's real aaamgr component is a Python package and does not normally run as a compiled service.
There are also signs of timestomping: commands the group ran copied the timestamps and permissions of existing files onto its own files.
Affected Releases and Fixes
CVE-2026-20127 affects the Catalyst SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart), Manager (formerly vManage), and Validator (formerly vBond), regardless of their configuration. On-premises systems are affected, as are Cisco's hosted SD-WAN cloud deployments, including the Cisco Managed and FedRAMP environments. Cisco added the Validator to its advisory on June 16.
Cisco says it is aware of limited exploitation of the flaw. There is no workaround, and the first fixed releases are:
| Release train | First fixed release | 
|---|---|
| Earlier than 20.9 | Migrate to a fixed release | 
| 20.9 | 20.9.8.2 | 
| 20.11 | 20.12.6.1 | 
| 20.12 | 20.12.5.3 or 20.12.6.1 | 
| 20.13 | 20.15.4.2 | 
| 20.14 | 20.15.4.2 | 
| 20.15 | 20.15.4.2 | 
| 20.16 | 20.18.2.1 | 
| 20.18 | 20.18.2.1 | 
Releases earlier than 20.9 and the 20.11, 20.13, 20.14 and 20.16 trains have reached end of software maintenance.
Until they can upgrade, on-premises customers can limit access to ports 22 and 830 to the IP addresses of known controllers and other known systems. Cisco says this step worked in a test environment, but that customers should check how well it works in their own networks. Such guardrails are already in place for Cisco's hosted SD-WAN cloud deployments.
Blocking the ports does not remove malware already on a device.
Checking for KeyDrift
Talos advises organizations to install Cisco's fixes, follow Cisco's Catalyst SD-WAN hardening guide and watch for signs of post-compromise activity. Anyone who finds such signs should start incident response and can ask Cisco's Technical Assistance Center (TAC) for help.
That advice does not say whether upgrading removes KeyDrift from a device that was already compromised, or whether any keys should be replaced. Cisco's February remediation guide for this flaw warns that there could be "existing exploits which are still in place" from before an upgrade.
KeyDrift uses these files and locations, some given only by name:
- File: the run script under etc/sv/sshd/, modified to start conf_sshd
- Directory: /etc/sv/aaamgr/, a fake service on a compromised Validator
- File: aaamgrd, the packed loader
- File: conf_sshd, the loader script
- File: rsshd, the injector
- File: libdssl.so, PolyFlame
- File: libcommon.so, LittleFilch
- File: /tmp/system-vdaemon, the list of vdaemon process IDs
- File: /var/tmp/vdaemon.bin, LittleFilch's encrypted records
- File: /var/tmp/vdaemon.conf, LittleFilch's send settings, deleted after reading
Talos's report does not include a list of file hashes, IP addresses or domains for KeyDrift.
Talos released Snort rules on October 28 that look for inbound KeyDrift command-and-control connections: 67387 through 67416 for Snort 2, and 7:44 through 7:73 for Snort 3. Rules 65938 and 65958, already available, cover CVE-2026-20127 itself.
The October 28 rule update lists the Snort 2 rules as disabled by default, so users of the paid Snort Subscriber rule set must turn them on. The Snort 3 rules appear with no default state.
To check for exploitation of the flaw itself, Cisco says to look in /var/log/auth.log for Accepted publickey for vmanage-admin entries from unknown IP addresses. Before opening a TAC case, customers should run request admin-tech on each control component. The remediation guide also recommends rescanning those admin-tech files with the Check Bug Applicability feature on the Bug Search Tool page for bug CSCws52722.
For US federal civilian agencies, CISA's February 25 emergency directive sets out what to do if a root account compromise is found. They must report it to CISA, deploy fresh Manager, Controller and Validator instances from patched images, and move their edge routers to the new systems.

articles.title: PlayStation regala un juego de más de 40 dólares en PS Plus por tiempo limitado
articles.text:
PlayStation regala un juego de más de 40 dólares en PS Plus por tiempo limitado. Se trata de Dead Island 2, título con precio de referencia de 42 dólares que los suscriptores podrán sumar a su biblioteca a partir del 3 de noviembre de 2026, durante el período que dure la promoción mensual del servicio.
El juego llega como parte de la selección de títulos mensuales que PlayStation confirmó para noviembre y figura como uno de los atractivos principales de esa tanda. Estará disponible tanto para PlayStation 5 como para PlayStation 4, lo que amplía el alcance de la oferta entre los usuarios del servicio.
Cómo reclamar Dead Island 2 gratis en PS Plus
Los miembros de PlayStation Plus podrán reclamar Dead Island 2 desde el 3 de noviembre de este año y agregarlo de forma gratuita a su biblioteca mientras dure la promoción.
Pasado ese plazo, el título dejará de estar disponible para quienes no lo hayan reclamado a tiempo, por lo que la ventana de acceso es limitada.
Una vez incorporado a la cuenta, el juego podrá jugarse sin costo adicional mientras la suscripción al servicio se mantenga activa. Si la membresía se cancela, el acceso al título también se pierde, en línea con el funcionamiento habitual de los catálogos de PS Plus.
De qué trata Dead Island 2, el juego zombi de PS Plus
La historia transcurre en una versión de Los Ángeles devastada por un brote zombi. En ese escenario, los jugadores recorren distintos sectores de la ciudad, cumplen misiones y se enfrentan tanto a otros supervivientes como a criaturas mutadas.
La propuesta jugable combina elementos de rol con un sistema de combate cuerpo a cuerpo que habilita el uso de diferentes armas para enfrentar a las hordas de muertos vivientes.
Cabe señalar que la ambientación apuesta por la acción directa, con un tono marcado por el caos y el humor negro como sello distintivo de la experiencia.
Modo cooperativo: jugar en equipo en Dead Island 2
El videojuego Dead Island 2 ofrece la posibilidad de jugar en solitario o de formar equipos de hasta tres personas mediante su modo cooperativo online.
Esta función permite compartir la aventura con otros jugadores y enfrentar juntos los desafíos de Los Ángeles infestado de zombis, una alternativa pensada para quienes prefieren la experiencia en grupo antes que el recorrido individual por la ciudad devastada.
Dead Island: Definitive Edition: de qué trata la remasterización del clásico de zombis de Techland
Dead Island: Definitive Edition es la versión remasterizada del juego de rol y acción en primera persona desarrollado por Techland y distribuido por Deep Silver. El título original se lanzó en 2016 para PC, PlayStation 4 y Xbox One, y sitúa al jugador en Banoi, una isla tropical que pasa de ser un destino paradisíaco a un escenario infestado tras un apocalipsis zombi repentino.
La trama sigue a cuatro supervivientes inmunes al patógeno que provoca la infección. La propuesta combina la exploración de un mundo abierto con un sistema de progresión basado en árboles de habilidades, además de un combate cuerpo a cuerpo centrado en el desmembramiento, el desgaste físico de los personajes y la fabricación de armas personalizadas.
Esta edición remasterizada representó un salto técnico para el juego al migrarlo al motor gráfico Chrome Engine, el mismo utilizado en Dying Light. Ese cambio permitió incorporar modelados renovados, texturas de mayor resolución, un sistema de iluminación realista y una interfaz actualizada.
Más allá de las mejoras visuales y de rendimiento, Definitive Edition reúne la experiencia completa del juego al incluir todos los contenidos descargables lanzados con anterioridad, entre ellos la campaña Ryder White y la arena de supervivencia Bloodbath Arena. La edición conserva, además, el modo cooperativo en línea para hasta cuatro jugadores.

articles.title: SFR augmente ses tarifs : une nouvelle hausse qui va faire réagir
articles.text:
SFR est sur le point de disparaître. Mais ça n'empêche pas ses abonnements d'augmenter entretemps !
C'est le tube du moment. Les abonnements des forfaits dans les télécommunications augmentent un peu partout, que ce soit du côté des marques plutôt premier prix comme Sosh, que chez chez un opérateur comme Orange.Et SFR, dont le rachat par les trois autres opérateurs français est en cours, n'échappe pas au phénomène. Bien au contraire, comme on peut le voir avec cette nouvelle information !
Beaucoup d'abonnés SFR viennent de recevoir un mail indiquant une hausse de leur abonnement
La saison de l'inflation n'est pas terminée du côté de SFR. Car après RED by SFR, SFR augmente à son tour les prix, d'après des retours dans nos confrères de chez AlloForfait se font l'écho.
Et contrairement à ce qu'on a pu entendre chez d'autres opérateurs dernièrement, ici un certain nombre d'abonnés ont reçu un mail indiquant une hausse du tarif pouvant toucher autant un forfait mobile qu'un abonnement internet fixe. Et ça peut vite chiffrer quand un foyer est habitué de SFR.
Vous ne pouvez pas refuser… mais vous pouvez résilier !
Un client fait ainsi remarquer sur X qu'en deux mois, le foyer a pris 15 euros par mois en plus sur la facture, pour un box internet et trois forfaits mobiles - soit 180 euros en plus sur un an. Et, il faut le rappeler, il n'est pas possible de refuser une augmentation tarifaire de ce genre.
Le seul recours de l'abonné ici est de résilier le ou les abonnements. Il est permis de quitter ainsi un contrat dans cette situation pendant 4 mois à partir de la réception de l'annonce - et ce, sans frais ni pénalité. Une résiliation qui peut se faire par le courrier traditionnel, ou bien directement en ligne. Et vous, vous avez reçu une (mauvaise) nouvelle vous faisant état d'une telle hausse de tarif ?
Source : AlloForfait

articles.title: Getac says its new rugged notebooks offer faster AI-powered processing than ever — and seem to be targeting military and defense customers
articles.text:
Getac says its new rugged notebooks offer faster AI-powered processing than ever — and seem to be targeting military and defense customers
Panther Lake, Copilot+ and an Nvidia Blackwell option
- Getac's B360X and B360X Pro are bringing Intel Panther Lake chips, 14-inch 1,400-nit screens, and Wi-Fi 7 to its rugged B360 line
- The 180 TOPS headline only applies to the B360X with a Core Ultra X7, a chip Getac doesn't offer in the defense-focused Pro
- The Pro's integrated AI rating is about 98 TOPS, in line with last year's model, leaving an optional Nvidia RTX PRO 500 as its main AI upgrade
Getac has unveiled the B360X and B360X Pro, a pair of fully rugged 14-inch notebooks built around Intel's Core Ultra Series 3 "Panther Lake" processors and pitched at people who need to run AI workloads far from a reliable connection.
The Taiwanese company says the new machines deliver up to 180 TOPS of AI compute with both models due in November 2026 and no pricing announced.
Getac isn't subtle about who the Pro is for. Its product page calls it "purpose-built for defense and military professionals" and lists defense as its only industry, while the B360X is pitched at public safety, utilities, and industrial manufacturing. Our 2023 review noted that the B360 Pro is "sold as military-grade and mission-ready, out of the box," and that still seems true in 2026.
What has grown is the breadth of the push. In March, Getac launched CommandCore, a rugged drone ground control station that it pitches to "Army aviation and integrated air defense systems." Rivals are chasing the same customers, with Durabook's triple-screen Z14I-DX3 aimed at command posts and drone teams.
Plenty of upgrades under the hood even as focus remains centric to AI
Both notebooks replace the outgoing B360 and B360 Pro's 13.3-inch 1080p panel with a 14-inch, 1920 x 1200 LumiBond display rated at 1,400 nits, plus a touchscreen that Getac says works with compatible gloves or in the rain.
According to Getac's B360X spec sheet, the larger screen fits in the same 342 x 281mm footprint as the 13.3-inch models, with a slightly slimmer chassis and a 2.38kg weight.
Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 are standard, with 4G LTE, 5G Sub-6, and a dedicated L1/L5 GPS module optional, alongside up to two Thunderbolt 4 ports, a smart card reader, TPM 2.0, a 5MP Windows Hello camera, and an optional second SSD for up to 4TB in total. The usual rugged credentials are included: MIL-STD-810H, MIL-STD-461G, and IP66 ratings; a 6ft (1.8m) drop rating while operating; and optional salt fog certification.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Intel calls the 180 TOPS figure platform TOPS, which adds the NPU, integrated graphics, and CPU together. Only Panther Lake's "X" chips reach it because only they carry the 12-core Arc B390 graphics, which accounts for 122 TOPS on its own, plus a 50 TOPS NPU, according to Intel's figures.
Getac offers exactly one such chip, the Core Ultra X7 358H, and its own footnotes confirm it is only available on the B360X. The B360X Pro tops out at the Core Ultra 7 356H and 366H, which use a four-core graphics version, and the 356H is rated at 98 TOPS on the same measure.
That is essentially level with last year's hardware. The Core Ultra 7 255H offered in Getac's 2025 B360 range is rated at 96 TOPS, so on Intel's own yardstick, the defense-focused model's integrated AI budget has barely moved.
A lot of AI muscle on offer
What has changed is where those TOPS live. The NPU jumps from 13 TOPS on the older Arrow Lake H chips to as much as 50 TOPS, clearing the 40 TOPS bar Microsoft set for Copilot+ PCs, and Getac now lists both models under that banner on its website. That matters to the target audience and the need to know it is achievable on battery, since NPUs are built around sustained, low-power inference.
Even that isn't new for the family. Getac billed its Lunar Lake-based B360 Plus as the first fully rugged Copilot+ PC when it launched in June 2025, with a 48 TOPS NPU, and the Core Ultra 7 258V it offers is rated at around 115 platform TOPS. When we covered that machine, we warned that the practical benefits "may not be as clear-cut as the branding suggests," and things have since come full circle.
Microsoft has also cooled on the NPU push. As PCWorld pointed out in January 2026, few applications make use of NPUs, and Windows' newer AI tooling lets developers run inference on GPUs and CPUs as well. Getac's generational AI claims hold up for the top B360X configuration, and for NPU-bound work across the range. For the Pro, they are a stretch.
Getac hasn't explained why it reserves the X7 for the B360X, but Intel's platform rules likely explain it. The X-series models seem locked to LPDDR5x memory, and Notebookcheck's spec comparison shows the X7 358H exposes 12 PCIe lanes, versus 20 on the Core Ultra 7 356H. A machine built around a discrete GPU option and an expansion bay needs those lanes more than it needs a bigger iGPU. This means Getac's stated specs might need a small tweak to note that the B360X also comes in an LPDDR5X-touting trim, since it makes no mention of any memory but "DDR5" so far.
The B360X Pro takes a different route, offering an optional RTX PRO 500 Blackwell with 6GB of GDDR7. Getac's release frames it as a graphics upgrade, but this is where the Pro's real AI headroom sits.
Nvidia rates the RTX PRO 500 at 294 AI TOPS, but its own RTX PRO line card carries a crucial footnote: "NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs are based on FP4 AI TOPS with sparsity." Intel quotes 8-bit integer (INT8) operations without that sparsity assumption, so the two numbers can't be compared directly.
For context, the RTX 5090's headline 3,352 AI TOPS corresponds to 838 INT8 TOPS without sparsity, a four-to-one ratio. Applying the same ratio to the RTX PRO 500 puts it at roughly 74 dense INT8 TOPS, below the 122 TOPS Intel claims for the X7's integrated graphics.
That doesn't make the B360X the better AI machine for every job. The Nvidia card brings 288GB/s of dedicated memory bandwidth, native FP4 support, and CUDA, still the default target for much AI software, although 6GB of VRAM limits the size of the model it can hold. Getac hasn't published benchmarks for either configuration.
Via TechPowerUp

Having built hundreds of gaming PCs and being an avid gamer in his spare time, Rahim tends to have stronger opinions about hardware than most. This is particularly on display when he gets his way with powerful, but minimalistic RGB builds even as Small Form Factor (SFF) PCs come a close second.

articles.title: Ubisoft Has No Other Assassin's Creed Remakes in the Works After Black Flag Resynced
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
Ubisoft Has No Other Assassin's Creed Remakes in the Works After Black Flag Resynced
Ubisoft says it currently has no other Assassin's Creed remake in active development, according to its Fall 2026 franchise update. Black Flag Resynced, which launched on July 9, was the series' first-ever remake, and Ubisoft called rebuilding its old systems from scratch "a massive undertaking." The game has reportedly done well, and it just received its final major content update, so plenty of fans were probably hoping for another nostalgia trip. Rumors were circulating about an Assassin's Creed 1 remake, but it looks like Ubisoft won't be going down that route just yet. Instead, Ubisoft says its teams are focused on the next Assassin's Creed titles, including unannounced projects with new settings and stories. The company isn't ruling out remakes for good, though, and says it will keep exploring ways to bring older games back.
Codename Hexe, the darker Assassin's Creed project, is apparently making "steady progress," but its next major update won't come until 2027. Ubisoft didn't give a release window, although an insider claimed back in July that Hexe won't launch before the second half of 2027. The Hexe section of the post also ends with a line of scrambled, coded text that fans will probably try to decode. The multiplayer project, Codename Invictus, is being reworked too, after hundreds of players tried an early prototype in a private Insiders Session. They liked the return of PvP, the parkour, and playing as different Assassin's Creed characters, but asked for more of the series' core pillars.Meanwhile, Assassin's Creed Valhalla, which recently passed 40 million players, is finally getting New Game+ on November 5. The update also brings an optional progression mode, new runes, a stash system, a new upgrade resource called Mithril, and a Master Assassin outfit inspired by Naoe from Shadows. Ubisoft says player feedback on it could lead to similar updates for other games in the series. On the TV side, production of Netflix's live-action Assassin's Creed series is nearing completion in Rome, with composer Hannah Peel scoring it, though there's still no release date. Assassin's Creed turns 20 in 2027, and Ubisoft is planning a year of reveals, updates, and rewards to mark the anniversary.

articles.title: Black Friday 2026 – L'aspirateur balai Dyson V8 Cyclone à 249,00 € (-17%)
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 – L'aspirateur balai Dyson V8 Cyclone à 249,00 € (-17%)
L'aspirateur balai Dyson V8 Cyclone passe sous les 250 € chez Boulanger.com soit une baisse d'environ 17% sur le prix habituellement constaté.
L'innovation peut-elle se nicher dans la réinterprétation ? Ce qui apparaît comme un sujet de bac de philo trouvera peut-être une réponse après notre test du Dyson V8 Cyclone, la vision 2025 d'un aspirateur-balai sorti en 2016.
Dyson V8 Cyclone

Points forts
- Belles performances d'aspiration.
- Entretien facile.
- Relativement discret, aussi bien visuellement qu'acoustiquement.
Points faibles
- Autonomie trop faible à la puissance turbo.
- Extraction de la brosse pénible.
- Manque d'astuces pratiques (pas d'indicateur d'autonomie, de rampe de leds…).
Dans les grandes lignes, le Dyson V8 Cyclone reste le même que le V8 “normal”. Pour le meilleur et pour le pire, serait-on tenté d'ajouter. Certes, il existe quelques menues différences au niveau de la prise en main, une amélioration de la gestion du bruit, et on ne peut que féliciter Dyson d'avoir enfin pris le virage de la batterie amovible. On regrette d'autant plus que cet aspirateur-balai n'ait pas pris celui de l'indicateur d'autonomie précis, ou encore de la rampe de leds sur la tête d'aspiration. Ceci étant, malgré une durée de vie en mode turbo famélique, le V8 Cyclone est un modèle efficace et très simple à entretenir.

articles.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploited VMware ESX Zero-Day to Reduce Audit Trail Visibility
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Wednesday added a security flaw impacting Broadcom VMware ESX to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, after CrowdStrike revealed that it had been weaponized by a China-nexus threat actor known as Warp Panda in attacks targeting the U.S. legal sector.
The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-41709 (CVSS score: 2.7), an a case of insufficient logging that could permit permit a malicious actor with admin access to perform certain operations without being logged.
In an advisory released in July 2026, Broadcom revealed that the issue was addressed in the following versions -
- VMware Cloud Foundation SXi-9.1.0.0-25370933 and ESXi-9.0.2.0100-25595025
- VMware vSphere Foundation SXi-9.1.0.0-25370933 and ESXi-9.0.2.0100-25595025
- VMware ESX ESXi80U3j-25429389
- VMware Cloud Foundation 5.2.4
- VMware Telco Cloud Platform ESXi80U3j-25429389
The development comes in response to CrowdStrike's 2026 Legal Threat Landscape Report, which revealed that Warp Panda had exploited CVE-2026-41709 as a zero-day in early 2026 with an aim to reduce audit trail visibility.
Warp Panda "exploits internet-facing edge devices using zero-day vulnerabilities and custom malware to maintain covert, persistent access," it said in the report shared with The Hacker News, adding the adversary "actively circumvents detection by bypassing audit logging, harvesting cloud session tokens, and registering rogue multi-factor authentication (MFA) devices."
The threat actor, also tracked as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221), Clay Typhoon, and VerdantBamboo, has a storied history of weaponizing zero-day vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler and Ivanti Connect Secure devices.
Earlier this month, Google-owned Mandiant also attributed the hacking crew to the zero-day exploitation of a critical improper origin validation flaw in BeyondTrust Remote Support (CVE-2026-102764, CVSS score: 9.3) to deliver malware families like SAWFLY and BARECLAW.
Attacks mounted by Warp Panda involve the exploitation of internet-facing edge devices to obtain initial access, after which the threat actor pivots to VMware vCenter environments to deploy custom malware like BRICKSTORM and SharpStorm to maintain persistent access without attracting attention.
Select intrusions have also involved the targeting of cloud services with an aim to extract user session tokens to access Microsoft 365 environments sans raising any credential-based alerts. In at least one case, Warp Panda is said to have registered a new MFA device on a compromised account as a way to set up persistent access even if the password is changed.
"Warp Panda represents a sustained and strategically focused China-nexus cyber espionage threat to U.S. entities across multiple sectors, including the legal sector," CrowdStrike said.
"The legal sector's concentration of client communications, merger and acquisition materials, active litigation strategy, and cross-client access makes it a high-value collection target for a state-directed adversary seeking intelligence with downstream operational utility."
In light of active exploitation of CVE-2026-41709, Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies are recommended to apply the fixes by November 11, 2026.

articles.title: Instagram habría pagado hasta USD 500.000 a influenciadores para competir con YouTube con videos largos
articles.text:
Instagram habría propuesto acuerdos de hasta USD 500.000 a algunos influenciadores para que publiquen contenidos extensos en Features, una función en pruebas que permitiría subir videos horizontales de hasta 90 minutos.
Ciertos creadores habrían recibido ofertas de USD 50.000, mientras que otras alcanzarían cifras de seis dígitos, según Business Insider, que atribuyó los datos a fuentes con conocimiento de los acuerdos.
“Hemos hecho público que estamos financiando contenido destacado directamente con algunos creadores para apoyarlos”, dijo un vocero de Meta al medio. “Los detalles de esos acuerdos son confidenciales, pero nos entusiasma ver el contenido publicado”, agregó.
Los acuerdos con los influenciadores no serían exclusivos
Los convenios, de acuerdo con el medio, no obligarían a los creadores a abandonar otras plataformas. Una de las fuentes consultadas sostuvo que Instagram les habría pedido publicar el mismo día en Features los videos de larga duración que suban a YouTube.
La plataforma de videos de Google conserva una presencia relevante entre quienes producen entrevistas, podcast, documentales y programas de mayor duración. Instagram, por su parte, se concentró durante los últimos años en los Reels y los formatos breves.
Adam Mosseri sobre la monetización de videos largos en Instagram
Adam Mosseri, director de Instagram, afirmó que la herramienta todavía no fue lanzada de forma completa. En una publicación en Threads realizada el mismo día que se anunció la función, señaló que el acceso se ampliará de manera gradual mientras la compañía recibe opiniones de los creadores incluidos en la prueba.
“Entendemos que la economía es muy importante, y estamos explorando múltiples opciones para ayudar a los creadores de videos de formato largo a recibir pago”, escribió Mosseri.
La declaración confirma que Instagram evalúa fórmulas de monetización, aunque no precisa cuáles serían, cuándo entrarían en vigor ni quiénes podrían acceder a ellas.
Instagram intentaría conectar los Reels con producciones más extensas
La plataforma también probaría herramientas para recortar videos largos y convertir sus fragmentos en Reels. Esos clips podrían dirigir al público hacia la producción completa sin que tenga que salir de Instagram.
La compañía ya había utilizado incentivos económicos para atraer contenido a sus aplicaciones.
En 2021, durante la etapa de IGTV, financió producciones episódicas de algunos creadores. Meta también implementó programas de bonificaciones por el desempeño de Reels, aunque varios de ellos perdieron alcance con el tiempo.
Mientras Features continúa en fase de prueba, Instagram no anunció una fecha para su disponibilidad general ni un sistema permanente de reparto de ingresos para los videos de larga duración.
Qué dice el director de Instagram sobre la IA
Adam Mosseri, director de Instagram, afirmó que el rechazo y la preocupación por la inteligencia artificial crecerán durante los próximos años, en especial entre artistas y creadores. En una entrevista en el podcast Colin y Samir, sostuvo que muchas personas temen perder oportunidades laborales o quedar rezagadas por la rápida expansión de estas herramientas.
El ejecutivo señaló que las inquietudes abarcan el uso de obras originales para entrenar modelos, la propiedad intelectual, el manejo de datos personales y la posible automatización de empleos.
Según su mirada, el malestar no se limita a quienes trabajan en áreas creativas, ya que también alcanza a ingenieros, matemáticos y otros sectores vinculados a la tecnología.
Mosseri reconoció que una parte de ese temor tiene fundamentos y anticipó un escenario de mayor frustración.
Por ello, planteó que la inteligencia artificial debería ampliar las capacidades de las personas, en lugar de generar la sensación de que la tecnología las desplaza sin ofrecerles beneficios. En el caso de Instagram, dijo que el objetivo sería dar más herramientas a los creadores.
La plataforma actualizó en agosto de 2026 las etiquetas para identificar perfiles creados con inteligencia artificial.
La decisión buscó diferenciar esas cuentas de las administradas por personas, aunque Mosseri admitió que esta tarea será más difícil a medida que mejoren los sistemas capaces de generar imágenes, videos y textos.

articles.title: Le modèle français Mistral Large 4 passe en open source et rivalise avec les meilleurs modèles chinois en code
articles.text:
Trois semaines après sa préversion, Mistral a publié jeudi les poids de Mistral Large 4. Le modèle d'IA open source français revendique la première place mondiale des modèles ouverts en code agentique et mise clairement sur la cyberdéfense.
Beaucoup attendaient ce jour, voilà que Mistral a publié les poids de Mistral Large 4, son modèle d'IA ouvert de 1 000 milliards de paramètres, téléchargeable par tous sur Hugging Face depuis ce jeudi 29 octobre 2026. Depuis la grande annonce et la préversion du 6 octobre et ce lancement, le « Chonk » a rempilé pour trois semaines d'entraînement supplémentaire, et c'est en programmation que la différence se voit le plus. En cyberdéfense, le bulletin réclame une lecture plus attentive, ce qui n'a pas dissuadé Microsoft, Orange Cyberdefense ou l'agence européenne de cybersécurité de se pencher sur son cas.
Le modèle d’IA le plus massif de Mistral est désormais téléchargeable par tous
Que le petit chat orange choisi comme emblème ne trompe personne. Mistral Large 4, dit ML4, n'est pas un poids plume. Déjà, il aligne 1 000 milliards de paramètres. Les paramètres, ce sont des réglages ajustés pendant l'entraînement, qui façonnent chacune des réponses du modèle. Publier les « poids », cela revient à livrer la valeur de tous ces réglages. Chacun peut alors installer le modèle sur ses propres machines, l'examiner ou le retoucher. Petite astuce de conception, ML4 n'en sollicite que 52 milliards à la fois, seule une fraction du réseau se met au travail à chaque requête. La facture de calcul s'en trouve allégée, sans que la carrure en pâtisse. Il est multimodal de façon native, et comprend aussi bien le texte que l'image.
Depuis le 6 octobre, ML4 a pu faire ses classes sur le terrain. Des clients en accès anticipé et des partenaires spécialisés en cybersécurité l'ont mis à l'épreuve, pendant que Mistral prolongeait son apprentissage par renforcement, afin de récompenser les bonnes réponses pour polir le comportement du modèle. Trois modes de raisonnement sont au menu, comme on en a l'habitude avec d'autres outils, à savoir bas, moyen et élevé. On dose ainsi l'effort selon qu'on corrige une coquille ou qu'on s'attaque à un problème un peu poilu.
Le vice-président science de Mistral, Pierre Stock, salue la démonstration d'une équipe capable d'« innover vite ». Il est vrai qu'en moins de trois semaines, dans la même session d'entraînement, deux modes de raisonnement supplémentaires ont été ajoutés à partir des retours clients. Le modèle est aussi devenu plus efficace, aussi plus personnalisable. Les gains seraient « substantiels », selon Mistral, sans « aucun signe de saturation ». Le « Chonk », surnom donné à Mistral Large 4, n'a peut-être pas fini de prendre du muscle.
En programmation, Mistral Large 4 coiffe GLM-5.3 d'un cheveu
Le code, c'est justement là que la cure porte ses fruits. Pour le mesurer, Mistral s’appuie d'ailleurs sur Terminal-Bench 4.0, un banc d'essai qui lâche l'IA dans un terminal, la fenêtre un brin austère où les développeurs pilotent un ordinateur à coups de commandes tapées au clavier. Concrètement, l'IA y travaille sans aide humaine. Elle tape ses commandes, lit les réponses de la machine, repère ses erreurs et corrige le tir jusqu'à boucler la tâche. Les missions touchent au développement logiciel, à la sécurité, à l'apprentissage automatique ou encore au matériel, et le score indique simplement la proportion de missions réussies. La préversion d’octobre en bouclait 28 %, la version publiée aujourd’hui en réussit 41 %. Il y a un petit bémol de méthode, tout de même, car le premier chiffre a été annoncé par Mistral, qui a fait passer le test lui-même. Le second provient d'Artificial Analysis, un organisme indépendant qui soumet de nombreux modèles à ces épreuves. Les conditions de test pouvant varier d'un examinateur à l'autre, mieux vaut manier la comparaison avec prudence.
Ce résultat place ML4 un point devant le chinois GLM-5.3 (40 %), et loin devant DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (31 %) ou Kimi K3 (21 %). Sur l'indice de code global d'Artificial Analysis, Mistral revendique même le titre de meilleur modèle ouvert au monde en code agentique, c'est-à-dire capable d'enchaîner seul les étapes d'un projet de développement. Sur Terminal-Bench, son communiqué parle en revanche d'égalité avec GLM-5.3. Quant à la précision de « meilleur modèle ouvert conçu en Occident », elle en dit long. La concurrence la plus rude se trouve actuellement en Chine, chez GLM-5.3, Kimi K3 ou DeepSeek.
Le véritable atout du Chonk, c'est la sobriété. Sur le même indice, ML4 rivalise avec GLM-5.3 en consommant en moyenne 47 % de tokens en moins par tâche. Ces fragments de mots servent d'unité de facturation aux fournisseurs d'IA, alors même que leur prix augmentait, souligne Mistral. Les secteurs régulés, qui tiennent à garder leur code à l'abri, peuvent en prime faire tourner le modèle chez eux. L'éditeur voit aussi ses clients s'en servir en finance, pour digérer tableurs complexes et rapports financiers. Dans l'industrie, il pourrait convertir un plan 2D en modèle 3D dans un logiciel de CAO.
Cyberdéfense et souveraineté, l'autre pari de Mistral Large 4
Puis il y a le volet ô combien important de la cyberdéfense. Mistral promet aux entreprises et aux États un outil capable de détecter, d'analyser et de contrer des menaces dans le code et les infrastructures informatiques. Hébergé chez eux, il ne pourra être ni restreint, ni désactivé par un tiers. Sur CyberGym-E2E, le modèle doit débusquer de vraies failles de sécurité mémoire dans des logiciels libres écrits en C et C++, les reproduire, puis les corriger sans rien casser. ML4 y obtient 79 %, à égalité avec MiMo-V2.6-Pro et juste devant DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (76 %). GLM-5.3, son rival du code, s'écroule à 29 %. Lors de la préversion, Mistral affichait 82 sur CyberGym, mais on se demande si les deux mesures sont strictement comparables.
La liste des partenaires fournie par Mistral, elle en tout cas assez impressionnante. Microsoft devient le premier fournisseur cloud à proposer ML4, depuis sa plateforme Foundry. Lors de ses tests internes, Booz Allen Hamilton a vu le modèle égaler d'autres IA de pointe dans la détection de vulnérabilités, avec une « courbe de coûts convaincante ». L'ENISA, l'agence européenne de cybersécurité, le teste pour auditer du code et analyser des journaux de sécurité. L'Agence spatiale européenne (ESA) compte bâtir dessus des outils pour ses données d'observation de la Terre, terrain où ML4 doit permettre de repérer un feu de forêt ou de surveiller des lignes électriques sur des images satellite.
Orange Cyberdefense, Crédit Agricole, CrowdStrike et le néerlandais ASML, maître des machines à graver les puces sur le Vieux continent, figurent aussi parmi les soutiens affichés. Orange Cyberdefense a par exemple expliqué, ce jeudi après-midi, s'en servir pour la conception de services de sécurité managés.
Le tout a été entraîné sur 3 800 puces NVIDIA Grace Blackwell, parmi les plus puissantes du marché pour l'IA, dans les centres de données européens de Mistral. Selon la start-up, il lui a fallu pour cela une fraction de la puissance de calcul et des capitaux engagés par les laboratoires fermés, ceux qui gardent leurs modèles sous clé. Arthur Mensch, son patron, juge l'open source « essentiel » pour éviter que l'IA de pointe ne finisse « concentrée entre les mains de quelques acteurs ». Il rappelle que d'autres ont levé « des centaines de milliards » de dollars, quand Mistral en a réuni environ 6 en trois ans. Les poids de ML4 sont désormais en ligne sur Hugging Face, la plateforme de référence pour le partage de modèles d'IA. Les développeurs peuvent aussi l'intégrer à leurs services via l'API de Mistral, et certains utilisateurs de Vibe, l'assistant de Mistral anciennement baptisé Le Chat, y ont déjà accès. Après Voxtral 3, une famille de modèles et d'agents vocaux, d'autres modèles de cette nouvelle génération sont promis dans les mois à venir.

articles.title: 'A calm and sensible aesthetic is preferable to an overwrought and wilful one, but I'm concerned that for the PD5, Astell & Kern may have bypassed its industrial design team altogether': the DAP's sound is without question the best at the level, but I can't help missing A&K's visual design flourishes
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
It’s not cheap (despite what Astell & Kern would have you believe) but in terms of sound quality the PD5 is worth every penny. Pair it with similarly capable headphones, concentrate on the sound rather than the look or the feel, and ignore its (very) occasionally glitchy operation, and it’s a really rewarding device.
Reasons to buy
- + Staggeringly clean, open and revealing sound
- + Thoroughly specified
- + Plenty of scope for user influence
Reasons to avoid
- - Some operational quirks
- - Looks and feels less premium than the price demands
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Astell & Kern PD5: Two-minute review
It’s been a long time since Astell & Kern has had a genuinely affordable digital audio player in its line-up, and the launch of the PD5 does nothing to change that.
It’s been a while since the company had anything as visually unremarkable as this in its catalog, too — but try not to get hung up on the perceived value and instead concentrate on the priceless nature of its sound quality.
And besides, a considerable amount of money put Astell & Kern’s way for a PD5 may not buy you much in the way of design or tactility but it gets you an extremely thoroughly specified device. Eight Cirrus Logic DACs? 20-point EQ adjustment? Balanced and unbalanced headphone outputs? The ability to work as a desktop DAC? Enough power to get a tune out even the most uncooperative headphones? The PD5 has all of this, and more — and it’s all in the service of audio performance that’s as good as any portable device at anything like this price point.
When it comes to clarity, to detail retrieval and to outright fidelity, the PD5 is extremely hard to criticise and yes, it fully emphatically deserves a place in our best MP3 players guide. And its talents don’t stop there, not even close — its sound is punchily robust, effortlessly dynamic, brilliantly controlled and organised, and thoroughly engaging. If you take your portable listening experience seriously (or your desktop listening experience for that matter — the PD5 is also an excellent USB DAC), this Astell & Kern absolutely demands your attention.
Away from audio quality the PD5 isn’t perfect; there are rare occasions on which it can be glitchy in operation, its on-screen menus are approaching ‘miniscule’, and it neither looks nor feels quite as expensive as it actually is. All of this, though, is made to seem fairly trivial by the way the PD5 performs its primary function.
Astell & Kern PD5 review: Price and release date
- Priced $1,049 / £899 / AU$1,349
- Announced in August 2026; released in September 2026
The Astell & Kern PD5 digital audio player is on sale now, and in the United Kingdom it costs £899. In the United States it will set you back $1,049, while in Australia it goes for AU$1,349.
Anyone familiar with such devices knows that for an A&K player, that's actually not so expensive — again, note my 'for an A&K player' wording there. This company's flagship DAPs go for $3,999 / £3,799 / AU$6,599 (Astell & Kern A&ultima SP4000 and its newer T-suffixed sibling, I'm looking at you), but you can also get a hi-res player from A&K's sub-brand — called the Activo P1 — for $430 / £399 (around AU$869).
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
There are crucial differences in the specifications which I'll go into, but it's good to have an idea of the market at least, when looking at such a fee and being told by its makers that it is "entry level".
Astell & Kern PD5 review: Features
- Eight (count ‘em!) Cirrus Logic CS43198 DACs
- Balanced and unbalanced headphone outputs
- Bluetooth 5.3 with aptX HD support
The PD5 isn’t the first Astell & Kern product that’s been so thoroughly specified that discussing every one of its features in any kind of depth might take up most of your day. So let’s say right from the off that no eventuality has been overlooked where the PD5 is concerned, and then let’s deal with the headlines and then try not to get too bogged down in all the rest of it…
Never knowingly understated, Astell & Kern has fitted eight Cirrus Logic CS43198 DAC chipsets here. The user interface gives you the option of listening using four, or all eight — listening in octa-mode offers optimal sound quality, but eats into battery life quite badly (engage all eight DACs and you’re looking at 15 hours of playback as opposed to the 28 or so you should get when listening to ‘just’ four). Taking the battery from ‘flat’ to ‘full’ takes around two-and-a-half hours.
In terms of feeding digital audio content to that considerable digital-to-analog conversion line-up, you have a few options. The bare-bones Android user interface Astell & Kern has deployed here, along with dual-band wi-fi, allows you to download the app of your favourite music streaming service(s), and 64GB of internal memory allows you to store some content to the PD5’s local storage. There’s a microSD card slot on the bottom of the frame (next to the USB-C slot that’s used for data transfer and for battery charging) too — it can accept cards of up to 1.5TB, which should prove adequate for all the hi-res content you might desire.
The player can deal with resolutions of up to 32bit/384kHz PCM and DSD256, and is Roon Ready as well as featuring full-on Qobuz Connect integration. Or you might decide to bypass the fancy-pants D-to-A circuitry altogether and use Bluetooth to drive a pair of wireless headphones (although it does seem a bit of a weird idea to spend £899 on a player in order to use it like a smartphone).
The PD5 features Bluetooth 5.3 with codec support up to and including aptX HD. It also has two headphone outputs: an unbalanced 3.5mm socket and a balanced 4.4mm alternative that’s compatible with five-pole jacks. Use the 4.4mm output, select octa-DAC mode, and the Astell & Kern can summon a mammoth 8Vrms of power — so even the most demanding headphones will have to do as they are told. But there are quite a few ways in which the sound can be affected, both by the device and by the person using it, before it reaches these outputs.
The ‘EnviroTune’ feature uses a mic integrated into the top edge of the PD5 to analyse ambient noise in real time and correct those frequencies affected by it without just making everything louder. The ‘Teraton Alpha’ audio engine that’s familiar from some of Astell & Kern’s uber-pricey DAPs minimises noise from the power supply and creates amplification that’s as stable and distortion-free as possible. And ‘Enhanced Signal Alignment’ technology synchronises outgoing signals in an effort to negate phase distortion and deliver the most coherent sonic image possible.
The end user, meanwhile, gets a choice of digital filters and some quite in-depth EQ adjustment to look into. The default filter is ‘low latency fast’, and it is as distinct in its effect as ‘low latency slow’, ‘phase compensated fast’ and ‘phase compensated slow’ are from each other. A ten-band EQ offers fairly granular adjustment of the sound, and an ‘advanced’ EQ interface allows frequency response to be defined using a graph with 20 (!) plotting points.
The PD5 will function as a desktop too, thanks to its USB-C slot’s ability with data transfer. Simply make a hard connection to, say, your laptop, select ‘DAC input’ in the ‘USB Mode’ sub-menu, and the Astell & Kern automatically switches on octa-DAC mode in order to give your computer a proper go at sounding decent for once.
Features score: 5 / 5
Astell & Kern PD5 review: Sound quality
- Clarity, detail and dynamism in equal measure
- Organised and fully resolved sound
- Well-controlled punch and drive
The Astell & Kern PD5 is an admirably unpicky device, although obviously there are limits. Give it the sort of standard content available on a proper music streaming service (which means a CD-quality resolution of 16bit/44.1kHz) and it does an admirable job of maximising the information available to it. Step down from there, though, to the sort of squashed nonsense served up by Apple Music or Spotify, and the PD5 struggles to conceal its disdain. But you didn’t spend proper money to listen to compressed poverty-spec streams, did you?
So a 16bit/44.1kHz stream of Hood’s Western Housing Concerns is delivered in tremendous fashion. The presentation is open and spacious, with an expansive soundstage on which each element of the recording gets ample room in which to stretch out and express itself. The layout is rigorously observed, and the PD5’s powers or organisation mean the stage is locked in place and completely convincing.
Tonality is absolutely neutral, the player offering neither heat nor chill to the colour of the recording. There’s excellent clarity to the presentation, a really dark and quiet background in front of which the band perform — and at every stage of the frequency range, there’s absolutely fanatical attention to detail. No matter how minor an occurrence, how far back in the mix, or how fleeting, the Astell & Kern will seize upon it and give it precisely the amount of weight and emphasis it requires.
Frequency response is similarly even-handed, and similarly convincing as a result. A switch to a DSD64 file of Michael Jackson’s Don’t Stop ‘Til You Get Enough reveals deep, textured, tremendously varied and thrillingly solid low-frequency response, and bass is controlled to the point that rhythmic expression is never less than positive and confident. Midrange resolution is no less accomplished, with the singer’s mic technique made every bit as apparent as his tone and timbre. The top of the frequency range strikes a lovely balance between substance and brilliance, and again there’s an absolutely stack of information available. The PD5 doesn’t over- or underemphasise any part of the frequency range, and as a result this glossy, audibly expensive recording sounds as natural and polished as it ever did.
Dynamic headroom is considerable when it’s time to describe big variations in volume or intensity or attack, and the more subtle dynamics of harmonic variation and transient response are never overlooked. The entire presentation hangs together seamlessly, the Astell & Kern offering a proper sense of unity and singularity to recordings of every type.
And perhaps best of all, there’s nothing show-y or even especially analytical about the way the PD5 goes about things. As far as insight into a recording goes it’s basically untouchable at the money, but that’s not what defines the Astell & Kern. It’s the energy of its sound, the engaged and engaging nature of its performance, that makes it as entertaining a listen as you’ll get from a portable device costing less than four figures.
Sound quality score: 5 / 5
Astell & Kern PD5 review: Design
- 120 x 70 x 16mm (HxWxD)
- 4.1in touchscreen display
- 198g
There’s absolutely nothing wrong with the Astell & Kern PD5 as a physical object, let me make that clear from the off. The dimensions are nicely palm-sized, the weight is sufficient to make it feel like a premium product without being a burden to a jacket pocket, and the standard of fit and finish is impeccable.
And I’m not about to pretend I miss the painfully pointy edges of some previous Astell & Kern models, either — the PD5 is a much friendlier proposition in this respect — nor the painfully self-conscious offset screen of the old SR35. But there’s nothing remarkable about the design of the PD5, nothing to set it apart from the pack of products competing with it for your hard-earned. Even the volume dial, previously a little Astell & Kern design flourish, is unremarkable here.
I realise I can’t have it all ways, and a calm and sensible aesthetic is preferable to something overwrought and wilful. But I find myself slightly concerned that for the PD5, Astell & Kern may have bypassed its industrial design team altogether…
Design score: 4.5 / 5
Astell & Kern PD5 review: Usability and setup
- Bright, rather reflective screen
- In-depth menus
- Occasional operational oddities
As mentioned, the PD5 uses a stripped-back version of Android as its user interface — and it’s all the better for it. Too many digital audio players pointlessly include a lot of your smartphone’s functionality for no reason, as far as I can tell, other than to eat into the machine’s local memory.
The 4.1in touchscreen is bright, although rather more reflective than is ideal, and it’s responsive without being on a hair trigger. The Astell & Kern’s menus are extensive, and as a result the font size is really very small — but squint and you should be able to make out what’s what (even if the occasional use of ‘red on black’ for text is a terrible idea).
Setting up the PD5 to your satisfaction isn’t the work of a moment. But when you finally get finished you can at least be sure you have a digital audio player that’s primed to do exactly what you want, and in the manner you want it.
There are occasional glitches in operation, though — or, at least, that’s my experience. I install the Tidal music streaming app, and also insert a microSD card full of hi-res content. But every now and then, both sources will play at the same time. Pressing ‘play’ on a Tidal file usually stops playback from the local storage and vice versa — but not always, which is a weird one and no mistake.
Usability and setup score: 3.5 / 5
Astell & Kern PD5 review: Value
Because the majority of the money you’ve spent on a PD5 has gone on the internals, it’s difficult to suggest its perceived value is especially high even if you accept that it’s beautifully constructed and even quite tactile. No, the value for money Astell & Kern is offering here doesn’t reveal itself until you start listening — and then it becomes quickly apparent that your money has been very well spent indeed.
Value score: 4.5 / 5
Should I buy the Astell & Kern PD5?
Buy it if...
You have needy headphones
The PD5 is equipped to make even the most difficult headphones bend to its will.
You’re after uncompromised sound quality
With the Astell & Kern you get what you pay for and then some.
You’re sharp-eyed as well as sharp-eared
Navigating those set-up menus is no job for anyone who’s misplaced their spectacles. 
Don't buy it if...
You want to see, as well as hear, where your money has gone
The PD5 is a perfectly pleasant little device, but its appearance doesn’t exactly shout “almost a grand!”
You don’t own decent wired headphones
The Astell & Kern sounds perfectly fine via Bluetooth, but really your smartphone will do a pretty similar job. 
Astell & Kern PD5 review: Also consider
FiiO M23
The FiiO M23 has been around for a couple of years now, but really this only means it’s now competing almost directly with the PD5 on price. It remains a biggish, bulky-ish device, it’s true, but it also remains one of the most poised, direct and downright musical digital audio players around. Give it the right stuff to work with in terms of content and headphones, and the sound quality is enthralling. Read our full FiiO M23 review
How I tested the Astell & Kern PD5
- Listened using Tidal and Qobuz files
- Popped a 512GB microSD card loaded with extremely hi-res content into it
- Used Sennheiser IE900 and Meze Audio Strada for most of my testing
I installed the Tidal music streaming app and also deployed Qobuz Connect (it’s a slicker experience altogether than installing the app onto the player), and I inserted a 512GB microSD card loaded with extremely high-resolution content.
Then I connected a pair of Sennheiser IE900 IEMs using the 4.4mm balanced output, and also used a pair of Meze Audio Strada headphones connected the same way.
I also investigated the PD5’s desktop DAC credentials by plugging it into an Apple MacBook Pro and using the Qobuz and Tidal desktop apps to listen to hi-res using the same pairs of headphones.
- First reviewed in October 2026
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.
Simon Lucas is a senior editorial professional with deep experience of print/digital publishing and the consumer electronics landscape. Based in Brighton, Simon worked at TechRadar's sister site What HiFi? for a number of years, as both a features editor and a digital editor, before embarking on a career in freelance consultancy, content creation, and journalism for some of the biggest brands and publications in the world.
With enormous expertise in all things home entertainment, Simon reviews everything from turntables to soundbars for TechRadar, and also likes to dip his toes into longform features and buying guides. His bylines include GQ, The Guardian, Hi-Fi+, Metro, The Observer, Pocket Lint, Shortlist, Stuff T3, Tom's Guide, Trusted Reviews, and more.
