articles.title: AI architecture startup Dream launches with $17M in funding - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI architecture startup Dream launches with $17M in funding
Dream Technologies Inc., a startup using artificial intelligence to generate building designs, launched today with $17 million in funding.
Andreessen Horowitz led the seed round. It was joined by SV Angel, XYZ, Zigg Capital and several others.
San Francisco-based Dream was founded last year by former Palantir Technologies Inc. executives Andy Elder and Arjun Mathur. Elder headed the software maker’s product design team, while Mathur was the senior vice president of its private sector business. Dream’s leadership team also includes former engineers from Okta Inc. and Siemens AG.
Crafting a building plan manually can take a team of architects several months. Dream has developed a series of AI models designed to speed up the task. According to the company, its algorithms can generate hundreds of design variations in a few minutes. Dream says its software thereby not only accelerates construction projects but also lowers costs.
The company trained its models on data about 100 million square feet of U.S. real estate. The properties in the dataset include commercial buildings, apartments and single-family homes. Dream stores the blueprints its models process using a custom schema, a file that defines how a set of records should be organized. The schema is designed to ease the task of verifying architectural calculations.
Architecture teams craft building designs through an iterative process that involves numerous revisions. Those revisions are time-consuming because implementing even a small change often requires engineers to modify several blueprint elements. For example, adding an extra cooling system to a server hall might necessitate upgrades to the room’s electrical wiring and ventilation system.
Dream says its models speed up such changes. Additionally, they reduce the amount of work involved in adapting an existing building design to a new location. A retailer looking to open a store in a new city could reuse one of its existing venues’ designs and have Dream adapt it to local building codes.
The company’s models generate blueprints through a multistep process. First, they analyze the site where a building is set to be constructed and review the associated operational constraints. Dream uses those data points to generate a layout that defines which building elements should be placed where. Its models then define more granular details such as the dimensions of individual structural components.
“A hallucination in an LLM is a typo. A hallucination in a building is a structural fault, with potentially catastrophic consequences,” said Elder. “We built Dream to be exact — down to how a duct routes through a wall — because precision at that level is what actually shortens timelines and takes cost out of a project.”
The company is also working on a tool that can speed up internal design projects. According to Dream, the tool combines the U.S. real-estate dataset that underpins its models with information about 73 popular design and architectural styles.
Dream doesn’t sell its software but rather provides ready-to-use blueprints to construction and architecture firms. The company acts as an architect of record, which means that it takes legal responsibility for its plans. Dream disclosed today that it’s already supporting 10 construction projects in California and Texas with a combined value of $20 million.

articles.title: A full Windows 11 Pro license just dropped to $10 — no, that’s not a typo

Upgrade to Windows 11 Pro for $10 and get BitLocker and Hyper-V for 95% off
The bundle includes the operating system, BitLocker, Hyper-V, and Azure AD
We called Windows 11 "the best operating system made by Microsoft," when we took the OS out for a spin in our review. Since then, I'd argue it's grown from strength to strength. And while I'm not sure the company will ever hit the highs of Win98 and XP, Windows 11 still the operating system I use on all my personal and professional computers.
And I've just found a Windows 11 Pro license with BitLocker, Azure AD, and Hyper-V priced at $10 (was $199) on StackSocial. A 95% discount is enough to make anyone sit up and take notice. The site says it's sold by an authorized Microsoft partner, and is a verified license key.
• Best for: Professionals upgrading to Microsoft's latest OS without paying full price for additionals like BitLocker.
• Why we like it: The price is the eye-catching feature here - at $10 you're getting a perpetual license to the operating system, alongside business-critical security and virtualization services.
• What you need to know: This is a download key, not sold direct from Microsoft, and I'd recommend checking your system requirements before purchase.
This license key offers full access to Windows 11 Pro, as well as Bitlocker security, virtual machines manager Hyper-V, and identity and access management service Azure AD. A Windows 11 Home license is also available for the same price, and from the same seller.
Why we recommend it
Upgrading to Windows 11 Pro is pricey, at $200. And with Microsoft dropping support for Windows 10 this time last year, more and more businesses are looking for ways to upgrade.
The operating system itself scored 4 stars in our review. With regular updates and improvements, we called it "a great operating system, and if you use a Windows-powered device that’s currently on Windows 10, it’s probably time to consider an upgrade and take advantage of what Windows 11 has to offer. As things stand, Windows 11 has earned its place as a new classic in Microsoft’s lineup, ready to embrace what AI and handheld gaming will offer in the future."
Value verdict
This Windows 11 Pro deal is exceptionally good value. For comparison, Microsoft sells a license for Windows 11 Pro for $200 on its site. There, you can also buy a pre-loaded USB version, but if you're happy with a download code, this is the better deal.

articles.title: Jusqu'à 6 000 lumens et 10 000:1 de contraste : XGIMI dévoile ses vidéoprojecteurs les plus ambitieux
articles.text:
Avec ses nouveaux Horizon 30 Pro, Max et Ultra Max, XGIMI franchit un cap dans la vidéoprojection domestique. Ces trois projecteurs laser RGB promettent une luminosité grimpant à 6 000 lumens ISO, un contraste natif jusqu'à 10 000:1 et une véritable restitution 4K à 120 Hz.
XGIMI poursuit sa montée en gamme à l'occasion de sa nouvelle série. Après avoir popularisé les vidéoprojecteurs tout-en-un faciles à installer, le constructeur s'attaque désormais plus en profondeur au marché du home cinéma exigeant. Sa nouvelle série Horizon 30 veut lier forte luminosité, contraste élevé, souplesse d'installation et performances gaming.
Trois modèles, trois niveaux de luminosité et contraste
Succédant à la série Horizon 20, les Horizon 30 Pro, Max et Ultra Max font leur apparition au catalogue du fabricant chinois. Une fois n'est pas coutume chez XGIMI, ils utilisent tous les trois une source lumineuse triple laser RGB, associant directement les trois couleurs primaires.
XGIMI annonce 110 % de couverture de l'espace BT.2020 et une précision colorimétrique avec un Delta E inférieur à 0,8. Des performances ambitieuses, que nous aurons prochainement l'occasion de vérifier.
Si le Horizon 30 Pro offre jusqu'à 4 800 lumens ISO, et un contraste annoncé de 8 000:1, son grand frère le 30 Max, annnonce monter à 5 300 lumens ISO pour un contraste de 9 000:1. Le cador de la gamme, le HORIZON 30 Ultra Max annonce quant à lui une luminosité maximale de 6 000 lumens ISO pour un contraste natif grimpant à 10 000:1.
Enfin, il faut bien accepter quelques compromis. Si l'utilisateur souhaite privilégier la fidélité colorimétrique, en mode cinéma, le Pro descend à 2 300 lumens ISO, le Max à 2 400 et l'Ultra Max à 3 000. En mode lumineux, ces valeurs atteignent respectivement 2 800, 2 970 et 3 500 lumens.
Un double iris pour des noirs profonds
L'autre promesse majeure concerne le contraste. XGIMI revendique jusqu'à 10 000:1 en natif grâce à son système Dual Intelligent Iris. Le fabricant présente notamment jusqu'à cinq ouvertures réglables, de f/2.0 à f/7.0. Cette technologie permet d'adapter la quantité de lumière projetée à l'environnement. L'ouverture maximale fera son travail dans une pièce éclairée, en adoptant une fermeture progressive pour privilégier les tons de noir dans une pièce obscure.
Le fabricant ne précise toutefois pas dans quelles conditions les contrastes natifs ont été mesurés.
De la véritable 4K à 120 Hz
Le constructeur indique que son architecture repose sur deux contrôleurs Texas Instruments DLPC8545. L'intérêt d'une telle architecture est de permettre la restitution effective de la 4K Ultra HD à 120 Hz, plutôt que de simplement accepter le signal entrant à cette fréquence pour le convertir.
Pour les amateurs de cinéma, le 120 Hz présente également un avantage : les films, généralement tournés à 24 images par seconde, peuvent être affichés sans saccades supplémentaires. Chaque image est reproduite cinq fois à intervalles réguliers, ce qui permet de respecter la fluidité d'origine du film, sans avoir besoin d'inventer des images intermédiaires.
Côté audio, le système est assuré par Harman Kardon, comme à l'accoutumée chez XGIMI. La gamme Horizon 30 intègre deux haut-parleurs de 12 watts chacun. Une barre de son peut être la bienvenue pour améliorer l'expérience audio.
Zoom optique et Lens Shift : de vrais arguments pour les cinéphiles
Les Horizon 30 adoptent un objectif X-Master Red Ring Lens, avec une transmission lumineuse annoncée de 99,6 % et un traitement optique à 14 couches.
Surtout, le zoom optique offre un rapport de projection de 1,2:1 à 1,5:1. Une image de 100 pouces peut ainsi être obtenue avec entre 2,66 et 3,32 mètres de recul, sans recourir à une réduction numérique.
Le Lens Shift annoncé atteint environ 50 % horizontalement et environ 130 % verticalement, selon la convention de mesure du constructeur.
XGIMI évoque également six mémoires de position permettant à l'appareil de se rappeler des paramètres de zoom, mise au point et décalage optique. Un atout pour passer d'un programme 16:9 à un film au format CinemaScope 2,35:1 ou 21:9.
Gaming : 240 Hz, FreeSync Premium et 1 ms annoncé
Un vidéoprojecteur, c'est très bien pour regarder des films, mais ça peut également être intéressant pour jouer, et XGIMI n'oublie pas les gamers avec cette nouvelle série Horizon 30.
Nonobstant la 4K UHD à 120 Hz, XGIMI annonce un mode 1080p à 240 Hz pour plus de fluidité, mais également la compatibilité VRR, AMD FreeSync Premium et ALLM.
Le constructeur se targue même d'une latence de seulement 1 ms en 1080p à 240 Hz, mais ne donne pas d'information concernant cette donnée quand l'appareil est en 4K Ultra HD.
Par ailleurs, les trois modèles prennent en charge les technologies Dolby Vision, HDR10, HDR10+ et HLG, avec un traitement dynamique des contenus HDR.
Quels tarifs pour la série Horizon 30 ?
Les Horizon 30 Pro et Max sont annoncés pour le 1er novembre 2026. Quant à la version Ultra Max, cette dernière arrivera un peu plus tard, le 11 novembre selon le fabricant.
Le Horizon 30 Pro sera commercialisé au prix de 2 499 €, il est disponible en précommande à 1 999 €.
Côté Horizon 30 Max, ce dernier sera commercialisé à 2 799€, il est disponible à la précommande au prix de 2 499 €. Enfin, le Horizon 30 Ultra Max sera vendu au tarif public conseillé de 3 299 €, en précommande, son tarif chute à 2 999 €. Pour ce dernier, deux paires de lunettes 3D sont offertes, ainsi qu'un support au choix, pour installer l'appareil.
Quel avenir pour XGIMI ? Quelles gammes changeront en 2027 ?
Le constructeur nous a teasé une nouvelle catégorie de produits à venir pour le courant de l'année 2027. XGIMI veut "raconter l'histoire autour de la lumière et de la technologie laser", nous indique Julien Labbé, directeur marketing Europe de la marque, sans laisser fuiter plus de détails.
Les lunettes lancées en ce début d'année, les MemoMind, verront une V2 arriver sur le marché en janvier 2027. Par ailleurs, le fabricant entend bien renforcer son positionnement haut de gamme, avec deux nouveaux appareils dans la gamme Titan en 2027. Pour la fin de l'année prochaine, on peut également s'attendre à un renouvellement de la gamme MoGo, avec l'arrivée de la série MoGo 5.
Les prochaines nouveautés du constructeur ne seront pas annoncées avant le CES de Las Vegas, qui se déroulera du 6 au 9 janvier 2027.

articles.title: HAVN Launches the HS 360 & HS 360 VGPU PC Cases
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
HAVN Launches the HS 360 & HS 360 VGPU PC Cases
HAVN is proud to announce the launch of its latest PC cases, the HS 360 and HS 360 VGPU. The HS 360 builds on the success of the HS 420 and has been refined through direct feedback from partners and reviewers. As a result, we have packed HAVN's panoramic, GPU-centric Hybrid Structure into a chassis that's 19.4% smaller and 29.5% lighter than the HS 420.
Steven Levitt, Brand Marketing Manager"With the HS 360, our goal wasn't simply to make the HS 420 smaller. We wanted to take everything we learned from the original design, listen to feedback from the community, and refine while improving performance."
[Editor's note: Our in-depth review of HAVN HS 360 VGPU is now live]The HAVN engineering team has focused on improving the building experience and performance of the HS series, introducing several key enhancements:
- Integrated magnetic Airflow Divider (VGPU model only), delivering up to 6°C lower GPU temperatures, alongside adjustable anti-vibration GPU pads.
- Supports Back-Connect ATX motherboards.
- Refined UniSheet panoramic glass with a 31.8% tighter bend radius, for a clearer, more seamless view.
- 36% greater structural strength compared to the HS 420, despite its smaller and lighter design.
- SimpliCable routing system for clean and easy cable management.
- Redesigned, rear-mount fan brackets for hassle-free installation.
- Top and bottom fan brackets are aligned to simplify custom water-cooling builds.
- Every detachable bracket features integrated anti-vibration contact points.
The HS 360 and HS 360 VGPU continue HAVN's commitment to thoughtful engineering, combining a more compact footprint with improvements that make building, cooling, and showcasing high-performance systems easier than ever.Available globally starting October 29, 2026,
- HS 360: €199.90 / $199.99 / £169.99
- HS 360 VGPU: €279.90 / $279.99 / £239.99

articles.title: Google simplifica el día a día integrando apps cotidianas en el buscador y en Gemini
articles.text:
Pedir la compra del supermercado, armar una lista de reproducción o reservar una cita médica son tareas que suelen requerir abrir varias apps distintas. Google busca cambiar esa dinámica con una plataforma que conecta aplicaciones externas directamente dentro de la Búsqueda y de Gemini, de modo que los usuarios puedan resolver gestiones cotidianas sin salir de esos dos entornos.
Según informó el blog de Google, la compañía lanzó la versión preliminar de esta plataforma, llamada Connected Apps, con el objetivo de que más desarrolladores integren sus funcionalidades de forma directa en ambos productos.
Junto con este anuncio, la empresa presentó una lista de socios que ya forman parte de la iniciativa, con el fin de ampliar las opciones disponibles para optimizar la vida diaria de sus usuarios.
Cómo funciona la nueva plataforma de apps conectadas de Google
Connected Apps permite a los desarrolladores crear una integración única que luego puede llegar a usuarios con alta intención de compra, tanto desde la Búsqueda como desde la app Gemini. Para lograrlo, según explicó el blog de Google, los desarrolladores deben integrarse con un servidor MCP alojado en la nube o con Android MCP mediante las API de AppFunctions.
El siguiente paso consiste en utilizar la consola de Google Connected para registrar, probar y enviar la aplicación. Antes de que esta pase por el proceso de revisión, cada desarrollador decide si su integración se publicará en la Búsqueda, en Gemini o en ambas plataformas de forma simultánea.
Una vez que la aplicación queda publicada, los desarrolladores pueden hacer seguimiento de métricas de funcionamiento como el tráfico, la latencia y las tasas de error. El sistema también contempla el control de la identidad de marca, lo que incluye logotipos verificados y cuentas autenticadas para cada integración.
Google adelantó que el acceso a la plataforma se abrirá por fases. La compañía prevé sumar más desarrolladores, mercados y productos propios en los próximos meses, lo que sugiere una expansión progresiva del ecosistema de apps conectadas.
Esta plataforma responde a una necesidad concreta: permitir que las funciones de aplicaciones externas se ejecuten sin fricciones dentro de los servicios que millones de personas usan a diario para buscar información o resolver tareas con inteligencia artificial.
Qué aplicaciones ya están disponibles en Search y Gemini
Google confirmó el lanzamiento de más de 50 aplicaciones conectadas que operan tanto en Search como en Gemini. Estas integraciones cubren áreas diversas, entre ellas productividad, venta de entradas para eventos, salud y bienestar.
Entre los socios que ya cuentan con integraciones activas se encuentran Adobe, Experian, Localiza y Peloton. Estas aplicaciones están disponibles en este momento para los usuarios de Gemini, y de acuerdo con lo publicado por Google, se sumarán también a Search en las próximas semanas.
La compañía anunció además una nueva integración con Calm, que se lanzará de manera simultánea tanto en Search como en Gemini. Esta incorporación refuerza el área de salud y bienestar dentro del catálogo de aplicaciones conectadas.
Google reorganiza Gemini: cómo funcionarán las nuevas Skills y Tareas
Google inició una reorganización profunda en las funciones y la nomenclatura de su inteligencia artificial Gemini, un proceso que comienza en octubre de 2026 y continuará hasta 2027 para usuarios de cuentas corporativas y educativas.
Lejos de tratarse de un simple ajuste estético, esta actualización redefine la forma en que los usuarios interactúan con las herramientas de la plataforma, priorizando la integración directa dentro del hilo principal de conversación en lugar de dispersar las tareas en ventanas independientes.
El cambio más representativo es la transformación de los Gems en Skills. A diferencia del formato anterior —que exigía abrir chats separados para cada bot personalizado—, las nuevas Skills se invocan directamente en el chat habitual escribiendo una barra diagonal o mediante la detección automática del sistema.
Además de permitir la combinación de varias instrucciones en una misma interacción (como tono de voz e identidad de marca), adoptan el formato abierto SKILL.md y se integran en Google Workspace. No obstante, en esta fase inicial quedan temporalmente excluidas herramientas como Canvas, la generación de video o música, y la vinculación de archivos de Google Drive.
Por otro lado, el agente autónomo conocido como Spark pasa a denominarse simplemente Tarea, integrándose en un selector junto a la caja de texto. Esta herramienta, capaz de seguir operando en máquinas virtuales de Google Cloud incluso si el usuario apaga su dispositivo, ejecuta procesos complejos como monitoreos o investigaciones en la web.
Para garantizar la seguridad del usuario, el sistema incorpora puntos de control obligatorios que solicitan aprobación previa antes de concretar acciones críticas, compras, envíos de datos o el ingreso de contraseñas.
Finalmente, la función de Acciones programadas mantiene su nombre original dentro del ecosistema, estableciendo un límite operativo de hasta diez ejecuciones simultáneas.

articles.title: I’ve tested hundreds of iPhone cases — here are 9 of my favorite iPhone 18 Pro cases from Moft, CASETiFY, Apple, and more
articles.text:
If you’ve just picked up a shiny new iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max, you’re probably sifting through a gazillion case options to better protect it from drops and scratches.
The very best iPhone cases are stylish, durable, and feel great in the hand, but having tested hundreds of different models over the years, let me tell you: not all iPhone cases are created equal.
So, to help you find the treasure in a sea of trash, I’ve rounded up nine of my favorite iPhone 18 Pro-specific cases from Moft, Troubadour, CASETiFY, and more.
Apple Silicone Case with MagSafe
Apple’s classic Silicone Case for the iPhone 18 Pro is the definition of a safe bet. As we’ve come to expect from these largely unchanging models, this case feels great in the hand and is grippier than many of the leather options included elsewhere on this list. But if by some miracle Apple’s Silicone Case does slip from your grasp, its rubbery construction provides a good amount of shock absorption for your precious iPhone.
If I’ve got any criticisms of Apple’s Silicone Case, it’s that it picks up lint pretty easily (a consequence of that extra grippiness) and it's prone to showing circular marks when attached to MagSafe charging accessories for long periods. These circles are temporary, only appearing when the case itself heats up during charging, but their existence is worth noting nonetheless.
For extra protection, you can pair Apple’s Silicone Case with a compatible Wrist Strap or Crossbody Strap, which are both sold separately. I'm not cool enough to pull off either of those things, but you might be.
Buy the iPhone 18 Pro Silicone Case with MagSafe
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
ESR Atelier Silicone Leather Magnetic Case
Crafted from soft silicone leather (which I can only assume is a synthetic leather-adjacent material), the ESR Atelier Silicone Leather Magnetic Case feels comfortable to hold and is chunky enough to protect your iPhone from reasonably high drops.
But the selling point of this case is its built-in stand, which sits around the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera plateau. It can be adjusted from 15 to 69 degrees and is sturdy as heck at all angles, so whether you’re watching a YouTube video with breakfast or a movie on the train, you don’t have to worry about your iPhone collapsing backwards on itself.
A 90-degree extension option would’ve been nice, but if going beyond 69 degrees would necessitate a bulkier module around the camera plateau, I’m happy with the trade-off.
Buy the ESR iPhone 18 Pro Atelier Silicone Leather Magnetic Case
Troubadour Modular Case
I’ve written about my favorite iPhone cases from Troubadour (formerly Mujjo) before, and for the iPhone 18 Pro, the case-maker has shaken up its lineup with a modular version of its classic Leather Case.
This Terracotta model features a removable magnetic back panel, which lets you pop out a portion of the case if you’d rather leave the rear of your iPhone 18 Pro exposed. I’m not entirely sure why anyone would want to do this — a backless phone looks cool, but feels strange in the hand — but I suppose it’s nice to have the option to do so.
The bigger benefit of having a removable back panel is that you can swap out the standard piece for custom MagSafe accessories that sit inside the cavity, rather than stacking onto the back of the case itself. Troubadour’s MagSafe Card Leather Wallet Stand is sold separately, but it’s absolutely worth picking up: it’s big enough to hold three cards, and features a fold-out stand that can prop up the iPhone 18 Pro in either portrait or landscape positions.
Buy the Troubadour iPhone 18 Pro Modular Case
CASETiFY Ripple Case
CASETiFY never does things by halves (remember when the brand partnered with The Andy Warhol Foundation?), and its latest Ripple Case for the iPhone 18 Pro is characteristically fun and durable.
Featuring four raised corners, this silicone case has been engineered to absorb and disperse force when dropped from multiple angles. CASETiFY says it’s been tested to withstand drops from up to 6.6 feet high, and while I wasn’t brave enough to raise my own iPhone 18 Pro above my 6-foot frame and drop it to the floor, I can believe the company’s claim: this thing bounces around like a ping-pong ball (complimentary).
Another nice feature of the Ripple case is its ability to withstand light-induced yellowing and object staining. You can rub ketchup, crayons, and coffee all over it — or even leave it out in the sun all day — and it’ll look good as new after a quick wipe. Parents, rejoice!
Buy the CASETiFY iPhone 18 Pro Ripple Case
Wave MagSafe Case
Wave’s MagSafe cases are unfussy, eco-friendly, and devoid of flashy features. Crucially, they’re made from biodegradable wheat straw, so they’re (much) better for the planet than many of the other options in this list — including those made from vegan leather.
I don’t love that Wave’s cases leave your iPhone’s Camera Control button exposed, which makes the button itself harder to reach given the width added to the phone by the case. But if you’re conscious about what might happen to your case after you’re done with it, there aren’t many better options than the Wave case.
Buy the Wave iPhone 18 Pro MagSafe Compatible Case
Peak Design SlimLink Everyday Loop Case
If you’re someone who likes to attach your phone to your vehicle, Peak Design’s SlimLink cases are the way to go. The SlimLink Everyday Loop Case for the iPhone 18 Pro can be attached to the brand’s car, bike, and motorcycle mounts (sold separately) via a novel magnetic-plus-mechanical mount system, which is more resistant to vibrations and bumps than magnets alone.
But even if you’re not fussed about mounting your phone to your, err, mount, the SlimLink Everyday Loop Case feels awesome in the hand, looks super smart (particularly in the Sage color pictured above), and features an optional finger loop for added peace of mind when you’re leaning over the railings at Niagara Falls to get the perfect shot.
I’m going to cheat and add a second Peak Design option in this same entry: the brand’s MagSafe-only Everyday Case is also a great pick if you’d rather avoid the bells and whistles of its SlimLink system and finger loop. It’s available in Charcoal, Sage, Ocean, Redwood Clarino (pictured above), Dusk Clarino, Cirrus Clarino, Black Leather, and Amber Leather.
Buy the Peak Design SlimLink Everyday Loop Case for iPhone 18 Pro
Moft Snap Case MOVAS
The Moft Snap Case MOVAS is an absolutely gorgeous iPhone 18 Pro case, but I urge you to exercise patience if, when putting it on your iPhone for the first time, it seems defective.
This is the tightest iPhone case I have ever used, which means it’s a bit of a challenge to get on and off. And once you do manage to snap it around your iPhone, it can sometimes ‘lock’ the power button into depression erroneously, which will force you to remove and re-apply the case until the power button becomes clickable as normal.
However, once you do find the perfect fit (I suggest leading with the power button side, and ‘pushing down’ with the volume rocker side), I’d wager that this is the nicest-feeling and nicest-looking iPhone 18 Pro case around.
There is something remarkably soft about Moft’s proprietary vegan leather, which is topped with a silicone-based surface treatment for a skin-like feel. And the aforementioned tightness of this case means it adds almost zero bulk to your iPhone 18 Pro. If you’re concerned about aesthetics above all else, this is the case to choose — especially in the Blackberry color, which complements Apple’s new Burgundy shade perfectly.
Buy the Moft Snap Case MOVAS for iPhone 18 Pro
Moment Camera Case II
Here’s one for the camera aficionados: the Moment Camera Case II lets you attach extra mobile lenses, physical photo filters, and mounting hardware to your iPhone 18 Pro.
Maybe you want to add some cinematic depth to your wide shots, or more optical character to your macro shots? Moment has attachments that help you do both those things, and the Camera Case II is the rig onto which these attachments, well, attach.
The brand’s twist-and-lock system works seamlessly, and the Camera Case II’s Camera Control button is the best of any case I’ve tested. Sure, this is a chunky piece of kit, and I don’t particularly like the ribbed material on the rear panel (think mild carpet burn), but this is the case to choose if you’re looking to take your iPhone photography to the next level.
Buy the Moment Camera Case II for iPhone 18 Pro

articles.title: Intel shares plummet more than 20% following weak guidance blamed on PC market slowdown - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Intel shares plummet more than 20% following weak guidance blamed on PC market slowdown
Intel Corp. somehow managed to beat expectations despite facing softness in the personal computer market, but its weak forecast for the current quarter sparked panic among investors, and its stock plunged more than 22% in late trading today.
The computer chipmaker reported third-quarter earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of 52 cents per share, easily beating Wall Street’s guidance of 40 cents per share. Revenue for the quarter rose 21% from a year earlier, to $16.51 billion, edging past the Street’s target of $16.5 billion. All told, the company posted net income of $3.3 billion, down from the $4.1 billion it earned in the same period last year.
However, the results couldn’t mask the poor performance of Intel’s client computing and physical AI business, where revenue dropped 5% from a year earlier, to $8.1 billion, missing the Street’s target. The company was held up by its data center and AI unit, where revenue soared 78%, to $7.3 billion.
The client computing business is struggling because the PC market is currently in decline. Global PC shipments fell 4% in the second quarter according to data from Counterpoint Research, partly due to the soaring costs of memory and other components.
Things are likely to get even worse in the PC market, which is why Intel could only offer a tepid forecast going forward. The company said it’s looking for fourth-quarter earnings of about 25 cents per share at the midpoint of its guidance range, with revenue at between $15 billion and $16 billion. Analysts are targeting earnings of 43 cents per share and sales of $17.1 billion.
Intel’s finance chief David Zinsner said the company sees the PC slowdown continuing until at least the first half of next year. “We will continue making disciplined investments capacity and working capital to increase supply and support future growth,” he told investors.
During the quarter, the company suffered a tragic setback when an explosion occurred at one of its chip fabrication plants in Israel, resulting in the deaths of two workers and serious injuries to a third person. That incident will cost the company about $600 million in lost revenue over the next two quarters, Zinsner told analysts on a conference call. Chief Executive Lip-Bu Tan (pictured) said the “unfortunate and tragic accident” resulted in an “extended shutdown” at the plant, delaying shipments of new 10-nanometer chips.
Today’s after-hours drop slams the brakes on what had been one of the fastest-growing technology stocks this year. Intel’s stock had been on an upward tear all year, rising more than 150% since January. However, the stock’s growth had already stalled since the beginning of the month amid growing concerns about the tech industry’s runaway spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure. “We will remain disciplined as we invest and we will not spend $1 of capital unless we have confidence in the health of our products and process technologies and clear evidence of customer demand,” Zinsner said in an effort to reassure investors.
Intel is best known for the central processing units that power much of the world’s PCs, but its recent revival has primarily been driven by the emergence of agentic AI workloads. Chatbots such as ChatGPT and Gemini primarily use the graphics processing units sold by rival chipmakers like Nvidia Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc., but AI agents such as Meta Platforms Inc.’s Muse and OpenAI Group PBC’s Dots run more efficiently on CPUs. As agentic AI has grown in popularity this year, so too have Intel’s chips.
“Despite near term headwinds affecting the broader PC industry, we continue to see robust demand for CPUs and more broadly, for all our computing platforms in the long term,” Tan insisted.
However, the demand for Intel’s CPUs has been offset by the struggles of its nascent foundry business, which was spun out as a separate business unit a couple of years ago but has struggled to gain traction with customers. So far, its only major customer is Intel itself.
The company’s fab in Arizona is the only U.S.-based facility that’s able to mass produce advanced logic chips. “We are going to have a couple of customers ready to announce in the next two quarters,” Tan promised analysts on the call. He added that the company is also making “tremendous progress” with its forthcoming 14A chips.
Intel, which had previously fallen behind on its roadmap for seven- and 10-nanometer chips, has been struggling to get back on track but has benefited from a vote of confidence by President Donald Trump, whose administration took a 10% stake in the company last year. Since then, Nvidia and SoftBank Group Corp. have also invested billions of dollars into the chipmaker.
Tan is generally viewed as being more cautious than his predecessor, Pat Gelsinger, who made the decision to spin out the foundry business and try to attract external customers. But at the same time, he has also given the green light to some significant investments such as a new chip fab in Ohio that was first expected to come online last year. So far it hasn’t, but Intel said last week that construction crews have installed the first structural truss at the facility.
Last month, reports emerged that Intel was talking to the high-bandwidth memory chip manufacturer SK hynix Inc. about the prospect of it leasing a part of the Ohio fab’s capacity. The South Korean firm reportedly wants to manufacture some of its memory chips at the new site, but so far nothing concrete has been announced. Tan refused to acknowledge those talks, telling analysts that the company “continues to evaluate unique and highly differentiated opportunities to accelerate our Ohio buildout, and I hope to share more on this in the near future.”

articles.title: Piratage à Strasbourg : les données de 230 000 clients de la CTS compromises
articles.text:
La Compagnie des transports strasbourgeois (CTS) a été victime d’un vol de données touchant environ 230 000 comptes clients. Si les mots de passe et les coordonnées bancaires n’ont pas été compromis, les informations dérobées pourraient faciliter des tentatives d’hameçonnage. Méfiance donc.
Officialisée hier 28 octobre, la cyberattaque concerne près de 40 % des comptes clients de la CTS. Une fuite de données qui a conduit l’opérateur de transports strasbourgeois à prévenir les personnes concernées par courriel. Comme le rapporte Ici.fr, l’incident remonte à la mi-octobre et la faille exploitée a depuis été corrigée.
230 000 comptes clients concernés par le piratage
Dans le détail, les pirates ont pu récupérer plusieurs informations personnelles telles que le nom, le prénom, la date de naissance, l’adresse postale ainsi que l’identifiant Badgéo associé au compte client. En revanche, la CTS assure que les mots de passe et les données bancaires ne font pas partie des informations exfiltrées.
Le directeur général de la CTS, Emmanuel Auneau, précise que l’attaque s’est produite dans la nuit du dimanche 18 au lundi 19 octobre. L’entreprise annonce avoir détecté une activité anormale, caractérisée par une sollicitation particulièrement élevée de sa base de données.
Le responsable tient également à préciser la méthode employée par les pirates : « Nos serveurs ne sont pas altérés, les hackeurs ne se sont pas infiltrés dans notre système informatique, ils ont utilisé une API pour voler des données. La faille est depuis corrigée. ».
Les assaillants ont donc exploité une interface permettant à différents logiciels de communiquer avec le site, sans nécessairement pénétrer dans l’ensemble du système informatique de l’opérateur.
Des risques de phishing pour les clients de la CTS
Si aucune donnée bancaire ni aucun mot de passe n’ont été dérobés, l’incident n’est pas pour autant sans conséquence pour les usagers. Les informations récupérées peuvent en effet servir à concevoir des messages frauduleux particulièrement convaincants (et donc dangereux) en reprenant des éléments personnels pour inspirer confiance à leurs destinataires.
Un faux courriel évoquant un abonnement Badgéo, une régularisation ou encore un remboursement sont autant de scénarios qui pourraient sembler parfaitement légitimes. Tout récemment, c’est Engie qui a tenu à prévenir ses clients après un vol de données personnelles.
Emmanuel Auneau indique : « Je suis vraiment désolé pour nos clients mais ils risquent au pire d’être importunés par des mails indésirables ».
La prudence reste donc de mise, et la CTS rappelle qu’elle ne demande pas à ses clients d’effectuer une transaction financière ou de communiquer leurs coordonnées bancaires par courriel. Comme toujours, en cas de message suspect, on évite soigneusement les liens proposés et on vérifie directement les informations auprès de l’opérateur.
Une plainte va être déposée après la fuite de données
La CTS confirme aussi avoir stoppé l’exfiltration dès la détection de l’incident et renforcé la sécurité de son site Internet. Une déclaration a été effectuée auprès de la Commission nationale de l’informatique et des libertés (CNIL), tandis qu’une plainte doit être déposée auprès du tribunal de Strasbourg.
L’entreprise ne sait pas encore si les données dérobées ont été revendues ou diffusées, et il faudra donc surveiller les éventuelles conséquences de cette fuite, alors que la protection des informations personnelles représente un enjeu majeur pour les services numériques du quotidien.
Ce n’est pas la première fois que la CTS est confrontée à un incident de sécurité, puisqu’il y a deux ans, certains comptes clients avaient déjà fait l’objet d’accès frauduleux. Cette fois, l’ampleur de l’exfiltration est nettement plus importante, avec environ 230 000 comptes concernés.

articles.title: Steam añade 2 juegos gratis y un DLC para PC por tiempo limitado: Football Manager 27, Hexologic y más
articles.text:
Steam habilitó tres promociones gratuitas por tiempo limitado para PC: Football Manager 27, Hexologic y el contenido descargable Hunting Simulator 3 - Classic American Hunter Pack.
La plataforma permite conservar Hexologic si se reclama antes del 31 de octubre de 2026. El Classic American Hunter Pack estará disponible sin costo hasta el 12 de noviembre, aunque requiere tener el juego base Hunting Simulator 3. En tanto, Football Manager 27 se puede jugar gratis hasta el 3 de noviembre.
Para acceder a las promociones, los usuarios deben ingresar con una cuenta de Steam desde la página de cada producto. En los casos de Hexologic y del paquete para Hunting Simulator 3, el contenido quedará asociado a la biblioteca una vez reclamado dentro del plazo.
De qué tratan los nuevos juegos gratuitos de Steam
Hexologic es un juego de puzles numéricos con casillas hexagonales. Su propuesta combina mecánicas inspiradas en el sudoku con desafíos de lógica y una estética colorida.
En Football Manager 27, los jugadores asumen el rol de entrenador de un club de fútbol. El título permite definir tácticas, gestionar planteles, entrenar al equipo y tomar decisiones durante los partidos.
Por su parte, Hunting Simulator 3 - Classic American Hunter Pack es un contenido descargable para Hunting Simulator 3. Para utilizarlo, es necesario contar previamente con el juego base en la biblioteca de Steam.
Cómo acceder a estos juegos de Steam
Para reclamar Hexologic, hay que abrir su página en Steam, iniciar sesión y seleccionar la opción para obtenerlo sin costo antes de que finalice la promoción. Una vez añadido, el juego permanecerá en la biblioteca del usuario.
El procedimiento para el contenido descargable de Hunting Simulator 3 es similar: se debe acceder a su ficha, iniciar sesión y añadirlo a la cuenta antes del 12 de noviembre. El paquete no puede utilizarse sin el juego principal.
En el caso de Football Manager 27, los usuarios pueden entrar a su página de Steam y seleccionar la opción de juego gratuito. La prueba estará disponible hasta el 3 de noviembre, por lo que no se trata de una incorporación permanente a la biblioteca.
CEO de Epic Games arremete contra los dueños de Steam
Tim Sweeney, CEO de Epic Games, volvió a cuestionar a Valve, dueña de Steam, al acusarla de haber limitado el crecimiento de la industria de videojuegos para PC mediante un ecosistema cerrado.
La discusión resurgió en octubre de 2026 a partir de una publicación en X de Kiaran Ritchie, exprogramador principal de animación de Epic, quien criticó la comisión del 30% que Steam cobra en buena parte de las ventas realizadas en su plataforma.
Ritchie afirmó que sería posible crear una alternativa a Steam en poco tiempo, pero reconoció que la gran barrera es la cantidad de usuarios que ya posee la tienda y el valor de las bibliotecas digitales que los jugadores acumularon durante años.
Según su postura, esa dependencia afecta los ingresos de los estudios y dificulta la aparición de competidores.
Sweeney respaldó esas críticas y sostuvo que Valve mantuvo los juegos de PC en un entorno social que complica la comunicación entre jugadores de PC, consolas y dispositivos móviles.
El ejecutivo defiende un modelo abierto en el que estudios y usuarios puedan conectarse sin importar si utilizan PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch, iOS, Android o computadoras.
Además, planteó que ese sistema permitiría colaboraciones entre distintos videojuegos, incluso con objetos que pudieran trasladarse de un título a otro. Epic Games prevé explorar estas posibilidades con Unreal Engine 6.
El conflicto se suma a las críticas de Sweeney contra la política de Steam que exige declarar el uso de inteligencia artificial en el desarrollo de videojuegos. El CEO de Epic considera que esas etiquetas pueden provocar rechazo hacia los estudios.

articles.title: Black Friday 2026 : toutes les dates à retenir pour ce mois de promotions folles
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : toutes les dates à retenir pour ce mois de promotions folles
Le Black Friday 2026 approche à grands pas, mais face à l'étalement des promotions, il est parfois difficile de s'y retrouver. Black Month, Black Week, vendredi noir ou Cyber Monday : à quel moment faut-il dégainer sa carte bancaire pour réaliser les meilleures affaires avant les fêtes ? Voici le calendrier complet des dates clés pour bien vous préparer.
Historiquement concentré sur une seule journée, l'événement s'est progressivement transformé. Désormais, le marché s'emballe sur un mois complet : c'est le "Black Month". Les e-commerçants n'attendent plus la fin novembre pour brader leurs stocks et anticipent de plus en plus leurs opérations pour lisser les achats de Noël. Cette année, le coup d'envoi est d'ailleurs imminent : Boulanger dégaine ses premières baisses de prix dès le 30 octobre, et Cdiscount entrera dans la danse à partir du 2 novembre.
La Black Week : la montée en puissance à partir du 23 novembre
Si les premières semaines de novembre permettent de dénicher des offres anticipées, le rythme s'accélère véritablement lors de la fameuse "Black Week". Cette semaine de chauffe, qui précède le jour J, débutera officiellement le lundi 23 novembre 2026. C'est à ce moment-là que l'ensemble des acteurs, comme Amazon, la Fnac ou Darty, commencent à multiplier les ventes flash quotidiennes et les offres agressives sur la tech et l'électroménager pour faire monter la pression.
Le "vrai" Black Friday : le rendez-vous incontournable du 27 novembre
C'est LA date à entourer en rouge dans votre agenda : cette année, le véritable Black Friday aura lieu le vendredi 27 novembre 2026. Si de bonnes affaires sont disponibles tout au long du mois, c'est lors de ce fameux "vendredi noir" (et durant le week-end qui suit) que les enseignes débloquent leurs plus fortes remises et liquident leurs produits phares à des prix défiant toute concurrence. Sur les références les plus populaires, les stocks fondent généralement en quelques heures, exigeant une réactivité absolue.
Le Cyber Monday : l'ultime séance de rattrapage du 30 novembre
Passé le week-end du Black Friday, la folle période promotionnelle de novembre s'achève avec le Cyber Monday, fixé au lundi 30 novembre 2026. À l'origine réservé aux achats en ligne (quand le Black Friday se cantonnait aux magasins physiques), ce rendez-vous est aujourd'hui une vaste séance de rattrapage. Historiquement très orienté vers le matériel high-tech et informatique, c'est la toute dernière occasion de boucler sa liste au Père Noël à prix cassé avant que les tarifs ne remontent brutalement début décembre.
Pour ne rater aucun de ces rendez-vous, la rédaction des Numériques sera sur le pont tout au long de cette période pour éplucher les catalogues et ne vous remonter que les vrais bons plans, portant exclusivement sur des produits que nous avons rigoureusement testés et approuvés.

articles.title: Keychron Launches Steampunk Q19 HE 8K Gaming Keyboard
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
Keychron Launches Steampunk Q19 HE 8K Gaming Keyboard
Keychron's ongoing efforts to update its keyboard line-up with new models has produced the Q19 HE 8K as its latest special colorway of the 60% Hall effect PCB first introduced with the Q16 HE 8K and recently made another appearance in the Carbon 60 HE. The Q19 HE uses the exact same Keychron Ultra-Fast Magnetic Lime switches as the Carbon 60 HE and the Q16 HE 8K, but it opts for a CNC-machined 6063 aluminium tray-mount case with steampunk embellishments. 
Both the patina on the aluminium case and the keycaps bear the steampunk design, with dye-sublimated keycap legends featuring a serif font and a compass accent key on the escape key. The bottom of the keyboard also has an etched Golden Compass pattern. The keycaps follow a more traditional Cherry profile, instead of Keychron's usual KSA or OSA, and they are made from PBT. The Q19 HE 8K has an FR4 switch plate and plate-mounted stabilizers. It is currently available on Keychron's online store for $254.99.The Q19 HE 8K measures in at 115.3 × 303.3 mm and has a front height of 29.2 mm including the keycaps, with the typing angle coming in at 7°. Despite the compact size, the Q19 HE 8K weighs in at 1,488 g. It also features south-facing per-key RGB backlighting, which is customizable via the Keychron Launcher web app, where users can also set the actuation distance and customize features like SOCD, DKS, ModTap, and analogue input. The keyboard also features on-board macros, making it viable as more than just a gaming keyboard.The Keychron Q19 HE 8K also eschews any wireless connectivity, in favor of a simple USB Type-C connection, and it has 8 kHz polling for those who want it. It also includes keycaps for both Windows and macOS modifiers, although it is compatible with Linux as well.

articles.title: Virgin Galactic présente enfin son vaisseau ultra futuriste, le dernier grand espoir du tourisme spatial
articles.text:
Virgin Galactic vient de baptiser le premier vaisseau de sa nouvelle génération : Apeiron. Alors que le tourisme spatial est à l’arrêt, c’est désormais sur lui que reposent les espoirs du secteur. Encore faut-il être en mesure de répondre aux attentes…
Cela fait plus de deux ans que Virgin Galactic n’a plus emmené de passagers aux portes de l’espace. Son dernier vol, assuré par VSS Unity, remonte à juin 2024, et la compagnie a depuis tout misé sur une nouvelle génération de vaisseaux, baptisée Delta. Mais en août, elle a dû repousser le premier vol commercial de ce nouvel appareil, prévu fin 2026, à février 2027. De quoi laisser planer le doute sur le calendrier.
Apeiron, un vaisseau enfin baptisé et prêt pour les essais
L’entreprise vient enfin de franchir une étape symbolique. Ce mercredi 28 octobre, elle a dévoilé le nom du premier vaisseau de sa gamme flambant neuve : Apeiron, un mot du grec ancien qui signifie « l’illimité ». Un choix issu d’un vote public auquel des milliers de personnes ont participé, depuis 83 pays et six continents. Apeiron l’a emporté face à Horizon, Explorer et Ascend, les quatre finalistes retenus parmi 276 idées proposées par les salariés.
Il « illustre l’ambition des vols spatiaux habités et les perspectives qu’ils ouvrent pour l’humanité », assure Michael Colglazier, P.-D.G de Virgin Galactic. L’appareil pourra accueillir six personnes pour un vol suborbital qui franchira la ligne de Kármán, à 100 kilomètres d’altitude, et leur laissera quelques minutes d’apesanteur avec la Terre en toile de fond. À terme, la société espère faire voler chaque aéronef jusqu’à huit fois par mois.
Ainsi, Apeiron, fixé sous son avion porteur Eve, vient de quitter son usine de Mesa, en Arizona, pour rejoindre l’État voisin du Nouveau-Mexique. Les ingénieurs y finaliseront l’avionique et le logiciel de vol avant une vague d’essais au sol, des vols captifs sous Eve, un largage, puis un premier vol propulsé au-delà de 80 kilomètres d’altitude. Concrètement, le chemin à parcourir est encore long avant de pouvoir accueillir les premiers clients.
Virgin Galactic a le champ libre
Virgin Galactic s’apprête à reprendre du service dans un secteur très prometteur il y a quelques années, et désormais abandonné par quasi tout le monde. Aux États-Unis, aucune mission de tourisme spatial n’a eu lieu depuis dix mois, lorsque Blue Origin a décidé de mettre New Shepard en pause pour se concentrer sur New Glenn et la Lune. SpaceX, de son côté, a effectué sa dernière mission touristique avec Crew Dragon en avril 2025, et concentre aujourd’hui toute son énergie sur Starship et l’IA.
Une opportunité en or pour l’entreprise de Richard Branson, qui vise un premier vol commercial au début du deuxième trimestre 2027. Une échéance à prendre, encore une fois, avec prudence. En parallèle, un second vaisseau Delta est déjà en construction pour épauler Apeiron. Car les candidats ne manquent pas : environ 675 clients attendent toujours leur place, dont plus de cent commencent déjà leur préparation.
Mais il va aussi falloir démontrer que ce modèle est rentable. Les appareils devront ainsi être irréprochables et surtout, capables d’enchaîner les vols.
Sources : Ars Technica, Space.com, Virgin Galactic

articles.title: Despite cloud boom, Amazon's stock falls on disappointing earnings and revenue miss - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Despite cloud boom, Amazon’s stock falls on disappointing earnings and revenue miss
Shares of Amazon.com Inc. fell more than 7% in late trading today after the company missed expectations on earnings and revenue and reported rising negative free cash flow as it continues to throw billions of dollars at its cloud infrastructure build out.
The company reported third-quarter earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of just $1.89 per share, trailing Wall Street’s target of $1.96 per share by a fair distance. Revenue for the period came to $201.94 billion, up 12% from a year earlier but below the analyst consensus estimate of $202.31 billion.
Amazon’s results looked even worse as its net income dropped to $20.69 billion, down from $21.19 billion in the same period one year earlier. However, that decrease was primarily due to last year’s $9.5 billion pretax gain from its investment in the artificial intelligence startup Anthropic PBC, which was recorded in last year’s quarter.
The company did better in terms of operating income, which is a more direct indicator of its financial health because it excludes profits and losses from investments unrelated to business performance. Operating income for the quarter came to $28.1 billion, above the Street’s forecast of $26.2 billion.
In a conference call with analysts, Amazon Chief Financial Officer Brian Olsavsky reiterated the company’s capital expenditure forecast, saying the company expects spending to reach $220 billion this year.
Technology giants have been spending money at a blistering pace as they strive to build out their data center networks to meet the surging demand for AI infrastructure, but in recent weeks signs have begun to emerge that the capital expenditure splurge may be peaking. This week, Microsoft Corp. said it’s reducing its capex forecast for the year to $170 billion, down from an earlier target of $175 billion, while Alphabet Inc. maintained its forecast of between $195 billion and $205 billion.
However, Amazon’s decision to reiterate its annual capex target obscured the fact that it spent far more during the previous quarter than anyone had expected — or anyone else. Its third-quarter capex bill reached $77.3 billion, well ahead of the Street’s $58.7 billion estimate, and up from $35.1 billion in the same period last year. On the conference call, Amazon Chief Executive Andy Jassy (pictured) told analysts that the company plans to “spend more meaningfully in 2027,” adding that it has a “clear line of sight to attractive financial returns.”
But investors appeared to be more concerned with how the spending has been eating into the company’s cash flow than any future opportunities it might lead to. The company reported negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion in the quarter, which came after it posted a deficit in the previous quarter too. Olsavsky said the company spent more in the last quarter because it had to purchase more property and equipment for its AI investments.
Amazon had further disappointment for investors when it offered its guidance for the current quarter. It said it’s targeting between $240 billion and $247 billion in fourth quarter revenue, with the midpoint of that range trailing the Street’s forecast of $244.5 billion. The fourth quarter is traditionally Amazon’s biggest because its retail business benefits from holiday shopping season sales revenue.
The more important business is Amazon Web Services, the company’s cloud computing infrastructure unit. It was a bright spot during the quarter, with sales growing 39% from a year earlier to $45..98 billion, just ahead of the Street’s target of $45.9 billion. Jassy told analysts that he’s expecting sales growth to accelerate to “over 40%” in the next year and in fiscal 2028 as a result of the company’s ongoing investments in its AI buildout. “Our AWS investment in functionality and infrastructure is working,” he insisted.
According to Jassy, AWS is on track to generate more than $1 trillion in annual revenue within the next five to 10 years.
Despite that boast, the company remains under pressure to start showing more substantial returns from its ballooning capex spending. Jassy responded, pointing to the growing traction in Amazon Bedrock, which is the company’s AI model marketplace, and increased revenue from its Graviton and Trainium AI chips. Indeed, the chips business “continues to grow triple-digit percentages year-over-year,” Jassy said. He added that the company has plans to make the Trainium chips available to external customers toward the end of next year.
Forrester analyst Tracy Woo told SiliconANGLE that AWS’s results stood out, with the unit continuing to drive strong profitability even as it funds one of the largest of all the AI infrastructure buildouts, with Amazon spending significantly more capital than either Google or Microsoft. “That investment profile suggests Amazon sees future capacity constraints rather than demand constraints,” she said. “For enterprise customers, this demonstrates that cloud competition is increasingly shifting from price to access, with GPUs, foundation models and AI capacity becoming strategic differentiators. AWS’s margin performance suggests customers are currently prioritizing access to these scarce resources over cost optimization.”
The strong showing from AWS was sorely needed because Amazon’s other main business segments struggled to generate much enthusiasm, as both the retail and the advertising units fell short of Wall Street’s expectations. Online sales rose 2% from a year earlier, to $68.47 billion, shy of the $69.68 billion analyst target. That marked a dramatic slowdown from the year-ago quarter, when retail sales grew by almost 10%.
In the advertising segment, revenue rose 11%, to $19.64 billion, trailing the Street’s forecast of $20.82 billion. Jassy said the disappointing performance in both segments was partly the result of the company’s decision to bring its annual Prime Day sale forward in several countries this year. It typically takes place during the third quarter, but it was held during the second quarter instead to avoid conflicting with the FIFA World Cup in July.

articles.title: Want a more affordable iPad alternative? This stylish Oppo tablet I tested could be exactly what you’re looking for, but it's worth keeping these limitations in mind
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Oppo Pad 5 is a capable, affordable tablet with a vibrant and attractive display, stellar software support, and a sleek, attractive build. It may be slightly hefty, and its performance isn’t quite top-tier, but its excellent battery life, bloat-free user experience, and impressive build quality ensure it’s still worth its asking price.
Reasons to buy
- + Beautiful, vivid display
- + Great software experience with limited bloat
- + Excellent battery life
- + Sleek, attractive build…
Reasons to avoid
- - …but not the most lightweight
- - Performance isn’t top-tier
- - Sluggish charging capabilities
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Oppo Pad 5: two-minute review
The Oppo Pad 5 delivers in almost every area that matters. It has a delightfully vibrant display with a smooth 120Hz refresh rate, a user-friendly interface with years' worth of OS and security updates, and boasts a huge battery life to boot.
I’ve been testing the tablet for three weeks now and, overall, I think that it’s worth the £349 asking price, which gives you 8GB of RAM and 128GB worth of storage. It serves up a bloat-free software experience, looks sleek and surprisingly premium, and even performs pretty decently when all’s said and done.
Sure, the MediaTek Dimensity 7300-Ultra processor isn’t the mightiest around, so you shouldn’t expect the sort of performance that the best tablets around can deliver (the Pad 5's bigger brother, the Oppo Pad 5 Pro, has a more powerful Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset), but for simple tasks like drawing and note-taking, scrolling on social media, and light gaming, I found it to be perfectly capable.
You’ll notice some occasional hiccups when running more intensive gaming software or using the split view mode with more demanding programs but, for most users, it will almost certainly do the job.
Some aspects of performance could be better, though. For instance, the built-in speakers don’t sound great, and the onboard cameras are hardly the most impressive (though good enough for video calls). My biggest criticism, though, is that the tablet only supports 33W wired charging, which is too slow for a device with a gigantic mAh battery capacity. As a result, you’ll be waiting for a good couple of hours to get to 100% again.
Still, I didn’t need to charge the Oppo Pad 5 very much during testing at all — only a handful of times across a three-week period. And, all in all, I think it offers plenty for £349. It may not have an OLED screen, but the 2.8K LCD display looks great, with punchy colors, solid contrast, and even Dolby Vision support.
The tablet’s standard of build is also pretty admirable — the aluminium frame and understated colour options make it seem more luxurious than it truly is.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Yes, it's not the lightest tablet around, and there’s no stylus or keyboard bundled in here, but I’d still recommend the Oppo Pad 5 overall. It's a relatively stylish option with largely stable performance and a stand-out display, helping it to compete against pricier rivals, such as the iPad 11-inch (2025).
Oppo Pad 5 review: price & availability
- Priced at £349
- Available now in the UK
- Not sold directly in the US
The Oppo Pad 5 was revealed in 2025, but widespread availability in the UK only came about in 2026. It can't be purchased directly in the US, but could potentially be imported. The tablet is priced at £349, placing it somewhere between the entry level and mid-range categories. It's worth noting, though, that there’s no stylus or keyboard bundled in at this price, so for the full experience you could end up spending upwards of £400 here.
Oppo Pad 5 review: specs
| OS | ColorOS 16.0 | 
| Chipset | MediaTek Dimensity 7300-Ultra | 
| RAM | 8GB | 
| Storage | 128GB | 
| Display | 12.1-inch LCD (2800 x 1980) | 
| Weight | 597g | 
| Battery | 10,050mAh | 
| Charging | 33W wired | 
| Cameras | 8MP rear, 8MP front | 
Oppo Pad 5 review: display
- 12.1-inch LCD screen
- 2800 x 1980 resolution with 120Hz refresh rate
- Solid 900 nits peak brightness
The Oppo Pad 5 has a nice and broad 12.1-inch screen, which is plenty large enough for drawing and playing more intensive games. It has an LCD display rather than OLED, which would’ve been nice to see for deeper black levels and enhanced contrast, but it's common for a more budget-friendly model to opt for LCD.
In terms of resolution, you’re looking at 2.8K on the Oppo Pad 5. There’s also HDR10 and Dolby Vision support, and when I tried watching a movie in the latter format, I was impressed with the detail, vibrancy of colours and quality of contrast on show.
You also get a fairly bright, vivid picture from the Oppo Pad 5, which boasts a peak brightness of 900 nits. I found this to be perfect for brighter indoor spaces, and even moderate outdoor use.
As you may expect, the Oppo Pad 5 has an adaptive refresh rate of 120Hz. This makes basic navigation feel silky smooth, and when gaming, will enable you to play select titles at up to 120fps, so long as the software supports this.
Overall, I was impressed with the display of the Oppo Pad 5. It looks surprisingly sharp given its use of an LCD panel, and its replication of rich, punchy colours exceeded my expectations. It was also nice and responsive, well-sized, and relatively bright making it convenient for everyday use.
- Display score: 4/5
Oppo Pad 5 review: design
- Solid aluminium frame
- Sleek, enticing look…
- …but heftier than you may expect
The Oppo Pad 5 is a nice looking tablet, in my view. Its slim, sleek, and its quality aluminium frame makes it seem like a more premium product than it truly is.
I tried the Starlight Black version, which appears to be reliably available in the UK, with a seemingly elusive Aurora Pink alternative also exists. I like the look of the Starlight Black colorway — it's understated and classy, only adding to that sense that this tablet is punching above its weight, at least in the looks department.
One thing I didn’t love about the Oppo Pad 5, though, was its weight. It comes in at 597g, meaning it’s quite hefty in-use. For reference, that makes the Oppo Pad 5 more than 100g heavier than the Apple iPad 11-inch (2025), so if you want ultimate comfort for long usage sessions, you may be better served elsewhere.
As someone who only typically dips in and out of using my tablet, the Oppo Pad 5’s weight was no problem at all, though. And I did like other aspects of its design. For instance, the buttons are fairly small and low-key, which paired with some smart placement, ensured that I never triggered any accidental presses.
Some may find its IP40 dust and waterproof rating a bit underwhelming, though. This means that the tablet resists larger particle ingress, but is not waterproof whatsoever — so you’ll want to keep it well protected and dry at all times.
The underwhelming IP40 rating and weight of this tablet means that it's not quite a design marvel, but its attractive look and solid build quality ensures that it still feels more premium than its price may suggest.
- Design score: 4/5
Oppo Pad 5 review: software
- ColorOS delivers an excellent user experience
- Next to no bloat whatsoever
- Five years of OS and six years of security updates pledged
Here’s where we get to arguably the best part of the Oppo Pad 5 — the fantastic software experience it provides.
Out of the box, this tablet is running Oppo’s ColorOS 16.0 (running on Android 16), which Android users will find familiar and practical. The user interface is well laid out, and even looks relatively stylish. It's seamless to access apps and settings too, and you can easily customize the home screen and switch between button or motion controls during setup.
What’s great to see is that the Oppo Pad 5 has excellent, long-term software support too. It will receive five years of OS updates, as well as six years of security patches. That’s a commendable pledge from Oppo, and means that users can confidently use this tablet for years to come.
Something else I loved about the Oppo Pad 5 was its almost total lack of bloatware. I’ve reviewed many devices where I’ve been met with a slew of unwanted mobile games, shopping apps, and AI slop, but the Oppo Pad 5 shows more respect to its users. There are a few pre-downloaded third-party apps, like Netflix and LinkedIn, but I’d wager that a large chunk of users would actually want these, so the streamlined app selection gets a big tick from me.
Another positive is that the Oppo Pad 5 is far less concerned with the generative AI nonsense that you see elsewhere, including on some of Oppo’s own products. The AI studio is still here, which enables you to generate some imagery, and there are a few other features, like AI Writer (for proof-reading and formatting) and AI-enabled translation, but again, this functionality isn’t being relentlessly pushed onto you.
- Software score: 5/5
Oppo Pad 5 review: performance
- Solid yet slightly unremarkable chipset
- 8GB of RAM enough for multi-tasking
- Quad speakers don’t sound great
The Oppo Pad 5 runs well overall, but it’s not going to provide you with totally flawless performance.
It uses the MediaTek Dimensity 7300-Ultra processor, which we’ve seen in a bunch of similarly priced rival models, like the OnePlus Pad Go 2. In addition, you get 8GB of RAM, which is easily enough for some basic multi-tasking. And I found the Oppo Pad 5 to run smoothly for the most part, with next to no hiccups when performing basic productivity tasks like note-taking, playing lighter games such as Tetris, or simply scrolling on social media.
I did pick-up on the occasional frame drop with more demanding software, such as 3D mobile games, and some occasional delays when using the split-view mode with Google Chrome, but unless you’re a more intensive user, I think you’ll get by just fine with this model.
One thing that I found to be a little disappointing, though, were the built-in quad speakers. These just don’t sound as refined as I’d hoped, with speech sometimes sounding boxed-in and generally a bit unclear. They’re not plating up super-tinny or shrill sound, sure, and the tablet has excellent codec support for music listening with headphones or speakers, but the built-in sound is lacking.
The built-in cameras are fine enough, though. They’re 8MP on both the front and rear, which is totally adequate for taking video calls, though I didn’t find the results to be overly detailed or natural-looking when snapping some photos.
- Performance score: 3.5/5
Oppo Pad 5 review: battery
- Huge 10,050mAh battery
- Got me through multiple days of use when testing
- Wired charging is disappointingly slow
The Oppo Pad 5 has a huge, 10,050mAh battery capacity, which really impressed me during testing.
Unless you’re an especially intensive user, you’ll easily be able to use the Oppo Pad 5 for multiple days without needing to juice it up whatsoever — I could count on one hand the amount of times I had to charge it across my three weeks of testing. On top of this, you get a number of battery settings, including a power saving, super-power saving, and high-performance mode, and some battery health options.
However, I do have one critique of the Oppo Pad 5 in the battery life department: its underwhelming charging speeds. It supports 33W wired charging, which definitely feels on the low side for a device with a battery this large. After one hour of charging, I discovered that the Oppo Pad 5 hadn’t even hit 50% yet, which is just too slow in my view.
- Battery score: 4/5
Should I buy the Oppo Pad 5?
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
|---|---|---|
| Display | It may not be OLED, but the display is bright, detailed, and colorful. | 4/5 | 
| Design | Sleek, attractive, well-made tablet, but lacks waterproofing and is a tad hefty. | 4/5 | 
| Software | Clean and easy to use UI, excellent OS and security support, next to no bloat. | 5/5 | 
| Performance | Good enough for light everyday use, but not the most powerful, and built-in speakers could be better. | 3.5/5 | 
| Battery | Giant battery capacity let down slightly by underwhelming 33W charging. | 4/5 | 
Buy it if...
You want a top-tier Android user-experience
The Oppo Pad 5 plates up an excellent software experience, with the neat ColorOS, almost no bloatware whatsoever, and years worth of OS and security updates on the way. If you’re looking for an Android tablet that gives you a seamless user-experience, this is one to go for.
You want seriously long battery life
The Oppo Pad 5 comes equipped with a 10,050mAh capacity battery, meaning it will last for multiple days without needing to be charged, unless you’re an especially intensive user.
Don't buy it if...
You want peak performance
You can get better performance from some of the Oppo Pad 5’s rivals, largely due to its slightly middling chipset — even if it's still steady enough for general everyday use.
You’re looking for something ultra-lightweight
The Oppo Pad 5 is slightly on the heavy side, so if you’re looking for an almost feather-weight model that you can take on the go, it may be worth looking elsewhere. 
Oppo Pad 5 review: also consider
| Header Cell - Column 0 | Oppo Pad 5 | Apple iPad 11-inch (2025) | OnePlus Pad Go 2 | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Price | £349 | Starts at £429 | Starts at £319 | 
| OS | ColorOS 16.0 | iPadOS 18 | OxygenOS 15.0.1 | 
| Chipset | MediaTek Dimensity 7300-Ultra | A16 | MediaTek Dimensity 7300-Ultra | 
| RAM | 8GB | 6GB | 8GB | 
| Storage | 128GB | 128GB / 256GB / 512GB | 128GB / 256GB | 
| Display | 12.1-inch LCD (2800 x 1980) | 11-inch LED Backlit (2360 x 1640) IPS LCD | 12.1-inch LCD (2800 x 1980) | 
| Weight | 597g | 475g | 597g | 
| Battery | 10,050mAh | 28.93Wh | 10,050mAh | 
| Charging | 33W wired | 45W wired | 33W wired | 
| Cameras | 8MP rear, 8MP front | 12MP rear, 12MP front | 8MP rear, 8MP front | 
Apple iPad 11-inch (2025)
With ongoing global RAM shortages raging, Apple decided to increase the prices of a lot of its gadgets, and unfortunately, the iPad 11-inch (2025) was among those affected. Now, it starts at £429, but this is still a solid price for the quality on offer. This tablet is stunning, delivers impressive performance, and is lighter than the Oppo Pad 5. Read our full Apple iPad 11-inch (2025) review.
OnePlus Pad Go 2
Just look at that specs table. There are almost no differences whatsoever between the Oppo Pad 5 and the OnePlus Pad Go 2. But if you can grab this one for cheaper, or if you prefer its overall look, it may well be worth picking up instead. It can also be purchased with 256GB of storage in the UK, unlike the Oppo Pad 5. Read our full OnePlus Pad Go 2 review.
How I tested the Oppo Pad 5
- Tested across the course of three weeks
- Tried all major features
- Used for streaming video, playing games, and doing everyday tasks
I used the Oppo Pad 5 as my main tablet across the course of three weeks. During this time, I gradually tested all of its core features and made sure to assess everything from display quality to battery life.
During testing, I tried out video streaming, playing games, and performing everyday tasks to measure the tablet’s performance across the most crucial areas.
More generally, I’ve spent years testing gadgets here at TechRadar, where I serve as a Senior Reviews Writer. I’ve tested everything from Dolby Atmos soundbars like the Sonos Beam Ultra to phones like the Nothing Phone 4(a). I’ve also reviewed tablets during my time here, such as the Huawei MatePad 11.5.

Harry is a Senior Reviews Writer for TechRadar. He reviews everything from party speakers to wall chargers and has a particular interest in the worlds of audio and gaming. Harry has a background in business tech journalism, particularly around the telecoms industry.
