articles.title: Et si une seule ligne de commande suffisait pour installer vos logiciels ?
articles.text:
Pour installer un programme sur Windows, vous avez l'habitude de télécharger un exécutable et de lancer l’assistant ? Et si vous voulez installer plusieurs logiciels, vous répétez cette opération autant de fois que nécessaire… Avec Chocolatey, de nombreux logiciels sont installés et gérés depuis une ligne de commande, à partir de paquets qui peuvent aussi prendre en charge les mises à jour et les dépendances.
Chocolatey est beaucoup plus ancien que Winget, le gestionnaire de paquets propre à Windows. Il s’adresse aussi bien aux particuliers qu’aux administrateurs qui gèrent un parc informatique. Il évite de lancer chaque installateur séparément et regroupe tout en une seule commande.
Une commande plutôt qu’un installateur à chaque fois
Avec Chocolatey, l’installation d’un logiciel passe par une commande telle que choco install firefox. L'outil récupère alors le paquet correspondant et lance l’installation. Il est ainsi possible d’enchaîner plusieurs installations sans ouvrir un par un les assistants respectifs. Par exemple, la commande choco install firefox 7zip notepadplusplus -y permet d'installer ces trois logiciels en une fois, sans demander de confirmation.
Un gain de productivité important lorsqu’il faut remettre un PC en état ou équiper plusieurs machines. Les paquets peuvent gérer des dépendances, tandis que Chocolatey permet de suivre les versions installées et de cibler une version précise lorsqu'elle est disponible. Chocolatey permet également de mettre à jour ou de désinstaller les programmes depuis la même interface. Les utilisateurs avancés peuvent aussi créer leurs propres paquets à partir d’installeurs, de fichiers ZIP ou de scripts PowerShell.
- Installation scriptable
- Dépôts internes compatibles
- Client open source
L'outil open source qui simplifie les installations multiples
Chocolatey ne se contente pas de remplacer quelques clics par une ligne de commande. Il automatise l'installation de plusieurs logiciels. Les paquets peuvent être enchaînés pour préparer une machine complète. Les administrateurs disposent ainsi de fonctions idéales pour le déploiement automatisé et la gestion d’un parc. Pour un usage professionnel, il est toutefois préférable de privilégier un dépôt interne plutôt que de dépendre uniquement du catalogue communautaire.
Cette puissance implique toutefois d'être à l'aise avec les lignes de commande et avec le fonctionnement des paquets. L’installation initiale demande généralement des droits administrateur, même si une installation sans ces privilèges reste possible sous certaines conditions. La version gratuite de Chocolatey suffit pour un usage de base, mais certaines fonctions de gestion d’entreprise sont réservées aux offres commerciales.
Chocolatey facilite la reproduction d'une même configuration logicielle en deux coups de cuillère à pot. Pour quelques programmes de temps en temps, l’intérêt est limité. Dès qu’il faut équiper, réinstaller ou maintenir plusieurs machines, le gain de temps est indéniable.

articles.title: Microsoft Posts Record Q3 2026 Revenue of $92.3 Billion
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
Microsoft Posts Record Q3 2026 Revenue of $92.3 Billion
Microsoft Corp. today announced the following results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the corresponding period of last fiscal year:
- Revenue was $92.3 billion and increased 19%
- Operating income was $45.9 billion and increased 21% (up 22% in constant currency)
- Net income was $36.6 billion and increased 32% on a GAAP basis, and was $36.4 billion and increased 18% (up 19% in constant currency) on a non-GAAP basis
- Diluted earnings per share was $4.92 and increased 32% on a GAAP basis, and was $4.89 and increased 18% (up 19% in constant currency) on a non-GAAP basis
- Non-GAAP results exclude the impact from investments in OpenAI, explained in the Non-GAAP Definition section below
"We are delivering greater capability, choice, control, and cost efficiency for customers across our entire stack," said Satya Nadella, chairman and chief executive officer of Microsoft. "By helping organizations build and own their own intelligence, and earning trust through agent safety and security, we are translating our innovation into growing adoption and real-world impact across every industry."
"We delivered a strong start to the fiscal year with Microsoft Cloud revenue of $63.9 billion, with growth accelerating to 30% (up 31% in constant currency) year-over-year," said Amy Hood, executive vice president and chief financial officer of Microsoft. "Results exceeded expectations across revenue, operating income, and earnings per share."
The following table adjusts for the impact from investments in OpenAI and reconciles our financial results reported in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) to non-GAAP financial results. Additional information regarding our non-GAAP definition is provided below. All growth comparisons relate to the corresponding period in the last fiscal year.*Impact from OpenAI adjusts for the impact from investments in OpenAI
Business Highlights
Revenue in Agents and Infra was $76.8 billion and increased 25%, with the following business highlights:
- Commercial remaining performance obligation increased 73% to $677 billion
- Microsoft Cloud revenue was $63.9 billion and increased 30% (up 31% in constant currency)
- Azure revenue increased 48%
- Microsoft 365 commercial cloud revenue increased 18% (up 19% in constant currency) on an adjusted basis, normalized for a 1-point benefit from in-period revenue recognition in the prior year, and increased 17% (up 18% in constant currency) on a reported basis
- Microsoft 365 consumer cloud revenue increased 17% (up 16% in constant currency)
- Industry solutions cloud revenue increased 10%
Revenue in Devices and Consumer was $15.5 billion and decreased 3%, with the following business highlights:
- Search and advertising revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs increased 12%
- XBOX content and services revenue decreased 2% (down 1% in constant currency)
- Windows OEM and Devices revenue decreased 22%
Microsoft returned $10.2 billion to shareholders in the form of dividends and share repurchases in the first quarter of fiscal year 2027.
Business Outlook
Microsoft will provide forward-looking guidance in connection with this quarterly earnings announcement on its earnings conference call and webcast.
Quarterly Highlights, Product Releases, and Customer Stories
Every quarter Microsoft delivers hundreds of products, services, and enhancements. These releases are driven by years of significant research and development investments, to empower customers with greater productivity, security, and differentiated value.
This momentum is reflected in stories that showcase how our technology is shaping industries and driving customer success. We share innovation updates on our product blogs across Azure, Microsoft 365, and more on our Official Microsoft blog.
Webcast Details
Satya Nadella, chairman and chief executive officer, Amy Hood, executive vice president and chief financial officer, Alice Jolla, chief accounting officer, Brian DeFoe, deputy general counsel and corporate secretary, and Jonathan Neilson, vice president of investor relations, will host a conference call and webcast at 2:30 p.m. Pacific time (5:30 p.m. Eastern time) today to discuss details of the company's performance for the quarter and certain forward-looking information. The session may be accessed at www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor. Participants can also dial into the conference call at (877) 407-0666 or +1 (201) 689-8023 for international, no password required. The webcast will be available for replay through the close of business on October 28, 2027.
Non-GAAP Definition
Impact from investments in OpenAI. In the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, net income and diluted earnings per share were impacted by net gains from investments in OpenAI, which resulted in an increase in net income and diluted earnings per share of $207 million and $0.03, respectively. In the first quarter of fiscal year 2026, net income and diluted earnings per share were impacted by net losses from investments in OpenAI, which resulted in a decrease in net income and diluted earnings per share of $3.1 billion and $0.41, respectively.
Microsoft has provided non-GAAP financial measures related to the impact from investments in OpenAI to aid investors in better understanding our performance. Microsoft believes these non-GAAP measures assist investors by providing additional insight into its operational performance and help clarify trends affecting its business. For comparability of reporting, management considers non-GAAP measures in conjunction with GAAP financial results in evaluating business performance. The non-GAAP financial measures presented in this release should not be considered as a substitute for, or superior to, the measures of financial performance prepared in accordance with GAAP.
Constant Currency
Microsoft presents constant currency information to provide a framework for assessing how our underlying businesses performed excluding the effect of foreign currency rate fluctuations. To present this information, current and comparative prior period results for entities reporting in currencies other than United States dollars are converted into United States dollars using the average exchange rates from the comparative period rather than the actual exchange rates in effect during the respective periods. All growth comparisons relate to the corresponding period in the last fiscal year. Microsoft has provided this non-GAAP financial information to aid investors in better understanding our performance. Statements in this release that are "forward-looking statements" are based on current expectations and assumptions that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results could differ materially because of factors such as:

articles.title: Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 prices hit $2,000, costing more than the RTX 5090 did at launch and with limited stock available — original $999 MSRP long forgotten, with prices now 2-3x higher
articles.text:
Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 prices hit $2,000, costing more than the RTX 5090 did at launch and with limited stock available — original $999 MSRP long forgotten, with prices now 2-3x higher
Nvidia RTX 50-series GPU prices just haven't stopped going up
The Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080, Nvidia's second-fastest GPU from its current generation, now costs as much as the RTX 5090 did, on paper, when it launched. Prices have reached $2,000 and higher, with most of the available stock online limited to third-party sellers. If you can find it in stock, it may end up costing you two to three times as much as it did when it launched.
The cheapest, in-stock RTX 5080 available to buy from a reputable seller online for delivery is this PNY RTX 5080 for $1,999 from Best Buy, the same price as the RTX 5090's on-paper MSRP. You might otherwise end up paying $2,299.99, at least, for this Asus ROG Astral mode at Newegg, or you could pay nearly $3000 for this Gigabyte RTX 5080 from MemoryC, now priced at $2,983.23.
Stock for the RTX 5080 is otherwise limited everywhere, with just one or two available for local pickup (in Best Buy's case), and limited options for delivery. You can also find similar in-store-only pricing at Micro Center, depending on location, which has a Gigabyte card for $1,979.99.
You'll also see a lot of the listings online from sketchy, third-party sellers.. For instance, you could pay at least $2,211.17 for this PNY RTX 5080 from a third-party Amazon seller. Empowered PC, the seller for this card, has had 81% positive ratings over the last 12 months, with 202 ratings in total.
Reputable seller or not, this price scale means you're paying significantly more than the $999 launch price for this GPU. As our GPU price tracking shows, though, this isn't an isolated case. RTX 5080 prices have, like the rest of the RTX 50-series, risen steadily since it launched. However, this is the first time that its price floor has been around the RTX 5090's launch price. That PNY RTX 5080, for instance, was being sold for around $1,500 on average back in August.
It's a bitter pill for gamers, though, that the RTX 5080 has now reached and breached the RTX 5090's launch pricing. That GPU has an MSRP of $1,999, although it'll now cost you thousands more. Prices for the RTX 5090 hit as high as $9,500 last month, but the situation is even worse today. What little stock that remains on sale online can be found for as high as $12,000.
The RTX 5080 uses Nvidia's GB203 GPU and comes with 10,752 CUDA cores, along with 16GB of GDDR7 VRAM. Unfortunately, it, like the rest of the consumer gaming GPU market, is being affected by AI. Demand for high-end GPUs hasn't stopped, but Nvidia's attention has shifted to the enterprise market. So, too, has the focus of memory manufacturers, meaning DRAM allocations and production lines that would otherwise produce memory chips for graphics cards have instead gone to feeding the demand for high-margin HBM for AI data centers.

articles.title: I reviewed a dozen of the year's top TVs — here's why the LG C6 is our TV of the Year, ending Samsung's reign, and holding back next-gen RGB TVs with sheer unbeatable value
articles.text:
Why the LG C6 OLED is my TV of the Year, beating new tech innovations from Samsung, Sony and, uh, LG to prove that the underdog can come out on top
One TV to rule them all
In a year that saw the arrival of next-gen RGB mini-LED to the mass market and elite OLEDs get more impressive and flexible than ever for brightness, my TV of the Year at the TechRadar Product of the year Awards 2026 is, in fact, the mid-range LG C6 OLED TV.
The latest in the LG C-series lineage, the LG C6 earned the full five stars in my LG C6 review, delivering what has always made LG’s C-series TVs among the best TVs around, but taking a few key features to another level (more on that below).
When I compared it to its predecessor, the LG C5, my admiration for the C6 was further solidified, again as the latter showed major upgrades over the former — that's not something you always see in newer TV models. At the time, I said I thought the C5 was better value — but six months on, the C6's price has dropped significantly, and it's now phenomenal value.
This win actually marks LG’s first return to the top of the TV of the Year podium since 2022, with Samsung’s mid-range QD-OLED the S90C taking the crown in 2023, with subsequent victories for Samsung’s flagship OLED models, the S95D in 2024 and the S95F last year. While Samsung released very impressive TVs in 2026, one of the key things we're all looking for even more than usual this year is value, and C6 has a few key elements that make it the best bang for buck.
Accuracy, brightness and power
One of the LG C6’s big upgrades was to its processor. While previous generations of the C-series had used LG's Alpha 9, the C6 was fitted with the Alpha 11 AI Gen 3: LG's most powerful chip, and the same one used in the flagship LG G6. This meant faster processing times for easier use and navigation, as well as upgraded picture features including 13-bit image processing for reduced color banding, and an upgraded brightness booster.
But did these features actually translate into real-world improvements? When I compared the C6 to the C5, the answer was a resounding yes. The C6 registered 1,438 nits peak HDR brightness in Filmmaker Mode in a 10% window — a notable step-up over the C5’s 1,180 nits in the same test. It even hit 245 nits fullscreen HDR brightness, which was 50 nits higher than the C5. That may not sound like much, but for an OLED battling against reflections in bright rooms, it makes a clear difference.
As for actual real-world viewing, the HDR brightness boost was best demonstrated in scenes with a sunset on horizon, such as Wicked and Top Gun: Maverick, where the C6 clearly had higher peak brightness, resulting in punchier HDR highlights. Bright scenes and colors also looked more impactful and engaging on the C6, particularly when large areas of white, such as snow, were on screen.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
But, the thing that impressed me the most with the C6 during my testing was its color temperature accuracy. When I viewed the C6 and C5 together, it was obvious that the C6 had a green tint effect on it (something that has affected OLED panels in the past), which you don't really register when you're watching it solo, but is clear when comparing against other high-end panels.
This was most noticeable in The Batman, namely the scene after he fought with a gang on a subway platform. Watching the scene on both the C6 and C5, they both demonstrated excellent contrast with well-balanced dark and bright tones, but the C6 clearly had a much more accurate color temperature, meaning the gray tones of the walls and platform actually looked gray, whereas the C5’s green tint took away some of that true-to-life accuracy.
Outside of this, the C6 also delivered bolder colors that popped more on screen, more accurate skin tones and slightly more refined dark tones than the C5. Watching Elemental during my C6 testing was a particular treat, as the red, purples, pinks and blues throughout really dazzled on screen. The C5 had also done a great job with that movie, but the C6 just had more.
Unbeatable value
The C6 is not a ‘cheap’ TV by any means, but one thing the C-series has always excelled at is value for money. It’s got a full suite of gaming features, and when you pair it with responsive, smooth performance, it’s easily the best gaming TV available. Its motion is also super smooth for sports, and because it's available in sizes from 42 inches to 83 inches, it’s versatile for any space. It really is a jack-of-all-trades TV.
But in this year’s C6, an exciting new twist happened with its larger 77- and 83-inch models, both known as the LG C6H: they received the same Tandem RGB OLED panel used in the LG G6. And the best part? This came at no changed cost from the LG C5, which used a less-advanced OLED EX panel. So at these sizes, the LG C6 is practically the same TV as the LG G6, but cheaper.
We always worry about price increases from previous models when a TV launches, due to inflation as well as upgrades touted by manufacturers — and obviously this year has been especially hard for tech price rises.
However, the C6 launched for nearly identical prices and those prices have been dropping ever since. At the time of writing, several months from its release in April 2026, you can pick up a 65-inch C6 for $1,499 / £1,799 / AU$3,995 already, which is a $1,200 / £700 price drop (none in Australia yet unfortunately). And with Black Friday around the corner, there’s only more opportunities to get one for less.
When you put its upgraded performance and features over its predecessor, stable prices, upgraded panels in larger sizes at no extra cost and its genuine value for money together, the C6 is my obvious pick for TV of the Year. Yes, there may be more impressive TVs out there if money's no object, but here in 2026 money very much is an object — and no other TV ticks all the box boxes, including value, so impressively.

articles.title: Microsoft cambiará el botón de reinicio de Windows 11 para evitar confusiones al actualizar
articles.text:
Microsoft prepara cambios en Windows Update para evitar que los usuarios de Windows 11 reinicien sus computadoras mientras una actualización de seguridad todavía está en proceso de instalación.
La decisión llega después de que trabajadores de la compañía y especialistas en seguridad informática advirtieran que el sistema muestra el botón azul “Reiniciar ahora” antes de que todos los componentes estén listos.
El problema quedó expuesto durante la instalación de la actualización de seguridad KB5127648, correspondiente a octubre de 2026. En una captura compartida en X por Nathan McNulty, arquitecto de seguridad y profesional reconocido por Microsoft como MVP, Windows Update mostraba que el parche apenas había alcanzado el 2 % de progreso, pero ya ofrecía la posibilidad de reiniciar el equipo.
Microsoft confirmó que este comportamiento responde al diseño actual de Windows Update y no a un error de programación. Sin embargo, Aria Hanson, responsable de producto de Windows, señaló que la compañía estudia modificar el aviso para distinguir mejor entre las actualizaciones que ya están listas y aquellas que todavía necesitan tiempo para completarse.
Por qué Windows 11 muestra el botón antes de terminar
La confusión surge porque Windows Update puede gestionar varias actualizaciones al mismo tiempo. En la captura difundida por McNulty, el parche acumulativo de seguridad seguía instalándose, mientras una actualización de .NET Framework y un controlador de audio ya figuraban como pendientes de reinicio.
Ante ese escenario, el sistema muestra el botón azul «Reiniciar ahora» para permitir que los usuarios instalen los componentes que ya están preparados. El inconveniente es que el aviso no deja suficientemente claro que otras tareas siguen en curso.
Jen Gentleman, responsable de Microsoft, explicó que algunas actualizaciones pueden estar listas para instalarse tras un reinicio, aunque otras todavía no hayan terminado. Por su parte, Hanson sostuvo que quienes acceden manualmente a Windows Update suelen tener experiencia con la administración de sus equipos o reciben una notificación cuando el proceso está completo.
Sin embargo, esta lógica puede inducir a error a quienes interpretan el aviso como una señal de que todas las actualizaciones finalizaron.
El calendario de actualizaciones explica el comportamiento
El funcionamiento también está relacionado con una modificación que Microsoft introdujo el 28 de julio de 2026. Desde entonces, la compañía retiene en los equipos personales determinadas actualizaciones de .NET, controladores y firmware para instalarlas junto con el parche mensual de seguridad.
El objetivo es reducir la cantidad de reinicios que necesita una computadora durante el mes. En lugar de solicitar varios reinicios por separado, Windows intenta agrupar las tareas en un mismo proceso.
No obstante, esa coordinación puede provocar que algunos componentes queden listos antes que la actualización principal. Por eso, el aviso de reinicio puede aparecer cuando el parche de seguridad todavía está en ejecución.
Qué ocurre si el usuario reinicia antes de tiempo
Reiniciar cuando una actualización acumulativa todavía se está instalando puede prolongar el arranque y dejar el equipo temporalmente fuera de servicio. Joel Coehoorn, especialista reconocido por Microsoft como MVP, advirtió que Windows podría necesitar completar las tareas pendientes durante el inicio del sistema.
En algunos casos, ese proceso puede extenderse durante aproximadamente media hora. También existe la posibilidad de que el equipo solicite un segundo reinicio para terminar de aplicar los cambios.
El riesgo no significa necesariamente que la computadora vaya a sufrir daños, pero sí puede generar interrupciones y retrasos, especialmente en equipos utilizados para trabajar.
Microsoft revisará el aviso de Windows Update
Hanson confirmó que el equipo de Windows está evaluando un cambio que permita atender dos necesidades: quienes quieren reiniciar cuanto antes porque sus actualizaciones prioritarias ya están listas y quienes prefieren esperar hasta que termine toda la instalación.
La compañía no ha anunciado una fecha para implementar el rediseño ni ha detallado cómo será la nueva interfaz. Mientras tanto, los usuarios pueden reducir el riesgo de confusión al revisar el estado de cada actualización antes de reiniciar.
La recomendación es desplegar la lista completa de tareas y comprobar que ninguna siga instalándose. También conviene prestar atención al porcentaje de progreso y no confiar únicamente en el botón azul o en el icono de reinicio de la barra de tareas.
El problema, además, no es nuevo: usuarios de Windows ya habían reportado un comportamiento similar en 2020. Casi seis años después, Microsoft reconoce la necesidad de mejorar la información que presenta Windows Update, aunque el cambio todavía no tiene fecha confirmada.

articles.title: Underwater data centers are heading for waters that endangered whales call home
articles.text:
In context: Pilot projects have demonstrated that undersea data centers can operate reliably without significant heat-dissipation issues. However, underwater environments support fragile ecosystems that could be seriously disrupted by artificial computing infrastructure.
Earlier this year, DeepGreen Holdings filed a preliminary permit application with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC). The company is seeking to develop two data center projects designed to take advantage of underwater environments, but the proposed locations overlap with habitats of two endangered whale populations. Local communities have also voiced strong opposition to the projects.
DeepGreen plans to build its facilities beneath Cook Inlet, in Alaska, and in the Gulf of Maine. The proposed Cook Inlet facility would consist of 66 modular data center "pods," powered by 330 to 350 tidal turbines. The company expects the installation to generate 100 megawatts of power, most of which would be used to run the underwater data center.
The Maine project would be smaller, with 50 tidal turbines providing 51 megawatts of power to a cluster of data center pods. Both projects could affect the habitats of two distinct endangered whale populations. Cook Inlet is home to a genetically isolated population of beluga whales, while the Gulf of Maine serves as a feeding ground for North Atlantic right whales.
Cook Inlet's beluga population numbers around 300 individuals, while fewer than 400 North Atlantic right whales remain in the population relevant to the Maine project. Whales rely on echolocation to navigate underwater environments, find food, and communicate with one another. The proposed data centers could affect their surroundings both during construction and once the facilities are operational.
According to Arial Brewer, a beluga researcher at the University of Washington and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, "skittish" animals such as whales could experience stress in different and unpredictable ways as a result of the proposed underwater data centers.
DeepGreen's plans are unprecedented in both scale and the extent of the areas they could affect. Pilot projects such as Microsoft's Project Natick have demonstrated that underwater data centers can support reliable computing operations without significant overheating problems. Seawater helps dissipate heat, potentially limiting some of the environmental impacts associated with cooling.
However, no one has yet attempted a project on the scale DeepGreen is proposing. Only two operational underwater data centers are currently known to exist, and both are located in Chinese waters. The proposed US facilities would be substantially larger, leaving little directly comparable evidence to establish their potential environmental impact.
For now, construction has not begun. FERC representative Celeste Miller said that a preliminary permit does not authorize a project to be built. The commission also required DeepGreen to amend its original proposal because it did not provide sufficient documentation concerning Indigenous tribes with historical ties to the affected areas.
According to real estate developer Louis Wolfson, who is behind DeepGreen, the company has no immediate plans to begin construction. He said DeepGreen is willing to comply with any requirements designed to protect the local environment, adding that equipment would be deployed only if it could "operate safely well within federal marine mammal thresholds."

articles.title: Microsoft fixes a Windows 11 annoyance as PC revenue declines
articles.text:
Microsoft is beginning the rollout of a Windows 11 preview update that finally addresses a persistent power user complaint with the operating system: the right-click menu that obliterated years of muscle memory on command locations and hid others behind an additional click. The timing is notable, as the announcement comes alongside Microsoft’s quarterly financial report, which showed a continued decline in the business of selling Windows licenses for new PCs.
The preview update, KB5127936, is cumulative for Windows 11 versions 26H2 and 25H2. The update will be a gradual rollout before eventually moving on to a normal rollout for all Windows 11 devices once it reaches general availability. The highlight of the new update should calm annoyed users who have spent years with custom scripts and services in an attempt to shape Windows the way they would prefer it. Users will get a “customize menu” button that controls what commands appear when they right-click their mouse. Users can toggle built-in commands such as Send To or Create Shortcut on or off, rearrange what appears on the main menu, and control which third-party extensions show up in either the main or submenus. The gripe with the right-click menu had been that Microsoft hid familiar command locations behind a top row of icons while moving other familiar commands under the “Show more options” submenu. Now, Windows users can customize the whole thing around their habits.
The new preview also highlights a new Windows feature called Cloud Rebuild, a recovery option that can reinstall Windows 11 directly from the cloud, even when an existing Windows 11 fails to boot. Cloud Rebuild will pull the Windows 11 image and needed system drivers directly from Windows Update. Users will not need a custom recovery image or external media to reinstall Windows. There is an important distinction to note, however. Microsoft classifies Cloud Rebuild as a recovery option, but it behaves more like a fresh Windows install than a repair, as existing applications and files will not be included. Those worried about data security can sanitize entire system drives prior to reinstalling. For a full list of improvements coming to Windows 11, including changes to Xbox mode and settings, you can view the official Microsoft release announcement.

articles.title: Andy Jassy says Prime Video is on track to earn 'tens of billions of dollars' | TechCrunch
articles.text:
It’s been four years since Amazon bought MGM for $8.5 billion. But coming off the blockbuster success of this year’s hit movie “Project Hail Mary,” Hollywood has become a lucrative business for the e-commerce giant.
Prime Video, Amazon’s streaming service, “has emerged as a significant business with a revenue run rate in the tens of billions of dollars and is now profitable in its own right,” Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on the quarterly earnings call on Thursday. Jassy had previously told investors in May that Prime Video was profitable, but being on track to generate tens of billions is a new detail.
Amazon said its movie studio, Amazon MGM Studios, has brought in more than $1.2 billion in global box office sales so far this year, helped by hits like “Project Hail Mary” and “Verity.”
“Project Hail Mary” grossed an estimated $684 million worldwide, according to The Numbers. Starring Ryan Gosling and based on Andy Weir’s novel, the film opened in theaters in March and became Amazon MGM Studios’ highest-grossing release, according to entertainment reports. (The studio also had at least one notable flop this year: “Melania.”)
Jassy also named a number of TV shows as hits, including “Carrie,” “The Summer I Turned Pretty,” “The Boys,” “Off Campus,” “Fallout,” and “Reacher.” Season 4 of “Reacher” drew 66 million viewers globally in its first 28 days, the company says, with more to come. Season 5 is filming now, and the show was picked up for a sixth season. (And if you don’t follow Alan Ritchson, the star of “Reacher,” on Threads, you are missing out on an actor who has turned a friendly-yet-witty reply into an art form.)
Sports have also been a significant driver. Prime Video broadcasts NASCAR, the Masters, and UEFA Champions League soccer, but Thursday Night Football appears to be its biggest success this year. The first six games of this season have averaged 17.7 million viewers, up 16% from last year, according to Nielsen figures Amazon shared. The streaming service also attracted over 2 million viewers for its second season of the NBA on Prime, Nielsen said.

articles.title: HyperX Omen 35L review: A polished gaming PC for deep pockets
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The HyperX Omen 35L delivers a premium gaming PC experience, pairing a striking black-and-white styling, quiet operation, enthusiast-grade features, and excellent 4K gaming performance. Top-end configurations make the most sense, as entry-level models are expensive for the hardware.
Reasons to buy
- + Impressive gaming performance
- + Sharp black-and-white case
- + Standard liquid cooling
- + Quiet operation
- + Fully modular power supply
Reasons to avoid
- - Steep starting price
- - No USB4/Thunderbolt 4 ports
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
HP’s HyperX Omen 35L is ambitious, and it’s hard not to be impressed by it in our maxed-out test guise with a Ryzen 9 9950X3D and Nvidia RTX 5080. From its monochrome design and extensive RGB lighting to its top-tier components, it checks the boxes enthusiasts are looking for.
But when a PC is $6,211 like our test configuration, it raises the question of whether the Omen 35L’s blend of style, performance, and premium features is enough to justify a purchase, even if that's what high-end PCs cost right now.
Design of the HyperX Omen 35L
The HyperX Omen 35L’s black and white case stands out, looking refreshingly modern, even though parent company HP has used similar designs before. At 8.27 by 16.06 by 16.14 inches, it’s firmly in mid-tower territory. The metal case feels reassuringly solid and makes extensive use of tempered glass. Bright RGB fans shine through the front while many RGB-lit components are visible through the side panel. It’s a classy system.
The contrast continues inside, where the black motherboard, graphics card, and power supply are easily visible against the white case. The white liquid cooling loops are especially attractive, as is the CPU cooler featuring its own LCD panel. The latter shows CPU and GPU temperatures.
HyperX Omen 35L Specifications
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D | 
| Motherboard | HP AMD B850 | 
| Memory | 64GB DDR5-6000 (2x 32GB) | 
| Graphics | Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 (16GB GDDR7, 2,617 MHz boost clock) | 
| Storage | 2x 1TB PCIe 5.0 SSDs (non-RAID) | 
| Networking | Realtek 8922AE Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.0 | 
| Front Ports | 10 Gbps USB-C, 2x 5 Gbps USB-A, audio combo jack | 
| Rear Ports | 2x 10 Gbps USB-C, 2x 5 Gbps USB-A, 4x USB 2.0, DisplayPort 1.4, Ethernet | 
| Power Supply | 1,000 W fully modular | 
| Cooling | 240 mm LCD liquid cooler | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 Pro | 
| Dimensions (WxDxH) | 8.27 x 16.06 x 16.14 inches (210 x 408 x 410 mm) | 
| Price (as configured) | $6,210.98 | 
Ports and Upgradeability on the HyperX Omen 35L
HyperX’s top-mounted front ports include USB-C (10 Gbps), two USB-A (5 Gbps), and an audio combo jack. This location works well if the desktop is on the floor.
At the back, the tower offers a pair of USB-C ports (10 Gbps), two USB-A (5 Gbps), four USB 2.0, DisplayPort 1.4 output, Ethernet, and audio jacks. It’s disappointing to see a desktop this expensive offers neither USB4 nor Thunderbolt 4, though it does include Wi-iFi 7 and Bluetooth 6.0 from a Realtek 8922AE networking card. The wireless antennas are built into the chassis, eliminating the need for external protrusions. It’s also notable that HP offers a Clear CMOS button, a surprise on a mainstream tower.
The HyperX Omen 35L offers about as much upgradeability as expected from a mid-tower, without proprietary parts. Its side doors are secured with thumbscrews; the slide rearward and away. The mATX-style motherboard offers four DDR5 DIMM slots, populated in our review unit with two 32GB RGB HyperX modules running at 6,000 MHz.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The system also supports two M.2 2280 drives. The primary slot is covered in a substantial heatsink just above the RTX 5080. Accessing the other slot requires removing the RTX 5080. The card is secured with five screws, two of which hold it to the front support bracket. Deft fingers are required to reinstall the screws at the back of the card.
HP’s wiring work is tidy for a mainstream tower. Sleeved cables would have improved the refinement. On the plus side, HP includes a fully modular power supply, an uncommon feature in big box systems.
Gaming and Graphics on the HyperX Omen 35L
We tested the HyperX Omen 35L in a maxed-out configuration featuring a Ryzen 9 9950X3D processor, 64GB of RAM, and a GeForce RTX 5080.
I fired up 007 First Light to test out this system’s prowess. At a 3840 x 2160 resolution with high settings and post effects enabled, I saw up to 120 frames per second (fps) indoors and in the mid-90 fps range in more complex scenes without DLSS. The game never stuttered and remained supremely playable.
The systems we’re using for comparison include a pair of RTX 5090 towers, the Alienware Area-51 (Ryzen 9950X3D, $5,749.99 when tested, $8,899.99 as of this writing) and the Maingear MG-1 (Ryzen 9 9950X3D2, $7,067 when tested, $9,076 as of this writing), plus Corsair’s Vengeance a7500 powered by a Ryzen 7 9800X3D and an RTX 5070 Ti ($2,799.99 when tested, $3,299.99 as of this writing). With its RTX 5080, the HyperX desktop ought to slot in the middle of this group.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The HyperX desktop performed as expected given its RTX 5080. That said, the 1080p numbers show significant variance from system to system. In Shadow of the Tomb Raider (Highest detail preset), the HyperX produced 300 fps to outperform even the Alienware (248 fps), though it couldn’t catch the Maingear (355 fps). In other instances, even the RTX 5070-powered Corsair was able to pull ahead as seen in Far Cry 6 (Ultra settings), where it produced 197 fps against the HyperX’s 141 fps.
But these desktops are designed for 4K play. At that resolution, the HyperX’s RTX 5080 produced admirable numbers. Naturally, it wasn’t in the same league as the RTX 5090 systems; in Red Dead Redemption 2 (Medium settings), the HyperX produced 83 fps against the Alienware’s 122 fps and the Maingear’s 121 fps, and in Borderlands 3 (Badass settings), the HyperX landed at 115 fps against Alienware’s 166 fps and Maingear’s 186 fps. The differences narrowed in Far Cry 6, with the HyperX producing 118 fps to Alienware’s 128 fps. The largest deltas were seen in Cyberpunk 2077 (Ray Tracing Ultra preset), where the HyperX produced 36 fps, well ahead of the Corsair’s 29 fps, but significantly behind the Alienware’s 55 fps. Overall, though, this HyperX desktop is well-suited to 4K play.
We stress-test gaming desktops running 15 loops of the Metro Exodus benchmark at RTX settings, simulating about half an hour of gameplay. During the test, the HyperX desktop averaged 172.21 fps across all runs with a sub-one fps variance, indicating stable performance. During the test, the Ryzen 9 9950X3D averaged 4.79 GHz and 48 degrees Celsius while the RTX 5080 ran at 2.74 GHz and 50 C.
Productivity Performance on the HyperX Omen 35L
Our HyperX test unit features a Ryzen 9 9950X3D processor, 64GB of RAM, and two 1TB PCIe 5.0 drives running separately, one hosting the OS andthe other for storage.
Featuring the same Ryzen 9 9950X3D processor, the HyperX and Alienware systems performed similarly across our CPU tests. In Geekbench 6, the HyperX system produced 19,923 points against Alienware’s 20,411 points, though it was handily outperformed by the Ryzen 9 9950X3D2-powered Maingear, at 23,741 points. With fewer cores, the Ryzen 7 9800X3D-powered Corsair finished last, at 18,124 points.
The HyperX desktop finished our Handbrake 4K-to-1080p video transcoding test in 1 minute and 47 seconds, tying the Alienware, though the Maingear edged ahead, at 1:32. The Corsair took nearly twice as long, at 3:02.
In our 25GB file transfer test, the HyperX’s average transfer speed of 3,197.42 MBps was excellent, just behind Alienware’s 3,414.29 MBps and ahead of the Corsair’s 2,659.94 MBps and Maingear’s 2,782.43 MBps.
Software and Warranty on the HyperX Omen 35L
HP includes several useful apps. Omen Gaming Hub app provides performance control, with per-fan RPM settings and, in Extreme mode, PPT and EDC settings for the Ryzen 9 CPU. The Advanced Performance Tuning section also provides PBO, CPU Boost, and voltage curve controls plus a benchmark to test your settings. For quick access, the app provides an overlay that shows your power profiles and system monitoring, including component temperatures and fan speeds.
Gaming Hub also provides customization of the LCD display on the liquid cooler. Many faces are available, from system monitoring to static images, GIFs, videos, and a clock. It seems simple, but it’s one of the most fun features of the system, allowing you to easily change up the look.
Lighting is managed through Omen Light Studio, which provides per-device RGB control. Fine control is possible – each of the five fans has 10 LEDs, which are individually selectable. Clicking and dragging selects multiple fans and LEDs at a time, to which you can apply preconfigured light recipes – Galaxy, Ocean, Jungle, Volcano, and Omen – and apply an effect, such as wave, static, ambient, breathing, color cycle, an audio visualizer, and radial. The speed and direction of the effect is also configurable. You can also create layered effects and save everything in profiles that you can export or import. HP covers the HyperX Omen 35L with a standard one-year warranty.
HyperX Omen 35L Configurations
We tested the HyperX Omen 35L with a Ryzen 9 9950X3D processor, 64GB of dual-channel DDR5-6000 RAM, GeForce RTX 5080 graphics, Windows 11 Pro, and two 1TB PCIe 5.0 solid-state drives. The system uses a 1,000W power supply and a 240 mm liquid CPU cooling with a built-in LCD display. This configuration represents the top of the stack, retailing for $6,210.98.
The entry-level is probably where the Omen 35L offers the least value – with standard liquid cooling and a modular power supply, this system is for premium builds. AMD-based starter configurations begin at $2,399.99 with a Ryzen 5 9600X or $2,589.99 with an Intel Core Ultra 5 250KF Plus. Standard components include a GeForce RTX 5060 Ti (8GB), 16GB of memory, and 1TB of PCIe 4.0 storage. Memory tops out at 128GB and two SSDs are supported up to 2TB each.
Bottom Line
Primarily, the HyperX Omen 35L gets one thing right: it feels genuinely premium. Its sharp black-and-white design, quality lighting, quiet operation, and enthusiast-grade components like a modular power supply give it the polish it needs to compete against boutique builders and aftermarket systems. Its performance in our test system with a Ryzen 9 9950X3D and an RTX 5080 match the expectations for this lofty price point.
That said, it’s clear that this desktop is aimed at the more premium side of the market, as prices of the entry-level configurations are difficult to justify given their level of hardware. But if you have deep enough pockets for a well-equipped configuration, the HyperX Omen 35L is a highly compelling gaming desktop well worth considering alongside anything the market has to offer.
Charles Jefferies is a freelance reviewer for Tom’s Hardware US. He covers laptop and desktop PCs, especially gaming models.

articles.title: Maxed-out Mac Studio costs nearly $45K in Canada
articles.text:
Apple’s Mac computers are known for being on the pricey side, and the ongoing memory and component shortage caused by AI data centres and other issues hasn’t helped. Still, the company’s new maxed-out Mac Studio spec is… well, it costs as much as a new car.
$44,898.98, to be exact. Here’s the breakdown:
- In Canada, the Mac Studio M5 Ultra starts at $7,799.
- The 36-core CPU, 80-core GPU is $1,950, bringing your total to $9,749.
- Now this is the big money. If you want 512GB of RAM, it’s $23,250, bringing your total to $32,999.
- 16TB of storage costs $11,250, bringing your total to $44,249.
- And if you want to add some software like Final Cut Pro pre-installed, it’s $399.99, and Logic Pro pre-installed costs $249.99.
- Bringing your total to $44,898.98 or $2,030.20/mo for 24 months at 7.99 per cent APR.
While fun to point at the big, crazy number and have a laugh, this isn’t a purchase most people will make.
A fully loaded Mac like this might make sense for high-level video work, 3D modelling, locally run AI workloads, and other stuff that requires huge amounts of memory.

articles.title: Samsung pode lançar dobrável mais barato após sucesso do Galaxy Z Fold 8 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Samsung pode lançar dobrável mais barato após sucesso do Galaxy Z Fold 8
Fabricante avalia ampliar a linha de dobráveis em 2027 com uma versão de tela maior ou outra mais barata.
A Samsung pode expandir sua linha de dobráveis no ano que vem com um modelo mais em conta. Segundo um novo vazamento da cadeia de fornecimento na Coreia do Sul, a fabricante avalia lançar um segundo celular dobrável no formato mais largo, como o Galaxy Z Fold 8, após as vendas do aparelho atual superarem as expectativas.
A empresa estaria considerando duas opções: uma versão com tela interna maior ou um modelo com dimensões semelhantes às do Z Fold 8, mas com especificações mais simples e, consequentemente, preço menor. Apenas uma das alternativas deve chegar ao mercado.
Os nomes Galaxy Z Fold 9 Plus e Galaxy Z Fold 9 FE seriam considerados para o novo dispositivo. Vale lembrar que a família Z pode chegar ainda maior no ano que vem: além do modelo base, Ultra e dessa suposta terceira versão, a sul-coreana também considera lançar uma segunda geração do Galaxy Z TriFold na mesma janela. O Galaxy Z Flip, por outro lado, pode ser aposentado.
A avaliação de um segundo modelo do tipo passaporte teria sido motivada pelo desempenho comercial do Galaxy Z Fold 8. A fabricante não divulga números individuais de vendas dos dois modelos, mas informou que o Galaxy Z Fold 8 e Fold 8 Ultra venderam juntos 45% mais unidades na Europa durante as primeiras nove semanas do que a geração anterior no mesmo período após o lançamento, segundo o GSMArena.
A expansão da família também ocorre em um momento de maior concorrência entre dobráveis de formato semelhante, que estreou com o Huawei Pura X Max em abril, mas que deve se tornar ainda mais popular com o recém-lançado iPhone Duo, primeiro dobrável da Apple.
Rumores também apontam que gigante de Cupertino estaria planejando versões em formatos diferentes e em configurações mais básicas para os próximos ciclos.

articles.title: Binance estimates $6.3B impact from security breach, freezes $3B in crypto assets
articles.text:
Binance estimates $6.3B impact from security breach, freezes $3B in crypto assets
Binance said a preliminary investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop as the possible entry point for the breach. The exchange has suspended deposits and withdrawals and pledged to cover customer losses.
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has estimated the total impact of a major security incident at around $6.3 billion, with approximately $3 billion worth of affected digital assets frozen on-chain in coordination with blockchain partners.
In an update issued on October 30, 2026, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume said its preliminary investigation suggested that the incident may have originated from a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer. The attacker allegedly used the access to enter a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.
Binance said it had found no evidence of any wallet private-key compromise. It added that a detailed technical post-mortem would be published once the investigation was complete and the findings verified.
Binance has temporarily suspended all deposits and withdrawals as a precaution while security checks are underway. It has also revoked authorisation for the affected address and engaged law enforcement agencies and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and recover the funds.
Binance said it would cover all losses arising from the incident through its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company funds, assuring customers that their assets remained safe. It also plans to publish an updated Proof of Reserves once remediation is complete.
The incident has prompted a wider industry response, with blockchain partners and digital asset issuers freezing funds linked to the breach. Binance said that approximately $3 billion had been frozen on-chain so far, with recovery efforts continuing.
The exchange said it is working with law enforcement agencies to identify those responsible. The full extent of the breach and the final amount of losses remain subject to investigation.

articles.title: Pentagon IG refuses to investigate Starlink/Starshield slowdown in Ukraine
articles.text:
The Pentagon inspector general’s office declined a request from US senators to investigate restrictions recently imposed on the Ukraine military’s use of SpaceX’s satellite network.
Ukraine, which uses SpaceX’s Starlink service and the military version known as Starshield, said earlier this month that military drones lost satellite connectivity when traveling above 161 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour). The limit was removed after about 10 days.
Five Democratic and four Republican senators sent an October 15 letter to Department of Defense Inspector General Platte Moring, asking for a probe into the reported disruptions of Starlink and Starshield. The letter asked, among other things, “whether any restrictions on Starlink or Starshield services were directed, authorized, or implemented by SpaceX, the Department of Defense, or other US government entities; whether such restrictions were consistent with applicable US government contracts, and what actions, if any, the Department of Defense took in response.”
Platte told the senators in a letter Tuesday that the questions should be directed to the US Air Force and Space Force, according to CNN. “They are better suited to address the matters raised in your letter and to coordinate any Department responses to your questions,” Moring wrote.
A spokesperson for the Pentagon inspector general’s office told Ars today, “The Department of War Office of Inspector General (The DoW OIG) answered recent correspondence from members of Congress regarding Starlink… We carefully considered the congressional request and determined that the matters raised were best addressed by the DOW. Should new information come to light, we may reconsider.”
We asked the Department of Defense whether it plans to investigate and will update this article if it responds.
Democrats and Republicans want answers
The satellite problems “were discovered after the administration threatened to withhold intelligence to Kyiv over its strikes on Russian refineries and after President Donald Trump made a deal to buy Russian diesel and ease sanctions on Moscow,” CNN wrote.

articles.title: Algunos familiares de las víctimas de Urda están recibiendo SMS falsos sobre la identificación de los fallecidos
articles.text:
Mientras continúan los trabajos para identificar a las víctimas del accidente ferroviario de Urda, en Toledo, algunos familiares de posibles víctimas mortales han recibido SMS falsos en los que alguien se hace pasar por la Guardia Civil. Los mensajes informan de supuestas identificaciones, pero el instituto armado ha desmentido que los envíe y ha aclarado que estas comunicaciones se realizan siempre en persona.
La aclaración va más allá de los SMS denunciados por las familias. En un vídeo publicado en sus canales oficiales, uno de sus portavoces explica que las identificaciones se comunican "de forma presencial y personal, nunca vía mensajes de texto, WhatsApp o llamada telefónica". Es decir, tampoco una llamada o un WhatsApp constituyen vías válidas para recibir esta información.
La advertencia no procede únicamente de la Guardia Civil. El Centro de Integración de Datos (CID), formado por especialistas forenses y miembros de los cuerpos de seguridad, también ha alertado de esta suplantación. En un comunicado difundido por el Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Castilla-La Mancha, el organismo pide a los posibles afectados que no den credibilidad a estas comunicaciones.
Para facilitar este proceso, la Guardia Civil ha solicitado la colaboración de los familiares de primer grado de las personas desaparecidas. En las oficinas habilitadas pueden aportar información y muestras de ADN que ayuden a establecer la identidad de las víctimas. La institución ha pedido que acudan lo antes posible para agilizar los trabajos y ha precisado que, si ya han facilitado sus datos en estas dependencias, serán los agentes quienes se pondrán en contacto con ellos cuando tengan noticias.
La suplantación de una institución mediante mensajes de texto recuerda a una práctica conocida en ciberseguridad como smishing. El Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad (INCIBE) explica que esta modalidad de fraude busca obtener información o comprometer dispositivos. En el caso de Urda, sin embargo, lo confirmado es la suplantación de la Guardia Civil para comunicar supuestas identificaciones. No han trascendido demasiados detalles sobre el contenido de los mensajes ni se conoce quién está detrás de estas comunicaciones o cómo ha conseguido los números de teléfono de los familiares.
Los familiares que necesiten información pueden acudir directamente a las dependencias habilitadas por la Guardia Civil en cuatro ciudades: Madrid, en Batalla del Salado, 32; Sevilla, en avenida de la Borbolla, 8; Córdoba, con entrada por avenida de los Mozárabes; y Toledo, en avenida Barber, 42. Además, existen cuatro teléfonos de asistencia: el 062 de la Guardia Civil, el 900 122 112 del Servicio de Emergencias de Castilla-La Mancha, el 900 10 10 20 de Renfe y el 900 001 403 de Iryo. Todos ellos son canales de información y ayuda, no vías para notificar identificaciones.

articles.title: Vivo pode comprar Vero e reforçar operação de fibra • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Vivo pode comprar Vero e reforçar operação de fibra
Segundo o Estadão, conversas seguem sem acordo; provedora também atua no mercado de telefonia móvel virtual.
A Telefônica Brasil, dona da Vivo, estaria avaliando a compra da provedora Vero. Segundo apuração do Estadão, assessores já teriam sido contratados e as negociações estariam em andamento, mas ainda não existe um acordo.
Se avançar, a operação reforçaria a presença da Vivo no mercado de fibra óptica e ampliaria sua base de clientes. A Vero também levaria para a companhia uma operação de telefonia móvel virtual que atende consumidores e fornece estrutura para outras marcas.
O principal ativo é a base de banda larga. Dados da Anatel colocam a Vero com aproximadamente 1,29 milhão de acessos de internet fixa, na sexta posição do mercado brasileiro. A Vivo aparece em segundo lugar, com cerca de 8,54 milhões, atrás apenas da Claro.
A Vero atende centenas de municípios em estados como Minas Gerais, São Paulo, Paraná, Santa Catarina e Rio Grande do Sul. Uma eventual compra também se encaixaria em meio à integração entre outros grandes e médios provedores. Nesta semana, a Giga+ admitiu que mantém conversas com a Sky sobre uma possível combinação.
Além da internet fixa, a Vero é uma operadora móvel virtual (MVNO) que utiliza a rede da TIM. Em junho, a companhia tinha cerca de 340 mil usuários móveis, que já representavam 7% de sua receita. A empresa também fornece infraestrutura para que outras companhias ofereçam planos de celular com suas próprias marcas.
Entre as empresas credenciadas estão Veek, Salvy, Ampernet e provedores regionais. Esse negócio poderia interessar à Vivo por oferecer uma estrutura já montada para atender marcas menores, embora ainda não esteja claro qual seria seu papel em uma eventual aquisição.
A possível venda ocorre em um momento de pressão financeira. A Vero teria dívida líquida próxima de R$ 3 bilhões e perdeu parte de sua base de assinantes neste ano. A Vivo, por sua vez, vem reforçando sua infraestrutura de fibra. Em maio, passou a controlar 100% da FiBrasil, companhia criada para operar redes de fibra óptica. A compra da Vero ampliaria sua presença no varejo de banda larga e acrescentaria a operação móvel virtual.
Por enquanto, não há contrato assinado nem garantia de que o negócio será concluído. Até que as empresas anunciem uma decisão, também não há mudanças confirmadas para os clientes.

articles.title: Une faille critique vieille de 16 ans menace des serveurs dans le monde entier, et la patcher partout s'annonce compliqué
articles.text:
Branle-bas de combat chez les principaux fournisseurs de firmwares UEFI. Une faille critique dans EDK II permet à un attaquant d'exécuter du code malveillant avant même le chargement du système d'exploitation. Le nombre de serveurs concernés demeure inconnu, mais la diffusion de ce code pourrait imposer des vérifications et des mises à jour à très grande échelle.
Cette fois, mettre à jour l’OS ne suffira pas à régler le problème : la vulnérabilité touche le firmware UEFI chargé d'initialiser le matériel et de préparer le démarrage avant que le système d'exploitation prenne la main. Pour le concevoir, des fournisseurs comme AMI, Insyde et Phoenix s'appuient sur EDK II, une base de code open source reprise dans les firmwares de serveurs du monde entier. Des chercheurs d'Anthropic et de Google y ont décelé une erreur de gestion de la mémoire vieille de 16 ans, que TianoCore, la communauté responsable du projet, a rendue publique la semaine dernière. Le correctif a déjà été intégré au code source d'EDK II, mais sa distribution s'annonce autrement plus compliquée que sa mise au point.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Une erreur de mémoire exploitable avant le chargement du système
Pour comprendre de quoi il retourne, il faut savoir que dans les centres de données, le démarrage réseau, ou PXE, permet aux administrateurs d'installer ou de restaurer des serveurs sans intervenir physiquement sur chacun d'eux. Lorsqu'une machine démarre de cette façon, elle récupère sur le réseau un programme qui lui permet ensuite de lancer un système d'exploitation, un outil d'installation ou un environnement de maintenance. Elle peut ainsi être préparée à distance, même si son disque ne contient encore aucun système fonctionnel.
Pendant cette opération, le firmware reçoit également des messages ICMP, utilisés entre autres pour signaler des erreurs de communication sur le réseau. EDK II leur réserve un espace mémoire de 504 octets, mais le programme ne vérifie pas correctement la quantité de données qu'il y copie. Lorsqu'un message dépasse la taille prévue, les données supplémentaires débordent de cet espace et écrasent une partie de la mémoire voisine. Ce dépassement de tampon, désormais référencé CVE-2026-97631, affiche un score de gravité de 9,5/10 selon TianoCore.
Si cette faille est considérée comme critique, c'est parce qu'un attaquant capable d'envoyer un message ICMP piégé pendant cette phase de démarrage peut provoquer le plantage du serveur et empêcher le lancement du système. Plus grave encore, s'il connaît suffisamment bien la version du firmware ciblé, il peut également détourner l'exécution du programme pour lancer son propre code au niveau de privilège le plus élevé du processeur. Et comme l'attaque se joue avant que Secure Boot ait pu vérifier les composants du système d'exploitation, elle pourrait permettre l'installation d'une charge malveillante persistante.
Un correctif publié trop tôt, mais qui pourrait arriver très tard
Selon Ars Technica, les chercheurs Alex Matrosov, d'Anthropic, et Dan Holmes-Mitra, de Google, avaient initialement prévu de révéler la vulnérabilité en janvier 2027, afin de laisser aux fabricants le temps de préparer leurs patchs. Mais dès septembre, AMI a bousculé ce calendrier en publiant sur GitHub une proposition de correction qui permettait aussi de repérer les lignes de code à l'origine de la faille. TianoCore a finalement intégré le correctif à EDK II le 15 octobre, avant de publier son avis de sécurité une semaine plus tard.
Le patch ne nécessite pas de modifier les clés ou les certificats Secure Boot, contrairement à certaines vulnérabilités découvertes par le passé. Son déploiement doit néanmoins passer par plusieurs intermédiaires : les fournisseurs de firmwares doivent d'abord intégrer le code corrigé, puis les fabricants de serveurs publier de nouvelles versions UEFI pour leurs équipements. Les entreprises devront ensuite installer ces mises à jour sur leurs machines.
Cette chaîne de mises à jour s'annonce d'autant plus laborieuse que l'étendue exacte des équipements affectés demeure inconnue. Intel assure n'avoir identifié aucun produit vulnérable parmi ceux qu'il prend encore en charge, tout en précisant que des fabricants de cartes mères peuvent avoir intégré le composant à leurs propres firmwares. Arm estime de son côté que la faille ne touche pas directement ses produits. AMD, AMI, Phoenix, Microsoft et Amazon n'avaient pas répondu aux sollicitations d'Ars Technica lors de la publication de son enquête.
Du côté des hébergeurs, Hetzner a annoncé le 28 octobre avoir ouvert une enquête pour déterminer si ses équipements sont concernés, tout en recommandant à ses clients d'éviter les redémarrages des machines utilisant PXE jusqu'à nouvel ordre.
En attendant, les administrateurs doivent vérifier auprès des fabricants si leurs serveurs embarquent le composant vulnérable et désactiver le démarrage réseau lorsqu'il n'est pas nécessaire. Les serveurs qui ne reçoivent plus de mises à jour de leur fabricant pourraient ne jamais bénéficier du correctif.

articles.title: Noté 8/10 chez nous, le TV Mini LED TCL 75X11L perd 800 € en avant-première du Black Friday — Frandroid
articles.text:
Jusqu’ici réservée aux diagonales géantes et quasi introuvable en magasin, la série X11 de TCL change de formule en 2026. Le TCL 75X11L en est la porte d’entrée, et il se place au-dessus du C89L dans la gamme du fabricant. Ses cibles sont ambitieuses (et assumées) : les OLED LG G6 et Samsung S99H, mais aussi les RGB Mini LED comme le Samsung R95H ou le Sony Bravia 9 II. Noté 8/10 dans notre test, il ne coche pas toutes les cases, mais les 800 euros de remise pendant cette période de pré-Black Friday peuvent changer la donne.
Les atouts du TCL 75X11L
- Une dalle SQD Mini LED avec 11 520 zones de rétroéclairage
- Une excellente colorimétrie en HDR, avec Dolby Vision et HDR10+
- Quatre ports HDMI 2.1 et une dalle 144 Hz pour jouer
Le TCL 75X11L passe de 3 299 euros à 2 499 euros chez Boulanger, dans le cadre des offres Black Friday en avant-première.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant le TCL 75X11L. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Une image qui brille de face, beaucoup moins de côté
Le 75X11L repose sur une dalle SQD Mini LED découpée en 11 520 zones de rétroéclairage. TCL revendique jusqu’à 10 000 cd/m² sur les plus grandes diagonales (9 000 cd/m² annoncés pour ce 75 pouces), mais dans notre test, ce pic lumineux s’est montré bref. Il se rattrape sur la couleur. En HDR, la colorimétrie est excellente et la couverture de l’espace BT.2020 large. Le blooming (ces halos autour des objets lumineux sur fond noir) est bien maîtrisé quand on est assis bien en face.
En revanche, les angles de vision sont très limités : dès que l’on s’éloigne de l’axe, le blooming refait surface et l’image perd de sa superbe. Le traitement antireflet déçoit aussi pour un TV de ce prix.
Un vrai terrain de jeu, avec un meuble à prévoir
Pour le jeu vidéo, le 75X11L est exemplaire. La dalle monte à 144 Hz en natif (jusqu’à 288 Hz en Full HD avec le mode Game Accelerator), et les quatre ports HDMI 2.1 permettent de brancher une console de salon, un PC de jeu et une box sans jouer aux chaises musicales avec les câbles. VRR, ALLM et FreeSync Premium Pro sont aussi de la partie. Côté logiciel, il tourne sous Google TV avec Gemini.
Le design est soigné, avec des finitions premium et une petite barre de son Bang & Olufsen intégrée au bas de l’écran. Attention en revanche à l’encombrement. Les pieds se fixent sur les côtés, et l’ensemble mesure 165,8 cm de large. Il vous faudra donc un meuble très large, ou passer par la fixation murale (support non fourni).

articles.title: La révélation tant attendue de The Elder Scrolls 6 serait imminente
articles.text:
En juin 2018, lors de l’E3, Bethesda officialisait The Elder Scrolls 6 avec un court teaser, sans rien de concret à se mettre sous la dent. Depuis, Todd Howard, directeur du jeu, a reconnu à plusieurs reprises qu’il aurait préféré l’annoncer « plus discrètement ». La fenêtre de sortie, elle, reste inconnue.
Huit ans ont passé, donc, et les choses pourraient enfin bouger pour le RPG devenu une arlésienne. Selon Tom Warren, journaliste de The Verge, qui a publié l’information ce jeudi 29 octobre, un certain The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel pourrait refaire parler de lui dès le mois prochain. Bethesda Game Studios a montré le jeu en interne ces derniers mois, avec des sessions de jeu en direct, dont l’une devant Asha Sharma, patronne de Xbox.
Le nom de The Elder Scrolls 6 serait bientôt officiel
Bethesda et Microsoft continueraient d’opter pour une communication assez chiche, en n’officialisant que le nom complet. The Verge relie cette annonce aux 15 ans de Skyrim, sorti le 11 novembre 2011, soit huit jours avant la sortie de GTA 6, prévue le 19 novembre. Un timing étrange. Ce serait donc The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, une information qui avait été devinée par les fans après un message d’Asha Sharma. En août, elle avait écrit : « Session de jeu en direct de The Elder Scrolls VI: ******** ce matin. L’ampleur et la grandeur sont incroyables. L’histoire est encore plus grandiose. » Les « ******** » renvoient aux huit lettres formant le mot « Sentinel ».
The Verge en profite pour ajouter que les indiscrétions à propos de la région où se déroulerait The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel sont justes. On ferait donc cap vers Hammerfell (Martelfell ou Lenclume), territoire désertique au climat chaud dont sont originaires les Rougegardes (des guerriers redoutables à la peau foncée). La région est déjà apparue dans la saga, dans The Elder Scrolls 2: Daggerfall, The Elder Scrolls Adventures: Redguard et le MMO The Elder Scrolls Online.
Toujours selon Tom Warren, Sentinel serait le premier épisode consacré à l’histoire des Elder Scrolls eux-mêmes, ces mystérieux artefacts antiques qui donnent son nom à la saga.
On espère que la communication finira par s’accélérer pour The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel. La révélation du nom en novembre pourrait n’être qu’un petit apéritif pour une présentation beaucoup plus poussée à l’occasion des Game Awards, le 10 décembre, vitrine idéale pour montrer le jeu, éventuellement en guise de one more thing.

articles.text:
Enceintes portables, enceinte de soirée, home cinéma sans compromis et casque gamer : la sélection avant le Black Friday couvre un large spectre de besoins audio, avec des prix réduits allant jusqu’à moins 50 %. Les meilleures offres audio du pré Black Friday
- JBL Charge 5 à 99 euros au lieu de 199 euros
- JBL Xtreme 4 à 199 euros au lieu de 329 euros
- Sony Bravia Theatre Quad à 1490 euros au lieu de 1999 euros
- JBL Quantum 950 à 199 euros au lieu de 299 euros

Cette sélection ne vous inspire pas ? Nous vous proposons de consulter notre guide d’achat des meilleures enceintes Bluetooth. En complément, nous avons une sélection des meilleures barres de son du marché. Enfin pour être complet, nous avons un guide d’achat des meilleures enceintes de soirée.
JBL Charge 5
Vous êtes à la recherche d’une enceinte Bluetooth compacte, robuste et vraiment musicale ? La JBL Charge 5 mérite qu’on s’y arrête. Contrairement à sa prédécesseure, elle embarque une architecture à deux voies : un haut-parleur dédié aux basses et médiums, un tweeter pour les aigus, chacun avec son propre amplificateur. Le résultat est un son articulé, équilibré, sans agressivité dans les hautes fréquences. Certifiée IP67, elle encaisse l’eau et la poussière sans broncher, et son autonomie annoncée de 20 heures tient la distance. À noter : pas de microphone intégré, les appels mains libres sont donc impossibles.
Les points forts de la JBL Charge 5
- Architecture 2 voies avec tweeter dédié
- Autonomie annoncée de 20 heures
- Certification IP67, étanche et anti-poussière
La JBL Charge 5 est disponible à 99 euros chez Boulanger au lieu de 199 euros, soit 100 euros d’économie.
JBL Xtreme 4
Plus imposante, la JBL Xtreme 4 vise un usage tout-terrain : plage, jardin, camping, soirée en extérieur. Ses quatre transducteurs délivrent 100 watts, avec un équilibre tonal soigné et une extension dans les graves que la Charge 5 ne peut pas égaler. Elle passe la barre des 2 kg, mais sa sangle amovible rend le transport raisonnable. La batterie est remplaçable par l’utilisateur, ce qui est rare dans cette catégorie. Le port USB-C fonctionne dans les deux sens : il charge l’enceinte, mais aussi vos appareils. En revanche, le mode longue autonomie tronque sensiblement les basses fréquences, ce qui peut décevoir à l’écoute.
Les points forts de la JBL Xtreme 4
- 100 watts, son ample et bien équilibré
- IP67, résistante à l’eau et à la poussière
- Batterie remplaçable par l’utilisateur
La JBL Xtreme 4 est proposée à 199 euros chez Boulanger au lieu de 329 euros, soit 130 euros d’économie.
Sony Bravia Theatre Quad
Le Sony Bravia Theatre Quad s’adresse à ceux qui veulent transformer leur salon en véritable salle de cinéma. Ce système audio est conçu pour reproduire un son spatial complet : il prend en charge le Dolby Atmos et le DTS:X, et se connecte au téléviseur via HDMI eARC pour une intégration sans compromis. Avec ses dimensions compactes pour un système de cette envergure (30,6 cm de hauteur), il s’installe discrètement sous un écran. C’est un investissement conséquent, pensé avant tout pour les installations home cinéma exigeantes.
Les points forts du Sony Bravia Theatre Quad
- Dolby Atmos et DTS:X pour le son spatial
- Connexion HDMI eARC pour intégration téléviseur
- Format compact pour un système home cinéma complet
Le Sony Bravia Theatre Quad est affiché à 1490 euros chez Boulanger au lieu de 1999 euros, soit 509 euros d’économie.
JBL Quantum 950
Vous cherchez un casque gaming sans fil polyvalent sans y mettre le prix fort ? Le JBL Quantum 950 est conçu pour le jeu sur PC, mais aussi sur console, avec une connectivité sans fil via son dongle USB et le Bluetooth en complément. Il embarque un microphone détachable et une réduction de bruit active, deux atouts appréciables pour les longues sessions ou le jeu en équipe. Son positionnement tarifaire le place dans la catégorie des casques gaming milieu de gamme sérieux. Pour le replacer parmi ses concurrents, notre guide des meilleurs casques gaming pour PC liste les alternatives à considérer.
Les points forts du JBL Quantum 950
- Connexion sans fil via dongle USB et Bluetooth
- Réduction de bruit active intégrée
- Microphone détachable pour le jeu en équipe
Le JBL Quantum 950 est disponible à 199 euros chez Boulanger au lieu de 299 euros, soit 100 euros d’économie.
JBL Partybox Club 120
Pour animer une soirée, la JBL PartyBox Club 120 n’a pas grand-chose à envier aux équipements de sonorisation professionnels d’entrée de gamme. Ses 160 watts et ses quatre transducteurs produisent jusqu’à 100 dB, avec un grave profond et une résolution sonore qui surprend pour une enceinte festive. Trois zones d’éclairage dynamiques accompagnent la musique, et la connectique est complète : entrées ligne, micro et guitare, pour brancher à peu près n’importe quelle source. La batterie est amovible et l’autonomie annoncée atteint 12 heures. En dehors des soirées, elle peut aussi s’utiliser en écoute quotidienne, d’autant qu’elle fonctionne par paire en stéréo. Sa seule limite réelle : à 11 kg, elle ne se glisse pas dans un sac à dos.
