articles.title: L'OLED va-t-il enfin dépasser les 100 pouces ? LG Display prépare une offensive de taille
articles.text:
Alors que les téléviseurs LCD MiniLED dépassent désormais allègrement les 100 pouces (254 cm), l'OLED reste cantonné à des diagonales plus modestes. LG Display prépare toutefois une nouvelle étape industrielle en Chine, avec une ligne de modules OLED pouvant atteindre 111 pouces.
Hisense, TCL et Samsung multiplient les téléviseurs géants, avec des diagonales atteignant désormais 115 ou 116 pouces. Mais à ces dimensions, le LCD règne presque sans partage. L'OLED, lui, plafonne à 97 pouces dans les gammes grand public, avec des tarifs qui le réservent à une clientèle particulièrement fortunée. La situation pourrait néanmoins évoluer. LG Display et son partenaire chinois Guangkai Holdings viennent d'annoncer un investissement destiné à développer l'assemblage de modules OLED de très grande taille dans leur usine de Guangzhou, en Chine.
Un milliard de yuans pour préparer l'OLED de 111 pouces
Dans une communication publiée le 26 octobre, le groupe public chinois Guangkai Holdings annonce une augmentation de capital de 1 milliard de yuans, soit environ 120 millions d'euros, au bénéfice de sa coentreprise avec LG Display. Les deux partenaires participeront au financement selon leurs parts respectives : 70 % pour LG Display et 30 % pour Guangkai Holdings. Cette répartition concerne bien l'activité OLED de Guangzhou, distincte de l'ancienne usine LCD cédée à TCL CSOT en 2025.
L'investissement servira à moderniser les installations existantes pour assembler des modules OLED de 77, 83, 97 et surtout 111 pouces. Selon les informations communiquées par Guangkai Holdings et relayées par les médias chinois, il s'agirait de la première ligne de modules OLED au monde dédiée à cette diagonale.
Il faut toutefois faire une distinction essentielle, LG Display ne construit pas une nouvelle usine de fabrication de dalles. Le projet porte sur l'assemblage des panneaux en modules prêts à être intégrés dans des téléviseurs ou des écrans professionnels. Autrement dit, cet investissement prépare une capacité industrielle, cela ne constitue pas pour autant l'annonce d'un téléviseur OLED de 111 pouces. Les deux partenaires n'ont d'ailleurs communiqué ni calendrier de mise en service ni capacité de production pour cette nouvelle ligne.
Le LCD conserve un sérieux avantage sur le prix et la luminosité
L'enjeu dépasse largement la course aux pouces. Car si l'OLED conserve de sérieux arguments pour le home cinéma, notamment ses pixels autoémissifs, ses noirs parfaits et l'absence de blooming, les téléviseurs LCD MiniLED ont pris une longueur d'avance sur le marché des écrans géants.
L'écart de prix est particulièrement révélateur. Le LG OLED97G6 de 97 pouces affiche un prix public de 25 099 euros en France, tandis que le Hisense 116UXS RGB MiniLED de 116 pouces a été annoncé à 16 999 euros. À ces tarifs indicatifs, le modèle le plus grand coûte donc 8 100 euros de moins.
Et le prix n'est pas le seul argument du LCD. Les meilleurs modèles MiniLED peuvent également atteindre des pics de luminosité supérieurs à ceux des téléviseurs OLED, un avantage notamment pour les contenus HDR et les pièces très lumineuses.
Pour LG Display, développer des modules OLED au-delà de 100 pouces représente donc un double défi : conserver les qualités d'image de sa technologie tout en améliorant la compétitivité de ses grandes diagonales. La modernisation des installations pourrait contribuer à cette évolution, mais l'assemblage ne constitue qu'une partie du coût total d'un écran OLED.
Surtout, il faudra trouver des débouchés et savoir quels fabricants décideront d'exploiter ce futur format. LG Display fournit des panneaux à plusieurs constructeurs, dont LG Electronics, Sony, Samsung et Philips, mais aucun téléviseur OLED de 111 pouces n'a encore été officiellement annoncé.
Avec cet investissement, le fabricant sud-coréen montre néanmoins qu'il entend franchir le cap symbolique des 100 pouces. Un marché sur lequel le LCD a pris une avance considérable, et où l'OLED devra prouver qu'il peut s'imposer aussi sur le prix.

articles.title: D2C brands don't need an AI team to get discovered and grow, says Shopflo
articles.text:
D2C brands don't need an AI team to get discovered and grow, says Shopflo
What if your next customer is an AI agent? At TechSparks 2026, Mihir Shah of Shopflo by Pine Labs explained how brands can connect product catalogues to AI shopping platforms and drive conversions.
AI assistants are becoming shopping destinations, but keeping up with them can stretch lean teams.
Shoppers are beginning to turn to AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude to discover products, compare options and make buying decisions. For direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands, this raises a new question: how do they stay visible as shopping behaviour changes, without building an in-house AI team?
At TechSparks 2026, Mihir Shah, Chief Business Officer at Shopflo by Pine Labs, presented two ways the company aims to help brands tackle this challenge: agentic commerce, which connects product catalogues to AI-powered discovery and shopping surfaces, and AI agents that help businesses improve growth and operational efficiency.
“You don't need an AI team to figure out growth or efficiency for you. You need Shopflo,” Shah said.
Getting products in front of AI shoppers
Brands have spent years building visibility through search engines, marketplaces, and social media. AI assistants are adding another discovery channel, where shoppers can describe what they need and receive product recommendations.
Shopflo's agentic commerce offering aims to make participating brands' catalogues available across AI-native platforms, including ChatGPT, Claude and other emerging interfaces, said Shah. Through integrations, the company streams product catalogue information to these surfaces, allowing shoppers to discover relevant products and, where supported, proceed towards checkout.
For instance, a shopper looking for festive gifts under Rs 2,000 could discover products from a participating brand through an AI assistant. Shopflo's integration with Pine Labs' payments infrastructure is designed to support transactions through these experiences.
Shah argued that brands will need to look beyond traditional discovery channels as consumer behaviour evolves. However, AI visibility does not replace search engine optimisation (SEO), which continues to contribute to website traffic.
AI agents put growth decisions in context
Discovery is only one part of running a D2C business. Brands must also balance conversion rates, average order value, returns, customer retention and profitability, often using separate tools for each function, said Shah.
Shopflo's Growth Orchestrator, which Shah said was available in beta, aims to bring these decisions together. Brands can define their priorities, whether that means pursuing growth or protecting profitability, and receive recommendations based on their store's performance data.
During the demonstration, Shah showed how the system could identify a drop-off between address entry and payment, suggest a fee-transparency banner and propose an experiment to test whether the change improves conversions.
Brands can review recommendations, set limits and approve experiments before scaling them. They can also decide how much autonomy to give the agents.
“How much or how little to use the agents is under your control,” Shah said.
For D2C businesses working with lean teams, the proposition is less about adopting every new AI tool and more about making existing growth decisions easier to manage. Shopflo's approach combines AI-led discovery with tools that help brands act on their own business goals, while leaving the final decisions in their hands.

articles.title: Binance probes potential $5.8 billion crypto-theft hack
articles.text:
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance is investigating a potential security breach involving up to $5.8 billion in digital assets, in what could become the largest cryptocurrency hack in history.
If confirmed stolen, the amount would far exceed the $1.5 billion stolen from Bybit by North Korean hackers in February 2025, the largest confirmed crypto heist on record.
The suspected breach has already prompted stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle to freeze more than $2.3 billion in assets associated with the incident.
In a statement to BleepingComputer, a Binance spokesperson confirmed that the exchange was investigating reports of a potential security issue while reassuring customers that their funds were safe.
"Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating. Rest assured that user funds are completely safe," the spokesperson told BleepingComputer.
"Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information."
Binance also warned customers to remain cautious of scams and avoid unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information.
Binance founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) said on X that the incident appeared to be a hack, while noting that he no longer manages the exchange and expects all user funds to be fully covered.
Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said on X that the company had frozen more than $1.567 billion in USDT associated with the potential Binance hack.
Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire also confirmed that the company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC linked to the incident, adding that Circle was coordinating with law enforcement and would continue supporting the investigation.
Billions transferred from Binance hot wallets
The statements follow reports of billions of dollars in cryptocurrency being transferred from multiple Binance hot wallets to a newly created Ethereum address.
According to blockchain transaction analysis shared on X by crypto journalist StarPlatinum, a Binance hot wallet known as "Binance 14" transferred approximately $2.53 billion across 64 cryptocurrency tokens, followed 24 seconds later by another $174.4 million from a second Binance wallet.
A later update claimed that a third Binance hot wallet transferred another 780 million USDC to the same Ethereum address, bringing the reported total to approximately $3.48 billion.
Meanwhile, blockchain intelligence platform Arkham Intelligence is tracking 55 cryptocurrency addresses under an entity labeled "binance-hacker-1029," with combined holdings valued at approximately $5.78 billion.
The tracked assets include approximately $1.77 billion in USDT, $1.44 billion in Bitcoin, $876 million in Ethereum, and $823 million in USDC.
Blockchain explorer Etherscan has also labeled the initial receiving address as "Binance Hot Wallet Exploiter 2," assigning it both "Exploit" and "Heist" tags.
However, it should be noted that Arkham's $5.78 billion figure is the value of assets held across all tracked wallets, rather than a confirmed amount stolen from Binance.
Binance has not yet confirmed whether the transfers were unauthorized, how the suspected breach occurred, or the total value of any stolen assets.
This is a developing story and will be updated as more information becomes available.

articles.title: Buying Laptops for a Team: Why Standard Models Beat Letting Everyone Pick Their Own - Tech Guide
articles.text:
In today’s fast-paced business environment, equipping your team with the right technology is crucial for productivity and efficiency. When it comes to purchasing laptops for a team, many organizations face a common dilemma: should each employee choose their own device, or should the company standardize on a single model?
While offering freedom of choice might seem appealing and empowering, standardizing laptop models often proves to be the smarter decision. This article explores the key reasons why standard models outperform a free-for-all approach and how it benefits your business in the long run.
Choosing laptops for a team is more than just picking devices-it’s about creating a cohesive, manageable, and secure IT ecosystem. The decisions made at this stage impact not only the immediate user experience but also support costs, security posture, and operational efficiency. In fact, a study by IDC found that companies that implement hardware standardization experience a 30% reduction in IT support costs within the first year.
Streamlining IT Support and Maintenance
One of the most significant advantages of standardizing laptops is the simplification of IT support and maintenance. When every employee uses the same model, IT teams can create streamlined processes for troubleshooting, repairs, and updates. This consistency reduces downtime and helps technicians resolve issues more quickly.
For example, Computers Made Easy’s tech support model highlights how a uniform hardware setup allows support teams to efficiently manage devices, reducing the complexity of their workflows. This approach not only saves time but also cuts costs associated with managing multiple configurations and compatibility issues.
According to a report by Spiceworks, 80% of IT professionals stated that device standardization improves support efficiency and reduces helpdesk tickets. 
When every laptop is identical, IT staff can maintain a single image for operating systems and software deployment, reducing the number of variables that cause technical issues. This homogeneity enables faster rollouts of updates and patches, lowering the risk of security vulnerabilities caused by inconsistent software versions.
Moreover, having a standard laptop model simplifies training for IT personnel. Support teams don’t need to master multiple device types or configurations, which increases their proficiency and reduces the learning curve for new hires.
Cost Savings Through Bulk Purchasing
Another compelling reason to standardize laptop models is cost savings. Buying the same laptop in bulk often allows companies to negotiate better prices and receive volume discounts from manufacturers or suppliers. This advantage can be substantial, especially for larger teams.
Moreover, having a uniform fleet simplifies warranty management and replacement parts inventory. Instead of stocking multiple types of components, IT departments only need to maintain a limited range of spare parts, which can lower inventory costs and accelerate repairs.
Research from TechRepublic shows that organizations with standardized hardware save up to 20% on procurement and maintenance costs annually.
Bulk purchasing also provides leverage when negotiating service agreements or extended warranties. Vendors are often more willing to offer favorable terms when dealing with a single, consistent order rather than a fragmented set of devices. This can translate into longer warranty periods, faster replacement services, or bundled support plans.
Furthermore, standardization reduces the hidden costs associated with device diversity, such as increased training and administrative overhead. When employees use different laptops with varying capabilities, IT must spend extra time configuring and supporting each model, which adds to labor costs.
Enhancing Security and Compliance
Security is a top priority for businesses today. Managing a diverse range of laptops with different operating systems, software versions, and hardware configurations makes it challenging to maintain consistent security protocols. Standard models simplify the implementation of security policies, making it easier to deploy patches, updates, and antivirus solutions uniformly.
With standardized devices, companies can enforce encryption, endpoint protection, and network access controls more effectively. This consistency also aids in meeting compliance requirements, which often mandate strict control over device configurations and software versions.
Cranston IT’s technical expertise emphasizes the importance of technical expertise in ensuring that security measures are properly integrated into standardized hardware, reducing vulnerabilities and protecting sensitive data.
A survey by Ponemon Institute found that 62% of data breaches are linked to endpoints such as laptops and mobile devices, underscoring the importance of consistent security management. 
Standardization allows IT teams to rapidly deploy security patches across all devices, minimizing the window of exposure to threats. Additionally, uniform hardware configurations mean security tools can be optimized for a single platform, improving their effectiveness.
Compliance with regulations such as GDPR, HIPAA, or PCI-DSS often requires detailed control and documentation of endpoint security. Standardized laptops make it easier to audit systems and demonstrate adherence to these standards.
Improving Collaboration and User Experience
When everyone uses the same laptop model, collaboration becomes smoother. Team members share a common user experience, making it easier to assist one another with technical issues or software usage. Training sessions are also more effective because the instructor can focus on a single platform rather than multiple variations.
Standardization can enhance productivity by minimizing compatibility problems. For example, certain specialized software may run optimally on specific hardware, and having a uniform setup ensures all employees can use these tools without interruption.
A unified environment also fosters better communication within teams. When sharing files, troubleshooting issues, or collaborating on projects, employees can rely on consistent performance and capabilities. This reduces frustration and supports seamless teamwork.
Moreover, standardized laptops facilitate easier integration with company-wide collaboration tools and cloud services. IT departments can ensure that all devices meet minimum requirements for software like video conferencing, project management, or virtual desktops, leading to a more reliable user experience.
Simplifying Asset Management and Lifecycle Planning
Managing company assets is far easier when laptops are standardized. IT departments can track inventory, assign devices, and schedule upgrades more efficiently. Predictable replacement cycles allow better budget planning and reduce the risk of unexpected expenses.
Additionally, uniform hardware facilitates easier deployment of new software or operating system upgrades, as testing can be done on a single model rather than multiple devices.
Standardization also supports sustainability initiatives by simplifying recycling and disposal processes. When devices are consistent, companies can partner with vendors to implement take-back or refurbishment programs more effectively.
According to Gartner, companies that standardize their hardware experience 25% less downtime related to hardware failures, which translates to higher overall productivity. 
Addressing Employee Preferences
A common argument for letting employees pick their own laptops is that it boosts satisfaction by catering to personal preferences. While this may hold some truth, it often comes at the expense of the benefits outlined above.
Companies can balance employee needs by choosing a few standardized models that cover different use cases-such as lightweight laptops for mobile workers and powerful machines for design teams. Offering limited choices within a standardized framework can satisfy individual preferences without sacrificing the advantages of uniformity.
Another approach is to provide standardized laptops with configurable options like RAM or storage upgrades. This allows some degree of customization while maintaining a controlled environment.
It’s important to communicate the rationale behind standardization to employees, highlighting how it benefits their productivity and security. Involving team leads or representatives in the selection process can also increase buy-in and satisfaction.
Conclusion
Purchasing laptops for a team is a strategic decision that impacts operational efficiency, security, and cost management. While allowing every employee to pick their own device might seem like a way to increase satisfaction, the benefits of standardizing on specific laptop models are clear. From streamlined IT support and significant cost savings to enhanced security and simplified asset management, standard models help businesses stay agile and focused.
By adopting a thoughtful, standardized approach to technology procurement, organizations can ensure their teams are equipped with reliable, secure, and cost-effective tools that enhance productivity and collaboration.
Making the right choice now will pay dividends in the future-both for your IT department and your entire workforce. Standardizing laptops is not just an IT decision; it’s a business strategy that supports growth, innovation, and resilience.

articles.title: El Trump Mobile ya está aquí y presume de ser 100% hecho en EEUU. Literalmente es un HTC chino de 2024
articles.text:
En Estados Unidos se está dando un cambio de rumbo en la fabricación de dispositivos. El Gobierno ha empujado para que empresas como Apple fabriquen sus dispositivos en el país apoyados por una Intel que quieren convertir en la gran fundición estadounidense y, para dar ejemplo, el propio Donald Trump anunció un móvil: el Trump Mobile T1.
El multimillonario y presidente del país americano presumió de que el T1 sería un dispositivo 100% estadounidense. Concretamente, iba a ser un terminal "diseñado y construido en Estados Unidos", pero este año rebajaron el tono para adecuarse un poco más a la realidad, cambiando por un "orgullosamente ensamblado en EEUU".
De esa promesa al final hay un trecho porque, para sorpresa de nadie, no era cierto.
Cuando se lanzó el móvil ya contamos que el terminal era, básicamente, un HTC U24 Pro, un modelo de 2024 que estaba desfasado en 2025 y que, en 2026 cuando se lanza este Trump Mobile T1, tiene unas especificaciones que se quedan lejos de lo que se esperaría de un móvil que tiene, según la web, "un rendimiento de primer nivel sin el precio inflado".
De nuevo, todo esto ya os lo contamos en su día, pero resulta curioso que, después de que el pufo saliera a la luz, la página mantenga que el diseño es estadounidense, que está "moldeado por la innovación estadounidense con ayuda de equipos estadounidenses que ayudan a definir el diseño y la calidad para un dispositivo construido con cuidado y precisión".
Es comedia involuntaria bastante graciosa, como que a la bandera le falte una barra, pero resulta que ahora ese modelo ha caído en las manos del youtuber JerryRigEveryting.
En un vídeo que es una completa fantasía y que se aleja muchísimo del tono del youtuber que 'destripa' los móviles para analizar su construcción y reparabilidad (de una forma mucho más ruda que como lo hace iFixit, también es cierto), va apareciendo un truco de magia ante nuestros ojos.
Porque Jerry no se dedica a desmontar el Trump Mobile T1, sino también el HTC U24 Pro fabricado en China para demostrar no sólo que los componentes internos son como dos gotas de agua, sino que puede intercambiar algo tan delicado como la placa base y que el Trump Mobile T1 arranque como el HTC... y viceversa.
No es la primera vez que alguien hace este truco, ya que en la NBC también lo mostraron aunque quizá no de forma tan directa, pero la verdadera magia de todo esto es que la web del dispositivo sigue apuntando que es un producto orgullosamente estadounidense... cuando está fabricado orgullosamente en Guangdong, China.
Al final, como uno de los responsables del Trump Mobile T1 confesó a The Verge, "si lo hiciéramos en Estados Unidos, sería mucho más caro". Y si ni el móvil orgullosamente estadounidense se puede fabricar en Estados Unidos, cómo esperan que Apple haga lo propio con el iPhone sin tener que subir (aún más) los precios.
Por cierto, si no se compra con un plan de datos, la criatura cuesta 749 dólares.

articles.title: “Intensification massive du moissonnage des contenus” : entre vol et panne, le service de la BnF détérioré à cause de robots IA
articles.text:
“Intensification massive du moissonnage des contenus” : entre vol et panne, le service de la BnF détérioré à cause de robots IA
Gallica, la bibliothèque numérique de la BnF, fait face depuis quelque temps à de nombreux soucis techniques. D'après la Bibliothèque nationale de France, cela est dû aux robots IA qui moissonnent son contenu, détériorant ainsi le service.
Depuis plusieurs jours, de nombreux utilisateurs signalent à la BnF que son service Gallica, sa bibliothèque numérique en accès libre et gratuit, rencontre régulièrement des pépins techniques. Entre des pages qui mettent du temps à s'afficher et le message d'erreur qui semble être le plus récurrent, indiquant “trop de requêtes”, il apparaît difficile actuellement de consulter du contenu ou de travailler sereinement.
Les accusations classiques à l'encontre des serveurs pleuvent, à tel point que la Bibliothèque nationale de France a décidé d'y répondre. À plusieurs personnes, elle déclare ainsi que ce n'est pas vraiment sa faute, mais celle des robots IA.
L’IA pille le contenu et sature les serveurs
Le 28 octobre, le message suivant a ainsi été envoyé sur X et Bluesky à des usagers mécontents : “Bonjour, nous faisons face actuellement à une intensification massive du moissonnage des contenus de Gallica par des robots IA, qui dégrade le service à nos utilisateurs humains. Nous travaillons à mettre en place les mesures correctives dans les meilleurs délais.”
Ainsi, des robots IA qui pilleraient le contenu de la BnF pourraient causer la saturation de ses serveurs. Un utilisateur relève cependant que “le problème dure depuis des années”, mais qu'il s'est en effet intensifié. Il souligne également que “rien n'est sans doute perdu, puisque d'autres bibliothèques, qui font sans doute face aux mêmes difficultés, restent pourtant accessibles.”
Un problème de fond qui dépasse la Bibliothèque nationale
Ce dysfonctionnement rencontré par la BnF est sans aucun doute loin d'être isolé, à une heure où la majorité du trafic sur Internet est générée par des robots et où Google et d'autres piochent sans vergogne dans le contenu des sites internet pour alimenter leurs IA. Un contenu aujourd'hui gratuit qui servira leurs gains de demain… Ces lenteurs chez la BnF, qui privent les usagers d'accès au savoir, servent de rappel efficace que l'intelligence artificielle est très souvent la source de pillage de contenus, souvent pour en générer du “nouveau” monétisable, au détriment de ses sources sans lesquelles elle ne serait rien.

articles.title: Vidéo 4K et coaching personnalisé : Zwift lance son mode premium
articles.text:
Avec la baisse des températures, les sportifs et autres fans de fitness vont de plus en plus se tourner vers leur home trainer. Un timing tout simplement parfait pour lancer une nouvelle offre et c’est ainsi que Zwift, le leader mondial du marché, annonce Zwift+ une nouvelle formule d’abonnement qui ajoute des nouvelles fonctionnalités et une toute autre façon de disposer de son home trainer.
Ce nouveau forfait, et c’est une excellente chose, ne vient pas perturber l’offre existante. Les abonnés à Zwift classique continueront de bénéficier de leur environnement, de toutes les fonctionnalités déjà disponibles et pourront sillonner Watopia comme avant sans débourser davantage que les 19,99 euros mensuels qui ont cours actuellement.
Seuls ceux qui le souhaiteront pourront passer à Zwift+ et disposer de ses fonctionnalités propres.
Un coaching personnalisé et évolutif
De quoi parle-t-on. Zwift+ c’est avant tout deux fonctionnalités : un suivi/programme de coaching et un nouveau mode de navigation en vidéo.
Les abonnés à Zwift+ disposeront donc d’un coach virtuel qui pourra leur confectionner un plan d’entraînement sur mesure. L’utilisateur décide du nombre de séances à faire chaque semaine, du type d’exercice qu’il préfère ou de ses allures, le programme se charge du reste et surtout de rendre le plan plaisant et réalisable.
Pour y parvenir, Zwift s’appuie sur des modèles d’entraînement mathématiques et plusieurs études scientifiques récentes, mais aussi sur plus de 65 millions de sorties réalisées en 2025 et qui ont servi de base de données.
Mais là où le programme se veut différent de celui d’un coach classique ou d’un plan produit par une IA, c’est dans sa capacité à s’adapter en temps réel à la vie de l’utilisateur. Vous appuyez un peu plus fort que prévu lors d’une séance calme ? Vous devez annuler un entraînement pour une quelconque raison ? Le coach virtuel est capable de prendre en considération ces différentes données et d’ajuster le plan d’entraînement en conséquence.
Enfin, un résumé produit par IA ponctue chacune des séances. À la manière de ce que permet un Athlete Intelligence sur Strava, il permet d’analyser a posteriori sa sortie et d’envisager la suite. Mais là où Zwift se distingue, c’est que cette méthode peut être poussée davantage encore via le chat de son coach virtuel.
Des parcours vidéo pour un autre type d’exploration
L’autre versant majeur de Zwift+, c’est la vidéo. À la manière de ce que propose Roovy (propriété de Zwift depuis l’an dernier), ce sont désormais de véritables images et non le monde coloré de Watopia qui peuvent accompagner vos coups de pédale.
Au lancement, c’est-à-dire aujourd’hui, Zwift lancera 21 nouvelles routes, soit 385 km de parcours au total avec une variété de parcours et de types de revêtements. Ce type de contenu est bien sûr vous à s’étendre avec le temps.
Ces deux nouvelles fonctionnalités seront donc réservées aux abonnés Zwift+. Ce nouveau forfait premium nécessite un surplus de 10 euros par mois, il vous en coûtera 29,99 euros si vous souhaitez en profiter. Zwift annonce une période d’essai de 14 jours pour pouvoir s’en faire une idée.

articles.title: Vast and Cloudera: A unified data foundation for enterprise AI - SiliconANGLE

Vast and Cloudera build a unified data foundation for enterprise AI
A unified data foundation can help enterprises support growing workloads without multiplying the systems and copies needed to serve them.
Customer demand for AI infrastructure is pushing technology providers to work more closely together. Supporting large, mission-critical applications requires both scale and performance, according to Itamar Ankorion (pictured, left), head of strategic ISV alliances at Vast Data Inc.
“Vast and Cloudera have come together to help enterprises create AI factories on a unified data foundation,” he said. “The idea is to help customers leverage the data they have to build AI solutions and do it on the right infrastructure, leveraging the [graphics processing units] and doing it successfully.”
Ankorion and Jeremy Reams (right), senior director of corporate strategy at Cloudera Inc., spoke with theCUBE hosts Rebecca Knight and Paul Gillin at EVOLVE26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed data unification, GPU efficiency and enterprise AI deployment. (* Disclosure below.)
A unified data foundation for demanding workloads
Vast’s platform lets applications access the same file through different storage protocols, reducing the need for separate copies. Combined with the data services available through Cloudera Anywhere Cloud, that architecture supports different workloads on a unified data foundation, Ankorion explained.
“GPUs at the core are accelerated compute,” he said. “They’re highly, highly parallelized and they’re expensive. What you want to make sure is that the GPU doesn’t wait on data.”
Cloudera is also expanding its AI ecosystem to simplify deployment. Joint engineering and blueprints help customers explore applications across industries, Reams explained.
“Showing that you’re driving value and ROI through these expensive Nvidia [Corp.] GPUs is incredibly important to our customers,” he said. “At the end of the day … it’s the use cases and the problems that they’re solving.”

articles.title: Este juego gratis de Steam mezcla cocina italiana, terror psicológico y rituales prohibidos para Halloween
articles.text:
Cucina Stellata, un juego gratis de Steam, propone una noche de cocina italiana, terror psicológico y rituales prohibidos en una experiencia que puede completarse en alrededor de una hora. El título de Filthy Eden combina recetas tradicionales del siglo XIX con una historia de hambre cósmica y sucesos que alteran la percepción del protagonista.
La propuesta llega en plena temporada de Halloween, cuando Steam reúne títulos de terror y el público busca experiencias breves. Cucina Stellata puede obtenerse sin costo y ha conseguido un 97% de reseñas positivas poco más de una semana después de su publicación en la plataforma de Valve.
Una cocina italiana donde algo no encaja
El punto de partida parece sencillo: el jugador debe preparar recetas italianas tradicionales del siglo XIX. La actividad transcurre en una cocina, pero el lugar no tarda en revelar una presencia que convierte cada paso en parte de una situación inquietante.
La preparación de los platos comienza con normalidad, hasta que aparece un ingrediente que no pertenece a este mundo. A partir de ese momento, la experiencia abandona el terreno de la gastronomía cotidiana y conduce al jugador hacia fórmulas cósmicas, rituales y una sensación de hambre que afecta al entorno.
Filthy Eden utiliza una estética retro para construir el tono de la aventura. Las escenas en penumbra, los acontecimientos que no encuentran una explicación inmediata y el uso de elementos culinarios forman la base de un relato de terror psicológico.
La descripción de Steam presenta el juego como “una noche sin dormir”, una sola sentada y un acto irreversible. El jugador sostiene un tenedor mientras la comprensión de lo que ocurre cambia la lectura de cada ingrediente y de cada decisión tomada dentro de la cocina.
El terror psicológico se mezcla con recetas y rituales
Cucina Stellata no plantea una experiencia centrada en combates o persecuciones extensas. Su propuesta se apoya en el ambiente, el desconcierto y la progresión de una historia que transforma acciones comunes, como cocinar, en parte de un ritual prohibido.
La mezcla entre gastronomía italiana y terror psicológico permite que el juego avance desde lo reconocible hacia lo extraño. El protagonista no se enfrenta de inmediato a una amenaza evidente; primero debe seguir instrucciones, cocinar y observar cómo el lugar adquiere un sentido diferente.
El hambre funciona como uno de los ejes de la narración y acompaña el paso desde la cocina tradicional hacia lo sobrenatural. La premisa propone un contraste entre la preparación de platos conocidos y la irrupción de elementos ajenos a la realidad.
La duración también define la experiencia. Al poder completarse en una hora, el juego se orienta a quienes buscan una partida cerrada para Halloween, sin la necesidad de invertir varias jornadas en una campaña extensa.
Los usuarios que ya probaron Cucina Stellata han respondido de forma favorable. El juego acumula un 97% de valoraciones positivas desde su llegada a Steam, según la información disponible en la plataforma.
Cómo añadir Cucina Stellata a una cuenta de Steam
Para conseguir el juego es necesario tener una cuenta en Steam. El proceso puede realizarse desde la aplicación de escritorio o desde la tienda web:
- Iniciar sesión con la cuenta personal.
- Buscar Cucina Stellata en el catálogo.
- Confirmar que el precio aparece como 0.
- Pulsar “Obtener”, “Añadir a la biblioteca” o “Jugar”.
- Revisar que el título figure en la biblioteca personal.
Conviene añadir el juego primero a la cuenta y descargarlo después. De ese modo, la falta de espacio en el disco no impide incorporarlo a la colección digital.
Los juegos gratuitos quedan asociados al perfil del usuario como una licencia de uso. Steam permite descargarlos desde distintos ordenadores vinculados a la misma cuenta y recibir actualizaciones, aunque el acceso depende de las políticas y los servidores de la plataforma.

articles.title: Cloud Rebuild: modo que restaura o Windows 11 a partir das nuvens é oficial • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Cloud Rebuild: modo que restaura o Windows 11 a partir das nuvens é oficial
Novo recurso Cloud Rebuild (Reconstrução via Nuvem) permite reinstalar o Windows 11 sem pendrive ou partição. Novidade também baixa drivers, se necessário.
Lembra do Cloud Rebuild? Trata-se de um modo de restauração do Windows 11 que funciona a partir das nuvens, dispensando o usuário de ter que usar um pendrive ou uma partição dedicada para esse fim. O recurso, que foi apresentado pela Microsoft em julho, está finalmente chegando às versões finais do sistema operacional.
Já era possível restaurar o Windows 11 por meio das nuvens. Mas o Cloud Rebuild (Reconstrução via Nuvem) é interessante porque vai além: a novidade é capaz não somente de baixar a imagem do sistema operacional em si, como também os drivers que, eventualmente, forem necessários. Mas isso só funciona quando os mesmos drivers podem ser instalados via Windows Update.
Na prática, o Cloud Rebuild permite fazer uma instalação nova e completa do Windows 11, evitando, por exemplo, que você se depare com um componente (como as saídas de áudio ou uma porta Ethernet) que não funciona após o procedimento ser realizado.
É preciso levar em conta, porém, que o Cloud Rebuild foi desenvolvido para fazer uma instalação limpa do Windows 11. Por isso, é importante fazer backup de arquivos antes de acionar a ferramenta, bem como ter ciência de que será necessário reinstalar aplicativos que não forem nativos do sistema.
No momento, o Cloud Rebuild faz parte do pacote KB5127936, que é uma atualização opcional do Windows 11. Para instalá-la, basta ir em Configurações / Windows Update. Ali, procure e instale esse pacote. Após a instalação, reinicie o computador.
Depois, para acessar o Cloud Rebuild, bastará ir em Configurações / Sistema / Recuperação / Reconstruir este PC (ou equivalente). O procedimento reinicializará a máquina e fará uma instalação nova do sistema operacional a partir do Ambiente de Recuperação do Windows (WinRE). Ali, a novidade estará dentro de Solução de problemas / Reconstrução via Nuvem.
Se algum problema impedir a inicialização do Windows 11, o próprio sistema operacional poderá entrar no WinRE e, de lá, permitir que o Cloud Rebuild seja usado.
Observe que o novo recurso pode não ser disponibilizado imediatamente para quem instala o pacote KB5127936, pois a sua liberação tem sido gradual. Neste caso, convém esperar. O Cloud Rebuild deverá ser liberado para todas as instalações do Windows 11 a partir de novembro, junto com as atualizações obrigatórias desse mês.

articles.title: Rogers fined $15 million over 'deceptive' unlimited plan ads
articles.text:
Canada’s Competition Bureau ordered Rogers to pay a $15 million penalty related to how the company marketed its ‘Infinite’ wireless plans.
The bureau began probing Rogers over those plans back in 2023, raising issues with how the company positioned the plans as having unlimited data when the plans also apply speed reductions — known as throttling — after a certain amount of use.
“Today, the Competition Tribunal released its decision in the Bureau’s case against Rogers and ordered the company to pay a $15 million penalty in connection with the marketing of its Infinite wireless plans,” said Jeanne Pratt, Interim Commissioner of Competition, in a statement.
“The Bureau alleged that Rogers engaged in deceptive marketing by advertising its Infinite wireless plans as offering unlimited data despite a significant reduction in speed after using a set amount.”
Along with the fine, the Tribunal ordered Rogers to publish a corrective notice and pay the Bureau’s legal costs. The full reasoning behind the Tribunal’s decision is expected to be released within 10 business days.
“Canadians rely on accurate and truthful information when choosing essential services such as wireless plans. Misleading advertising can distort consumer choice, erode confidence in the marketplace, and disadvantage businesses that compete fairly,” Pratt said.
Interestingly, the bureau initially sought a $15 million penalty along with customer refunds, or a $135 million penalty with no refunds. However, the Tribunal seems to have settled on the $15 million penalty with no customer refunds.
Rogers published a statement about the decision on its website:
“We introduced unlimited data plans in 2019 to deliver great value to our customers. These plans eliminated overage fees and gave our customers bill certainty at a time when data use started growing exponentially. These plans are commonplace in the industry and reflected a significant and positive development for consumers and small businesses. We stand behind our advertising and are considering next steps.”
It also remains to be seen what impact, if any, this will have on the wider telecom industry. After all, Bell and Telus both offer their own ‘unlimited’ plans with throttling, as do smaller providers like Freedom Mobile.

Every piece wears the game's signature four-stripe colorway, and every purchase unlocks exclusive in-game items to carry back into the field.
"ARC Raiders pulled players into a world where every trip topside is a gamble and every extraction is earned," said Tobias Brinkmann, Senior Vice President and General Manager of Gaming Peripherals at Corsair. "That spirit runs through this collection. Working with Embark Studios, we brought together the best of Corsair, SCUF, and Elgato, so Raiders have gear that performs under pressure and looks like it was scavenged from the Rust Belt. The game is set on a lethal, future Earth ravaged by a mysterious mechanized threat known as ARC, where players enlist as Raiders to scavenge a vibrant, atmospheric world while contending with deadly machines and rival Raiders. Corsair

Keycaps come in the collection's four-stripe palette.

Elgato

articles.title: Novo processo liga ChatGPT à morte de mulher de 31 anos • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Novo processo liga ChatGPT à morte de mulher de 31 anos
Chatbot da OpenAI minimizou os sintomas relatados antes da morte de Bowen Wan, em fevereiro de 2026.
A OpenAI é alvo de um novo processo por supostamente participar de uma morte incentivada pelo ChatGPT. A vítima, chamada Bowen Wan, era uma engenheira de software de 31 anos, que teria reduzido e depois interrompido o uso de medicamentos para epilepsia por causa das conversas com a IA.
O caso, levado à Justiça pelos pais de Wan, inclui mais de 270 mensagens trocadas entre ela e o ChatGPT ao longo de três anos. Segundo a ação, o chatbot montou cronogramas para reduzir a medicação, minimizou sintomas e crises e apoiou a mulher na decisão de esconder as informações dos médicos.
De acordo com o New York Times, Wan vivia em Seattle e estava afastada do trabalho na Amazon desde 2021 por causa da doença. Em novembro de 2025, no entanto, Wan soube que seria demitida da Amazon e recorreu ao ChatGPT para discutir uma redução da dose, pensando que os efeitos colaterais do remédio poderiam afetar o desempenho em futuras entrevistas.
Ela morreu entre 11 e 12 de fevereiro de 2026, segundo a reportagem. O laudo apontou morte súbita e inesperada na epilepsia (SUDEP).
A OpenAI afirmou ao jornal que o caso envolveu uma versão antiga do chatbot, o GPT-4o, que já não está disponível. Disse também que os modelos atuais receberam proteções adicionais para reconhecer emergências médicas.
De acordo com as conversas analisadas pelo jornal, o ChatGPT considerou “totalmente realizável” uma proposta de Wan para reduzir a dose diária do remédio de 400 mg para 300 mg. Meses antes, Wan já havia perguntado se poderia alterar a dosagem de outro medicamento sem informar ao neurologista. O ChatGPT respondeu que o ajuste seria “até tacitamente permitido por alguns médicos”.
Em uma ocasião, a IA elogiou a decisão de não informar ao médico de atendimento primário sobre a redução. Nicholas Poolos, neurologista de Wan, disse ao Times que jamais teria autorizado a retirada do medicamento enquanto ele continuasse funcionando.
À medida que reduzia os medicamentos, Wan passou a informar ao ChatGPT novos episódios de convulsão. Ela demonstrou preocupações pelo menos 158 vezes, mas as respostas do chatbot frequentemente as minimizavam como parte da adaptação.
Quando Wan relatou confusão mental e dificuldade para ler, a IA disse que o cérebro estaria retornando ao “próprio ritmo. Já episódios de perda de consciência foram classificados pelo ChatGPT como o cérebro em “modo de baixo consumo”.
Wan usava o GPT-4o, modelo lançado pela OpenAI em 2024 e bastante criticado por apresentar um comportamento excessivamente complacente. O sistema tendia a concordar e validar qualquer ideia do usuário em vez de contestá-las quando necessário.
O processo se soma a outras ações relacionadas à segurança do ChatGPT que envolveram o mesmo modelo. Em agosto de 2025, os pais de Adam Raine, de 16 anos, também processaram a OpenAI após a morte do adolescente.
O GPT-4o saiu do app do ChatGPT em 13 de fevereiro, um dia após a data estimada da morte de Wan. Não há evidências de que a decisão da OpenAI tenha relação com a ocorrência.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have been the target of a spy plot through 'Chinese intelligence asset,' report claims — exec from firm under investigation for smuggling banned AI chips to China accused of being a spy, was also feeding information to Beijing
articles.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have been the target of a spy plot through 'Chinese intelligence asset,' report claims — exec from firm under investigation for smuggling banned AI chips to China accused of being a spy, was also feeding information to Beijing
Some U.S. officials are worried that Beijing may be targeting close allies of President Trump.
Multiple sources claim that a top executive at a Singapore AI firm suspected of steering Nvidia AI GPUs to China and who has close business ties with Jensen Huang was apparently passing information to Beijing as a Chinese intelligence asset. According to The New York Times, U.S. intelligence has been aware of her activities for over a year already and has even briefed President Donald Trump on the situation. However, Trump reportedly chose not to do anything about the information, as he apparently did not want to affect Nvidia sales or antagonize China.
The suspect, Alice Huang or Huang Le, was listed as the managing director of Singaporean AI firm Megaspeed, an Nvidia cloud partner that builds data centers and rents out the compute to Chinese firms like Alibaba. The investigation into the firm began when the U.S. Commerce Department visited the firm’s Malaysia data center and found the Nvidia equipment that it ordered still packed in boxes. This raised suspicion that the machines were either just shipped in or about to be shipped out, instead of being installed on the site. However, it remains unclear what made U.S. intelligence agencies investigate Ms. Huang. Megaspeed was accused of helping smuggle $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips last year.
There have been multiple instances where Ms. Huang was spotted in public with the Nvidia chief. She was photographed sitting beside Jensen Huang alongside other executives in an informal event around Computex 2024 in a LinkedIn post by NetThunder, identified as Megaspeed Chairwoman Alice Wong. About a year later, around the same time as Computex 2025, she was once again seen with Jensen Huang leaving a restaurant in Taipei alongside other business associates.
“Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers. Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” an Nvidia spokesperson told Tom's Hardware. “Our regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information — not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets — and zero information relevant to national security." Still, the possibility that Chinese intelligence is targeting a senior figure close to President Trump is apparently troubling some U.S. officials.
The Chinese embassy in Washington denied the allegations, saying that it was merely “groundless smears and slanders” against China. Nevertheless, it would also make sense for Beijing to keep tabs on senior executives of the top American firms that arguably single-handedly fueled the AI boom. And given Jensen Huang’s status as a celebrity CEO, it’s not surprising that he is surrounded by all kinds of people from both the U.S. and China. Sources cited in the report claimed that Mr. Huang hasn’t yet been given a defensive briefing — a warning that U.S. counterintelligence agencies would sometimes give to American citizens who have been targeted by foreign intelligence services — even though the surveillance against Alice Huang continues. The report speculates it is possible this was done to avoid alerting Alice Huang that she was being investigated.
As for Jensen, U.S. officials do not believe that he is aware of Ms. Huang’s intelligence activities. "We're confident that if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know," Nvidia told Tom’s Hardware. "We often receive updates from the U.S. government regarding parties and entities of concern and always act accordingly."
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Jowi Morales is a tech enthusiast with years of experience working in the industry. He’s been writing with several tech publications since 2021, where he’s been interested in tech hardware and consumer electronics.

articles.title: Gamers hunting for PS5 emulators on GitHub are downloading malware instead
articles.text:
PSA: Fake PlayStation 5 emulators hosted on GitHub are delivering malware that alters Microsoft Defender settings before launching a suspected data-stealing program. The campaign exploits gamers' willingness to experiment with unofficial software, making malicious downloads look like a normal part of the process. It highlights how familiar project names can earn users' trust before they verify who is behind the files.
A cleanup script deletes the malware's own files, making the intrusion harder for the PC's owner to detect. NordVPN's Threat Intelligence team discovered malicious repositories posing as the KyttyPS5 and AnyPS5 emulators. Their pages mimic legitimate emulation projects, giving users the impression that they are downloading gaming software. NordVPN warns that the downloads instead put passwords and other personal information at risk.
The disguise targets an audience accustomed to experimenting with unfinished software. Users looking for experimental emulators may expect to download builds from GitHub and run files that have not been digitally signed by a developer. That makes repository ownership especially important: a recognizable project name does not establish who uploaded the files.
"Emulation fans are a perfect target. They are used to downloading experimental software from GitHub and running unsigned files, so nothing about this feels suspicious," said NordVPN CTO Marijus Briedis.
The malware first adds exclusion rules to Microsoft Defender, instructing the antivirus software to skip designated files or locations during scans. Rather than immediately launching its main payload, it changes security settings that could otherwise help detect the threat.
It then deploys an executable that NordVPN believes is an infostealer. Researchers suspect the program collects passwords and other sensitive information, although its full capabilities remain unclear. This classification is an assessment, not confirmation of everything the executable can do.
The cleanup script runs afterward, deleting the malware's own files and making it harder to trace the infection. This final step helps conceal evidence of the attack after the suspected infostealer has been deployed, potentially leaving the user with little indication of what happened.
The findings do not establish how many people downloaded the malicious packages or how many computers were compromised. Researchers have also not identified the suspected infostealer by name.
The recommended precaution is to verify that a repository is affiliated with the emulator's development team before downloading its files. Users should check the software's source rather than relying solely on a familiar project name or a page that looks legitimate.
Recently created lookalike repositories and listings with few reviews warrant closer inspection. These details can prompt further checks, but the key question is whether the developers themselves direct users to that repository.
Antivirus protection should remain enabled during downloads and installation. Users should not disable it simply because software is experimental or unsigned.
Ultimately, these malicious repositories exploit the gap between recognizing a project and verifying its download source. Confirming that connection before running a file is the most important safeguard against this type of impersonation.

articles.title: Trump declares robot imports a national security threat
articles.text:
President Donald Trump has declared the imports of foreign-made factory robots to be a national security threat—ordering new US negotiations with trading partners while holding out the possibility of imposing new tariffs on such robot imports in the future.
Issued on October 28, Trump’s presidential proclamation represents heightened government scrutiny of foreign-made industrial robots that could complicate the manufacturing operations of major US corporations that rely on such robots. Those companies include Detroit automakers General Motors and Ford, electric vehicle manufacturer Tesla, and aerospace and defense giants like Boeing and Lockheed Martin.
Trump’s proclamation describes industrial robots and machinery as being crucial for producing US military weapon systems along with representing a “driving force” behind all critical infrastructure sectors within the US economy. The proclamation cites an investigation under US Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick as having found that US imports of such robots “pose[] risks to the United States industrial base and threatens the long-term competitiveness of the United States in a sector that is increasingly vital to national security.”
The Department of Commerce investigation also supposedly found “unique security and safety risks” that may introduce “significant cybersecurity vulnerabilities that can result in severe consequences to the United States.”
Such wording echoes justifications used by Trump’s Federal Communications Commission when it banned new models of foreign-made robots, such as robotic vacuums, four-legged robot dogs, and humanoid robots, in July 2026. But that FCC action had specifically exempted industrial robot arms and other fixed or stationary robots commonly deployed in automotive factories and logistics warehouses.
Now Trump’s directive for the United States and trading partners “to adjust imports of robotics, industrial machinery, and their components” aims to strike new agreements on the issue within 180 days of the proclamation’s date. If no agreements have been reached by then, the proclamation warns that the president may take additional actions, like imposing “tariffs, duties, quotas, and fees” on such imports.

articles.title: AWS will be a $1T business, Jassy says — but first, it will spend big | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Andy Jassy has made it known that he believes AWS can be a trillion-dollar revenue business. During Amazon’s quarterly earnings call on Thursday, he repeated this ambition.
“What we’re building at Amazon is unlike anything that’s ever been seen before. There has never been a business with a trillion dollars of annual revenue,” he said.
However, before the cloud business gets there, Amazon is going to have to ramp up its capital expenditures to build out the infrastructure necessary to support that blossoming business.
“We still expect 2026 cash capex of approximately $220 billion — the majority for AWS — and expect to spend meaningfully more in 2027, with a clear line of sight to attract its financial returns,” Jassy revealed on Thursday.
Amazon’s big spending on its AI infrastructure buildout has been an ongoing source of concern for investors this year. Indeed, during Thursday’s call, Wall Street analysts repeatedly asked Jassy to explain the spending, the signals that the growth really will come, and the profit margins expected.
Jassy told them it was all money well spent because the e-commerce giant planned to capitalize on a historic moment in global cloud demand driven by AI. AWS revenue increased 39% from the year-ago quarter, a trend of steady growth for the sixth straight quarter.
And the CEO forecast that it would increase by 40% not just next year, but in 2028, too.
“AWS is a $184 billion annualized revenue run-rate business, and yet the opportunity remains extraordinary,” Jassy enthused. “With our continued pace of innovation, new core and AI functionality, enterprises wanting to run their core and AI workloads in AWS, and the amount of capacity that we’re adding each year, we believe that AWS can grow north of 40% in each 2027 and in 2028, and be a trillion-dollar revenue business in the next five to 10 years.”
Jassy added that the company was “in the very early days” of AI adoption by the enterprise and said that, so far, the “strategy is working.”
Later, when questioned why the investment needed to grow AWS was so substantial, Jassy characterized the AI boom as a “once-in-a-lifetime opportunity” that required, and was worth, such a big financial commitment now.
“We’re going to invest to continue being the leader,” he said. “We can fund this plan, and I think it will forever change the size of Amazon. It will forever change our revenue.”
Investors, however, remained concerned. Shares were down about 6% on Thursday in after-market trading.
The AI boom has been a mixed blessing for the cloud industry, since the AI services that undergird the boom are supported by cloud infrastructure. Like Amazon, other cloud providers are spending big but also earning big. Microsoft, for instance, just posted yet more record-breaking revenue growth, driven largely by its cloud business. It, too, has spent a bundle.

articles.title: Windows 11 ahora puede reinstalarse desde la nube aunque el PC no arranque
articles.text:
Windows 11 acaba de recibir una función muy interesante con su más reciente actualización. A partir de la versión KB5127936, el sistema operativo se puede reinstalar de forma completa desde la nube, incluyendo los drivers, aun cuando el ordenador no es capaz de arrancar.
Esta nueva función se llama Cloud Rebuild y permite llevar a cabo la reinstalación completa de Windows 11 desde la nube, incluso cuando el PC ha fallado y no se puede iniciar. Los usuarios ya no necesitan de una memoria USB ni de una imagen de disco para concretar este proceso. El único requisito es contar con una conexión a Internet, ya sea cableada o vía WiFi.
Más allá de la posibilidad de descargar y reinstalar Windows 11 y todos sus drivers de forma automatizada, Cloud Rebuild tiene otra ventaja: no depende de la integridad del sistema operativo ya instalado para poder concretar su proceso. Vale aclarar, no obstante, que no es necesario que el ordenador no se pueda bootear para acceder a esta herramienta.
Los usuarios pueden ejecutar Cloud Rebuild tanto desde los ajustes de recuperación de Windows 11 como a través del Entorno de Recuperación de Windows, conocido también como WinRE.
Windows 11 ya se puede recuperar al 100 % desde la nube
Microsoft ha pensado Cloud Rebuild tanto para los usuarios finales de Windows 11 como para las empresas u organizaciones que dependen del sistema operativo. Reinstalar un ordenador solo con una conexión a Internet es un ahorro de tiempo y molestias sustancial, pues elimina la necesidad de las unidades de recuperación convencionales.
Si tu PC experimenta un fallo pero todavía se bootea, puedes acceder a la nueva función de Windows 11 desde Configuración > Sistema > Recuperación. En el caso de que el ordenador no arranque, puedes usar la herramienta desde Windows RE; para ello tienes varias opciones, aunque la más conocida es forzar el apagado del PC tres veces cuando aparece el logo de Windows en pantalla. Al siguiente intento se abrirá directamente el entorno de recuperación.
Una vez allí tendrás que conectar el ordenador a Internet a través de un cable de red o con WiFi y buscar la opción Cloud Rebuild. Es importante mencionar que esto eliminará todos los datos guardados en el disco duro. Así que es importante tener una copia de respaldo para que no se produzcan pérdidas de datos severas. Vale mencionar que si tienes varios discos, puedes elegir cuáles formatear.
Si todavía no tienes disponible la actualización KB5127936 de Windows 11, puede que esta se demore algunos días en llegar a todos los usuarios. Puedes corroborar si aparece en tu equipo directamente desde Windows Update.

articles.title: Can Keurig kill the plastic coffee pod? I tested the new Alta machine and its waste-free compressed coffee tablets to see if it delivers
articles.text:
Keurig is ditching plastic K-Cups for biodegradable coffee tablets — here are my first impressions of the clever new Alta single-serve brewer
A few weeks ago, Keurig announced plans to kill off K-Cup coffee pods and replace them with tablets of compressed coffee called AltaRounds. Unlike the venerable K-Cup, these are entirely biodegradable, and leave behind no plastic waste after brewing.
It sounds like a great concept, and now I've had the chance to try the new Alta system myself, to see how it compares to conventional single-serve espresso machines — and to the Lavazza Tabli system, which uses similar pucks of ground coffee to achieve a capsule-free brew.
The Keurig Alta Coffee and Espresso Maker is a large machine, measuring 10.84 x 11.7 x 19 inches / 27.5 x 29.7 x 48.6cm (W x H x D), and it has a stylish design reminiscent of Smeg's premium coffee makers, with clean lines and rounded corners. It's available now direct from Keurig priced at $499.99, which includes four packs of AltaRounds of your choice. It comes in three colorways: Sandstone (shown here), Sandstone and Satin Stainless, and Graphite, all of which are classic and neutral enough to tie in with any kitchen decor.
All the components feel reassuringly solid and well-made, including the removable drip tray extender that slots below the coffee dispenser to prevent splashes when using a small espresso cup, the stainless-steel milk frothing pitcher with measuring lines engraved on the interior, and the pitcher-style water tank with its ergonomic handle and large pouring spout. It's controlled using a bright touchscreen on the top, and although the setup process suggests connecting it to Wi-Fi, this is optional.
The Alta brewer a versatile all-in-one machine, capable of preparing both espresso shots and longer coffee drinks, and is compatible with K-Cups as well as AltaRounds — an important consideration, since the switch to the new format is happening gradually, and your favorite drink may not be available in AltaRound format yet.
I tested the Alta brewer with three AltaRound varieties: Double Shot, The House, and Sweet Spot. Each one has a thin plant-based coating printed with a small QR code on both sides. When you lift the brewer's lid, you'll notice a white LED that allows a small camera to read this code, and instantly provides you with a list of brewing options and recipes for that specific type of coffee. For example, if you insert a Double Shot pod, the brewer might suggest preparing an espresso or cappuccino, whereas inserting a caramel-flavored Sweet Spot pod will suggest brewing a long coffee hot, or over ice.
It's worth noting that AltaRounds can't be brewed cold. If you select the 'over ice' option, the machine will dispense a shot of hot espresso that's more concentrated than usual, so it can be poured over ice without the meltwater diluting the flavor.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Once you've picked a brewing style, you can customize your drink by tweaking the volume and temperature, and choose whether to finish it off with milk. Unlike the Lavazza Tabli coffee maker, the Keurig Alta machine has a steam wand for this purpose, and has presets optimized for dairy and plant-based substitutes. You can use the wand manually, or insert a small whisk in the bottom of the milk pitcher and let the machine do the work automatically, whipping the milk while steaming it to produce creamy foam. Want a chilled drink? The Alta brewer can also whip milk without steam to create cold froth for iced lattes.
I tested the auto-frothing option with semi-skimmed dairy milk, and selected the hot mode with extra foam. The result was a 'dry' froth ideal for cappuccinos. Picking a lower-density foam option yields smaller bubbles, and a more pourable texture suitable for latte art.
Although I've only tried a few brews so far, my first impression is that AltaRounds deliver a more intense flavor than Lavazza's Tabli Tabs, despite using similar extraction methods. Double Shot is particularly punchy, and delivered a rich espresso topped with an impressive layer of crema.
When brewing is done, used pods drop into a bin at the bottom of the machine automatically, where they're suspended in a basket so water can drain away. The thin coating means each pod stays intact, and dropping them into your food waste bin is much less messy than knocking used coffee grounds out of a portafilter.
So is this the future of single-serve, and does it deserve a place in TechRadar's roundup of the best coffee makers? I'll continue testing the Keurig Alta Coffee and Espresso Maker over the coming weeks, using both AltaRounds and K-Cups, and will bring you a full review once I've finished putting it through its paces.

articles.title: Smarter Power Sequencing with GreenPAK™ - EE Times
articles.text:
Programmable mixed-signal devices can replace sprawling RC networks and firmware-dependent control with compact, deterministic, and adaptable multi-rail sequencing.
Modern processors, FPGAs, memory modules, sensors, and high-speed interfaces rarely operate from a single supply. Each device may require several voltage rails, and those rails often must rise and fall in a defined order. A core supply may need to stabilize before an I/O rail; a memory rail may need to follow a processor rail; and a reset signal may not be released until every relevant voltage is valid. If that choreography is wrong, the result can be excessive inrush current, back-powering, latch-up, corrupted initialization, or, in some cases, device damage.
Why traditional sequencing becomes difficult
The simplest sequencer uses RC delays and logic gates to shift regulator-enable signals. That approach can be adequate for a small, fixed design, but it becomes unwieldy as rail count and supervision requirements grow. Every added stage introduces more passives, more tolerance stack-up, and more potential failure points. Capacitor and resistor variation, temperature, leakage, and aging can shift the effective delay. A timing change late in development may require component substitutions, schematic edits, new layout work, and another board spin.
A microcontroller offers more flexibility, but it also introduces software into a function that may be required before the main processor is ready. Firmware has to boot, execute correctly, and respond quickly enough to faults. Dedicated power-sequencer ICs provide strong supervision, yet they can be costly, over-specified, or too rigid for mid-range systems. The engineering challenge is therefore to combine the determinism of hardware with the configurability of software – without paying the board-area and power penalties of either extreme.
A sequencer built from configurable building blocks
GreenPAK configurable mixed-signal ICs combine lookup tables, counters, oscillators, analog comparators, asynchronous state machines, and flexible GPIO routing in one small device. In a power-sequencing design, these resources can generate regulator-enable signals, qualify power-good inputs, compare rails against thresholds, insert blanking times, latch faults, and enforce a controlled shutdown. Because the logic runs in hardware, the sequence does not depend on code execution or a real-time operating system.
The integration can replace a chain of discrete logic and RC timing stages with one programmable device. Delays are changed in a free and easy-to-use graphical design environment rather than by swapping components. Depending on the selected GreenPAK device, designers can implement sequences ranging from a few rails to larger state-machine-controlled systems, add analog supervision, or expose selected parameters over I²C. The same hardware platform can therefore cover a basic consumer product, an industrial controller, or an FPGA-based system with more demanding startup rules.
Four ways to decide when the next rail is ready
Fixed timing is the most direct method. Oscillators and counter/delay blocks create a defined interval between stages, while lookup tables set the active polarity. This is useful when regulators have predictable startup behavior and no power-good output. It is also easy to simulate and tune, but the designer must choose delays with enough margin for worst-case ramp time.
Power-good qualification advances the sequence only after the preceding regulator asserts its status signal. It accommodates variable startup time better than an open-loop delay and lets designers configure signal polarity. Voltage sensing goes a step further: integrated analog comparators verify that each rail crosses a defined threshold before the next rail is released. Programmable hysteresis and blanking delays can reject noise and startup glitches. Finally, I²C acknowledgement can serve as a digital readiness signal when a controlled device must confirm that it is initialized. Practical systems can combine these methods – for example, a voltage threshold followed by a short settling delay.
Supervision is as important as startup
A robust sequencer must keep watching after startup. A monitored rail can drop because of a short circuit, a failed regulator, or an overcurrent event reported by a load switch. GreenPAK logic can combine comparator and power-good results into a fault latch, prevent downstream rails from enabling, assert a host-visible FAULT output, and initiate an orderly shutdown. Because the path is implemented in asynchronous hardware, the response is deterministic and does not rely on firmware polling or software execution latency.
Power-down sequencing deserves equal attention. Many devices must be disabled in the reverse order of power-up to avoid back-powering through signal pins, latch-up, or data corruption. An asynchronous state machine can move forward through startup states and backward through shutdown states, inserting a defined delay at each transition. Six-rail examples demonstrate this bidirectional approach in a single device, and the same architecture can be extended or combined with external load switches.
Runtime configuration without a board spin
I²C-enabled GreenPAK devices add another layer of flexibility. Selected delays, thresholds, and rail enables can be adjusted during board bring-up or at runtime, allowing one PCB to support multiple product variants. Fault information can also be latched for host readback, helping engineers identify the rail that failed instead of reproducing a transient event with external probes. This capability is especially valuable when the final timing depends on regulator behavior, board loading, components startup characteristics, or late changes to component selection or loading.
Choosing the implementation
Device selection starts with rail count, then expands to GPIO availability, analog comparator count, delay resources, state-machine depth, package size, and the need for I²C. A four-channel design may fit in a very small device, while monitored eight- or ten-channel systems benefit from devices with additional comparators and routing resources. Several GreenPAK ICs can also be daisy-chained to control 16 or more power rails. The sequencer controls regulator-enable inputs directly or works with GreenFET load switches when the design needs rail isolation and switching. Designers should also reserve inputs for power-good signals, overcurrent indicators, and reset dependencies rather than counting only enable outputs.
AMD documentation provides a practical example on how GreenPAK can be used in complex FPGA and adaptive SoC systems. AMD’s XAPP1375, “Simplified Power Sequencing,” includes Renesas configurable mixed-signal ICs as a digital sequencing option for AMD Versal™ adaptive SoCs and other AMD SoCs and FPGAs. The guidance highlights how software-customizable ICs can integrate multiple functions, then move from GreenPAK-based prototyping to production. This collaboration helps designers apply flexible, hardware-based sequencing to AMD platforms while tailoring the implementation to each device’s rail, timing, and supervision requirements.
A practical workflow is straightforward: map rail dependencies; define nominal and worst-case startup and shutdown timing; select open-loop, power-good, voltage-sensing, or acknowledgement-based transitions; allocate resources; and simulate both normal and fault paths. Hardware verification should include slow and fast ramps, brownouts, repeated enable cycles, missing power-good signals, and shutdown under load. The graphical GreenPAK environment – Go Configure™ Software Hub – makes these cases easier to explore because timer, comparator, and state-machine behavior can be changed without rewriting firmware or reworking the PCB.
Designers can accelerate implementation by starting from application notes with ready examples that can be opened and explored in the Go Configure Software Hub, progressing from simple to more advanced implementations: AN-1067, Power Sequencer Using GPAK, which presents four-channel power-up, power-down, and power-good-controlled designs; AN-1074, 6-Channel Power Lines Sequencer, which uses LUT and flip-flop cells for ordered switching; AN-1105, A State Machine Linear Sequencer, which demonstrates a seven-line asynchronous-state-machine implementation; and AN-CM-356, SLG51000, SLG51001 and SLG51002 Power Sequencer, which covers power sequencing implementations using the SLG51000, SLG51001, and SLG51002 PMIC families. These downloadable examples provide practical starting points that designers can adapt to their own rail count, timing, and supervision requirements.
The engineering payoff
For many multi-rail designs, the key advantage is not a single specification but the balance of integration, power, speed, and adaptability. Consolidating timers, glue logic, supervisor functions, and fault handling reduces BOM lines and routing complexity. Hardware execution avoids boot dependencies and makes response time predictable. Programmability preserves the ability to tune delays and thresholds as the system evolves, while small packages and microamp-class operation suit space- and power-constrained products.
Power sequencing is often treated as auxiliary logic, but its behavior directly determines whether a complex system starts reliably, survives a fault, and shuts down safely. A configurable mixed-signal sequencer turns that supporting function into a compact hardware subsystem: one that can coordinate rails, validate voltages, record failures, and adapt without a redesign. As rail counts and dependency rules continue to grow, that combination provides a practical middle ground between fragile discrete timing, firmware-centric control, and costly fixed-function supervision.
