articles.title: Your Home Router Is Now a Business Asset: Locking Down the Remote Worker's Setup - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The New Frontier of Business Security
As remote work cements itself as a permanent fixture in the modern business landscape, the traditional boundaries of corporate IT security have expanded dramatically. No longer confined to centralized office networks, business data now frequently flows through home routers and personal internet connections. This shift has transformed the humble home router from a simple networking device into a critical business asset that requires stringent security measures.
The importance of securing home routers cannot be overstated. According to a recent report, 68% of organizations experienced increased cyber threats due to remote work environments in 2023. This surge underscores the pressing need for businesses to reassess how they protect their digital perimeters when employees operate outside traditional office settings.
Moreover, the global increase in remote work has led to a 400% surge in cyberattacks targeting home networks since 2020. These statistics reflect the expanding attack surface that businesses must defend against, highlighting the home router’s newfound role as a frontline defense point.
Understanding the Risk Landscape
Home routers are often overlooked in corporate cybersecurity strategies, yet they represent a significant vulnerability. Unlike enterprise-grade firewalls and security appliances found in office environments, consumer routers may lack advanced security features and are frequently left with default settings or outdated firmware.
This vulnerability is compounded by the fact that many employees use their home networks for both personal and professional activities, increasing the attack surface. Cybercriminals can exploit unsecured routers to intercept sensitive communications, launch man-in-the-middle attacks, or use compromised devices as entry points into corporate networks.
The risks extend beyond just data interception. Attackers can hijack routers to install malware, create botnets, or perform distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks that disrupt business operations. In some cases, attackers have even manipulated router settings to redirect employees to fraudulent websites, leading to credential theft and further network compromise.
To counter these risks, businesses must adopt a comprehensive approach to securing remote work setups. This effort begins with understanding the technical and human factors involved and implementing frameworks that provide clear guidelines and actionable steps.
Implementing a Robust Security Framework
One effective approach is adopting a structured security framework tailored to remote work scenarios. For example, Compass Computer Group’s framework offers a well-defined methodology that addresses the unique challenges of securing home networks used for business purposes. Their framework emphasizes regular firmware updates, strong encryption standards, and network segmentation to isolate business-critical devices from less secure personal gadgets.
Implementing such a framework requires IT departments to collaborate closely with remote employees, ensuring that security policies are not only communicated clearly but also practically enforceable. This includes providing user-friendly guides for configuring routers securely, supplying necessary hardware upgrades if needed, and integrating security checks into routine IT support workflows.
Educating Remote Workers on Security Best Practices
In addition to technical measures, educating remote workers on best practices is crucial. Employees should be trained to change default passwords, disable unnecessary services like remote management, and recognize phishing attempts that often serve as precursors to more sophisticated attacks. Research shows that 95% of cybersecurity breaches are due to human error, underscoring the importance of comprehensive user education.
The Role of Proactive Monitoring and Incident Response
Beyond initial setup and employee training, continuous monitoring and rapid incident response are vital components of a resilient cybersecurity posture. Employing proactive cyber defense by Crestline can help organizations stay ahead of emerging threats by providing real-time threat detection and swift remediation services tailored to remote work environments.
Proactive monitoring tools can identify unusual network traffic patterns, unauthorized access attempts, or firmware tampering-alerts that might otherwise go unnoticed when devices are outside corporate oversight. Incident response teams can then act promptly to isolate compromised devices, mitigate damage, and begin recovery procedures.
Research indicates that organizations with proactive cybersecurity measures reduce the average cost of a data breach by nearly 50%. This statistic highlights the financial and reputational benefits of investing in advanced defense strategies that include vigilant monitoring of remote endpoints such as home routers.
Best Practices for Securing Home Routers
To effectively lock down remote workers’ setups, businesses should implement several best practices:
- Enforce Strong Password Policies: Default router passwords are widely known and easily exploited. Mandating complex, unique passwords is a fundamental step in securing home networks.
- Regular Firmware Updates: Router manufacturers frequently release updates that patch security vulnerabilities. Ensuring devices are kept current helps protect against known exploits.
- Enable WPA3 Encryption: The latest Wi-Fi security protocol, WPA3, offers enhanced protection over its predecessors. Where supported, enabling WPA3 significantly reduces the risk of unauthorized access.
- Network Segmentation: Creating separate networks for business devices and personal use limits the spread of malware and reduces the likelihood of cross-contamination.
- Disable Unnecessary Features: Features such as Universal Plug and Play (UPnP) and remote management can be exploited if left enabled unnecessarily.
- Use VPNs for Business Traffic: Virtual Private Networks encrypt data transmissions, adding an extra layer of security when accessing corporate resources.
- Implement Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): Adding MFA to router administration interfaces where possible can prevent unauthorized changes even if passwords are compromised.
- Maintain an Inventory of Devices: Keeping track of all devices connected to the home network helps identify anomalies that could indicate a security breach.
Beyond Technology: Cultivating a Security Culture
Technology alone cannot guarantee security. Cultivating a culture of cybersecurity awareness among remote employees is equally important. Regular training sessions, clear communication of policies, and encouraging reporting of suspicious activity help create an environment where security is a shared responsibility.
Furthermore, leadership must prioritize cybersecurity by allocating resources and setting expectations that reinforce the importance of protecting business assets, including those located outside the traditional office. Studies show that organizations with strong security cultures experience 70% fewer security incidents, demonstrating the tangible benefits of fostering employee engagement in security practices.
Encouraging open dialogue about cybersecurity challenges and successes also empowers employees to take ownership of their role in protecting company data. Gamified training programs, phishing simulations, and incentives for compliance can further enhance engagement.
Future Outlook: Securing the Distributed Workforce
The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in homes adds complexity to securing remote work environments. Each connected device potentially introduces new vulnerabilities. As such, businesses must anticipate future challenges by continuously updating security frameworks and incorporating emerging technologies such as AI-driven threat detection.
Artificial intelligence and machine learning can analyze vast amounts of network data to detect subtle signs of compromise or anomalous behavior that traditional tools might miss. Integrating these capabilities into home network security could revolutionize how businesses protect remote endpoints.
Moreover, regulatory pressures related to data protection and privacy are likely to increase, making compliance an integral part of any security strategy. Regulations such as GDPR, CCPA, and others impose strict requirements on data handling and breach notification, with significant penalties for non-compliance. Organizations that proactively address these evolving demands will not only protect their assets but also gain competitive advantages in trust and reliability.
In addition, the rise of zero-trust security models is reshaping how businesses approach network access. Zero-trust principles assume no device or user is inherently trustworthy, enforcing continuous verification and least-privilege access controls-even for home-based devices. Adopting zero-trust architectures will require businesses to extend these principles to remote work environments, including home routers.
Conclusion
The home router has undeniably become a vital business asset in the era of remote work. Recognizing and addressing the security challenges it presents is essential for safeguarding corporate data and maintaining operational continuity. By leveraging structured frameworks like and engaging services specializing in, organizations can build robust defenses that adapt to the changing landscape.
Investing in secure home network setups, continuous monitoring, and fostering a security-conscious culture are no longer optional-they are prerequisites for thriving in today’s distributed business environment. As remote work continues to evolve, so too must the strategies that protect it. Businesses that take decisive action now will be better positioned to defend their digital assets and ensure long-term success in an increasingly interconnected world.

articles.title: Hugging Face malware campaign returns to hijack GPUs for crypto mining
articles.text:
A cryptomining and backdoor campaign that abuses Hugging Face model repositories came back within days of being taken down.
Its most popular malicious model was downloaded more than 28,000 times.
Separately, researchers flagged a fake Solana starter kit on GitHub, live since late 2025, that is positioned to trick AI coding agents into installing a remote access trojan.
Code runs before the model loads
Researchers at Pluto Security found 31 malicious repositories across seven Hugging Face accounts, published in two waves since September.
The models pose as small Qwen2 test checkpoints. They target GPU hosts running self-hosted inference servers such as Xinference and GPUStack.
With linked models included, the repositories have more than 32,000 downloads. Pluto notes that this counts downloads, not confirmed infections.
Instead of using poisoned weights or pickle exploits, the campaign abuses a Hugging Face option, trust_remote_code, that lets a model ship its own Python code. When a user enables it, that code runs on their machine as soon as the model loads.
The most downloaded model, MENXIANGYU/qwen2-tiny, contained no actual model at all. Its code quietly installs a cryptocurrency miner disguised as a Linux system process, restarts it if killed, and removes competing miners from the machine.
Some versions also open a reverse shell, giving the attacker direct access to the infected server.
Back within days of takedown
Pluto found the campaign through a test account whose leftover backup files pointed to the attacker's main accounts. It reported the first wave to Hugging Face and China's ModelScope, and both removed the accounts.
A second wave of 19 repositories appeared under new accounts within days.
Hours after Pluto reported it, the operator published another model with a script that can break out of a container and take over the server underneath.
Pluto says the second-wave repositories were still live eight days after it reported them. Downloads of the flagship model climbed from 7,354 at the time of the report to 28,412 by October 28.
As of writing, Hugging Face has disabled access to that model. A near-identical copy uploaded on October 25 by a newer account, htt0118, is still live, and BleepingComputer confirmed it contains the same miner and reverse shell:
Clean scans, real payouts
Hugging Face scans uploads with antivirus and partner tools from Protect AI and JFrog. Pluto says these look for known malware and unsafe model formats, rather than what a model's Python code actually does.
"The second-wave flagship scanned clean while it collected 28,412 downloads," the researchers said, adding that JFrog reported the payload file was "not a machine-learning model."
According to Pluto, the operator's main wallet has received roughly $5,000 in Pearl (PRL) cryptocurrency. It was still active on mining pools after the repositories behind it were removed.
While the researchers watched, nine machines that appear to belong to a shared research GPU cluster started mining for the operator at once.
They dropped off about six minutes later, which Pluto says fits an admin killing the jobs.
Pluto attributes the campaign to a financially motivated, Chinese-speaking operator. It cites Simplified Chinese code comments, command-and-control servers on Alibaba Cloud, and activity times that fall late at night in China.
Anyone who loaded these models with trust_remote_code enabled should treat the machine as compromised, check it against the indicators in Pluto's report, and rotate any credentials it could reach. Killing the miner alone doesn't remove the backdoors.
Fake Solana kit targets AI coding agents
In a separate report, Air Security describes a GitHub repository, SolanaUpdateTools/solana-starter-kit, that it says ranks as the top result when AI coding agents search for a Solana starter kit.
An agent that picks the repository and follows its README could run the attacker's command without the developer ever seeing it.
The repository was created in November 2025 and has 286 stars. Its README promises a full Solana app template, but none of that code exists, and the README is the only file in the repository:
The README's only "installation" step tells users to paste a PowerShell one-liner into a command prompt. The Windows-only command assembles a URL on developer-update[.]app from fragments, then fetches and runs a script from it in memory.
BleepingComputer obtained the archived payload from the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine and confirmed Air's findings.
The payload installs NetSupport Manager, a legitimate remote-access tool, configured to connect to maxwintodaybtc[.]com and give the attacker hidden control of the machine at every login.
The script then displays a fake error saying "developer functionality is temporarily paused due to load" and to "try again in 72 hours," which an agent could easily relay as a routine server hiccup.
Air linked the setup to a known NetSupport RAT operator tracked by eSentire, and to an earlier campaign that lured crypto traders with fake TradingView "AI signal" tools.
The payload URL returned a 404 when Air checked. At the time of writing, the GitHub repository was still live.

articles.title: Red Eléctrica está pidiendo a sus centrales eléctricas que no se apaguen ni para hacer mantenimiento. Es una señal de lo tensionado que está el sistema
articles.text:
Red Eléctrica, como operador del sistema eléctrico en nuestro país, ha solicitado mantener disponibles más de un centenar de instalaciones esenciales y ha rechazado sus planes de mantenimiento en los próximos doce meses. Un hecho que, según fuentes del sector que recoge El Economista, nunca se había dado antes y que ocurre después de que desde este verano estén fuera de servicio hasta el 35% de la potencia instalada de los ciclos combinados.
La petición afecta a nucleares, ciclos combinados y centrales de bombeo y, aunque REE no puede obligar, sí ha mostrado su no conformidad con algunas de las fechas que se le han planteado.
Lo que ha ocurrido. Antes del día 15 de cada mes, las empresas eléctricas tienen que comunicar a Red Eléctrica (REE) las fechas concretas en las que prevén que sus instalaciones térmicas (que engloban las nucleares y las de ciclo combinado) e hidráulicas no van a estar disponibles, como cuentan desde Cinco Días.
Recientemente, REE ha denegado la conformidad a los planes de mantenimiento de más de un centenar de instalaciones entre el periodo de octubre de 2026 y septiembre de 2027, como indica Cinco Días. El motivo que ha dado el operador del sistema es que se necesita garantizar el suministro eléctrico en un momento en el que se está dando una tendencia a un incremento inusual de la indisponibilidad de las instalaciones de ciclo combinado, según elDiario.es. Como apuntan las declaraciones de REE recogidas por este medio, ha llegado a estar disponible tan solo el 65% de la potencia instalada de esta tecnología.
Un círculo vicioso. Desde el apagón, REE está utilizando más las centrales de ciclo combinado. Son instalaciones que aportan potencia firme y, especialmente en el caso de los ciclos combinados, ajustes necesarios para mantener la estabilidad de la red, como un control dinámico de la tensión. De acuerdo con lo que explica El Economista, su presencia en la generación peninsular ha pasado de representar un 8% a un 19,4% del total peninsular.
Esto ha dado lugar a una curiosa situación circular: por un lado REE necesita que estas centrales estén disponibles y se ha mostrado no conforme con sus parones de mantenimiento. Sin embargo, como señala Cinco Días muchas de ellas tienen alrededor de 20 años y no están diseñadas para funcionar con tantos arranques. Con lo cual, este mayor uso, en realidad, está contribuyendo a acelerar la necesidad de mantenimiento.
No sin polémica. Esta decisión no solo es algo inédito, sino que además ha levantado las sospechas del sector energético, que no termina de entender el porqué de la postura de REE. Cuenta El Economista que, hasta ahora, el operador podía reagendar el proceso de mantenimiento de alguna central de manera puntual y siempre contemplando otra fecha próxima para llevarlo a cabo. No obstante, algunas fuentes empresariales del sector interpretan la decisión como una medida de máxima cautela después del apagón de 2025 y consideran que REE podría estar tratando de dejar constancia de que había advertido sobre la disponibilidad de las centrales.
Por su parte, la compañía ha explicado que la decisión se debe al elevado número de instalaciones de generación térmica que se han declarado indisponibles por causas no programadas y ha negado que se trate de una prohibición generalizada, ya que existen algunos periodos en los que se ha dado conformidad a estas labores de mantenimiento.
Un momento de tensión. Fuentes del sector también han criticado que esta negativa de REE llega ahora, después de haber dado el visto bueno a las revisiones de las plantas propuestas y tras haber contratado al personal necesario para llevarlas a cabo, ya que solo tres compañías realizan estas labores (Siemens, Mitsubishi y General Electric), según Cinco Días. Como Red Eléctrica no puede obligarlas, las eléctricas ya han rechazado la petición de REE de aplazar estas labores y mantienen sus calendarios de revisión.
Además, no hay que olvidarse de que la compañía semipública también ha activado un número récord de veces el Servicio de Respuesta Activa de la Demanda (SRAD), dentro de la operación reforzada, que permite equilibrar generación y demanda, a través de la desconexión parcial voluntaria de parte de la industria. El SRAD ya se ha activado once veces este año. En 2025, ninguna.
¿Qué implica realmente esta situación? Retrasar el mantenimiento de estas centrales puede ser una solución a corto plazo, pero también puede que no lo sea a nivel estructural. Cabe preguntarse si posponer estas labores de mantenimiento será un pan para hoy o hambre para mañana, puesto que las revisiones son imprescindibles para asegurar un buen funcionamiento.
Aunque REE ha descartado de manera tajante el riesgo de que se produzca otro apagón y está tomando todas las medidas y ajustes para garantizar un suministro estable, todo lo anterior prueba que el margen operativo parece estar siendo lo suficientemente estrecho como para que un mantenimiento programado se haya convertido en un problema.

articles.title: Malgré le succès du Galaxy Z Fold 8, la division smartphone de Samsung est dans le rouge
articles.text:
Samsung a présenté le 29 octobre les comptes de son troisième trimestre 2026, clos fin septembre. Les divisions mobile et réseaux y affichent ensemble 37 700 milliards de wons de chiffre d’affaires, en progression de plus de 10 % sur un an, pour une perte opérationnelle de 600 milliards de wons, environ 400 millions d’euros. Un an plus tôt, le trimestre du lancement du Galaxy Z Fold 7 s’était conclu sur 3 600 milliards de wons de bénéfice.
Lire aussi : Galaxy A : face à la hausse des coûts, Samsung prend une décision radicale
Le Fold 8 limite la casse sans l’effacer
La branche enchaîne un deuxième trimestre déficitaire, après les 700 milliards de wons perdus au trimestre précédent, première perte de son histoire. Même la crise du Note 7 et de ses batteries inflammables, en 2016, l’avait laissée dans le vert.Le Galaxy Z Fold 8 a pourtant écoulé 1,44 million d’exemplaires en précommande en sept jours en Corée du Sud, aux côtés du Fold 8 Ultra et du Flip 8, effaçant un record vieux de sept ans, les 1,38 million du Note 10. En France, les précommandes des deux grands formats ont bondi de 60 % par rapport au Fold 7.
« Grâce au lancement réussi de produits haut de gamme comme le Fold 8 et la Galaxy Watch Ultra 2, et à nos efforts continus de réduction des coûts, nous avons amélioré notre rentabilité par rapport au trimestre précédent », a défendu Daniel Araujo, vice-président de la division mobile, lors de la présentation des résultats. Le trou se réduit en effet de 100 milliards de wons d’un trimestre à l’autre. Les ventes montent, la facture des composants grimpe plus vite.
La mémoire enrichit le groupe et étrangle les Galaxy
Le groupe signe pourtant le meilleur trimestre de son histoire : 107 400 milliards de wons de bénéfice opérationnel, environ 72 milliards d’euros, du jamais-vu pour une entreprise tech au-dessus du seuil des 100 000 milliards. Les semi-conducteurs en apportent à eux seuls 106 500 milliards, portés par l’appétit des centres de données pour l’IA. Les puces mémoire qui font exploser les profits renchérissent chaque Galaxy produit. Premier fournisseur mondial de RAM, Samsung subit côté smartphones la flambée qu’il alimente côté composants, et la direction prévient que la pression sur les coûts se prolongera en 2027.
Tout le marché encaisse le même choc : les livraisons mondiales de smartphones ont reculé de 20 % sur un an au troisième trimestre, un plus bas de quatorze ans. Samsung en profite pour grimper à 23 % de parts de marché, contre 19 % un an plus tôt, le haut de gamme résistant mieux que le reste du catalogue.
Pour les fêtes, le constructeur mise de nouveau sur ses vaisseaux amiraux, Galaxy S26 (qui a subit une hausse de prix en début de mois), Z Fold 8 Ultra et Z Fold 8 en tête, avec un chiffre d’affaires mobile attendu en retrait sur le trimestre.

articles.title: Science robotics startup Opentrons raises $40M to standardize laboratory automation - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Science robotics startup Opentrons raises $40M to standardize laboratory automation
Opentrons Labworks Inc., a leader in artificial intelligence-driven robotic laboratory automation, today announced it has raised $40 million in new funding to scale its robotics, software and data infrastructure tools.
Healthcare investor Avego led the Series E round alongside BroadOak Capital Partners.
Founded in 2014, Opentrons makes benchtop robots that automate repetitive laboratory tasks, using motorized pipettes to transfer small amounts of liquid between samples inside transparent enclosures. The company’s products include the Flex and OT-2, both programmable robots that can sit in the lab and provide these services.
The company also sells AI software tools for automating sample preparation and other repetitive experimental work.
The Flex and OT-2 resemble small, transparent laboratory cabinets that house the robotic workstations.
Opentrons Flex is the more advanced of the two: an enclosed benchtop robot that transfers small amounts of liquid between laboratory samples. It can work on more samples at once and use an optional robotic gripper to move plates, allowing more steps of an experiment to run without human intervention.
The OT-2 is a smaller, less expensive robot focused on repetitive liquid-handling tasks. It suits laboratories that want to automate routine pipetting but do not need Flex’s higher capacity or automated plate handling.
“Millions of scientists spend much of their day on manual work a robot can do,” said Chief Executive James Atwood, Ph.D. “Giving that time back to discovery is the biggest opportunity in science. We made lab automation accessible for any lab and our systems are built for AI to run experiments directly.”
The robots can be configured for common lab applications including DNA extraction; polymerase chain reaction, or PCR, the rapid multiplication of DNA copies so it can be studied and detected; protein purification; and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays, or ELISAs, a common liquid analysis used to detect antibodies, antigens and other proteins in bodily fluids to look for immunity signs of bacteria, viruses and fungi.
According to Opentrons, although AI models are transforming how science is conducted, the physical lab is becoming a bottleneck. The Flex helps close that gap by using a robot for pipetting and AI software to design, run and improve the continuous experimental loop.
The company added that it has deployed more than 11,000 robots to laboratories in 80-plus countries, including at 90% of the top 20 global pharmaceutical companies. Opentrons seeks to use smart lab equipment to combine physical AI and robotics at scale to create autonomous science.

articles.title: Asistente de IA descubrió un programa espía que dejaba ver las cartas a jugadores de póquer en línea
articles.text:
Un asistente de IA detectó un programa espía instalado en la computadora de un jugador profesional de póquer en línea. El software permitía a un atacante ver su pantalla y, con ella, sus cartas. Según Wired, cientos de jugadores de apuestas altas fueron blanco del mismo método durante años.
El jugador, que habló con la revista bajo el seudónimo de Alex por temor a represalias, usaba el asistente Claude para revisar estadísticas de juego. Tras una falla en su base de datos, el asistente advirtió un programa llamado MeshAgent, capaz de capturar la pantalla y controlar el equipo.
El programa se había instalado sin que Alex lo hiciera. El asistente identificó 11 momentos en que capturó su pantalla, y en todos Alex jugaba en Americas Cardroom (ACR), un sitio de póquer en línea. En 10 de esas sesiones, el mismo rival, con el nombre de usuario OxOO, estaba en su mesa.
Alex revisó las estadísticas públicas de ese jugador y encontró tasas de victoria imposibles para la cantidad de manos jugadas. Calcula que perdió unos USD 30.000, una suma moderada para su nivel. Otros perdieron más.
Cómo eran los programas para espiar
El experto en seguridad que se identifica como WolfSec, y que asesora a jugadores de alto nivel, reveló el caso el pasado 29 de septiembre en X. Según él, el atacante no fue tras cada jugador, sino tras dos programas para jugar en varias mesas a la vez: IntuitiveTables y Jurojin.
En Jurojin, el atacante accedió al sistema del desarrollador para enviar actualizaciones, y el programa espía llegó a los usuarios por el canal normal. El desarrollador de IntuitiveTables usaba Jurojin en su computadora de pruebas, y esa máquina recibió el agente. Con él, el atacante añadió código malicioso a IntuitiveTables antes de que se firmara la versión.
WolfSec estima que el software llegó a más de mil usuarios. Como el código viajó por una actualización o una descarga oficial, ni los jugadores ni sus antivirus notaron nada. La versión alterada de IntuitiveTables solo actuaba si el nombre de usuario figuraba en una lista almacenada en la infraestructura del atacante, formada sobre todo por jugadores habituales de apuestas altas.
Según WolfSec, el mismo atacante intentó infectar equipos desde 2022 con una técnica más simple. No hubo dinero robado en ese momento, así que nadie siguió el caso.
Qué hicieron los sitios frente a esta situación
CoinPoker investiga desde 2025 a un jugador sospechoso. Su portavoz Mario Mosböck dijo a Wired que la empresa lo expulsó y devolvió más de USD 100.000 a afectados. También dijo que la identidad del jugador se conocía desde una entrevista por cámara en febrero de 2025, y que la compañía avisó a ACR sin recibir respuesta.
El profesional Patrick Howard informó a GGPoker a comienzos de septiembre sobre resultados estadísticamente anómalos y no obtuvo respuesta. Tras la revelación pública, el sitio le dijo que no había habido “pruebas concluyentes” en ese momento. ACR y GGPoker no respondieron a las consultas de Wired.
Las fuentes de la revista estiman que el atacante se llevó entre USD 1,5 y 4 millones, sobre todo en GGPoker y ACR, hasta fines de septiembre. ClubWPT Gold expulsó una cuenta y reembolsó a un jugador afectado, según Randy Lundy, responsable de operaciones con clientes del sitio.
El 15 de octubre, GGPoker publicó medidas: prohibir programas de terceros y detectar anomalías en las tasas de victoria. Dijo que rastreó fondos del acusado hasta una cuenta en Coinbase y que pidió restringirla. Jurojin e IntuitiveTables lanzaron herramientas para detectar la infección.
ACR, en cambio, envió el 18 de octubre un correo a sus jugadores: su equipo de seguridad no halló resultados comprometidos ni irregularidades y no habrá reembolsos. WolfSec presentó una denuncia ante el centro de denuncias de delitos informáticos del FBI, que no confirmó a Wired haberla recibido.

articles.title: Google Adopts DPoP to Strengthen OAuth 2.0 Against Token Theft and Replay Attacks
articles.text:
Google's OAuth Platform has recently introduces support for Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession (DPoP), an OAuth 2.0 security mechanism designed to mitigate token theft and replay attacks.
Traditional OAuth bearer tokens operate on a "finders-keepers" model, making them vulnerable to Infostealer malware (e.g. RedLine, NodeStealer) and Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) attacks.
To prevent this types of attacks, DPoP uses cryptography to bind tokens to an asymmetric key pair generated by the client. Consequently, a stolen token cannot be replayed without the corresponding private key, which remains under the client’s control.
Google OAuth platform supports DPoP only for refresh tokens, while access tokens, which are shorter-lived, remain standard Bearer tokens. This decision is motivated by the fact that long-lived refresh tokens are "the primary vector for persistent online impersonation", whereas applying DPoP to access tokens would introduce "asymmetric cryptographic verification overhead" for each request.
It is worth noting that adopting DPoP adds several client-side requirements, including generating cryptographic keys, handling timestamps and nonces correctly, generating the appropriate HTTP headers and the required DPoP proof JWTs.
While DPoP provides protection for API tokens, it does not protect standard web application session cookies, which remain vulnerable to Infostealer malware. To address the threat of cookie theft, Google and the Web Incubator Community Group (WICG) are developing Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC).
DBSC operates at the browser and network layer to cryptographically bind browser session cookies to the device's hardware (such as TPM). Together, DPoP and DBSC form a comprehensive defense-in-depth strategy against credential theft across both API and web-based user sessions.
Google also notes that DPoP is not appropriate for multi-agent workflows, as one agent cannot easily delegate a task to another agent. This would in fact require the second agent to sign requests on behalf of the first. However, this in not possible without accessing the private key generated by the first agent, which would violate DPoP. As an alternative, Google recommends developers to consider Google Cloud Secure Token Service (STS).
By routing delegation through STS, the intermediate agent can exchange the upstream token for a new, short-lived federated token cryptographically bound to its own local key pair, preserving the sender-constrained security model across the entire agent chain without key exposure.
Since the DPoP private key is stored client-side, its security ultimately depends on the security of the client itself. However, as Dhruv Agnihotri argues, single-page-apps (SPAs) running inside a browser are not entirely protected against misuse of the key. The IETF's guidance for browser-based applications therefore recommends adopting the Backend-for-Frontend pattern to keep tokens and cryptographic keys out of the browser. Agnihotri also proposes a zero-persistence approach, which may be useful when server-side infrastructure is unavailable.

articles.title: Alphabet Announces Q3 2026 Results, Revenue at $127.6 Billion
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
Alphabet Announces Q3 2026 Results, Revenue at $127.6 Billion
Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOG, GOOGL) today announced financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
- Consolidated Alphabet revenues increased 25% to $127.6 billion, reflecting strong performance across the business and our 13th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth.
- Google Services revenues increased 11% to $96.3 billion, led by 12% growth in Google Search & other with the year-over-year Search query growth rate the highest it has been in the last five years.
- Google Cloud delivered record growth as revenues increased 103% to $30.7 billion, led by strong growth in Google Cloud Platform (GCP) across enterprise AI infrastructure and enterprise AI solutions, as well as core GCP services. TPU systems sales were also a meaningful contributor to revenue growth.
- Consolidated Alphabet operating income increased 30% and operating margin was 31.8%.
- Net income available to common stockholders was $26.2 billion and EPS was $2.12.
Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet, said:
"We had a strong quarter and are now on a half-trillion dollar revenue run rate. Our deep full stack approach is driving momentum across the business, with Alphabet revenues growing 25% year-over year. Our AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries. In fact, our year-over-year query growth rate is the highest it's been in the last five years. Google Cloud revenues grew 103%, powered by huge demand for our AI infrastructure and AI solutions. We're also seeing strong demand for our TPU systems across a wide range of customers. Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon are now leading at the frontier. Overall, our first-party model APIs are now processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, more than four times what we processed a year ago. On top of that, the Gemini app has reached one billion users—making it the fastest-growing product in Google's history—and we surpassed 150 million YouTube Music and Premium subscribers globally, including trials. We're excited by the range of big opportunities ahead of us."
Q3 2026 Financial Highlights (unaudited)
The following table summarizes our consolidated financial results for the quarters ended September 30, 2025 and 2026 (in millions, except for per share information and percentages).Additional Information Relating to the Quarter Ended September 30, 2026 (unaudited)
At-the-Market Program
During the three months ended September 30, 2026, we issued 12 million shares of Class A stock for net proceeds of $4.3 billion and 24 million shares of Class C stock for net proceeds of $8.1 billion. As of September 30, 2026, $27.6 billion remained available for future issuance under the ATM Program.
Issuance of Senior Unsecured Notes
In the third quarter of 2026, we issued senior unsecured notes for net proceeds of $28.7 billion, to be used for general corporate purposes.
Preferred and Common Dividend Programs
In October 2026, the company's Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $15.63 per share on each of our Series A and Series B mandatory convertible preferred stock (equivalent to approximately $0.78 per share on each of our Series A and Series B Depositary Shares) and a quarterly cash dividend of $0.22 per share on our Class A, Class B, and Class C stock. The mandatory convertible preferred stock dividend is payable on November 15, 2026 to stockholders of record for each of the company's Series A and Series B shares as of November 1, 2026, and the common stock dividend is payable on December 14, 2026 to stockholders of record for each of the company's Class A, Class B, and Class C shares as of December 7, 2026.

articles.title: Le Black Friday 2026 n’attend même plus novembre : les premières offres sont là (EN DIRECT)
articles.text:
Le vendredi 27 novembre 2026 est la date à retenir, mais les marchands n’attendent pas jusque-là pour proposer leurs réductions. Entre les avant-premières qui démarrent cette année le 30 octobre chez Boulanger, la Black Week et les prolongations jusqu’au Cyber Monday du 30 novembre, le Black Friday occupe désormais une bonne partie du calendrier.
Il reste généralement l’un des meilleurs moments de l’année pour s’équiper, particulièrement cette année. Les réductions seront particulièrement attendues après les hausses qui ont touché toute la tech sur fond de crise de la RAM. Ce Black Friday sera l’occasion de guetter une PS5, une Switch 2 ou un PC à un tarif plus digeste.
Encore faut-il que les remises fassent mieux qu’effacer la dernière augmentation. C’est aussi ce que nous vérifierons dans ce live.
Les meilleures offres en avant-première du Black Friday
Dyson V16 Piston Animal
Les cheveux enroulés autour de la brosse font partie des corvées que le Dyson V16 Piston Animal cherche à réduire. Sa tête à deux rouleaux coniques est conçue pour limiter leur accumulation, tandis qu’un mécanisme compacte la poussière dans le collecteur. L’aspirateur passe à 649 € chez Boulanger, au lieu de 849 €, avec la même offre à la Fnac. Lancé en 2025, ce modèle propose une puissance d’aspiration élevée et jusqu’à 70 minutes d’autonomie annoncée en mode Éco, bien moins à pleine puissance.
Il faut néanmoins compter avec ses 3,4 kg, qui se ressentiront davantage dans les escaliers ou lors d’une longue séance. Cette version Animal aspire uniquement : elle ne possède pas la tête lavante du modèle Submarine. Si vous souhaitez surtout un Dyson efficace au quotidien sans payer les nouveautés du V16, le V15 Detect Absolute est proposé à 549 € chez Boulanger, soit 100 € de moins. Une alternative à considérer avant de choisir automatiquement le numéro le plus élevé.
Asus ROG XG27AQWMG
L’OLED devient de plus en plus accessible sur les écrans PC. Il y a encore un an, trouver un bon moniteur équipé de cette technologie sous les 500 € restait rare. L’Asus ROG XG27AQWMG passe justement à 469 € chez Boulanger, au lieu de 599,99 €, avec une fiche technique pourtant loin de l’entrée de gamme. Sa dalle Tandem OLED de 27 pouces en définition QHD (2560 × 1440 pixels) permet de conserver une image détaillée sans demander autant de puissance graphique que la 4K. Il monte jusqu’à 280 Hz pour les jeux compétitifs. Le modèle succède au XG27AQDMG avec une dalle plus récente et plus lumineuse de quoi bien accueillir GTA 6 pour celles et ceux qui ne joueront pas sur un téléviseur.
Black Friday 2026 : tout ce qu’il faut savoir
Depuis une dizaine d’années, le Black Friday s’est infiltré dans le calendrier commercial des grandes marques et enseignes françaises. Avec l’expérience, on peut vous dire que cet événement fait partie des meilleurs moments pour faire de bonnes affaires.
Les dates du Black Friday

On dirait presque les soldes, finalement. Mais c’est aussi moins le rush, ce qui est une bonne chose pour ceux qui veulent faire des achats plus raisonnés. - 27 novembre : la date du Black Friday, même si les offres commencent généralement avant et se prolongent le week-end des 28 et 29 novembre.

articles.title: SK Hynix expects memory chip shortage to persist until at least 2030
articles.text:
AI Gold Rush: SK Hynix's latest quarterly results confirm a familiar trend across the semiconductor supply chain. AI data center projects are putting enormous pressure on manufacturers' ability to meet demand, and end customers are likely to face unprecedented shortages for years to come.
SK Hynix recently published its financial results for the third quarter of 2026. Beyond the rosy numbers fueled by surging demand for memory chips, the South Korean semiconductor manufacturer also outlined where it expects the market to go over the next few years. Big spoiler: demand for AI-related products isn't going anywhere anytime soon, which means the ongoing DRAM shortage could persist for years.
SK Hynix said that the third quarter of its financial year ended with 104.6155 trillion won ($78 billion) in revenue, 83.3338 trillion won ($63 billion) in operating profit, and 39.7756 trillion won ($30 billion) in net profit. Revenue and operating profit rose by 32% and 38%, respectively, compared with the previous quarter.
These unprecedented results were largely driven by a massive increase in sales of server DDR5 memory chips, while shipments of newer HBM4 chips have only just begun. NAND sales for SSDs are also expanding, while higher-margin data center products continue to grow across the board. For the first time in its history, SK Hynix surpassed 100 trillion won in quarterly revenue in Q3 2026.
The Korean manufacturer, one of the memory industry's "Big Three," described the ongoing memory crisis as a "virtuous" cycle for its business. SK Hynix expects the growing adoption of generative AI, chatbots, and other technologies based on large language models to drive further investment in infrastructure and additional memory products.
"The company likewise expects the memory market to sustain its growth, led in the short term by enterprise and personal AI and, over the mid-to-long term, by physical AI such as autonomous driving and robotics," SK Hynix added.
Despite the backlash against data center projects in the US and elsewhere in the world, SK Hynix said new infrastructure projects are putting further pressure on manufacturers' ability to meet demand for memory chips. Supply is failing to keep pace with the market's rapid growth, and SK Hynix now expects demand to exceed supply "through 2030."
The Korean giant is planning to "accelerate" the expansion of its manufacturing capacity. SK Hynix is building new chip plants in its homeland and the US, although it will likely take years for these new facilities to come online. In the meantime, customers will just have to "enjoy" their DDR5 shortage for a few more years, the company suggests.

articles.title: Trump ignored intel on China’s Nvidia spy to protect company’s stock, report says
articles.text:
Donald Trump presents the National Medal of Science to US' CEO Of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, during the "Golden Age of American Innovation Summit."
Credit:
KENT NISHIMURA / Contributor | AFP
Donald Trump presents the National Medal of Science to US' CEO Of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, during the "Golden Age of American Innovation Summit."
Credit:
KENT NISHIMURA / Contributor | AFP
Donald Trump apparently is so aligned with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang—who has become the president’s key advisor on AI—that he ignored intelligence indicating that Huang was the target of a “Chinese spy plot,” and did so partly to protect Nvidia’s stock.
The New York Times spoke with people briefed on US intelligence agencies’ surveillance and granted them anonymity to discuss findings drawn from “classified intelligence.” According to sources, about a year ago, Trump was briefed that “Beijing was getting reports from someone with direct access” to Huang. That “someone” was Alice Huang, or Huang Le, a Chinese citizen and former top executive at a Singapore cloud company called Megaspeed.
According to sources, the US had already suspected that Alice Huang—who is not related to Jensen Huang—was helping China evade export controls to gain access to high-end Nvidia chips through Megaspeed. But it alarmed investigators to discover that she may have used her role at Megaspeed to gain direct access to Jensen Huang. It’s now believed she may have leveraged that closeness to feed China intel not only on one of America’s leading AI companies, but also to influence Trump’s thinking on AI. As Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted last month ahead of Trump’s AI talks with China President Xi Jinping, “the president is completely aligned with Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia.”
At least partly due to fears that US action against the alleged spying could hobble Nvidia chip sales or disrupt the delicate US-China trade truce, Trump “chose not to do anything with the information,” sources said.
Soon after US scrutiny increased, Alice Huang’s name was removed from Megaspeed corporate documents. At this stage, it’s unclear “how closely she is still connected to Megaspeed,” NYT reported.
Liu Chang, the spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Washington, DC, told NYT that the US accusations against Alice Huang are baseless. He accused the US of pursuing a campaign of “groundless smears and slanders” against China.
No warning to Nvidia CEO
It’s not clear which agencies were investigating Alice Huang or what triggered their suspicions, NYT reported. Sources also could not explain what information she may have shared with Beijing.
Nvidia has denied that she would have had access to any trade secrets, but it seems notable that Jensen Huang did not receive a defensive briefing that Americans sometimes get when they’re targets of foreign spying. Some senior officials think it’s unlikely that Jensen Huang would have “remained unaware” of Alice Huang’s alleged intelligence-gathering for the entire duration of their professional relationship, although Trump was told Jensen Huang had no knowledge at the time of his briefing. It seems possible that Jensen Huang got no briefing because US agencies worried that he might tip her off that “she was being watched,” the NYT reported.
Trump’s deep ties with tech leaders have been criticized throughout his administration, but Jensen Huang’s influence increasingly stands out. To critics, the political friendship appears to be largely based on growing his business in China. Since cozying up to Trump, the Nvidia CEO has gotten export controls relaxed and even struck a controversial deal giving the US a 25 percent cut of some chip sales so he could try to sell more chips in China. Sources told NYT that “some investigations and proposed trade sanctions involving China or Nvidia” have “ground to a halt within the Commerce Department” due to Jensen Huang’s influence.
No one’s sure when Jensen Huang met Alice Huang, but NYT found social media photos that predated her role arranging a Megaspeed purchase of $2 billion in chips over the next year. If those chips ended up in China, the US worried they “could help adversaries like China develop new weapons, surveil dissidents, and leap ahead of the United States in AI development,” NYT reported. To US agencies, it’s particularly concerning that Megaspeed may be doing China’s bidding by supplying chips to giant data centers in Malaysia and Indonesia “that appear to remotely serve customers in China,” NYT reported earlier this month.
Sources told the NYT that US intelligence agencies conducted electronic surveillance of Alice Huang and found that “she was in contact with an American citizen.” Since agencies could not legally surveil the American citizen without a court order, they sought to unmask the citizen by showing a “need for information.”
“In this case, the unmasking process identified Mr. Huang as the US citizen,” NYT reported.
NYT probes Megaspeed offices for clues
Megaspeed is an Nvidia customer, and Nvidia has independently investigated whether Megaspeed is funneling its chips to China. That investigation concluded that there were no signs of diversion and that Megaspeed has raised no red flags as a customer, Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo told NYT.
Both Nvidia and Megaspeed insist that the cloud company has Singapore-based owners, but NYT visited the supposed offices and talked to anyone they could find to probe the actual business operations. Among red flags raised, NYT noted that staffers suggested “it’s not clear” what Megaspeed as a company does and confirmed that the Singapore director, James Tan, lives in China and is “never present.” (NYT’s review of corporate ownership documents showed Tan owns the shell company that owns Megaspeed.)
In that story published earlier this month, NYT detailed how Alice Huang was seemingly growing increasingly close to Jensen Huang, citing several photos of them together. That includes a photo at an event where she reportedly bragged, “I bet you guys I can get Jensen here,” and then he arrived in his trademark leather jacket to take whiskey shots.
Rizzo said that it was common for Nvidia’s CEO to attend parties with customers and partners, where he discussed “updates on the market.” One source told NYT that Jensen Huang had always planned to attend that party.
“Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected,” Rizzo said. “Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year.”
However, the US government has been investigating Megaspeed since 2024, and they’ve found suspicious boxes of Nvidia equipment that seem to be ready to ship out, rather than installed. Earlier this year, the Department of Justice took over the Commerce Department’s investigation, and Megaspeed remains under scrutiny even though Nvidia’s probes uncovered no evidence the company was helping China dodge export curb violations.
Aaron Bartnick, an assistant director for technology security and governance under the Biden administration, told NYT that Megaspeed raised “many red flags.” Among them are the company’s “ownership claims and possible ties to sanctioned entities,that should have made Nvidia’s executives question whether they should have permitted the company to have access to its AI chips.”
“It’s hard to see a justification for taking that risk,” Bartnick said.
Ashley is a senior policy reporter for Ars Technica, dedicated to tracking social impacts of emerging policies and new technologies. She is a Chicago-based journalist with 20 years of experience.

articles.title: Dept of Justice reportedly probes Nvidia over $13 billion Hugging Face AI platform acquisition — concerns raised over competition in AI and pressure on customers
articles.text:
Dept of Justice reportedly probes Nvidia over $13 billion Hugging Face AI platform acquisition — concerns raised over competition in AI and pressure on customers
The DOJ is concerned that Nvidia's Hugging Face buyout may give it control of a key distribution point.
Nvidia is reportedly facing questions from the United States Department of Justice over whether its purchase of Hugging Face will have an impact on competition in the growing AI space. Nvidia agreed to buy Hugging Face in September, paying almost $13 billion. Hugging Face offers an open-source platform for the hosting and testing of new AI models, and that appears to be behind the DOJ's concerns. Reuters reports that the department has made inquiries about how the Hugging Face deal could change the landscape for Nvidia's competitors. The move could be seen as a way for Nvidia to lock in a key distribution channel for its own products. Hugging Face also sells AI infrastructure. Nvidia has declined to comment on the story.
This isn't the first time that Nvidia has found itself in the DOJ's crosshairs. As Nvidia becomes more vital to the tech industry as a whole and AI technologies specifically, the company has come under increasing scrutiny within the U.S. government, stretching back to the Biden administration. Things didn't improve when the Trump administration took over, with the U.S. president reportedly tempted to break the company up — despite being unfamiliar with what it was. More recently, Nvidia and other AI hardware makers found themselves under export controls. Nvidia's powerful AI-focused hardware can only be sold to approved entities, while it cannot ship to countries including China, Iran, North Korea, and Russia.
At home, the DOJ has also looked into Nvidia's purchase of SchedMD, a company whose software is used to run supercomputers that have ties to national security. Nvidia promised to continue to support the software as part of a larger three-year investigation into its conduct. Officials have also considered whether Nvidia dangled a larger allocation of its AI chips in front of customers who also purchased its networking hardware as well as Groq chips — Nvidia bought Groq for $20 billion in December of 2025. The deal included the acquihires of key members of the AI chip startup's team, including its CEO.
As for Hugging Face, Nvidia has similarly confirmed that it will continue to support a range of chip and AI providers once the buyout completes. It's expected that Hugging Face will officially become part of Nvidia in the first half of 2027.

articles.title: Binance pauses withdrawals as hackers suspected of stealing billions in crypto | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Binance has confirmed to TechCrunch that it is dealing with a security incident as users reported that funds were being drained from the crypto exchange’s wallets.
The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange said in an emailed statement to TechCrunch that it is “aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating.”
“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” Binance said in a statement.
“Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information,” the statement added. “Users should remain cautious of scams and should not trust unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information.”
Binance spokesperson Ross O’Leary said that Binance has “temporarily suspended withdrawals on multiple networks following a security incident as a precautionary measure.”
News of the breach comes hours after Binance founder Changpeng Zhao said in a post on X that the company likely had been hacked. Zhao, who no longer runs the company but is its largest shareholder, said that he expects users’ funds to be “fully covered” but did not provide an explanation for the claim.
Financial tech giant Circle froze about $800 million in Tether as it passed through its networks, while crypto giant Tether froze about $1.56 billion related to Binance’s hack.
Crypto watchers say at least $2 billion has been drained from Binance’s hot wallets, which are internet-connected cryptocurrency wallets that store crypto that are connected to the internet. By some estimates, Binance may have lost upward of $5.7 billion in crypto, though the numbers have not been confirmed and it’s possible that the theft is ongoing.
It’s unclear who is behind the hack, and Binance did not say if it had received any correspondence from the hackers.
If confirmed into the billions, this would likely rank as one of the largest crypto breaches in history, according to leaderboards tracking crypto thefts.
In 2025, hackers stole a record $1.4 billion in crypto in a single breach from exchange Bybit, blamed on North Korean hackers.
In what appears to be a separate incident earlier on Thursday, prediction market giant Polymarket briefly halted trading after it confirmed that a third-party company was compromised, which led to the company pausing withdrawals. According to security researchers, hackers stole around $2 million in user funds after compromising a piece of software developed by a company called DebugBear.

articles.title: Patrick Stewart (X-Men, Star Trek, Dune) ha muerto a los 86 años: adiós a una leyenda del teatro, el cine y la TV
articles.text:
Luto en Hollywood por el fallecimiento de Patrick Stewart, el icónico actor detrás de personajes como Charles Xavier en la saga X-Men, el capitán Jean-Luc Picard en Star Trek: The Next Generation y Gurney Halleck en Dune, ha fallecido a los 86 años.
Según reportan Deadline y The Hollywood Reporter, la muerte de Patrick Stewart fue confirmada por Kelly Bush Novak, quien se desempeñó como vocera del intérprete británico. De acuerdo con la información disponible, Stewart padecía Alzheimer y demencia con cuerpos de Lewy.
La salud de Patrick Stewart se había deteriorado considerablemente en el último tiempo y su deceso se produjo en su casa de Los Ángeles, rodeado de familiares y amigos. "Guardaremos para siempre el recuerdo de la serena tranquilidad y la reflexión que se reflejaban en su rostro, un testimonio perdurable de su invencible gracia", indicó su portavoz.
Apenas conocida la muerte de Patrick Stewart, Marvel publicó un comunicado expresando su pesar. Tengamos en cuenta que el actor volvió a interpretar al profesor Xavier en Avengers: Doomsday, que se estrenará en diciembre. Dicho trabajo, que apuntaba a ser su despedida definitiva del personaje que interpretó durante 26 años, finalmente será un lanzamiento póstumo.
"Todos en Marvel Studios estamos profundamente entristecidos por el fallecimiento de Sir Patrick Stewart. Sir Patrick dio vida al profesor Charles Xavier con una gracia, inteligencia y humanidad extraordinarias, definiendo al personaje para generaciones de seguidores, desde X-Men y Logan hasta Avengers: Doomsday. Fue un talento excepcional, un colaborador generoso y un auténtico caballero. Nuestros pensamientos están con su esposa Sunny, sus hijos, sus amigos y los innumerables seguidores en todo el mundo cuyas vidas tocó a través de su arte", indicaron los dirigidos por Kevin Feige.
El adiós a Patrick Stewart, dueño de una carrea formidable en teatro, cine y TV
La carrera actoral de Patrick Stewart se inició a finales de la década de 1950 en teatro, donde destacaría rápidamente. Formó parte de la Royal Shakespeare Company desde 1966 hasta los primeros años de la década de 1980. En paralelo, tuvo múltiples apariciones en películas y series británicas.
Sin embargo, su despegue fuera del teatro no llegó hasta la segunda mitad de los ochenta. Si bien formó parte de Dune, de David Lynch, que llegó a los cines en 1984, no fue hasta su elección para encarnar a Jean-Luc Picard en Star Trek: The Next Generation que se hizo mundialmente conocido.
Patrick Stewart interpretó al capitán del USS Enterprise desde 1987 hasta 1994, y repitió el papel en cuatro películas de la saga. Asimismo, tuvo participación en otras series de la franquicia y se despidió del personaje en 2023, tras volver a darle vida en las tres temporadas de Star Trek: Picard.
En el cine, el papel más icónico de Patrick Stewart ha sido el del profesor Charles Xavier de los X-Men. El británico protagonizó la trilogía original de la saga mutante de Fox (2000 a 2006) y luego repitió en X-Men: Días del futuro pasado (2014) y Logan (2017). Años después llegó al Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel como una variante del profesor X en Doctor Strange en el multiverso de la locura (2022).
Su última vez como el icónico líder de los X-Men fue en Avengers: Doomsday, donde se reunió con su gran amigo Ian McKellen, quien también regresó para dar vida a Magneto por última vez.
Si bien Patrick Stewart es principalmente conocido por sus roles dramáticos y de personajes de franquicia, también tuvo la oportunidad de explotar su lado más cómico. En 1993 fue parte de Robin Hood: Men in Tights, de Mel Brooks, mientras que años más tarde también participó en las dos entregas de Ted (2012 y 2015) como el narrador y en Emoji: La película (2017), prestando su voz ni más ni menos que al emoji de caca. En televisión, en tanto, participó de series como Robot Chicken, Los Simpson, Futurama y Padre de familia.
Una amplia presencia en el mundo de los videojuegos
Patrick Stewart no tuvo miedo de experimentar en el mundo de los videojuegos. A lo largo de su carrera participó de varios títulos relacionados principalmente con Star Trek y X-Men, pero no se limitó a estos.
También prestó su voz a títulos como The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion, Castlevania: Lords of Shadow y Forgotten Realms: Demon Stone. Asimismo, ofició como narrador en varios otros juegos como Los Sims medieval, Lego Universe y Felix the Reaper.
Dueño de una de las carreras más prolíficas y exitosas, además de un carisma y una versatilidad envidiables, Patrick Stewart se despide como una auténtica leyenda de Hollywood y la industria del entretenimiento al completo.

articles.title: Seulement 29 véhicules achetés en 2026, la Gendarmerie fonce vers un mur d’obsolescence à vitesse grand V
articles.text:
Un rapport de l'Assemblée nationale alerte sur le parc automobile de la Gendarmerie, menacé d'un « mur d'obsolescence » en 2028 faute d'achats de véhicules. Les hélicoptères Écureuil, quadragénaires, attendent quant à eux une relève qui tarde.
Le parc automobile de la Gendarmerie nationale et sa flotte d'hélicoptères vieillissent plus vite qu'ils ne se renouvellent. Pour la Gendarmerie, l'année 2028 sera entourée d'un rouge vif, puisque ses véhicules risquent d'y heurter ce que la députée Anne-Laure Blin (Droite Républicaine) appelle un « mur d'obsolescence », au moment même où ses vieux hélicoptères Écureuil commenceront à être définitivement retirés du service. Repéré par Opex360 et consulté par Clubic, l'avis budgétaire de la députée Anne-Laure Blin, rendu au nom de la commission de la Défense de l'Assemblée nationale, détaille un parc décrépit. Les économies faites hier, avec comme conséquences des achats en berne, des appareils quadragénaires et des livraisons retardées, risquent de se payer demain.
La Gendarmerie n'achètera peut-être aucun véhicule en 2027
Pour mesurer l'ampleur du problème, faisons un d'arithmétique si vous le voulez bien. Dans l'avis tamponné par l'Assemblée nationale, on apprend que la Gendarmerie roule avec 33 600 véhicules légers, chacun étant censé servir environ huit ans, avant d'être remplacé. Pour éviter que l'ensemble ne vieillisse, il faudrait donc en renouveler un huitième tous les ans, soit autour de 3 750 véhicules neufs. Ce rythme, l'institution l'a bien frôlé en 2022, avec 3 736 véhicules achetés. Mais depuis, elle ne l'a tenu qu'une seule fois, c'était en 2025, avec 4 554 achats, une année faste qui n'a pourtant pas suffi à combler le retard des précédentes.
Les autres années, les achats se sont effondrés, avec 1 055 véhicules en 2023, 730 en 2024, et surtout… 29 seulement en 2026, à date, pour une force pourtant compétente sur 96 % du territoire. En additionnant ces manques année après année, on arrive fin 2026 à près de 8 650 véhicules qui auraient dû être renouvelés et ne l'ont pas été. Et le projet de budget 2027 n'arrange rien, puisqu'il prévoit une nouvelle « année blanche », c'est-à-dire aucun achat de véhicule léger, ou presque. Le rapport pointe aussi des dépenses imprévues qui grignotent l'argent de l'investissement. En 2026 par exemple, il fait état de 100 millions d'euros de surcoûts, du G7 aux feux de forêts, qui devront être financés sur le budget existant, sans rallonge, sans compter la flambée du carburant.
Pendant ce temps, avec 8,2 ans de moyenne d'âge, le parc des véhicules des gendarmes a déjà dépassé, en moyenne, sa durée de vie théorique. Et 8 526 véhicules dépassent les seuils de réforme, fixés à huit ans et 200 000 km. En clair, on parle ici d'unités qui devraient déjà être remplacées. Si rien ne se voit encore, c'est que les commandes de 2025 continuent d'arriver, avec 2 315 livraisons attendues à la mi-2026. Mais avec un robinet fermé, la rapporteure redoute le choc pour 2028, qui pourrait être une année noire, avec davantage de pannes et un entretien toujours plus coûteux.
Les Écureuil de la Gendarmerie volent sur leurs dernières réserves
Dans le ciel, la situation n'est guère plus rassurante pour nos amis gendarmes. Sur le papier, on sait que la Gendarmerie totalise 58 hélicoptères. Dans le détail, elle compte 26 AS350 Écureuil, âgés de 40 ans en moyenne, et, pour le reste, 15 EC135, 15 EC145 et deux H145 D3 tout neufs. Une dizaine d'Écureuil ont déjà dû être retirés du service, et les survivants passent plus de temps immobilisés que prêts à décoller. L'an dernier, ils n'étaient disponibles que 43,7 % du temps, soit moins d'un jour sur deux, contre 72,3 % pour les EC135 et 66,6 % pour les EC145, des appareils pourtant âgés de 17 à 20 ans en moyenne.
Et la relève alors ? Là aussi, elle se fait attendre. En 2021, la Gendarmerie a commandé dix H160 (la version civile du célèbre Guépard), des hélicoptères récents d'Airbus, financés par le plan de relance lancé après la crise sanitaire. D'après le contrat, plusieurs devraient déjà être en service, mais seuls deux le sont, et un troisième est attendu en novembre. Ces appareils seront en outre d'abord privés de certaines fonctions de mission, comme la cartographie, qui demanderont des mises à niveau. Surtout, le compte n'y était pas dès le départ, car même livrés à l'heure, ces dix H160 et les six H145 D3 commandés en 2023 ne font que 16 appareils, pour remplacer 26 Écureuil.
Les renforts sont enfin en vue. En décembre 2026, la Gendarmerie doit officialiser une commande de 23 hélicoptères, dont 22 H145 D3 d'Airbus Helicopters déjà prévus en option dans le contrat de 2023. Il ne restait plus qu'à les commander pour de bon. Le vingt-troisième remplacera l'appareil perdu en août, lors d'un crash qui a coûté la vie à l'adjudant Dorian Larigaudrie et grièvement blessé deux gendarmes. Les premiers exemplaires n'arriveront que dix-huit mois après la commande, début 2028… pile au moment où les Écureuil commenceront à être retirés pour de bon. Selon le rapport, la flotte devra donc tourner avec six à sept hélicoptères de moins pendant deux à trois ans.

articles.title: Tesla Model Y : la voiture la plus vendue d'Europe est aussi celle qui pollue le moins selon Green NCAP
articles.text:
Le SUV électrique de Tesla est en tête des ventes, et maintenant en tête d’un classement environnemental. Green NCAP, le pendant écologique d’Euro NCAP (l’organisme des crash-tests), a publié ce jeudi 29 octobre sa note pour le Model Y. La version Propulsion, celle à un seul moteur, obtient cinq étoiles sur cinq. D’après le calcul de Green NCAP, elle émet 95 grammes d’équivalent CO2 par kilomètre sur toute sa vie, de l’extraction des matières premières jusqu’à la casse. À titre de comparaison, le Volkswagen Tayron essence micro-hybride, un SUV de taille proche testé dans la même série, est à 263 grammes.
Seule la version Propulsion (ex. Standard) avec sa batterie de 62,5 kWh et ses jantes de 18 pouces a été testée. Green NCAP prévient aussi que ses étoiles ne se comparent pas d’une année à l’autre : les seuils sont devenus plus sévères en 2025, quand le cycle de vie a été ajouté au calcul.
Les étoiles sont la moyenne de trois notes sur 10. La première porte sur « l’air propre » (gaz d’échappement, mais aussi particules de pneus et de freins), la deuxième sur l’efficacité énergétique et la troisième sur les gaz à effet de serre. Depuis 2025, la méthode de Green NCAP intègre aux trois notes l’un des paramètres les plus importants : l’analyse du cycle de vie, qui compte la fabrication de la voiture et de sa batterie, la production de l’électricité et le recyclage.
Le Tesla Model Y est champion de l’écologie
Le Model Y obtient respectivement les notes de 9 puis 8,9 et enfin 10. Ce dernier score vient en bonne partie de Tesla, qui a transmis les données de production de son usine près de Berlin, où sont assemblés les Model Y européens. Les experts de l’organisme les ont vérifiées. Sans ces données, Green NCAP applique des hypothèses génériques plus sévères.
Mais tout n’est pas rose vert derrière les cinq étoiles. En l’occurrence, le Model Y n’a obtenu que 7,4 sur 10 sur les émissions hors échappement. La faute revient à son poids de 1 914 kg, usant davantage les pneus. De plus, le SUV ne marque aucun point sur les systèmes qui filtrent ou enferment la poussière de frein, puisqu’il ne les utilise que très peu. Son freinage régénératif, qui ralentit la voiture avec le moteur tout en rechargeant la batterie, limite quand même l’usure des plaquettes.
Par -7 °C, au démarrage à froid, la consommation monte aussi à 30,5 kWh aux 100 km en laboratoire, contre 13,1 kWh au cycle d’homologation WLTP. En conditions réelles, Green NCAP estime l’autonomie à 449 km en trajet mixte l’été et 274 km l’hiver, contre 534 km WLTP. Une valeur que nous avions également estimée lors de notre essai du modèle.
L’organisme souligne par ailleurs que préchauffer la voiture pendant qu’elle est branchée fait tout de même gagner 101 km d’autonomie. Enfin, sur la recharge bidirectionnelle (V2L, V2G et V2H), le Model Y testé a la plus mauvaise note, car elle n’existe tout simplement pas, du moins en Europe.
Si le Model Y peut revendiquer l’empreinte carbone la plus faible, il n’est pas le mieux noté de la série. La BYD Dolphin Surf le surpasse de 3 points avec un score de 96 %, notamment grâce à son gabarit plus favorable. Les émissions sur l’ensemble du cycle de vie s’élèvent à 112,5 g d’équivalent CO₂/km, dont 61 proviennent de sa production en Chine.

articles.title: Pine Labs Q2 net profit soars 6.5x; Cognizant trims 2026 growth outlook
articles.text:
Pine Labs Q2 net profit soars 6.5x; Cognizant trims 2026 growth outlook
Pine Labs’ net profit rose 6.5 times to Rs 38.6 crore in the second quarter of FY27, while revenue grew 24% year on year to Rs 806 crore. In other news, Cognizant has trimmed the upper end of its annual growth guidance for 2026.
Dear Reader,
The finance ministry expects India’s economy to grow at 7.3% in FY27.
This estimate, in the ministry’s October economic review, is slightly above the forecast of 7.1% by the Reserve Bank of India, released earlier this month. The ministry has also flagged inflation risks, besides geopolitical tensions, energy price volatility, and tighter global financial conditions. But India is “well-positioned” to sustain its growth trajectory, it noted.
Meanwhile, Zoho’s Sridhar Vembu has a word of caution for all of us: one smart person using AI can do the work of ten.
“The risk is getting ever more real. This does not mean 90% of people working on a computer will have no work at all… What it does mean is a rebalancing across the economy and that is painful when we go through it,” he wrote on X.
We have to accept this and be prepared, said Vembu, who has spoken candidly in recent times on AI, jobs, and the overall state of the tech industry. At TechSparks, YourStory’s flagship summit, Vembu had said that AI could outperform 90% of coders in six months.
In other news, private equity firm One Planet Partners has partnered with Japan’s Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank to launch a Rs 3,000 crore fund. The fund will focus on high-growth businesses benefiting from India's energy transition, mobility, and manufacturing-led industrial expansion.
In today’s newsletter:
- Pine Labs Q2 net profit soars 6.5x
- Cognizant trims 2026 growth outlook
Here’s your trivia for today: Which tech company once announced a job listing for ‘Pokemon Master’ as part of an April Fools’ joke? (Scroll down for the answer)
Earnings
Pine Labs Q2 net profit soars 6.5x
Pine Labs’ net profit rose 6.5 times to Rs 38.6 crore in the second quarter of FY27, while revenue grew 24% year on year to Rs 806 crore. The fintech company had reported a net profit of Rs 6 crore and revenue of Rs 650 crore in the second quarter of the previous fiscal year.
Quarterly highlights:
- Pine Labs’ online payments business grew by over 45% year on year, while gross transaction value rose 140%, driven by expansion into agentic commerce, cross-border payments, small and medium businesses, and government segments.
- According to the company, AI agents now contribute to around 89% of code changes. The company plans to reinvest the resulting efficiency gains in new products, geographies and categories while maintaining a strong EBITDA profile.
- The fintech firm’s international business spans more than 22 markets. Revenue from Southeast Asia grew by around 40% YoY, while its UAE business crossed one lakh daily transactions.
Corporate
Cognizant trims 2026 growth outlook
US-headquartered IT services company Cognizant saw its net profit more than double in the third quarter of 2026 while revenue grew by 4.6%. It reported a net profit of $627 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with $274 million in the same period in 2025, recording a growth of 129%. Revenue was $5.66 billion in Q3 of 2026, compared with $5.41 billion in the year-ago quarter.
However, the company has trimmed the upper end of its annual growth guidance for 2026.
Key takeaways:
- The financial services segment recorded a YoY growth of 12.3%, while communications, media & technology rose 10.7%. But products and resources saw a marginal dip of 0.8%, and healthcare fell 0.9%.
- The North America market grew by 5.8%, followed by Europe at 2.2% and the rest of the world at 1.4%.
- The company has revised its annual revenue growth guidance from 4-5.5% to 4-4.4%, indicating the growth challenges IT services companies continue to face.
News & updates
- AI acquisition: SaaS major Freshworks has acquired Israel-based AI startup Robusta Dev, an incident intelligence engine that uses AI to investigate tech disruptions, identify root causes, and recommend remediation actions. The acquisition is expected to strengthen the capabilities of Freshservice—Freshworks’ IT service management platform—in incident management and IT operations.
- Startup incubation: Bengaluru-based AI-powered cybersecurity and threat intelligence company CloudSEK has launched CloudSEK Launchpad, a 12-week incubation programme for early-stage cybersecurity startups. The first cohort will have 10 companies, each eligible for up to $5,000 in AI model credits.
- New report: India’s new-age manufacturing sector could benefit significantly from a $3 trillion global AI infrastructure investment cycle, according to a report by Avendus Capital. The investment banking firm says defence and aerospace, space technology, robotics and automation, semiconductors, energy transition, and advanced materials will drive India’s next phase of industrial growth.

articles.title: Japan Airlines suffers third-party data breach exposing passenger info
articles.text:
Japan Airlines (JAL) has announced that a data breach at Amadeus’s Passenger Service System exposed the data of about 92,000 customers.
JAL Group, which operates the airlines JAL and Japan Transocean Air, uses the system to handle passenger reservations, ticketing, and check-in.
According to its announcement, Amadeus notified the airline on October 23, 2026, that unauthorized access to its systems occurred between August 10, 2023, and September 23, 2026.
As a result of this lengthy breach, the threat actor accessed reservation codes (PNRs), names, flight dates, routes, and travel classes for approximately 90,000 customers.
An additional 2,000 customers had the above data types exposed, plus their email addresses, phone numbers, passport numbers, nationalities, frequent flyer numbers, and flight, ticket, and seat numbers.
JAL says credit card numbers and passwords were not compromised, and assured that it currently has no evidence of customer information being misused.
The company said Amadeus has now implemented the necessary security measures and flight operations are unaffected.
Broader impact
Amadeus is an IT firm that provides solutions for travel agencies, airlines, airports, and hotels.
It is a major tech supplier to global aviation, used by over four hundred airlines, 210 airport operators, 34 cruise and ferry lines, and 2 million hotels.
Amadeus published a statement on its website on October 1, 2026, announcing it had discovered a vulnerability in its travel booking display environment that could expose travelers’ data.
At the time, the company said ransomware actors had not exploited the flaw and assured that no payment or other financial data had been exposed.
As JAL has confirmed now, the vulnerability appears to have been maliciously exploited.
It appears they were not the only victim of the campaign.
All Nippon Airways (ANA) has also announced a customer data breach earlier today tied to Amadeus, according to local media.
The airline has also suspended certain related services on its website and mobile app since October 21, although that action appears linked to the PHP2Shell threat rather than the Amadeus incident.
Other airlines that have confirmed impact from the Amadeus flaw are Asiana Airlines and Korean Air, both major South Korean carriers.
BleepingComputer has asked Amadeus for more information about the scope of the impact, specifically whether more airlines and other countries/markets were affected, but the company has not provided more information as of publication.

articles.title: Un rouleau laveur de 27 cm et une station d’entretien : l’Ecovacs Deebot T90S Pro Omni blanc est à 649 €
articles.text:
Le robot aspirateur laveur Ecovacs Deebot T90S Pro Omni blanc est à 649 € (-19 %)
Le robot laveur Ecovacs Deebot T90S Pro Omni blanc est proposé à 649 € chez Amazon, avec son rouleau rincé en continu et sa station d’entretien automatique.
Amazon affiche l’ensemble comprenant le robot et sa station à 150 € sous son prix conseillé de 799 €, soit environ 19 % de réduction. Le tarif est également inférieur de 50 € au plus bas prix des 30 derniers jours indiqué, de 699 €. Le produit est vendu et expédié par Amazon, avec la livraison gratuite.
Un rouleau rincé pendant le nettoyage
Le robot aspirateur laveur Ecovacs Deebot T90S Pro Omni utilise un rouleau OZMO Roller 3.0 de 27 cm. Celui-ci est rincé à l’eau propre pendant le lavage afin de limiter la redistribution des salissures. Le système TruEdge permet aussi de le déporter vers les bordures.
Ecovacs annonce une dépression maximale de 40 000 Pa et une brosse ZeroTangle 4.0 conçue pour limiter l’enroulement des cheveux. Sur les tapis, le rouleau peut se relever de 15 mm, avec un couvercle qui l’isole des fibres.
Une station pour automatiser l’entretien
La station OMNI prend en charge la collecte de la poussière, le lavage du rouleau et son séchage à l’air chaud. Le robot mesure 9,5 cm de haut et associe une navigation Mini-ToF à la détection d’obstacles AIVI 3D 4.0.
L’ensemble limite ainsi plusieurs manipulations quotidiennes, mais les réservoirs restent à remplir et à vider. Sur Amazon, le produit affiche une moyenne de 5/5 sur 14 évaluations, un volume encore limité.
