articles.title: Nvidia está financiando a sus proveedores para garantizar que podrá fabricar todos los chips de IA que quiere vender
articles.text:
Nvidia está viviendo un momento muy dulce. En apenas dos años ha multiplicado por más de tres sus ingresos y por cuatro su beneficio neto. Y lo ha logrado gracias a la enorme demanda de sus aceleradores que ha desencadenado la eclosión de la inteligencia artificial (IA). Sus cifras son espectaculares. Durante el ejercicio fiscal de 2024 sus beneficios crecieron un 581%. En 2025 se incrementaron un 145%. Y en el ejercicio fiscal de 2026, que concluyó el pasado 25 de enero (su calendario fiscal no coincide con el año natural), tuvo un beneficio neto de 120.067 millones de dólares.
Esta evolución pone encima de la mesa una realidad inapelable: el negocio de esta compañía se ha transformado. Su motor históricamente eran las GPU para videojuegos, pero ya no lo son en absoluto. Durante el segundo trimestre de su ejercicio fiscal 2027, que terminó el 26 de julio, el 92,5% de sus ingresos procedió de los centros de datos. No hace falta añadir nada más. Actualmente los aceleradores para IA y su ecosistema lo son todo para Nvidia. O casi todo.
En este escenario, Nvidia está haciendo lo que cualquier entidad con ánimo de lucro haría: asegurar en la medida de lo posible su mercado y dedicar una parte de sus recursos al sostenimiento de su crecimiento. La estrategia que han puesto a punto Jensen Huang y sus colaboradores tiene mucho sentido: están adelantando miles de millones de dólares a sus proveedores para que amplíen sus instalaciones y reserven capacidad de producción para sus aceleradores de IA.
Nvidia necesita reforzar su cadena de suministro
La demanda de chips para IA está creciendo más rápido que la capacidad de fabricación que son capaces de soportar las compañías involucradas en su producción, como TSMC, SK hynix, Samsung o Micron. Estas son las empresas más conocidas, pero Nvidia también necesita a otras corporaciones. De hecho, ha anunciado acuerdos con seis proveedores de componentes esenciales para sus aceleradores de IA. Estas empresas le proporcionan sustratos, capacidad de empaquetado avanzado, pruebas de semiconductores y motores ópticos.
Nvidia quiere incrementar la producción de sustratos 2,5 veces durante los próximos tres años
Los sustratos son unos componentes fundamentales para conectar los chips de un acelerador para IA a la placa de circuito impreso. Su fabricación es muy compleja, lo que ha provocado que su disponibilidad sea uno de los mayores obstáculos a los que se enfrentan los fabricantes de semiconductores para incrementar la producción de aceleradores de IA. Sea como sea, Nvidia tiene un plan: quiere incrementar la producción de sustratos 2,5 veces durante los próximos tres años. Y para lograrlo ha llegado a acuerdos con Ibiden, Samsung Electro-Mechanics y Unimicron, tres empresas esenciales en su cadena de suministro.
El empaquetado avanzado es otro de los recursos fundamentales para que la compañía liderada por Jensen Huang pueda sostener su negocio. La producción de un acelerador de IA no acaba cuando se fabrican sus chips. Las GPU modernas integran varios componentes, como las memorias HBM, que tienen que ser ensamblados utilizando técnicas de empaquetado muy sofisticadas. En este terreno Nvidia está respaldando a su principal proveedor de capacidad de empaquetado avanzado, Amkor, para incrementar su capacidad de fabricación de obleas de interposición en más de un 300% antes de que termine 2028. Ambición, desde luego, no le falta.

articles.title: « Pourri jusqu'à la moelle » : Apple et OpenAI s'apprêtent à s'affronter devant la justice
articles.text:
Le juge fédéral Edward Davila a arrêté le 28 octobre le calendrier du procès qui opposera Apple à OpenAI devant le tribunal de San José, en Californie. Les débats s’ouvriront le 19 juillet 2027 à 9 heures, un peu plus d’un an après la plainte déposée le 10 juillet dernier. Apple y accuse la société de Sam Altman, sa branche matérielle io Products et deux anciens ingénieurs maison d’avoir siphonné ses secrets de fabrication pour accélérer le premier appareil du champion de l’IA.
Lire aussi : OpenAI branche ChatGPT à iCloud, en plein procès contre Apple
Un calendrier serré jusqu’à l’été 2027
L’ordonnance déroule toute une série d’étapes : collecte des preuves factuelles bouclée en mars 2027, avocats des deux camps tenus de discuter d’un accord amiable avant le 1er juin, conférence préparatoire le 24 juin, puis ouverture du procès trois semaines plus tard. La plainte de 41 pages donne le ton depuis juillet : l’activité matérielle d’OpenAI y est décrite comme « pourrie jusqu’à la moelle ». En ligne de mire, deux transfuges : Tang Tan, 24 ans chez Apple à façonner l’iPod, l’iPhone et l’Apple Watch, dirige aujourd’hui le matériel d’OpenAI, et aurait encouragé des ingénieurs de son ancien employeur à se présenter en entretien avec de vraies pièces sous le bras. Chang Liu, ingénieur systèmes électriques pendant huit ans chez Apple, l’a suivi.
Le procès tombe l’année du premier appareil d’OpenAI
À l’audience du 14 octobre, le juge s’est déjà dit « très probablement » prêt à accorder l’injonction réclamée par Apple, tout en jugeant sa première mouture trop large. Sans attendre, OpenAI s’est engagée à ne pas exploiter les secrets allégués tant que l’affaire court, et à faire copier les appareils de quatorze salariés pour les experts.
La veille, le juge avait ouvert à Apple une collecte accélérée de preuves : dépositions des deux anciens ingénieurs et d’une troisième recrue, copies d’appareils, scripts des entretiens d’embauche. Les documents de recherche d’OpenAI sur les finitions métalliques, l’alimentation et les batteries restent, eux, dans le circuit ordinaire.
En parallèle, la demande de rejet pur et simple, plaidée le même jour, attend toujours sa décision. OpenAI, qui avait riposté dès l’été par un billet au titre sans détour, « Apple fait fausse route », y répète qu’aucun secret précis n’est nommé et renvoie la plainte à l’incapacité de la marque à retenir ses talents.
io Products, cofondée par Jony Ive, le designer historique d’Apple, a coûté 6,5 milliards de dollars à OpenAI en 2025 pour bâtir son premier appareil grand public. Devant le tribunal, l’entreprise a précisé qu’aucun produit ne sortirait avant fin février 2027. Le procès s’invitera donc en pleine année de lancement.

articles.title: Signs Your Business Has Outgrown the Person Who Is Good With Computers - Tech Guide
articles.text:
In the early stages of a business, it’s common for owners or employees who have a knack for technology to manage all IT-related tasks. This might include troubleshooting hardware issues, setting up software, managing networks, and maintaining cybersecurity.
Often, these individuals are the “go-to” person for anything computer-related, and their efforts keep the business running smoothly without the expense of dedicated IT staff. However, as businesses grow, these tech-savvy employees often find themselves overwhelmed by the increasing demands, leaving critical IT needs unmet. Recognizing when your business has outgrown relying on a person who is merely good with computers is critical to maintaining operational efficiency, security, and long-term success.
Many small businesses start with informal IT support, but the reality is that technology needs evolve rapidly. According to a report by CompTIA, 70% of small businesses experience significant IT challenges as they scale, underscoring the importance of professional IT management. This article explores the key signs that indicate it’s time to move beyond informal IT support and invest in professional services or dedicated IT staff.
Increased Complexity of IT Needs
One of the most obvious signs your business has surpassed the capabilities of an in-house tech enthusiast is the increasing complexity of your IT infrastructure. Initially, a simple network and basic software were sufficient. Now, with more employees, cloud services, and customer data, your IT environment demands specialized knowledge.
For example, integrating complex systems such as customer relationship management (CRM) tools, enterprise resource planning (ERP) solutions, or advanced cybersecurity measures requires expertise that goes beyond basic computer skills. If your current IT person struggles to implement or maintain these systems, it’s time to consider professional IT services.
As your business grows, you may find yourself needing to manage hybrid cloud environments, automate workflows, or ensure seamless integration between various software platforms. These tasks require advanced skills in network architecture, system administration, and cybersecurity. According to a recent survey, 61% of small to medium-sized businesses experience IT challenges that hinder their growth, emphasizing the need for dedicated IT resources.
Failing to address these complexities can lead to inefficient processes, data silos, and security vulnerabilities. This is why many expanding businesses transition from relying on a “computer-savvy” employee to engaging IT professionals who can design and manage scalable, robust systems.
Increasing Security Risks and Compliance Requirements
Cybersecurity threats are becoming more sophisticated, and businesses face increasing regulatory demands regarding data protection. A person who is good with computers may lack the specialized knowledge to implement advanced security protocols or maintain compliance with standards like GDPR or HIPAA.
For example, data breaches have increased by 17% over the past year, affecting companies of all sizes. Failing to adequately protect sensitive customer and company data can result in severe financial penalties and damaged reputation. If your IT support is unable to provide robust security measures or keep up with compliance requirements, it’s time to reassess your approach.
Resources such as CentraLink’s website offer insights into compliance and system requirements that can guide businesses in upgrading their IT practices.
Moreover, cybersecurity today requires continuous monitoring, threat detection, incident response, and employee training. These are complex tasks that go beyond fixing computer problems and require dedicated expertise.
Frequent Downtime and Delayed Problem Resolution
When your business depends on a single individual who is good with computers rather than a trained IT professional, downtime can become a major problem. Frequent system crashes, slow network speeds, or unresolved technical issues can significantly impact productivity and customer satisfaction.
If you notice recurring IT problems that take days to fix or disrupt daily operations, this is a major red flag. Downtime costs businesses an average of $5,600 per minute, underscoring the financial impact of inadequate IT support.
For example, if your sales team cannot access the CRM due to server issues or your employees experience frequent email outages, the resulting delays can lead to missed opportunities and frustrated customers. Moreover, the person handling these problems might be juggling multiple roles, limiting their ability to respond quickly and effectively.
At this stage, outsourcing IT support or partnering with a managed services provider can ensure rapid response and proactive maintenance, minimizing downtime and improving system reliability. These providers often offer 24/7 monitoring and help desk support, ensuring issues are addressed before they escalate.
Lack of Strategic IT Planning
A person who is simply good with computers may be excellent at fixing immediate problems but might lack the strategic vision required for IT planning aligned with business goals. As your company grows, your technology needs should evolve in tandem with your expansion plans.
For instance, planning for scalable cloud solutions, cybersecurity frameworks, and compliance with industry regulations requires expertise in IT strategy. Without this, your business risks falling behind competitors who leverage technology effectively.
Strategic IT planning involves assessing future technology needs, budgeting for IT investments, and aligning technology initiatives with business objectives. If your current IT support doesn’t contribute to long-term planning or innovation, it’s a sign to seek professional guidance.
Many businesses choose to work with Complete Technology Solutions to ensure their IT infrastructure supports their growth ambitions.
Proactive IT planning can lead to better resource allocation, improved security postures, and enhanced operational agility. Without it, companies often face reactive approaches to technology issues, which can hinder growth and increase costs.
Employee Frustration and Inefficiency
When IT issues are frequent and unresolved, employee frustration grows, leading to decreased productivity and morale. If your team spends significant time waiting for technical help or dealing with slow systems, it’s a clear indication that your current IT support setup is insufficient.
Studies show that employees lose an average of 22 minutes per day dealing with IT problems, which adds up to nearly two weeks of lost productivity annually. 
This lost time can translate into missed deadlines, lower quality of work, and higher turnover rates. Employees who feel supported by their IT infrastructure tend to be more engaged and focused on their core responsibilities.
Investing in professional IT services can streamline operations, improve employee satisfaction, and free up internal resources to focus on core business activities. This investment often pays for itself through increased efficiency and reduced downtime.
Preparing for Future Growth
Beyond addressing current issues, outgrowing the person who is good with computers means preparing your business for future technological advancements. Emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and automation offer significant opportunities but require specialized knowledge to implement effectively.
A professional IT team can help your business adopt these innovations strategically, ensuring you remain competitive in a rapidly evolving marketplace. Additionally, they can provide training and support to help your staff adapt to new systems and workflows.
Furthermore, as your business expands geographically or into new markets, your IT needs will become more complex, involving multi-site connectivity, remote access solutions, and compliance with diverse regulations. Having a dedicated IT strategy and support system is essential to navigate these challenges successfully.
Conclusion
Relying on a person who is merely good with computers is a common approach for startups and smaller businesses. However, as your company grows, this arrangement can hinder progress, expose you to security risks, and reduce overall efficiency. Signs such as increased IT complexity, frequent downtime, lack of strategic planning, rising security threats, and employee frustration indicate that it’s time to upgrade your IT support.
By recognizing these warning signs early, you can make informed decisions to partner with professional IT providers who offer scalable, secure, and strategic technology solutions tailored to your business goals. Whether it’s seeking advice from resources like or choosing to, taking proactive steps will help ensure your technology infrastructure supports your growth now and into the future.
Making this transition not only safeguards your business operations but also empowers your team to focus on innovation and growth, positioning your company for long-term success in an increasingly digital world.

articles.title: Tus mensajes de Discord pueden aparecer en Google: cómo evitar que cualquiera los encuentre
articles.text:
Discord comenzará a mostrar parte del contenido publicado en sus comunidades públicas en los buscadores de internet, incluido Google. El cambio permitirá que usuarios que no tienen una cuenta en la plataforma encuentren información compartida en determinados servidores, pero también abre un nuevo debate sobre la privacidad de las conversaciones digitales. Para evitar que los mensajes propios aparezcan en estos resultados, es necesario desactivar una opción desde los ajustes de la cuenta.
La medida afectará a los llamados Canales Descubribles, comunidades públicas con al menos 1.000 miembros que aparecen en el sistema de descubrimiento de Discord. Según el calendario anunciado por la compañía, las páginas públicas de estos espacios comenzarán a mostrarse en internet el 16 de noviembre de 2026, mientras que la indexación de los mensajes en los buscadores está prevista para mediados de diciembre.
Discord explicó en su blog que busca facilitar el acceso a las conversaciones que se producen en sus comunidades. La empresa pretende recuperar parte de la dinámica de los antiguos foros de internet, donde las personas podían encontrar respuestas y participar en debates sin necesidad de pertenecer a un grupo cerrado.
Sin embargo, para quienes utilizan la plataforma para conversar en comunidades públicas, el cambio implica que algunos mensajes podrán llegar a una audiencia más amplia de la prevista.
Cómo evitar que tus mensajes de Discord aparezcan en Google
Los usuarios que no quieran que sus mensajes de los canales descubribles se muestren en los buscadores pueden desactivar la función desde la configuración de privacidad de Discord. El procedimiento es el siguiente:
- Abre Discord e ingresa a los ajustes de tu cuenta.
- En el menú lateral, selecciona Datos y privacidad.
- Busca la opción “Mostrar el contenido de mis mensajes de los canales descubribles en la web”.
- Desactiva esa opción para impedir que tus mensajes de estos espacios se incorporen a la indexación web mediante esta función.
Con este ajuste, el usuario puede evitar que sus publicaciones en los canales descubribles se expongan a través del mecanismo anunciado por Discord. La configuración es especialmente relevante para quienes participan en comunidades públicas, pero prefieren que sus mensajes permanezcan dentro de la plataforma.
Conviene tener en cuenta que desactivar la opción no garantiza que desaparezca de Google cualquier contenido que ya se encuentre indexado o que haya sido copiado por terceros. Si un mensaje ya fue publicado en otro sitio o almacenado por un buscador, podría seguir siendo accesible hasta que se retire de la fuente correspondiente o se actualicen los resultados.
Qué mensajes de Discord podrán aparecer en internet
La nueva función no se aplicará a todas las conversaciones de Discord. El cambio está dirigido a los canales públicos que forman parte de los Canales Descubribles, es decir, comunidades que cumplen los requisitos establecidos por la plataforma para aparecer en su sistema de descubrimiento.
Discord pretende que estos espacios tengan páginas públicas accesibles desde un navegador. En ellas se mostrará información sobre cada comunidad y resúmenes automáticos de las conversaciones de sus canales públicos.
Posteriormente, la compañía prevé que determinados mensajes también puedan aparecer en los resultados de los buscadores. De esta manera, una persona que busque una respuesta en Google podría encontrar una conversación publicada en Discord sin tener que abrir la aplicación ni unirse al servidor.
La iniciativa busca aprovechar el contenido que se genera en las comunidades para responder preguntas y facilitar el descubrimiento de información. Al mismo tiempo, modifica la manera en que algunos usuarios pueden percibir la privacidad de sus publicaciones.
Qué información mostrará Discord en los buscadores
La compañía señaló que los mensajes indexados no incluirán el nombre de usuario ni la fotografía de perfil de quien los escribió. También indicó que la medida contempla los mensajes publicados a partir del 16 de noviembre de 2026, fecha prevista para el inicio de las páginas públicas.
No obstante, ocultar el nombre y la imagen de perfil no equivale a garantizar el anonimato. El contenido de un mensaje podría incluir datos personales o detalles que permitan reconocer a su autor por el contexto.
Por eso, es recomendable evitar compartir información sensible en comunidades públicas, independientemente de que sus mensajes aparezcan o no en Google.
Los administradores también podrán limitar la exposición
Los administradores de los servidores tendrán herramientas para decidir qué canales participan en la indexación o desactivar la exposición pública de su comunidad, según las opciones anunciadas por Discord.
Esto significa que la visibilidad de los mensajes dependerá tanto de las preferencias individuales de los usuarios como de la configuración de cada servidor.
La principal recomendación es revisar los ajustes de privacidad antes de que la función entre en vigor. De esta manera, quienes no quieran que sus mensajes de Discord aparezcan en los resultados de búsqueda podrán tomar medidas preventivas y controlar mejor la exposición de sus publicaciones.

articles.title: Advisory services reshape accounting education at Intuit - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Intuit rewires accounting education as AI pushes new hires toward client work
As AI automates routine finance work, the repetitive tasks that once defined entry-level accounting are disappearing, and advisory services are moving to the center of how firms create value. That shift leaves colleges racing to prepare graduates for a job that looks very different from the one in the textbooks.
Closing the gap between classroom and practice is now a priority for Intuit Inc. Accounting firms spend time retraining new hires, while fewer students are choosing the major out of fear that AI will take the jobs they expected to do, according to David Zasada (pictured), vice president of education and corporate engagement at Intuit.
“AI may be taking some of the tasks that are more repetitive and taking those over, but it’s opening up a whole other class of jobs with client advisory skills, and that’s growing,” Zasada said. “Those are better paying jobs than even the entry level.”
Zasada spoke with theCUBE Research’s Christophe Bertrand and co-host Alison Kosik at Intuit Connect, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed the role of AI in advisory services. (* Disclosure below.)
Teaching advisory services skills before graduation
Intuit’s response is the Accounting Futures program, a free curriculum developed with educators and practicing accountants. It pairs AI fluency modules with training in durable skills such as communication, problem-solving and judgment. Those skills matter more once new hires are sitting across from clients instead of behind a screen, Zasada explained.
“You actually have to start to develop a relationship with the client. You got to be able to communicate with them and you got to be able to help them analyze the information that they’re getting,” he said. “The durable skills are more important than they ever were before.”
Students practice that judgment on QuickBooks case studies drawn from real accounting firm scenarios, and then take on paid micro-internships that can run as short as 10 hours. Intuit also recently unveiled Intuit Industry Advisors as part of the program, tightening its ties to the profession. For firms, the payoff is graduates ready to take on advisory services from their first day, according to Zasada.
“They need to really hit the ground running and provide more value in client advisory services roles, and that is a segment of an accounting firm’s business that’s really on the rise,” he said. “It’s allowing them to have time to focus more on actually communicating and coaching their clients on how to be successful.”

articles.title: Sam Altman almost scrapped token pricing. Here’s why he backed off.
articles.text:
Sam Altman almost scrapped token pricing. Here’s why he backed off.
OpenAI considered dropping token-based pricing for its next model, letting developers submit a prompt and receive a price for the work, before negative customer feedback convinced the company to back away from the idea, CEO Sam Altman says.
The flat-fee pricing idea
Speaking Thursday with Stripe President John Collison on the Cheeky Pint podcast, Altman recalls that OpenAI “almost made a very — what would’ve been a bad call” to stop pricing its next model in tokens altogether, moving instead to an arrangement where a developer hands over a prompt and OpenAI hands back a price.
The billing would have worked “like AWS,” he explained, where you “just do something and we send you a bill” rather than metering the exchange token by token. Altman does not name the model in question or give a timeline for when the change was under consideration.
We’ve cued up the exchange in the video below:
Why customers pushed back
The idea ran into resistance when OpenAI tried to gauge how customers felt about receiving a price with no breakdown. “The customer response on that is so negative,” Altman recounts, with buyers telling the company, “’I need to know what I’m paying for somehow.’”
“’I need to know what I’m paying for somehow.’”
Developers already spend plenty of time tracking input and output tokens to keep costs down and estimate what they’ll spend as usage grows. Getting a price without knowing how it was calculated would only make that harder.
Paying more for clarity
What makes the admission worth a second look is that, according to Altman, the people he consulted would rather pay more to keep that visibility. He put the question to “a few people,” asking whether they would take a higher rate for the same output as long as it stayed priced in consistent tokens, and the answer, he said, was that they would “much rather you inflate the tokens and pay more,” because “I know there’s a real thing there.”
“much rather you inflate the tokens and pay more … I know there’s a real thing there.”
Developers resist a single opaque price, he reasons, because they suspect that over the long run they are “gonna get screwed somehow,” the same instinct that once had buyers paying for CPU hours instead of for a finished job.
The proposal could have had significant implications for developers building agents, whose multistep workflows already consume unpredictable amounts of compute and make spending difficult to forecast even under today’s token-based model. Altman does not explain how OpenAI would have set those per-job prices, or whether customers could have weighed one charge against another.
Tokens, a ‘fake unit’
The subject came up when Collison pressed Altman on whether tokens were the right way to measure AI usage. Altman acknowledged the limitations of token pricing but had no clear alternative to offer.
“Tokens are a kind of fake unit … they’re real in some sense, but they’re not a good unit.”
“Tokens are a kind of fake unit,” he said. “I mean, they’re real in some sense, but they’re not a good unit.” He balked at Collison’s half-serious pitch to coin an intelligence-equivalent token, comparing it to the way chipmakers still market nanometer figures that no longer correspond to any physical measurement on the chip.
Altman admits developers incur real overhead when choosing between a cheaper model and a more capable one, especially when they also have to guess how much reasoning a given task will demand. “That’s just cognitive overhead that I don’t think actually adds any value,” he said.
The exchange comes as OpenAI continues to rely on token pricing, even as Altman has argued that the cost of a given level of AI falls roughly tenfold a year. For now, token pricing remains in place, even as Altman acknowledges its shortcomings and OpenAI struggles to find a better alternative.

articles.title: Samsung Electronics Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
Samsung Electronics Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results
Samsung Electronics today reported financial results for the third quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026. The Company posted KRW 195.3 trillion in consolidated revenue, another all-time quarterly high, representing a quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) increase of 14%. Operating profit reached KRW 107.4 trillion, making Samsung Electronics the world's first tech company to exceed KRW 100 trillion in quarterly operating profit.
The Device Solutions (DS) Division posted a QoQ sales increase of 15%, with the Memory Business setting an all-time high for quarterly revenue and operating profit, as semiconductor demand is set to remain robust. The Device eXperience (DX) Division posted a QoQ revenue increase of 8% and recorded an operating loss of KRW 0.8 trillion.DS To Sustain Growth by Proactively Meeting Growing Demand for AI Applications
The DS Division posted KRW 147.1 trillion in consolidated revenue and KRW 106.5 trillion in operating profit for the third quarter.
The Memory Business achieved another record-breaking quarter by managing its product mix, with a focus on AI products, amid capacity constraints. Strong demand momentum for servers led to higher market prices across all applications.
Additionally, the Business experienced continued robust demand, driven by AI applications. It significantly scaled up sales of HBM4 on the back of industry-leading product competitiveness while proactively addressing growing demand for server SSDs.
In Q4 2026, the Memory Business expects industry-wide competition for AI leadership to drive continued AI infrastructure investment. Memory demand growth is projected to revolve around new CPU and GPU platform-related products, while surging QLC SSD demand will be linked to the expansion of personal AI agent services.
The Memory Business will also maintain a sales strategy focused on AI applications in order to solidify market leadership. Leveraging its industry-leading products and unmatched scale, the Business aims to achieve this by further increasing HBM, server DRAM, and SSD sales, while also increasing the supply of high-speed server DDR5 products and QLC SSDs.
In 2027, the Business expects AI infrastructure capital expenditure to reach a historic level as the AI ecosystem expands. Additionally, increasing AI-driven demand will far exceed the industry supply in comparison with 2026. The Business also aims to leverage its superior technology to bolster market leadership and optimize product mix in alignment with market trends and customer needs.
It plans to lead the high-end market and sharpen its AI-driven portfolio while building a stable sales base by securing multi-year contracts and ensuring timely readiness of new products tailored to the requirements of AI applications.
The System LSI Business achieved revenue growth in Q3 2026, driven by the mass production of systems-on-a-chip (SoCs) and image sensors for new models launched in H2. Additionally, the custom SoC business secured projects by establishing new customer partnerships.
In Q4 2026, the Business plans to maintain stable production and sales of flagship SoCs and 200MP image sensors.
In 2027, the System LSI Business aims to expand flagship SoC sales and strengthen partnerships with custom SoC customers. It also plans to accelerate sales of flagship high-resolution image sensors and diversify into non-mobile applications.
The Foundry Business experienced a notable revenue and earnings improvement on HBM base-die sales growth and expanded advanced-node sales, as well as continued order wins centered on 2 nm HPC customers, including major hyperscalers.
Looking ahead to Q4 2026, the Foundry Business plans to achieve double-digit revenue growth and continued earnings improvement on new mobile products, mass production ramp-up of 4 nm NPUs, and expanded memory product sales.
In 2027, the Business will aim for revenue growth led by 4 nm and 2 nm advanced nodes based on strong AI and HPC demand. It also expects to strengthen its global supply capabilities with the commencement of operations at its new fab in Taylor, Texas.
SDC To Build On Growth With Enhanced, Diversified Product Lineup
Samsung Display Corporation (SDC) posted KRW 8.0 trillion in consolidated revenue and KRW 1.1 trillion in operating profit for the third quarter.
For the small and medium display business, SDC reported improved earnings based on solid demand for high-end mobile products, while the large display business expanded sales volume and revenue on the growth of the gaming monitor market.
In Q4 2026, SDC expects a positive effect from year-end peak seasonal demand and new product launches, but it anticipates a limited improvement in earnings due to external factors.
During the quarter, the small and medium display business will pursue sales expansion by actively responding to customer demand, while the large display business will focus on improving profitability centered on gaming monitors.
In 2027, SDC expects continued market demand weakness amid ongoing uncertainty. For smartphones, the small and medium display business aims to increase the portion of premium products like foldables, and for IT, the business will pursue sales expansion through the ramp-up of the new 8.6G IT line and strengthening of the product lineup. The large display business aims to continue pursuing improved profitability centered on high value-added models.
MX To Maintain Mobile Leadership by Capitalizing on the High-Growth Premium Market
The MX and Networks Businesses posted a combined KRW 37.7 trillion in consolidated revenue and reported an operating loss of KRW 0.6 trillion for the third quarter. Revenue increased QoQ and year-on-year (YoY), mainly driven by new flagship launches including foldables. Earnings increased QoQ with an improved flagship sales mix, but declined YoY due to cost pressures.
In Q4 2026, the MX Business plans to drive year-end peak-season sales growth centered on flagships including the Galaxy S26 series, Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, and Z Fold8, as well as new ecosystem products. It will also seek to mitigate profitability risks through efficiency improvements across all business processes.
In 2027, the MX Business aims to maintain its mobile leadership by focusing on three strategic priorities. First, it will improve its product mix, centered on flagships with differentiated experiences by customer segment. Second, it will enhance the desirability and deliver tangible value of products through hardware and form-factor innovation. Third, it will minimize declines in profit with agile market responses and operational efficiency initiatives.
In Q3 2026, the Networks Business saw a decline in earnings QoQ and YoY due to lower North American and high-margin software sales. In Q4 2026, the Business aims to secure profitability through revenue growth in North America, Korea, and Japan. In 2027, the Business plans to drive profitable growth by securing new orders amid telco investment headwinds.
VD/DA Businesses and Harman To Extend AI-Based Product Innovation
The Visual Display (VD) and Digital Appliances (DA) Businesses posted a combined KRW 13.9 trillion in consolidated revenue and reported an operating loss of KRW 0.2 trillion for the third quarter.
The VD Business saw revenue decline due to the conclusion of major sporting events, while earnings decreased due to increased costs. In Q4 2026, the Business aims to capture peak season demand through strengthened channel partnerships and differentiated marketing, while expanding sales of premium products in order to offset the impact of rising costs. In 2027, while overall TV demand is expected to remain flat or decline slightly, the Business will focus on securing profitable growth engines by delivering differentiated TV experiences, as well as strengthening the service and platform businesses.
Meanwhile, the DA Business' earnings declined due to higher costs related to raw materials and logistics, despite stronger domestic marketing efforts and growth in the B2B and subscription businesses. In Q4 2026, the Business intends to improve profitability with a higher premium mix, and in 2027, it aims to secure profitability by expanding sales of innovative AI products and growing its high-margin B2B businesses.
Harman posted improved earnings on expanded audio and automotive sales, with a boost from non-recurring U.S. tariff refunds. Looking ahead, the Business will seek to maintain stable growth momentum by developing new automotive business and extending audio leadership through portfolio enhancements.
Shareholder Return: Q3 Dividend Details and Total Payout
The third-quarter cash dividend amounts to KRW 4,601 per common share and KRW 4,601 per preferred share, totaling KRW 30 trillion.
Of the estimated KRW 90~110 trillion in total shareholder returns for 2026, and with KRW 35 trillion already planned or completed, the company anticipates the remaining funds to be KRW 55~75 trillion.
The return of the remaining funds will include a substantial share repurchase and cancellation program, along with cash dividends.
The Company recognizes the growing market interest in the price gap between common and preferred shares, and is committed to actively considering and adjusting the proportion of preferred shares in our share repurchase and cancellation program based on market conditions.
The next shareholder return policy, along with the final amount of shareholder returns and the specific execution plans for the remaining funds for 2026, will be finalized at the Board meeting scheduled for late January 2027, with an announcement to follow.
Third Quarter 2026 Capital Expenditures
In the third quarter, Samsung Electronics' capital expenditure reached KRW 29 trillion, an increase of KRW 12.2 trillion quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) and KRW 19.8 trillion year-on-year (YoY). Capital expenditure consisted of KRW 27.2 trillion spent in the Device Solutions (DS) Division and KRW 1.1 trillion in Samsung Display Corporation (SDC). The cumulative total for the January-September period is KRW 56.9 trillion, up KRW 24.7 trillion YoY, with KRW 52.8 trillion allocated to the DS Division and KRW 2.4 trillion to SDC.
The full-year capital expenditure for 2026 is expected at approximately KRW 84.4 trillion, including KRW 76.8 trillion allocated to the DS Division and KRW 3.9 trillion to SDC.
For the DS Division, investments are planned for new fabs and other infrastructure to meet strong AI and HPC demand while ensuring readiness for the mid-to long term. For SDC, investments will focus on upgrades to existing production lines.
Source:
				Samsung Investor Relations

articles.text:
Linearbytes released Bug0 QA Agent, a source-available Playwright library for agentic browser regression testing. The AI agent associates the test instructions expressed in natural language to actions on the user interface, caches those when appropriate for faster CI replays, remapping them to test specifications when the user interface changes. Verification is based on consensus from up to three LLMs and evaluations from vision models.
At one end of the spectrum, legacy approaches to web application testing, while largely automated, do not incorporate AI as a key productivity factor. At the other extremity, innovative teams follow a fully agent-based automated approach to testing where the agent is front and center, handling every browser interaction dynamically.
The legacy approaches often falls prey to known pain points. Test suites commonly depend on implementation details (CSS classes, attributes, data-testid) that may change even when the specifications remain constant, causing unnecessary test rewriting and refactoring. Flaky tests result from the inherently inpredictible nature of the complex, asynchronous and distributed systems underlying web applications (race conditions, latency, dropped calls).
AI-first testing approaches on the other hand suffer from high latency that makes them impractical for large regression suites. LLMs can routinely add several seconds of latency per step, escalate API token costs, and introduce their own brand of flakyness due to the non-determinism of the actions performed. On the bright side, test generation resists well to changes in the implementation; image and video models may provide visual verification with some success.
Bug0 proposes an hybrid approach in which its autonomous agent decouples the initial visual exploration from routine regression execution. Developers write declarative test steps in plain English inside standard Playwright specs.
test("Shopping cart tests", async ({ page }) => {
  await runSteps({
    page,
    test,
    expect,
    userFlow: "Add product to cart",
    steps: [
      { description: "Navigate to https://demo.vercel.store" },
      { description: "Click Acme Circles T-Shirt" },
      { description: "Select color", data: { value: "White" } },
      { description: "Select size", data: { value: "M" } },
      { description: "Add to cart", waitUntil: "My Cart is visible" },
    ],
    assertions: [{ assertion: "Cart shows the Acme Circles T-Shirt" }],
  });
});
During an initial execution, the agent inspects the accessibility tree and screenshots to understand the user interface and perform the requested actions. Once a single-action step executes successfully, the framework compiles the interaction into concrete browser operations and caches them into an in-memory Redis store. On following runs, the suite replays the cached action directly through Playwright, eschewing the latency cost of a new LLM inference.
When implementation details of the user interface change (e.g., button coordinates updated, form hierarchies modified), the replayed Playwright action may as a result throw an execution failure. Rather than failing the entire test run, Bug0 QA Agent detects the break, invalidates the action cache, and re-invokes the multimodal agent loop. Important caveat: caching applies only to single-action steps; complex, multi-action directives re-execute through the agent on every run.
Unlike action steps, assertion verification is not cached. Assertions execute through vision models on every pass. Claude and Gemini independently evaluate every assertion, with a third model breaking ties. Video models allow catching transient UI defects (e.g., auto-dismissing toast alerts, flashing banner errors).
The framework embeds disposable email testing via mailsink and community-built adapters like Mailinator, allowing tests to extract one-time passwords (OTPs) and magic links via natural language prompts like {{email.otp:Extract the 6-digit code}}.
Chevrot et al. (Are Autonomous Web Agents Good Testers?) reports that their best-performing autonomous testing architecture (ATA) agreed with human professional testers for only about 60% of test runs, identifying assertion verifiability and grounding (identification of the relevant elements of the target application for the test action) as primary drivers of improvement to scale usage of autonomous testing agents. The paper was published in April 2025 and used GPT-4o, Sonnet, and Gemini. As language models and harnesses regularly improve, so do the efforts to use AI to improve the productivy of testing in all its aspects (generation, self-healing, execution, triage, analytics).
Bug0 QA Agent is released under the Functional Source License, Version 1.1, ALv2 Future License. The Functional Source License is a source-available license (i.e., not open-source), that imposes non-compete restrictions during the first two years of usage. The license came of existence to, in the words of Sentry, its first proponent, “grant freedom without harmful free-riding.”

articles.title: No Name Mobile flash sale: get $29/50GB, $34/70GB until Nov. 4
articles.text:
No Name Mobile is running a flash sale on some wireless plans, offering additional data for a limited time.
Until Nov. 4, customers can get an extra 10GB of data on No Name’s $29/mo and $34/mo plans.
The $29/mo plan typically includes 40GB of data, but during the promotion, customers get 50GB instead. However, the catch is that the extra data is only available if you sign up for automatic payments.
Similarly, the $34/mo plan comes with 70GB instead of 60GB until Nov. 4, as long as you use auto-pay.
Both plans include 4G data, unlimited calling Canada-wide and to the U.S., Canada and international texting, and other standard features like call display, voicemail, call forwarding, and suspicious call detection.
At this price point, No Name’s plans look pretty good. Telus-owned Public Mobile’s $30/35GB 4G plan isn’t as good, and the $35/50GB plan has less data than No Name’s $34 plan but does include 5G — a decent trade-off for those who value speed over data. Similarly, Freedom’s $35/35GB plan offers 5G and other features like Canada/U.S./Mexico roaming — more features and less data for a similar price.
No Name’s plans also offer quite a bit more data than comparably priced plans from the likes of Chatr and Lucky Mobile.
You can check out the plans on No Name’s website.

articles.title: Google fatura menos com Modo IA do que com a busca tradicional • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Google fatura menos com Modo IA do que com a busca tradicional
Buscas com IA ajudam a aumentar o número de consultas, mas ainda geram menos receita.
O Modo IA está fazendo as pessoas pesquisarem mais no Google, mas ainda gera menos receita por consulta do que a busca tradicional. A Alphabet reconheceu que as consultas feitas na ferramenta baseada em inteligência artificial têm uma taxa de monetização inferior à das pesquisas convencionais.
A revelação veio durante a apresentação dos resultados do terceiro trimestre. A receita de busca e outros anúncios avançou 12% na comparação anual, para US$ 63,3 bilhões (cerca de R$ 338,7 bilhões em conversão direta), mas o ritmo de crescimento desacelerou em relação aos 17% registrados no segundo trimestre.
O diretor de negócios Philipp Schindler explicou que parte da diferença está no próprio formato das pesquisas. Muitas das consultas ocorrem em etapas iniciais da decisão de compra, o que significa que nem todas têm uma finalidade comercial.
De acordo com o Google, uma consulta no Modo IA tem, em média, três vezes mais palavras que uma busca tradicional. O recurso aceita perguntas complexas e permite continuar a conversa com novas solicitações.
O Modo IA está disponível em português e oferece uma experiência mais próxima de chatbots como Gemini e ChatGPT. Em vez de simplesmente apresentar uma lista de links, a ferramenta divide perguntas em várias pesquisas e monta uma resposta com informações encontradas na web.
A estratégia passa por colocar mais anúncios na ferramenta. O Google testa publicidade no Modo IA desde maio de 2025, com links patrocinados que podem aparecer dentro ou abaixo das respostas geradas pela inteligência artificial.
Nesta semana, a companhia anunciou que vai ampliar os anúncios do Modo IA para Austrália, Canadá, Índia e outros sete mercados. Brasil, México e Reino Unido devem entrar na expansão ainda no quarto trimestre de 2026. Nos Estados Unidos, o Google também começou a testar anúncios exibidos durante perguntas na mesma conversa.
A busca continua sendo uma das maiores máquinas de dinheiro da Alphabet. A receita do segmento avançou no trimestre, mas o crescimento de 12% ficou abaixo segundo (17%) e do primeiro (19%) trimestres. A monetização menor do Modo IA chama ainda mais atenção, porque o Google está gastando mais para sustentar sua estratégia de inteligência artificial.
Os investimentos da Alphabet em infraestrutura chegaram a US$ 51,4 bilhões no trimestre, mais de R$ 275 bilhões em conversão direta. Isso aumenta a pressão para que os novos produtos de IA também colaborem para sustentar o negócio publicitário da companhia.
Ao mesmo tempo, o Google não pretende desacelerar. A companhia afirma que as ferramentas de IA já estão aumentando o número de pesquisas e pretende investir ainda mais na tecnologia em 2027. O desafio agora é fazer com que essas novas buscas sejam tão rentáveis quanto as antigas.

articles.title: Tech whiz's internet-accessible Synology NAS gets bit by ransomware attack from 18-month-old remote code execution flaw — security updates neglected in a series of catastrophic errors
articles.text:
Tech whiz's internet-accessible Synology NAS gets bit by ransomware attack from 18-month-old remote code execution flaw — security updates neglected in a series of catastrophic errors
In their defense, Synology's misleading update policies didn't help.
Systems administrators are among the first to point out lax security policies in other companies' or people's setups. Sometimes, they are the ones who get bitten by not taking the same advice they will so readily dispense. Such is the tale of Reddit user NakamuraHwang, who had files on their Synology DS918+ NAS encrypted by a ransomware attack after making a series of unforced errors.
Hwang appears to be quite technically proficient and provided a detailed write-up of the situation. The key points, however, are that the unit in question (a) had its web interface exposed to the internet and (b) was roughly 18 months out-of-date with security patches. Just like the recent PHP snafu has adeptly shown, complacency is a far worse enemy than an army of AI bots.
The tech has a 3-2-1 backup setup, so they seemingly didn't lose any data. They attached the disks to a Proxmox machine for further inspection — Synology's DSM operating system uses mdraid underneath, so you can take the disks to another box and mount them there. Investigation of logs and the operating system files revealed that the attack was likely performed by abusing the CVE-2024-10441 remote code execution vulnerability, revealed a year and a half ago.
As most any other sysadmin will tell you, it's never advisable to expose devices directly to the internet without some layer of protection in between, chiefly but not only a VPN or an SSH tunnel. Tailscale, for instance, makes having a VPN fairly painless these days, and its free plan covers most home installations.
Synology had published its own advisory regarding the exploit, but that's where the NAS' behavior regarding updates complicates matters. According to multiple comments on the thread and in other forums, the UI will happily tell you that your device is up to date, all while there are critical security updates that need to be manually installed. The manual for DSM indicates that units from 2025 onwards have automatic updates, apparently implying that those of previous makes need to be configured so.
Furthermore, Synology apparently doesn't have a direct channel to warn its customers of critical security vulnerabilities —a simple e-mail notification would suffice. Although the firm is seemingly shifting away from consumer gear, it still sells small units that regular users might buy, and it's not reasonable to expect them to even be aware of security bulletins. Plus, package updates like the patch for the PHP2Shell vulnerability have to be installed separately, too.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

Who wouldn't feel unsafe after months, let alone years without security updates?
One of my old cellphones hasn't had an update in years and I'm fully aware that it's an unsafe device (so I treat it as such), even though the manufacturer says that "it is up to date".
If automatic updates aren't working on your device, check manually (and there were plenty of updates), else search for alternatives because your device is not safe. Reply

That admin interface being an application web page makes it a ludicrously irresponsible bad idea.What exactly do you mean by admin interface on an application web page? I have access to google admin console at work through a google webpage. Does that count in your book as something 'ludicrously irresponsible'? Reply
- ejolson The NAS here felt unsafe from the day it was installed. Internally everything runs as root and there is no way to install a standard Linux distribution.Reply
- BoxmenSEO Worth checking UPnP on the router too. Synology can open ports on its own through it, so some people end up with the admin page exposed without ever forwarding anything themselves. If you need remote access, a VPN like Tailscale or WireGuard is the easy way around it.Reply

- skiwi44 Important to note that the Synology 918+ is a 2017/18 box and as such it will not automatically update to the latest version of DSM. It issued with DSM 6, and will happily stay on DSM 6 until you manually ask it to upgrade to DSM 7. The reason for this is that DSM 7 deprecated a number of DSM 6 software apps.
Once upgraded to DSM 7, it will continue to update with the latest patches (including the PHP ones).
Secondly, you can setup DSM to automatically update or to manually update. It will nag you to do so, but you must initiate the process yourself. Reply

Appliances are notorious for running very old versions of common software / libraries that are uneconomical to update. This can be made safe through internal safeguards but not internet facing. Reply

But I think the idea was in a scenario where say someone gained access to your nas you could regain control and have had a role effectively set up that there was a time frame where even an admin couldn’t delete your snapshots. Seems like that would have been useful in this case.Reply

articles.title: Turning a solar power system into its own backup
articles.text:
Rather than directly converting photons into electricity, concentrated solar energy uses mirrors to turn sunlight into heat, which can then be used to drive traditional generating turbines. Up to about a decade ago, there was a case to be made that concentrated solar energy had a bright future, as improvements in heat storage had turned it into a way to generate power around the clock.
It wasn’t to be. While concentrated solar costs fell enough to compete with nuclear power, the price of photovoltaics plunged, making solar panels the cheapest source of power in most locations. Currently, if you have a good site to generate solar power, then the economics of PV panels are hard to beat.
That has left us needing to build a mixture of other facilities—typically batteries and natural gas facilities—to handle overnight needs or weather-driven shortfalls. But a small company is promising that it can help avoid the need to build a separate facility. Its version of concentrated solar is designed so that a fossil-fueled backup system shares most of the generating hardware with the solar side.
Back to the future?
Concentrated solar, also called solar thermal, is pretty simple in principle. Most of the site is covered with heliostats, devices that incorporate mirrors and a motorized tracking system that can keep their focus on a single point as the Sun moves across the sky. The point of focus is in a tower, where sunlight heats a working fluid. The hot fluid can then be used to power a traditional steam turbine, or its heat can be stored and used to generate power overnight.
There are many potential variations, however: different working fluids and methods of heat storage, trough-shaped mirrors that eliminate the need for a tower, and so on. All of those variants are meant to reduce some of the issues inherent to solar thermal: lots of moving parts, potentially corrosive fluids, and so on. Those issues and the lack of standardization have helped ensure that the costs of these plants haven’t come close to keeping pace with photovoltaics.

articles.title: The GTX 750 Ti is back with 8GB of memory, and it can still barely run Cyberpunk
articles.text:
Going overkill: The GTX 750 Ti was a go-to upgrade for budget PCs back in 2014, largely because it could fit into an old office tower without requiring extra power cables. It came with just 2GB of memory, though – a limitation that many games released in recent years can easily run into. Now, a version with four times as much memory is available on Amazon. According to reports, it can even run Cyberpunk 2077 at around 30 fps.
UK YouTuber RandomGaminginHD picked one up from the little-known brand Xynsviu for around £160. That's more than the $149 Nvidia originally charged for the card. In the US, the same model was listed on the brand's eBay storefront for $189.
He paired it with a Core i5-12400F and 32GB of DDR5 memory for testing. In Cyberpunk 2077, the card averaged 32 fps at 1080p using the lowest preset and FSR 2.1 in Performance mode. Battlefield 6 ran at 35 fps on its lowest settings with the render scale set to 50%. Those averages hide some ugly problems, though, including textures that never loaded and objects that popped into view late..
ARC Raiders looked respectable on paper at 48 fps, but performance occasionally plunged to just 9 fps. Lighter games fared much better. Counter-Strike 2 ran at 102 fps on medium settings, while Fortnite managed 75 fps in Performance mode.
The extra memory does pay off in Red Dead Redemption 2. Ultra textures are available directly in the settings menu, without the configuration-file tweak required by the 2GB version. Even so, the game reached just 37 fps with the resolution scale reduced to 50%. Across the entire test suite, RandomGaminginHD found that the card performs much like the original 2GB model.
That's hardly surprising, given that the underlying GPU hasn't changed. GPU-Z identifies a full GM107 die with all 640 CUDA cores, unlike the 8GB "Ti" model that surfaced a few months ago but actually used a standard GTX 750 GPU. Xynsviu also clocks its eight 1GB GDDR5 memory chips at 1,253 MHz, below the stock 1,350 MHz. That reduces memory bandwidth from 86.4 GB/s to 80.2 GB/s, matching the regular GTX 750's figure.
Gaming might not have been the main goal, anyway. Xynsviu's lineup consists mostly of older Nvidia and AMD GPUs repurposed for multi-monitor use, ranging from the GT 730 to the RX 580. This model features four HDMI outputs on a dual-fan, low-profile board and, like the original GTX 750 Ti, draws all its power through the PCIe slot.
Whatever its intended use, the card relies on a Maxwell GPU that Nvidia no longer optimizes drivers for. Game Ready support ended with the 580 driver branch, meaning new game releases won't receive day-one fixes. The card will continue to receive quarterly security updates through October 2028, however.
New, affordable graphics cards are also becoming harder to find this year. Zotac and Inno3D owner PC Partner warned in its half-year results that entry-level GPU shortages would worsen through the rest of 2026 as memory costs rise. Cards such as the RTX 5050 are already selling above their suggested retail prices in some markets.

articles.title: Elon Musk is 'truly a genius,' says Vladimir Putin | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Russian president Vladimir Putin said that he and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk are in “close contact” about Rassvet, Russia’s answer to Starlink, Musk’s internet satellite service.
“Elon Musk is a genius, truly a genius,” Putin said at the Russia-Africa Summit on Wednesday. “He has already had more than 5,000 such satellites in orbit, while we are only taking the first steps.”
A potential relationship between Putin and Musk could have serious implications. Musk has recently voiced frustration with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy, whose country has been fighting a Russian invasion since 2022. After the U.S. eased sanctions on Russia earlier this month, Ukrainian officials became concerned that Ukraine could lose access to Starshield, the military version of Musk’s Starlink network, which Ukrainian forces rely on.
There was some merit to these concerns. For about 10 days earlier this month, Ukrainian drones experienced frequent losses of connectivity. According to the Wall Street Journal, Musk ordered SpaceX to limit Ukraine’s Starlink access, though other reports say the order came from the White House. Musk claimed in a post on X that Ukraine violated Starlink terms of service by using the technology for “offensive drone strikes to kill people.”
Starlink service in Ukraine appears to have since resumed normal operations.
“Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately,” Musk also wrote on X. “This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact.”

articles.title: US workers are less engaged at their jobs than ever — and many are blaming AI, particularly remote and hybrid workers
articles.text:
US workers are less engaged at their jobs than ever — and many are blaming AI, particularly remote and hybrid workers
Gallup report finds hybrid and remote workers are more affected
- Gallup report finds US workers are feeling less engaged at work than ever
- Remote and hybrid workers are feeling particularly unenthused
- Lack of clarity on AI is also affecting worker happiness
With wide-ranging layoffs, the risk of AI replacement and cost of living increases, it might be no wonder that many employees are feeling less engaged with their jobs, but new research has shown just how much the dissatisfaction has become.
Gallup’s latest quarterly engagement poll for US workers found job engagement fell to its lowest level since 2011 in the third quarter of 2026.
The measure, which tracks workers’ focus, motivation and enthusiasm for their jobs, found engagement fell to 29% in Q3 2026, with remote and hybrid workers particularly disaffected with the state of things.
Lack of engagement
Although the figure sounds dramatically low, it should be pointed out that the engagement figure is never particularly high in Gallup's report - having peaked at 36% in 2020, the figure then fell to 31% by 2024, before its recent drop.
The company noted that the decline was particularly noticeable among remote and hybrid employees, especially those working in organizations which have adopted AI tools.
Gallup noted engagement fell five points among fully remote employees and two points among hybrid employees, compared with approximately one point among on-site employees and those with jobs that cannot be performed remotely.
This was not the first time such trends had been spotted, as Gallup pointed to its earlier research which found hybrid and fully remote employees have experienced larger declines in clarity of expectations than on-site employees in remote-capable jobs.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
"These findings raise the possibility that physical distance can contribute to psychological distance between employees and their organizations, particularly as companies navigate the use of AI at work," it said.
Turning to AI, Gallup noted that although research earlier in 2026 had indicated a potential thawing in engagement with employees and AI, this had now declined.
It found workers in "AI-integrated organizations" were now reporting similar levels of engagement than those who weren't - with hybrid and remote workers again saying they were less happy and engaged.
"U.S. employee engagement has fallen to its lowest level in 15 years, with particularly large declines among hybrid and remote employees in organizations that have adopted AI," the report concludes.
"At the same time, fewer employees report clear expectations or feel that someone at work cares about them. The pattern suggests that AI adoption may be outpacing the communication and managerial support needed to make it effective."
