Despite the digital transformation of workplaces, office printers remain a necessary and often troublesome piece of equipment. They generate a significant portion of IT support calls primarily due to mechanical issues, connectivity problems, outdated drivers, and user errors. By understanding these challenges and implementing a combination of preventative maintenance, employee education, and expert support services such as and, businesses can reduce printer-related disruptions.
Reducing printer support calls not only improves productivity but also lowers operational costs and enhances employee satisfaction. With the right strategies and partnerships, companies can finally tame the office printer and transform it from a persistent headache into a dependable workhorse-one that supports rather than hinders daily business operations.

articles.title: IG Defence, Oman’s MSA Global explore production of drone systems
articles.text:
IG Defence, Oman’s MSA Global explore production of drone systems
India’s IG Defence and Oman’s MSA Global have signed an exploratory MoU to explore co-development and local manufacture of drone and counter-drone systems for Oman and the wider Gulf.
India’s IG Defence and Oman-based MSA Global have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to explore the co-development and local manufacture of drone and counter-drone systems for Oman and the wider Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC).
The agreement links India’s defence-export ambitions with Gulf security concerns, but remains exploratory and does not confirm an order, factory or deployment.
Reuters reported in October that Iran and allied groups had carried out at least 135 drone and missile attacks against 84 infrastructure sites across Gulf Arab states since the United States and Israel began bombing Iran in February.
“The evolving security environment in the Gulf reinforces the importance of strengthening indigenous defence capabilities and developing resilient regional manufacturing ecosystems,” MSA Global chairman Col M. S. Atwal (Retd.) said.
The MoU was exchanged during the India-Oman Defence Industry Cooperation Seminar in Muscat in October. India and Oman already have established defence ties, including joint exercises involving all three branches of India’s armed forces.
IG Defence, formerly known as IG Drones, said discussions will cover three systems. KAL is described by the company as a one-way attack unmanned aerial system with a stated range of up to 1,000 kilometres. BAJ is an unmanned aerial interceptor intended for counter-unmanned aircraft system (C-UAS) use, while JWALA is a micro-missile system under development for counter-drone applications.
“Our partnership with MSA Global reflects our vision of taking India's indigenous defence technologies to global markets through strategic industrial collaboration,” IG Defence Chief Executive Officer Bodhisattwa Sanghapriya said.
The agreement comes as India’s defence exports reached Rs 23,622 crore in the 2024-25 financial year, up 12.04% from the previous year. On October 26, India also approved in principle Rs 2,12,000 crore in military acquisitions, including counter-drone systems and long-range attack drones.
Other companies are responding to similar demand. In May, France’s CS Group won a NATO contract to supply two counter-drone systems for its Brussels headquarters. In August, US firm Powerus announced a separate contract for counter-drone technology to protect Middle Eastern energy infrastructure.

articles.title: La Dynamic Island de l'iPhone arrive sur le MacBook Pro : voici tout ce qu'elle peut faire
articles.text:
Ce 28 octobre, Apple a annoncé son premier MacBook Pro tactile. Mais la nouveauté de cet ordinateur ne réside pas uniquement dans le fait qu’on peut le contrôler au doigt. C’est aussi l’arrivée de la Dynamic Island des iPhone sur cet ordinateur portable. Une fonction qui vient avec un changement de design : finie l’encoche pour la webcam, elle est directement dans un poinçon, comme sur les iPhone. Attention, contrairement à l’iPhone, la Dynamic Island de ce MacBook n’arrive pas avec Face ID, il faut toujours utiliser Touch ID.
À quoi sert la Dynamic Island sur un MacBook Pro ?
Dans son communiqué de presse, Apple explique que la Dynamic Island « devient le nouvel espace de Spotlight, des Activités en direct et de Siri AI ». Lorsqu’on déclenche Spotlight pour rechercher quelque chose, c’est via cette fenêtre qui s’ouvre au niveau de l’encoche. Même chose lorsqu’on souhaite avoir des informations en direct ou qu’on utilise Siri AI, l’assistant intelligent présent sur ce MacBook Pro. En bref, Apple a cherché à unifier l’expérience de la Dynamic Island entre les iPhone et ce MacBook Pro, la présentant comme « un moyen rapide et intuitif de consulter les informations importantes et d’y réagir. »
C’est aussi via cette fonction qu’on peut prendre un appel téléphonique, contrôler la musique, ou encore accepter une demande AirDrop. Certaines notifications et fenêtres, qui étaient auparavant en haut à droite de l’écran, sont déplacées en haut et au milieu, de sorte à ce qu’on les voit mieux. Comme ce MacBook Pro est tactile, on peut interagir avec cette Dynamic Island au doigt.
Une fonction encore limitée sur MacBook
À noter que Spotlight est intégré dans la Dynamic Island uniquement si Siri AI est disponible et activée. Problème : Siri AI est disponible en français en version bêta uniquement, dans macOS 27.2, la dernière itération du système d’exploitation des Mac arrivée il y a quelques jours. La version finalisée de l’assistant n’est pour le moment pas disponible en version finalisée et on ignore quand est-ce qu’elle le sera.
Autre souci par rapport à la Dynamic Island des iPhone : pour le moment, on ne peut pas faire grand-chose avec, si ce n’est appliquer les usages développés par Apple. Et c’est normal, puisque sur les iPhone, ce sont les développeurs d’applications qui se sont emparés de cette fonction et qui l’ont enrichie avec des Activités en direct. Espérons que les développeurs d’applications Mac prendront aussi le pli ici et rendront la Dynamic Island de ce MacBook Pro plus utile.

articles.title: SK Hynix esgota estoques e prevê escassez de memória até 2030 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
SK Hynix esgota estoques e prevê escassez de memória até 2030
Falta de componentes pressiona os preços de eletrônicos de consumo.
Resumo
- A SK Hynix tem toda a sua produção de memórias DRAM e HBM prevista para os próximos três anos já comprometida.
- A oferta de memórias deve continuar abaixo da demanda até 2030, impulsionada principalmente pelos investimentos em infraestrutura de inteligência artificial.
- A escassez de componentes deve continuar elevando os preços de eletrônicos de consumo, afetando produtos como computadores, smartphones e TVs.
A SK Hynix anunciou que praticamente toda a sua produção de memórias DRAM e HBM prevista para os próximos três anos está comprometida. A fabricante também prevê que a oferta continue abaixo da demanda até 2030, impulsionada principalmente pelos investimentos em infraestrutura de inteligência artificial.
As projeções foram apresentadas nesta quarta-feira (28/10), durante a divulgação dos resultados financeiros do terceiro trimestre, e sugam a pouca esperança aberta pela concorrente Micron, em janeiro, de que os preços dos componentes pudessem se estabilizar até 2028.
Segundo a companhia, contratos de longo prazo já assinados e encomendas em negociação deixam pouco espaço disponível para atender a novos pedidos nos próximos anos.
Além da sul-coreana, Samsung, que adiantou o possível aumento de demanda no começo do ano, e Micron já tinham vendido a quantidade total de chips de memória projetada para o ano que vem. As três concentram grande parte da produção global desses componentes.
Contratos já cobrem maior parte da produção
Em comunicado, a SK Hynix alega que fechou acordou de fornecimento de longo prazo com 14 grandes clientes, incluindo algumas das principais provedoras globais de computação em nuvem. Os contratos já garantidos correspondem a mais de 50% da capacidade total de produção prevista para 2027 e 2028.
A situação fica ainda mais apertada quando entram na conta pedidos que ainda estão em negociação. Segundo a empresa, a soma dos contratos assinados com demandas baseadas em planos concretos de compra faz com que os volumes de DRAM e HBM estejam “efetivamente esgotados” até 2029.
A fabricante também já concluiu as negociações de volume e preços de HBM para 2027 e espera crescimento tanto nas vendas quanto na rentabilidade do segmento. Após o crescimento do setor, a empresa conseguiu superar a Samsung pela primeira vez em valor de mercado, em junho, e bateu recorde na estreia na bolsa estadunidense.
Memória para IA encarece produtos eletrônicos
A principal pressão vem da expensão de datacenters e servidores dedicados à IA. A memória HBM é usada em aceleradores para permitir a transferência de grandes volumes de dados em alta velocidade. Segundo a SK Hynix, os pedidos feitos por clientes para esse tipo de componente já chegam a mais que o dobro da oferta disponível.
A companhia está aumentando os investimentos na ampliação da capacidade de fabricação com novas instalação. No entanto, seguindo o padrão da indústria, a empresa afirma que leva anos até que a operação de uma nova fábrica se inicie, e a demanda deve continuar acima da oferta até 2030.
Até lá, o consumidor final de produtos eletrônicos deve continuar sentindo o peso desse foco em IA no bolso. Memórias DRAM e NAND, também fabricadas pelas três, são usadas em computadores, smartphones, TVs, eletrodomésticos “inteligentes” e até carros com sistemas digitais mais avançados.
No mercado de smartphones, por exemplo, vimos recentemente aumentos em linhas da Samsung e Apple, que pode subir ainda mais no ano que vem. As companhias já vêm se preparando desde o ano passado e não há uma previsão certa de que os preços voltem ao patamar dos anos anteriores, segundo a Lenovo.

articles.title: Google admits AI search makes less money, but it's fixing that with more ads
articles.text:
Google parent Alphabet reported its Q3 financial results on Wednesday afternoon, showing a healthy rise in revenue for the months of July to September. But the company’s stock price has taken a beating, marking one of the largest post-earnings drops in its history. It comes down to several troubling aspects of the new report, including an admission by the company that AI search isn’t earning as much as organic search, and despite that, Google expects to spend even more on AI next year.
The company took in almost $128 billion in Q3 2026, earning more than $26 billion in net income. These may sound like good numbers, but financial markets are not impressed. While revenue is up 25 percent versus last year, net income is almost $9 billion lower. As of this story’s publication, the stock price is down almost 12 percent, and it was down about 13 percent earlier in the day.
While revenue was up 25 percent year over year, analysts expected more. Google reported earnings per share of $2.12, but the consensus projection ahead of Wednesday was $3.02. Google’s Cloud products actually beat expectations, crossing $30 billion in revenue. That’s about a billion more than analyst guesses.
Google is still making a huge amount of money, but there are several troubling trends emerging. The last few years at the company have been all about AI, with generative technology appearing in products from Gmail to Android. Most notably, Google is shifting to an AI search platform powered by Gemini models.
During the earnings call, Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler discussed the company’s search volume. This is one of the key metrics by which Google tracks its own performance. In the last quarter, Google saw search grow by 12 percent versus last year. Good for the company, right? Except that’s a much slower rate than previous quarters. Growth in Q2 was 17 percent, and Q1 saw 19 percent growth over 2025. Search revenue was also flat in Q3.
So that’s the first problem, likely driven by more consumers using AI chatbots to find answers. The other issue is that Google’s take on AI search isn’t pulling in revenue like standard web search yet. According to Schindler, each AI Mode query earns less revenue compared to a similar web search—there are fewer ads, and they cost less to run.

articles.title: Serval raises $150M at $3B valuation to bring its automation agents beyond IT - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Serval raises $150M at $3B valuation to bring its automation agents beyond IT
Enterprise service management startup Serval Inc. announced today it has raised $150 million in new funding at a $3 billion valuation to bring its automation agents to more departments beyond information technology.
Serval offers a service management platform where staff describe a workflow in plain language and artificial intelligence agents write the automation, then use it to resolve employee requests as they arrive. Older IT service management products, according to the company, mostly just track tickets. Founded in 2024, Serval started out on the IT help desk, and customers have since pulled the software into human resources, finance and legal work.
A good part of the new money will go to Catalyst, which Serval launched in August. The agent scans support tickets for repetitive tasks and drafts automations that an administrator reviews before anything goes live. Alex McLeod, Serval’s co-founder and chief technology officer, said the point is to give employees outside engineering “a powerful code generation tool” they can use to automate their least fulfilling work.
The round also funds ProServal, a new professional services unit. Over the next 12 months the unit plans to hire more than 100 automation engineers to work on site at large customers, where they will map how work moves between teams and build automations in days. About half will be recent graduates put through a four-week training program.
The hiring is aimed at people who have “grown up building with AI,” according to Jake Stauch, Serval’s co-founder and chief executive. “Nobody has 10 years of experience doing this, because two years ago the tools didn’t exist,” he said.
Headcount at Serval is 10 times what it was a year ago, and the company plans to hire more than 500 additional staff, the ProServal engineers among them, as it opens offices in New York, London and Austin to go with its San Francisco headquarters.
Two Fortune 20 companies have signed on in the last few months to deploy automations across their organizations, joining a customer list that also includes Fox Corp., WPP plc and Live Nation Entertainment Inc. Serval did not disclose its annual recurring revenue. By the company’s account the figure has doubled every quarter since December, and most customers are up and running inside 30 days.
Serval considers ServiceNow Inc. its main competitor. Some large customers are ripping out the incumbent platform altogether, the company claimed, and one automaker completed the switch in 45 days. That migration covered IT service management and the configuration management database along with asset tracking for hardware and software.
Sequoia Capital Operations led the Series C round, Serval’s third in just over a year. Serval’s $75 million Series B round in December, also led by Sequoia, valued the company at $1 billion. Conviction Capital and Headline Management Co. are new investors this time, and Redpoint Ventures LP, General Catalyst Group Management, First Round Capital LP, Evantic Capital and Elad Gil all came back.
Anas Biad, a partner at Sequoia, said Serval is “winning over major enterprises” and has become the system of record for some of them.
Including the $47 million Series A round that Redpoint led in October 2025, investors have now put $277 million into Serval.

articles.title: 'Karateka' (★★★★☆), la épica historia de Sandra Sánchez es el drama deportivo del año
articles.text:
Por fin se estrena en cines Karateka, la película española que busca convertirse en la tercera vía de un año dominado por La Bola Negra y El ser querido. Una ambiciosa producción que, en forma de drama deportivo, presenta al público una de las historias reales más fascinantes y épicas que ha dado la competición de alto rendimiento en nuestro país.
Karateka es la historia de Sandra Sánchez, una mujer que nunca dejó de creer y que desafió todas las convenciones. Enamorada del karate desde niña, por motivos personales tuvo que dejar su entrenamiento cuando era una de las grandes promesas del país. Pero su camino le llevó de ser descartada por el sistema a convertirse en la mejor karateka de todos los tiempos.
Con la guía de Jesús del Moral, su entrenador y compañero de vida, Sandra emprendió un viaje imposible. Para empezar, recuperar la chispa y su nivel. Y, sobre todo, conquistar el oro olímpico a los 39 años y redefinir el significado de la perseverancia en un deporte dominado por los japoneses y donde los más veteranos se retiran a los 30 años.
Épico drama deportivo de los de siempre
Empezaré diciendo que una película que arranca con una referencia a Goku y Dragon Ball ya tiene toda mi atención. Y es que Karateka sabe muy bien lo que busca: enganchar, en primer lugar, a todos los aficionados a las artes marciales y a los dramas deportivos en general. A partir de ahí, gracias a las propias vivencias increíbles de Sandra Sánchez, conquistar al resto de públicos.
Porque si algo tiene Karateka es que se estructura exactamente como tantas y tantas otras películas de su género. Y lo hace con solvencia. Es el clásico camino del héroe, una travesía complicadísima hacia la gloria, una historia de superación. Las hemos visto mil veces y nos siguen cautivando.
El filme nos presentan los baches que Sánchez tuvo que superar para alcanzar sus objetivos. Su talento innato, la gente que creía en ella y también la que no. Los reveses inevitables que da la vida y los sacrificios que tuvo que acometer. Personas que se convierten en villanos y también otras que se vuelven inesperados aliados... Karateka no busca un enfoque más llamativo ni distinto a otros dramas deportivos. Solo quiere hacer valer su propia historia y explotar sus virtudes a partir de ahí.
Si algo destaca en esta habitual receta es el meticuloso mimo que pone la película en todo lo relacionado con el karate. El trabajo de guion y también del director Aritz Moreno hacen que este deporte, para muchos desconocido, se convierta en algo fascinante incluso a ojos de quien jamás ha visto de cerca un tatami. Los rituales, la filosofía que hay detrás, su legado centenario. A este respecto, el filme ejecuta una kata precisa, impecable, inapelable.
Un ejercicio imperfecto
Hay que señalar, eso sí, que la película en su conjunto no es tan perfecta ni mucho menos. Su ritmo a ratos es irregular, con acelerones y frenazos drásticos que entorpecen el desarrollo de la trama. También hay un montón de cuestiones que se plantean solo de una forma muy velada y de las que apenas se intuye su solución. Así como otras de las que jamás se vuelve a saber, como el intrigante pasado de Jesús o el momento en el que uno de los compañeros de equipo levanta la voz por el trato favorable hacia Sandra.
No son errores groseros ni evidentes. No molestan. Entre tanto drama y tanta épica quedan totalmente camuflados y solo el espectador más tiquismiquis se quedará dándoles vueltas una vez que la película acaba. Pero es cierto que quizá algo más de equilibrio le habría sentado aún mejor a Karateka.
Dos protagonistas de lujo
Un último punto a favor de Karateka, y del que sí se hablará (o debería hablarse) es su magnífica dupla protagonista. Andrea Ros se mimetiza a la perfección con ese carácter a la vez fuerte y adorable de Sandra Sánchez. La interpretación que ofrece la actriz es de mucho nivel, se nota que se ha preparado a conciencia. Pase lo que pase en esa temporada de premios que pareciera que ya tiene nombres y apellidos, el trabajo de Ros quedará para siempre como una de las mejores actuaciones del cine español de 2026.
Y lo mismo puede decirse de Patrick Criado, que sigue demostrando lo mucho que está creciendo como artista. Está fabuloso como compañero de entrenamientos y de vida de la protagonista. El magnetismo del que ambos hacen gala, especialmente por la buena química que hay entre ellos, lleva en volandas toda la película. El mejor ejemplo de su sobresaliente esfuerzo se aprecia en los créditos, cuando los Sandra y Jesús reales aparecen en una breve escena y queda patente que Ros y Criado les han plasmado en la pantalla a la perfección. Ojalá se les reconozca como merecen.
En definitiva, Karateka es una película genial que enamorará a los fans del cine deportivo y de las artes marciales, pero que a la vez trascenderá al resto de públicos por su derroche de personalidad. Un drama sólido, vibrante y emocionante que lleva al cine una historia tan asombrosa como cierta. Pese a que no es perfecta, Andrea Ros y Patrick Criado brillan con luz propia y hacen del karate una experiencia cinematográfica magnífica.
Karateka se estrena en cines el 30 de octubre.

articles.title: Microsoft’s new Copilot harness makes agents easy — until you want to switch
articles.text:
Microsoft’s new Copilot harness makes agents easy — until you want to switch
Microsoft is opening up the GitHub Copilot agent harness to outside developers through Microsoft Foundry, bringing the same orchestration infrastructure used across its Copilot products into a managed service for building and deploying autonomous agents.
Announced Wednesday, the Microsoft Copilot harness is now available in public preview through Foundry Agent Service. It comes with built-in sandboxing, reusable skills, MCP integrations, and support for subagents. Microsoft takes care of running the agent and managing its execution environment, leaving developers to choose a supported model and configure the instructions and tools for their applications.
The same harness now supports Copilot Code, Copilot Studio, GitHub Copilot, the CLI, and VS Code.
The company is also using GitHub’s agent infrastructure across more of its Copilot products. It’s a continuation of the Foundry strategy outlined at Build 2026, which focuses on making AI agents easier for companies to run, manage, and control. The same harness now supports Copilot Code, Copilot Studio, GitHub Copilot, the CLI, and VS Code.
Inside the managed Copilot harness
Microsoft’s harness manages model and tool calls, tracks context, and keeps agents within configured policies. Skills can package instructions, scripts, and supporting resources, while MCP integrations require authentication and approval. Agents can also work with files, run code, and delegate tasks to subagents, with the main agent coordinating the results.
Microsoft’s harness manages model and tool calls, tracks context, and keeps agents within configured policies.
How developers deploy agents
The company’s technical walkthrough shows how this works with a research agent. A Markdown-based skill lays out the steps for collecting evidence, analyzing data, and writing a report, while an azure.yaml file defines the model deployment, tools, instructions, and harness.
Developers select microsoft_copilot_preview as the harness type, deploy the agent using azd deploy --all and invoke it through the Azure Developer CLI. They can keep agent configurations and supporting files in source control, making it easier to track changes alongside their application code.
Runtime limits and lock-in
The Copilot harness must be selected when creating a prompt agent, and that choice can’t be changed later, even in a new version. Microsoft also controls how much CPU and memory the agent gets and how long it can sit idle. Developers can decide what their agents do, but have less control over the environment they run in.
Developers can decide what their agents do, but have less control over the environment they run in.
Microsoft is positioning its broader harness strategy as multi-model, although there are limits. Developers can choose from compatible models deployed through Foundry, but bringing their own models isn’t supported with the managed Copilot harness.
Teams that want more control can use Foundry’s hosted agents instead. Teams can build and run agents using their own frameworks and customize how they operate, while Microsoft handles the hosting. The company also announced general availability of long-running resilience for hosted agents on Wednesday, helping them recover from interruptions during tasks that take hours or even days to complete.
Foundry agent pricing explained
The Copilot harness in Foundry Agent Service for free until December 1, 2026, although model inference and some tools and connected services still come with separate charges.
After that, Microsoft will charge $0.0994 per vCPU-hour for compute and $0.0118 per GiB-hour for memory. Those rates may vary depending on the region and customer agreement.

articles.title: Smartphones Samsung : cette application disparaîtra de votre écran d'accueil le 21 décembre 2026
articles.text:
Le grand ménage continue dans l’écosystème logiciel de Samsung. Après avoir récemment supprimé Samsung Daily Plus et revu des plateformes comme Samsung Community, le constructeur coréen s’attaque cette fois à son application d’actualités. Lancée en 2023 pour succéder à Samsung Free (lui-même héritier de Samsung Daily et Bixby Home), Samsung News tentait de s’imposer face à Google Discover et Apple News grâce à des résumés quotidiens et des partenariats avec la presse. Malgré ces efforts, la plateforme n’a pas réussi à s’imposer durablement sur les tablettes et smartphones Samsung.
Ce qui change sur l’écran d’accueil de votre Samsung
Le panneau situé tout à gauche sur l’écran d’accueil de One UI, qui affichait jusqu’à présent Samsung News en complément de Google Discover, basculera vraisemblablement vers un affichage exclusif de Google Discover. Aucun service de remplacement n’a pour l’instant été annoncé par la marque.
Le widget dédié ne recevra plus aucune mise à jour, ce qui pousse l’entreprise à recommander directement aux utilisateurs de le supprimer de leur interface. Les données personnelles récoltées par l’application seront quant à elles supprimées à la date de fermeture, le 21 décembre 2026, à l’exception des éléments que la législation locale impose de conserver.
Clap de fin pour Samsung News
La décision de tuer Samsung News marque un tournant dans la stratégie du géant coréen dans la mesure où aucun nouveau portail d’actualités maison n’est prévu pour prendre le relais, ce qui confirme que la marque préfère se retirer de ce genre de service pour laisser la place à d’autres, plus populaires.
À lire : One UI 10 (Android 18) : tout savoir sur la prochaine interface de Samsung
Si vous étiez habitué à utiliser Samsung News, vous devrez donc vous tourner vers d’autres solutions intégrées (comme Google Discover) ou des applications tierces. Samsung tourne ainsi la page d’une dizaine d’années à essayer de proposer son propre flux d’actualités sur ses interfaces mobiles.

articles.title: La IA ya empieza a dejar huella en el paro español. Los más expuestos: programadores y diseñadores
articles.text:
Cuando una pared cede, el primer aviso casi nunca es un derrumbe inmediato. Suele ser una fina grieta en la pintura apenas perceptible, a menos que la estés buscando. Con la IA y el empleo pasa algo parecido: tres años pronósticos catastrofistas que dibujaban un apocalipsis laboral y, por ahora, solo una grieta.
Un equipo del Institut d'Economia de Barcelona estuvo buscando esa grieta entre los datos de empleo de los últimos cinco años, ocupación por ocupación. El resultado permite extraer algunas conclusiones interesantes sobre el impacto de la IA en las profesiones más expuestas a ella.
Una brecha pequeña, pero con dirección. El documento de trabajo publicado por los investigadores compara 502 ocupaciones con datos del SEPE entre enero de 2021 y marzo de 2026. Por cada diez puntos adicionales de exposición a la IA, el paro de cada profesión subió un 1,2% en los 25 meses tras el lanzamiento de ChatGPT a finales de 2022.
Más allá de ese periodo, con la IA más presente en las empresas, el porcentaje de paro por cada diez puntos de exposición se incrementa hasta el 1,7%. Sin embargo, los propios autores admiten que ese dato es impreciso y no puede tenerse en cuenta con fines estadísticos, sino más como una referencia indicadora de una tendencia.
Código, datos y diseño en la primera línea. Para medir la exposición de los puestos a la IA, el equipo de investigadores usó la medida de Anthropic, que analiza el uso real de Claude en cada puesto de trabajo. Los programadores encabezan la lista de profesiones más expuestas a la automatización de tareas con IA, con un 75% de sus tareas ya cubiertas. Les siguen los grabadores de datos, los agentes comerciales y los analistas financieros. Los analistas y diseñadores de software y multimedia también entran en el top 10 de profesiones con mayor riesgo de perder sus empleos por la IA.
El mapa de profesiones afectadas por la IA que dibujan los investigadores del IEB guarda muchas similitudes con el que revelaron los datos del estudio que hizo Anthropic en el que no hallaron subidas destacables del desempleo entre las profesiones más expuestas, aunque sí algún indicio de menos contratación junior. Los investigadores de la Universidad de Barcelona hablan de una "acumulación de desempleo registrado", pero no de un descenso en el número de contrataciones en las profesiones más vinculadas a la IA.
El empleo no se hunde, pero tampoco sube. La pequeña grieta que los investigadores del IEB han encontrado en el mercado laboral español no es la única que se ha detectado. Según apuntaba un informe de BBVA Research y Fedea, el empleo en las ocupaciones más expuestas a la IA no solo no ha registrado el apocalipsis laboral que vaticinaban algunos, sino que su tasa de empleo crece por encima de la media, desvinculando la relación negativa entre exposición y desempleo.
Según los datos obtenidos por el estudio, en las ocupaciones más expuestas a la IA no se contrata menos, pero aun así, en esas ocupaciones hay más parados registrados. Es decir, en esas profesiones se contrata igual, pero el paro se va acumulando. Los autores no profundizan si es porque se incorporan más profesionales a esos sectores, o porque los parados tardan más en encontrar un empleo.
Los jóvenes, otra vez en el centro. Investigadores de Stanford descubrieron que el empleo de los jóvenes de entre 22 y 25 años en ocupaciones expuestas a la IA está un 19% por debajo de lo esperado. Según sus autores, ocurre sobre todo porque se contrata menos, no porque se despida más. Es decir, se atribuye a que la IA ha cambiado el perfil de los empleados que necesitan las empresas, priorizando a aquellos con más experiencia.
Según los datos recogidos en la propia plantilla de Anthropic, los perfiles junior pasaron del 27% al 9% de sus contrataciones técnicas entre principios de 2025 y junio de 2026. En España el estudio del IEB detectó que el paro sube más entre los empleados de 30 a 39 años, hasta un 3,4% por cada diez puntos en el último tramo. En cambio, los contratos a menores de 30 años en las ocupaciones más expuestas también crecen, aunque quizá por registrar una mayor rotación y no por ser empleos más estables.

articles.title: AI that speaks, codes and takes action: Inside Google Cloud’s Gemini masterclass
articles.text:
AI that speaks, codes and takes action: Inside Google Cloud’s Gemini masterclass
Why make AI do the talking when it can do the work too? At TechSparks 2026, Google Cloud’s Rajesh Shivani showed how Gemini agents can talk, code and crunch data.
Imagine handing AI 80,000 files and getting back a presentation with charts, images and a clear narrative. Or asking it to build a detailed 3D scene using code, without dedicated rendering software. These are examples of AI moving beyond answering prompts to taking on complex tasks.
At TechSparks 2026, Rajesh Shivani, Head of AI Customer Engineering for Digital Natives, Startups and ITES at Google Cloud, demonstrated how Gemini is being used across voice AI, autonomous agents and software development.
His masterclass explored how businesses can move from using AI for answers to delegating work to it.
From chatbots to autonomous coworkers
AI tools initially gained traction through chat interfaces that answered questions. The next stage is agentic AI, where systems can plan tasks, access information, and use tools to act on a user’s behalf.
“An agent is nothing now but a model plus a harness,” Rajesh said, describing the infrastructure around a model that manages memory, context, permissions and task execution.
Building useful agents requires four elements: a goal, clear instructions, relevant knowledge and tools to act on that knowledge. A company’s internal data is particularly important because general-purpose models may not have access to its specific processes or customer information.
Shivani also discussed Google’s Open Knowledge Format (OKF), which aims to give organisations a structured way to make information accessible to AI agents.
Voice AI takes on real-world tasks
Voice was one of the key demonstrations. A system developed for Singapore-based Grab helped passengers and drivers coordinate airport pickups despite language barriers. The demo highlighted how voice AI could support interactions across more than 85 languages.
Another example showed AI dubbing an English video into Marathi and Malayalam while matching lip movements and facial expressions. Such capabilities could help businesses produce multilingual training material, marketing videos and customer communications with fewer production steps.
“Voice is becoming the new user interface,” Rajesh Shivani stated, pointing to the growing role of voice-based interactions for customers and employees.
He also showcased a virtual banking assistant created for Citibank’s retail banking experience. In the demonstration, the AI avatar explained options for a maturing certificate of deposit and submitted a renewal after the customer selected a 12-month term.
AI that builds, checks and creates
Beyond voice, Shivani highlighted Google’s tools for coding and cybersecurity. Antigravity helps developers build applications, while CodeMender can identify code vulnerabilities, generate patches and test them in a sandbox.
In one demonstration, Gemini analysed 80,000 files from NASA’s open archives, including Mars weather readings and helicopter telemetry, and produced a presentation using a supplied template and design guidelines.
Another demo showed a model generating a detailed 3D library scene using Python and NumPy, without dedicated rendering software or external assets.
For businesses weighing the cost of AI adoption, Shivani stressed that the most powerful model is not always necessary. “You don’t need to have a frontier model for everything,” he said, explaining why simpler tasks can use faster, lower-cost models.
Preparing businesses for AI agents
As agents take on more work, businesses will need to rethink how their systems handle permissions, security, costs and automated activity. Shivani urged organisations to consider a future in which agents, not just people, interact with their systems.
Developers, he suggested, could increasingly become managers of agents rather than handling every step themselves.
The challenge is no longer simply choosing a capable AI model. It is giving agents the right knowledge and tools, while ensuring they can complete tasks reliably and safely.

articles.title: GM reaches $220M settlement over selling drivers' private data | TechCrunch
articles.text:
General Motors will pay $220 million to 36 states to settle allegations that it illegally sold private driving behavior and location information to data brokers.
As part of the settlement, GM must get drivers’ express consent before it collects or shares their driving and location data — terms that are in line with separate agreements it previously reached with California and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC). This settlement does contain a new requirement that GM must have a third party assess the automaker’s compliance with the privacy program it has put in place.
The agreement announced Thursday settles a lawsuit brought by a coalition of attorneys general from 36 states that alleged GM had sold the information to data brokers, which in turn then sold it to insurance providers.
“This agreement addresses Smart Driver, a product we ended in 2024, and reinforces steps we’ve taken to strengthen our privacy practices,” GM said in an emailed statement. “Safer, more helpful and personalized experiences are enabled by connected vehicle data, and GM is committed to being clear about what information is used, how it’s protected, and the choices customers have about what they share.”
The settlement comes more than two years after a New York Times report showed how GM and OnStar collected, used, and sold drivers’ precise geolocation data and driving behavior to third parties, including data brokers LexisNexis and Verisk. The data was collected through GM’s Smart Driver program, a free feature contained within its connected car apps that tracked and rated driving behaviors and seat belt use. Data brokers sold this information to insurance providers, which could affect customers’ rates, the NYT reported at the time.
GM discontinued Smart Driver in 2024, but that didn’t stop legal action. In January, the FTC finalized an order that bans GM and its OnStar telematics service from sharing certain consumer data. The FTC settlement, as well as the multistate one announced Thursday, also requires GM to be more transparent with its consumers and receive their explicit consent for certain collection.
The company now says it is focused on protecting the privacy of its customers and will no longer sell vehicle information that can be linked to an individual, their vehicle location, or how they drive. However, GM may still disclose anonymized data not tied to an individual with certain partners. GM has also updated the language in its privacy policy and created a consumer-facing Privacy Center.
The settlement and mandated changes to how GM handles customer driving data come as more sensor-laden vehicles equipped with computing power enter the market. Automakers have made large bets on software-centric vehicles that drivers and passengers can interact with and connect with other digital apps such as their calendar, messages, and email.
For instance, GM is adding a personal AI assistant to OnStar, its 30-year-old safety and roadside assistance service. Cameras on the vehicle will be connected to the software to offer live views as well as crash and safety recordings. Users will also be able to use voice to control certain functions on the vehicle, including climate, and ask questions about any specific vehicle feature.
The automaker emphasized its privacy protections when it announced the new assistant during its GM Forward event in October. The company said customers will have the ability to decide what data is shared and that the recordings have time limits and are encrypted. GM said it and OnStar cannot access Connected Camera recordings. Customers will also be able to manage permissions. However, customers who opt not to share their data will likely have limited access to certain features, according to GM.

articles.title: Fake crypto app on Apple App Store linked to $23K wallet theft
articles.text:
A fake cryptocurrency trading app called Padre Terminal, previously available on the Apple App Store for iOS devices, has been linked to the theft of approximately $23,000 from 27 Solana wallets.
Blockchain investigator Iris confirmed that one victim was compromised through the malicious App Store app, but has not determined how the other affected wallets were compromised.
The researcher says the app drains wallets after unsuspecting users import their private keys into it.
Padre was a cryptocurrency trading platform, mainly used to buy and sell meme coins on Solana. It was later renamed Terminal by pump.fun, a platform focused on creating, buying, and selling cryptocurrency “meme coins” on the Solana blockchain.
Iris says the legitimate Padre trading service, now Terminal by pump.fun, is web-only, so any mobile apps impersonating it, including the one previously available on the App Store, are malicious.
At the time of BleepingComputer's initial investigation, we found two Padre apps on the App Store (ID 6802739263 and ID 6717572591). The former was the Iris-confirmed drainer app, while the latter is likely pump.fun's official app, live since October 2024.
The malicious Padre Terminal app has since been removed from the App Store, with its listing now returning a 404 error.
Iris told BleepingComputer it suspects the trading interface of the fake app is served remotely, but has not directly observed the wallet-draining screen.
According to Iris, the operation has drained 27 Solana wallets since October 25, 2026, stealing approximately $23,000 in cryptocurrency. The stolen cryptocurrency was traced to the Solana address 3LAgKYoNenWrGWT3U4XWhpgVJWyYkP9wKpiPk8TJT1LN.
Iris says the attacker converted all remaining USDC (4,070 tokens) into SOL on October 29, eliminating the possibility of Circle freezing those funds.
The attacker then transferred 192 SOL to a new wallet (H84yazsUVCF8eJ6brh27rURMHjdKEVv2BuLS4iuUUQbu). According to Iris, the two wallets held a combined 229.66 SOL, with no funds cashed out at the time of the researcher's update.
The drainer remained active after the app's removal, with the latest reported theft occurring at 17:06 UTC on October 29.
More suspicious apps on the App Store
Iris identified at least five suspected crypto-brand impersonators on the App Store, including Padre Terminal, Axiom Pro: Focus, GMGN AI, HyperTerminal-HyperliquidTools, and Pump Fun Tokens & Analitycs.
Their listings feature seemingly harmless descriptions, but user reviews below sometimes reveal their true nature, with many exposing them for wallet theft and scams.
The Axiom Pro: Focus app, for example, had approximately 25 user reviews alleging wallet theft since February. One reviewer claimed the app had presented itself as a meme coin trading platform before changing into a focus application.
A review of the GMGN AI app alleged that $2,000 had been stolen, while a review associated with HyperTerminal-HyperliquidTools reported the theft of $2,020.
Another app, Pump Fun Tokens & Analitycs, presented itself as a notes application but had a review explicitly accusing it of stealing cryptocurrency.
Iris also found a script on the fake Axiom website containing backend addresses associated with Axiom, Aster, and GMGN impersonators, suggesting a common operator. However, Padre Terminal was not linked to that cluster.
Also, a script on the GMGN website blocks visitors from several CIS countries, potentially indicating that the attackers are attempting to avoid targeting users in those regions.
Iris has not independently confirmed cryptocurrency theft for the four suspicious apps.
BleepingComputer has contacted Apple about the Padre drainer and the other four suspicious apps available on the App Store, but we have not heard back as of publication.
In March 2024, a fake Leather cryptocurrency wallet app appeared on the Apple App Store, and multiple users reported losing their assets after connecting their wallets to it.
Apple eventually removed the app two weeks later and blocked the publisher from its developer program.
Users are recommended to follow links to the App Store from the projects' official websites and avoid installing apps with only a handful of downloads and reviews, or those published by entities with names that appear completely unrelated to the project.

articles.title: Pendant dix ans, Apple nous a expliqué pourquoi un Mac tactile était une mauvaise idée. Qu'est-ce qui a changé ?
articles.text:
Pendant plus de dix ans, Apple a défendu l’idée qu’un écran tactile n’avait pas sa place sur un Mac. Alors que son premier MacBook Pro tactile vient d’être présenté, trois de ses principaux dirigeants expliquent pourquoi l’entreprise a finalement changé d’avis.
Il y a des convictions qui semblent gravées dans le marbre chez Apple. Pendant des années, le constructeur a soigneusement séparé l’iPad, pensé pour les doigts, et le Mac, conçu autour du vénérable couple clavier/trackpad. Une position répétée avec insistance, jusqu’à la présentation de son premier MacBook Pro à écran tactile, ce 28 octobre. Comment une fonction jugée inconfortable, voire contraire à la philosophie du Mac, est-elle soudain devenue suffisamment intéressante pour équiper l’un des ordinateurs les plus prestigieux de la marque ?
Quand Apple expliquait que le tactile n’avait aucun sens sur un Mac
La réticence d’Apple ne date pas d’hier. Dès 2010, Steve Jobs critiquait l’ergonomie des écrans tactiles verticaux, qui obligent à maintenir le bras levé et provoquent rapidement une certaine fatigue. Pour lui, mieux valait conserver une surface tactile horizontale, à l’image du trackpad.
En 2015, Phil Schiller, alors responsable du marketing mondial d’Apple, développait cette idée auprès du journaliste Steven Levy : « D’un point de vue ergonomique, nous avons étudié la question de manière assez approfondie. Nous pensons que, dans un environnement de bureau avec un clavier fixe, devoir tendre le bras vers un écran pour utiliser des interfaces tactiles est inconfortable », expliquait-il.
Mais l’argument ne s’arrêtait pas là. Apple considérait également que macOS et iOS devaient conserver des interfaces distinctes, chacune adaptée à son mode d'interaction.
« Ces deux univers sont différents volontairement, et c’est une bonne chose. Nous pouvons optimiser la meilleure expérience pour chacun, plutôt que d’essayer de les fusionner dans une expérience fondée sur le plus petit dénominateur commun », poursuivait Schiller.
Un an plus tard, lors du lancement des MacBook Pro équipés de la Touch Bar, le dirigeant enfonçait le clou. Adapter la barre de menus de macOS aux doigts risquerait, selon lui, de dégrader son utilisation avec une souris ou un trackpad. « On ne peut pas optimiser pour les deux », affirmait-il.
Apple avait même réalisé des essais avec des Mac tactiles. Et Schiller semblait particulièrement satisfait du résultat : « Nous en sommes absolument arrivés à la conclusion que ce n’était pas la bonne chose à faire. Notre intuition était juste »
En 2021, le responsable de l'ingénierie de l'époque et maintenant patron d'Apple, John Ternus, reprenait encore cet argumentaire, expliquant que le Mac était entièrement optimisé pour les interactions indirectes et qu’Apple ne ressentait aucune raison de changer cette approche.
Cinq ans plus tard, le discours a considérablement évolué.
« Dix ans, c’est très, très long » : les dirigeants d’Apple justifient leur revirement
Dans un entretien accordé à WIRED, John Ternus, désormais patron d’Apple, Johny Srouji et Greg Joswiak reviennent sur ce changement de cap. Ternus commence par rappeler que l’entreprise n’entend pas transformer le Mac en iPad.
« Le Mac reste avant tout un appareil conçu pour une interaction indirecte, autour du trackpad et du clavier. Mais je pense qu’il y a des moments où le tactile est confortable et pratique », explique-t-il.
Pourquoi avoir attendu si longtemps ? Selon le dirigeant, Apple refusait d’intégrer cette fonction au prix de compromis sur la conception de ses ordinateurs.
« Nous devions atteindre un stade où l'ajout du tactile ne dégrade le produit d’aucune manière. Il ne devait pas devenir plus lourd, ni plus épais. Tout cela s’est concrétisé avec l’écran OLED, le meilleur écran que nous ayons jamais intégré à un Mac »
Johny Srouji, responsable de l’ingénierie matérielle, défend lui aussi cette évolution technologique. « Dix ans, c’est très, très long. Beaucoup de choses ont changé, qu'il s’agisse des technologies d’affichage, de nos propres puces ou d’autres éléments », explique-t-il.
Concrètement, Apple a revu le refroidissement pour éviter que la dalle ne devienne désagréablement chaude lorsqu’on la manipule. La charnière a également été repensée pour limiter les mouvements de l’écran sous la pression des doigts, tandis que macOS adapte désormais la taille de certaines commandes aux interactions tactiles.
Greg Joswiak, vice-président en charge du marketing, avance toutefois un argument moins technique, et peut-être plus révélateur : les attentes des utilisateurs ont changé. « La plupart des professionnels possèdent un iPad, et presque tous ont un iPhone. C'est donc quelque chose de naturel pour eux. Une génération de jeunes créateurs et d’utilisateurs de nos MacBook Pro s’attend désormais à pouvoir toucher l'écran ».
Voilà qui remet les anciennes certitudes d’Apple en perspective. Les progrès techniques permettent certainement une meilleure intégration du tactile, mais les fabricants de PC proposent cette fonctionnalité depuis des années. La différence tient peut-être autant à la manière dont Apple souhaite l’intégrer qu’à la technologie elle-même.
Quant à savoir si les MacBook Air et les iMac adopteront à leur tour un écran tactile, John Ternus préfère rester prudent : « Vous savez bien que je ne vous dirai jamais rien sur nos futurs produits ».
Une précaution plutôt bienvenue, quand on se souvient de tout ce qu’Apple a pu affirmer sur les Mac tactiles.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE: London’s Ares Intelligence raises €2.6 million to turn employee insights into AI adoption plans | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Ares Intelligence, a London-based startup building what it describes as an evidence-based platform for AI transformation, has secured €2.6 million in funding.
The round was backed by Creandum and Lakestar, with participation from angels connected to Google DeepMind.
“Enterprise AI today is mostly coding, and that’s only the start. The opportunity across the rest of the business is far bigger and still largely untapped, and we’re at the very beginning of enterprise adoption,” said Richard Keuntje, Vice President, Creandum.
Founded in 2026 by Matt Falconer and 21-year-old Alfie Ranstead, Ares Intelligence was built to solve a problem the founders encountered first-hand while running Instruct, their previous automation company. It says customers ran into the same problem: they wanted to automate parts of their business but had no reliable way of knowing where to begin. Ares Intelligence was to fix this knowledge gap.
The platform deploys an AI interviewer that holds confidential, voice-based conversations with every employee in an organisation, in more than 70 languages. Within weeks, leadership receives a prioritised, evidence-led roadmap identifying where AI can save time and money.
Ares’ platform is GDPR- and SOC 2-compliant, with anonymisation controls that let businesses mask names, redact voices, or strip role metadata before reports reach leadership. Customers can deploy it on their own cloud or use Ares’ infrastructure, in the EU or the US, with data retention windows set by the business.
The founders say the entire process, from training employees on what AI can do to conducting individual interviews, collecting insights and drafting recommendations, takes weeks rather than the months usually taken by a consulting firm.
Ares Intelligence’s approach also flips the script on top-down AI strategy by not relying only on a handful of senior managers to identify AI transformation opportunities. The company’s AI interviewer captures the knowledge of the people closest to the day-to-day work, identifies gaps such as manual workarounds, broken handoffs, and use of unapproved AI tools.
“Businesses across Europe know they need to adopt AI, but many still don’t know where to start. It’s vital that companies begin their AI transformations now to avoid falling behind,” said Falconer, co-founder and CEO, Ares Intelligence.
He added, “The people doing the work every day have a huge amount of knowledge about where AI could make a difference, but they’re rarely asked. Ares gives them a voice across departments, countries and languages, and turns what they share into a practical plan. This funding helps us expand and bring that approach to more businesses.”
Since launch, Ares Intelligence has signed enterprise customers across Europe and the United States in approximately seven months. Tremonia, a Mercedes-Benz spin-out, uncovered more than 400 hours of avoidable manual work per month within four weeks of Ares’ AI interviewer interviewing everyone from senior leadership to the paint shop floor.
“The gap between AI ambition and real-world evidence is the right challenge to back. I’m building a business with AI myself, and there’s a significant difference between an impressive demo and something you can rely on in your actual work. What appeals to me about Ares Intelligence is getting the insight from the people closest to the work,” said Enrico Mellis, Venture Partner, Lakestar.
Ares Intelligence says the fresh capital will help the company expand operations and bring its AI-driven workforce intelligence to more businesses.

articles.title: PROLED XDR : anatomie du nouvel écran Tandem Oled des MacBook Pro 14 & 16 pouces
articles.text:
PROLED XDR : anatomie du nouvel écran Tandem Oled des MacBook Pro 14 & 16 pouces
Apple fait évoluer l’affichage de ses MacBook Pro avec le PROLED XDR. Cette dalle Tandem Oled cherche à corriger les limites de la technologie Mini-Led utilisée depuis 2021, tout en ajoutant le tactile.
Depuis 2021, les MacBook Pro 14 et 16 pouces sont équipés de la dalle Liquid Retina XDR. Sous l’appellation marketing se cache l’utilisation d’une dalle Mini-Led qui, il y a cinq ans, nous avait impressionnés par des pics HDR inédits dépassant 1500 cd/m² et un noir très profond. Toutefois, cette technologie reposait sur une dalle LCD IPS rétroéclairée par 2554 zones (sur le 16 pouces), chaque zone couvrant environ 30 mm². Malgré les optimisations de l'époque, un léger effet de halo (blooming) demeurait perceptible autour des petits éléments lumineux contrastés, comme les sous-titres sur fond noir.
Avec la nouvelle dalle PROLED XDR annoncée sur les MacBook Pro, Apple délaisse le LCD et le rétroéclairage par zones pour adopter la technologie Tandem Oled. En superposant deux couches émettrices organiques où chaque pixel produit sa propre lumière, la dalle supprime mécaniquement tout phénomène de blooming et améliore grandement le contraste. De plus, le passage à des pixels auto-émissifs réduit le temps de réponse en réglant une bonne fois pour toutes les éventuels problèmes de rémanence caractéristiques de la dalle IPS précédente.
Apple MacBook Pro 14 (PROLED XDR)
Contraste : pourquoi le passage de 1 000 000:1 à 10 000 000:1 ne changera probablement rien
Sur la fiche technique, le taux de contraste passe de 1 000 000:1 sur l'ancien Mini-Led à 10 000 000:1 sur cette dalle Oled, mais ces chiffres marketing n’ont pas grand intérêt. L’Oled reste la meilleure technologie en matière de contraste pour la profondeur des noirs qu’elle offre, mais l’écran Liquid Retina était déjà excellent.
Nous verrons lors de nos tests si les micro-contrastes de l’image sont en effet meilleurs, mais la différence ne devrait pas être aussi flagrante que sur des grandes dalles de téléviseurs.
Une luminosité étendue pour l'extérieur et le SDR
Sur la dalle Liquid Retina XDR de 2021, les 1000 cd/m² constants et les pics lumineux étaient réservés aux contenus HDR, le mode standard (SDR) étant évidemment bien plus limité au quotidien. Apple précise dans sa documentation technique accompagnant la sortie de la dalle PROLED XDR que les 1000 cd/m² en plein écran sont désormais accessibles aussi bien en HDR qu'en SDR (sous 25 °C). Surtout, Apple pousse la luminosité jusqu'à 2000 cd/m² en pic HDR, mais autorise également le SDR à monter temporairement à ce même plafond de 2000 cd/m² en plein soleil.
À l’opposé, la luminosité minimale peut descendre à 1 cd/m². Pour gérer les risques de marquage propres aux composants organiques, le contrôleur d'affichage intégré aux puces M5 Pro et M5 Max applique une compensation en temps réel pixel par pixel en fonction de l'usage et de la température, afin d'éviter le burn-in de l’écran.
Verre nanotexturé
Pour limiter les reflets, Apple annonce une réflectance de 1 % avec la surface en verre standard. Ici, nous sommes obligés de nous fier aux allégations d’Apple puisque c’est la première fois que la marque évoque la réflectance sur les MacBook. Par exemple, le moniteur Studio Display XDR sans l’option verre nanotexturé est annoncé avec une réflectance de 1,65 %. Dans tous les cas, l’option verre nanotexturé reste disponible et, lors de son passage sous notre réflectomètre, nous avions obtenu une moyenne inférieure à 10 %. (lien vers actu labo)
Toutefois, Apple n’est pas le premier constructeur à proposer ce type d'équipement sur le marché des ordinateurs portables. Asus exploite déjà la technologie Tandem Oled au sein de ses gammes et même le GoogleBook 14, associée à un traitement antireflet signé Corning capable d’égaler le niveau de réflectance proposé par le verre nanotexturé d'Apple.
Intégration tactile et fréquences de fonctionnement
Autre évolution notable mentionnée par le constructeur : l'arrivée de capacités tactiles via une conception spécifique. Le capteur Touch est directement intégré à la dalle de l’écran — et non superposé. Cela permet, selon Apple, de réduire la latence au point de donner l’impression de toucher directement l’image. Cette intégration physique au cœur de la structure évite l'ajout d'une couche intermédiaire qui aurait pu dégrader la finesse ou la transmission lumineuse. Elle empêche également la grille tactile de devenir visible sous certains angles de lumière ou sur fond blanc, un compromis que l'on observe parfois sur des tablettes ou des PC portables plus abordables.
La technologie ProMotion, équivalente au VRR, déjà présente sur la dalle Liquid Retina XDR, adapte quant à elle le rafraîchissement entre 10 et 120 Hz, tout en permettant aux monteurs vidéo de verrouiller des fréquences fixes conformes aux normes de diffusion et de cinéma : 47,95 Hz, 48,00 Hz, 50,00 Hz, 59,94 Hz, 60,00 Hz et 120,00 Hz, sans oublier l'alignement automatique sur le 23,976 i/s lors de la lecture plein écran.
Colorimétrie et imagerie médicale avec le protocole DICOM-GSDF
Couvrant simultanément les espaces colorimétriques P3 et Adobe RGB au sein d’un même profil, la dalle bénéficie d’un étalonnage d’usine calibré selon la formule Apple CMF 2026. L’écran intègre également deux modes de référence (DICOM-350 cd/m² et DICOM-600 cd/m²) conformes à la norme DICOM-GSDF (Grayscale Standard Display Function).
Ce protocole ajuste la distribution des niveaux de gris en fonction de la perception humaine et de la lumière ambiante, offrant ainsi aux praticiens une lisibilité optimale lors de la consultation clinique de radiographies ou d’imageries numériques, hors visée diagnostique.
Il reste désormais à vérifier comment ces caractéristiques se traduisent en pratique. Nous avons hâte de poser nos sondes et nos outils de mesure sur un MacBook Pro équipé de cette dalle PROLED XDR afin d'évaluer concrètement les affirmations d'Apple concernant la luminosité réelle, la réflectance du traitement de surface et la fidélité colorimétrique.
Apple MacBook Pro 16 (PROLED XDR)

articles.title: En Argentina, robot aprende a abrir puertas viendo videos tutoriales
articles.text:
Un robot capaz de abrir puertas que nunca vio antes funciona en pruebas dentro del Distrito Tecnológico de Parque Patricios, en Buenos Aires. No lo guía ningún operador humano ni tiene cargado un plano de cada acceso: aprendió observando más de mil videos de manijas, pestillos y giros.
La máquina, equipada con ruedas y un brazo de seis grados de libertad, logró en una de sus pruebas abrir una puerta metálica a los 22 centímetros de desplazamiento tras varios intentos fallidos, según informó Diario22.
Qué significa que un robot “aprenda” de videos y no de instrucciones
Un robot logra abrir puertas desconocidas entrenándose exclusivamente con grabaciones, sin planos ni control remoto previo. El sistema identifica patrones de manijas, alturas y resistencias a partir de lo observado, y aplica esas reglas a situaciones nuevas con una efectividad del 84% en las pruebas realizadas en la ciudad.
Esa cifra surgió al exponer el robot a 14 puertas inéditas en tres edificios de Retiro, Balvanera y Núñez: madera con marco viejo, chapa cortafuego, vidrio con herrajes cromados y aluminio negro. De 56 intentos, el tiempo promedio de apertura fue de 19 segundos desde el primer fotograma captado.
Las fallas se concentraron en dos escenarios puntuales: perillas redondas sin palanca, donde el mecanismo de agarre no encuentra puntos de apoyo claros, y superficies muy reflectantes, que distorsionan la lectura de las cámaras.
La base de datos detrás del aprendizaje
Para llegar a ese nivel de generalización, el equipo filmó 1.280 clips de entre 8 y 30 segundos en cuatro edificios porteños: oficinas en Almagro, un centro médico en Once, un consorcio en Caballito y un cowork en Microcentro. De 64 horas de grabación bruta, quedaron 9 horas útiles tras el proceso de depuración.
El etiquetado de esos videos no requirió trabajo manual. El sistema usó señales propias de la grabación: flujo óptico en la zona de la manija, variación de ángulos de giro y un “clic” detectado por micrófono en el momento exacto en que el pestillo libera. Con esa información armó pares de causa y efecto que se tradujeron en un objetivo simple: puerta abierta o no abierta.
Cómo decide el robot en fracciones de segundo
Una vez entrenado, el funcionamiento en tiempo real combina dos cámaras RGB y una cámara de profundidad que procesan imagen a 30 fotogramas por segundo. Con eso, el sistema calcula dónde ubicar el agarre con un margen de 12 centímetros respecto del borde de la manija, y ajusta la fuerza de giro según la resistencia que detecta.
“La clave no es ver la manija, sino anticipar la fricción. Retrocede 5 milímetros si el pestillo no cede y vuelve a intentar en un ángulo más bajo”, señaló Lucía Herrera, de 34 años, coordinadora del proyecto.
Todo ese ciclo se completa en 340 milisegundos en promedio. La mejora en la precisión llegó de la mano de tres ajustes puntuales: microgiros progresivos de 5 en 5 grados antes de forzar la apertura, un filtro que descarta reflejos que desviaban el punto de agarre entre 2 y 4 centímetros, y una memoria corta de 2,4 segundos que evita repetir errores de aproximación recientes. Con esos cambios, los daños sobre las puertas bajaron a cero en 112 interacciones consecutivas.
Cuánto cuesta y qué resguardos tiene el sistema
El hardware detrás del robot ronda los 6.600 dólares: la plataforma móvil cuesta cerca de 1.800 dólares, el brazo 3.200, las cámaras y el profundímetro 600, y la computadora de a bordo 1.000. El conjunto pesa 13,5 kilos y su batería de 220 Wh rinde 2,8 horas de pruebas con video activo.
Las pruebas no estuvieron libres de incidentes menores. En la primera semana se registraron tres marcas leves sobre las puertas, antes de que los ajustes en la política de exploración redujeran ese número a cero. También debieron reemplazarse dos pestillos dañados, a 14.000 pesos cada uno.
Para evitar roturas, el sistema opera con un tope de fuerza de 20 newtons y un toque exploratorio inicial de apenas 2 newtons antes de intentar el giro completo. Si no obtiene respuesta, el brazo se repliega 10 milímetros y recalcula la maniobra. El protocolo de prueba, además, exige la presencia de tres personas: una que opera el panel de control, otra que observa la puerta y una tercera que registra los tiempos de cada intento.

articles.title: When Risk Becomes Personal: What Security Leaders Can Learn From a Cancer Diagnosis
articles.text:
Risk management leaders educate people on measuring exposure, testing assumptions and advising on how best to prepare for incidents they hope won’t occur. They know that the absence of a security alert does not stand for safety; that resilience depends on preparedness, and that a plan is only as good as the people who can execute it.
But when the risk is personal, those ideas take on a heavier meaning.
Receiving a Cancer Diagnosis
I was diagnosed after a routine physical that included a PSA blood test. I had not noticed any symptoms and had no known family history. That raised a few eyebrows and ultimately, a stage-three prostate cancer diagnosis.
My experience is not a case for making a personal health choice or offering clinical advice. That’s far from my wheelhouse. However, it is a helpful framework for a profession that often talks about preparedness, leadership and resilience, but sometimes forgets to consider the people expected to deliver all three.
Risk Appetite Changes When the Asset is You
In professional life, leaders can be admirably objective. They can challenge a security control, decide whether a certain risk falls within an agreed tolerance, and explain to a board why a difficult trade-off is necessary. They are typically analyzing a faceless enterprise.
Risk management is more than recommending a set of analytical frameworks. It is also decision making under duress, usually done with incomplete information and nervous tempers. Leaders who never acknowledge that human aspect may be poorer prepared, not richer, when pressure mounts on their own lives or teams.
The parallel with cyber governance should be handled carefully, but it is useful. A security leader should not accept at face value a supplier assurance statement, a default technology configuration, or management recommendations without formal review.
Similarly, a patient should not be made to feel that asking questions is somehow confrontational. In both situations, agency derives from available information, psychological safety, feeling able to say: help me understand the options, the assumptions, and the consequences of the mitigation plan.
Resilience is Preparation, Not Performance
Before my radiotherapy, I prepared deliberately, focusing on fitness, diet, rest, meditation and mental conditioning. I had to reevaluate my relationship with alcohol and caffeine. I sought to make a game out of it, imagining my 37-week treatment as a daily tournament: one demanding day at a time, with the aim of arriving at my best condition possible for each “game.” Doing this gave structure to an experience where I would otherwise feel a loss of control.
The more general leadership lesson here is that resilience grows under certain conditions: clear routines, manageable goals, supportive relationships, and the right to rest. And to change course when the original plan has ceased to be appropriate.
At times I felt like I had overdone it; my body forced me to listen. That matters. Cyber teams are told to endure while normalizing exhaustion: pulling all-nighters for incident response, always on call, the idea that commitment is measured by availability.
But a security function cannot be resilient if its people have little opportunity to recover. Personal resilience is not an individual productivity program. It is an ability reinforced by support, boundaries, and a culture that sees recovery as part of a sustained performance.
Transparency Can Be a Control, Not a Liability
Cancer can carry stigma, especially in senior environments where strength is too often interpreted as invulnerability. I decided to go public with my diagnosis to raise awareness because I did not want to hide what was happening. Not surprisingly, the response was mixed. Some people just plain didn’t know what to say, while others were supportive.
That is a familiar dynamic for security leaders. We want people to disclose incidents early, raise concerns and ask for help. But organizations can unintentionally discourage the openness they say they value. If the culture demands polished certainty from leaders, it becomes harder for anyone to share a vulnerability or need.
Everyone should have the right to control what they disclose and when, and with whom. Leaders who embody the notion that humanity and accountability are not in opposition can help lead by example. They can model a better kind of strength: the ability to hold space for others without pretending to be invincible.
This is not only a show of goodwill to the employers. It is a resilience issue. Workplace support for people undergoing cancer treatment can come in many forms, from time off and flexible hours to adjusted responsibilities, regular check-ins, occupational health support or employee assistance.
A More Human Model of Risk Leadership
Of course, personal health and cybersecurity are not interchangeable. A PSA result is not a vulnerability scan, and treatment is not incident response. The analogy breaks down when trying to make illness sound like a management problem to be solved through willpower.
But risk leaders can still take away something important. The habits that help organizations confront uncertainty, things like curiosity, preparation, trusted expertise, purposeful communication and adaptive recovery, matter in human life too. So does acknowledging what those habits cannot control.
For a profession built around anticipating harm, the challenge is not to become more alarmed. It is to become more attuned to the weak signals we ignore, to the people we expect will cope in silence and to the difference between seeming okay and actually being supported.
We need to let go of stigmas or assumptions and begin an honest dialogue around prostate health for men. The responsible version of that message is just as blunt: talk to a clinician about your personal risk and what PSA testing can reveal.
Cybersecurity leaders often ask organizations if they are prepared for disruption. A more personal question may be just as important: are we creating an environment where people can freely discuss risk, ask for help if they need it and recover without having to compromise their dignity?
Disclaimer: This is a personal account of my experiences and not meant as medical advice. Concerned readers should consult with qualified healthcare professionals.

articles.title: QCon AI New York 2026 Program Committee Picks: Agent Identity, Context Costs, and Open-Source Infere
articles.text:
Who authorizes an agent’s actions? How should teams manage growing context costs? What changes when coding agents become part of everyday engineering work? The QCon AI New York 2026 program committee has selected six sessions they are looking forward to at the December 15–16 conference. Their picks examine these questions alongside open-source inference, agent standards, and audio AI.
Conference chair Hien Luu, an AI/ML leader, advisor, speaker, and author, joins committee members Wes Reisz, Technical Principal at Thoughtworks and creator of The InfoQ Podcast, and Faye Zhang, Staff Engineer at Google building autonomous agents for Gemini Enterprise, in sharing their selections.
Wes on Agent Identity and Context Costs
Wes Reisz selected When Software Becomes a User: Identity and Authorization for Agents in Production, a keynote by Nancy Wang, CTO at 1Password.
As agents take on more autonomous work, traditional identity and authorization models start to break down. Nancy will explore delegated authority, credential management, and securing agent interactions, foundational capabilities I believe we must get right to truly adopt agentic delivery.
Nancy’s keynote examines how authority is delegated across subagent chains and how agents can access the credentials they need without exposing secrets in their context.
Wes’s second choice is Make Each Token Count: Compression, Caching, and Retrieval for Production LLM Context, by Tejas Chopra, CEO and co-founder of Headroom Labs.
Token costs and latency are real constraints when building production agents. Tejas will explore compression, caching, and retrieval strategies, particularly token compression, which I believe will become a must-have capability in modern agentic systems.
Tejas will cover learned prompt compression, prefix-cache-aware context alignment, and compress-cache-retrieve pipelines, including failure modes that affect tool calling and agent trajectories.
Hien on Engineering Organizations and Open-Source Inference
Hien Luu selected The Future of the Engineering Org, by Peter Bell, founder and CTO of Gather.dev.
Drawing on conversations with engineering leaders at organizations including Anthropic, OpenAI, Shopify, and Coinbase, Peter will examine how engineering structures and practices are changing around coding agents. Topics include team size and rituals, hiring and assessing engineers, changes in engineering leadership, and the future of junior developers.
Hien’s second pick is Open Source Agentic Inference: Unlocking the Harness with vLLM, by Francisco Javier Arceo, Forward Deployed Engineer at Baseten and maintainer of the vLLM Agentic API project.
Francisco will follow a coding task from the harness through model generation, tool execution, and continuation using Agentic API, vLLM, and llm-d. The session examines where tools run, who owns context, and how serving infrastructure supports these workloads. It also explores how repeated inference and context growth affect cost, including why cost per completed task matters more than token price alone.
Faye on Agent Standards and Audio AI
Faye Zhang described her selections as "two talks at the intersection of frontier research and production engineering". Her first choice is Navigating Agentic Standards: What to Build On Now and What to Watch, by Kevin Kelley, Technical Lead for Standards at Anthropic.
She also highlighted how standards such as MCP, A2A, and OAuth can establish interoperable agent identity, delegated authorization, and trust boundaries without creating new security vulnerabilities. Kevin’s session organizes the standards landscape around questions such as which agent is acting, on whose behalf, and how it reaches tools and other agents. It distinguishes what has shipped from work that remains open.
Her second selection is Audio Processing with Large Language Models, a keynote by Tara Sainath, Distinguished Research Scientist at Google DeepMind and lead of the Gemini audio area.
Faye highlighted the questions raised by LLMs reshaping speech and audio modeling: unified multilingual representations, end-to-end versus cascaded architectures, and the latency–quality trade-offs required for real-time conversational intelligence. Tara’s keynote will discuss research and product developments at Google across speech recognition, generation, translation, and dialogue.
Early-Bird Pricing Changes November 10
QCon AI New York 2026 takes place December 15–16 at the Westin Jersey City Newport, one PATH stop from Lower Manhattan. The two-day conference focuses on production AI for senior software engineers, architects, and engineering leaders.
Early-bird pricing is $1,705 until November 10, after which the two-day pass rises to $1,790. Anyone planning to use their remaining 2026 learning and development budget can explore the QCon AI New York program and the "convince your manager" approval email on the conference website.

articles.title: Global OLED Notebook Shipments Forecast to Grow Over 40% YoY in 2027
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
Global OLED Notebook Shipments Forecast to Grow Over 40% YoY in 2027
Apple's newly unveiled MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display marks a significant milestone in the evolution of MacBook display technology and user experience, becoming the first model in the lineup to feature a tandem OLED touchscreen. TrendForce estimates that shipments of the new model will reach 1.2-1.5 million units in 2027. Apple's entry into the OLED notebook market is also providing fresh impetus for panel makers to accelerate the development of advanced display technologies.
However, TrendForce notes that the new MacBook Pro's premium starting price of US$2,899 for the 14-inch model, coupled with its initial availability alongside existing Mini-LED models, could temper near-term replacement demand.Nevertheless, the launch further reinforces Apple's reputation for technological innovation and premium positioning. Together with the MacBook Neo's departure from Apple's traditional entry-level pricing strategy, the move reflects the company's broader efforts to expand its product portfolio across a wider spectrum of price points.
Until now, the OLED notebook market has been driven primarily by Windows-based brands such as Lenovo, HP, and ASUS, which have gradually expanded their OLED offerings across different price segments. Apple's arrival is expected to give the market additional momentum, encouraging brands to prioritize OLED models in their product roadmaps while strengthening consumer acceptance of the technology. This, in turn, could pave the way for broader OLED adoption in notebook displays.
Despite an anticipated contraction in the overall notebook market for two consecutive years, TrendForce forecasts that OLED notebook shipments will grow nearly 40% YoY in 2026, followed by another increase of more than 40% in 2027.
Samsung Display secures exclusive supply position as rivals set their sights on the OLED MacBook Air
Samsung Display (SDC) is currently the exclusive panel supplier for the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display. The company has designated Phase 1 of its G8.6 A6 production line at its Asan campus in South Korea as a dedicated facility for Apple.
The new MacBook Pro carries considerable strategic significance as the first product to enter mass production on SDC's G8.6 fine metal mask (FMM) OLED line. Its selection as the display for Apple's first and most premium OLED notebook underscores SDC's technological capabilities and strengthens its position at the forefront of the OLED market.
TrendForce explains that the new MacBook Pro's tandem OLED architecture and pixel density of 254 pixels per inch (PPI) impose exceptionally demanding requirements on panel production. Meeting these specifications presents substantial challenges for suppliers, particularly in terms of material costs and manufacturing yields.
Although other panel makers are conducting qualification programs, the high cost of meeting Apple's stringent specifications, combined with SDC's established position as the primary supplier, presents considerable barriers to entry. As a result, competing OLED panel makers, including LG Display, BOE, and TCL CSOT, are largely directing their efforts toward securing a place in the supply chain for the OLED MacBook Air, which is expected to debut in 2029.
Source:
				TrendForce
