articles.title: TVs da LG perdem acesso à IA da Microsoft • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
TVs da LG perdem acesso à IA da Microsoft
Integração com o Copilot acaba até o final do ano, mas ainda não tem dia certo para acontecer. Decisão impacta o Brasil.
A LG não terá mais o Copilot em suas smart TVs. A integração com a inteligência artificial da Microsoft será encerrada até o fim de 2026, conforme aponta notificação enviada para o sistema webOS dos modelos da marca. O recurso estava presente desde 2025 como IA nativa das TVs, permitindo tirar dúvidas e receber recomendações com base nas suas atividades.
Segundo a mensagem enviada aos televisores, a decisão pelo fim do suporte veio da Microsoft e atinge tanto o app de chat do Copilot quanto suas atividades no sistema operacional. O Tecnoblog realizou testes e confirmou o fim da integração em aparelho vendido no Brasil.
De acordo com o Windows Central, o movimento teria a ver com uma mudança de estratégia adotada pela gigante americana. A Microsoft anunciou mudanças nos serviços de IA em setembro e voltou suas operações para produtividade.
A Microsoft unificou os dois apps disponíveis até então, o Copilot padrão e o Microsoft 365 Copilot. A partir disso, a ideia é que o serviço funcione menos como um chat e mais como um recurso de produtividade, seja para atuar junto ao pacote Office ou realizar trabalhos mais aprofundados de programação.
Com a mudança de estratégia, a presença do modelo nas TVs da LG parou de fazer sentido. Vale lembrar que televisores da Samsung também receberam a integração com o Copilot, mas o app também já não aparece mais nos sistemas Tizen.
A presença do Copilot nas smart TVs da LG foi curta e cercada de polêmica. Apesar do anúncio feito durante a CES 2025, em janeiro, a integração começou de fato em dezembro, com um aplicativo web que não podia ser deletado. Além disso, a chegada do app se deu por meio de um download “forçado” nas TVs da marca.
Na época, muitos usuários foram pegos de surpresa e reclamaram da presença do app. Apesar de “nativo”, o recurso contava basicamente com uma versão web na IA, sem integração total com o televisor. Pouco mais de 10 meses depois, usuários recebem a notificação do fim da parceria.

articles.title: The Commodore 64C returns, complete with original 1980s molds and modern hardware
articles.text:
In context: The Commodore 64 that most people picture is the chunky beige "breadbin" from 1982, but that wasn't the only shape it came in. In 1986, Commodore moved the same internals into a flatter, wedge-shaped case that matched its newer Commodore 128. That version, the 64C, stayed on sale until the company folded in 1994. So, for a lot of people who got their first computer in the late '80s, the 64C is the C64 they actually remember.
Now, the 64C is back as a brand-new computer. The revived Commodore started shipping its 64C Ultimate to pre-order customers this week. Anyone who skipped the campaign can order one as well, starting at $299.99.
Inside, very little has changed from the breadbin-style 64 Ultimate that Commodore launched last year. An AMD Artix-7 FPGA still recreates the original hardware cycle for cycle. The company claims up to 99% compatibility with original software and peripherals, so old cartridges, joysticks, and disk drives should still plug in and work.
The new model does ship with the latest firmware, though. It also works with a regular USB mouse now. That's handy for the bundled GEOS suite, a point-and-click desktop with a word processor, spreadsheet, and paint program. GEOS shipped with the original 64C back in 1986, too, so the pairing doubles as a neat nod to the machine's past.
The case, on the other hand, comes straight out of the same injection molds Commodore used for 64C housings in the '80s. Those molds were used in Japan and later at Commodore's US operations. They turned up at an auction in 2014, survived a factory fire, and ended up with German retro hardware maker Individual Computers before the revived company bought them back.
Because of that, the new shells carry the same quirk as the old ones. The 1986 molds used a two-point flow pattern that cooled the plastic unevenly. That left faint, semicircular marks on the cases that most owners never even noticed.
As before, there are three editions to pick from at the same prices as the breadbin lineup. The $299.99 BASIC Beige is a straight copy of the original. Spend $50 more, and the Starlight Edition swaps in a translucent case with LEDs that react to whatever game is running. The $499.99 Founder's Edition gets gold keycaps, 24K gold-plated badges, and a faintly translucent white shell.
The original breadbin 64 Ultimate is still on sale alongside it, so for most people, the choice now comes down to which case they grew up with.

articles.title: Massive leak exposes 41,000 DHS workers and undercover ICE agents
articles.text:
An unprecedented leak of Department of Homeland Security records has exposed details of more than 41,000 employees or contractors who work for the department and its constituent agencies. The records include email addresses, phone numbers, and office addresses, but also references to internal systems and sensitive information on undercover and surveillance programs. In all, the leak provides a map of how DHS is organized and how it operates.
The records, which span DHS itself as well as seven component agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement and US Customs and Border Protection, were last updated on August 19, 2026. The transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets and cybersecurity researcher and journalist maia arson crimew previewed the data for WIRED, which they say they obtained from a group calling itself the Department of Peace.
DDoSecrets published the archive, which it calls “Icepick,” on Wednesday. In a press release, DDoSecrets says the data is from DHS’s Okta login system. In a note with the files, the hackers wrote, “They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs.”
An Okta spokesperson tells WIRED that it is unaware of any breach of its systems. “We are aware of this report. Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised,” the spokesperson says.
The leak comes as DHS has aggressively pursued its critics, seeking to unmask anonymous social media users, obtain customer records on protesters, and secure warrants for surveillance tools aimed at reporters. Since the start of the second Trump administration, DHS and the federal government have moved to hide DHS employees’ names and faces. The agency has also expanded its definition of “doxing”—a term that typically refers to publishing someone’s home address and other personal details for malicious purposes—to encompass the publication of basic facts about public employees, like their names and titles.
The leak follows a breach in which a group of hackers known as ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen personal information on nearly every FBI employee and their families. Law enforcement agencies have arrested several suspects and detained another who is alleged to be part of the group.

articles.title: India’s new-age manufacturers to benefit from $3 trillion global AI investment cycle: Avendus Capital
articles.text:
India’s new-age manufacturers to benefit from $3 trillion global AI investment cycle: Avendus Capital
The investment banking firm has identified defence and aerospace, space technology, robotics and automation, semiconductors, energy transition, and advanced materials as the sectors that will drive India’s next phase of industrial growth.
India’s new-age manufacturing sector could benefit significantly from a $3 trillion global AI infrastructure investment cycle, according to a report by Avendus Capital.
The investment banking firm has identified defence and aerospace, space technology, robotics and automation, semiconductors, energy transition, and advanced materials as the sectors poised to drive India’s next phase of industrial growth, offering key opportunities for domestic companies.
The report highlighted 2027–28 as a critical period for commercialisation as companies move from policy support and project approvals towards production.
The opportunity is being driven by rising global investments in AI infrastructure, increasing demand for energy infrastructure, and growing geopolitical security concerns. India’s domestic demand, engineering talent and policy framework could help manufacturers reduce import dependence and build globally competitive capabilities.
“India's new-age manufacturing opportunity is substantial, but its right-to-win manifests in select segments,” said Koushik Bhattacharyya, Managing Director and Head of Industrials Investment Banking at Avendus Capital.
With more than 80% of the $3 trillion AI infrastructure investment yet to be deployed globally, India has an opportunity to capitalise on its domestic demand base, engineering capabilities, and policy support, he said.
Semiconductors and space technology are among the segments showing significant growth potential. India’s semiconductor consumption is projected to more than double from $49.5 billion in 2025 to $106.5 billion by 2030, creating opportunities in chip design, packaging, testing, and specialised materials.
India’s space economy is expected to expand more than threefold, from approximately $13 billion in 2025 to $44 billion by 2033. Domestic defence production is projected to reach around $31.6 billion by 2030, while the robotics market could grow nearly fourfold to $4.6 billion by 2030, supported by wider adoption and import substitution.
The report also expects India’s clean-energy manufacturing ecosystem to move further upstream over the next five years. By the end of the decade, the country could establish an integrated solar manufacturing chain spanning ingots to modules, several gigawatt-hour-scale battery cell plants, and commercial production of indigenous electrolyser stacks and rare-earth-free motor technology.
Advanced materials represent another emerging opportunity, with rising domestic demand and heavy import dependence creating scope for local capacity building. Recycling is expected to scale first, followed by battery materials, while rare-earth magnet manufacturing could advance with policy support.
The coming years will test India’s ability to translate these opportunities into commercially viable manufacturing capabilities, the report said.

articles.title: Rowenta X-Clean 12: las preguntas que nos habéis enviado (y sus respuestas) sobre esta fregona eléctrica
articles.text:
Vamos a responder a vuestras preguntas sobre la Rowenta X-Clean 12, una fregadora eléctrica que aspira y friega suelos. La hemos estado probando varios días, y ahora te traemos un vídeo con todas las respuestas a las preguntas que nos habéis ido enviando sobre ella a nuestro perfil de Instagram.
Q&A de la Rowenta X-Clean 12
Las aspiradoras eléctricas hacen ya años que han subido de nivel, y su nuevo escalón evolutivo las combina con fregadoras. Y es aquí donde está la carrera actualmente, un sector donde Rowenta se está posicionando con fuerza gracias a dispositivos como su X-Clean 12.
La primera pregunta es la que todos nos hacemos cuando vemos un dispositivo como este: ¿Puede aspirar y fregar al mismo tiempo? La respuesta es que sí, y que este es precisamente su factor diferenciador. No es necesario dar primero una pasada aspirando y luego otra fregando, puedes hacer las dos cosas a la vez de una sola pasada.
La X-Clean 12 puede recoger líquidos, sólidos, polvo y pelos de mascotas en suelos duros. Y como nos preguntáis también por otros tipos de suelo, decir que esta fregadora también puede usarse en parquet y otros suelos de madera de forma segura. Todo gracias a su sistema de dosificación automático inteligente para usar la dosis justa de agua y detergente sin que haya encharcamientos.
También nos preguntáis por los niveles de potencia, y son cuatro. Vas a poder controlarlos desde la pantalla del mango, y son un modo para suelos de madera, uno silencioso, un tercero para recoger cosas con líquidos, y un cuarto que es el modo automático para detectar el tipo de suelo y usar el modo necesario automáticamente.
En el vídeo aprovechamos para hacer varias demostraciones y que puedas ver cómo funciona recogiendo líquidos. También te hablamos de lo útil que es para limpiar en casas de mascotas, con un cepillo y una cuchilla para no tener que desenredar los pelos del cabezal.
Este dispositivo tiene un sistema de limpieza automático con secado, y también te hablamos de los detergentes que puedes utilizar con ella, además de otros aspectos como la autonomía, potencia y otros aspectos técnicos. Pero lo mejor es que veas el vídeo completo para ver todas las respuestas que damos a las preguntas que nos habéis enviado.
Este contenido es una colaboración y patrocinio entre Xataka y la marca, pero no hay pacto sobre el guión ni la selección de los temas. El contenido editorial está elaborado íntegramente por Xataka.

articles.title: Cloudflare finds the largest DDoS attacks fell 69% as total attacks rose 208% - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Cloudflare finds the largest DDoS attacks fell 69% as total attacks rose 208%
A new report out today from Cloudflare Inc.’s Cloudforce One threat intelligence unit finds that the largest distributed denial-of-service attacks fell nearly 69% in the third quarter, and network-layer attacks overall more than tripled from a year earlier, to 18.2 million.
The “Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3” details 251 attacks above 1 terabit per second between July and September. The second quarter produced 805, after a sixfold rise from the first three months of the year. Cloudflare ties the drop, tentatively, to law enforcement action earlier this year against four of the largest botnets built from compromised internet of things devices.
The Justice Department announced the disruption of Aisuru, Kimwolf, JackSkid and Mossad in March, when authorities in Canada and Germany also moved against people allegedly behind them. Internet of things botnets remain a durable, high-volume threat in Cloudflare’s assessment, with new variants such as Dysphoria and Evooo1Bot already circulating.
August was the heaviest month for Mirai-classified traffic, at 57.23 petabytes. The quarter’s longest Mirai attack began Aug. 19 and kept going for 49.7 hours.
Small attacks made up most of the quarter’s 18.2 million, which work out to about 8,226 an hour. Nearly all were over quickly, 96% of them inside 10 minutes, and bandwidth stayed under 1 gigabit per second in 98% of cases.
The report points out that a flood that size is still more than enough to overwhelm a server or website. Cloudflare reads the overall profile as the signature of DDoS-for-hire “booter” services.
Attackers also switched methods. Floods abusing the Connectionless Lightweight Directory Access Protocol grew 580% in the first half of the year, according to the report. In the third quarter CLDAP made up just 0.05% of attacks, down 99.5% on the second quarter.
Other connectionless protocols filled the gap. Amplification attacks using the Domain Name System rose 215% from the second quarter to 3.4% of the network-layer total. The bigger beneficiary was the generic User Datagram Protocol flood, which went from 14.1% of attacks to 31.3%. Plain DNS floods held steady as the most common method, at 39.3%.
Media, production and publishing kept the top spot among industries with only about a fourth of the share it held from April to June, as attackers spread their aim more widely. The internet sector climbed to sixth from 12th. Further down the table, consumer services rose nine places to eighth and adult entertainment entered the top 10 in ninth after ranking 21st three months earlier.
Geographically, the U.S. was the most-attacked country in the third quarter after finishing second to China in the first half. Indonesia rose to third with 2.93% of attacks.
Canada and Israel made the sharpest climbs. Canada went from 16th to sixth on attacks against retail, telecommunications and marketing companies, during what the report called “an already turbulent period of bilateral trade disputes.” Israel moved up seven places to 10th on sustained DDoS activity in mid-September. That stretch brought contentious decisions ahead of parliamentary elections as well as the Rosh Hashanah holiday, the report noted, against a wider surge in hostile cyber warfare targeting Israel this year.
Cloudflare’s systems detect and mitigate attacks without human intervention. The report says they have to, since most attacks in the quarter “end long before a human analyst could see the alert.”

articles.title: 4 neue Funktionen für Whatsapp Gruppenchats
articles.text:
Fixieren, filtern und mehr: Whatsapp führt 4 neue Funktionen für Gruppenchats ein
Im Februar 2026 hatte Whatsapp – laut eigenen Angaben auf Bitten von Nutzer:innen – den Nachrichtenverlauf für Gruppen eingeführt. Seitdem können Gruppenadmins und -mitglieder Neuankömmlingen in Whatsapp-Gruppenchats einen gewissen Teil des bisherigen Nachrichtenverlaufs zuschicken, damit diese auf dem Laufenden sind.
Mehr Übersicht für Gruppenchats
Jetzt bringt Whatsapp vier neue Gruppenchat-Funktionen, die es Nutzer:innen erleichtern sollen, die Übersicht zu behalten. Eines dieser neuen Features ist eine Erweiterung der Nachrichtenverlauf-Funktion, wie Whatsapp in einem Blogeintrag schreibt. Demnach soll es künftig möglich sein, Personen auch rückwirkend aktuelle Nachrichten zu senden, nachdem sie einer Gruppe beigetreten sind.
Dazu tippen Nutzer:innen einfach auf den Namen der betreffenden Person im Chat und wählen die Funktion aus. Whatsapp verspricht, dass diese Nachrichten Ende-zu-Ende-verschlüsselt sind. Darüber hinaus sollen sich wichtige Nachrichten jetzt dauerhaft fixieren lassen. Ein vorab festgelegtes Zeitlimit ist nicht notwendig.
Statusmeldungen für bestimmte Gruppen
Ebenfalls neu ist die Möglichkeit, eigene Statusmeldungen auf bestimmte Whatsapp-Gruppenchats zu begrenzen. Bestimmte Updates, die etwa in den Familienchat passen, können dort geteilt, aber etwa dem Arbeitschat vorenthalten werden. Die Gruppenstatusmeldungen verschwinden wie herkömmliche Statusmeldungen nach 24 Stunden.
Nutzer:innen, die in mehreren Gruppenchats aktiv sind, können bei Unterhaltungen schnell den Überblick verlieren. Mit dem neuen Chatfilter sollen sich alle ungelesenen Unterhaltungen in einem Gruppenchat, in denen man entweder erwähnt wurde oder wo man eine direkte Antwort erhalten hat, anzeigen lassen. Das betrifft auch die an alle Gruppenmitglieder gerichteten Nachrichten (@alle).
Whatsapp will Gruppenchats weiter verbessern
Die vier neuen Funktionen fügen sich in eine ganze Reihe von Neuerungen ein, mit denen Whatsapp seine Gruppenchats aufpolieren will. So können Mitglieder Personen in einer Gruppe privat antworten, um nicht die gesamte Unterhaltung zu stören.
Auch können Nutzer:innen über sogenannte Mitgliedslabels gruppenbezogene Informationen über sich teilen. Whatsapp hat angekündigt, die Gruppenchats „weiter verbessern“ zu wollen.

articles.title: Hackers leak details of 41,000 Homeland Security employees, exposing undercover operations and surveillance tools
articles.text:
What we know so far: Hackers have leaked login records for more than 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employees and contractors, revealing not only who works at the agency but also which surveillance and investigative tools they are cleared to use. Taken together, the files offer a rare inside look at the technology behind the department's investigations and the chain of command that directs them. The release also sharpens the debate over whether exposing the people behind federal immigration enforcement serves accountability or creates a security threat.
The transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets published the archive, which it calls "Icepick," on Wednesday. It spans DHS and seven of its component agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement and US Customs and Border Protection.
The files include email addresses, phone numbers and office addresses, along with more than 55,000 permission groups that control access to internal systems. Some group names reference Palantir's Falcon investigative platform and PenLink, which analyzes phone records and social media. Others point to tools for pulling data from seized phones, systems for reaching immigration court records, a "Title III Intercept Program" for wiretaps, a "Communications Intercept Center TechOps (CICTO) Program" and an "Illicit Sensor Intercept Program (ISIP)."
The records were last updated in August. DDoSecrets says they came from DHS' Okta login system, which Okta disputes. "We are aware of this report. Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised," a company spokesperson told Wired.
Nearly everyone in the leak belongs to at least one of these groups, and the membership lists show who holds which capabilities. At Homeland Security Investigations, ICE's investigative arm, 39 employees in more than a dozen field offices sit in groups named "CUC," which government court filings say stands for "certified undercover operation." A group that appears tied to HSI's St. Paul, Minnesota, area of operations references "Keyhole." Federal court filings describe Keyhole as a certified undercover operation that funded HSI's undercover surveillance of Minneapolis protest groups earlier this year.
More than 200 CBP accounts belong to a group referencing Mobile Fortify, the face-recognition app immigration agents use to identify people. Members include field supervisors, special response team operators and tactical and intelligence agents. More than 700 accounts, nearly all of them CBP, link to a group that appears to reference the encrypted messaging app Signal.
Other groups reference AI tools, including OpenAI's ChatGPT, Google's Gemini and Microsoft's Copilot. One, labeled "Grok.com," includes eight DHS technology officials, among them the department's former chief information officer and chief data officer.
Two more, "Executive Leadership" and "AI Access," appear to list people exempted from the DHS web filter that blocks some sites for employees. Both list the same 13 people, including former DHS head Kristi Noem; Antoine McCord, the recently departed CIO who has returned to defense tech company Anduril; Philip Hegseth, a senior adviser to the secretary and younger brother of defense secretary Pete Hegseth; and policy adviser Jayce Krachenfels. None of the four responded to requests for comment.
Most records also name a supervisor, so the data can be used to rebuild reporting lines across the department. More than 300 records belong to senior headquarters officials, including those overseeing intelligence, technology, biometrics and privacy.
Alexander Leslie, a national security expert at threat intelligence company Recorded Future, says that if the data is real and up to date, it is an extremely valuable intelligence resource for anyone trying to get inside DHS. He adds that its value grows when combined with previously stolen information, commercial data and other intelligence. He says an adversary could spend months using these connections to find vulnerable employees, convincingly impersonate staff, or compromise ongoing investigations.
A Wired analysis found CBP staff make up more than half the records. ICE accounts for about 10,000, roughly a third in HSI. US Citizenship and Immigration Services has 6,200, and nearly 1,000 are tied to the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. Together, they make up about a seventh of the DHS workforce.
The account data also tracks the buildup of enforcement. About 1,300 ICE enforcement accounts were created after July 2025, when Trump signed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which paid for 10,000 new ICE Enforcement and Removal officers by the end of 2025. Nearly 20 accounts appear to belong to Defense Department personnel, eight in a group titled "ICE Tip Line DOW Surge." About 170 accounts provide "military processing support" at ICE facilities, and 35 identify National Guard members.
DDoSecrets and the researcher and journalist Maia Arson Crimew say the files came from a group calling itself the Department of Peace. "They have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs," the hackers wrote. Crimew built a website that makes the records searchable. "I don't think we should let them scare us into not looking into them," she told Wired.
The release comes as DHS works to keep its staff out of public view. The department has sought to unmask anonymous online critics and broadened its definition of doxing to include publishing employees' names and titles. In June, 15 Minnesota residents faced stalking- and threat-related charges that prosecutors linked to activities opposing ICE.
Adam Steinbaugh, a senior attorney at the civil liberties group FIRE, says the administration has taken an expansive view of 18 USC 119, which bars sharing "restricted personal information" about federal officers with intent to threaten them. "This is information that would be on a business card," he says. "That's not something the government can criminalize."
DHS and the Justice Department did not respond to Wired. The FBI referred questions to DHS.

articles.title: SpaceX no longer needs NASA, and that's a problem for America's space agency
articles.text:
For nearly a quarter of a century, Elon Musk and his essential partner at SpaceX, Gwynne Shotwell, viewed the United States government as El Dorado, the mythical city of gold.
Like machete-wielding treasure hunters, Musk and Shotwell hacked through a tangled jungle filled with lurking carnivores such as Boeing and Lockheed Martin, as well as bean counters and regulators. Over time, against long odds, the pair cleared a path for SpaceX to contracts at NASA and the US military. They sued when things did not go their way. They hollered about unfair playing fields. Most importantly, they delivered quality space products to the US government for less.
And so, after a while, SpaceX found El Dorado and a city of contracts.
Then they started winning everything. So much so that the relationship between the customer and contractor began to change. Slowly at first, but ever more quickly, SpaceX went from needing the US government as an indispensable customer to becoming an indispensable contractor for the nation.
The pendulum has swung so far now that SpaceX seems increasingly disinterested in the US government for most contracts outside of data services, such as Starshield for military communications and observations.
“I guess I am still in denial that there is a divorce pending,” said Lori Garver, a deputy NASA administrator during the Obama White House years who was instrumental in expanding the agency’s use of commercial contracts with companies like SpaceX. “I literally cannot wrap my head around a future yet where SpaceX stops flying Dragon and Falcon. Not yet.”
But the signs point to at least a partial breakup. Consider the following data points:
- SpaceX has told NASA it will stop flying Crew Dragon, the space agency’s only reliable astronaut transportation to the International Space Station, by or before 2030. Shotwell said in September that NASA should rely instead on Boeing for astronaut transportation. “We’re just gonna let them have some business,” she said of Boeing. “They should fly their capsule. The government paid a lot of money for that.” As a result, NASA is investing more in Boeing.
- Ars reported in October that SpaceX had stopped selling commercial launches on the Falcon 9 rocket for missions after the year 2028.
- SpaceX may also still stop flying Falcon 9 for NASA missions. In late October, during a meeting of NASA’s Safety Advisory Panel, Kent Rominger said if the US Deorbit Vehicle (a modified Dragon spacecraft) launches to the International Space Station after 2030, “it may require” a rocket other than the Falcon 9.
- Politico reported last week that SpaceX told the US Space Force it would not bid on three new launch contracts in the late 2020s that would have gone above and beyond its existing commitments to the US military.
- SpaceX previously provided “Rough Order of Magnitude” estimates, or ROMs, for launch costs to US companies building small landers for NASA’s Moon Base as part of the Commercial Lunar Payload Services program. But according to three sources, SpaceX recently told these lunar companies they will not provide launch services.

articles.title: Fan-fiction site Archive of Our Own (AO3) could be offline for up to 4 weeks after security incident | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Archive of our Own (AO3), the popular site where fans publish and read stories about their favorite characters and worlds, has bad news for its community. After going offline for what was supposed to be routine overnight maintenance, the site says it could stay online for almost a whole month.
AO3 did not initially share details about what caused the outage, but published a longer statement hours after announcing that the site would likely be down for two to four weeks.
“Earlier today, we detected evidence of a security incident on AO3,” the statement reads. “We are still in the early stages of response to this security incident and determining its scope. AO3 will remain down while we continue investigating and addressing what has been found so far.”
AO3 is a project of the nonprofit Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), which relies on volunteers and donations to keep the site afloat. The site has such a passionate user base that, within two hours of the announcement that it would go offline, its status page’s posts had garnered millions of views (and much panicked commentary) across social media.
“While we currently don’t believe that the user database was stolen, we are also unable to rule it out. The AO3 database contains account information that may include your username, email address, IP address, and a hashed version of your password,” the OTW added.
Though AO3 stores user passwords by using an industry-standard hashing technique, the site recommended that as a precaution, users should change their passwords on any other sites where they may have used the same password.
Some fans may suspect this issue is related to last week’s “PHP Armageddon,” when tools from OpenAI and Google Wiz uncovered two critical flaws in PHP, the programming language that runs the behind-the-scenes software of about 70% of the internet. But AO3 is not among that majority. Instead, the site is built on a different framework (a toolkit for running websites), Ruby on Rails, so the outage is unlikely to be related.
OTW and AO3 did not reply to requests for comment.
Updated, 10/29/26, 9:45 PM ET, after OTW published a statement about the nature of the outage.

articles.title: La serie de 'Harry Potter' de HBO muestra al fin el primer vistazo del castillo de Hogwarts en su mágico póster
articles.text:
Aunque HBO ya había lanzado numerosas imágenes y avances de la nueva serie de Harry Potter, había algo que los fans llevaban muchos meses pidiendo: el castillo de Hogwarts. El escenario principal de la saga, colegio de magia y hechicería donde estudian Harry, Ron y Hermione, es uno de los enclaves más queridos por los seguidores de la franquicia. Y, por fin, hemos podido ver por primera vez cómo será esta nueva versión.
Porque ahora, a falta de dos meses para su estreno, la serie de Harry Potter de HBO ha lanzado un nuevo espectacular póster de su temporada 1, La Piedra Filosofal. En él aparece el pequeño protagonista en un primer plano. Solo le vemos la mitad de la cara, que nos deja al descubierto sus grandes ojos azules (como los de su madre), sus icónicas gafas y, por supuesto, la cicatriz con forma de rayo que le quedó tras el ataque de Voldemort.
Pero lo interesante se encuentra dentro de la propia lente de las gafas. Y es que en ella, difuminado, aparece el castillo de Hogwarts. Hasta el momento, habíamos visto fragmentos del colegio en los tráileres de la serie de Harry Potter. Pero nunca habíamos tenido un vistazo completo tan nítido como este.
El diseño de Hogwarts en la serie de Harry Potter apunta a ser muy similar al de las películas. Un enorme castillo gótico de dimensiones colosales. Con espectaculares torreones que sobresalen por todas partes, destacando una central aún más grande que el resto. Eso sí, aunque parecido, guarda varias diferencias con respecto al de la saga cinematográfica, demostrando una vez que más que, si bien guardará un profundo respeto por ellas, la serie quiere encontrar su propia identidad.
Reparto y fecha de estreno de la serie de Harry Potter
El reparto principal de la serie lo conforman Dominic McLaughlin como Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton como Hermione Granger, Alastair Stout como Ron Weasley, John Lithgow como Albus Dumbledore, Janet McTeer como Minerva McGonagall, Paapa Essiedu como Severus Snape, Nick Frost como Rubeus Hagrid, Rory Wilmot como Neville Longbottom o Lox Pratt como Draco Malfoy, entre otros muchos.
Date de alta en HBO MAX y tendrás acceso a las mejores series y películas exclusivas como The Wire, Los Soprano o Casa del Dragón. Incluye todo el catálogo de Warner, los clásicos de Cartoon Network, los grandes estrenos y el mejor deporte.
Además, se sabe que para la segunda temporada, la serie de Harry Potter contará con los fichajes de Kit Harington como Gilderoy Lockhart, Bonnie Hill como Ginny Weasley, Lenny Rush como Dobby, Billy Barratt como Tom Ryddle, Rafe Spall como Arthur Weasley, Molly Hewitt-Richards como Myrtle la Llorona y Jasper Ambrose como Colin Creevey.

articles.title: Staff Phones on the Company Network: Setting Up Bring Your Own Device Without the Headaches - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Introduction to BYOD in the Modern Workplace
The Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) trend has fundamentally transformed how organizations approach their communications and IT infrastructure. By allowing employees to use personal smartphones and other mobile devices on the company network, businesses can offer greater flexibility and potentially boost workforce productivity. However, this integration also introduces a host of challenges that, if not properly addressed, can lead to security vulnerabilities, compliance issues, and operational inefficiencies. This article explores effective strategies for setting up staff phones on the company network, focusing on how to implement BYOD programs while avoiding the common pitfalls that many organizations face.
Why BYOD Matters for Businesses Today
The adoption of BYOD is no longer an emerging trend; it has become a mainstream practice across industries worldwide. Recent studies indicate that over 70% of employees use their own devices to perform work-related tasks. This shift is driven by several factors, including employee preference for familiar technology, the rise of remote and hybrid work models, and the potential for significant cost savings on company hardware expenditures.
BYOD programs can enable more agile workflows by allowing employees to access corporate resources anytime and anywhere. However, this flexibility can come at a price if not carefully managed. Without appropriate safeguards, personal devices can become entry points for cyberattacks, data leaks, and unauthorized access to sensitive company information. Consequently, businesses must develop robust IT policies and secure network architectures that protect corporate assets while supporting employee mobility.
Starting Strong: Deploying BYOD with Expert Support
Launching a BYOD initiative requires more than just allowing devices on the network; it demands a strategic approach supported by expert guidance. Attentus’s managed IT deployment provides comprehensive solutions that help organizations manage device integration seamlessly. Their services include device onboarding, security policy enforcement, and continuous monitoring to mitigate risks associated with personal devices accessing corporate systems.
Partnering with experienced IT service providers ensures that businesses maintain control over network access and data security without stifling employee flexibility. These experts can also assist in navigating complex compliance requirements, such as GDPR or HIPAA, which may apply depending on the industry or geographic location. By leveraging their expertise, companies can avoid common mistakes that lead to costly data breaches or operational disruptions.
Choosing the Right Provider for Your BYOD Strategy
Selecting a trusted provider like Link High is a critical step toward a successful BYOD rollout. Such providers specialize in offering tailored IT management services that address the unique challenges posed by BYOD environments. These challenges include managing diverse device types and operating systems, enforcing security policies consistently, and ensuring network performance remains optimal despite increased device load.
A capable provider will implement device management platforms, such as Mobile Device Management (MDM) or Enterprise Mobility Management (EMM) solutions, that enable centralized control over personal devices. They can also establish network segmentation practices to isolate BYOD traffic from sensitive corporate resources, reducing the risk of lateral movement by attackers in case of device compromise.
Moreover, providers bring valuable insights into user training and policy development, helping organizations foster a culture of security awareness among employees. This holistic approach ensures that the BYOD program supports business goals without becoming a source of headaches for IT teams.
Key Considerations When Integrating Staff Phones
Before permitting personal devices on the company network, organizations must carefully consider several critical factors to ensure security, compliance, and operational efficiency.
Security and Compliance
Security remains the foremost concern when integrating staff phones into corporate networks. Deploying Mobile Device Management (MDM) solutions is essential to enforce encryption, implement remote wipe capabilities, and control app installations on personal devices. These measures help protect sensitive data in case devices are lost or stolen.
Statistics reveal that 59% of businesses have experienced mobile security incidents linked to BYOD devices. This underscores the importance of rigorous security controls and constant vigilance. Compliance with industry regulations such as GDPR, HIPAA, or PCI-DSS also requires careful handling of personal devices accessing protected data.
Network Segmentation
To minimize risk, organizations should separate personal devices from critical business systems through network segmentation. Establishing dedicated VLANs or guest networks specifically for BYOD devices confines potential threats and prevents unauthorized access to sensitive company data.
Network segmentation not only enhances security but also improves performance by managing traffic flow and reducing congestion on core corporate networks. It allows IT teams to apply tailored security policies and monitor BYOD activity more effectively.
Clear Usage Policies
Developing clear, comprehensive usage policies is vital to set employee expectations and responsibilities regarding personal device use on company networks. Policies should outline acceptable use, data privacy guidelines, and consequences for non-compliance.
Effective policies encourage employees to adhere to security best practices, such as using strong passwords, avoiding unsecured Wi-Fi networks, and reporting lost or stolen devices promptly. They also help reduce legal risks by clarifying data ownership and privacy boundaries.
Technical Steps to Enable BYOD on Your Network
Implementing a BYOD program without headaches involves a series of technical best practices designed to secure and optimize network access.
- Inventory and Compatibility Checks: Conduct an audit to understand the types of devices employees intend to use and verify their compatibility with existing network infrastructure. This helps prevent connectivity issues and ensures that security tools support all device platforms.
- Access Controls: Implement strong authentication protocols such as WPA3 for Wi-Fi access, and consider using digital certificates or VPNs to secure connections between personal devices and corporate resources. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) adds an additional layer of protection against unauthorized access.
- Regular Updates and Monitoring: Continuously monitor device activity on the network to detect anomalies or suspicious behavior. Push security updates and patches promptly to all managed devices to close vulnerabilities before they can be exploited.
- User Training: Educate employees about security risks associated with BYOD and provide guidelines on safe device usage. Training reduces human error, which is often the weakest link in cybersecurity.
Benefits of a Well-Managed BYOD Program
When properly executed, BYOD initiatives can deliver substantial benefits to organizations. A study found that companies with effective BYOD strategies reported a 20% increase in employee productivity and a 15% reduction in IT expenses. This productivity boost is often attributed to employees’ comfort and familiarity with their own devices, which can lead to faster task completion and improved communication.
Additionally, BYOD reduces the need for organizations to invest heavily in purchasing and maintaining hardware, lowering operational costs. It also supports flexible work arrangements, enabling employees to work remotely or on the go without disruption.
However, these benefits are contingent on effective management practices and security controls. Without them, BYOD can become a liability rather than an asset.
Overcoming Common BYOD Challenges
Despite its advantages, BYOD programs can face hurdles that need proactive management.
– Device Diversity: Supporting a wide range of device types, operating systems, and versions can strain IT resources. Standardizing minimum requirements and using cross-platform management tools can alleviate this issue.
– Data Privacy Concerns: Employees may worry about their personal data being accessed or monitored by the company. Transparent policies and privacy-respecting management solutions help build trust.
– Network Performance: Increased device connectivity can lead to bandwidth congestion. Network upgrades and segmentation help maintain performance levels.
– Legal and Compliance Risks: Failure to comply with data protection laws can result in hefty fines. Regular audits and adherence to regulatory frameworks are essential.
Addressing these challenges through strategic planning and expert support ensures that BYOD programs run smoothly and securely.
Conclusion: Balancing Flexibility and Security
The integration of staff phones into the company network via Bring Your Own Device initiatives represents a strategic opportunity to enhance workforce agility and reduce costs. However, successful implementation demands a delicate balance between flexibility and security. Engaging with specialized providers and adopting comprehensive policies are critical steps to ensure smooth deployment and sustained network integrity.
By following best practices such as employing Mobile Device Management solutions, enforcing network segmentation, and providing user training, businesses can mitigate risks associated with personal devices. Moreover, leveraging expert support from trusted partners helps navigate technical complexities and compliance requirements.
Ultimately, a well-managed BYOD program empowers organizations to capitalize on the benefits of employee-owned devices without the headaches-driving productivity, cost savings, and competitive advantage in today’s dynamic business environment.

articles.title: "Un véritable génie" : Poutine encense Elon Musk, et c’est tout sauf anodin
articles.text:
Vladimir Poutine a publiquement encensé Elon Musk, quelques jours seulement après le fiasco de Starlink en Ukraine. Un éloge qui ne passe pas inaperçu.
Poutine complimente Musk
Ainsi, Vladimir Poutine a assuré tout mettre en œuvre avec l’entreprise américaine pour éviter les collisions en orbite, rapporte la BBC. Un sujet brûlant alors que SpaceX publiait, il y a quelques jours, un long billet de blog dénonçant les agissements de certains opérateurs.
Il a aussi laissé entendre qu’il s’entretenait régulièrement avec l’homme le plus riche du monde : » Nous sommes en contact étroit avec nos partenaires américains, dont Mr Musk », a-t-il affirmé. Mais ce n’est pas tout, et le président russe n’a certainement pas manqué de compliments pour décrire l’entrepreneur : « C’est un génie, un vrai génie », a-t-il lancé.
Il a insisté sur l’importance de ce dialogue, qui doit permettre que les satellites de Rassvet et de Starlink n’« interfèrent pas entre eux en orbite ». « Nous et nos partenaires américains y accordons de la valeur de part et d’autre, et malgré toutes les questions politiques, nous travaillons dur », a-t-il poursuivi.
L’ambassade de Russie en Afrique du Sud a ensuite confirmé que » la Russie entretient des contacts étroits avec les États-Unis dans le domaine spatial, y compris avec Elon Musk ».
Les États-Unis se rapprochent de la Russie
Ces mots résonnent d’autant plus fort qu’ils arrivent peu après le bridage de Starlink en Ukraine, que Musk aurait lui-même commandité. Kiev a en effet vu ses connexions militaires brutalement dégradées, l’empêchant de manœuvrer ses drones intercepteurs. Voir le patron de SpaceX couvert d’éloges par le chef du Kremlin quelques jours plus tard n’a rien d’anodin.
Car en toile de fond, on assiste à un rapprochement clair entre Donald Trump et Vladimir Poutine. Le président américain a, par exemple, annoncé un accord avec Moscou pour importer du diesel, afin de faire baisser des prix de l’énergie qui flambent depuis la guerre avec l’Iran. Il a ensuite suspendu de lourdes sanctions contre la Russie qui devaient entrer en vigueur.
Si ce virage fait clairement grincer des dents aux États-Unis, il marque de profonds changements dans les relations internationales. Flatter Musk dans ce contexte en dit long, puisqu’il est aussi question d’un partenaire privilégié de la Maison-Blanche et surtout, du plus important soutien financier du président.

articles.title: Réservations d’hôtel, identité des accompagnants, documents personnels : ces deux éditeurs français de logiciels ont été piratés à quelques jours d’intervalle
articles.text:
C’est à travers le mail d’un hôtel situé près de Paris que l’alerte nous est remontée.
Dans ce message adressé à ses clients le 29 octobre 2026, l’établissement expliquait que deux incidents de sécurité « distincts et indépendants l’un de l’autre » avaient touché deux de ses prestataires techniques, et que certaines données personnelles liées aux réservations faites dans l’établissement étaient concernées.
Deux logiciels y sont pointés du doigt. Le premier est D-EDGE, qui fournit le moteur permettant de réserver directement sur le site de l’hôtel. Le second est Misterbooking, l’outil de gestion des réservations et des séjours édité par Septeo Hospitality. Deux entreprises françaises qui occupent une place centrale dans la chaîne technique de l’hôtellerie, ce qui laisse penser que l’établissement à l’origine du mail est loin d’être le seul concerné.
À la publication de cet article, ni D-EDGE ni Septeo n’avaient répondu à nos sollicitations.
Ce que l’on sait de l’incident chez D-EDGE
D’après le mail de l’hôtel, une faille due à un défaut de configuration chez D-EDGE a permis à des tiers malveillants d’accéder à des données de réservation les 20 et 21 octobre 2026. L’entreprise n’a prévenu l’établissement que le 23 octobre. Les informations exposées comprennent :
- les noms et prénoms des clients
- les dates et la référence de leur réservation
- le nombre de personnes
- le montant du séjour et le nom de l’hôtel
- et pour certaines réservations l’adresse e-mail et le numéro de téléphone.
Le nombre d’établissements touchés n’a pas été communiqué, mais le périmètre potentiel est large. D-EDGE se présente comme un éditeur de solutions cloud de commerce en ligne utilisées par plus de 17 000 hôtels dans plus de 150 pays.
Ce que l’on sait de l’attaque contre Misterbooking
L’incident chez Misterbooking relève quant à lui d’une intrusion. L’éditeur Septeo Hospitality a détecté le 19 octobre qu’un tiers malveillant avait obtenu un accès illégitime à l’un des serveurs du logiciel, et l’hôtel précise dans son mail que « l’attaquant a pu extraire une partie des données » avant que l’accès ne soit coupé, dans la matinée du même jour.
Dans une note publiée le 23 octobre à destination de ses adhérents, le GHR, organisation professionnelle de l’hôtellerie-restauration, se montre moins rassurant et évoque l’extraction d’une « partie significative » des données enregistrées.
Les données concernées sont plus sensibles que dans le cas de D-EDGE, puisqu’elles incluent :
- l’identité et les coordonnées des clients et de leurs accompagnants
- les informations de réservation et les documents joints aux dossiers clients
L’ampleur reste inconnue, l’hôtel indiquant lui-même ne pas encore connaître la nature exacte ni le volume des données qui le concernent. Pour mesurer l’enjeu, Misterbooking est utilisé par 1 800 établissements, et son rachat a porté Septeo Hospitality à 4 000 hôtels équipés en France, en Espagne et dans d’autres pays européens.
Méfiez-vous des messages trop bien renseignés
Si aucune donnée complète de carte bancaire ne serait concernée par ces deux incidents, ces fuites laissent présager des vagues d’arnaques très crédibles.
Le scénario s’est déjà produit ce mois-ci, après le piratage de Medialog, un autre éditeur français de logiciels hôteliers, puisque des clients d’hôtels ont été ciblés sur WhatsApp et par mail avec leurs véritables informations de réservation, notamment leur nom, l’établissement et les dates de séjour.
Pour rappel, un message qui cite votre numéro de réservation, vos dates et le montant de votre séjour n’est donc plus une preuve d’authenticité. S’il vous demande de confirmer votre carte bancaire, de régler un acompte ou de cliquer sur un lien pour éviter une annulation, ne répondez pas et appelez l’hôtel au numéro affiché sur son site officiel ou sur votre confirmation d’origine.

articles.title: African food-tech startups invited to apply for FoodTech 500 2026 - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
African startups working at the intersection of food, technology and sustainability are invited to apply for the 2026 edition of the FoodTech 500.
Run by Forward Fooding and inspired by the Fortune 500, the FoodTech 500 bills itself as the world’s first definitive list of global entrepreneurial talent in the food-tech space. The list ranks international startups and scaleups using a unique methodology that assesses their business size, digital footprint and sustainability practices.
The opportunity is global, meaning African companies are eligible to apply alongside peers from all other regions. It is open to businesses at all stages, from early-stage startups to more established scaleups.
To qualify, applicants must meet three baseline requirements: they must be incorporated, have an active website, and be less than 15 years old.
Applications are open here until November 15.

articles.title: 7 Things emotionally intelligent people do differently
articles.text:
7 Things emotionally intelligent people do differently
Discover seven things emotionally intelligent people do differently to manage emotions, communicate better, and build healthier relationships.
Emotional intelligence is not about staying calm all the time or knowing exactly what to say in every situation. It is about understanding your emotions, recognising how others feel, and choosing how to respond rather than reacting impulsively.
In everyday life, emotional intelligence can influence how we handle disagreements, build relationships, respond to criticism, and navigate difficult situations. People who develop this skill are often better equipped to communicate clearly, understand different perspectives, and manage their emotions constructively.
The good news is that emotional intelligence is not simply something you are born with. Many of its essential skills can be practised and strengthened over time.
7 Things emotionally intelligent people do differently
1. They pause before reacting
When someone criticises them, disagrees with them, or says something hurtful, emotionally intelligent people try not to respond immediately out of anger.
They understand that an emotional reaction can sometimes make a difficult situation worse. Instead of sending an impulsive message or saying something they might regret, they give themselves time to process what happened.
For example, if a colleague points out a mistake, they may initially feel embarrassed or defensive. Rather than immediately arguing, they consider whether the feedback is useful and how they can respond constructively.
Pausing does not mean ignoring your emotions or pretending that nothing bothers you. It means allowing yourself to feel an emotion without letting it make every decision for you.
The lesson: You cannot always control what you feel, but you can practise choosing how you respond.
2. They try to understand before judging
Emotionally intelligent people recognise that their perspective is not the only possible explanation for a situation.
When someone behaves unexpectedly, they try to understand the circumstances before making assumptions about their intentions.
For instance, if a friend takes hours to reply to a message, it is easy to assume that they are losing interest or deliberately ignoring you. However, they might be dealing with work, family responsibilities, or something they have not shared.
Instead of immediately jumping to conclusions, emotionally intelligent people leave room for other explanations and communicate when clarification is needed.
This does not mean excusing repeated disrespect or ignoring unhealthy behaviour. It means distinguishing between what you know and what you are assuming.
The lesson: Understanding another person's perspective can prevent unnecessary misunderstandings and help you respond more fairly.
3. They can admit when they are wrong
Admitting a mistake is not always easy. It can challenge your pride, make you feel uncomfortable, or force you to reconsider something you strongly believed.
However, emotionally intelligent people understand that being wrong does not make them less valuable.
When they hurt someone, misunderstand a situation, or make a poor decision, they try to acknowledge their role instead of shifting all the blame onto others.
A genuine apology involves more than saying, "I'm sorry you felt that way." It means recognising the impact of your actions, taking responsibility where appropriate, and making an effort to behave differently.
They also understand that an apology does not automatically entitle them to forgiveness. Rebuilding trust often requires consistent actions over time.
The lesson: Taking responsibility for your mistakes is a sign of self-awareness, not weakness.
4. They set boundaries without feeling obligated to explain everything
Emotionally intelligent people understand that being considerate does not mean making themselves available to everyone at all times.
They recognise their limits and communicate them clearly. If they are exhausted, overwhelmed, or unable to take on another responsibility, they can say no without turning the decision into a lengthy justification.
For example, they might tell a friend, "I care about you, but I don't have the energy for a conversation tonight. Can we talk tomorrow?"
This approach respects both their own needs and the other person's feelings.
Healthy boundaries also apply to work, family expectations, personal time, and emotional availability. They help people maintain relationships without constantly ignoring their own well-being.
Setting boundaries does not mean becoming selfish or indifferent. It means understanding that care and availability are not the same thing.
The lesson: You can care about other people without taking responsibility for every expectation they have of you.
5. They listen to understand, not just to reply
In many conversations, people spend more time preparing their responses than listening to what the other person is saying.
Emotionally intelligent people try to avoid this habit. They pay attention to the speaker's words, ask questions when something is unclear, and consider the feelings behind the message.
For example, when a friend talks about a difficult day, they do not immediately offer advice or compare the experience with their own. They might first ask, "Do you want me to help you figure it out, or do you just need someone to listen?"
This simple question can make conversations more supportive because it acknowledges that different people need different kinds of help.
Active listening also involves noticing when your assumptions are influencing your interpretation of what someone says.
The lesson: Sometimes, the most helpful response is not advice but the willingness to listen without rushing to fix everything.
6. They do not depend on everyone's approval
Emotionally intelligent people care about their relationships, but they do not treat universal approval as a requirement for feeling secure.
They understand that people have different expectations, values, and opinions. As a result, not everyone will agree with their choices, and that disagreement does not automatically mean they have done something wrong.
For instance, choosing a different career path, declining an invitation, or expressing an unpopular opinion may disappoint someone. Emotionally intelligent people can consider that person's perspective without automatically abandoning their own judgement.
They remain open to constructive criticism while recognising that criticism is not always accurate or fair.
This balance helps them make decisions based on their values rather than constantly changing themselves to avoid disappointing others.
The lesson: You can value other people's opinions without allowing those opinions to define your self-worth.
7. They recognise that other people's emotions are not always their responsibility
Emotionally intelligent people can show empathy without assuming they must fix every uncomfortable feeling another person experiences.
They understand the difference between supporting someone and taking complete responsibility for that person's emotional state.
For example, if they respectfully decline a request and the other person becomes disappointed, they can acknowledge that disappointment without automatically reversing their decision.
Similarly, if a friend is upset, they can offer support while recognising that they cannot control how the friend processes the situation.
This does not mean ignoring the consequences of their own actions. If they have caused harm, taking responsibility matters. The distinction is between being accountable for your behaviour and trying to manage every emotion someone else feels.
Learning this difference can make relationships healthier and reduce the pressure to keep everyone happy.
The lesson: Empathy means caring about how others feel, not believing you must control how they feel.
Final thoughts
Emotional intelligence is often reflected in small, everyday decisions: pausing before responding, listening without interrupting, admitting mistakes, and setting boundaries respectfully.
These behaviours do not mean emotionally intelligent people never feel jealous, angry, insecure, or overwhelmed. They experience difficult emotions like everyone else. The difference is that they can gradually learn to recognise those emotions and respond to them more thoughtfully.
You do not have to master all seven habits at once. Start by noticing one situation in which you tend to react impulsively, seek approval, or struggle to express your needs.
With practice, greater self-awareness and more thoughtful communication can help you build healthier relationships with both yourself and the people around you.

articles.title: Râper directement dans le plat : le robot Kenwood MultiPro Express est à 119,90 €
articles.text:
Le robot multifonction Kenwood MultiPro Express de 3 litres est à 119,90 € (-24 %)
Avec son bol de 3 litres, son blender et son système de découpe directement dans le plat, le Kenwood MultiPro Express passe sous les 120 € chez Amazon.
Amazon propose le robot multifonction Kenwood MultiPro Express FDP65.590SI à 119,90 €, contre 158,35 € auparavant, également affichés comme le plus bas prix des 30 derniers jours. L’économie atteint 38,45 €, soit environ 24 %. L’appareil est vendu et expédié par Amazon, avec la livraison gratuite.
Un bol de 3 litres et une découpe à l’extérieur
Le robot multifonction Kenwood MultiPro Express associe un moteur de 1 000 W à un bol de 3 litres. Son sélecteur propose deux vitesses et une fonction Pulse pour travailler par impulsions, notamment afin de contrôler la texture d’un hachage.
Le couvercle Express Serve permet de râper ou d’émincer directement dans une assiette ou un saladier placé à côté. Pour préparer davantage de légumes, il évite ainsi de devoir vider régulièrement le bol principal.
Un blender et plusieurs accessoires de préparation
Un blender de 1,5 litre complète l’ensemble pour les préparations mixées. Deux disques de préparation, une lame, un pétrin, un presse-agrumes et un émulsionneur sont également annoncés. Cette combinaison couvre plusieurs tâches courantes sans multiplier les bases motorisées sur le plan de travail.
Il s’agit toutefois d’un robot de préparation, sans fonction de cuisson : il ne remplace donc pas un robot cuiseur. Sur Amazon, le produit affiche une moyenne de 4,3/5 sur 311 évaluations.

articles.title: Si la pregunta es si es legal un ERE que sustituya a trabajadores por IA, una sentencia del TSJ de Madrid la responde: depende
articles.text:
El debate (y la amenaza) sobre el impacto de la IA el mercado laboral está cada vez más presente y de forma transversal a cada vez más sectores. Una de las dudas que se planteaban muchas personas es si la adopción de la IA sería una causa válida para justificar un ERE que termine de un plumazo con varias decenas de puestos de trabajo. La Sala de lo Social del Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Madrid acaba de resolverlo en una sentencia que deja muchas puertas abiertas.
La sentencia del TSJ de Madrid sobre un ERE que se aplicó en un estudio de desarrollo de videojuegos es la primera en abordar la implantación de la IA como argumento para despedir a algunos de sus trabajadores, aunque hay importantes matices en esa decisión.
Lo que se juzgó de verdad. La sentencia 864/2026 del TSJM, del pasado 8 de octubre, resuelve el recurso de una guionista que consideraba que su despido (en el marco de un ERE) debía considerarse como nulo. Un juzgado de instrucción ya había declarado previamente ese despido como improcedente y pedía la nulidad y daños morales para ella. En su carta de despido no se mencionaba a la IA como motivo para justificar el despido.
Por otro lado, una modeladora de gráficos 3D que trabajaba para el mismo estudio y estaba sujeta al mismo ERE, recibió una carta de despido en la que sí se citaba la IA, pero el juzgado de instrucción ya había declarado como procedente su despido. El TSJ de Madrid no examinó este último despido que no había sido recurrido y se cerró como procedente. Es decir, en este segundo caso, la justicia sí veía la implementación de la IA como un justificado para despedir a la empleada porque se estaban cambiando los modelos de producción y eso reducía el número de empleados que la empresa necesitaba.
La carta que cita la IA. La carta de despido de la modeladora mencionaba que la IA mejoraba la calidad visual y "permite ser más ágiles y eficientes". Por eso bastaban dos artistas 3D sénior y su puesto desaparecía. La empresa alegó causas económicas, técnicas, productivas y organizativas, pero la carta se apoya, sobre todo, en las económicas y las productivas. No en las técnicas que habría dejado la petición en el límite para considerarla improcedente.
El artículo 51 del Estatuto de los Trabajadores en el que se regulan las causas de despidos colectivos, se marca una diferencia importante entre las causas. La técnica toca los medios de producción, la organizativa los métodos de trabajo y la productiva la demanda de productos. Encajar la IA es discutible, porque la carta de despido de la modeladora 3D hablaba de un "cambio en la forma de trabajar". Es decir, una causa productiva, no de una nueva herramienta en sí misma, que sería una causa técnica. De hecho, la Inspección de Trabajo aceptó las causas económicas, organizativas y productivas.
Bancarrota y cambio en los pedidos. La empresa justificó muy bien esa prioridad por las causas económicas, organizativas y productivas, y no presentó la implantación del uso de la IA como una causa directa, sino como una consecuencia impuesta por sus clientes.
La empresa se encontraba en una situación económica límite y pasó de ganar 646.297 euros en 2023 a perder 3.546.027 euros en 2024. Su cifra de negocio cayó de 7,99 a 4,60 millones. De hecho, en octubre de 2024, comunicó su insolvencia a un juzgado de Madrid y, como consecuencia de ello, presentó un ERE que afectó a 13 de sus 83 trabajadores.
En la sentencia se recoge que la empresa alegó que: "la utilización de imágenes generadas por inteligencia artificial impacta en un doble aspecto. Por un lado, mejora la calidad visual de nuestros productos y, con ello, mejora la valoración por parte de los usuarios y, por otro lado, permite ser más ágiles y eficientes ya que la inversión de tiempo necesaria por escena es mucho menor, por lo que, desde un punto de vista estratégico, se hace necesaria la implementación de un nuevo proceso de producción basado en el uso de Inteligencia Artificial (IA)". Es decir, no es el uso de IA lo que causa el despido, sino el cambio de procesos productivos orientados a que la empresa sea viable económicamente. Aunque esto implique usar IA.
Por sí misma la IA no justifica el despido. El matiz que introduce el TSJM es importante, porque contextualiza el papel de la IA en la decisión de las causas del despido y su presencia no vincula la improcedencia o no de los despidos, sino que la vincula a las razones de su implantación.
Una sentencia del Tribunal de Instancia de Bilbao declaró improcedente el despido de un empleado cuyo puesto había sido sustituido por una IA, sin que en esa decisión hubieran incurrido otros motivos económicos u organizativos. Es decir, sustituir sin más a los empleados por una IA, puede costar muy caro a las empresas, a no ser que el motivo de despido no sea la sustitución directa por una IA, sino un cambio completo del modelo productivo o por motivos económicos que obliguen a cambiar ese modelo.

articles.title: Hackers exploit Cisco SD-WAN flaw to deploy custom KeyDrift malware
articles.text:
A newly identified advanced persistent threat (APT) group tracked as UAT-11473 was observed exploiting CVE-2026-20127, an authentication-bypass flaw in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controllers, to deploy a custom malware framework called KeyDrift.
CVE-2026-20127 is a max-severity flaw that Cisco patched in February 2026, which allows remote attackers to gain privileged access to Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager and add rogue peers.
UAT-8616 has exploited the vulnerability as a zero-day since at least 2023, and recent research also linked its exploitation to the Chinese Volt Typhoon state-sponsored hacking group.
According to Cisco Talos researchers who reported on the activity, the UAT-11473 threat cluster appears to overlap with Volt Typhoon’s "Silent Train" covert access network, but they made no definitive links.
In a report Lumen released yesterday, researchers revealed that the Silent Train framework allowed Volt Typhoon to evade detection while conducting zero-day vulnerability attacks.
Deploying KeyDrift
The attacks Cisco researchers observed targeted space and satellite services, defense and aerospace technology, and policy research organizations, using the KeyDrift malware, which is a custom malware framework designed to operate on Cisco SD-WAN controller instances.
"Talos assesses with high confidence that the framework is designed to provide long-term persistent access and automated exfiltration of sensitive keying material," explained Cisco Talos.
"KeyDrift operates inside SD-WAN control-plane processes and is capable of intercepting decrypted control traffic, extracting control-session metadata and data-plane keying material, and staging or transmitting the collected material using encrypted records."
KeyDrift has two primary components, PolyFlame and LittleFilch, for which Talos saw signs of ongoing development, including new anti-debugging mechanisms and varied process impersonation.
PolyFlame runs inside legitimate vdaemon processes using modified service startup scripts and an injector for deployment.
It supports command execution through a TinyShell-styled component, file uploads and downloads, and relaying communications between an attacker’s command-and-control (C2) server and multiple peers.
LittleFilch is a control-session interception module that hooks SSL_read to inspect control-plane messages after they have been decrypted inside the controller.
For predefined edge nodes, it extracts IP identifiers and a 32-byte field that Talos assesses to be AES-256 IPsec data-plane key material.
It uses RSA encryption to protect the collected information, saves it to /var/tmp/vdaemon.bin, and then transmits it over UDP to the attackers.
Talos believes with high confidence that KeyDrift is designed to maintain persistent access to Cisco SD-WAN controllers, intercept control-plane traffic, extract cryptographic keys, and securely stage or exfiltrate the stolen data.
Cisco recommends that system administrators apply the available security updates for CVE-2026-20127 and also consult the vendor’s dedicated hardening guide for Catalyst SD-WAN deployments.

articles.text:
Ce 28 octobre 2026, Apple a dévoilé son premier MacBook Pro équipé d’un écran OLED tactile. Si les prix des différents modèles vous paraissent élevés, attendez de voir celui du modèle qui présente la configuration maximale. Dans les années à venir, l’entreprise à la pomme vendra-t-elle des produits dont le prix dépassera les 20 000 euros ? Autant dire que cette hypothèse ne semble pas dénuée de sens.
Un MacBook Pro 16 pouces vendu à 16 264 €
Les prix des MacBook Pro 16 pouces OLED avec écran tactile varient bien entendu en fonction de leur configuration. Ainsi le modèle avec une puce M5 Pro, 24 Go de RAM et 1 To de stockage est proposé à 3 899 euros (soit « le moins cher » de la gamme). Le modèle avec une puce M5 Max, 48 Go de RAM et 2 To de stockage affiche quant à lui le tarif de 6 199 euros. Autant dire que nous sommes déjà sur des tarifs assez élevés.
Mais Apple propose également sur son site français la configuration maximale pour le MacBook Pro 16 pouces : puce M5 Max avec GPU 40 cœurs, 128 gigaoctets de mémoire, 16 téraoctets de stockage et verre d’écran nano-texturé. Son prix ? 16 264 euros, soit le MacBook le plus cher jamais vendu par la firme. Comme le souligne MacGeneration, 7 700 euros sur les 16 264 euros servent uniquement à passer de 2 à 16 téraoctets de stockage. Ce n’est donc pas moins de 47 % du prix total qui est consacré au stockage. Le reste du prix correspond au passage à 128 gigaoctets de mémoire et au verre nano-texturé.
Pour rappel, les nouveaux MacBook Pro 14 pouces et 16 pouces avec écran OLED tactile sont disponibles en précommande dès maintenant. Les livraisons commenceront à partir du 6 novembre prochain. Une chose est sûre : le modèle 16 téraoctets de stockage ne risque pas de se vendre comme des petits pains.
Les prix des prochains MacBook Pro s’annoncent très élevés
Autant dire que les tarifs exorbitants de ces MacBook Pro OLED tactiles ont de quoi inquiéter pour la suite. Nous vous en parlions en juillet dernier, Apple pourrait lancer le produit le plus cher de son histoire en 2028, avec un Mac Studio équipé de la puce M7 Ultra dédiée à l’IA.
De son côté, le toujours très bien informé Mark Gurman, journaliste chez Bloomberg, a annoncé qu’Apple prépare des MacBook Pro tactiles équipés des puces M7 Pro et M7 Max pour l’automne 2027. Si le prix du MacBook Pro tactile de 16 pouces, doté de 16 téraoctets de stockage, dépasse déjà les 15 000 euros, quel prix pourrait atteindre un MacBook Pro équipé de la puce M7 Max ? Autant dire que nous craignons le pire, la crise mondiale de la mémoire ne semblant pas se terminer de sitôt.
