articles.title: OPINION: Your product is no longer a competitive advantage | EU-Startups
articles.text:
A friend of mine runs a company that builds software for other companies. He has the same problem in most sales meetings. He shows what the system can do, the prospect leans forward and asks how it works, and my friend, who is not daft, goes slightly vague. If he explains it properly, they might go away and build it themselves.
Some of them go away and build it anyway. About a year later, a fair number rang back and asked for help.
So there is still money in knowing how to make something work. What AI has done is make the gap between a clever demo and a defensible company rather uncomfortable to look at. The tools that let your team build sophisticated software cheaply let a competitor rebuild it cheaply too, and your customers can have a go over a long weekend. The development bill has come down for everyone. That includes the people trying to put you out of business.
Your supplier has a product team too
In my previous article, I asked what would happen to a startup if its model disappeared tomorrow. There is a quieter version of that dependency. The supplier carries on answering your API calls and starts selling what you sell.
On 24 February, Anthropic released finance plugins for Claude covering equity research, investment banking, private equity and wealth management, with workflows that run across Excel and PowerPoint. If you were selling an AI equity research assistant on 23 February, you had a new slide to write for your next board meeting.
Figma had it worse. On 17 February, it announced an integration with Claude Code, letting interfaces built in Claude drop straight onto the Figma canvas. On 17 April, Anthropic launched Claude Design, which produces interface mockups and interactive prototypes. Three days earlier, Anthropic’s chief product officer had stepped down from Figma’s board, which, in hindsight, was something of a hint. Figma’s shares fell 7% on launch day. Presumably the next partnership meeting had a slightly different atmosphere.
You may also be using that provider’s tools to build the product it is about to replace. I wouldn’t hold that against anyone. I would just keep it in mind.
Somebody else’s high street
In February 2025, Chegg, which sells homework help to students, reported that its non-subscriber traffic for January was down 49%, against a decline of 8% in the second quarter of 2024. It blamed Google’s AI Overviews for answering the questions that used to send students to its site, and sued Google that same week. That is Chegg’s account, and Google disputes it. The shape of the problem reaches well beyond homework.
The platform that sends customers to your door can start answering their questions on the doorstep. You still have a website. Fewer people have a reason to visit it.
Before anyone talks about a moat, it is worth checking how much of the surrounding land you actually own.
Six months used to be a moat
A feature that once took six months of engineering may now take a fraction of that. Marvellous, until you realise those six months were most of what kept the competition out.
Customers do the same sum. Some will decide their own developers can rebuild enough of your product in-house. They will underestimate the maintenance and the awkward exceptions, as my friend’s returning clients did. Their attempt still costs him a year of sales, and he doesn’t get the year back when they ring.
So where is the moat?
It starts with knowing how to get a better result. It deepens with the things you learn that a competitor can’t pick up by watching your demo.
Take my own industry. Getting an AI to produce a plausible trade recommendation is easy to show on stage. Getting software to behave inside a broker’s real trading infrastructure is another matter. Permissions have to hold when an instruction is ambiguous; someone has to reconcile the books when a transaction fails halfway through. None of this appears in the sales presentation. It turns up in the third week of production, usually on a Monday.
A competitor can copy your screen without knowing how you handle any of that. A customer can build a prototype without ever finding out why your production version took so long.
Proprietary data helps, provided you actually have the rights to use it. A pile of public documents anyone can download offers rather less protection. Calling it a knowledge base does not make it yours.
The test is simple enough. If someone offered your visible features at half the price, would your customers stay? “We shipped first” is not an answer.
Make sure you can change the engine
Whatever the advantage is, it has to survive a change of model.
Founders should know what they would run instead of their current provider, and whether it is good enough on their customers’ actual work. Benchmarks are not customers. For some applications, an open-weight model hosted in-house is the sensible answer.
Buying a server does not give you a moat. It does stop a supplier’s product roadmap from closing your company.
If switching providers would strip out everything your customers value, then the valuable part was never yours. You were renting it.
Whose moat does regulation dig?
This is also why I am skeptical of calls for an AI slowdown. A voluntary pause is hard to hold when competitors keep building and customers can leave. The data centres still need paying for.
Regulation can do something a voluntary pause can’t. It can make getting in more expensive.
A large provider spreads the cost of compliance across a business that already exists. A startup has to find that money before it has much revenue. Rules that make independent models prohibitively expensive would leave smaller companies even more dependent on the suppliers already eating into their margins.
There are good reasons to regulate AI. But when the biggest providers ask for more rules, I’d like to know who can afford to follow them. A requirement their legal department absorbs before lunch may be enough to stop a smaller competitor getting funded at all.
Europe’s AI Act makes some allowances for this, including exemptions for certain open-source models. Much depends on the detail. Writing rules that only the largest companies can afford to follow is an excellent way of keeping them the largest companies.
What they were paying for
Founders should assume cheaper development means more competition. The defence has to be something that grows every time you serve a customer and is still standing after the next model release.
Clients came back because copying the idea was easier than delivering the result. AI made their first attempt cheaper. It did not give them the vendor’s experience. They saved on development and spent a year finding out what they had been paying for.
The pattern is familiar. An internal team looks at a vendor’s product and concludes it could be rebuilt in a couple of sprints. Occasionally, it can. More often, the organisation pays for the lesson twice: once in the build, and again in the operational gaps that only appear in production.

articles.title: Samsung-Smartphone bei Aldi: Wie gut ist dieses Discounter-Angebot?
articles.text:
Samsung-Smartphone bei Aldi: Wie gut ist dieses Discounter-Angebot?
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Smartphones könnten in den kommenden Monaten immer weiter zu Luxus-Gadgets avancieren. Als Reaktion auf die Speicherkrise haben in den vergangenen Wochen viele große Hersteller die Preise für ihre Modelle erhöht. Betroffen sind vor allem die Top-Modelle. Wer da nicht mitgehen will – und zu Abstrichen bereit ist –, fährt mit einem Einsteiger-Smartphone günstiger. Ein solches bietet Aldi in Form des Samsung Galaxy A18 ab dem 29. Oktober 2026 in seinen Filialen reduziert an. Kostenpunkt: 219 statt 279 Euro.
Diese Abstriche müsst ihr beim Galaxy A18 in Kauf nehmen
Selbst bei der unverbindlichen Preisempfehlung wird schon klar: Raketentechnik gibt es hier nicht zu kaufen. Entsprechend liest sich das Datenblatt. Mit dem Exynos 1610 ist Samsungs eigener Einsteiger-Prozessor an Bord. 5G unterstützt er nicht. Ihr surft unterwegs maximal mit LTE‑Geschwindigkeit. Dazu gibt es magere vier Gigabyte Arbeitsspeicher. Zum Vergleich: Das etwa 150 Euro teurere Galaxy A56 bietet acht Gigabyte RAM. Mit der Funktion RAM Plus soll das Smartphone auf bis zu vier Gigabyte virtuellen Arbeitsspeicher zugreifen können. Dabei greift das Gerät dann auf 128 Gigabyte großen Datenspeicher zu. Einen sehr großen Leistungsschub sollte man sich davon nicht erwarten.
Abstriche müsst ihr außerdem beim Gehäuse machen. Das ist nach IP64 nur gegen Spritzwasser, aber nicht gegen dauerhaftes Untertauchen geschützt. Wie gut die Dreifachkamera auf der Rückseite performt, lässt sich nur schwer einschätzen. Mit teureren Modellen können die Systeme in günstigen Smartphones in der Regel aber nicht mithalten. Immerhin: Der Speicher lässt sich per microSD-Karte erweitern. Das ist heutzutage längst nicht mehr selbstverständlich.
Wie gut ist der Aldi-Deal?
Wer sich für das Smartphone dennoch interessiert, muss nicht zwingend den Discounter besuchen. Die üblichen Online-Shops bieten das Gerät schließlich schon für 209 Euro an. Mancher Ebay‑Händler ist hier sogar noch etwas günstiger, berechnet allerdings zusätzliche Versandkosten, sodass ihr mit den Angeboten von Amazon, Saturn und Mediamarkt insgesamt besser fahrt.
Einziger Vorteil beim Discounter: Aldi legt noch ein Starter-Set von Aldi-Talk mit einem Guthaben in Höhe von 10 Euro bei. Das fehlt bei den Elektronikriesen und Versandhändlern natürlich. Braucht ihr eh noch eine Prepaidkarte, kann sich der Gang zu Aldi lohnen.

articles.title: The Download: AI agent tracking and climate feedback loops
articles.text:
The Download: AI agent tracking and climate feedback loops
Plus: Hackers exposed 41,000 Homeland Security workers.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
Opinion: We urgently need to monitor AI agents’ actions in real time
—Madhulika Srikumar and Claire Leibowicz from the Partnership on AI, a nonprofit advancing best practices in AI governance.
AI agents are taking unauthorized actions, from hacking websites to accessing private government files. In many cases, they’ve eluded the very researchers and safety teams tasked with monitoring them.
As agents roll out across critical sectors, from finance to government to medicine, we must be able to monitor them in real time to prevent potentially devastating consequences. And while safety depends on monitoring, monitoring requires observability.
In other words, we need to know what the agent did and why it did it. Because right now, we’re effectively flying blind when deploying these tools.
Our climate models have a big, dangerous blind spot
Climate change itself increasingly fuels climate change. Rising greenhouse gas concentrations are driving up global temperatures, creating dangerous feedback loops that aren’t fully represented in our climate models—or our emissions-reduction goals.
Scientists have long warned that warming would propel further warming. Now, a growing number of observations and studies are indicating how powerful these cascading effects could be. By extension, they’re also showing how much faster the planet may warm this century.
Read more about the dangerous feedback loops accelerating global warming.
—James Temple
This article is from The Spark, our weekly climate tech newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Wednesday.
Are we there yet? Solid-state batteries
Lithium-ion batteries power everything from personal electronics to grid-scale energy storage, but their liquid electrolytes have drawbacks, not least a troubling tendency to catch fire. Enter the solid-state battery, which swaps liquid for a solid ceramic or polymer.
The technology promises faster charging, longer life, greater energy density and improved safety, and a new generation of companies aims to bring it to market. If their bets pan out, the tech could ease the shift away from fossil fuels.
Find out how close solid-state batteries are to delivering on their promise.
—Alexander C. Kaufman
This story is part of “Are we there yet?”, our series that takes stock of six technologies that have long promised to change the world—and scores them on a progress meter. We’re exploring each one in The Download, so stay tuned, and subscribe to read the rest of the stories in our new Impossible issue.
The must-reads
I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
1 Hackers exposed 41,000 Homeland Security workers
Including undercover ICE agents. (Wired $)
+ Much of the data relates to Customs and Border Protection. (TechCrunch)
+ It also linked the agencies to specific surveillance tools. (Reuters $)
+ Big Tech is pushing back against ICE’s demands for user data. (WSJ $)
+ Activists want ChatGPT users to quit over ICE ties. (MIT Technology Review)
2 Putin says Russia is coordinating with “genius” Musk on satellites
He said the cooperation maintains order in orbit. (Bloomberg $)
+ Russia is developing its own version of Starlink. (Guardian)
+ Moscow added Apple and Microsoft to a surveillance registry. (Quartz)
+ Here’s all the stuff we’ve put up in space. (MIT Technology Review)
3 Apple just announced its first-ever MacBook with a touchscreen
It joins a blitz of product launches under new CEO John Ternus. (CNN)
+ Steve Jobs and Tim Cook had both dismissed the idea. (NYT $)
+ Executives say touchscreen advances mean it’s now worthwhile. (Wired $)
4 Bloomberg and trading firms are paying to get Trump’s posts faster
They’ve signed up for Truth Social’s pay-for-access plan. (Reuters $)
5 As US ties fray, Europe is planning its first subsea cable to Greenland
It will bypass the US to link Canada, Japan, and South Korea. (Ars Technica)
+ The EU’s AI champion says Europe can rival US tech giants. (FT $)
6 Palantir’s defense chief says AI could make China target Taiwan
He says Beijing may act to stop the US pulling ahead in AI. (Bloomberg $)
+ Taiwan's “silicon shield” could be weakening. (MIT Technology Review)
7 Musk’s xAI has offered to buy homes if residents drop a noise lawsuit
The suit targets noise from powering its Mississippi data centres. (Guardian)
8 The world’s first spinal cord transplant has sparked controversy
Experts say there’s little evidence the operation will work. (New Scientist $)
9 China’s tech giants are fighting for attention with AI microdramas
Tencent and ByteDance are battling over the booming market. (SCMP)
+ Chinese microdramas are AI content machines. (MIT Technology Review)
10 Astronomers have spotted a possible new dwarf planet beyond Pluto
The icy world would be the solar system’s sixth dwarf planet. (Gizmodo)
Quote of the day
“They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs.”
—A hacking group explains why it leaked personal information from the US Department of Homeland Security, NPR reports.
One more thing
How the Pentagon is adapting to China’s technological rise
It’s been just over a year since Kathleen Hicks stepped down as US deputy secretary of defense.
As the highest-ranking woman in Pentagon history, Hicks shaped US military posture through an era defined by renewed competition between powerful countries and a scramble to modernize defense technology.
In this conversation with MIT Technology Review, Hicks reflects on how the Pentagon is adapting—or failing to adapt—to a new era of geopolitical competition. She discusses China’s technological rise, the future of AI in warfare, and her signature initiative: Replicator.
—Caiwei Chen
We can still have nice things
A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line.)
+ Astronomers have found a green star 280 light-years from Earth.
+ A Scottish labrador that detects “sea vomit” has won the Animal of the Year award.
+ England’s iconic Sycamore Gap is showing signs of new life three years on from its felling.
+ From Lime-bike jousting to chainmail-wearing pop stars, youth culture is embracing the medieval era.

articles.title: Valve won't ban AI games from Steam despite growing complaints and extortion threats
articles.text:
TL;DR: During the most recent Next Fest demo showcase, many Steam users complained about having to sift through vibe-coded titles with AI-generated assets. The emerging threat of AI-coded clones has also made some developers hesitant to release demos. Valve, sticking to its usual open-door philosophy, advised developers to simply make their games better while promising to continue investigating the issue.
Although Valve forces developers to disclose how they use generative AI in making their games, the company refuses to ban the technology's use outright from Steam. Valve also recently recommended that indie developers concerned about AI clones strive to make their original games better through constant updates and community building.
The company held an extensive Q&A session with developers at the 2026 Busan Indie Connect Festival, with AI a leading topic. Games with AI-generated assets have drawn complaints from Steam users since at least 2025, but the situation arguably intensified this year as vibe-coded titles add to the controversy.
One developer at the event claimed that some developers had received extortion emails threatening to release AI-generated clones of their projects if they didn't pay. Valve's Tom Giardino said this was the first he'd heard of such cases but promised the company would look into them and recommended that affected developers contact law enforcement.
Otherwise, Valve advised indies to make their games harder to copy by continually adding features and gradually building loyal communities instead of relying on a single selling point. Comparing AI games to prior controversies with Greenlight and the current Steam Direct release system, the company reiterated that it doesn't aim to be an arbiter of which titles deserve to be released.
Valve also explained why shoppers might have seen so many AI-generated games during this month's Next Fest, which prompted calls for an AI filter. The company revealed that the event's front page displays games almost completely at random for the first two days before tailoring suggestions to users' preferences. Valve acknowledged that the strategy can surface a lot of low-quality content, but stressed that it keeps things fair. The company is still thinking of ways to address the issue.
While users criticize Valve for its leniency regarding AI, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney has once again called on Valve to drop its AI labeling policy. Calling the rule a "political act," Sweeney accused the company of fomenting an anti-AI hate mob. Epic Games recently released a new vibe-coded version of its launcher, and Sweeney admitted to using AI to develop Unreal Engine features.

articles.title: Rivian expands joint venture with VW to include AI assistant | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The $5.8 billion joint venture between Rivian and Volkswagen Group is expanding to include AI assistants.
Rivian is now licensing elements of its AI voice assistant technology to Volkswagen Group as part of the broader joint venture, according to the company’s third-quarter investor presentation released Thursday.
Rivian didn’t disclose the licensing fees, payment terms, or which Volkswagen vehicles will use the technology. However, the AI assistant, which recently rolled out to Rivian vehicles, could make its Volkswagen debut in the automaker’s low-cost EV called the ID EVERY1. The small four-door hatchback is slated to be the first VW vehicle to use Rivian’s software and electrical architecture under the joint venture established in 2024.
The joint venture between Rivian and VW Group has already expanded once before, at least financially. The companies initially announced a joint venture valued up to $5 billion, but within months VW upped its commitment to invest up to $5.8 billion in Rivian by 2027. The initial tie-up, formalized through an independent company that kicked off in November 2024, focused on bringing Rivian’s electrical architecture and software to Volkswagen’s next generation of vehicles.
Rivian described the expansion to include elements of its AI assistant technology as “a proof point for the extensibility of the platform we’ve built in-house.”
Rivian spent two years developing its AI assistant before showing it off last year. That development work continued longer than expected, with the assistant finally rolling out in May 2026 to its flagship R1S SUV, R1T pickup truck, and in October to its new midsize R2 SUV.
Rivian has big aspirations for its AI assistant, which allows drivers and passengers to interact with the vehicle and control certain functions. Rivian founder and CEO RJ Scaringe told TechCrunch onstage at Disrupt 2026 that the company has created its own in-house agentic framework that understands what action a person wants to take when they talk to the vehicle, and routes it to the right part of the car’s software. That capability could eventually allow Rivian vehicles to run AI agents created by other companies, including Anthropic.
The in-house AI assistant program also fits into Rivian’s push to become more vertically integrated — a strategy the company emphasized in its third-quarter earnings report.
“Our relentless focus on vertical integration remains a core competitive differentiator, allowing Rivian to seamlessly unify our hardware and software architecture to deliver significant value to our customers,” the company noted in its investor presentation.
That strategy led to Rivian overhauling its flagship R1T truck and R1S SUV, changing everything from the battery pack and suspension system to the electrical architecture, sensor stack, and software user interface. Its new electric architecture system and compute platform slashed the amount of wiring used and reduced the total number of electronic control units, or computers, used to control the vehicle from 17 different ECUs to seven. That foundation, Rivian argued, would allow it to build vehicles that can handle the computing demands required for advanced software and automated driving.
That technology caught the attention (and money) of VW, which has struggled to offer customers a modern software-centric vehicle found in competitors like Tesla.
Rivian made that vertical-integration case repeatedly in its investor presentation, noting that because it controls the entire technology stack, including compute, sensors, displays, lighting, and sound, “it can roll out rapid, vehicle-wide OTA updates that go well beyond the basics.”
This article was updated to provide the two separate rollout dates for the AI assistant.

articles.title: Confira o Olhar Digital News na íntegra (29/10/2026)
articles.text:
Veja os destaques do Olhar Digital News desta quinta-feira (29/10).
Há exatos 57 anos, a primeira mensagem era enviada pela internet
No fim da década de 1960, o governo dos Estados Unidos colocou em funcionamento a Arpanet, uma rede experimental que conectava computadores de instituições de pesquisa. O objetivo era permitir que cientistas acessassem máquinas remotamente e compartilhassem recursos. A primeira transmissão ocorreu no dia 29 de outubro de 1969, há exatos 57 anos, entre a Universidade da Califórnia em Los Angeles e o Instituto de Pesquisa de Stanford, posteriormente conhecido como SRI International.
MPT exige que Meta remova conteúdos de assédio eleitoral das redes
O Ministério Público do Trabalho entrou com ação judicial contra a Meta, dona do Instagram, Facebook e WhatsApp, para exigir a remoção de conteúdos que incentivem empresários a perseguir ou demitir funcionários por causa de suas escolhas políticas. A ação foi apresentada nesta quinta-feira (29). O órgão pede que as publicações sejam retiradas do ar em até 24 horas e cobra R$ 50 milhões por danos morais coletivos.
Executiva ligada à Nvidia é suspeita de ser uma espiã chinesa
O governo dos Estados Unidos suspeita que uma executiva chinesa do setor de tecnologia tenha atuado como agente de inteligência de Pequim. Ela mantinha contato próximo com Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia. Segundo as investigações, a empresária atuava como executiva da Megaspeed, companhia sediada em Singapura que compra chips avançados de inteligência artificial e opera centros de dados no Sudeste Asiático.
Poeira de Marte é tão fina que pode ameaçar futuras missões ao planeta vermelho
O rover Perseverance, da NASA, detectou em Marte partículas de poeira com cerca de 100 nanômetros de largura, aproximadamente 500 vezes mais finas que um fio de cabelo humano. A detecção foi feita pelo instrumento PIXL, que analisou partículas acumuladas nos equipamentos do rover e em amostras de materiais transportadas para avaliar sua interação com a poeira.
Alessandro Di Lorenzo é editor do Olhar Digital e formado em jornalismo pela Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS).
André Milhomem integra a equipe de redes sociais do Olhar Digital e do programa Olhar Digital News.

articles.title: Cohere deal won’t be last time feds take stake in Canadian tech companies, AI minister says
articles.text:
Canada’s investment in Cohere won’t be the last time the government takes an equity position in a domestic tech company, as it looks to bolster capacity in AI and other strategic industries.
The news: Prime Minister Mark Carney announced today in Montréal that the federal government will invest up to $1.6 billion CAD in Toronto AI developer Cohere, as part of a larger Series E funding round. The federal government said the investment will be made in stages, with regular reporting from Cohere about jobs and investments made in Canada.
In an interview, AI and digital innovation minister Evan Solomon told BetaKit that while thise equity funding was negotiated through the Canada Development Investment Corporation, a Crown corporation that manages government assets, a forthcoming tech fund from the feds will also be designed to allow the feds to invest in companies. First announced in the AI strategy, the $500-million Canadian Tech Growth Fund is meant to provide “flexible growth capital” to promising AI companies and sometimes take equity stakes in them.
From the source: The Canadian Tech Growth Fund “will be designed to have various facilities, but yes, to take equity positions in small and medium-sized companies to instill growth and to crowd in capital,” Solomon told BetaKit.
“We believe Canadians have made a good, valuable investment in an important company that gives us a seat at the table to control and build this technology,” he added about the Cohere deal.
The context: Government funding into Canadian tech companies is nothing new, but it has traditionally come through arm’s-length Crown corporations like the Business Development Bank of Canada or through various federal programs offering loans, grants, non-repayable contributions, and equity. For example, the Strategic Response Fund (a successor to the Strategic Innovation Fund) recently authorized nearly $200 million CAD for quantum company Xanadu in repayable funds.
But the Cohere deal, three times the size of the proposed Canadian Tech Growth Fund, likely represents the largest single Canadian government equity commitment ever made to a tech company. The federal government has been uplifting Cohere as Canada’s de facto entrant into the AI race for more than a year. At the industry conference ALL IN last year, industry minister Mélanie Joly declared that the government would make Cohere “a Canadian champion.”
Final thought: Government ownership of private companies is on the rise globally; under President Donald Trump, the US bought 10 percent of chip maker Intel. Canada is no exception: this summer, the feds announced their intention to buy a $400-million stake in critical minerals company Teck Resources.
Though Teck and Cohere are in vastly different fields, critical minerals and emerging technologies were both identified as top priorities in the feds’ new national security strategy today.
Feature image courtesy Evan Solomon via X.

articles.title: Reddit’s CEO says Google’s AI Mode ‘does not drive traffic’
articles.text:
Reddit CEO Steve Huffman said in an earnings call today that Google’s AI-powered search modes do not help with traffic to the platform, echoing problems facing other websites and publishers. As part of its Q3 2026 earnings, Reddit revealed that search traffic in October has “dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week,” and he attributes part of the company’s struggles with Google traffic to how AI Mode and AI Overviews change the search experience.
Reddit’s CEO says Google’s AI Mode ‘does not drive traffic’
Although Google’s AI-powered modes reduce traffic to Reddit, Steve Huffman says that Reddit is still a ‘top search term’ on Google.
“The reality is, AI Mode does not drive traffic,” Huffman says. “Not for us, and not to anybody, as far as I know. That’s just a fundamental shift in how Google works. It used to be a traffic driver, now it’s not.”
He says that AI Overviews and AI Mode have “evolved a lot” and now, at a “minimum,” push “everyone down the search page.” Huffman also says that Reddit believes its content that’s machine-translated into other languages is being ranked lower in search results, which he says would primarily affect the company outside the US.
However, Reddit is still a “top search term in Google,” Huffman says. “This doesn’t say anything about the internet consumers’ demand for Reddit. People still want Reddit. It says Google is not sending them to Reddit the way they used to.” He also says that Google is “crawling us as hard as ever, so the demand hasn’t changed from their point of view, either.”
(Google’s business has been affected by AI Mode, too: it said yesterday that it’s seeing “lower monetization” in AI Mode ads, though it’s now bringing AI ads to more countries.)
To try and combat the search referral difficulties, Reddit is working to make the platform a “direct, sticky, daily destination.” Yesterday, it introduced a “For You” feed with recommendations related to your interests, and in August, it started testing an experiment that uses AI to turn posts into short videos.
Reddit also announced today that it’s going to force everyone to log in, which Huffman claims will be “better for user experience, better for our ads business, is more in line with safety regulations, and more protective of Reddit data.”

articles.title: Hasta la caca de perro será un arma en 'GTA 6': revelada la última locura de Rockstar
articles.text:
Con GTA 6 a solo semanas de distancia, Rockstar Games reveló un clip de gameplay de lo más peculiar; no solo por el modo que eligió para mostrarlo, sino también por su contenido. El estudio aprovechó el más reciente episodio de South Park e introdujo un fragmento del nuevo Grand Theft Auto VI con una situación muy curiosa que involucra la caca de un perro.
La aparición de GTA 6 se da en el capítulo Guinea Pig On A Stick de South Park, donde una mujer destaca la calidad gráfica y el realismo del juego ante los protagonistas de la serie. Sin dudas, un modo muy ingenioso por parte de Rockstar y Take-Two Interactive de llegar a su público objetivo con su mensaje irreverente.
Más allá de la escena de South Park en sí, lo que nos interesa es lo que se muestra en el gameplay de GTA 6. El clip se inicia con un perro haciendo caca en la playa de Vice City y con su dueño recogiéndola y siguiendo su camino. Sin embargo, la historia se sale de los rieles cuando uno de los protagonistas del juego ataca al NPC que pasea a la mascota.
En el vídeo se observa que Jason le arroja un objeto por la espalda al NPC, y luego recoge la bolsa con caca y se la estrella en el rostro. Acción escatológica en su máxima expresión, sin lugar a dudas. Esta es una muestra más de que GTA 6 no piensa contenerse ni ponerse límites, y que las posibilidades que entregará el juego serán inacabables.
GTA 6 te permitirá usar caca de perro para atacar a los NPC
El uso de South Park para mostrar gameplay de GTA 6 hasta aquí nunca visto es una de las decisiones de marketing más peculiares (y geniales) de Rockstar Games. La expectación por el nuevo juego se encuentra en niveles altísimos y todo apunta a que su lanzamiento tendrá un impacto que no se limitará a la industria del gaming.
Según Firstpost, GTA 6 podría provocar una pérdida de productividad de hasta 1.000 millones de dólares a la economía estadounidense en solo un día. Otro reporte sostiene que las solicitudes de jornada libre para el 19 de noviembre, el día de estreno del título, se han incrementado hasta un 17 % en comparación con los pedidos normales para un tercer jueves de noviembre.
Strauss Zelnick, CEO de Take-Two Interactive, vaticinó meses atrás que muchas personas fingirían una enfermedad para no trabajar cuando se lance GTA 6. En tanto que Steven Adams, jugador de Houston Rockets de la NBA, sostuvo que todas las ligas deportivas top verán una marcada caída en su rendimiento durante noviembre por la atención sobre el juego.
Y como si no fuese suficiente con las persecuciones, los tiroteos, la acción al desnudo (guiño, guiño), el mapa inmenso, el clima realista y un sinfín de etcéteras, GTA 6 también te dará la libertad de embarrarle la cara con caca de perro a un personaje no jugable.
GTA 6 llega a PS5, PS5 Pro y Xbox Series X|S el 19 de noviembre. La versión de PC aún no tiene fecha confirmada, aunque se especula que podría llegar en el primer trimestre de 2027.

articles.title: Blaupause: So haben wir in Alltagssprache einen KI-Agenten erstellt
articles.text:
Blaupause: So haben wir in Alltagssprache einen KI-Agenten erstellt
Im Werbegeschäft mündet jeder Verkauf in eine Auftragsbestätigung. Sie kommt als PDF und listet alle Leistungen, die ein Kunde gebucht hat, etwa ein Podcast-Sponsoring oder zwei Sponsored Posts. Bevor die Umsetzung beginnt, braucht jede dieser Leistungen eine eigene Aufgabe im Projekttool, mit Unteraufgaben und Terminen. Bei uns erledigte das bis Mitte August 2026 die Kampagnenabwicklung von Hand, Auftrag für Auftrag in Asana. Bei großen Buchungen dauerte das bis zu 40 Minuten. Der t3n PRO Use Case zeigt als Blaupause, wie das Team diese Arbeit einem KI-Agenten beigebracht hat.
KI-Agenten erstellen ohne Entwicklerteam
Zum Einstieg fragte die Projektverantwortliche Claude, was er braucht, um die Auftragsanlage in Asana zu automatisieren. Ein interner Skill sorgte dafür, dass Claude ausführlich zurückfragte. Als Material bekam er die knappe Prozessdokumentation und zehn echte Auftragsbestätigungen. Er spielte Aufträge durch, die das Team schon angelegt hatte, und glich sein Ergebnis mit dem echten Eintrag ab. Aus den Abweichungen entstand an einem Nachmittag seine erste Anleitung.
Diese erste Fassung reichte für den Alltag nicht. Also ging die Arbeit im Slack-Thread weiter, das Team benannte Fehler in normalen Sätzen, und Claude trug jede Korrektur in seine Anleitung ein. Beim ersten Test fand er umgekehrt zwei Fehler in einem Eintrag, den das Team von Hand angelegt hatte. Nach 24 Stunden stand die Anleitung bei Version 12. Die Werkzeuge waren alle vorhanden: Claude ist mit den internen Tools des Unternehmens verbunden, und das Asana-Board mit festen Feldern und Vorlagen gab es längst.
Mitte August ging der Agent mit echten Aufträgen live, eine Testkopie des Boards hat das Team nie angelegt. Seither reicht es, Claude im Slack-Thread zur Auftragsbestätigung zu markieren. Was er anlegt, prüft das Team: bei einfachen Aufträgen in unter fünf Minuten, bei großen in höchstens zehn. In den ersten gut zwei Monaten ist kein Fehler bis ins Tagesgeschäft durchgerutscht. Am deutlichsten merkt das Team den Unterschied, wenn jemand im Urlaub ist.
Was du in dieser Blaupause bekommst
In diesem t3n PRO Use Case zeigen wir, wie sich die Kampagnenabwicklung von t3n einen KI-Agenten für die Auftragsanlage gebaut hat:
- Einblick in die Regeln, die Claude aus zehn echten Aufträgen ableitete
- Die Kanalanweisung, mit der Claude im Slack-Kanal arbeitet
- Ein Auszug aus dem Slack-Thread zum ersten echten Auftrag
Jetzt freischalten mit t3n PRO.
Du möchtest mehr erfahren?
t3n PRO auschecken
Du bist bereits Teil der t3n PRO Community? Hier anmelden
Neu & exklusiv in t3n PRO: Use Cases
KI ist überall – echte Orientierung Mangelware. Unsere Use Cases zeigen, wie Unternehmen KI produktiv einsetzen: mit konkreten Zahlen, realistischem Aufwand und echten Learnings.

articles.title: Top 7 Web3 Platforms for Node.js Developers - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Quick answer: The best Web3 platforms for Node.js developers in 2026 are Autheo, Ethereum, Solana, Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, and Avalanche. Autheo ranks first because it combines an EVM-compatible Layer-1, standard JSON-RPC support, TypeScript and JavaScript SDKs, and an integrated developer workspace. Node.js developers can use familiar tools such as viem, ethers.js, Hardhat, npm, and REST APIs while connecting to a broader platform designed to bring identity, compute, storage, interoperability, and AI tooling into one environment.
Choosing a Web3 platform used to mean selecting a blockchain. Today, it means selecting an entire development stack: the execution environment, client libraries, smart contract language, backend infrastructure, data storage, wallet integration, testing tools, and deployment workflow. Every additional vendor increases integration work, operational costs, and the number of potential failure points.
This guide compares seven Web3 platforms Node.js developers are actively using in 2026, including what each platform does best, which JavaScript and TypeScript tools it supports, and where its limitations become important.
The Best Web3 Platforms for Node.js Developers in 2026
The top seven platforms are:
- Autheo
- Ethereum
- Solana
- Base
- Polygon
- Arbitrum
- Avalanche
These rankings consider Node.js compatibility, TypeScript support, SDK quality, smart contract tooling, backend development, scalability, interoperability, documentation, and the overall number of external services developers must integrate.
1. Autheo
Best overall Web3 platform for Node.js developers
Autheo is the best overall choice for Node.js developers who want familiar Ethereum development tools without assembling an entire application stack from unrelated services.
Autheo provides an EVM-compatible blockchain built on the Cosmos SDK. Its standard JSON-RPC interface allows Node.js developers to connect using viem, ethers.js, and other Ethereum-compatible libraries. Existing TypeScript types, Node.js services, React applications, and contract integration patterns can be adapted primarily by changing the network configuration and RPC endpoint.
For smart contract development, Autheo supports Solidity deployment through Hardhat, Foundry, and Remix. Developers who prefer npm-based workflows can use JavaScript and TypeScript SDK packages designed to provide typed access to Autheo’s APIs and platform services.
Why Autheo Works Well With Node.js
Node.js developers can use Autheo for:
- Backend services that read and write blockchain data
- TypeScript scripts for contract deployment and administration
- Wallet connections using viem or ethers.js
- Event listeners and transaction monitoring
- REST and JSON-RPC integrations
- Cross-chain applications using IBC
- Full-stack dApps with JavaScript or TypeScript frontends
- Automated testing and deployment through DevHub
Autheo’s DevHub brings documentation, testing, deployment, monitoring, SDK access, contract exploration, and testnet resources into a more centralized development environment. This can reduce the amount of external infrastructure a team must configure before launching an application.
The platform’s broader goal is to integrate blockchain execution, identity, decentralized compute, persistent storage, AI assistance, and developer tooling. The EVM-compatible chain, staking, fees, SDKs, IBC functionality, and DevHub are available today. TheoID, decentralized compute, expanded storage, post-quantum features, and THEO AI capabilities are being introduced according to the platform’s rollout roadmap.
Where Autheo Falls Short
Autheo has a smaller existing application ecosystem than Ethereum, Solana, or the largest Ethereum Layer-2 networks. Some of the platform’s most differentiated services are also still rolling out.
Developers should evaluate the tools currently available separately from roadmap features. Even with that limitation, Autheo’s Node.js compatibility and integrated infrastructure model make it a strong option for teams that want to reduce fragmented third-party integrations.
Best for: Node.js teams building full-stack dApps, cross-chain services, AI-enabled Web3 applications, backend automation, identity applications, and products that need an integrated development environment.
2. Ethereum
Best for libraries, documentation, and ecosystem maturity
Ethereum remains the most established Web3 platform for JavaScript and Node.js developers. It has the largest collection of libraries, tutorials, development frameworks, infrastructure providers, contract standards, and production examples.
Node.js developers can use ethers.js or viem to connect to Ethereum nodes, read blockchain data, call smart contracts, send transactions, estimate gas, monitor events, and operate backend services. Solidity is also syntactically familiar to JavaScript developers, although it has a very different security and execution model.
Ethereum’s official documentation identifies ethers.js and viem as prominent JavaScript and TypeScript interfaces. It also notes that Web3.js was archived in March 2025, so new Node.js projects should generally use a maintained alternative such as ethers.js or viem.
Why Ethereum Works Well With Node.js
Ethereum offers:
- Mature npm libraries
- Extensive TypeScript support
- Hardhat and Foundry compatibility
- Standard JSON-RPC interfaces
- Large collections of open-source contracts
- Established token and wallet standards
- Numerous hosted node providers
- Strong support for backend scripts, bots, APIs, and indexers
A Node.js service can use Ethereum libraries to communicate with contracts without running an Ethereum client locally. Developers can connect through an RPC provider and build conventional API routes, queues, databases, and background workers around blockchain activity.
Where Ethereum Falls Short
Ethereum mainnet can be expensive for applications that require frequent transactions. Developers may also need separate providers for nodes, indexing, storage, identity, monitoring, automation, and wallet infrastructure.
Ethereum offers the deepest ecosystem, but its development stack is often assembled from multiple independent services.
Best for: DeFi protocols, established token projects, high-value applications, infrastructure products, developer tools, and teams requiring maximum composability.
3. Solana
Best non-EVM platform for TypeScript applications
Solana is one of the strongest Web3 platforms for Node.js and TypeScript developers who do not require EVM compatibility.
The recommended TypeScript SDK is Solana Kit, available through the @solana/kit package. It provides tools for RPC connections, transactions, codecs, signers, wallets, and generated program clients. Solana also offers Web3.js version 3 for developers who prefer its familiar class-based interface or need to modernize an existing Solana Web3.js application.
Developers can use Node.js to create transaction services, payment systems, token applications, bots, data pipelines, game backends, wallet services, and APIs.
Why Solana Works Well With Node.js
Solana provides:
- Official JavaScript and TypeScript SDKs
- npm-based client libraries
- JSON-RPC and WebSocket APIs
- Generated TypeScript clients for onchain programs
- Tools for token and wallet integration
- Strong support for high-frequency applications
- React and Next.js integration options
The main difference is that Solana is not EVM-compatible. Its onchain programs are commonly written in Rust, while JavaScript and TypeScript are used for clients, tests, backend services, transaction construction, and user interfaces.
This means a Node.js developer can build much of a Solana application in TypeScript, but learning Rust or working with a Rust developer may be necessary when creating custom onchain programs.
Where Solana Falls Short
Solana’s account model, transaction construction, program architecture, and development workflow differ significantly from Ethereum. Developers migrating from EVM networks face a steeper learning curve than they would when moving to another EVM-compatible platform.
Best for: Payments, trading applications, consumer products, games, token platforms, high-frequency applications, and Node.js teams willing to work outside the EVM ecosystem.
4. Base
Best for consumer apps and rapid JavaScript deployment
Base is an Ethereum Layer-2 network incubated by Coinbase. It is a strong option for Node.js developers building consumer applications, payment products, creator platforms, social experiences, and lightweight mini apps.
Because Base is EVM-compatible, Node.js developers can use ethers.js, viem, Hardhat, Solidity, Next.js, and standard Ethereum JSON-RPC methods. Existing Ethereum applications can often be adapted by changing network settings and reviewing Base-specific deployment requirements.
Base also provides MiniKit, a development framework intended to help teams build applications using familiar technologies such as Next.js. Its documentation includes templates and rapid deployment workflows for publishing mini apps.
Why Base Works Well With Node.js
Base is well suited for:
- js and TypeScript applications
- js payment backends
- Consumer-facing mini apps
- Wallet and account integrations
- Solidity contract deployment
- Social and creator applications
- Products seeking Coinbase-related distribution
Developers can reuse much of the Ethereum JavaScript ecosystem while accessing lower transaction costs than Ethereum mainnet.
Where Base Falls Short
Base is still an Ethereum Layer-2 network. Developers must understand bridging, sequencer dependencies, settlement timing, and Layer-2 withdrawal mechanics.
Its strongest distribution advantages may also be most relevant to applications that fit the broader Coinbase and Base ecosystem.
Best for: Consumer Web3 applications, social apps, creator tools, payments, mini apps, and Node.js teams already comfortable with Next.js and Ethereum libraries.
5. Polygon
Best for full-stack EVM development with multiple scaling options
Polygon offers a broad set of Ethereum scaling technologies and EVM-compatible development environments. It is a practical choice for Node.js developers who want to use familiar Ethereum tools while accessing lower-cost transactions.
Developers can connect to Polygon using viem, ethers.js, JSON-RPC providers, and other standard EVM libraries. Smart contracts can be written in Solidity and deployed through tools such as Hardhat, Foundry, or Remix.
Polygon also provides a dApp Launchpad that initializes a full-stack project with a Next.js frontend and Hardhat smart contract environment. It can automate contract artifact updates, redeployment, and frontend hot module replacement.
Why Polygon Works Well With Node.js
Polygon supports:
- js and TypeScript backends
- js application development
- Hardhat contract projects
- Standard EVM libraries
- Solidity smart contracts
- Automated dApp project creation
- Ethereum-compatible wallets
- Low-cost consumer transactions
Polygon can work particularly well for marketplaces, loyalty programs, games, digital collectibles, and enterprise applications that need frequent onchain activity.
Where Polygon Falls Short
Polygon includes multiple networks and scaling products. Developers must determine which environment matches their security, interoperability, transaction cost, and performance requirements.
The number of available options creates flexibility, but it can also make architecture decisions more complicated.
Best for: Full-stack JavaScript applications, games, marketplaces, loyalty systems, enterprise dApps, and teams that want multiple Ethereum scaling options.
6. Arbitrum
Best for Node.js DeFi backends and established Layer-2 applications
Arbitrum is a mature Ethereum Layer-2 ecosystem designed to support lower-cost, higher-capacity smart contract applications.
Node.js developers can use common Ethereum libraries such as ethers.js, viem, and Web3.js, although viem or ethers.js are preferable for new projects. Arbitrum also supports development frameworks such as Hardhat and Foundry.
For a JavaScript or TypeScript team, deploying to Arbitrum can feel similar to deploying to Ethereum. Existing contract ABIs, wallet connections, backend scripts, event listeners, and testing patterns can frequently be reused.
Why Arbitrum Works Well With Node.js
Arbitrum is a strong choice for:
- DeFi dashboards
- Trading interfaces
- Transaction monitoring services
- js bots and automation
- High-activity smart contract applications
- Ethereum applications expanding to Layer 2
- Backend systems that monitor contract events
Its established DeFi ecosystem gives developers access to existing contracts, liquidity, wallets, bridges, analytics platforms, and infrastructure providers.
Where Arbitrum Falls Short
Developers must account for Layer-2 settlement, bridging, withdrawal periods, gas behavior, and differences between Arbitrum networks.
Arbitrum reduces transaction costs, but it does not eliminate the need for external RPC, indexing, monitoring, storage, and deployment services.
Best for: DeFi, trading applications, financial dashboards, games, automation tools, and existing Ethereum projects moving to Layer 2.
7. Avalanche
Best for TypeScript teams building configurable EVM networks
Avalanche provides an EVM-compatible C-Chain and tools for launching customizable Avalanche Layer-1 networks. It is particularly valuable for Node.js teams that need more control over their blockchain environment.
The Avalanche Client SDK provides a TypeScript interface for interacting with the network and currently requires Node.js 20 or newer. Developers can also use ethers.js, Hardhat, Solidity, and familiar EVM deployment patterns.
Why Avalanche Works Well With Node.js
Avalanche offers:
- A dedicated TypeScript SDK
- js support for network interaction
- EVM-compatible smart contracts
- Hardhat deployment workflows
- Customizable Avalanche Layer-1 networks
- Cross-network messaging capabilities
- Infrastructure for application-specific blockchains
Node.js developers can build backend APIs, transaction services, administrative scripts, data monitoring systems, wallet integrations, and contract deployment pipelines.
Where Avalanche Falls Short
Launching a customized Avalanche Layer-1 requires more architecture and operational planning than deploying an application to a shared public network.
Projects must decide whether they actually need a dedicated network. For many applications, deploying contracts to an existing shared chain will be simpler and less expensive to operate.
Best for: Enterprise systems, institutional applications, games, regulated environments, application-specific networks, and TypeScript teams that need greater control over blockchain configuration.
What Is a Web3 Platform for Node.js Developers?
A Web3 platform for Node.js developers is a blockchain or development environment that lets JavaScript and TypeScript applications communicate with decentralized networks.
Node.js is commonly used for the offchain portion of a Web3 application, including:
- API servers
- Transaction relayers
- Blockchain event listeners
- Wallet services
- Deployment scripts
- Trading bots
- Background workers
- Data indexing
- Notification systems
- Testing and automation
Node.js is not necessarily the language used for the smart contract itself. On EVM networks, smart contracts are usually written in Solidity. On Solana, custom programs are commonly written in Rust. Node.js connects those onchain programs to websites, mobile applications, databases, APIs, and other business systems.
Which JavaScript Library Should Web3 Developers Use in 2026?
For new EVM-compatible Node.js projects, viem and ethers.js are the leading choices.
Viem is a TypeScript-first option with strong type safety and modular interfaces. It works well for modern applications using TypeScript, React, Next.js, and related tools.
Ethers.js remains a widely supported library for wallets, providers, contracts, transactions, signatures, and utility functions.
Web3.js was historically one of the most recognizable Ethereum JavaScript libraries, but it was archived in 2025. It may remain in older applications, but developers starting new projects should generally choose an actively maintained alternative.
For Solana, developers should evaluate @solana/kit or the current version of @solana/web3.js. Solana’s Web3.js package is separate from the archived Ethereum Web3.js project.
How to Choose a Web3 Platform for a Node.js Project
Before selecting a platform, evaluate the following questions:
- Does the team need EVM compatibility?
- Will developers write contracts in Solidity, Rust, or another language?
- Which Node.js and TypeScript SDKs are officially supported?
- Does the platform provide stable JSON-RPC or REST APIs?
- How will the application index blockchain data?
- Which wallet and authentication tools are required?
- Will the project need cross-chain communication?
- How many third-party infrastructure providers must be integrated?
- What are the expected transaction volume and fees?
- Which platform already reaches the application’s intended users?
The platform with the highest transaction throughput is not automatically the best choice. Developer tooling, documentation, integration complexity, ecosystem fit, and operational requirements can have a greater effect on the project’s success.
Which Web3 Platform Is Best for Node.js Developers?
Autheo is the best overall Web3 platform in this ranking for Node.js developers who want EVM compatibility, TypeScript support, standard JavaScript libraries, Cosmos interoperability, and an integrated developer workspace.
Ethereum remains the best choice for ecosystem depth and composability. Solana is the leading non-EVM option for TypeScript developers building high-throughput applications. Base is particularly strong for consumer apps, Polygon provides flexible Ethereum scaling options, Arbitrum offers a mature Layer-2 environment, and Avalanche is well suited for configurable EVM networks.
The Bottom Line
Node.js developers have more Web3 options in 2026 than ever before. The biggest difference between platforms is no longer whether they provide a JavaScript SDK. Most major networks now offer JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON-RPC, or REST-based access.
The more important question is how much of the complete application stack each platform provides.
Autheo ranks first because it supports familiar Node.js and EVM development workflows while working toward a unified environment for blockchain execution, identity, interoperability, storage, compute, AI tooling, testing, and deployment. For JavaScript and TypeScript teams that want to build Web3 applications without managing a large collection of disconnected services, that integrated model offers a compelling alternative to the traditional multi-vendor development stack.

articles.title: Pine Labs sees 6.5x growth in net profit in Q2 FY27
articles.text:
Pine Labs sees 6.5x growth in net profit in Q2 FY27
In its international business, which spans more than 22 markets, revenue from Southeast Asia (SEA) grew by around 40% year-on-year, while its UAE business crossed one lakh daily transactions, the company said.
Fintech company Pine Labs reported a 6.5x rise in net profit to Rs 38.6 crore in the second quarter of FY27, while revenue grew 24% year-on-year to Rs 806 crore.
The fintech company's net profit stood at Rs 6 crore in the same quarter last fiscal, while revenue was Rs 650 crore.
"Q2 was an all-round quarter - growth across acceptance and issuing, 15% of revenues from global markets, and 14% from products launched only in the last two years," said Amrish Rau, CEO, Pine Labs.
According to Pine Labs, it now processes more than 25 million transactions a day across businesses, up from over 22% on a year-on-year basis.
Pine Labs said its online payments business grew by over 45% year-on-year, while gross transaction value (GTV) rose 140%, driven by expansion into agentic commerce, cross-border payments, small and medium businesses (SMBs), and government segments.
In its international business, which spans more than 22 markets, revenue from Southeast Asia (SEA) grew by around 40% year-on-year, while its UAE business crossed one lakh daily transactions, the company said.
Pine Labs also said AI agents now contribute to around 89% of code changes. The company plans to reinvest the resulting efficiency gains into new products, geographies and categories while maintaining a strong EBITDA profile.
According to Pine Labs it is stepping up brand investments to position itself as the default commerce infrastructure for the global south.
"The opportunity set in front of us is widening, not narrowing," said Rau. "A wider set of new products this quarter, 10 lakh soundboxes committed over the medium term, agentic commerce live on a top Indian marketplace, and a UPI monetisation window opening up — this is the time to build.”

articles.title: Jobs dijo que un Mac táctil no funcionaba y Ternus dice que "ahora no cuesta nada". En esa diferencia está la nueva Apple
articles.text:
En octubre de 2010, Steve Jobs proyectó la imagen de una mano tocando la pantalla de un portátil y la descartó. "Las superficies táctiles no quieren estar en vertical", dijo: "al rato el brazo se cansa y al final se te quiere caer". Habían hecho muchas pruebas con usuarios y no funcionaba. Sobre esa premisa han seguido tres lustros de MacBook sin pantalla táctil.
Este miércoles, John Ternus ha presentado un MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil.
Lo fácil es leerlo como una enmienda a Jobs, como un tabula rasa respecto a la larguísima sombra del fundador. Pero lo interesante es cómo justifica Ternus el cambio, porque ahí aparece el criterio con el que va a dirigir la empresa, presumiblemente.
En 2021, siendo jefe de ingeniería de hardware, Ternus le dijo a la enorme Joanna Stern que el Mac estaba optimizado para la entrada indirecta y que no veían motivos para cambiarlo. Cinco años después, en su entrevista con Steven Levy en Wired, arranca con la misma idea: el Mac es, ante todo, un dispositivo de entrada indirecta.
El principio es el mismo. La conclusión, la contraria. Lo que ha cambiado lo explica él mismo: necesitaban llegar a un punto en que el tacto no empeorase el producto en nada, ni en peso ni en grosor. Eso solo ha sido posible con el OLED con el sensor integrado. Y remata con una frase que resume toda la presentación: "todo esto y, ah, sí, también es táctil". Bien jugado.
Jobs formulaba sus decisiones como veredictos. "Eso no funciona". Si ves un stylus, la han cagado. Tim Cook mantuvo ese tono en 2012, cuando dijo que se podía fusionar una tostadora con una nevera, pero que el resultado no agradaría a nadie: juntar dos cosas obliga a ceder en ambas.
No es que Ternus discuta esa idea, simplemente le añade una condición: si juntarlas ya no obliga a ceder, se juntan. El táctil no llega al Mac porque Apple haya cambiado de opinión sobre la ergonomía, sino porque ha dejado de "costar". El nuevo MacBook Pro de 14 pulgadas, de hecho, pesa 220 gramos menos que el anterior. El de 16, casi 300.
El patrón se repite en el iPhone Duo. Ternus le contó a TIME que los plegables de la competencia le parecían baratos y chapuceros, y a Tom's Guide que el momento decisivo llegó al ver un prototipo con cristal nanotexturizado que disimulaba el pliegue. Apple no ha sido la primera en hacer un plegable, pero ha esperado a encontrar la forma de hacer desaparecer el defecto que hacía dudar del formato.
En esa misma entrevista le preguntaron por el Apple Pencil en un iPhone, que aparentemente contradice otra frase célebre de Jobs (en realidad no lo hace porque es distinto un stylus para controlar la interfaz que un lápiz capacitivo opcional para dibujar y escribir). Respondió que nunca lo había visto como una regla.
Y ahí está la diferencia. Para Jobs, un "no" era una posición, una brújula moral. Para Ternus, un "no" solo es algo provisional: lo que todavía no se puede hacer sin pagar un precio. Tampoco quiero forzar la lectura porque ambos productos se gestaron con Ternus dirigiendo el hardware, y dos lanzamientos no definen una etapa. Jobs tampoco decidía únicamente por intuición, porque también mencionaba ciertas pruebas con usuarios. Pero la forma de explicar las decisiones sí dice mucho de quien las toma.
La Apple de Ternus difícilmente va a decir que algo no se puede hacer. Lo que hará es esperar, a veces más de la cuenta, hasta que hacerlo "no cueste nada". Es un método menos épico y más difícil de convertir en leyenda, pero hace tiempo que el mesianismo terminó en Apple. Así que la pregunta para esta etapa ya no es qué se niega a hacer Apple, sino cuánto tiempo está dispuesta a esperar.

articles.title: GTA 6 : la bande originale composée par Justice à droit à une super édition vinyle en précommande
articles.text:
GTA 6 sort le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series. Depuis ce jeudi 29 octobre, les collectionneurs peuvent aussi précommander sa bande originale en CD et en vinyle. Baptisée Grand Theft Auto VI: Original Score, cette bande originale signée Justice sera commercialisée le 11 décembre 2026. Elle comprendra 30 morceaux originaux, dont Flower In A Hurricane, enregistré avec Tame Impala, SZA et King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard, ainsi que Pusher, en collaboration avec Gesaffelstein. Attention à ne pas confondre cette sortie avec GTA VI: The Album, une compilation distincte consacrée aux chansons d’artistes qui accompagneront le jeu, également en précommande.
Trois formats physiques sont disponibles pour cette bande originale : un triple vinyle noir, une édition limitée en vinyle transparent et un double CD. Voilà où les trouver en précommande :
L’édition vinyle standard :
L’édition vinyle limitée :
L’édition CD :
Justice aux commandes de la bande originale de GTA 6
Le duo électronique français Justice, formé par Gaspard Augé et Xavier de Rosnay, signe cette bande originale de 30 nouveaux morceaux, soit environ trois heures de musique. Deux titres sont déjà mis en avant : Flower In A Hurricane, qui réunit Tame Impala, SZA et King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard, et Pusher, enregistré avec Gesaffelstein. Le premier accompagne notamment la bande-annonce de lancement du jeu, tandis que le second a été dévoilé ce jeudi 29 octobre.
Le même jour, l’Original Score sortira aussi sur les principales plateformes de streaming musical. Plusieurs morceaux bonus en numérique sont inclus dans tous les formats.
Cette Original Score est à distinguer de GTA VI: The Album, qui rassemble 34 chansons de différents artistes et sortira le 19 novembre, le même jour que le jeu. L’Original Score correspond, elle, à la musique composée par Justice pour accompagner le jeu, en grande partie instrumentale.
L’édition limitée de Grand Theft Auto VI: Original Score est présentée sous la forme d’un triple vinyle Crystal Clear. Les trois disques transparents sont rangés dans une pochette ouvrante avec une finition brillante (vernis UV). Comme les deux autres éditions, elle donne aussi accès à plusieurs morceaux bonus en numérique.
Cette édition coûte 4 euros de plus que la version noire, pour exactement les mêmes morceaux : seule la couleur des disques change.
Les trois éditions arriveront le 11 décembre 2026, un peu plus de trois semaines après le jeu. D’ici là, deux morceaux de la bande originale de Justice sont déjà disponibles en écoute, Flower In A Hurricane et Pusher.

articles.title: Bioplastique, format carte bancaire : à quoi va ressembler le cash de demain ?
articles.text:
Bioplastique, format carte bancaire : à quoi va ressembler le cash de demain ?
L’imprimerie fédérale allemande réinvente le billet de banque à l’heure du tout-numérique
L'imprimerie fédérale allemande vient de dévoiler STELLA, un prototype de billet de banque réduit au format 85 × 54 mm, soit exactement la taille d'une carte de crédit. Imprimé sur un polymère biosourcé, bardé de dispositifs de sécurité inédits, il dessine ce que pourrait devenir l'argent liquide dans un monde qui ne jure plus que par le sans-contact.
Vous pensiez que le billet de banque avait atteint sa forme définitive ? La Bundesdruckerei, institution bicentenaire qui imprime les documents les plus sensibles de l'État allemand, vient de prouver le contraire. Présenté le 13 mai à la Banknote Conference de Washington, STELLA est un billet noir au format carte bancaire, deuxième prototype de la série expérimentale EX NIHILO, après IGNIS, déjà primé en 2024, qui intégrait une puce ultrafine dans du papier noir.
Moins de matière, plus de sécurité
Le substrat de STELLA est un polymère fabriqué à partir de matières premières renouvelables, non fossiles. Résultat : une durée de vie prolongée dans le circuit monétaire et une empreinte environnementale réduite. Le format miniaturisé permet de produire près de cent billets par feuille d'impression, contre une poignée pour un billet classique. Moins de substrat, moins d'encre, moins d'énergie.
Malgré cette cure d'amincissement, STELLA ne sacrifie rien en matière de sécurité : la Bundesdruckerei a développé un design “bord à bord” : les éléments de protection courent jusqu'aux extrémités du billet, certains scindés en deux moitiés qui se complètent d'une face à l'autre. Encres réactives à l'infrarouge, lentille intégrée qui projette des images par réfraction, encoches tactiles pour les personnes malvoyantes. Le tout compressé sur 46 cm².
Le cash mute
La pression du numérique est visible partout en Europe. En France, les paiements par carte ont dépassé les espèces dans les commerces pour la première fois en 2024 : 48 % des transactions ont été réglées par carte, contre 43 % en liquide. Pourtant, 95 % des commerçants français acceptent toujours les espèces. Un paradoxe qui résume bien l'époque : tandis que l'Europe construit son autonomie dans les paiements numériques avec des initiatives comme Wero, l'Allemagne explore déjà ce que pourrait devenir le billet de banque du futur.

articles.title: El jefe de Instagram asegura que el rechazo y el miedo a la IA van a empeorar en los próximos años
articles.text:
Adam Mosseri, jefe de Instagram, anticipó que el rechazo hacia la inteligencia artificial (IA) seguirá creciendo entre los usuarios por la ansiedad, la frustración y el temor a que esta tecnología los deje atrás, sobre todo en los sectores creativos.
El máximo responsable de la red social de Meta sostuvo en el podcast Colin y Samir que la percepción ya se deteriora en las plataformas de Meta y que la tendencia continuará durante los próximos años.
Por qué crece el temor y la ansiedad hacia la inteligencia artificial
Mosseri afirmó que las inquietudes de los usuarios abarcan la propiedad de sus contenidos, el entrenamiento de modelos de IA con ese material, la seguridad de los datos personales y el posible reemplazo de puestos de trabajo. La preocupación alcanza tanto a creadores de contenido como a ingenieros y matemáticos.
Para Mosseri, ese conjunto de temores se concentra en una sensación común: el miedo a perder terreno frente a una transformación tecnológica que avanza con rapidez.
“Creo que veremos más frustración y enfado, parte fundado, parte infundado, en los próximos años, y eso lo va a complicar para mucha gente, no solo en la industria”, afirmó.
Cuáles sectores son los que más sienten repulsión y dudas hacia la IA
Las industrias creativas concentran una inquietud más intensa, según Mosseri, que defendió la adopción de herramientas que otorguen capacidades a las personas en lugar de hacerles sentir que no obtienen beneficios de ellas. En el caso de la plataforma, planteó que la inteligencia artificial debe servir para “darle poder a las personas creativas”.
En este sentido, Instagram actualizó en agosto de 2026 sus etiquetas para perfiles creados con inteligencia artificial, con el objetivo de que los usuarios puedan distinguirlos de las cuentas administradas por personas. La medida busca hacer visible el origen automatizado de una identidad dentro de la red social.
El directivo admitió que esa distinción será cada vez más compleja a medida que mejoren los sistemas de generación de imágenes, videos y textos. Agregó que no todos los materiales producidos con inteligencia artificial son deficientes, pero reconoció la abundancia de slop, contenido de baja calidad creado de forma automatizada.
Ante las dudas, Mosseri sostuvo que la plataforma intentará dirigir más tráfico hacia los autores originales cuando existan versiones automatizadas de sus trabajos. Si un creador de inteligencia artificial reproduce contenido de forma descarada, consideró que sería conveniente determinar qué acción corresponde adoptar.
La red social ya dispone de un mecanismo para presentar reclamos por derechos de autor y retirar material protegido que haya sido robado. El responsable de Instagram definió el problema como complejo por la creciente dificultad para distinguir entre una obra original, una imitación y un contenido generado por inteligencia artificial.
Qué dicen otros líderes sobre el avance de la inteligencia artificial
La expansión de capacidades técnicas de la IA preocupa a Sam Altman, director ejecutivo de OpenAI, quien advirtió que la próxima generación de modelos de inteligencia artificial podría plantear riesgos que gobiernos, empresas y usuarios aún no comprenden por completo.
Altman señaló que los sistemas más avanzados podrían descubrir vulnerabilidades fuera de los mecanismos habituales de ciberseguridad. Esa posibilidad obligaría a revisar la protección de redes, equipos e infraestructuras ante modelos con niveles de autonomía más amplios.
El ejecutivo cuestionó la preparación institucional ante ese escenario: “No encuentro una palabra lo bastante dramática para describir el problema que se nos viene encima”.
La preocupación incluye posibles vulnerabilidades en programas informáticos y en componentes físicos, como chips, servidores y redes. Según la mente detrás de ChatGPT, los próximos modelos de IA podrían encontrar “fallos increíbles” que no forman parte de los cálculos convencionales de seguridad.

articles.title: ¿Se ha acabado el espacio de almacenamiento del teléfono? La razón puede estar en otro lugar que no sean las fotos
articles.text:
Borras cientos de fotos y vídeos de la galería y tu Android sigue mostrando que falta espacio. Puede que sea normal y que no sea culpa de la galería. El uso del móvil genera archivos temporales de las aplicaciones y vídeos recibidos por mensajería, además de contenido descargado para verlo sin conexión de internet y archivos de los que quizá te hayas olvidado.
¿Por dónde se empieza? Ajustes > Almacenamiento, donde, según la ayuda de Google, debes seleccionar una categoría para ver cuánto ocupa (ese menú es diferente según cada fabricante). Allí puedes ver cuánto ocupan las aplicaciones y los archivos multimedia por separado, sin haber hecho nada.
Ten en cuenta que la eliminación de fotos quizá no libere el espacio al instante. Lo que se haya eliminado puede quedar en la papelera de la galería hasta que pasa cierto tiempo y se elimina definitivamente. La papelera de Google Fotos, por ejemplo, almacena los elementos 30 días y se borran antes si vacías la papelera, y no pueden recuperarse una vez vaciada. Por lo tanto, vacía también la papelera.
Las aplicaciones almacenan archivos temporales, o caché, para mejorar su funcionamiento. Por ejemplo, Spotify admite explícitamente (en su centro de ayuda) que almacena parte de la música y los podcasts en la memoria del móvil en forma de caché, además de los archivos descargados para escucharlos sin conexión. Lo más seguro es que vacíes la caché, ya que almacena datos temporales (la propia aplicación podría tardar un poco más en abrirse). Esto se hace en el menú de Ajustes del móvil en la información de cada aplicación; la ruta es diferente según el fabricante del terminal.
Mensajería: WhatsApp y Telegram
Las aplicaciones de mensajería suelen ser las más propensas a acumular datos. En el caso de WhatsApp, hay una herramienta incorporada llamada “Administrar el almacenamiento” (en Ajustes > Almacenamiento y datos), que muestra cuánto espacio ocupa la aplicación y analiza los archivos grandes o reenviados, ordenados por tamaño y filtrados para ver los de más de 5 MB (según el centro de ayuda de WhatsApp). Lo que se borra así desaparecerá de la aplicación para siempre y solo para ti; y, si tu teléfono contiene varias copias de ese archivo, tendrás que encontrarlas todas para liberar el espacio.
Si es un grupo de WhatsApp el que más espacio ocupa, en lugar de borrar todo el grupo, simplemente abre la conversación y toca el nombre del grupo en la parte superior, donde aparecerá Administrar el almacenamiento (o bien borra solo los archivos multimedia y no los mensajes). Nosotros describimos cinco pasos para limpiar WhatsApp y, ese mismo mes, también relatamos cómo vaciar 70 GB de chats, tras exportarlos a un ordenador o a un disco duro externo, con los pasos detallados para iPhone.
Telegram permite eliminar la caché de los archivos multimedia desde la propia aplicación. En Ajustes > Datos y almacenamiento > Uso del almacenamiento, hay opciones para borrar el caché de los chats privados, los grupos y los canales, con la posibilidad de excluir chats específicos, según explicó el propio servicio en diciembre de 2022: se puede borrar todo lo que se descarga en la aplicación y, posteriormente, volver a descargarlo desde la nube de Telegram.
Juegos y descargas sin conexión
Los grandes juegos pueden tener un engaño. El requisito de espacio para instalar el juego no refleja el tamaño actual del juego, y el requisito de espacio tampoco indica si el juego va a descargar más datos adicionales. Según la documentación de Android para desarrolladores, hay juegos en los que el tamaño de instalación es pequeño, pero que van descargando datos adicionales más tarde, y juegos que descargan varios gigabytes.
Lo mismo ocurre con los archivos de medios descargados para almacenarlos temporalmente: por ejemplo, la ayuda de Netflix describe cómo borrar cualquier descarga de la lista de Descargas o, en Ajustes, en Mi Netflix, borrar todas las descargas.
Herramientas para limpiar y archivar
La carpeta Descargas es un gran acumulador de archivos de los que quizá te hayas olvidado, a saber: PDF, archivos comprimidos y otros guardados hace años y que ocupan espacio. Te aconsejo que la examines por tu cuenta.
Para cualquier otra cosa, existe una aplicación de Google llamada Files by Google. En su Menú > Limpiar, la tarjeta de archivos basura (según el centro de ayuda de Google) borra información temporal de las aplicaciones sin tocar sus ajustes; sin embargo, lo que se borra se pierde para siempre, mientras que la opción de archivos duplicados (del mismo centro de ayuda) marca una copia como original y Google recomienda conservarla.
El Almacenamiento inteligente de Android te permite eliminar fotos y vídeos que se han guardado con copia de seguridad en tu cuenta de Google, activándolo en Ajustes > Almacenamiento > Liberar espacio.
Las siguientes indicaciones pueden ayudarte a organizar el trabajo: en primer lugar, los ajustes para saber en qué se está perdiendo espacio; segundo, las aplicaciones que ocupan más espacio y su caché; la mensajería, las cosas descargadas para verlas sin conexión, la carpeta Descargas y la papelera con fotos de la galería, en ese orden. Eliminar cientos de fotos puede ser un esfuerzo inútil si el peso está dentro de unas cuantas aplicaciones muy utilizadas.
Cuando se trata de una aplicación que ocupa mucho espacio en tu móvil y de la que apenas utilizas una o ninguna función, existe la opción de archivar la aplicación. El centro de ayuda de Android describe que, al archivar una aplicación, el sistema quita el software y los permisos, borra los archivos temporales y detiene las notificaciones, pero conserva el icono y los datos.
Esto se hace en Ajustes > Aplicaciones, seleccionando una aplicación y pulsando Archivar; para reactivar el icono de la aplicación, toca el icono que tiene en tu pantalla de inicio; sin embargo, la aplicación debe estar disponible en su respectiva tienda de aplicaciones. Google advierte de que algunos de estos pasos solo estarán disponibles en Android 15 o versiones posteriores.
