- Un SSD de 1 To (822 Go d’espace disponible au déballage)

articles.title: Banque Populaire et Caisse d’Épargne : des paiements affichés en double et des virements perturbés, que se passe-t-il ?
articles.text:
Si vous êtes clients de la Banque Populaire ou de la Caisse d’Épargne, vous avez peut-être remarqué un message inhabituel sur votre application bancaire. Ce jeudi 29 octobre 2026, certains utilisateurs sont avertis d’un incident susceptible de provoquer des débits en double sur leurs comptes.
« Nous vous informons qu’un incident touchant une autre banque française est susceptible de provoquer un débit en double de certains paiements par carte bancaire. Une régularisation est en cours », peut-on lire sur une capture d’écran transmise à Numerama.
Selon un conseiller bancaire interrogé par Numerama, les paiements pourraient apparaître deux fois dans l’historique des opérations, sans que les sommes soient réellement débitées deux fois. Cette information n’a toutefois pas encore été confirmée officiellement par le groupe BPCE — le message parle bien « d’un débit en double ».
Un incident qui concernerait très peu de clients de la Banque Populaire et la Caisse d’Épargne
Les paiements par carte ne sont pas les seuls concernés par les signalements. Plusieurs utilisateurs rapportent également des difficultés pour effectuer des virements bancaires. Selon une source interrogée par Numerama, un dysfonctionnement de Sécur’Pass, le système d’authentification utilisé notamment pour valider les virements et certains paiements en ligne, pourrait être à l’origine de ces difficultés.
Un client de la Caisse d’Épargne a également témoigné auprès de Numerama. Il indique avoir pu effectuer un virement instantané, bien pris en compte par sa banque, mais dont la somme n’apparaissait toujours pas sur le compte du destinataire.
Contacté par Numerama, le groupe BPCE, auquel appartiennent la Banque Populaire et la Caisse d’Épargne, se veut quant à lui rassurant. Selon lui, l’incident ne concernerait qu’un très faible nombre de clients et devrait être résolu rapidement. Le groupe confirme que le dysfonctionnement provient d’une autre banque française, sans toutefois préciser laquelle ni donner davantage de détails sur son origine.
Ce n’est pas la première fois que plusieurs banques françaises sont confrontées à ce type de problème. En janvier 2026, des clients de la Banque Populaire, de la Caisse d’Épargne, de BoursoBank et du Crédit Coopératif avaient constaté des paiements erronés sur leurs comptes.
L’incident provenait de Monext, une filiale du Crédit Mutuel Arkéa spécialisée dans les paiements. Dans un communiqué publié le 30 janvier, le groupe expliquait qu’un problème technique avait entraîné le traitement en double de transactions déjà comptabilisées entre 2023 et 2025.
Rien ne permet toutefois, à ce stade, d’affirmer que l’incident du 29 octobre a la même origine. En attendant la régularisation annoncée, les clients concernés peuvent garder un œil sur leurs opérations bancaires, notamment sur les éventuels paiements affichés en double.

articles.title: The EU-Startups Podcast | Interview with Jack Mardack, co-founder of Oyster | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Key points:
- Why impact should be treated as a design problem built into a business model from day one, rather than a values commitment bolted on later
- The difference between impact by intention and impact by design – and how founders and investors can tell the difference
- What it takes to prove impact with evidence, and why investors should fund proof rather than claims
- What replaces the ESG scorecard as the scorecard era comes to an end
- A ten-year vision for the European workforce if talent, capital, and opportunity finally connect across borders
In this conversation, recorded ahead of the MeOut Summit in Budapest, we sit down with Jack Mardack, co-founder of Oyster, the global employment platform that became one of only a handful of companies in the world to reach unicorn status while holding B Corp certification.
Jack shares what he learned scaling Oyster, why he believes the perceived trade-off between financial success and impact is a design failure rather than an economic law, and what the role of Chief Impact Officer actually involves day to day.
We also get into the bigger picture: why the ESG debate has become more ideological than useful, why the notable impact investing market suggests investors have already moved past that argument, and what it would mean for European capital allocation if investors started funding evidence of impact instead of claims of impact.
Finally, we look ahead: whether Europe is measuring itself against the US on the wrong dimensions, what the European workforce could look like in ten years if we get better at connecting talent, capital, and opportunity across borders, and why Jack will be sitting down at the MeOut Summit in Budapest with the founder of Hungary’s first B Corp. His book, “Impact Unleashed: Building Businesses That Scale Positive Change“, unpacks many of these ideas in depth.

articles.title: 3 Ways AI Agents Already Operate in Your Browser
articles.text:
Which AI agents can act inside your employees' browsers today? If an agent started browsing this morning, would you know it wasn't the employee? Most security teams can't answer those questions yet. That's not a failure of effort. It's a sign of how quickly AI moved from answering questions to taking action.
AI agents now operate browsers inside authenticated applications, and they get there in different ways: debugging interfaces, extensions, agentic browsers, and emerging standards like WebMCP. Each changes what an agent can access, how its actions are attributed, and whether existing controls can see them.
1. Remote Debugging: Applications Controlling the Browser
One way AI agents operate browsers isn't new at all. It's the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
CDP was built to help developers inspect, debug, and automate Chromium-based browsers. It provides programmatic access to navigation, page content, network activity, and user interactions. Tools like Playwright and Puppeteer have used it for years. AI agents use the same approach to navigate websites, extract information, fill forms, and interact with web applications.
The key distinction: automation doesn't have to originate inside the browser. An external application can connect to a browser with debugging enabled and control its tabs. If that browser has authenticated sessions, the automation can use that access.
To most security tools, a browser launched with debugging enabled and signed into corporate applications looks like any other authenticated browser session.
The question to ask: Which applications can launch or connect to debuggable browsers? Do your policies permit this, and which corporate sessions can those applications access?
2. AI Extensions and Agentic Browsers
The second approach puts the agent directly inside the browser.
Extensions such as Claude in Chrome can read pages, switch tabs, click buttons, and complete multistep workflows. This requires powerful permissions, including scripting, tab access, and the debugger API. These permissions enable the functionality but also expand what the extension can access.
Agentic browsers like Perplexity Comet and ChatGPT Desktop go further, building AI directly into the browsing experience. These capabilities aren't necessarily governed by extension permissions, so existing extension controls may not apply.
Without an inventory of browsers across your fleet, you may not know which agents are operating. Two risks stand out.
Agents act with the user's identity. When an agent downloads a document or changes an internal application setting, the application sees an authenticated user making an authorized request.
Without additional telemetry, neither the application nor its audit logs may distinguish the agent's actions from the employee's.
Agents treat content as input. A browser displays a page for someone to interpret. An agent reads that page and decides what to do next. This introduces prompt injection risks, where instructions embedded in websites, documents, or emails attempt to redirect its behavior.
The result is software interpreting untrusted content while operating with trusted permissions.
The question to ask: Which AI extensions and agentic browsers are running across your fleet, what access do they have, and can you distinguish their actions from an employee's?
Your security stack sees the login, not the agent
Once an AI agent is inside an authenticated tab, endpoint and network tools lose sight of what it reads and does.
Keep Aware monitors AI activity in the browser and enforces data protection policies before sensitive data leaves the tab.
Request a demo
3. WebMCP: Websites Exposing Tools Directly to Agents
The third approach changes how websites interact with agents.
WebMCP is an emerging web standard developed through the W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group, with contributions from Google and Microsoft. Rather than interpreting pages and simulating clicks, agents can call structured tools exposed directly by websites.
For example, instead of navigating a support portal and filling out forms, an agent could call a tool to create a ticket. Chrome introduced an early preview in 2026, and the specification continues to evolve.
But this introduces a new trust problem. Websites aren't just presenting content. They're defining actions agents can take.
Tool names, descriptions, and input schemas guide what an agent invokes. These definitions come from the website and shouldn't be treated as trusted instructions. A compromised or malicious site could use misleading descriptions or functionality to influence an agent's behavior.
Each tool operates within its website's security context, but agents working across multiple sites can move information between them. The concern isn't just what a tool does, but what data the agent provides when calling it.
The question to ask: What corporate data can agents pass to website tools, where does that data go, and can you control which tools they use?
What This Means for Browser Security
All three approaches share one thing: software is acting on websites with the access tied to a user's browser session.
That's why browser security can't assume a human is behind every click anymore. Endpoint, network, and application controls still matter. But they were built to see processes, traffic, and logins, not what an agent reads, decides, and does inside an authenticated tab. That's the gap.
The goal isn't to stop employees from using AI agents. Agents are going to become a normal part of how work gets done. The goal is to make sure the controls you already expect in the browser keep applying when an agent is the one operating it.
See What's Operating Your Browsers

We help you discover AI-enabled browsers and extensions, monitor AI activity across your workforce, and enforce data protection policies before sensitive information leaves the tab.

articles.title: Cómo los nombres de usuarios en WhatsApp pueden convertirse en un riesgo de suplantación
articles.text:
WhatsApp abrió a finales de junio de 2026 la reserva de nombres de usuario, una función que permite hablar con desconocidos sin entregar el número de teléfono. La promesa de privacidad convive con un riesgo: la suplantación de identidad.
Reservar un nombre casi idéntico al de una persona, una marca o una institución es más sencillo de lo que parece, y la propia compañía reconoce el problema al bloquear de antemano ciertos nombres.
Cómo funciona el nuevo sistema de nombres de usuario
El nombre de usuario es opcional y conviven dos vías para definirlo. La primera es reutilizar el identificador que ya existe en Instagram o Facebook. La segunda, crear uno separado, exclusivo para WhatsApp. Quien prefiera no tocar nada puede seguir usando el número de teléfono como hasta ahora.
El proceso se activa desde Ajustes > Cuenta > Nombre de usuario, admite solo letras minúsculas, números, puntos y guiones bajos, y requiere al menos una letra. Como cada nombre es único, la aplicación ofrece un generador de sugerencias para cuando la opción deseada ya está tomada.
Existe además una clave de nombre de usuario, también opcional, que funciona como un código adicional: quien conozca el nombre público de una persona necesita también esa clave para iniciarle una conversación. Activarla tiene sentido para quien va a publicar su nombre de usuario en una red social, una web o una tarjeta de presentación.
El riesgo de vincular el nombre con Instagram y Facebook
La organización de consumidores holandesa Consumentenbond advirtió sobre un efecto colateral de reutilizar el mismo nombre en las tres aplicaciones. Para reclamar en WhatsApp el nombre ya usado en Instagram o Facebook, Meta exige vincular las cuentas a través del Centro de Cuentas.
Esa vinculación no afecta el contenido de los mensajes, que siguen siendo privados, pero sí facilita que la identidad de WhatsApp quede conectada con otros perfiles públicos de la persona. Según las páginas de ayuda de la propia Meta, el Centro de Cuentas está diseñado para administrar experiencias conectadas entre Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp y otros productos, y permite compartir información entre esas cuentas vinculadas.
Esa coincidencia de nombres también abre una puerta a la ingeniería social: si alguien detecta o adivina el nombre de estilo Meta de una persona, puede cruzar esa información con lo que encuentre en sus perfiles de redes sociales para preparar un fraude dirigido.
Por eso, un nombre de usuario de WhatsApp exclusivo, distinto del usado en otras redes, reduce esa posibilidad de conexión entre cuentas y limita el margen de maniobra de quien intenta suplantar una identidad para estafar o acosar a otra persona.
Cómo protegerse de la suplantación de identidad
Ocultar el número de teléfono no elimina al estafador, solo le cierra una vía de ataque. Conviene elegir un nombre reconocible pero sin datos personales innecesarios, activar la clave de nombre de usuario si va a compartirse en abierto y desconfiar de mensajes inesperados aunque el remitente parezca legítimo.
Las organizaciones reales rara vez contactan sin aviso previo por una aplicación de mensajería, de modo que cualquier petición relacionada con dinero, contraseñas o información confidencial debería verificarse por otro canal antes de responder.
Mantener la aplicación actualizada y revisar periódicamente los ajustes de privacidad completa el conjunto de hábitos recomendados mientras la función de nombres de usuario termina de desplegarse en el resto de los países.
El ejemplo de suplantación en India
India encendió la alerta sobre los nombres de usuario de WhatsApp. TechCrunch halló disponibles identificadores que recordaban a figuras del país, como “indiamodi”, “shahrukh.actor” y “rbi_verify”, en referencia a Narendra Modi, actores de Bollywood y el banco central indio, aunque sin evidencia de uso fraudulento.
El caso sumó otro capítulo cuando “cz_binance” apareció como no disponible. Changpeng Zhao, fundador de Binance, aseguró: “Lo intenté, no pude reservar ese nombre. Así que, definitivamente, no fui yo”. Quién lo reservó sigue sin confirmarse.
El Ministerio de Electrónica y Tecnología de la Información indio notificó a WhatsApp que la función podría facilitar la suplantación de ciudadanos, organismos públicos y entidades financieras, y pidió pausar su despliegue en el país. Meta respondió que reserva preventivamente nombres de figuras públicas y gobiernos, y permite vincular identificadores con Instagram o Facebook.

articles.title: Iiyama X2793HSU-B1 : cet écran PC 27 pouces à 120 Hz chute sous les 85 euros — Frandroid
articles.text:
Un deuxième écran à côté du PC portable, un poste de télétravail plus confortable ou trois moniteurs alignés pour suivre vos tableurs : l’Iiyama X2793HSU-B1 vise précisément ces usages. Il propose une grande dalle IPS de 27 pouces, un taux de rafraîchissement de 120 Hz, et des bordures fines sur les quatre côtés. On reste sur un écran de bureau en Full HD, sans prétention gaming haut de gamme. À moins de 85 euros, il devient en revanche une option très sérieuse face aux 27 pouces d’entrée de gamme vendus par Dell, AOC ou Samsung.
Les atouts de l’Iiyama X2793HSU-B1
- Une dalle IPS de 27 pouces en Full HD, 350 cd/m²
- Un taux de rafraîchissement de 120 Hz, 1 ms de réponse (MPRT)
- Des bords fins sur quatre côtés, pratiques en multi-écran
Habituellement vendu 119,99 euros, l’Iiyama X2793HSU-B1 descend à 84,87 euros sur Joybuy, soit 35,12 euros de moins (environ 29 % de remise).
Protégez votre vie numérique avec Bitdefender, la protection européenne de confiance. Bitdefender vous protège contre les arnaques et les fraudes du web. Profitez de vos activités en ligne en toute tranquillité.
Un 27 pouces qui se fait discret dans une installation multi-écran
La dalle IPS de 27 pouces affiche une définition de 1920 × 1080 pixels, avec une luminosité de 350 cd/m² et un contraste annoncé de 1500:1. La technologie IPS assure de larges angles de vision, ce qui compte vraiment quand on aligne deux ou trois écrans et qu’on regarde ceux des côtés en biais. Les bordures fines sur les quatre côtés limitent la coupure entre deux moniteurs, et le design reste sobre sur un bureau. Cependant, il faut garder une limite en tête. Le Full HD étalé sur 27 pouces donne environ 82 pixels par pouce, donc un texte un peu moins net que sur un 24 pouces de même définition (si vous collez le nez à l’écran, vous verrez les pixels).
La connectique couvre l’essentiel avec une entrée HDMI, une entrée DisplayPort, un hub de deux ports USB et une prise casque. Le hub USB est utile pour brancher un clavier ou une souris directement sur l’écran. Il n’y a pas d’USB-C dans la liste, donc un PC portable récent passera par le HDMI ou par un adaptateur.
Des journées entières devant l’écran sans trop fatiguer
Les 120 Hz sont l’argument le plus intéressant de cette fiche technique. Sur un écran de bureau, ça se voit dès les premières minutes : le défilement d’une page web ou d’un long document devient plus fluide, tout comme le déplacement des fenêtres. Le temps de réponse de 1 ms annoncé et les 120 Hz permettent aussi quelques parties en Full HD le soir. Ce n’est clairement pas un écran pensé pour l’e-sport, mais pour une partie de temps en temps, ça fait le taf.
Pour les longues sessions, Iiyama a prévu une dalle sans scintillement et un réducteur de lumière bleue. Les haut-parleurs intégrés (2 x 2 watts) dépannent pour une visioconférence ou une vidéo YouTube, mais un casque branché sur la prise jack fera mieux pour la musique.

articles.title: NAISH: Inside Nigeria's $7.5M Gates-backed AI scaling hub
articles.text:
At Moonshot by TechCabal 2026, the Nigeria AI Scaling Hub (NAISH) showcased five organisations developing artificial intelligence solutions for healthcare, agriculture, and local languages, underscoring how shared digital infrastructure and institutional partnerships can transition local research into widespread commercial adoption.
The initiative brought together digital health provider mDoc, agritech platform Extension Africa, research enterprise Data Science Nigeria, language engine Awarri, and the Masakhane African Languages Hub to demonstrate how targeted machine-learning applications can solve tangible development challenges across the continent.
NAISH is backed by the Gates Foundation, which committed up to $7.5 million over three years to bridge the chasm between experimental prototypes and real-world national deployment.
Hosted by Lagos Business School and supported by the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy (FMCIDE), the hub functions as an operational springboard. It connects local innovators with compute credits, proprietary data pipelines, and policy frameworks needed to move beyond pilot purgatory into enterprise production.
The platform concentrates on critical public-interest sectors—principally healthcare, agriculture, education, and financial services—where automated tools can directly alleviate capacity deficits and improve service delivery.
Its focus includes priority sectors such as healthcare, agriculture, education, and financial services, where AI could improve service delivery, expand access to information, and help address persistent development challenges.
Using AI to improve healthcare and agricultural access
Among the showcased ventures, digital health company mDoc leverages conversational AI and virtual coaching to manage chronic illnesses, providing patients with continuous care protocols outside overburdened public hospitals.
However, as the company noted, technical efficacy in healthcare means little without secure health-data integration and patient accessibility across low-bandwidth environments.
In agriculture, Extension Africa pairs machine-learning models with a network of human field agents to deliver hyper-local agronomic advice to remote smallholders.
Reaching dispersed farming communities has historically proved prohibitively expensive; NAISH offsets these unit economics by brokering shared cloud credits, localized data infrastructure, and corporate partnerships. The collaboration proves that scaling agritech requires operational scaffolding as much as sophisticated algorithms.
Building AI around Nigerian languages
Two of the organisations showcased at Moonshot 2026 are working to address another challenge in AI adoption: the limited representation of African languages in digital technologies.
awarri is developing AI models that support Nigerian languages, including Igbo, Yoruba, and Hausa, as well as Nigerian Pidgin. Its technology supports translation and transcription and can be integrated into other systems.
Language remains an important consideration in making AI accessible to people who may be less comfortable interacting with technology in English.
Voice-based tools and local-language interfaces could expand how people access digital services, including those offered by businesses and public institutions.
awarri’s work also points to the need for AI systems that reflect Nigeria’s linguistic diversity rather than relying exclusively on technologies developed around more widely represented languages.
NAISH is helping the company showcase its work and its approach to scaling AI solutions, connecting its technology with a broader ecosystem focused on practical deployment.
The Masakhane African Languages Hub is pursuing a related goal through research and development in natural language processing (NLP), a field of AI concerned with how computers process and understand human language.
Anchored by the Masakhane Research Foundation, the initiative seeks to address the underrepresentation of African languages in AI research and digital technology. Its work centres on strengthening African-language research and ensuring that African researchers play a leading role in developing technologies for their communities.
Together, the two initiatives demonstrate why local language capabilities matter to the development of AI systems that are relevant to African users.
Serving as NAISH’s principal technical implementation partner, Data Science Nigeria (DSN) presented VoiceAgent, a conversational platform enabling government agencies and commercial enterprises to deploy interactive voice assistants.
Because voice-first computing bypasses literacy barriers, solutions like VoiceAgent allow citizens to query essential services through simple phone calls. DSN’s involvement provides NAISH with the engineering depth required to help early-stage ventures build, deploy, and maintain systems in complex field conditions.
Turning funding into measurable impact
The showcase at Moonshot 2026 reflected a mature shift in Nigeria’s technology dialogue: moving beyond vanity demos to solve structural inefficiencies.
While catalytic philanthropy from the Gates Foundation and backing from the Ministry of Communications provide foundational fuel, the real test for NAISH lies ahead.
Its ultimate success will not be measured by the sophistication of algorithms in laboratory settings, but by whether these five innovators can deliver cheaper medical interventions, higher crop yields, and accessible public services to millions of ordinary Nigerians.

articles.title: Un propietario aparca su moto junto a su coche en la misma plaza de garaje y los vecinos se quejan: la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal aclara los límites y si la comunidad le puede sancionar
articles.text:
Seguro que no te resulta extraño ver cómo un coche y una moto comparten una plaza de garaje, aprovechando al máximo el espacio y dejando un margen mínimo para maniobrar. Y puede que alguna vez te hayas preguntado si eso realmente se puede hacer, porque una cosa es que los dos vehículos quepan y otra que puedan dejarse allí sin más.
La Ley de Propiedad Horizontal responde a esta duda: no prohíbe de forma general aparcar un coche y una moto en la misma plaza.
Pero sí hay matices respecto al espacio que ocupan. La moto puede tener las ruedas dentro de las líneas y, aun así, sobresalir. Lo esencial es que los dos vehículos deben quedar dentro de la plaza y dejar libres las zonas de paso, sin dificultar las maniobras de los demás. Si el vecino tiene que esquivar una moto que invade el pasillo para poder salir, ya hay un problema que reclamar.
El artículo 9.1 de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal obliga a respetar los elementos comunes y a actuar con diligencia en las relaciones con los otros propietarios. Eso exige que, en el caso de que queramos reclarmar como vecinos, debamos concretar el motivo de la queja ya que la mera presencia de dos vehículos no demuestra que se esté incumpliendo una norma.
La comunidad también puede aprobar reglas de convivencia y de uso de las zonas comunes, como recoge el artículo sexto de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal. Estas deben respetar la legislación y los estatutos. Ahora bien, la ley no establece una multa automática por aparcar juntos el coche y la moto, y aprobarla en una reunión tampoco basta, por sí solo, para convertirla en una deuda exigible.
La reclamación sí puede llegar a los tribunales si se incumplen los estatutos o se realizan actividades que dañen la finca o contravengan las disposiciones sobre actividades molestas, insalubres, nocivas, peligrosas o ilícitas. Estos son los supuestos que recoge el artículo 7.2 de la misma ley. En esos casos, el presidente debe requerir que cese la actividad y, si el incumplimiento continúa, la junta puede autorizar la acción judicial para ponerle fin.
En cualquier caso, antes de discutir si hay que retirar la moto, conviene saber qué se está reclamando exactamente: una invasión del pasillo, una maniobra que queda bloqueada o una prohibición aplicable a esa plaza.

articles.title: Amazon Echo Show 16 : ce que propose le nouvel écran connecté
articles.text:
Amazon Echo Show 16 : agenda familial, maison connectée et Fire TV sur le même écran
La maison s'affiche
Avec l'Echo Show 16, Amazon réunit un téléviseur d'appoint, un agenda familial et des commandes domotiques sur un écran de 16 pouces. Sorti aux US, il faudra attendre encore pour espérer le voir débarquer en France.
Amazon veut confier au même écran un rendez-vous à ne pas oublier, une recette à suivre et une série pour vous accompagner pendant la cuisine. Annoncé aux États-Unis, l'Echo Show 16 est un écran connecté à installer au mur ou sur un support, avec une interface consacrée l'organisation familiale, à la maison connectée ou aux photos.
Amazon Echo Show 16
- 
                    
                        Amazon Echo Show 8 (3e génération) Meilleur prix : 169.99 €Voir le produit
- 
                    
                        SwitchBot AI Art Frame Meilleur prix : 149.99 €Voir le produit
Plusieurs types d'écran d'accueil sont proposées. Dans le mode familial, l'appareil rassemble les agendas avec des codes couleur, les tâches à attribuer, les menus de la semaine et les recettes enregistrées.
Le mode domotique affiche en permanence les commandes des équipements compatibles Alexa comme l'éclairage, le thermostat ou la diffusion musicale. Il peut aussi accueillir Alexa Home Map, une représentation interactive en 3D du logement sur laquelle les appareils sont positionnés.
Un autre mode transforme l'ensemble en cadre photo, avec une sélection manuelle des images ou des suggestions d'Alexa. Une barre latérale personnalisable donne accès aux fonctions favorites.
La dalle Full HD de 16 pouces offre s'agrandit 10 % par rapport à celle de l'Echo Show 15. Elle prend aussi place dans un cadre en aluminium plus fin. Amazon y loge huit petits haut-parleurs de graves et deux tweeters dans le boîtier. Une version baptisée Nanomatte propose une surface de verre texturée pour réduire les reflets.
Fire TV est intégré et la télécommande permet de naviguer parmi les services de streaming. L'Echo Show 16 peut donc servir de téléviseur d'appoint.
Alexa+ prend ses quartiers
La caméra grand-angle de 13 mégapixels dispose d'un cadrage automatique pour les appels vidéo. Amazon annonce aussi une portée de reconnaissance visuelle d'environ 5 m et l'arrivée de la vision nocturne. Cette dernière permet de consulter la pièce dans l'obscurité depuis l'application Alexa. Un bouton latéral sert à désactiver les microphones et la caméra.
Des capteurs de température et de présence peuvent par ailleurs déclencher des actions, comme allumer une lampe à l'arrivée d'un membre du foyer.
L'Echo Show 16 embarque enfin la nouvelle version d'Alexa+. En plus des échanges vocaux, l'assistant peut afficher des réponses visuelles avec des vidéos ou des événements du calendrier. Les informations liées à une tâche, comme une sortie prévue, sont regroupées dans des fiches consultables sur l'écran ou dans l'application.
Une addition encore en dollars
Aux États-Unis, les précommandes sont ouvertes à 499,99 $ pour l'écran standard et 569,99 $ pour le Nanomatte. Les livraisons doivent commencer avant la fin de l'année 2026. Les supports sont vendus séparément : 69,99 $ pour le modèle simple et 124,99 $ pour la version orientable et inclinable. Aucune date de commercialisation ni aucun prix n'ont encore été annoncés pour la France.

articles.title: « Beaucoup de choses ont changé » : pourquoi Apple s'est laissée convaincre par un MacBook avec écran tactile
articles.text:
Pour la première fois, Apple a présenté un MacBook Pro doté d’un écran tactile. On peut contrôler l’interface de macOS 27 au doigt directement sur l’écran. Pour Steve Jobs, fondateur d’Apple, c’était une hérésie : le bras fatigue trop vite. Vingt ans après, John Ternus a peut-être brisé un tabou avec ce nouveau MacBook Pro et le dirigeant d’Apple a ses raisons.
Comment ce tabou imposé par Steve Jobs a-t-il été rompu ?
Les explications viennent d’un article du journaliste Steven Levy publié dans Wired, dans lequel il interroge John Ternus, le responsable du matériel Johny Srouji ainsi que le responsable du marketing Greg Joswiak. Steven Levy raconte avoir interrogé en 2015 Phil Schiller, alors responsable du marketing produit chez Apple. Phil Schiller expliquait que « nous pensons que sur un ordinateur de bureau, avec un clavier fixe, devoir tendre le bras pour utiliser des interfaces tactiles est inconfortable ».
D’ailleurs, macOS demandait une grande précision permise par l’utilisation du curseur, contrairement à iPadOS ou à iOS : « ces deux univers [macOS et iOS/iPadOS] sont volontairement différents et c’est une bonne chose : nous pouvons ainsi optimiser l’expérience pour chacun ». Apple avait pourtant fait un petit effort en 2016, avec l’arrivée de la Touch Bar sur les MacBook Pro. Une petite langue sur toute la largeur du clavier qui était un écran qu’on pouvait contrôler pour mettre des raccourcis multimédia. Dix ans plus tard, Steven Levy demande frontalement à John Ternus si Apple ne serait pas sur le point de briser le tabou imposé par Steve Jobs de commercialiser un Mac avec un écran tactile. Le dirigeant répond : « Qui l’eût cru ? »
Les raisons d’Apple
Face aux polémiques des fans d’Apple et de Steve Jobs, le dirigeant d’Apple tente de tempérer : « Le Mac est avant tout un appareil à saisie indirecte, conçu autour du trackpad et du clavier. Mais je pense qu’il y a des moments où le tactile est pratique et confortable. » En clair, l’identité du MacBook Pro ne change pas : c’est toujours une machine à la pointe, dont la recette se bonifie avec le temps (et les itérations). John Ternus explique que « la fonction tactile ne dévalorise en rien le produit. Il ne l’alourdit pas, il ne l’épaissit pas. C’est ce que nous avons réalisé avec l’écran OLED, le meilleur écran jamais intégré à un Mac »
Pour Johny Srouji, « beaucoup de choses ont changé, qu’il s’agisse de la technologie d’affichage, des puces sur mesure, etc. » Apple utilisant des puces similaires entre iPhone, iPad et Mac, des dalles similaires, les difficultés matérielles se sont amoindries. La marque s’est laissée convaincre : « Je préfère que mes ingénieurs soient limités par les lois de la physique, et non par leur imagination ou des délais », ajoute Srouji.
Pour être sûrs que c’était une bonne idée, les ingénieurs en question ont tout fait pour éviter d’affecter le reste de l’expérience utilisateur sur MacBook. La charnière a été repensée pour que la dalle ne bouge pas lorsqu’on appuie dessus, le système thermique aussi pour éviter que l’écran ne chauffe. Le tabou a été rompu, sans détériorer le reste de ce qui a fait le MacBook Pro.

articles.title: SA’s Fynbos Money allows investors to connect portfolios directly to AI - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South African investtech startup Fynbos Money is allowing customers to connect their portfolios to ChatGPT, Claude and other AI assistants, helping them ask questions about their investments and receive detailed analysis.
Founded in 2024 by Adrian Hope-Bailie and based in Cape Town, Fynbos Money is a savings and investments platform that consolidates multiple financial products into a single interface. All deposits flow into a central cash account first and then automatically distribute according to a user’s custom rules
The new integration with AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT allows customers to ask questions about their own investments in everyday language and receive analysis based on their actual portfolio information.
Questions such as “Has my money actually grown, or have I just deposited more?”, “What am I actually invested in?” or “What could an extra R500 a month mean over 20 years?” can now be answered using information from their own accounts, giving investors access to insights that have traditionally required specialist financial knowledge.
The launch comes as AI companies push further into financial services. Anthropic, the company behind Claude, recently introduced Claude for Financial Advisors, connecting financial professionals with data and tools used for research, preparation and documentation. Fynbos is taking this shift directly to individual investors, making AI-powered financial analysis accessible to customers using their own investment data.
“Investing has become far more accessible, but access to useful financial insight hasn’t necessarily kept pace,” Hope-Bailie said. “AI has the potential to change that. By giving people the ability to interrogate their own investment information, we can make useful financial insight much more accessible.”
It’s an approach Hope-Bailie calls ‘bring your own intelligence’. Rather than building its own AI assistant, Fynbos allows customers to connect their investments to supported AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude, giving them the freedom to use the tools they’re already familiar with.
Customers can choose to connect their Fynbos account to a supported AI assistant, giving it access to read-only information about their accounts, balances and selected funds. The assistant can also use tools developed by Fynbos to perform calculations and projections and access fund information such as performance and fees.
The functionality has been built using Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard that allows AI applications to connect to external tools and data. This means Fynbos customers can use compatible AI assistants rather than being tied to a single provider.
Connecting is entirely optional, and access to the Fynbos account is read-only. AI assistants cannot use the connection to move money, buy or sell investments, switch funds or make any other changes to the account. Any information accessed through a connected AI assistant is subject to that provider’s own privacy, data processing and retention policies.
Fynbos has also launched its first mobile app, responding to one of its most requested customer features. The app introduces biometric login, faster performance and a more responsive mobile experience, while giving Fynbos access to security and usability features not available through its web platform.
“Both developments reflect the direction we want to take Fynbos Money,” said Hope-Bailie. “We want to build technology that makes investing simpler, gives customers greater control and helps them make more informed decisions about their money.”

articles.title: Americans are losing enthusiasm for their jobs, with AI and remote workers at the center of the decline
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Do you feel a lack of enthusiasm for your job, or struggle with motivation and focus at work? If you do, then you're in the majority. A recent poll of the US workforce found that employee engagement in Q3 fell to its lowest level since 2011. Much of the decline came from remote and hybrid employees across the country, especially those in organizations that have adopted AI.
Gallup began tracking employee engagement in 2000, when 26% of employees in the US said they were engaged. That figure stayed steady between 26% and 30% through 2013, then climbed to a peak of 36% in 2020.
But engagement has fallen since the start of the decade. It stood at 29% last quarter, the lowest level in 15 years. It's also two percentage points lower than the previous quarter.
Gallup writes that each percentage point in engagement represents approximately 1.6 million US employees. The Q3 decline is equivalent to about 3.2 million fewer engaged workers, bringing the total decrease since 2020 to approximately 11 million.
The decline reflected two aspects of employees' work experience: knowing what is expected of them and feeling cared about as a person.
Gallup says businesses should care more about their employees' morale, as disengaged workers can impact a firm's productivity, customer service, quality, safety and profitability.
Interestingly, employees' understanding of what was expected of them declined around twice as much among hybrid and fully remote workers. Jim Harter, chief scientist for Gallup's workplace management and wellbeing practices, suggests this could be due to physical distances contributing to psychological distance between employees and their organizations, especially as companies introduce AI at work.
AI's engagement advantage – the higher employee engagement seen in organizations that integrate AI --narrowed for remote and hybrid employees to just two percentage points in Q3, while remaining around four to five points for on-site workers.
Gallup's bottom line is that AI adoption may be outpacing the communication and managerial support needed to make it effective. It recommends clarifying AI expectations, strengthening manager support – especially for distributed teams – and tracking AI's impact on productivity and engagement.
Today's workplace is turbulent, to say the least. In addition to the AI-driven layoffs, many employees feel so pressured to adopt AI that they're pretending to use it to impress bosses – usually because they aren't confident that they can use it effectively.
Businesses might argue that AI cuts costs and saves them money. But a new Gartner survey found that was true for just 3% of organizations. Despite this, 85% still plan to spend more on the technology.

articles.title: Where was my invite to the — wait, what? Airbnb had a gala? | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Airbnb’s nonprofit held its inaugural gala on Wednesday in Los Angeles, and the internet had one reaction — the what gala?
In case you missed it, back in 2020, Airbnb launched a nonprofit that provides free and temporary housing to families impacted by crisis or disaster. Its gala makes sense, actually, in that significant causes often throw splashy events to please big donors.
In a press release shared with TechCrunch this week, Airbnb noted that the gala marked the launch of a new initiative for the nonprofit, in which Airbnb will start donating a portion of its commercial revenue from each stay booked starting from the day of the gala, October 28. The cut amounts to 10 cents, to be exact, but Airbnb did make $12.2 billion in revenue last year.
This initiative will help generate $500 million that will then go to the nonprofit over the next five years to help it provide free housing for 1 million nights each year, per the release. It will also let the company expand to supporting families also facing displacement due to domestic violence, veterans in need, or those traveling for medical needs.
A spokesperson for Airbnb said that the night was for its supporters and “marking the next chapter of our work.” Airbnb said that people had the option to donate, but “fundraising wasn’t the focus of the evening” and that the nonprofit “didn’t set a fundraising target.” The idea is for the Gala to happen each year, and last night was invite-only, the spokesperson said, with no tables or seats sold.
The gala was hosted by Jimmy Kimmel, with a live performance by Charli XCX, and food was curated by Chef José Andrés of World Central Kitchen. The guest list featured Serena Williams, Demi Lovato, Charlize Theron, and Cynthia Erivo. For the celebrities, it was a glamorous night in society for a helpful cause, joining the ranks of other Los Angeles events, like the Baby2Baby Gala and the Academy Museum Gala, as a place to be seen.
Still, people were literally confused as to why Airbnb was having a gala and how it attracted top-tier celebrities.
Again, a lovely event, and another data point showing that throwing a gala is one of the best ways to get rich people in a room to pay money and get media attention. And now a bunch of people on the internet know that Airbnb helps people in need, rather than perpetually making the news for negatively impacting the housing market.
This piece was updated.

articles.title: PrairiesCan minister says new regional funding shows Canada’s commitment to AI |
articles.text:
Canada’s recent top-up to its Regional AI Initiative (RAII) is evidence of the country’s commitment to staying competitive in the global AI race, says Minister of Emergency Management and Community Resilience Eleanor Olszewski.
The federal government officially announced the $500-million recapitalization last week after telegraphing the investment earlier this month. Olszewski, who is also the minister responsible for Prairies Economic Development Canada (PrairiesCan), said the funding increase was a response to a sustained desire for support from Canadian businesses.
“There’s a huge variety of ways AI can improve productivity, build a business, innovate, and increase workers hired.”
Eleanor Olszewski, PrairiesCan
“This increased funding is indicative of this government’s commitment to using AI technology,” Olszewski said, adding that she couldn’t speculate on whether the program would be sustainable in the long term or whether the government expected AI-related costs to lower in coming years.
“It shows … commitment to making sure we’re keeping up with other countries in terms of AI, and that we’re protecting our own sovereignty in that space,” Olszewski added.
The RAII is a national initiative designed to help support Canadian businesses and organizations onboard or expand AI in their operations. Funding is dispersed through Canada’s seven regional economic development agencies (RDAs).
The $500-million recapitalization, added over five years, brings the total funding for the RAII to $700 million. It launched with $200 million investment in 2024.
Olszewski said the program’s rollout in the Prairies has been successful in casting a wide net when it comes to the type of businesses it supports. The minister specifically referenced both Edmonton’s Samdesk, a crisis detection and management platform, and Saskatchewan-based Ground Truth Ag, an AgTech company using AI to evaluate grain, as recipients that stood out during the first round of funding. Ground Truth was honoured in BetaKit Most Ambitious this year for its work supporting Canada’s food supply chain.
“[There’s a] huge variety of ways in which AI can be used to improve productivity, build a business, innovate, and increase the number of workers hired,” she said. “[The RAII] helped Samdesk scale up and expand operations. That enabled it to move even more deeply into the US and international markets.”
RELATED: Feds make good on AI Strategy pledge with $500-million top-up for regional AI initiative
Applications for the second round of RAII funding are open until 2030, with RDAs evaluating applications across a variety of eligibility criteria. Olszewski said factors like the compute demand required by an applicant, as well as the potential economic returns, also come into play.
“It also might look at job creation, as well. There are a number of factors that PrairiesCan looks at to make that determination.”
Applications can be made through each region’s RDA, a list of which is available here.

articles.title: Scientists overcome a hidden obstacle to more powerful quantum computers
articles.text:
Scientists overcome a hidden obstacle to more powerful quantum computers
- Date:
- October 25, 2026
- Source:
- RIKEN
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a way to operate multiple silicon qubits simultaneously with remarkable accuracy, overcoming a major challenge in scaling up quantum computers. Their new technique maintained accuracy of approximately 99.9% even when all five qubits were running at once, opening the door to larger and more powerful quantum processors.
- Share:
Silicon spin qubits could play a major role in the future of quantum computing because they can be produced using the same semiconductor manufacturing methods that make today's computer chips. However, researchers have faced a significant challenge. When multiple silicon qubits are controlled at the same time, their operations tend to become less accurate. Building practical, large quantum computers will require scientists to control many qubits simultaneously while keeping errors to a minimum.
Researchers at the RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and their collaborators have now made important progress toward solving this problem. In a study published in Nature Physics, the team demonstrated highly accurate control of several silicon spin qubits operating simultaneously. Their experiments used an array of five qubits connected to a shared microwave control line. By identifying a major cause of errors during simultaneous operation, the scientists developed a technique to reduce those errors and maintain precision.
Leon Camenzind, a RIKEN research scientist and co-first author who supervised the experiments, explains the significance of the results: "This shows that high-fidelity control can be maintained even when several qubits are operated at the same time and represents an important step toward scaling up silicon-based quantum processors."
Scientists Identify a Hidden Source of Quantum Computing Errors
Unlike conventional computers, which store information as bits representing either 0 or 1, quantum computers use quantum bits, or qubits, that can exist in combinations of both states. Silicon spin qubits store this information using the spin of individual electrons confined within silicon. Performing reliable quantum calculations requires extremely precise control over these electron spins.
Microwave signals provide that control, but operating multiple qubits simultaneously can create unwanted effects that interfere with their accuracy. The researchers traced much of this problem to a phenomenon called the AC Stark shift.
This effect occurs when microwave control signals alter a qubit's effective energy levels, producing changes in the phase of its quantum state. Those phase shifts can disrupt the intended operation of individual qubits, particularly when several are being controlled at once.
To counteract the problem, the team created a calibration method that compensates for these unwanted shifts. Rather than separately calibrating every possible combination of qubits, the technique relies on calibrations performed between pairs of qubits. This makes the approach more practical for systems containing larger numbers of quantum bits.
"Rather than requiring an entirely separate calibration procedure for every possible combination of qubits, our method uses calibrations between pairs of qubits to compensate for the unwanted phase shifts," explains Yi-Hsien Wu, the first author who carried out the experiments as part of his PhD research.
Quantum Qubits Achieve Accuracy Above 99.99%
The researchers combined their calibration technique with an improved device design and carefully adjusted microwave control pulses. Their results showed that exceptionally high accuracy could be maintained even when multiple qubits were operating simultaneously.
When the five qubits were tested individually, each achieved single-qubit gate fidelity well above 99.99%, with the highest approaching 99.999%. Fidelity describes how closely a quantum operation matches its intended result.
The team then tested how well the system performed when several qubits were active together. With as many as three qubits operating simultaneously, fidelity remained above 99.99%. Even when all five qubits were controlled at once, accuracy stayed at approximately 99.9%, approaching the levels needed for practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.
Although the calibration method greatly reduced errors, it did not eliminate them entirely. The researchers found that the remaining loss of accuracy was linked to drive-induced decoherence, an effect caused by the greater microwave power required to operate multiple qubits simultaneously.
Unlike the unwanted phase shifts corrected by the new technique, decoherence involves the loss of the delicate quantum coherence needed for reliable operations.
According to Camenzind, "This is a limitation, but further improvements to device design could help mitigate this source of error."
A New Path Toward Larger Quantum Processors
The findings show that controlling several silicon spin qubits at the same time does not necessarily require a major sacrifice in accuracy. By correcting a key source of errors, the researchers have demonstrated a promising approach for operating more qubits through shared microwave control lines.
This is especially important for the development of large quantum processors. Giving every qubit its own independent control system would make increasingly complex devices difficult to manage. Shared control lines could offer a more practical way to expand these systems while maintaining the precision needed for quantum calculations.
"By addressing a key source of control errors through pairwise calibration," says Camenzind. "Our study supports the use of shared control lines as a practical approach to scaling up quantum processors. Combined with silicon's compatibility with established semiconductor manufacturing, we believe that this advance could help pave the way toward larger quantum processors capable of performing increasingly complex computations."
The broader objective is to develop quantum computers that can reliably perform calculations despite the errors and disturbances that affect quantum systems. Such machines, known as fault-tolerant quantum computers, will require precise, dependable control over large numbers of qubits.
"Our long-term goal is to build a fault-tolerant quantum computer based on silicon spin qubits, and reliable parallel control is an essential step toward that goal," adds Seigo Tarucha, project manager of a silicon quantum computing project under JST's Moonshot Goal 6.
Story Source:
Materials provided by RIKEN. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Yi-Hsien Wu, Leon C. Camenzind, Patrick Bütler, Ik Kyeong Jin, Akito Noiri, Kenta Takeda, Takashi Nakajima, Takashi Kobayashi, Giordano Scappucci, Hsi-Sheng Goan, Seigo Tarucha. Simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates in a spin qubit array. Nature Physics, 2026; DOI: 10.1038/s41567-026-03466-2

articles.title: Liam Neeson rompe su silencio tras ser sustituido por Meryl Streep como Aslan en 'Las Crónicas de Narnia'
articles.text:
La nueva película de Narnia: El sobrino del mago, será un reinicio a la franquicia, que esta vez arrancará con el primero de los libros en orden cronológico. Dirigida por Greta Gerwig, será una de las producciones más ambiciosas de Netflix, tanto que llegará a los cines como uno de los grandes estrenos de comienzos de año. Uno de los puntos más comentados ha sido el fichaje de Meryl Streep como Aslan en sustitución de Liam Neeson.
El veterano actor de La Lista de Schindler dio voz al mítico león en las películas de los años 2000. Ahora, sin embargo, la actriz con más nominaciones al Oscar de toda la historia toma el testigo para dotar al personaje de una nueva personalidad. Algo que el mismísimo Liam Neeson no sabía, tal y como ha reconocido en una entrevista concedida a ScreenRant. "Lo siento, esto es nuevo para mí", confiesa sobre la producción de la nueva película de Las Crónicas de Narnia.
"¿Meryl Streep va a hacer de Jesucristo?", comenta sorprendido a continuación. Y es que, recordemos, el león Aslan de Narnia es una representación del Jesús, el hijo de Dios en la religión cristiana. Y lo cierto es que a Liam Neeson la elección de la actriz para el papel le ha parecido fantástica. "Bueno, si vas a convertir a Cristo en mujer, nadie mejor que Meryl", confirma.
En realidad, en Narnia: El sobrino del mago, Aslan no será una leona. Simplemente tendrá la voz de Meryl Streep pero, por lo visto en el primer tráiler, mantendrá el aspecto físico de un león macho. En cualquier caso, el fichaje de Streep para el papel supone un gran golpe sobre la mesa del filme, que se asegura contar con una de las mejores intérpretes de todos los tiempos.
De qué va Narnia: El sobrino del mago
En Las Crónicas de Narnia: El sobrino del mago, al tocar un anillo mágico dos niños son transportados al antiguo mundo de Charn. Allí, por error despiertan a una poderosa y malvada hechicera de su sueño eterno. Sedienta de poder, ella no dudará en destruirlo todo y a todos a su paso. Pero el gran león Aslan hará despertar con su canción una nueva esperanza, un nuevo mundo: Narnia. Un lugar donde todo es posible.
Dirigida por la nominada al Oscar Greta Gerwig (Barbie), la película está protagonizada por David McKenna (El señor de las moscas), Beatrice Campbell (La trama fenicia), Emma Mackey (Sex Education), Carey Mulligan (Una joven prometedora), Ciarán Hinds (Juego de tronos), Daniel Craig (saga James Bond), Meryl Streep (El diablo viste de Prada), Kobna Holdbrook-Smith (Wonka), Denise Gough (Andor) y Susan Wokoma (Enola Holmes).
Narnia: El sobrino del mago se estrena en cines el 12 de febrero de 2027.

articles.title: One Planet Partners partners with Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank to launch Rs 3,000 Cr fund
articles.text:
One Planet Partners partners with Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank to launch Rs 3,000 Cr fund
Private equity firm One Planet Partner will invest in high-growth companies across the sectors of energy, mobility and manufacturing.
One Planet Partners, an India-focused private equity firm, has partnered with Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank to launch its Rs 3,000-crore maiden fund.
According to a statement, the Japanese financial institution has made an equity investment in One Planet Partners, alongside the anchoring of a dedicated private equity fund managed by One Planet. The fund will focus on high-growth businesses benefitting from India's energy transition, mobility, and manufacturing-led industrial expansion.
Founded in 2024, One Planet is a Mumbai-based asset management firm established by four founding partners Mukund Rajan, Bobby Pauly, Mrinalini Mirchandani, and Sheetal Thakkar.
One Planet Partners will focus on high-growth mid-market businesses, providing scale-up capital of Rs 100 crore to Rs 500 crore to enterprises with attractive unit economics and revenue between Rs 200 crore and Rs 2000 crore.
The firm aims to combine growth capital with active ownership and operational expertise to help businesses scale and strengthen their competitive positioning.
One Planet Partners Founder and Chairperson Mukund Rajan said, "With strong institutional support, our ambition is to build a world-class investment platform focused on high-growth businesses at the intersection of India's economic expansion, energy transition, and industrial transformation."
One Planet Partners has already commenced capital deployment. Bengaluru-based electric mobility company Yulu Bikes Private Limited is the first investment by the platform. The investment was made as part of Yulu's $93 million Series C funding round.
Kazuya Yoneda, General Manager – Equity Investment Department, of Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank, said, "India is one of the world’s most compelling long-term investment destinations. Our strategic investment reflects confidence in both the market and One Planet Partners’ proven track record, institutional approach, and differentiated ability to access and create value in India’s private markets.”

articles.title: Flock ignores Minnesota city’s orders not to reinstall AI surveillance cameras — citizens complain after spotting two cameras despite the city canceling its contract
articles.text:
Flock ignores Minnesota city’s orders not to reinstall AI surveillance cameras — citizens complain after spotting two cameras despite the city canceling its contract
More Flock controversy.
Flock's AI surveillance cameras are continuing to cause controversy, this time in Dayton, Minnesota, where it is alleged that the company reinstalled two cameras despite express orders from the city not to do so. The city's local government posted on Facebook to explain, claiming that the Police Department was made aware of a maintenance work order on September 17, to which Dayton responded the next day, stating the program had been put on hold and no work orders were to be completed. However, Flock went ahead and reinstalled them anyway without authorization from the city.
Dayton’s city council had already voted to suspend the automatic license plate reader program and Flock cameras on August 25, following community concerns over privacy and data misuse, The Drive reports. Flock is infamous nationwide, with instances of its cameras being used for unjust purposes, such as a car reviewer mistakenly being pulled over because one of its cameras misread the tags. In another case, Flock’s chief information security officer also falsely assured the Oshkosh City Council that Flock did not create a heat map of individual license plates, when it in fact does have a heat map feature in the Flock system.
Flock cameras in the city had already been broken and vandalized, leading police to disable and remove the cameras to prevent further damage on August 20, before the program’s suspension became official, local media reports. Despite the suspension, almost a full month later, on September 17, Flock submitted the offending work order, which led to this latest controversy.
We don’t know when Flock reinstalled the cameras, but Dayton citizens had already complained and reported spotting the two Flock cameras, leading to the September 29 Facebook post. The local government further stated that the Dayton Police Department had been informed and ordered to remove the cameras.
It is unclear what happened in the chain of communication from when the license plate reader program was suspended and canceled its contract to notify Flock to cease work orders; either Flock defiantly ignored the orders or instructions had not reached the people responsible for installing the cameras; either way, this could be another blow to Flock's reputation.

articles.title: Aus religiösen Gründen: Erster US-Universitätsmitarbeiter bekommt Ausnahme von KI-Zwang
articles.text:
Aus religiösen Gründen: Erster US-Universitätsmitarbeiter bekommt Ausnahme von KI-Zwang
Der Einsatz von KI erhitzt seit Längerem die Gemüter. Die einen sorgen sich um Cybergefahren oder kritisieren den KI-bedingten Stellenabbau. Andere fragen sich, welche Auswirkungen die neue Technologie konkret auf das menschliche Denken hat. Zu ihnen gehört David Durman. Er arbeitet als Verwaltungsmitarbeiter an der University of Kentucky und bezeichnet sich selbst als Humanist. Wie Religion News berichtet, hat er jetzt eine religiös begründete Ausnahmegenehmigung erhalten, die ihn vom KI-Einsatz befreit.
KI nicht mit Humanismus vereinbar?
Immer mehr Menschen müssen sich am Arbeitsplatz mit neuen KI-Tools auseinandersetzen. Oft sollen sie Prozesse beschleunigen und so die Produktivität steigern. Als die University of Kentucky ihre Mitarbeiter:innen aufforderte, KI in ihre Arbeitsabläufe zu integrieren, machte sich Durman Sorgen. Er hatte das Gefühl, er solle sein Denken in der täglichen Arbeit an einen Chatbot auslagern. Das empfand er als Verstoß gegen seine Überzeugungen.
„Der Prozess und die Arbeit, die damit verbunden sind, Situationen zu durchdenken – im Rahmen meiner Arbeit, meiner Ethik und der Art und Weise, wie ich mit anderen Menschen umgehe – sind ein wesentlicher Bestandteil meiner Entwicklung zu einem moralischen Menschen“, erklärte er im Interview mit Religion News. „Und diese Arbeit auszulagern, unabhängig davon, ob sie anstrengend ist oder nicht, untergräbt meine Fähigkeit, moralisch zu handeln.“
Mithilfe der American Humanist Association beantragte er eine Ausnahmeregelung gemäß eines Bundesgesetzes, das es Beschäftigten erlaubt, Änderungen ihrer Arbeitsanforderungen zu beantragen, um ihren religiösen Überzeugungen gerecht zu werden. Im September stimmte die Universität zu: Durman muss jetzt keine KI mehr für seine Arbeit einsetzen. Vertreter:innen der American Humanist Association gehen davon aus, dass Durman der erste Humanist ist, der eine solche KI-Ausnahmeregelung erzielen konnte.
Wie KI das kritische Denken untergräbt
Durman ist nicht der Einzige, dem es widerstrebt, sein Denken an eine KI auszulagern. Zuletzt forderten zahlreiche Mathematiker:innen in der neugegründeten Association for Human Mathematics, die Disziplin solle in menschlicher Hand bleiben. Kurz zuvor hatte OpenAI auf einen Schlag 722 Fachartikel veröffentlicht. Sie beweisen oder widerlegen mathematische Probleme, an denen Wissenschaftler:innen bisher gescheitert waren. Der Verband argumentiert, mathematischer Fortschritt erfordere menschliches Fachwissen, das durch sorgfältiges Denken entstehe. Die automatisierte Produktion und Rezeption von Mathematik untergrabe daher die intellektuellen Grundlagen des Fachgebiets.
Die Sorge, KI könne das Urteilsvermögen beeinträchtigen, ist nicht unbegründet. Laut einer Studie von Microsoft und der Carnegie Mellon University könnten Menschen, die sich zu sehr auf KI verlassen, die Fähigkeit verlieren, kritisch zu denken. Die Forscher:innen befragten 319 Personen, die beruflich Daten oder Informationen auswerten, zu ihren KI-Gewohnheiten. Sie beobachteten: Je stärker die Nutzer:innen von den Fähigkeiten der KI überzeugt waren, desto eigenständiger ließen sie die KI arbeiten. Dadurch könne eine übermäßige Abhängigkeit von KI-Tools ohne nachträgliche Prüfung entstehen.
Auch Papst Leo XIV. äußert sich kritisch
Durman geht sogar noch einen Schritt weiter. Er befürchtet, dass KI die Gesellschaft auf schädliche Weise beeinflussen könnte. Als Humanist glaube er an die Bedeutung der menschlichen Entfaltung: „Auf gesellschaftlicher Ebene denke ich, dass der Einsatz von KI-Technologie dem zuwiderläuft.“ Auch Papst Leo XIV. hatte sich zuvor ähnlich geäußert. In seiner Enzyklika warnte er Anfang dieses Jahres, dass KI die Demokratie und die Menschenwürde schwächen könnte. Bei Missbrauch könnten KI-Tools einer kleinen Elite zudem zusätzliche Macht verleihen, während der Rest der Menschheit zurückbleibe.

articles.title: BAE Says No Data Extracted in Incident Hitting Bankruptcy Courts
articles.text:
BAE Systems has restored the federal judiciary’s Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC) and says no data was taken in the cybersecurity incident that knocked it offline for more than two weeks.
“BAE Systems, Inc., working closely with the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts (AOUSC), has resumed operations of the Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC) system. No other systems were affected. No data was extracted. There was no breach of any PII,” a BAE Systems, Inc. spokesperson told SecurityWeek.
The BNC, which BAE operates under contract with the judiciary, is the channel through which all federal bankruptcy courts in the US send their notices. Notices stopped flowing through the center around October 9.
When the incident first came to light, neither BAE nor the judiciary addressed whether any data had been compromised. BAE’s new statement still leaves out what caused the incident and whether it was a cyberattack.
On October 27, the Administrative Office of the US Courts confirmed that, according to BAE, the problems had been fixed and the BNC was available again.
Bankruptcy court notices show the center came back on October 26 and began clearing the delayed notices, oldest first.
In response to the outage, the Judicial Conference declared a “Bankruptcy Rules emergency” on October 22. The declaration lets bankruptcy judges push back deadlines, pause time periods and issue related orders to deal with the fallout.
No ransomware or other cybercrime group appears to have publicly claimed responsibility for the incident.

articles.title: Rivian’s R2 is officially its best-selling vehicle
articles.text:
Rivian reported its third quarter earnings of 2026, providing us a closer look at the company’s financial health as it ramps up production of its all-important R2 electric vehicle — which is now, for the first time, outselling all of Rivian’s other EVs.
Rivian’s R2 is officially its best-selling vehicle
The mass-market R2 has quickly become the company’s top seller by volume, but high-margin software deals and the Volkswagen partnership are the real forces keeping the automaker in good financial health.
Rivian said it brought in $2.155 billion in revenue, a 38 percent increase compared to the $1.558 billion in Q3 2025. Of that amount, $1.55 billion came from automotive revenue, which is up 36 percent year over year. Comparatively, the company reported $605 million from software and subscription services, a 45 percent increase year over year. As EV sales slow down, the company is seeking to make more money from its digital products, including the Autonomy Plus package.
Automotive gross profits were on an upward trajectory, a sign that the company’s finances were improving as it delivered more vehicles. Rivian made $176 million in gross profit this quarter, a $152 million improvement compared to the same time last year. The company still lost $80 million in Q3 automotive gross profits, which is much better than the $130 million loss a year ago.
In other words, Rivian is losing less than it did a year ago because they sold more cars and made more money per vehicle. (Also, the company continued to sell pollution credits to other carmakers, and also received a tariff refund from the government — all of which was recorded as revenue.)
Rivian is losing less than it did a year ago because they sold more cars and made more money per vehicle.
Rivian brought in $256 million in profit in software and services, up $102 million from last year, with a strong 42 percent profit margin. Most of this cash came from licensing their tech to Volkswagen, alongside customer subscriptions for Rivian’s Autonomy Plus driving features. In many ways, Rivian’s tech partnership with Volkswagen and software sales are currently paying the bills, keeping the company profitable overall while it absorbs a lot of heavy upfront costs from launching the R2.
Earlier this month, Rivian reported a record sales quarter, with 19,751 vehicles produced and 19,248 delivered. That represents an 85 percent year-over-year increase in production and a 45 percent jump in deliveries. (For a direct-to-consumer automaker like Rivian, deliveries serve as a proxy for sales.)
Rivian doesn’t break down sales by model, so we don’t exactly how many R2s have reached customers so far. But the company said that the R2 is now the “best-selling Rivian vehicle by volume,” outselling the R1T and R1S, as well as the Electric Delivery Van (EDV).
“We had great results with R2 becoming our best selling vehicle by volume in the third quarter,” Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe said in a statement, ahead of the company’s earnings call this afternoon. “Customer and media feedback on R2 has been exceptional.”
The R2 was designed from the ground up to be Rivian’s higher-volume, mass-market offering — and by overtaking the company’s more expensive, lower-volume legacy vehicles, it seems to be doing just that. Still, the R2 isn’t bringing in the bulk of the revenue yet, as indicated by Rivian’s use of the phrase “by volume.” Most of the money is still coming from the VW partnership and its software division.
But that could change once Rivian starts shipping the more affordable versions of the R2, like the $55,485 Premium trim (coming in late 2026), the $49,985 Standard Long-Range (early 2027), and the $46,495 Standard (late 2027).
