articles.title: Lend and borrow resources across teams with AWS Batch’s quota management for SageMaker Training jobs | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Lend and borrow resources across teams with AWS Batch’s quota management for SageMaker Training jobs
With the launch of AWS Batch support for Amazon SageMaker Training jobs, customers gained a new fully managed way to queue, schedule, and retry machine learning (ML) training workloads without building their own infrastructure. Instead, they use the queuing and scheduling features of AWS Batch. As organizations scale their artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) operations and onboard more teams, coordinating access to shared graphics processing unit (GPU) capacity can introduce additional communication, coordination, and configuration overhead for administrators. This overhead includes setting up separate queues, adjusting capacity limits, and carefully orchestrating the right workloads to get the right resources at the right time. A core value proposition of AWS Batch is helping customers increase utilization of their compute, and as training environments grow, so does the opportunity to do more with existing capacity.
Working backward from customers managing multi-team training environments, we heard a consistent request: give us a way to define allocations per team or project, share idle capacity automatically, and run our highest-priority workloads first. This request led us to build quota management, a new scheduling capability for AWS Batch. Administrators can use it to divide compute capacity into quota shares, organized by team, project, or workload. Each quota share uses configurable resource-sharing strategies that maximize GPU utilization while honoring each team’s allocation when it matters most.
This post shows how quota management works, including how to configure quota shares with lending and borrowing strategies, set up in-share preemption for priority workloads, and get started using the SageMaker Python SDK.
Quota shares and preemption
Administrators can allocate and share constrained GPU resources by defining a quota share for separate entities, such as individual teams or projects. Each quota share includes compute quotas (capacity limits) and resource-sharing strategies for idle compute. These strategies determine whether idle compute is reserved until jobs arrive (RESERVE), lent to other quota shares that have work available (LEND), or both lent when idle and borrowed when the share has work that might benefit (LEND_AND_BORROW).
A quota share operates as a virtual queue nested hierarchically within an associated job queue. When scheduling jobs for a job queue, AWS Batch prioritizes quota shares that are under their capacity limits as it iterates through the associated quota shares. If jobs arrive in a quota share that has lent out its capacity, AWS Batch performs cross-share preemption. This reclaims resources for the lending quota share, so administrators don’t need to track down the jobs borrowing capacity and terminate them on their own. If jobs arrive in a quota share that is at or above its capacity limit, AWS Batch checks whether there’s available capacity to borrow from another quota share. If so, workloads can run using otherwise-idle capacity.
You can turn on priority-based in-share preemption when you configure a quota share. Where cross-share preemption reclaims lent capacity as jobs arrive in a lending quota share, in-share preemption preempts lower priority jobs that are in the SCHEDULED, STARTING, or RUNNING state. This allows higher priority jobs at the front of the queue to start running sooner.
Prerequisites
Before you proceed with this example, you must have an AWS account with permissions to create and manage AWS Batch resources. For this example, see the sample IAM permissions needed to invoke AWS Batch and SageMaker APIs.
The example uses the SageMaker Python SDK v3. Complete the setup required to install a compatible version of the SageMaker Python SDK:
Configuring quota management resources
Using the new quota management capabilities requires creating a Scheduling Policy that contains a quotaSharePolicy, a Service Environment that specifies its capacity limits in terms of specific instances, and a SageMaker Training job queue that is connected to both. After that, you can associate quota shares to a job queue. The user guide has AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and console examples for configuring quota management resources and quota shares. An end-to-end example of quota management integrated with the aws_batch module in the SageMaker Python SDK v3 is contained in a sample notebook. In this example, we step through code snippets that summarize the key components, and use the helper functions from the notebook to create a Scheduling Policy, Service Environment, Job Queue, and three Quota Shares.
The three quota shares configured here represent three different projects. Each has the same capacity limit set: a single ml.g5.xlarge instance. The QS1 quota share represents background jobs. For this project, you want to run the most important background job first and borrow as much spare capacity as is available. Within this quota share, no jobs are urgent, and preemptions are acceptable because all jobs use checkpointing. This quota share uses the LEND_AND_BORROW resource-sharing strategy and has in-share preemption turned on. Higher priority jobs within the same quota share can then preempt running jobs that are lower priority.
QS2 represents medium priority workloads. Teams choosing this configuration would prefer to wait for capacity to become available rather than endure additional preemptions. Those preemptions come from borrowed capacity being reclaimed or from in-share preemptions because of higher priority job submission. This is appropriate for shorter jobs, or when most submitted jobs have similar priorities. The quota share still benefits from job priority being taken into consideration at job dispatch. Submitted jobs trigger AWS Batch to reclaim any lent capacity needed to run the jobs.
QS3 represents workloads that need to start as quickly as possible with minimal interruptions. It’s configured to reserve capacity and neither lends nor borrows to other quota shares. It doesn’t experience cross-share preemptions, because its workloads don’t exceed their capacity limits. By also turning off in-share preemption, workloads submitted to this quota share are not preempted by AWS Batch as long as the capacity limit is unchanged.
These quota share configurations are inputs to the create_quota_management_resources function in the sample notebook, which also configures the corresponding Scheduling Policy, Service Environment, and Job Queue with the constant names chosen.
Submit SageMaker Training jobs to QS1
The aws_batch module within the SageMaker Python SDK has been extended to allow programmatic submission of SageMaker Training jobs to a quota-management-enabled AWS Batch job queue. To demonstrate these new capabilities, we use a Hello World ModelTrainer that’s submitted to the job queue. The following code snippet identifies an image URI to use based on the Region and instance type selected.
We use this image URI within a basic hello world model trainer example:
To use the job queue within the SageMaker Python SDK, provide the queue name to the TrainingQueue constructor within the aws_batch module.
We can then submit three jobs to QS1, our background jobs quota share. The first job submitted has the highest priority, followed by the medium priority job, and then the lowest priority job. As nothing is currently running in QS1 or QS2, two instances’ worth of jobs should start, corresponding to the first and second jobs submitted (as they had the highest relative priority). Note that because this is only a hello world training job, it doesn’t require data, but typically a ModelTrainer requires data to perform training.
Submitting jobs to QS2 triggers cross-share preemption to reclaim lent capacity
The team that owns QS2 might discover they have work to perform and submit a job to QS2. Doing so triggers a preemption of capacity back from QS1, which is currently borrowing that capacity (QS3’s capacity isn’t configured to be borrowed). This is a cross-share preemption.
Updating job priorities in QS1 triggers in-share preemption to run highest priority jobs
If a scientist realizes that the qs1_job_low job in QS1, which is still RUNNABLE, needs to begin running now because of changing priorities, they can use the new UpdateServiceJob API to increase the priority of an already submitted job in QS1. Because there’s no available capacity to borrow, this kicks off an in-share preemption, so that the job currently running is preempted and qs1_job_low can begin.
(Optional) Clean up created resources
To clean up the resources created in this post, run the following code:
Conclusion
In this post, we covered quota management, a new scheduling capability in AWS Batch, and how to use it with SageMaker Training jobs and get started setting up quota shares for your own projects. For more details, see the AWS Batch quota management user guide.
AWS Batch with quota management can help your organization increase compute utilization and more effectively prioritize your teams and workloads, freeing up time for your infrastructure admins and ML scientists. By implementing quota management, your teams can focus on their workloads and reduce time spent managing and coordinating infrastructure. This capability is especially powerful with Amazon SageMaker AI training plans, so that your organization can reserve capacity in the quantity you need, during the time you need it. By using AWS Batch with SageMaker AI, you can make full use of the training plan. We encourage you to try out this new capability so it can make a meaningful impact in your operations.

articles.title: La ESA y China ya tienen su primera imagen completa de la aurora boreal. Y no se parece a ninguna que hayas visto
articles.text:
Hay muchas formas de ver una aurora. Puede ser boreal o austral, según el hemisferio desde el que la observes. La puedes ver cerca de los polos, donde es más habitual, o en latitudes medias si la actividad solar es tan alta que lo permite. Generalmente las vemos desde la superficie terrestre, aunque algunos astronautas han logrado verlas desde el espacio. Incluso se han visto auroras en otros planetas. Pero, sin duda, nadie había visto las auroras como las ha mostrado recientemente la misión SMILE, fruto de la colaboración entre China y la Agencia Espacial Europea (ESA).
Anillo auroral completo. En las imágenes publicadas por el equipo de SMILE hace un mes, se ve el anillo auroral completo. Es decir, la franja, con forma de anillo donde se producen las auroras alrededor de cada polo magnético de la Tierra. Se ve más o menos como un aro blanco arremolinado. Hacía casi 20 años que ninguna misión lograba captarlo por completo. La última fue la nave Polar, de la NASA, pues entre sus instrumentos contaba con uan cámara ultravioleta, similar a la que usa SMILE. No obstante, SMILE cuenta con ventajas añadidas, como observar el anillo auroral durante 45 horas seguidas y captar imágenes simultáneamente en ultravioleta lejano y rayos X. Eso la convierte en una misión mucho más exhaustiva para estudiar la interacción entre el viento solar y la magnetosfera.
La misión de SMILE. El viento solar causa auroras cuando sus partículas cargadas eléctricamente interaccionan con las moléculas de nuestra atmósfera. Sin embargo, esa es solo la parte bonia. También pueden afectar mucho a nuestra infraestructura de telecomunicaciones. Por suerte, la Tierra dispone de un escudo llamado magnetosfera que nos protege de parte de ese viento solar. Es cierto que actúa como embudo y puede dirigir parte de los iones procedentes del Sol hacia los polos, por eso ahí son más comunes las auroras, pero en general nos protege de las peores consecuencias. ¿Cómo lo hace? Es algo que sabemos más o menos; pero, si queremos reforzar la seguridad, es importante saberlo de una forma mucho más exhaustiva. Ahí es donde entra en juego SMILE, cuya misión es estudiar las interacciones entre la magnetosfera y el viento solar.
Cámara ultravioleta. Las imágenes del anillo auroral, que fueron tomadas el pasado mes de julio de 2026, muestran el globo terráqueo como una bola de un azul pálido homogéneo. No se ven ni océanos ni continentes. Esto se debe a que el oxígeno molecular de la atmósfera terrestre absorbe la radiación ultravioleta que se emite desde la Tierra, de modo que no llega a salir hacia fuera. El instrumento de ultravioleta de SMILE, llamado UVI, está cegado a la luz visible para evitar interferencias y captar solo el UV. Si no puede ver la luz visible y la UV la bloquea la atmósfera, el resultado es prácticamente un lienzo en blanco. En cambio, las auroras, emiten desde las capas altas de la atmósfera, donde hay menos oxígeno concentrado, por lo que se ven en todo su esplendor, incluso en el lado iluminado del planeta.
Más instrumentos. Como hemos adelantado, SMILE no capta imágenes solo en el ultravioleta. También dispone de una cámara de rayos X llamada SXI, que se encargará de estudiar la frontera entre el viento solar y la magnetosfera. Esta es una región llamada magnetopausa. Por otro lado, la misión incluye otros dos instrumentos: el magnetómetro (MAG) y el analizador de iones ligeros (LIA).
Más de 300 auroras. Está planeado que SMILE lleve a cabo su trabajo durante al menos 3 años. En ese tiempo, si todo va bien, debería captar alrededor de 300 auroras. Dado que estas son uno de los resultados principales de la interacción entre la magnetosfera y el viento solar, podemos aprender mucho de todas ellas.

articles.title: How Next-Generation Mobile Processors Are Revolutionizing Smartphone Hardware and Graphics - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Gaming phones are getting ridiculously powerful. We’re well past the point where mobile gaming only means simple games designed to pass ten minutes while you’re waiting for something.
Newzoo expects 3.1 billion people to play mobile games in 2026, with the market generating $121.1 billion. Console gaming is forecast at $46.9 billion for the year, so mobile isn’t exactly the smaller side of gaming anymore.
Below, we’ll explore how gaming phones are closing the gap with consoles.
Advanced, Powerful Hardware and Graphics Potential
Current gaming phones have everything needed for demanding games, from processors to cooling systems.
The REDMAGIC 11 Pro, for example, uses Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 with an active cooling system and a 144Hz display. Testing by Android Authority found the chipset could comfortably run Call of Duty Mobile at 120fps, something we couldn’t have imagined even five years ago, and Genshin Impact held around 60fps at maximum settings.
Heat is still sometimes a bit of a limitation because you’re putting all that hardware inside something that fits in your pocket. But that’s also why gaming phones are investing more in vapor chambers, fans, and other cooling methods.
Remote For Cloud Gaming and Streaming, With More Options Than Ever Before
DEvelopers have identified the high potential of mobile gaming, and the market is now brimming with titles that have been optimized for the small screen. It’s not all about the app store downloads, either. Leading sites utilize advanced PWA technologies to offer smooth, high quality experiences without a single download needing to take place. True versatility vs apps that need to be added to a phone via a WiFi connection.
But the phone doesn’t always need to run the game, either. Xbox Cloud Gaming lets players stream supported console games directly to phones and tablets. Xbox Remote Play can also stream games installed on your own console, with progress carrying across devices.
GeForce NOW takes the same idea further on supported Android phones. NVIDIA currently supports streaming at up to 1440p and 120fps, although that level needs a compatible device, Ultimate membership, and at least a 35Mbps connection. Add a proper controller that can connect via Bluetooth, and we’re nowhere near what traditional mobile gaming was not so long ago.
Remember that cloud gaming is only as good as your connection, and bad Wi-Fi can ruin the illusion quickly.
Engagement Levels Competing With Consoles
Sensor Tower recorded around 221 billion hours of mobile gaming playtime during the first half of 2026.
Then you’ve got the 3.1 billion mobile players Newzoo expects this year. Mobile and console habits are still different, so not everyone will spend a 6-hour gaming session on their phone as they might on a console. But developers have an enormous audience that’s willing to spend a lot of time with mobile games.
Gaming phones are being built for those people rather than your parents occasionally playing Candy Crush on the bus or the sofa.
Cross-Platform Releases on Mobile and Console
Warframe launched globally on Android in February 2026. It’s not a small mobile spin-off. The Android release uses the same content build as the main game and supports cross-platform progression, letting players use the same account across mobile, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch, and PC.
Fortnite, Genshin Impact, and other major games already work across mobile and console ecosystems. Players are getting used to starting something on one device and continuing somewhere else rather than choosing one platform and staying there.
Gaming phones still have obvious disadvantages compared with consoles, such as smaller screens or batteries that run down, but the gap is definitely shrinking. It’ll be interesting to see how close the two become over the next ten years.

articles.title: Telesat posts Q3 losses as satellite company offers “no assurances” on ability to pay back debt
articles.text:
Ottawa-based satellite operator Telesat posted steep revenue losses in its third-quarter earnings on Thursday.
The news: Telesat, which trades on the TSX and Nasdaq under the symbol $TSAT, reported $81 million CAD in consolidated revenue for the three months ending Sept. 30, a 20-percent decrease from the same time last year. Its net loss for the quarter was $157 million, compared to a $121 million loss in Q3 2025.
Telesat attributed some of the revenue loss to a non-renewed broadcast contract from 2025, and reduced contracted capacity for a broadcast customer this year. The loss comes as Telesat attempts to maneuver a new recapitalization plan as it stares down an upcoming debt-repayment deadline, The Globe and Mail recently reported.
From the source: According to Telesat filings, the company has more than $2 billion in debt coming due at different points across this coming December, June 2027, and October 2027.
The filing states that management expects to address the debt obligations before they become due, but that addressing the debt will be dependent on “a number of factors outside of the company’s control” and “there can be no assurance that these initiatives will be completed successfully.”
The context: According to The Globe and Mail, Telesat’s lenders recently put forward a proposal to the company, in which they would receive 100 percent of their principal balance, plus accrued interest, through a $1.7-billion equity rights offering and a $1.5-billion loan.
The offering follows Telesat getting into a legal battle with its lenders earlier this year, after a pair of lawsuits alleged that the firm breached a credit agreement by moving part of its “crown-jewel” low-earth-orbit satellite communications business into an indirect subsidiary, and beyond lenders’ reach. Telesat has claimed the allegations are without merit.
Final thought: Despite the uncertainty, Telesat reported that its backlog represents just over $6 billion in revenue, and that it’s now set to receive $2 billion in milestone-based payments from the Canadian government between Q3 2026 and Q4 2028 as part of a military satellite contract it signed in August. Telesat investors still reacted unfavourably to the earnings report, dropping its stock price nearly four percent on Thursday, to just under $62 per share on the TSX at the time of this article’s publication.
Feature image courtesy Telesat.

articles.title: Jennifer Lawrence confirma su regreso a 'Los Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la cosecha': "Fue muy emotivo"
articles.text:
Lo que era un secreto a voces ya se ha confirmado oficialmente. Jennifer Lawrence regresa a la franquicia de Los Juegos del Hambre en su nueva película, Amanecer en la cosecha. La actriz volverá a dar vida a Katniss Everdeen y, además, no estará sola. Tanto Josh Hutcherson como Woody Harrelson también regresan en sus papeles de Peeta Mellark y Haymitch Abernathy.
Aunque Los Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la cosecha será una precuela, Jennifer Lawrence y sus compañeros aparecerán en al menos una escena, probablemente un flashforward que llenará de nostalgia los corazones de los fans de la saga. De hecho, ha sido la propia actriz la que ha confirmado la noticia en el podcast Call Her Daddy.
"Fue increíble. Fue una locura. Era el mismo equipo. El mismo asistente de dirección, con el que he trabajado un millón de veces porque le adoro. Y con Josh [Hutcherson] y Woody [Harrelson]… fue muy emotivo", asegura Jennifer Lawrence sobre su sorprendente regreso a Los Juegos del Hambre.
"Josh y yo no íbamos ni al baño sin estar abrazados. Fue precioso. Y Woody, como era de esperar, se coló por la ventana de mi habitación de hotel sin que nadie le invitara. No sería lo mismo si respetara los límites o utilizara la puerta", bromea también la actriz. Y es que, aunque la noticia de estos especiales regresos ya había trascendido en la prensa hace unos meses, ahora ha sido la propia Lawrence quien se ha encargado de confirmarlo definitivamente.
De qué va Los Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la cosecha
Los Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la cosecha llevará a la pantalla la 50ª edición de los Juegos organizados por el Capitolio. Se trata de una edición especialmente cruel y sangrienta porque el número de tributos de cada distrito será el doble. Por tanto, también habrá el doble de muertos en la arena. Uno de esos tributos será Haymitch Abernathy, quien posteriormente sabemos que será el mentor del Distrito 12 que entrenará y ayudará a Katniss y Peeta a sobrevivir.
En esta precuela se nos presenta a su versión joven, interpretada por Joseph Zada, que deberá mostrar cómo consiguió sobrevivir. El resto del reparto lo componen Ralph Fiennes como el presidente Snow, Jesse Plemons como Plutarch Heavensbee, Glenn Close como Drusilla Sickle, Elle Faning como Effie Trinket, Kieran Culkin como el presentador Caesar Flickerman, Maya Hawke como Wiress, Mckenna Grace como Maysilee Donner o Whitney Peak como Lenore Dove Baird, entre otros.
Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la cosecha se estrena en cines el 20 de noviembre.

articles.title: MIT scientists build a tiny robot that swims using living muscle cells
articles.text:
MIT scientists build a tiny robot that swims using living muscle cells
- Date:
- October 23, 2026
- Source:
- Massachusetts Institute of Technology
- Summary:
- MIT engineers have built a paper-thin swimming robot powered by living muscle cells that respond to flashes of light, allowing it to swim and steer through water. The breakthrough could pave the way for tiny, self-healing biological robots capable of exploring fragile environments that ordinary machines cannot safely navigate.
- Share:
A swimming robot does not necessarily need a bulky motor or powerful mechanical parts to move through water. MIT researchers have demonstrated that a single, carefully engineered layer of living muscle cells can generate enough force to propel a tiny robot forward.
The engineers developed an extremely thin swimming robot that uses living muscle tissue to move its fins. Described in a new study published in Advanced Functional Materials, the device has a flexible gel framework roughly the length and width of a stick of gum. The gel forms two fins, each coated with a layer of muscle cells far thinner than a human hair. These cells have been genetically modified to contract when exposed to light.
By directing light onto either fin, the researchers can trigger muscle contractions that make the fin flap and push the robot through water. Adjusting which fin receives light and how frequently it is illuminated allows the team to control both its speed and direction.
In experiments, the remarkably thin robot successfully swam and turned through a simple underwater maze. At maximum speed, it covered approximately four times its body length per minute. Although that is much slower than an Olympic swimmer, who can travel up to 65 body lengths per minute, it is comparable to the swimming pace of a cow shark moving leisurely through the ocean.
"It takes a lot of force to move through water versus air," says study author Ritu Raman, associate professor of mechanical engineering at MIT. "The robot's quite strong, given its size. "
A New Generation of Robots Powered by Living Muscle
The device represents the first demonstration of a very thin, two-dimensional robot that can move from place to place using living muscle tissue.
Most existing biohybrid robots rely on relatively large, three-dimensional structures made from laboratory-grown skeletal muscle. Producing these structures typically requires millions of cells. Raman explains that thinner designs could reduce manufacturing costs while potentially improving movement efficiency.
"Currently, biohybrid robots from our group and others' are built from bulky, 3D chunks of lab-grown skeletal muscle that require millions of cells to fabricate," says Raman, who notes that thinner, less bulky designs such as the team's new bot could be cheaper to build and could move more efficiently. "We believe that biohybrid robots powered by living muscle could one day perform delicate jobs like exploring environments too fragile or unpredictable for conventional hardware, because living tissue is soft, responsive to its surroundings, and can heal itself."
The MIT research team also included first author Maheera Bawa, along with Arielle Berman, Laura Schwendeman, Ferdows Afghah, and Seanbiron Johnson.
From Artificial Muscle to a Swimming Robot
The new swimming robot builds on an earlier achievement by Raman's laboratory. Last year, the researchers created an artificial muscle disk inspired by the human iris, demonstrating how a thin layer of living cells could produce precisely controlled movements.
For that project, the engineers patterned a gel disk with grooves extending outward from its center and forming concentric circles. They then placed living muscle cells on the surface, where the cells grew into a thin layer following the patterned channels.
When illuminated, the muscle tissue contracted in different directions, causing the disk to stretch and compress. Its movements resembled the way the iris of the human eye changes shape as the pupil expands or narrows.
The experiment established that researchers could grow extremely thin muscle layers in intricate arrangements and use light to control their movements along multiple directions.
"People hadn't seen this muscle architecture engineered from scratch before," Raman says. "And the cells were moving in multiple directions. But they only moved about 100 microns. From a robotics perspective, their movements were tiny."
For the latest project, the researchers wanted to dramatically increase the amount of movement and force generated by the muscle cells. Their goal was to produce contractions powerful enough to propel a robot through water.
They determined that achieving this would require a better foundation for the living muscle tissue.
The earlier artificial iris had used fibrin, an exceptionally soft gel, as its underlying structure. However, the team found that fibrin could quickly shrink under the forces exerted by contracting muscle cells, limiting the effectiveness of the resulting movement.
To overcome this problem, the engineers investigated three characteristics of the gel foundation: its chemical composition, its stiffness, and the dimensions and geometry of the grooves used to organize muscle growth.
"For engineering any type of tissue, it's known that these are knobs you can tune," Raman says. "And we wanted to optimize all these parameters to support live muscle cells."
Engineering a Stronger Muscle-Powered Robot
Finding the right supporting material required testing gels with different formulations, stiffness levels, and surface patterns.
The researchers compared several groove shapes, including narrow channels with square profiles and longer channels with curved bottoms. They discovered that muscle cells aligned more effectively inside square-shaped grooves.
This alignment was important because muscle cells that grow in the same direction are more likely to merge into fibers. Those fibers can then form stronger muscle tissue that contracts in a coordinated way. The square grooves therefore provided a more effective structure for producing force.
The team also replaced fibrin with gelatin methacrylate (GelMA), a material commonly used to grow and engineer biological tissue.
By adjusting the formulation of GelMA, the researchers produced supporting gels with varying degrees of stiffness. They then examined how muscle cells developed on each surface and measured their ability to generate force.
Stiffer gels produced the best results. On these firmer surfaces, muscle cells grew in better alignment and generated stronger contractions.
The engineers next investigated how thick the gel should be. They determined that a film measuring approximately half a millimeter offered an effective balance. It was sturdy enough to support a single layer of muscle cells while remaining sufficiently lightweight to prevent the contracting cells from detaching from the surface.
The team further improved muscle performance through a form of exercise. Repeated pulses of light stimulated the cells to contract, strengthening the muscle tissue before it was incorporated into the swimming robot.
How Light Makes the Living Robot Swim
With the gel structure optimized and the muscle cells strengthened, the researchers assembled their swimming device.
The finished robot consisted of a thin gel framework divided into two fins. Both sides of the gel were patterned with square-bottomed grooves and covered with living muscle cells. As the cells developed, they fused into organized muscle fibers capable of contracting together.
Each fin could be activated independently using light, giving the researchers a simple way to control the robot's movements.
"You can think of the robot as having two independent muscles," Raman says. "If we shine a light on just one, only that muscle moves. If shining on both, they both flap."
To test the device, the researchers placed it inside a large petri dish filled with water. They then moved a light source by hand, illuminating the fins to guide the robot through a maze positioned inside the dish.
As the muscles contracted, the fins flapped and propelled the robot through the water. By changing the light stimulation, the engineers successfully controlled its movement and helped it navigate the obstacles.
Although the robot demonstrated the ability to swim and steer, its current shape remains relatively simple. The primary objective of the experiment was to establish that an exceptionally thin layer of engineered muscle tissue could generate enough force for swimming.
The researchers now plan to refine the robot's body to improve its speed. Beyond demonstrating a new approach to biohybrid robotics, the technology could eventually be useful for monitoring aquatic environments or operating in locations where conventional rigid machines might cause damage.
"Our next goal is to optimize the body design to enable faster swimming," Raman says. "But even at slow swim speeds, one could imagine a muscle-powered swimmer being used for purposes like environmental monitoring in aquatic environments."
The Office of Naval Research provided partial funding for this research.

articles.title: Is It Getting Hot In Here? Why Thermal Is No Longer A Signoff Problem
articles.text:
Applying the appropriate level of simulation and abstraction at each stage of the design process is key to effective thermal analysis.
AI, high-performance computing and advanced semiconductor packaging have pushed power density higher, and that means managing heat is becoming one of the most consequential challenges in electronic design.
The issue is no longer simply how to cool a chip after it has been designed. Thermal behavior now affects decisions spanning device performance, package architecture, mechanical stress, reliability, floor planning and ultimately system performance. So engineering teams must shift thermal analysis to earlier in the design process as they consider a much broader multi-physics strategy.
Traditionally, engineers could isolate and analyze many physical effects separately. Electrical performance could be evaluated in one environment, thermal behavior in another and mechanical stress in another and so on. But with increasing integration, a change intended to improve performance in one domain can create unintended consequences elsewhere. Higher power can increase temperature; temperature can change electrical behavior; and thermal expansion can introduce mechanical stress that ultimately affects reliability.
This is particularly worrisome when it comes to chiplets, 3D-ICs and other advanced packaging architectures. Multiple dies, interconnects, substrates, materials and cooling approaches interact within a tightly integrated structure. Designers need to understand not only what happens within an individual die but how the entire assembly behaves as a system.
And addressing this means examining both accuracy and scale. The engineer developing a chip may need detailed information about localized behavior and potential hotspots. A package engineer needs a different level of abstraction, while a system architect may need to evaluate thermal and performance tradeoffs across an even larger environment. Simulating every element at maximum fidelity throughout the entire system would be computationally impractical.
The answer is not simply more simulation. It is applying the appropriate level of simulation and abstraction at each stage of the design process. Techniques such as reduced-order modeling and superposition can help engineering teams scale analysis while preserving the information needed to make architectural decisions. These techniques provide each engineer with the fidelity required for the task while maintaining connections between the physical domains that influence one another.
This also changes when multi-physics analysis needs to occur. Waiting until final verification to discover that a floor plan creates an unacceptable thermal or mechanical condition can lead to expensive redesigns or even a complete (and expensive) design re-spin. If engineers bring multi-physics analysis into architectural exploration and floor planning, they can evaluate performance, package size, thermal behavior and reliability together, when there is still flexibility to make meaningful changes.
AI and agentic engineering workflows offer another opportunity to accelerate this process by using Model Context Protocol (MCP) to help orchestrate increasingly complex tools, models and engineering data. But AI does not eliminate the need for trusted physics-based simulation. AI-generated decisions can be difficult to trace, and models can make mistakes. Engineering teams therefore need workflows that combine automation with reliable simulation and sufficient visibility into how results are produced.
This growing thermal challenge is part of a larger transformation in electronic design. Electrical, thermal, mechanical and other physical effects can no longer be treated as isolated disciplines. They are interconnected elements of the same engineering problem.
Keysight’s goal is to enable engineers to bring these domains together earlier in the development process, applying the right physics, fidelity and automation at the right time. By shifting multi-physics analysis left – from final verification toward architecture and design exploration –engineering teams can identify problems sooner, make better-informed tradeoffs and increase confidence that increasingly complex electronic systems will perform as intended before committing to physical hardware.
So is it getting hot in here? Absolutely. But with the right approach to design exploration and analysis, it doesn’t have to be your problem.

articles.title: Dar Blockchain, Hashgraph Association select 18 startups for Web3 incubation programme - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Dar Blockchain and The Hashgraph Association have selected 18 startups for a new Web3 incubation programme supporting winners of the Hedera Africa Hackathon.
Run in partnership with Tunisian incubator Wiki Startup and investment firm UGFS North Africa, with Softstack as security partner, the programme runs until January 2027. It aims to graduate at least five seed-ready companies by an investor demo day in the week of January 18.
The Hedera Africa Hackathon, which wrapped up in April, drew more than 13,000 developers and 1,300 project submissions. A portion of the hackathon’s prize pool has been set aside to support winners with product development, technical implementation and market validation during the incubation phase.
“Most hackathons stop when the winners are announced. For us, that’s where the real work begins,” said Jaafar Saied, co-founder of Dar Blockchain.
Selected startups will move through four sprints and five jury-audited gates, with 21 workshops, one-on-one expert support and introductions to investors. Teams will also be supported to deploy production-ready products on the Hedera mainnet. The programme targets more than 60 per cent of ventures securing signed letters of intent or launching active pilots by the third milestone gate.
The African startups selected are Nigeria’s GreenAfrica, Beyond Service Game, Upesa, Afiya and Cryptonia CITY; Egypt’s Carboni; South Africa’s Direla; Madagascar’s Nia; Zimbabwe’s RDZ Health; Morocco’s Hedron; and Côte d’Ivoire’s APIx.
They are joined by Effisend X Africa (Mexico), Silsilat Finance (Malaysia), Tedera (Romania), W.A.T.A (Brazil), CryptoMage (India), and US-based KeyRing and Building a Chain of Trust in the Green Power-to-X Market.

articles.title: Windows 11 permet enfin de personnaliser le menu du clic droit
articles.text:
Microsoft continue de distiller petit à petit les améliorations promises il y a quelques mois pour améliorer Windows 11. La dernière mise à jour facultative distribuée en preview le prouve encore. Estampillée KB5127936 et proposée sur les PC fonctionnant aussi bien sous Windows 11 25H2 que Windows 11 26H2, cette mise à jour fait le plein de nouveautés dans l’Explorateur de fichiers du système d’exploitation.
La firme de Redmond ne s’est pas arrêtée en si bon chemin et y a également intégré d’autres nouveautés notables, comme la prise en charge de nouveaux emojis, de nouveaux réglages dans les paramètres du Bluetooth ou encore l’amélioration de la gestion de l’alimentation. Voici un petit tour d’horizon des principales nouveautés à retenir dans la mise à jour KB5127936.
Le menu contextuel du clic droit enfin personnalisable
Voici sans doute l’une des plus grandes nouveautés apportées par cette mise à jour. Longtemps critiqué pour son manque de cohérence et de flexibilité, le menu contextuel du clic droit s’assouplit enfin. Microsoft vous autorise dorénavant à choisir précisément ce que vous voulez y faire apparaître.
Pour ce faire, il faut se rendre dans les Paramètres > Personnalisation > Menu contextuel.
Le menu permet ainsi de masquer les actions inutiles comme la possibilité d’imprimer, d’envoyer à, de créer un raccourci ou encore de faire pivoter l’image.
Un nouveau réglage permettant de regrouper toutes les extensions d’applications tierces ou natives au sein d’un menu dédié a par ailleurs fait son apparition.
Autre nouveauté qui a son importance, vous pouvez à présent configurer le menu hérité pour qu’il s’affiche directement sans avoir à maintenir la touche Maj enfoncée. Il faut pour cela activer l’option Afficher plus d’options dans le menu de personnalisation du menu contextuel.
À noter que l’accès aux options de personnalisation du menu contextuel du clic droit dans l’Explorateur de fichiers peut également se faire directement depuis celui-ci. Microsoft a en effet eu la brillante idée d’intégrer dans le menu contextuel un accès direct pour Personnaliser le menu (activé par défaut).
De nouvelles améliorations pour l’Explorateur de fichiers
Outre les nouvelles options de personnalisation du menu contextuel du clic droit, l’Explorateur de fichiers accueille aussi un certain nombre d’améliorations. Il sait par exemple afficher par défaut la prévisualisation des fichiers PDF dans le volet prévu à cet effet. Quant aux fichiers HTML téléchargés, Windows affiche un bouton de confirmation avant l’affichage.
Autre nouveauté, comme nous vous l’indiquions il y a quelques semaines, l’Explorateur de fichiers prend désormais en charge le raccourci ~ pour accéder rapidement aux dossiers de profils. Vous pouvez donc saisir directement dans la barre d’adresse de l’Explorateur ~\Téléchargements pour accéder au répertoire des téléchargements, par exemple.
Microsoft a également harmonisé l’application du thème sombre pour que la boîte de dialogue liée aux Options des dossiers soit enfin prise en charge. Enfin, la page d’accueil de l’Explorateur de fichiers conserve désormais son état (réduit ou développé) des différentes sections qu’elle comporte.
De nouvelles options pour la récupération du système
L’environnement de récupération de Windows 11 profite également de cette mise à jour. Comme Microsoft l’avait dévoilé au début de l’été, son module Cloud Rebuild, qui permet de réinstaller Windows 11 sans clé USB, en téléchargeant directement l’image disque ISO et les pilotes depuis les serveurs de Microsoft, est officiellement disponible.
En mode récupération, le système est d’ailleurs capable de réutiliser automatiquement les profils Wi-Fi enregistrés sur le PC pour se connecter tout seul à Internet afin de procéder à la restauration depuis le Cloud. Enfin, après une restauration système, Windows affiche automatiquement une fenêtre récapitulant les applications du Microsoft Store et les paramètres ayant été correctement réinstallés.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 29, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 29, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, October 29, 2026.
Artificial intelligence poses numerous challenges for employees but can improve governance in governments, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured stories
Vembu’s AI warning: one worker could do the work of ten
Artificial intelligence (AI) could allow one skilled employee to do work that previously required 10, reshaping employment even as it creates new opportunities. That is the warning from Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu. “What it does mean is a rebalancing across the economy and that is painful when we go through it. The only thing we can do is to accept that it is coming and be prepared for it,” he wrote on X.
Maharashtra launches MahaINDUS AI to speed up government work
Maharashtra is giving its government offices an AI upgrade. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis launched MahaINDUS, an AI platform designed for government offices, on October 28, 2026. The government said the initiative aims to improve transparency, accountability and administrative efficiency. By combining AI with integrated databases, departments are expected to find eligible beneficiaries, verify claims and assess welfare schemes more effectively.
Beyond AI infrastructure, India’s tech boom rests on the efficient use of power and water
At TechSparks 2026, founders of SolarSquare and Boson Whitewater unpack why overcoming perception, pricing gaps, and consumer trust matters far more in climatetech than just building the technology.
Funding news
Venttup raises $3M co-led by Rainmatter and Unicorn India Ventures
Industries 5.0 startup Venttup has raised $3 million in a pre-Series A funding round co-led by Rainmatter, backed by Zerodha, and Unicorn India Ventures. The company will use the funds to expand its engineering team, establish precision manufacturing capabilities and invest in rapid prototyping and AI-led sourcing.
Venttup is setting up a manufacturing facility in Bengaluru to support precision machining, turning and sheet metal production for energy transition, defence, aerospace and space applications. The company reported fivefold growth to ₹10 crore in FY2025-26 and has added over 15 blue-chip customers in the past year. Its business opportunity pipeline stands at approximately ₹30 crore.
Jagruti Rehabilitation Centre raises Rs 28 crore in Series A
Jagruti Rehabilitation Centre has raised Rs 28 crore in its first institutional funding round, led by Alkemi Growth Capital. The investment will support geographical expansion, increased clinical capacity, specialised care programmes and stronger insurance and corporate partnerships.
Founded in Pune in 2008, Jagruti provides mental healthcare, addiction treatment, rehabilitation and elder care services. The organisation currently operates more than 19 centres across nine cities, with over 1,600 beds and 40 doctors. It has supported more than 82,000 individuals. Jagruti plans to expand to over 40 centres and 4,000 beds across Tier I and Tier II cities over the next three to four years.
Coratia Technologies raises Rs 18 crore for underwater robotics
Underwater robotics startup Coratia Technologies has raised Rs 18 crore in a bridge funding round led by MGF Kavachh. The capital will support execution of its Rs 66 crore Indian Navy contract under the iDEX initiative, research and development, product development and manufacturing expansion.
Founded by Debendra Pradhan and Biswajit Swain, Coratia develops indigenous underwater robotic systems for defence, infrastructure and industrial applications. Its flagship Jalasimha underwater remotely operated vehicle has achieved Technology Readiness Level 9. The company's technologies can also support inspections of dams, bridges, ports, pipelines and offshore assets. Coratia had raised Rs 17 crore from MGF Kavachh, Piper and SIDBI in a pre-Series A round in 2025.
Carbelim secures Rs 10 crore from IIT Madras Unicorn Frontier Fund
Kerala-based deep-tech startup Carbelim has secured Rs 10 crore from the IIT Madras Unicorn Frontier Fund, becoming the first startup from the state to receive investment from the fund. Founded by Karthika Gopi and Rahul Babu, the company develops microalgae-based carbon capture and air-purification systems that absorb atmospheric carbon dioxide and convert it into oxygen. Carbelim has filed 13 patents, including seven in the US and six in India.
The funding is expected to help the company create more than 50 jobs and pursue its target of achieving Rs 100 crore in turnover through international markets. The Rs 1,000 crore fund is backed by IIT Madras, IIT Madras Research Park and Unicorn India Ventures.
Docterz raises Rs 5 crore, with doctors contributing 60% of funding
Healthcare technology company Docterz has raised Rs 5 crore from approximately 35 investors, including doctors who use its platform. Nearly 60% of the funding came from around 20 doctors, alongside investors such as SUGAR Cosmetics co-founder Vineeta Singh and former CaratLane CEO Avnish Anand. Founded by practising paediatrician Atish Laddad, Docterz provides digital medical records, appointment management, billing and patient engagement tools.
Its platform supports more than 5,000 doctors across India, with a strong presence in paediatrics. The company will use the capital to expand its reach, explore acquisitions and develop practical AI-enabled tools for medical practitioners, while maintaining a focus on patient data security and clinical independence.
ISLAND Beauty raises Rs 2.58 crore from AJ VC
Skincare brand ISLAND Beauty has raised Rs 2.58 crore from AJ VC to support product development, brand awareness and customer acquisition. Co-founded by Shirley Setia, Korean skincare expert Jinsoon Lee, Mayank Jain and Sakshi Jain, the company combines Korean skincare ingredients with formulations developed in India for local weather conditions and consumer needs. Its proprietary Core Barrier Matrix approach focuses on both skin-barrier repair and defence, encouraging simpler and more consistent skincare routines.
The brand's current portfolio includes cleansers, toners, serums, moisturisers and lip-care products. Over the next three years, ISLAND Beauty plans to expand its product range and strengthen its market presence, positioning itself around barrier-focused skincare for Indian consumers.
Viridian Ingni Propulsion raises Rs 1.47 crore in pre-seed round
Chennai-based propulsion technology startup Viridian Ingni Propulsion has raised ₹1.47 crore in a pre-seed round led by Inflection Point Ventures. The company has also secured ₹53.75 lakh in grants from government programmes and other institutions. Founded in February 2024 by Sriram G, the startup develops electric propulsion systems integrating motors, controllers and firmware. The funding will help it move from validated prototypes to pilot production, establish manufacturing infrastructure and complete certification requirements.
Other news
Dialog Axiata, IITM Pravartak partner on technology research
Sri Lankan connectivity provider Dialog Axiata has partnered with IITM Pravartak Technologies Foundation to advance applied research and technology development in Sri Lanka. The memorandum of understanding, signed in Colombo, will connect research networks with Sri Lankan universities, government bodies and industry stakeholders.
The collaboration will explore innovation and incubation, applied research, artificial intelligence, skills development and international knowledge sharing. Initial areas under consideration include Sinhala and Tamil conversational AI, technology-enabled dengue prevention and solutions to human-elephant conflict. The partnership will begin with selected pilot projects before considering wider deployment. The initiative aims to strengthen Sri Lanka's research capabilities and translate academic work into practical solutions addressing national and societal challenges.
Zoho upgrades Analytics with agentic AI capabilities
Chennai-based technology company Zoho has upgraded Zoho Analytics with an intelligence layer designed to connect business data, contextual understanding and automated actions. The platform introduces semantic and ontology layers to help AI agents interpret organisational structures, business terminology and key metrics. Its conversational business intelligence assistant, Ask Zia, uses six specialised sub-agents to handle data analysis, modelling, visualisation, preparation, coding and SQL generation. The platform also supports automated workflows, more than 500 existing data connectors and 30 additional connectors.
New governance features allow administrators to monitor agent activity, data access and costs. Zoho Analytics also introduces enhanced visualisations, forecasting tools and data science capabilities, enabling businesses to move from reporting towards AI-assisted operational execution.
Urban households expected to spend Rs 1.97 lakh crore this festive season: Local Circles
Urban Indian households are projected to spend approximately ₹1.97 lakh crore on festive purchases in 2026, according to a LocalCircles study. The estimate is around ₹12,000 crore higher than in 2024, despite moderating from the previous year's GST-related high. About 57% of urban households plan festive purchases, spending an average of nearly ₹20,000 each. Clothing, footwear and accessories lead planned purchases, followed by home appliances, furniture and travel. The study also points to growing demand for quick commerce as consumers postpone purchases until closer to festivals. Platforms including Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart, Zepto, Amazon Now and Flipkart Minutes are expanding their reach and reporting higher festive-season activity.
Fruugo partners with PayGlocal to help Indian sellers reach global markets
Global online marketplace Fruugo is entering India through a partnership with cross-border payments company PayGlocal and technology and operations provider DMSMatrix. The initiative will give PayGlocal's more than 12,000 merchants access to Fruugo's international marketplace, helping Indian businesses sell to consumers across more than 40 countries. Sellers in categories including electronics, clothing and home decor will be able to explore overseas demand and diversify their sales channels. The partnership combines Fruugo's international shopper network with PayGlocal's payments infrastructure and DMSMatrix's onboarding and operational capabilities. The initiative targets micro, small and medium enterprises seeking greater product visibility as domestic e-commerce competition intensifies and international online shopping continues to expand.
upGrad School of Technology partners with MongoDB
upGrad School of Technology has partnered with MongoDB to strengthen industry-integrated engineering education and prepare students for modern software development and AI applications. The collaboration will provide eligible students with access to MongoDB for Academia, technical learning resources and fully sponsored certification vouchers. The two organisations will also explore curriculum enhancements, hackathons, innovation challenges, guest lectures, internships and career opportunities. Faculty members will receive access to technical resources, while designated faculty champions will support adoption of modern database technologies.
The partnership aims to bridge the gap between academic learning and industry requirements, particularly in cloud-native development, artificial intelligence and database engineering. It will give students practical exposure and recognised credentials to improve career readiness.
Procol's AI procurement platform manages over $30 billion in spending
AI-powered procurement technology company Procol is helping manufacturing enterprises automate purchasing workflows across multiple plants, suppliers and business units. The company works with more than 150 manufacturing businesses across over 10 countries, including Havells, Emami, Blue Star and Aditya Birla Group. Its platform automates processes spanning supplier onboarding, requests for quotations, electronic auctions, approvals and accounts payable, while integrating with enterprise systems such as SAP and Oracle. Procol says its implementations have saved buyers more than 8,100 hours of manual work and enabled procurement cycles to become significantly faster. The company currently manages over $30 billion in spending and reports generating more than $1 billion in savings across its customer base.
Wadhwani FPO Entrepreneurship Program launched in Karnataka
The Centre of Excellence for Farmer Producer Organizations, supported by Karnataka's Department of Horticulture and the National Entrepreneurship Network, has launched the Wadhwani FPO Entrepreneurship Program in the state. The initiative aims to strengthen Farmer Producer Organizations through business planning, market access, mentoring and execution support.
Its first Growth Bootcamp brought together 27 FPOs and more than 60 participants, including government officials, business experts and FPO leaders.
Participating organisations assessed their businesses, identified growth opportunities and selected priority initiatives for the next 12 months. They will now enter a structured 10-week programme featuring expert-led group and individual sessions. The programme aims to help FPOs become more sustainable enterprises, improve farmer incomes and create rural economic opportunities.
Devnagri AI expands from translation to multilingual AI infrastructure
Language technology company Devnagri AI has announced an evolution from a translation-focused platform to multilingual AI infrastructure for enterprises. The company aims to integrate language capabilities directly into business workflows rather than treating translation as a standalone function. Its offerings include multilingual content processing and AI-driven communication tools designed for customer-facing services and internal operations.
The platform supports cloud, hybrid and on-premises deployment, enabling organisations to integrate language technology within their existing security and technology environments.
Founded in 2021 by Nakul Kundra and Himanshu Sharma, Devnagri AI focuses on helping businesses engage users in their preferred languages. The company believes contextual multilingual capabilities will be increasingly important as enterprises expand AI adoption across India's linguistically diverse markets.
TutorCloud AI launches integrated platform for K-12 education
TutorCloud AI has launched an integrated artificial intelligence-powered platform connecting students, teachers, parents and school administrators in one ecosystem. Designed for K-12 education, the platform aims to support personalised tutoring while giving educators and families greater visibility into students' learning journeys.
The initiative reflects a focus on using AI to help teachers understand learning progress and identify student needs, rather than simply generating answers. By bringing different stakeholders onto a common platform, TutorCloud AI seeks to improve coordination between classroom instruction, home support and school administration.
The company positions the system as a way to make learning more personalised and connected, while enabling educators to use technology to better understand and support individual students.
Wissen Technology strengthens Singapore leadership with Tinku Gupta
Wissen Technology is strengthening its Singapore operations through a delivery-led strategy focused on engineering expertise, product development and business outcomes. The technology services company has appointed Tinku Gupta as Vice Chairman of Wissen Technology Singapore. Gupta brings more than 30 years of experience spanning technology, financial market infrastructure, business operations and cybersecurity. Wissen aims to help enterprises modernise technology platforms and accelerate innovation.
Founded in 2000, the company says it has delivered projects worth more than $1 billion and serves over 20 Fortune 500 companies.
Vaani AI Research launches self-service platform for voice AI agents
Bengaluru- and Singapore-based Vaani AI Research has launched a self-service developer platform for building, deploying and managing voice AI agents. Users can describe the agent they want, preview its voice, configure actions and deploy it across phone calls, websites, applications and WhatsApp.
The platform is built around Vaani's voice infrastructure, which connects speech models with the systems needed to operate agents in production. Its capabilities include inference optimisation, memory and conversational controls.
The launch follows the company's experience deploying voice AI in enterprise workflows, where poor conversational experiences can frustrate customers and lead to lost opportunities. The platform aims to simplify development and deployment of voice-based AI services for businesses and developers.
Festive invoice financing crosses Rs 20,000 crore, says M1xchange
India's pre-festive financing volumes crossed Rs 20,000 crore in 2026, with micro, small and medium enterprises increasingly using formal invoice discounting to fund seasonal demand, according to trade receivables platform M1xchange. Financing for micro-MSMEs grew more than 100% year-on-year, while average daily festive financing increased over 40%. The company projects overall festive-season financing to grow approximately 30% this year.
Invoice discounting enables suppliers to access working capital against unpaid invoices, helping them purchase inventory and meet delivery commitments before customers make payments.
Sector-wise trends show strong festive-period activity in consumer durables, e-retail, e-commerce and paints. The findings highlight the growing role of formal credit mechanisms in supporting smaller suppliers during peak business periods.
Fluke begins local manufacturing of digital multimeter components in India
Fluke Corporation has launched a local manufacturing initiative in India, marking a step towards expanding its domestic manufacturing capabilities under the government's Make in India programme. The first phase covers manufacturing associated with the Fluke 115 and Fluke 117 digital multimeters, including local production of printed circuit board assemblies. The initiative follows the company's progression from Class II to Class I Local Supplier status.
Fluke said the move would strengthen its engagement with Indian customers and support the country's industrial development. The company aims to build local capabilities while maintaining its global standards for quality, precision and reliability. The initiative is intended to establish a foundation for further expansion of manufacturing operations in India.
Otto launches voice AI CRM for field sales teams
Voice AI company Otto, also known as Ottoverse, has launched a voice-based customer relationship management platform designed for field sales representatives. The system enables sales teams to manage CRM activities through phone calls rather than manually entering information after customer meetings. Representatives can report meeting outcomes, while Otto updates deal records, saves contacts, drafts follow-up emails, creates tasks and prepares summaries for managers.
The platform uses voice AI models trained on field sales conversations and is designed to recognise product names, part numbers and different accents. Its context layer connects calls, meetings, emails, calendars and enterprise resource planning records to provide relevant customer information. Headquartered in New York and Mumbai, Otto is backed by Gutter Capital.
Masai School cuts course fees by 50% in IIT Patna partnership
Masai School has reduced course fees by 50% across its programmes through a partnership with Vishlesan i-Hub at IIT Patna, aiming to make technology upskilling more accessible. The programmes include Analytics with Agentic AI and Applied AI and Machine Learning Essentials, with the latter also available in Tamil and Telugu.
About 70% of Masai's students come from Tier II and III cities. The collaboration will combine industry-led mentoring, access to the IIT ecosystem and placement support. Vishlesan i-Hub has enrolled 14,971 learners across its programmes, with nearly 60% studying in languages other than English. The initiative seeks to address affordability and language barriers affecting access to employment-oriented technology education.
Hoopr launches Smash Plus for music licensing in TV and OTT advertising
Music technology startup Hoopr has launched Hoopr Smash Plus, a platform for licensing music for television commercials, OTT advertising, films, web series and corporate productions. Kisna Jewellers is the first brand to use the service, licensing the track 'Woh Kisna Hai' from the Tips catalogue for a campaign featuring Shahid Kapoor and Mira Rajput Kapoor. The platform aims to simplify macro-sync licensing, which typically requires separate agreements with record labels, publishers and copyright societies.
Indian corporates drive flexible office demand as BFSI is fastest-growing sector: myHQ
India’s flexible office market is entering a more mature phase, with Indian corporates and banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) companies driving demand, according to a report by myHQ. Indian corporates accounted for 23.4% of flexible workspace demand in 2026, up from 21.9% in 2025, becoming the second-largest company segment after startups. Their average requirement increased from 25 seats in 2023 to 55 seats in 2026.
BFSI’s share of demand rose 2.7 times to 12.2% from 4.5% in 2023, making it the second-largest industry contributor. IT/ITeS remained the largest segment at 43.9%, while startups accounted for 39.2% of demand.
HomeLane turns EBITDA positive in Q4 FY26; targets Rs 1,000 crore revenue in FY27
HomeLane, a technology-enabled home interiors company, reported a return to growth following the integration of its businesses, with revenue increasing 19% and its order book expanding 37% year-on-year in the first half of FY27. The company turned operating EBITDA positive in the fourth quarter of FY26, reporting quarterly revenue of Rs 212 crore and an operating EBITDA margin of 5%.
HomeLane expects to cross Rs 1,000 crore in revenue in FY27 and remain EBITDA positive for the full financial year. The company said its growing order book provides visibility into the second half, as projects typically convert into revenue over six to nine months. For FY26, revenue remained steady at Rs 745 crore as HomeLane prioritised integrating DesignCafe. Direct project costs declined to 52% of revenue from 56.6% in FY25.
Sorry Sugar launches zero-added-sugar Diwali campaign
Zero-added-sugar beverage brand Sorry Sugar has launched its Diwali campaign, ‘Yeh Diwali, Bina Cheeni Wali’, featuring a music-driven film that challenges conventional perceptions of festive indulgence and healthy consumption.
The campaign seeks to position healthier choices as an alternative to traditional sugary treats without compromising on taste or celebration. It will be rolled out across the brand’s digital channels.
The company has also introduced an Assorted Coffee Gift Set featuring zero-added-sugar flavoured coffee premixes, a reusable organiser box and a complimentary frother. Founded in 2026, Sorry Sugar sells its products through its website and leading direct-to-consumer and quick-commerce platforms.

articles.title: Orgueil et Préjugés (1995) : où revoir gratuitement la série culte avant la version Netflix ?
articles.text:
Plus de trente ans après sa diffusion sur la BBC, la mini-série de 1995 reste pour beaucoup de fans l’adaptation de référence d’Orgueil et Préjugés de Jane Austen, devant même le film de Joe Wright avec Keira Knightley, sorti en 2005.
Avant de découvrir la nouvelle version de Netflix, avec Emma Corrin en Elizabeth Bennet et Jack Lowden en Mr. Darcy, c’est le bon moment pour la revoir. Bonne nouvelle : pas besoin de payer pour replonger dans les tourments sentimentaux de Longbourn et Pemberley.
M6+, Rakuten TV et Prime Video : trois adresses pour votre marathon Austen
M6+, la plateforme gratuite du groupe M6, propose les six épisodes de la mini-série (environ 50 minutes chacun) depuis le 1er avril. Le visionnage est gratuit, en échange de publicités. Rakuten TV diffuse aussi la série gratuitement, avec publicité.
La série de la BBC est aussi au catalogue de Prime Video, sans supplément pour les abonnés Amazon Prime. L’abonnement Amazon Prime, qui inclut Prime Video, coûte 6,99 euros par mois ou 69,90 euros par an avec publicité. Il faut compter 1,99 euro de plus par mois pour la retirer.
Pourquoi la version de 1995 d’Orgueil et Préjugés reste la référence des fans
Cette version de la BBC en six épisodes doit d’abord sa réputation au duo formé par ses deux acteurs principaux. Jennifer Ehle y joue une Elizabeth Bennet vive et indépendante, face au légendaire Mr. Darcy de Colin Firth. La série a fait entrer dans la pop culture la scène de la chemise mouillée, où Darcy sort trempé d’un lac.
Revoir la série maintenant permettra aussi de la comparer avec la version de Netflix, qui sort le jeudi 3 décembre. La version de 1995, écrite par Andrew Davies, servira de point de repère pour juger les choix de la nouvelle série, signée par la scénariste Dolly Alderton.

articles.title: Pieterjan Bouten’s Entourage closes €100 million second fund after surpassing €75 million target in two weeks | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Entourage, the London-based early-stage VC firm founded by Showpad co-founder and former CEO Pieterjan Bouten, today announced the close of its €100 million second fund, just over two years after launching its first fund in 2024.
Entourage Fund II has been backed entirely by entrepreneurs, family offices and private investors, including founders behind Aikido, TechWolf and Collibra. It has surpassed its original €75 million target in just 2 weeks and has secured over €100 million in commitments before being capped at €100 million. 
“When we launched Entourage two years ago, we had a simple ambition: to back the next generation of legendary founders. We wrote the first cheques into companies like Aikido, Conveo and Lexroom. What these founders have achieved in such a short time has only strengthened our conviction in our founder-first approach. With Fund II, we’re doubling down,” said Pieterjan (PJ) Bouten, Founder and General Partner of Entourage.
Founded in 2024 by Bouten, Entourage claims to bring a founder’s mindset and an operator’s experience to venture capital. It backs “exceptional founders” at the pre-Seed and Seed stages and invests across sectors, including AI, enterprise software, robotics, and DeepTech.
Bouten co-founded and scaled Showpad into a global software company generating more than €89.84 million ($100 million) in annual recurring revenue. He then became an active angel investor before launching Entourage.
In this episode of The EU-Startups Podcast, Bouten reflects on his journey from co-founding In the Pocket and scaling Showpad to now building and funding the next generation of B2B SaaS companies through Entourage Studio and Entourage Capital.
According to him, this experience helped forge Entourage’s approach: build conviction, invest early and keep founders firmly in the driver’s seat.
The firm states that it extends its founder-first philosophy to governance as well, and therefore rarely takes board seats despite leading or co-leading most of its investment rounds.
Bouten said, “Most VCs destroy value in early-stage boardrooms. Too few have built a company at scale. After more than a decade as a founder and CEO, and investments in over 60 companies, I’ve seen investors slow founders down with misplaced advice and operational interference. Great founders don’t need babysitting. They need trust, challenge when it counts and perspective at pivotal moments. That’s why we rarely take board seats, even when we lead a round.”
He also highlighted that the firm’s investor base reflects that philosophy. “Many of our investors have built companies themselves. They know what it takes. That creates a powerful alignment between the people funding Entourage and the founders we back,” he added. 
Since launching in 2024, Entourage reported that it has backed some of Europe’s fastest-growing technology companies, including Aikido Security, which reached unicorn status earlier this year; Conveo, which recently raised a €44.92 million ($50 million) Series A; and Lexroom, which reached €30 million in annual recurring revenue in just 24 months.
“Entourage was among the first investors in all three, backing their founders before major international venture capital firms arrived – often before a product launch or the first euro of Revenue,” the firm mentioned in the press release. 
Fund II will back around 25 companies at the pre-Seed and Seed stages across Europe and beyond, with initial cheques of €1 million to €5 million and “ample” capacity for follow-on investments.
Entourage states that it seeks “driven, ambitious founders building their life’s work.” It argues that while the first fund focused primarily on software, Fund II will broaden its focus to include AI and enterprise software, robotics, physical AI, and DeepTech.
The London-based VC firm also builds companies through Entourage Studio, its venture-building arm. Alongside Fund II, Entourage has expanded its investment team around partners Pieterjan Bouten, Evert Beeckman and Maarten Mortier. It has added three investors—Erwan Gardelle, Sixtine Riescher, and Illja Schiller—opened a London office and established a presence in Paris.

articles.title: Ce laptop gaming de MSI équipé de la RTX 3050 et de 16 Go de RAM perd 150 euros
articles.text:
Le MSI Cyborg 15 est une machine complète avec une configuration qui permet de jouer en 1 080p sans que vous ayez à vous ruiner puisque sur le site de Cdiscount, il est disponible pour 150 euros de moins grâce à un code promo.
En pleine inflation des composants pour PC, MSI a sorti son Cyborg 15 habituellement vendu pour 950 euros. Pour arriver à ce prix plus contenu, la marque a dû faire des choix et s'est arrêtée sur l'Intel Core i7 et 16 Go de RAM. Concernant la RAM, vous pouvez ajouter des barrettes supplémentaires pour atteindre 64 Go de RAM. En entrant le code 50GAMING849 sur le site de Cdiscount, le prix de la machine passe sous les 800 euros.
Sur le site de Cdiscount, le MSI Cyborg 15 passe de 949 euros à 799,99 euros
Pourquoi choisir le MSI Cyborg 15 ?
- Pour l'Intel Core i7 et 16 Go de RAM : Grâce à ce duo, le MSI Cyborg 15 permet de jouer aux titres les plus récents et de réaliser vos envies créatives en intégrant des éléments en 3D.
- Pour la RTX 3050 : Pour jouer en Full HD, MSI a intégré la RTX 3050 à sa machine. L'IA est aussi présente pour aider à l'upscaling ou pour créer des visuels pour vos montages vidéo.
- Pour son bel écran de 15 pouces : Que vous soyez un joueur ou un travailleur, vous serez à l'aise devant cet écran de 15,4 pouces qui possède un taux de rafraîchissement de 144 Hz. Malheureusement, la luminosité pêche comme c'est souvent le cas sur ces machines.
Une configuration polyvalente
Pour plaire aux gamers, MSI a offert l'Intel Core i7 et la RTX 3050 à son laptop, ce qui permet de jouer en 1080p aux titres les plus récents. Pour avoir un multitâche fluide, vous pourrez compter sur les 16 Go de RAM avec la possibilité de grimper à 64 Go. Outre le gaming, le laptop se destine aussi aux montages vidéo et tous les fichiers pourront être enregistrés dans le disque dur interne de 512 Go.
Ce MSI Cyborg 15 se présente avec une dalle de 15 pouces et un taux de rafraîchissement de 144 Hz. Comme souvent, la luminosité pêche avec un pic de luminosité qui dépasse légèrement 260 nits.
Autre défaut commun aux laptops gaming : l'autonomie. En jeu, vous peinerez à jouer plus de quatre heures sans brancher l'ordinateur.
Un design qui souffle le chaud et le froid
Le design de ce MSI Cyborg 15 peine à convaincre. Le clavier rétroéclairé est appréciable, mais le reste du design est moins convaincant. Deux petites charnières soutiennent l'écran, ce qui peut poser quelques questions concernant sa résistance sur le long terme. La mention "MSI True Gaming" est présente sur l'ordinateur avec une incrustation qui pourrait en déplaire à certains.
Même son de cloche du côté de la connectique. Le MSI Cyborg 15 aurait pu signer une copie parfaite dans cette catégorie puisqu'on retrouve un port HDMI, un port USB-C, deux ports USB-A ainsi qu'un combo jack. Cependant, MSI n'est pas allée au bout de sa démarche en faisant l'impasse sur un port pour les cartes SD.
✅ Les points forts
- Une configuration confortable pour jouer en 1 080p
- 16 Go de RAM pour le multitâche
- Un système de refroidissement pour des performances de haut niveau même lors des sessions les plus longues
❌ Les limites
- Une faible autonomie comme tous les laptops gaming
- Windows n'est pas intégré
Le MSI Cyborg 15 est actuellement disponible pour 799,99 euros au lieu de 949 euros sur le site de Cdiscount
Ce MSI Cyborg 15 possède une configuration polyvalente qui plaira aux joueurs, mais aussi aux créatifs. Si MSI s'est appliquée sur la fiche technique, la marque propose un design qui va diviser.
Autre point qui peut poser problème : l'absence de Windows qui forcera un second passage à la caisse.

articles.title: CISA warns of Fragnesia Linux flaw chained in PHP2Shell attacks
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies to patch a high-severity Linux kernel privilege escalation bug that attackers are chaining with the PHP2Shell flaws in the wild.
Tracked as CVE-2026-46300 and known as Fragnesia, this vulnerability stems from a logic bug in the Linux XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem that lets attackers run malicious code with root permissions.
Fragnesia belongs to the Dirty Frag vulnerability class and has a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit that local attackers can use to gain root privileges on major Linux distributions with kernels released before May 13, 2026.
CISA added CVE-2026-46300 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Wednesday and ordered federal agencies to patch their systems by Saturday 10, as mandated by its Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.
The cybersecurity agency didn't share details about ongoing Fragnesia attacks, but it noted that threat actors could chain it with two critical PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), collectively tracked as PHP2Shell, to deploy webshells on unpatched systems.
"This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root," CISA said.
Fragnesia and PHP2Shell exploit chain
While CISA didn't provide more information on attackers chaining the Fragnesia and PHP2Shell flaws, Dream Security analysts said in a Monday report that the vulnerabilities were used to breach more than two dozen servers, including three belonging to a US government-affiliated organization.
"Dream researchers identified a complete attack operation that included a custom weaponization of the PHP2Shell exploit chain (CVE-2026-109618/CVE-2026-109619) paired with the Fragnesia kernel privilege escalation (CVE-2026-46300), target lists, exploitation logs, and approximately 40 custom post-exploitation scripts," they said.
"This included artifacts of a campaign that had rooted 25 servers across the United States, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea. Once rooted, the attacker zeroed in on three specific servers in a US government-affiliated environment."
CISA also added the PHP2Shell flaws to its list of actively exploited vulnerabilities on Monday and mandated that Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies secure their networks by Thursday.
While the US cybersecurity agency has not yet provided further details on ongoing PHP2Shell attacks, Perplexity security engineer Adel Karimi confirmed in-the-wild exploitation over the weekend after their honeypots recorded evidence of remote code execution against an Apache mod_php installation running PHP 8.4.26.
A CISA spokesperson couldn't immediately share more information about threat actors potentially chaining Fragnesia and PHP2Shell in attacks when BleepingComputer reached out earlier today.
