articles.title: Ikea’s colorful donut-shaped smart lamp is $20 off
articles.text:
With its playful design, versatility, and relatively affordable price, the Ikea Varmblixt quickly became one of my colleague Jennifer Pattison Tuohy’s new favorite smart light products when she tested it in April. Now, the donut-shaped lamp is on sale for $79.99 ($20 off) through November 11th at Ikea.
Ikea’s colorful donut-shaped smart lamp is $20 off
The Varmblixt can display hundreds of colors thanks to its Matter support, and can be put on your table or wall
Don’t let us tell you where you can or cannot put your Varmblixt. But it’s meant to sit on a table or be mounted on a wall (it can hang from a drilled-in screw, nothing fancy). At just 180 lumens, it isn’t particularly bright, so it’s better suited for use as a bedside lamp or for mood lighting than being tasked to illuminate a room. The newer model lets you cycle through 12 preset colors, including shades of pink, blue, green, and white, as opposed to just orange with the predecessor. The included wireless remote lets you switch between colors, adjust the brightness, and turn the lamp on or off without needing an app or a separate hub (there’s a power button on the lamp itself) . You can also use the remote to control other compatible Ikea lights.
For those who want to embed the Varmblixt into their smart home setup, the lamp supports Matter, allowing it to work with compatible smart home platforms including Apple Home, Google Home, and Amazon Alexa. In addition to letting you control the lights with your voice, this gives you access to hundreds more colors, lets you set lighting schedules and sleep or wake-up routines, and allows you to connect the lamp with motion sensors and other smart lights you may have. You can unlock those features with Ikea’s Dirigera hub, as well, which also offers a feature through its Home Smart app that gradually adjusts the shade of white throughout the day akin to natural daylight.

articles.title: From Functional Monitoring To In-System Test: Extending Voltage-Aware Observability
articles.text:
Separate false failures caused by voltage droop from real structural defects.
By Aakash Jani, Henrique Mendes, and Robert Wilcox
In a previous blog, we highlighted the importance of combining physical and functional sensors to plan for new workloads. This use case remains relevant for high-performance AI and HPC systems because ‘spiky’ workloads induce severe droops that dominate power budgets.
Your $1 billion ASIC just had a scan failure during an In-System Test. How can you tell whether the failure is an actual structural failure, or one caused by physical phenomena like voltage droop? Scan patterns can often generate intense switching activity when long or multiple chains are toggled, which may induce a voltage droop. If the failure is due to a voltage droop, you have a few options: slow the shift clock, raise the voltage, or repartition your scan patterns. Without physical sensors that report conditions during the test, teams can’t tell the two cases apart and might throw away good parts on false failures.
Co-mingling physical and functional sensors is necessary across the system lifecycle because functional and physical failures are connected. Let’s move further down the system lifecycle into silicon deployment for another example.
The previous demo combined the Movellus Aeonic Insight Droop Detector with Siemens Tessent Embedded Analytics to correlate voltage events with processor and interconnect activity. Today, we are proud to announce an extension of physical and functional monitoring for system lifecycle management: adding Tessent In-System Test (IST) to the demo. Running structural test on deployed systems means the false-failure question follows the part off the tester and into the field, where a wrong call can get a healthy node pulled from service. Combined with voltage monitoring, IST helps engineers separate false failures caused by droop from real structural defects.
Meta ran silent-error tests across hundreds of thousands of fleet machines and flagged hundreds of CPUs that corrupted data without reporting an error.[1] Google has reported a similar rate in its own fleet.[2] Amazon also presented its results from using In-System Test technology on AWS silicon.[3] Tessent IST incorporates selected structural tests into deployed systems, allowing testing without removing the device, so faults like these can be investigated early.
However, structural testing can cause intense switching activity, which can lead to voltage droops during tests. These events depend on test patterns, sensor locations, and device conditions. A pass/fail result alone lacks context.
Combining IST with telemetry enables more detailed analysis: Did the droop coincide with testing? Which core was tested? Was other traffic active?
The updated demonstration integrates Tessent IST, alongside the previous solution, on a Siemens Veloce proFPGA platform: Movellus Aeonic Insight voltage-droop sensors, Tessent Embedded Analytics functional monitors and message infrastructure, and Siemens scan-and-test infrastructure for IST. The target design contains multiple DFT-instrumented RISC-V cores, which drive the workload observed in the functional mode, and then receive scan patterns when brought into test mode.
Fig. 1: Demo system including Tessent Embedded Analytics, the Movellus Aeonic Insight voltage-droop sensor, and scan-and-test infrastructure.
Functional Mode: a Movellus voltage droop detector is configured through an APB path and can issue a hardware event when a programmed threshold is crossed. Tessent Embedded Analytics receives the event through its trigger and message infrastructure. A Status Monitor records sensor and system signals with timestamps, while a Bus Monitor reports transaction activity on the SoC interconnect. The workflow shows how a physical event initiates collection of the functional evidence needed to investigate its root cause.
Fig. 2: Functional-mode workflow correlating voltage-droop events with timestamped processor and interconnect activity.
Test Mode: The Tessent IST support adds test control and test-state visibility. Test patterns are run on the demonstration platform, and test start and stop activity is observed through Tessent Embedded Analytics Status monitoring, which monitors an internal test-mode state, so that the test window can be aligned with voltage data. This gives the demonstration time-aligned test execution and sensor behavior.
The value of the combined approach is not that voltage telemetry replaces structural test, or that functional monitors determine whether a test pattern passed. The benefit comes from placing their outputs on a common timeline. Structural test identifies whether the targeted logic responds as expected. The voltage monitor reports the physical conditions during that test. Functional monitors reveal concurrent system activity that may have contributed to those conditions.
For example, if a voltage excursion appears only when a particular pattern group is active, the engineer has a focused starting point for investigation. If the excursion coincides instead with heavy traffic from a neighboring functional core, the test scheduler may avoid running that workload and the test concurrently. Repeated observations across sensor locations can also help determine whether an event is local or shared across part of the power-delivery network. These are diagnostic leads rather than conclusions, but they narrow the search space and reduce dependence on worst-case assumptions.
Fig. 3: Test-mode workflow aligning In-System test execution with voltage-sensor data using Status Monitor.
The previous blog showed how a voltage droop detector and functional monitoring can bridge the physical and functional domains. Adding Tessent IST extends that observability into test operation. The same sensor can contribute evidence during normal workloads and while structural test content is being applied, while Tessent Embedded Analytics supplies the timestamped context needed to relate those observations.
The current FPGA demonstration establishes the end-to-end concept by running IST patterns and correlating test start and stop with voltage and functional-monitor data. The next step is to complete direct sensor access through iJTAG, providing a path in which test control, sensor observability and functional telemetry can be coordinated through the deployed system.
Together, these capabilities move in-system diagnosis beyond isolated measurements and toward a repeatable detect-diagnose-test workflow.
Henrique Mendes is a product engineer for Tessent Embedded Analytics at Siemens EDA.
Robert Wilcox is a product engineer for Tessent Embedded Analytics at Siemens EDA.
Leave a Reply

articles.title: 12 Best AI Dance Video Generators in 2026 - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The AI video generation space has sharply divided into two distinct categories: tools that puppeteer a character based on an existing reference video (motion transfer), and tools that listen to audio and automatically choreograph original movement (music-driven).
Choosing the right ai dance video generator usually comes down to whether you are trying to replicate a trending clip or generate a completely new performance tailored to a specific song.
This guide evaluates the top tools available right now based on their ability to handle full-length tracks, maintain rhythm accuracy, and reduce the manual steps required to reach a finished export.
Quick Answer: AI dance video generator
For creators who start with a finished song and need rhythm-aware choreography, freebeat is the best overall AI dance video generator because it analyzes the track’s music signals to build a full-song performance. If you already have a reference video and just want to swap the character, Viggle is the best option for template-based motion transfer. Kling AI handles highly realistic single-shot prompts best, while tools like Vidu and Runway serve as specialized utilities for shorter, prompt-based cinematic clips.
Table 1: AI Dance Video Generator Capabilities and Pricing Overview
(Pricing verified as of September 2026)
| Product | Full-Song Performance (Not Clips) | Lip Sync While Dancing | Choreography Range | Steps to a Finished Video | Pricing | Free Tier Allowance | Watermark Policy | 
| freebeat | Up to 6 min (Pro tier) | ~90% accuracy (12+ languages) | 20+ styles via free-text prompt | 4 steps (Link/Audio → Photo → Mode → Generate) | From $4.99/week | 500 lifetime credits (No credit card) | Free tier includes watermark; Paid removes it | 
| Viggle | Clip-based | No | Depends entirely on reference video | 3 steps (Upload video & photo → Generate) | From $7.99/mo | 5 videos/day | Free tier includes watermark; Paid removes it | 
| Kling AI | Single shots | No | Limited by prompt interpretation | 3 steps (Prompt/image → Settings → Generate) | From $8.80/mo | 66 daily credits | Free tier includes watermark; Paid removes it | 
| Seedance | Engine capability | No | Prompt-based styles | 4 steps (Varies by host platform) | — | — | — | 
| Vidu | Clip-based | No | Prompt-based styles | 3 steps (Upload image → Prompt → Generate) | From $15/mo | 80 credits/mo | Free tier includes watermark; Paid removes it | 
| Alici | Clip-based | No | Prompt-based styles | 3 steps (Upload asset → Prompt → Generate) | From $12/mo | Basic free access | Free tier includes watermark; Paid removes it | 
| Runway | Up to 18s (Gen-3) | No | Prompt-based cinematic styles | 4 steps (Upload/Prompt → Adjust → Generate) | From $12/mo | 125 lifetime credits | No watermark on paid | 
| Media.io | Clip-based | No | Template-bound | 3 steps (Select template → Upload → Export) | From $7.99/mo | 3-5 credits for drafting | Free tier includes watermark; Paid removes it | 
| DeepMotion | 10-20s clips | No | Depends on input video | 5 steps (Upload video → Rig → Export 3D) | From $9/mo | 25-60 credits/mo | Free tier includes watermark; Paid removes it | 
| CapCut | Clip-based | No | Template-bound | 3 steps (Template → Replace media → Export) | — | — | — | 
| Mango AI | 3-5 min total (Free) | No | Presenter-style presets | 4 steps (Avatar → Script → Background → Export) | From $3.92/mo | 180 credits/mo | Free tier includes watermark; Paid removes it | 
| Lumigen | Clip-based | No | Template-bound avatars | 3 steps (Select avatar → Input script → Generate) | — | — | — | 
How we compared AI dance generator tools in 2026
To differentiate true choreography engines from basic video filters, we evaluated the recorded capabilities of these platforms as of September 2026. We utilized the Audio-Driven vs. Template-Driven Automation Matrix—a proprietary evaluation framework that categorizes AI dance generator tools based on two critical axes: the source of the movement (Does the AI listen to the music, or copy a video?) and the output duration (Does it output a 5-second clip, or a full song?).
Each tool was measured against the following dimensions:
- Full-Song Performance (Not Clips): Does the tool output a few seconds of looping footage, or can it generate a cohesive performance that spans a full 3-to-6-minute music track?
- Lip Sync While Dancing: Can the character sing the lyrics while performing complex choreography without the face distorting?
- Choreography Range: Is the user restricted to a dropdown menu of pre-baked animations, or can the AI generate dozens of unique styles dynamically?
- Steps to a Finished Video: How many manual actions are required between uploading the initial assets and downloading a ready-to-publish video?
1. freebeat — The Best Overall AI Dance Video Generator
Key Specifications
- Full-Song Performance (Not Clips): Generates full-length videos up to 6 minutes (on the Pro tier and above).
- Lip Sync While Dancing: Achieves ~90% accuracy across 12+ optimized languages.
- Choreography Range: 20+ common dance styles via free-text prompt (e.g., Hip-Hop, Jazz, Ballet, K-pop).
- Steps to a Finished Video: 4 steps (Input audio → Upload photo → Select mode → Generate).
How It Works
Unlike platforms that require an existing video to copy, freebeat’s AI dance video generator builds choreography directly from the rhythm of the music. The workflow begins with zero friction: users paste a track link (with native support for platforms like Suno, Udio, YouTube, and SoundCloud) or upload an audio file, followed by a single character photo using the ai singing photo generator.
The underlying Music Video Agent then analyzes the track across seven distinct music signals: tempo/BPM, a frame-accurate beat grid, percussive events, energy curves, spectral content, song sections, and section-level tags. Utilizing 5-tier beat quantization, the AI automatically plans the choreography so that movements, transitions, and cuts land exactly on the song’s real rhythm.
Users can opt for Studio mode for automated model selection and one-click generation, or switch to Custom mode to manually pair image models (like GPT-Image 2 or Nano Banana Pro) with specific video engines (such as Seedance 2.5, Wan 2.7, or HappyHorse). Background scenes are entirely customizable through prompts. For creators looking to generate a short, staged singing clip rather than a full track, freebeat’s Photo Karaoke video maker handles 30-second outputs, while the main agent handles full-length performances. Featured in Reuters for passing the one billion seconds milestone and utilized by 1,000,000+ creators across 150+ countries, the platform is built for scale. A known limitation is that rendering a highly complex, full-length 6-minute video consumes a significant amount of credits, requiring a higher-tier subscription.
Pricing
- Pricing: Starts at $4.99/week for the Basic plan (promo). The Pro plan costs $26.99/mo and unlocks generation up to 6 minutes. (official site, accessed September 2026).
- Free tier: 500 lifetime credits granted upon sign-up; no credit card required.
- Watermark: Free tier exports include a watermark. The Basic plan and above remove it entirely.
Bottom Line
For creators who start from a finished song, freebeat is the best overall pick because it builds genuine, beat-synced choreography directly from the music’s real rhythm rather than relying on copied reference footage.
2. Viggle — The Best AI Dance Video Generator for Motion Transfer
Key Specifications
- Full-Song Performance (Not Clips): Clip-based generation; manual stitching required for full songs.
- Lip Sync While Dancing: No built-in lip sync during complex movement.
- Choreography Range: Depends entirely on the reference video provided.
- Steps to a Finished Video: 3 steps (Upload reference video → Upload character photo → Generate).
How It Works
Viggle dominates the motion transfer space. Rather than listening to an audio track to invent choreography, Viggle requires a reference video of a human dancing. The AI then maps the physical motion from that reference video onto a new uploaded character photo. This makes it highly effective for recreating specific viral social media trends where the exact steps are already known. Users cannot prompt the AI to invent a dance style; the output is strictly bound to the input video’s physical movements.
Pricing
- Pricing: Pro plan starts at $7.99/mo (promotional, originally $9.99/mo) for 80 credits. (official site, accessed September 2026).
- Free tier: 5 free videos per day at $0.
- Watermark: Free tier includes a watermark. Paid plans feature no watermark.
Bottom Line
Viggle is the default choice for creators who already possess a video of the exact dance they want and simply need to replace the original performer with a new character photo.
3. Kling AI — The Best Realistic AI Dance Video Generator
Key Specifications
- Full-Song Performance (Not Clips): Single-shot clips; does not automatically sequence full songs.
- Lip Sync While Dancing: No simultaneous singing and dancing capability.
- Choreography Range: Prompt-based interpretation, though limited in precise rhythm adherence.
- Steps to a Finished Video: 3 steps (Input prompt/image → Adjust camera settings → Generate).
How It Works
Kling AI is highly regarded for its physical realism and high-fidelity textures. When tasked with an AI dance video generator prompt, Kling excels at rendering lifelike fabric physics, lighting, and human anatomy. While newer engines like hailuo focus on rapid prompt adherence, Kling prioritizes cinematic realism. However, because it lacks dedicated music analysis signals, the resulting dance movements are not synced to any specific BPM or audio track, making it a visual engine rather than a musical one.
Pricing
- Pricing: Paid subscriptions start around $8.80 to $10.00 per month for the Standard tier. (retrieved source, accessed September 2026).
- Free tier: 66 daily credits (which expire after 24 hours).
- Watermark: Free tier exports include a visible watermark. Paid membership tiers remove it.
Bottom Line
Kling AI produces the most realistic and visually stunning individual video shots, but it requires manual editing and external audio syncing to create a cohesive music video.
4. Seedance — The Engine for Beat-Synced Choreography
Key Specifications
- Full-Song Performance (Not Clips): Generally capped around 3 to 5 minutes depending on the host platform.
- Lip Sync While Dancing: No native lip-sync in the raw engine.
- Choreography Range: Prompt-based styles.
- Steps to a Finished Video: 4 steps, dictated by the overarching platform UI.
How It Works
Seedance operates primarily as an underlying generation engine rather than a standalone consumer application. It is highly capable of beat-synced choreography and is integrated into broader platforms. For example, Seedance 2.5 and Seedance 2.5 Fast are available directly inside freebeat’s Custom mode. When accessed through these platforms, the engine utilizes the host’s music analysis to output rhythm-aware movements.
Pricing
- Pricing: —
- Free tier: —
- Watermark: —
Bottom Line
Seedance provides a powerful backend engine for beat-synced movement, but creators will get the most value out of it by accessing it through a structured platform that handles the music analysis frontend.
5. Vidu — The Best Option for Multi-Reference Consistency
Key Specifications
- Full-Song Performance (Not Clips): Clip-based outputs.
- Lip Sync While Dancing: No.
- Choreography Range: Prompt-based interpretation.
- Steps to a Finished Video: 3 steps (Upload multi-angle image assets → Enter prompt → Generate).
How It Works
Vidu specializes in multi-reference image-to-video generation. If a creator has a complex original character, they can upload multiple reference images to ensure the AI maintains strict character consistency from various angles during the movement. It generates high-quality short clips, though users must manually stitch these clips together and align them to a beat in post-production software.
Pricing
- Pricing: Paid plans start at approximately $15 per month for the Starter plan. (retrieved source, accessed September 2026).
- Free tier: 80 credits per month.
- Watermark: Free-tier video generation includes a watermark and caps resolution at 720p. Paid tiers offer watermark-free commercial exports.
Bottom Line
Vidu is the strongest tool for preserving the exact visual details of a custom character across a short, prompt-generated movement clip.
6. Alici — The All-in-One Generator for Short Clips
Key Specifications
- Full-Song Performance (Not Clips): Clip-based.
- Lip Sync While Dancing: No.
- Choreography Range: Prompt-based styles.
- Steps to a Finished Video: 3 steps (Upload asset → Enter prompt → Generate).
How It Works
Alici (Alici AI) positions itself as an all-in-one generative suite. Its interface allows for straightforward image animation and basic dance movements based on text prompts. It serves as a rapid drafting tool for marketers and social media managers who need quick, isolated bursts of movement without the complexity of a full-scale timeline editor.
Pricing
- Pricing: Paid plans start at $12 per month for the Basic plan. (retrieved source, accessed September 2026).
- Free tier: Basic free access is provided for initial interface testing.
- Watermark: Free tier stamps outputs with a watermark. Paid tiers unlock watermark-free downloads.
Bottom Line
Alici provides a quick and accessible interface for generating short, isolated movement clips without a steep learning curve.
7. Runway — The Best for Cinematic AI Video Clips
Key Specifications
- Full-Song Performance (Not Clips): Outputs clips up to 18 seconds (via Gen-3).
- Lip Sync While Dancing: No simultaneous full-body dance and lip sync.
- Choreography Range: Cinematic, prompt-based styles.
- Steps to a Finished Video: 4 steps (Upload/Prompt → Adjust settings → Generate → Extend).
How It Works
Runway sets the industry standard for cinematic video generation. Similar to pika, it relies heavily on detailed text prompts to guide camera movement, lighting, and action. While Runway Act-Two handles expressive facial performances, generating a full-body AI dance video generator sequence requires precise prompting and iterative clip extensions. Because it does not analyze audio files for rhythm, any synchronization to music must be achieved manually by editing the generated clips together in a non-linear editor.
Pricing
- Pricing: Starts at $12/mo (billed annually) for 625 credits/mo. (official site, accessed September 2026).
- Free tier: 125 one-time lifetime credits.
- Watermark: Paid plans feature no watermarks.
Bottom Line
Runway is the premier choice for generating visually breathtaking, highly cinematic short clips that will be assembled into a larger project later.
8. Media.io — The Best Online Editor Toolkit
Key Specifications
- Full-Song Performance (Not Clips): Clip-based outputs restricted by timeline limits.
- Lip Sync While Dancing: No.
- Choreography Range: Template-bound.
- Steps to a Finished Video: 3 steps (Select template → Upload media → Export).
How It Works
Media.io functions less as a standalone generative model and more as a comprehensive online editor and AI toolkit. It offers a variety of quick-apply filters and templates that can animate a still photo into basic rhythmic motion. It is designed for casual users looking to create quick social media posts rather than professional choreographers requiring precise beat control.
Pricing
- Pricing: Standard plan starts at $7.99 to $9.99 per month. (retrieved source, accessed September 2026).
- Free tier: 3 daily check-in credits or 5 draft credits.
- Watermark: Free tier strictly carries an AI Gen watermark. Standard plan unlocks 1080p watermark-free exports.
Bottom Line
Media.io is a convenient, browser-based utility for users who want to apply basic animation templates to photos without dealing with complex prompting.
9. DeepMotion — The Best for 3D Animation and Motion Capture
Key Specifications
- Full-Song Performance (Not Clips): Limited to 10-20 second clips per generation.
- Lip Sync While Dancing: No.
- Choreography Range: Depends entirely on the input video’s physical motion.
- Steps to a Finished Video: 5 steps (Upload video → Process motion → Map to 3D rig → Adjust physics → Export).
How It Works
DeepMotion operates in a completely different paradigm from text-to-video generators. It is a markerless AI motion capture tool. Users upload a 2D video of a person dancing, and the AI extracts the skeletal motion data to animate a 3D digital avatar. This makes it an invaluable tool for game developers and 3D animators, though it requires an existing video source and does not generate original choreography from music.
Pricing
- Pricing: Paid plans start at $9 per month (billed annually). (retrieved source, accessed September 2026).
- Free tier: Provides 25 to 60 credits per month.
- Watermark: Free tier usage imposes visual branding/watermarks and lower resolutions. Paid plans offer clean exports.
Bottom Line
DeepMotion is strictly for 3D artists and developers who need to extract motion data from a real-world dance video to animate a custom 3D rig.
10. CapCut — The Best for Social Media Templates
Key Specifications
- Full-Song Performance (Not Clips): Clip-based, tied to specific social media audio trends.
- Lip Sync While Dancing: No.
- Choreography Range: Template-bound.
- Steps to a Finished Video: 3 steps (Select template → Replace media → Export).
How It Works
CapCut provides an ecosystem driven entirely by viral templates. While it includes AI effects that can make photos shake, zoom, or simulate dancing to a beat, it does not synthesize new human movement from scratch. Its strength lies in its massive library of user-generated templates that automatically sync photo transitions to trending TikTok audio.
Pricing
- Pricing: —
- Free tier: —
- Watermark: —
Bottom Line
CapCut is the fastest way to format existing photos and videos into a trending, beat-synced social media format using pre-made templates.
11. Mango AI — The Best for Presenter-Style Animations
Key Specifications
- Full-Song Performance (Not Clips): 3-5 minutes total video generation on free tier.
- Lip Sync While Dancing: Yes, but limited to stiff, presenter-style talking rather than dynamic dancing.
- Choreography Range: Presenter-style presets (gestures and pointing).
- Steps to a Finished Video: 4 steps (Select avatar → Input script → Set background → Export).
How It Works
Mango AI focuses heavily on corporate and educational content. It allows users to select a digital avatar, type a script, and generate a video where the avatar speaks the text with basic hand gestures. It is not designed to analyze music signals or output complex dance choreography, making it suitable only for talking-head presentations.
Pricing
- Pricing: Plans start at 7.90permonth(dropsto~3.92/month if billed annually). (retrieved source, accessed September 2026).
- Free tier: 180 credits per month.
- Watermark: Free-tier videos feature a prominent watermark. Starter plans and above remove it.
Bottom Line
Mango AI is designed for generating instructional and marketing videos featuring talking avatars, rather than rhythmic dance performances.
12. Lumigen — The Best for Script-to-Video UGC Avatars
Key Specifications
- Full-Song Performance (Not Clips): Clip-based.
- Lip Sync While Dancing: No.
- Choreography Range: Template-bound avatars.
- Steps to a Finished Video: 3 steps (Select avatar → Input script → Generate).
How It Works
Lumigen serves the performance marketing sector by turning text scripts into user-generated content (UGC) style videos. Like Mango AI, it puppeteers an avatar to deliver spoken lines. It lacks the engine infrastructure to interpret a music track’s BPM or energy curve, meaning it cannot generate a true dance video.
Pricing
- Pricing: —
- Free tier: —
- Watermark: —
Bottom Line
Lumigen is a specialized utility for creating spoken-word marketing ads quickly, completely bypassing the need for music-driven choreography.
Which should you choose
Selecting the right tool depends entirely on your starting material and your desired final output:
- If you have an audio track and want the AI to automatically build a full-length, beat-accurate performance from scratch, freebeat is the required engine.
- If you have an existing video of a dance and want to swap the person in the video with a different character, Viggle handles motion transfer effortlessly.
- If you need a highly realistic, cinematic 5-second establishing shot and plan to edit the footage manually to a beat later, Kling AI or Runway offer the highest visual fidelity.
- If you are building a 3D game and need to turn a 2D dance video into skeletal rig data, DeepMotion is the correct motion capture utility.
- If you simply want to animate a photo using a viral social media trend, CapCut offers the fastest template-driven workflow.
Frequently asked questions
What is the best ai dance video generator?
The best AI dance video generator depends on your workflow. If you want the AI to listen to a song and invent choreography that matches the real beat for the full length of the track, freebeat is the best overall choice. If you want to copy the exact movements from a pre-existing viral video and paste a new character onto it, Viggle is the best tool for that specific motion transfer task.
Does an AI dance generator actually match the beat of the music?
Most generic video generators do not; they simply output a visually appealing looping clip that you must manually align in an editor. However, dedicated music-first tools analyze the audio directly. For example, freebeat’s AI reads seven specific music signals—including a frame-accurate beat grid, percussive events, and the track’s energy curve—to ensure the generated choreography lands on the actual beat.
Can I use these tools for full commercial music videos?
Yes, but it depends on the platform’s terms and the tier you subscribe to. On platforms like freebeat, users own the copyright to the content they create and receive a full commercial-use license for it, provided they have the necessary rights to any uploaded music or photos. Always verify that your subscription tier includes watermark-free commercial exports, which are typically restricted on free tiers.
How much does a finished AI dance video typically cost?
Costs vary widely based on the pricing model. Clip-based generators often charge per second or per generation, meaning a 3-minute song stitched together from 5-second prompts can quickly become expensive. Subscription models like freebeat’s Pro plan ($26.99/mo) provide a monthly credit allowance specifically designed to accommodate full-song generations up to 6 minutes without unpredictable per-clip billing.
Do I need to know how to choreograph to use these generators?
No. Audio-driven platforms automatically plan the progression of the dance and the arrangement of the movements based on the song’s structure. You simply provide a free-text prompt specifying the style (like Hip-Hop or Jazz), and the AI handles the physical sequencing.
What is the difference between motion transfer and music-driven choreography?
Motion transfer tools require a reference video; the AI extracts the physical movement from that video and applies it to your photo. The movement comes from the video, not the music. Music-driven choreography tools do not require a reference video. The AI listens to the audio file you upload and invents original movement based on the rhythm, energy, and tempo of the track.

articles.title: Amazon dévoile 5 nouveaux appareils connectés Echo : voici tout ce qu’il faut savoir
articles.text:
Amazon vient de dévoiler sa nouvelle gamme d’appareils intelligents destinés à la maison. Nous comptons : l’Echo Dot de nouvelle génération, une enceinte équipée d’une caméra, un réveil intelligent, un cadre photo Alexa et surtout l’Echo Show 16. Voici tout ce qu’il faut savoir.
L’Echo Dot de nouvelle génération : une enceinte connectée qui intègre un répéteur Wi-Fi
L’Echo Dot de nouvelle génération est une enceinte connectée qui intègre un hub domotique, des fonctionnalités d’IA et un répéteur Wi-Fi eero. Amazon explique que l’appareil permet à Alexa « de se connecter à des milliers d’appareils compatibles (ampoules, serrures, thermostats, etc.) dès sa sortie de l’emballage ». Le répéteur Wi-Fi permettrait quant à lui d’étendre une couverture réseau existante jusqu’à 93 mètres carrés. Selon Amazon, le son émis par l’enceinte serait « exceptionnel », avec « des voix claires et des basses 50 % plus profondes que son prédécesseur ».
L’Echo Dot est proposé au prix de 104,99 €.
L’Echo Studio : une enceinte connectée équipée d’une caméra
La particularité de cette enceinte connectée est qu’elle intègre une caméra qui lui permet de visualiser en direct son environnement. Comme l’explique Amazon : « grâce à une meilleure perception de son environnement, Alexa peut vous aider en temps réel, par exemple en vous expliquant les règles d’un jeu de société, en reconnaissant une boîte de céréales pour vous aider à en recommander, ou en vous permettant de surveiller la pièce depuis l’application Alexa même en votre absence ». À noter que l’enceinte intègre un haut-parleur de graves à grande excursion et le Dolby Atmos.
L’Echo Studio doté d’une caméra est proposé au prix de 259,99 €.
L’Echo Time : un réveil intelligent
Ce réveil intelligent présente un écran, personnalisable, capable de s’illuminer progressivement à l’approche de votre alarme. L’objectif : simuler un lever de soleil. L’appareil intègre par ailleurs un capteur de sommeil qui vous réveille lorsque vous êtes dans une phase de sommeil léger. Amazon explique que cette « technologie de détection du sommeil, optimisée par Omnisense, détecte les phases de sommeil léger et vous réveille entre 10 et 60 minutes avant l’heure prévue, sans aucun appareil connecté ».
L’Echo Time est proposé au prix de 214,99 €.
Un cadre photo Alexa
Ce cadre photo intelligent se synchronise automatiquement avec Amazon Photos. Les dernières photos prises sont ainsi affichées sur l’écran tactile antireflet de 10 pouces, tandis que l’utilisateur peut demander à Alexa d’afficher une photo spécifique. Amazon explique d’ailleurs qu’ « Alexa sélectionne intelligemment les clichés à voir absolument – ceux où vous souriez, à la bonne saison – et masque les captures d’écran et les photos inutiles ».
Le cadre photo Alexa est proposé à partir de 199,99 $.
L’Echo Show 16
Enfin, le produit phare de cette nouvelle gamme d’appareils intelligents : l’Echo Show 16. L’appareil présente un écran de 16 pouces (soit 10 % de surface d’affichage supplémentaire par rapport à l’Echo Show 15), et serait 20 % plus puissant que son prédécesseur. Il présente par ailleurs des dimensions plus fines et une option de revêtement Nanomat antireflet. Notons également que l’Echo Show 16 intègre l’intégralité de l’expérience Fire TV, ainsi que « la meilleure caméra jamais conçue pour un Echo Show, avec un champ de vision ultra-large, un cadrage automatique qui garde tout le monde dans le cadre et, pour la première fois, la vision nocturne ».
L’Echo Show 16 est proposé aux États-Unis au prix de 499,99 $ ou de 569,99 $ avec l’écran Nanomatte. Nous ne connaissons pas encore les prix pour la France, ni la date de commercialisation de l’appareil sur notre territoire.

articles.title: Cisco SD-WAN Zero-Day Exploitation Tied to Volt Typhoon’s ‘Silent Train’ Network
articles.text:
A threat actor whose infrastructure overlaps with a covert network used by China’s Volt Typhoon exploited a critical Cisco SD-WAN vulnerability to deploy malware designed to harvest encryption keys, Cisco Talos reported on Wednesday.
The same day, Lumen’s Black Lotus Labs published research on that network, Silent Train, which Volt Typhoon used to target US organizations, including in a zero-day campaign exploiting the same Cisco flaw.
The vulnerability, CVE-2026-20127, has a CVSS score of 10 and was disclosed in February 2026. Without needing credentials, attackers can exploit it remotely to get past the peering authentication of SD-WAN controller components and obtain admin rights. Cisco warns that this access can be leveraged to alter the SD-WAN network’s configuration.
Attackers planted KeyDrift malware on SD-WAN controllers
Talos attributes the attacks to UAT-11473, which it describes as a highly sophisticated APT targeting space and satellite services, defense and aerospace technology, and policy research. Talos calls the activity historical but has not said when the attacks occurred.
According to Talos, the malware framework, named KeyDrift, was designed to give its operators persistent access to the SD-WAN controllers and to automatically siphon off keying material. It is injected into legitimate control-plane processes, giving it access to control traffic after it has been decrypted.
Its main module, PolyFlame, works as a backdoor and can also relay commands to other hosts as an intermediate command-and-control (C2) node. A second module, LittleFilch, collects keying material that Talos believes includes keys protecting data-plane traffic.
Talos assessed with high confidence that UAT-11473’s infrastructure “overlaps considerably with Volt Typhoon’s ‘Silent Train’ covert access network.” It does not say the two are the same group.
Volt Typhoon used Silent Train in several zero-day campaigns
Black Lotus Labs has monitored Silent Train since late 2023. The network routes the attackers’ traffic through chains of hacked small office routers, IoT devices and enterprise systems that are frequently replaced, and the operators clean up after each session.
Lumen’s monitoring led to hundreds of victim notifications. It also helped uncover at least four confirmed zero-day campaigns targeting Versa Director, N-able N-central, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, and VeloCloud Orchestrator, plus a likely zero-day campaign against Quest KACE.
According to Lumen, Volt Typhoon was exploiting CVE-2026-20127 by late 2025 and kept doing so long after Cisco’s disclosure. The group focuses on management platforms and other control-plane systems that offer broad access across an organization.
“Every zero-day campaign through Silent Train targeted this kind of platform,” Lumen noted.
Victims include telecoms firms, government entities, defense contractors, satellite and mission-critical communications providers, MSPs, universities with military ties, and critical infrastructure operators. Hawaii, California and Texas were targeted the most.
Lumen says the victimology points to an attempt to secure footholds in systems that would matter most during a geopolitical crisis, particularly one involving the Indo-Pacific region. However, Black Lotus Labs researcher Mike Horka told journalist Kim Zetter that the hackers have also exfiltrated documents on military operations and network structures, and he believes the activity combines pre-positioning and espionage.
Lumen’s report does not mention KeyDrift or UAT-11473.

articles.title: Bengaluru-based Inkle acquires Finally’s bookkeeping arm, expands team to 160
articles.text:
Bengaluru-based Inkle acquires Finally’s bookkeeping arm, expands team to 160
Bengaluru-built, San Francisco-headquartered CPA firm Inkle has acquired Finally's bookkeeping division in an undisclosed all-cash deal, taking its team to about 160 people across five countries and extending it from startups to non-tech small businesses.
San Francisco-headquartered Inkle, an AI-driven accounting and bookkeeping firm for US companies that develops its technology in Bengaluru, has purchased the bookkeeping arm of small-business finance platform Finally. The price has not been revealed. Inkle describes the deal as an all-cash asset purchase and says it is the company’s first acquisition.
Around 100 Finally employees based in the Dominican Republic, Colombia, Puerto Rico, Miami, Boca Raton and New York will join Inkle’s 60-member team in Bengaluru, comprising engineers, product designers, tax professionals and bookkeepers. With a workforce of about 160 across five countries, Inkle says it can provide round-the-clock support to clients across the Americas and Asia. Finally’s existing bookkeeping customers will continue working with their current teams, while accessing services through Inkle’s software.
The acquisition also changes who Inkle works for. Until now, the firm’s clients have been mainly venture-backed startups. Finally’s customers are largely non-tech small businesses, including contractors, clinics, restaurants, professional services firms and owner-operators, a group Inkle regards as the core of America’s employer base.
“Ranvir and I are delighted to announce Inkle’s first acquisition,” said Anand Krishna, co-founder and CEO of Inkle. “Inkle is an American company that serves American small businesses, and it’s built in Bengaluru. That combination is our edge: U.S. CPAs who own the outcome, and an engineering team in India building the software and AI that let them serve far more businesses, far better, than a traditional firm. We’re building the AI-powered Big Four, and this acquisition helps us take that to the businesses that make up most of the American economy.”
Inkle cites a shortage of accounting professionals in the US as a factor behind the deal, with many CPAs and bookkeepers nearing retirement and fewer new entrants joining the profession. The AICPA’s 2025 Trends Report recorded 55,152 accounting degrees awarded in 2023-24, down 6.6% from the previous year. Inkle expects technology-led platforms to play a role in addressing the talent gap, with Indian engineers and finance professionals contributing to their development.
The company was set up in 2022 by Krishna, who runs it from San Francisco, and Ranvir Singh, who oversees technology from Bengaluru. It combines a US-licensed CPA practice with product, engineering and AI development carried out in India. The Bengaluru team built both Inkle Books, the firm’s general ledger, and its tax and compliance platform. Because developers work next to the accountants who use their tools, Inkle says problems flagged by the delivery side are frequently resolved within a day. It sees moving Finally’s team onto this platform as the most demanding test of that approach so far.
Inkle is also a frequent first stop for Indian founders looking to expand internationally. Each year it helps hundreds of businesses incorporate in the US, many of them Delaware C-Corps formed to raise investment and win American customers. It then looks after their continuing obligations, from federal tax returns and Delaware franchise tax to cross-border filings such as Form 5472 and FBAR. It is also the cross-border compliance partner for Stripe Atlas for Indian founders.
On funding, Inkle says it has become profitable after raising only $1.5 million in pre-seed capital from Picus Capital, Saison Capital and Force Ventures. That is well below what competing firms have raised, and several of those better-funded rivals have since exited the market. Inkle’s software costs nothing to use, and the company charges only for its AI-assisted bookkeeping, tax and compliance services. These can be delivered on Inkle Books, QuickBooks, Xero, Zoho Books or Mercury Books.

articles.title: New Cisco firewall zero-day exploited to crash SSL VPN devices
articles.text:
Cisco released security updates to patch a denial-of-service zero-day in Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) and Threat Defense (FTD) software that attackers are exploiting to remotely crash vulnerable firewall devices.
Tracked as CVE-2026-76418, this high-severity vulnerability affects devices running ASA and FTD software with configurations containing the 'webvpn' keyword and SSL VPN enabled on at least one interface.
Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated, remote attackers to trigger a denial-of-service (DoS) condition, causing the device to reload unexpectedly.
Cisco advised customers to patch vulnerable firewalls after its Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) discovered evidence that the flaw was being exploited in the wild earlier this month. However, the company didn't provide indicators of compromise and hasn't shared additional information about the attacks, including which organizations are being targeted or who is exploiting the flaw.
"This vulnerability is due to logic errors when secondary authentication is configured on a tunnel group. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted request when connecting to the SSL remote access VPN. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the affected device to reload, resulting in a DoS condition," Cisco said.
"In October 2026, the Cisco PSIRT became aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability. Cisco strongly recommends that customers upgrade to a fixed software release to remediate this vulnerability."
While Cisco provided no workarounds that address this security issue, admins who can't immediately patch CVE-2026-76418 can mitigate it by disabling secondary authentication on the default DefaultWEBVPNGroup tunnel group or on any user-configured tunnel group list.
Currently, Internet monitoring platform Shadowserver tracks more than 51,000 Cisco ASA SSL VPN devices exposed online, but doesn't provide information on how many have already been secured or are honeypots.
Last year, Cisco patched two other flaws (CVE-2025-20362 and CVE-2025-20333) affecting ASA and FTD firewall devices in September and cautioned customers that attackers had exploited them in zero-day attacks targeting 5500-X Series devices with VPN web services enabled.
The same day, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) issued Emergency Directive 25-03, ordering federal agencies to secure their Cisco firewall devices within 24 hours.
Cisco linked the attacks to the ArcaneDoor campaign, which had also been exploiting two other zero-days (CVE-2024-20353 and CVE-2024-20359) to breach government networks since November 2023.
More recently, in August, Cisco addressed another denial-of-service zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-20349) that attackers were actively exploiting in the wild to crash affected ASA and FTD firewall devices with SSL listen sockets enabled.
Earlier this month, it also warned customers to patch an actively exploited zero-day (CVE-2026-76519) in its Secure Email Gateway (SEG) security solution that lets unauthenticated attackers execute commands remotely with root privileges.
Since November 2021, CISA has flagged 101 Cisco security flaws as exploited in the wild, seven of which were also abused by ransomware gangs.

articles.title: Une illustration de Donkey Kong de 1981 destinée à la poubelle s'est vendue 329 400 dollars aux enchères
articles.text:
Si vous fouillez dans votre poubelle, là, tout de suite, maintenant, vous devriez trouver quelques déchets peu séduisants, qui ne serviront pas à grand-chose. C’est le principe d’une poubelle, cela dit.
Donna Darbous, une ancienne responsable de la publicité chez Nintendo of America, n’a pas les mêmes poubelles que vous et moi. À la fin des années 1980, alors que la filiale américaine de Nintendo réorganisait ses locaux pour gagner de la place, plusieurs documents et illustrations devaient finir à la benne.
Dans la pile d’objets à jeter, Donna Darbous a repéré des enveloppes contenant des dessins originaux et les a récupérées avec l’autorisation de son supérieur, comme elle l’a raconté au New York Times le 8 octobre 2026. Ces documents sont ensuite restés oubliés pendant plusieurs décennies, jusqu’à ce qu’elle les retrouve en rangeant son garage. Parmi eux figurait une illustration originale de Donkey Kong, le jeu d’arcade de Nintendo sorti en 1981.
Elle a été vendue aux enchères ce mercredi 28 octobre, comme le relaye IGN, pour 329 400 dollars (environ 294 000 euros), plus du double de l’estimation, qui allait de 100 000 à 150 000 dollars (environ 89 000 à 134 000 euros).
L’illustration était proposée par la maison Landry Pop Auctions lors de la vente Jumpman : The Beginning of an Icon. D’après la maison d’enchères, ce prix établit un record pour une œuvre d’art originale liée au jeu vidéo vendue aux enchères. Le précédent record appartenait à la peinture originale de Robert Florczak pour une illustration de Prince of Persia, vendue 63 000 dollars (environ 56 000 euros) par Heritage Auctions en janvier 2023.
Une illustration originale liée à l’histoire de Nintendo
Réalisée par l’illustrateur Leslie Cabarga pour le prospectus destiné à vendre la borne Donkey Kong aux exploitants de salles d’arcade nord-américains, cette illustration représente le célèbre primate brandissant un tonneau, tandis que Mario, alors appelé Jumpman, escalade un bâtiment pour sauver Pauline. Landry Pop Auctions la présente comme la première apparition publique de Mario, ce qui explique en bonne partie son prix.
Le dessin a ensuite servi de base aux affiches distribuées aux États-Unis. Comme le rappelle GameSpot ce 28 octobre, il a été repris pendant des décennies sur des produits dérivés de Donkey Kong et a fixé l’apparence de Mario et du gorille dans leurs premières adaptations, notamment dans le dessin animé Saturday Supercade diffusé au début des années 1980.
Cette illustration faisait partie d’une vente de 49 lots issus de la collection de Donna Darbous, tous liés à l’histoire de Nintendo. Parmi les autres pièces figuraient une illustration originale de Mario et Luigi pour Super Mario Bros., vendue 17 080 dollars (environ 15 200 euros), près de trois fois son estimation, et un dessin de Goomba adjugé 10 370 dollars (environ 9 250 euros), plus du double de l’estimation.
L’illustration de Donkey Kong cumulait trois atouts aux yeux des collectionneurs qui peut expliquer son prix de vente astronomique : son ancienneté, son rôle dans la naissance de Mario et son parcours, puisqu’elle a échappé de peu à la benne. On ne sait pas qui a déboursé cette somme, ni si l’œuvre sera exposée au public ou restera dans le salon d’un collectionneur. Toujours est-il que la vente confirme le poids culturel de Mario, 45 ans après ses débuts sur une borne d’arcade.

articles.title: Pokémon Unite : c'est (bientôt) fini pour ce jeu Pokémon, qui fermera ses portes dans quelques mois
articles.text:
Trente ans plus tard, la « folie Pokémon » continue de battre son plein, mais tous les jeux de la franchise ne connaissent pas le même succès. Pokémon Unite s’apprête à tirer sa révérence en 2027, après plusieurs années de combats en équipe sur mobile et Nintendo Switch.
La licence Pokémon a beau fêter ses 30 ans en 2026, elle n’a clairement pas l’intention de ralentir. Entre les cartes à collectionner qui s’arrachent et les fans prêts à patienter des heures pour obtenir leur précieux sésame, l’engouement reste intact. Pourtant, du côté de Pokémon Unite, le compte à rebours est bel et bien lancé.
Pokémon Unite prépare son dernier combat
Lancé en 2021, Pokémon Unite proposait une formule différente des jeux Pokémon traditionnels, avec un MOBA (pour Multiplayer Online Battle Arena) dans lequel deux équipes de cinq joueurs s’affrontent pour marquer un maximum de points, en incarnant leurs créatures favorites. Accessible sur Nintendo Switch et sur smartphones, le titre entendait séduire aussi bien les amateurs de Pokémon que les adeptes de combats compétitifs.
Mais l’aventure a désormais une date de fin. Comme le rapporte notamment Kotaku, les serveurs du jeu fermeront leurs portes le 23 mars 2027. Une échéance qui laisse encore un peu de temps aux joueurs pour profiter de leurs dernières parties, mais qui marque la fin programmée de ce spin-off qui dépassait les 70 millions de téléchargements un peu avant son premier anniversaire, en avril 2022.
Comme souvent dans ce genre de cas, la fermeture ne se fera pas du jour au lendemain. Les achats de gemmes Aeos (la monnaie virtuelle du jeu) ont déjà été arrêtés dans certaines régions, tandis que les joueurs peuvent continuer à accéder au titre pendant la période qui précède sa disparition.
La folie Pokémon, elle, ne connaît pas la crise
La disparition de Pokémon Unite ne signifie évidemment pas que les monstres de poche ont perdu leur pouvoir d’attraction… Bien au contraire ! La licence continue de faire parler d’elle, et souvent bien au-delà des consoles et des smartphones.
La preuve avec ce phénomène pour le moins insolite, puisqu’à l’occasion des 30 ans de Pokémon, un service propose… de louer une personne chargée de faire la queue à votre place ! Une initiative révélatrice de l’engouement suscité par certains événements et produits dérivés, comme nous l’évoquions récemment dans Clubic.
Entre les jeux principaux, les cartes à collectionner et les innombrables produits dérivés, Pokémon dispose d’un univers suffisamment vaste pour continuer à mobiliser ses fans.
Pour ce qui est de Pokémon Unite, il rejoindra bientôt la liste des expériences vidéoludiques de la franchise qui n’auront pas survécu à l’épreuve du temps.

articles.title: “Urgency is an inherently subjective call”: Anthropic tells TNS how it grades Claude Duet
articles.text:
“Urgency is an inherently subjective call”: Anthropic tells TNS how it grades Claude Duet
Anthropic built Claude Duet, an AI assistant that monitors your connected apps and works on tasks in the background, to decide what needs your attention without being asked. A week after its October 21 debut, the frontier lab with an IPO in its sights has shared with The New Stack how it is testing whether Duet gets those priorities right.
Anthropic has developed internal graders to assess how Duet prioritizes tasks, though urgency can be subjective. The stakes rise when an agent manages work across email, calendars, and B2B apps. Duet can remain within its permissions and still get its priorities wrong.
Powered by Claude Opus 5.5, Duet can prepare work and flag items it thinks need attention without waiting for instructions. Anthropic has been testing that approach with its own employees, using their day-to-day work to see how Duet handles competing priorities.
Testing Duet’s judgment
“After using Duet for our day-to-day work at Anthropic, we calibrated graders that assess correctness in task prioritization, and we run them offline against cases representative of internal use and early external testing,” a company representative tells The New Stack.
Those graders measure whether Duet can distinguish what deserves attention from what can wait, though Anthropic acknowledges the difficulty of evaluating those decisions.
“Urgency is an inherently subjective call, so we found building an eval for it imperfect but quite helpful,” a company representative says.
Duet can spot tasks like an approaching deadline or an email requiring a reply, but it doesn’t always know which task should be a priority, and the company admits the agent can misread conversations or misjudge urgency. Anthropic’s public launch and support materials do not say how often that happens.
Testing Duet’s safeguards
On October 23, two days after Duet’s debut, Anthropic published a closer look at its safety, privacy, and security safeguards. Duet team lead Karan Ahuja pointed to the post while addressing feedback received through messages, emails, and public posts.
Anthropic keeps the part of Duet that does the work separate from the part that checks whether the work matches what the user actually asked for.
“A separate, automated check runs alongside each action, built on the auto mode classifier from Claude Code and extended for Claude Duet,” the rep tells The New Stack. “It assesses whether the action matches your intent.”
Because that check runs independently of the model performing the task, Anthropic says instructions hidden in a webpage can’t directly steer the classifier’s decision.
Anthropic says an outside firm penetration-tested Duet, but its public materials don’t show how reliably the separate check catches actions outside the user’s intent. Related research illustrates the difficulty of enforcing this agent scope: Researchers found that removing a prompt section defining authorized and out-of-scope actions in Claude Code tests increased out-of-scope actions, although that study did not test Duet’s separate classifier.
Limiting prompt injection
The separation is designed to reduce prompt injection, where malicious instructions embedded in emails, documents, or webpages try to redirect an agent. Researchers have already explored this risk by leaving hidden messages for rogue agents and observing how they responded. Anthropic’s support materials still tell users to review drafts and approval requests because Duet may encounter prompt injection.
Duet uses the apps already connected to a user’s Claude account. Disconnecting an app stops new access, but information Duet has already stored in memory remains until the user resets it. Anthropic says Duet never sees passwords, browser cookies, or sign-in tokens, and can’t save them to memory.
Duet is designed to seek approval before actions such as making payments or deleting items. Sharing private health or financial information requires consent, though an explicit request to share it can count as that consent, while trading securities, moving money between bank accounts, and accessing someone else’s account remain off-limits entirely.
Summaries, not surveillance
Users can see what Duet has finished and what’s still underway through its task list, with a separate page for each job. They can also give the agent new instructions while it’s working.
But users can’t see everything happening behind the scenes. During the research preview, users can’t watch Duet work in its cloud browser or take over the browser. Users can review its task activity and approve actions, but they can’t inspect each browser step as it happens. (The public launch and support materials do not describe a way to undo completed actions across connected apps.)
What background work costs
Duet uses the same allowance as regular Claude conversations, so background work counts against a subscriber’s plan limits. How much it uses depends on the job.
“Larger tasks, like building a financial model or a deck, will require more model turns and background work,” the Anthropic rep tells The New Stack.
Even Duet’s routine checks across connected apps count toward the five-hour session and weekly limits.
Those checks happen every few hours rather than continuously, partly to avoid using up a subscriber’s allowance. The downside is that something urgent could arrive between checks and go unnoticed until the next one. Checking more often would use more resources, while checking less often could leave users waiting longer for an alert. (Anthropic’s public launch and support materials do not quantify how much of a typical subscriber’s usage goes toward background activity.)
Duet’s research preview is available by waitlist to U.S. Pro and Max subscribers. Anthropic employees have used it to work through to-do lists while they’re away and talk through workloads on walks, though Anthropic admits the agent isn’t as reliable with consumer tasks like booking tickets.
The company expects to keep adjusting the product as testing continues.

articles.title: Cómo eliminar un virus troyano que se haya instalado en el computador
articles.text:
Un computador que empieza a fallar sin motivo aparente, con ventanas que se abren solas o un tráfico de internet que se dispara, puede estar albergando un troyano. Este tipo de malware se cuela disfrazado de programa inofensivo y, una vez dentro, puede operar sin que el usuario lo note.
Un troyano es un software malicioso que se presenta como un programa legítimo para infiltrarse en un sistema. Permite robar credenciales, cookies, archivos y datos bancarios, e incluso secuestrar el equipo para ataques de denegación de servicio (DDoS), sin que la víctima perciba su presencia.
Cómo llega un virus troyano al computador
Los troyanos no se instalan solos, necesitan que el usuario los ejecute sin saberlo. Los sitios web de archivos compartidos, entre ellos los de torrents, son una fuente habitual, ya que un atacante puede subir un software pirateado con el virus oculto dentro.
Los archivos adjuntos de correo electrónico también son una puerta de entrada frecuente. Pueden llegar en mensajes genéricos o dirigidos a un grupo específico de personas, con un documento que simula ser inofensivo.
A esto se suman los mensajes falsos en aplicaciones de chat, con nombres de usuario casi idénticos a contactos reales, los sitios web infectados que redirigen las descargas a servidores maliciosos, y las redes WiFi pirateadas, que imitan una red legítima para enviar al usuario a páginas falsas.
Cómo detectarlo un virus troyano
Entre los indicios de que un troyano está activo figuran la reducción del rendimiento del sistema, el aumento inusual del tráfico de internet, aplicaciones que se abren sin intervención o movimientos extraños del puntero del mouse.
El administrador de tareas de Windows sirve como primer filtro, aunque no siempre muestra todos los procesos en ejecución. Por eso conviene recurrir a un antivirus con examen completo.
Windows 11 incluye una herramienta propia, Seguridad de Windows, que permite correr un “Examen completo” desde la sección Protección contra virus y amenazas. Se recomienda combinarla con un examen offline de Microsoft Defender, que se ejecuta durante el arranque y tarda unos 15 minutos, lo que permite detectar amenazas que de otro modo quedarían fuera del alcance del sistema ya iniciado.
Pasos para eliminar el troyano
Antes de cualquier acción, el primer paso es desconectar el equipo de internet, para evitar que el virus siga enviando datos a un servidor externo.
Con la conexión cortada, se procede a ejecutar el antivirus o la herramienta antimalware, que en la mayoría de los casos elimina la amenaza de forma automática.
Si esto no funciona, la opción siguiente es iniciar Windows 11 en modo seguro, una versión reducida del sistema donde solo se cargan los servicios esenciales y el troyano queda desactivado, lo que facilita detectarlo y borrarlo con el programa antimalware.
Cuando ni siquiera el modo seguro resuelve el problema, corresponde restaurar el sistema a un punto anterior a la infección, mediante la función “SystemPropertiesProtection” accesible con la combinación Windows + R. Como último recurso, si el troyano persiste, la reinstalación completa del sistema operativo elimina todos los datos del equipo, incluido el malware, aunque exige hacer antes una copia de seguridad en un disco externo.
Cuando el antivirus tradicional no alcanza
Existen troyanos más avanzados, capaces de aprender a ocultarse y de evadir tanto el antivirus de Windows como soluciones de terceros, incluido el análisis sin conexión de Defender. Suelen ejecutarse sobre herramientas propias del sistema, como PowerShell, y abrir ventanas de terminal por períodos muy breves.
Ante este escenario, el procedimiento cambia. El primer paso es desconectar físicamente el Wi-Fi, el cable de red y el propio router, ya que el modo avión no siempre corta por completo la actividad del malware.
Luego se revisa la Biblioteca del programador de tareas, accesible con Windows + R y el comando “taskschd.msc”, en busca de tareas con nombres genéricos o cadenas aleatorias que redirijan a PowerShell, “cmd.exe” o comandos como “iex” e “iwr”.
También conviene revisar la carpeta de inicio automático, mediante “shell:startup”, y eliminar accesos directos o scripts con extensiones “.bat”, “.vbs” o “.ps1”, además de vaciar el contenido de la carpeta temporal del sistema (“%temp%”).
Completados estos pasos, se recomienda volver a ejecutar el examen offline de Microsoft Defender junto con herramientas adicionales como Malwarebytes o HitmanPro, que no requieren instalación, para confirmar que no quedó ningún residuo del virus.

articles.title: Una aceitera de Jaén coloca más de 5.150 placas solares a más de cuatro metros de altura sobre un olivar en producción para que la cosechadora pueda seguir pasando por debajo
articles.text:
Acesur, el grupo aceitero de Sevilla, propietario de las marcas Coosur, La Española y Guillén, ha puesto en marcha las obras de construcción de una planta solar en Vilches (Jaén), que se alzará sobre un olivar en producción. Serán más de 5.150 paneles elevados a más de cuatro metros, que suman 3,65 MWp (la potencia máxima en condiciones de pleno rendimiento) y se sitúan junto a la envasadora de la empresa, “respetando el 100 % de los árboles existentes”, según su comunicado.
Al estar elevados, según Acesur se puede mantener la labor agrícola habitual (incluso la recogida de la cosecha), aunque su instalación requiere una mayor complejidad estructural.
El sistema cuenta con un almacenamiento de 3 MWh diseñado para “optimizar el autoconsumo y mejorar la gestión de la energía generada”, según la empresa, y Greening, una empresa granadina de renovables, es la encargada de llevar a cabo la ejecución, con el apoyo de 2,8 millones de euros del Instituto para la Diversificación y Ahorro de la Energía (IDAE).
La Universidad de Jaén está colaborando en el proyecto a través de Pedro Pérez, catedrático de Tecnología Electrónica y asesor del proyecto, que aparece en el vídeo que Acesur y Greening han publicado con imágenes del prototipo de Navas de San Juan, a modo de referencia para el proyecto.
Se plantea la cuestión de si la sombra parcial supone una pérdida de cultivo de aceituna, o de si puede generar una cierta protección del olivo en periodos de estrés, pero la nota de prensa de Acesur no incluye los datos de producción del proyecto piloto.
“Para ACESUR, innovar tiene sentido cuando se hace desde el origen”, destaca Nicolás Tejada, director de Medio Ambiente de Acesur, que explica que el proyecto permite avanzar en autoconsumo renovable y “proteger el olivar del que nacen nuestros aceites”.
Juan José Pérez, responsable de I+D de Greening, señala que el proyecto demuestra “que la innovación energética puede integrarse en el territorio de forma respetuosa y eficiente”.
Qué dice el estudio de la Universidad de Jaén
Las sombras son un punto de comparación con otra investigación, de la Universidad de Jaén, que en 2023 publicó en Applied Energy un estudio titulado “Potential of agrivoltaics systems into olive groves in the Mediterranean region”, en el que se concluía que, en tal caso, los módulos deberían tener entre un 57 % y un 71 % de transparencia para no frenar el crecimiento del árbol; se trata, al parecer, de una característica específica de los olivares superintensivos, mientras que Acesur indica en su nota de prensa que el olivar de Vilches es tradicional.
Tal y como subraya la misma investigación, el modelo sugiere que un 1 % de la superficie de los olivares mediterráneos con este tipo de instalaciones podría suponer un aumento del 2,5 % de la capacidad fotovoltaica global y reducir unos cuatro millones de toneladas de CO₂ al año; sin embargo, se trata de una estimación basada en el modelo de los autores, que se refiere a otro tipo de olivar.
Cuánto producirá la planta
Tampoco figuran en la nota de prensa los MWh que generará la instalación al año (ni su cubrimiento de la demanda eléctrica, ni su coste, aparte de los 2,8 millones del IDAE, sin que se diga qué parte de la inversión total son). Las previsiones que han circulado hablan de más de 5.000 MWh al año, una cifra que tampoco especifica la nota de prensa.
Un cálculo en la herramienta de evaluación del potencial fotovoltaico (PVGIS), de la Comisión Europea y de acceso gratuito, sugiere unos 5.900 MWh al año para un sistema de 3,65 MWp, con las coordenadas de Vilches, paneles de silicio cristalino, orientación sur, inclinación de 30 grados y un factor de pérdida del 14 %, características de una planta convencional que pueden no ajustarse a las del sistema real.
Si la planta de Vilches se acercara a esa estimación, produciría más electricidad anual que las cuatro instalaciones que ya ha puesto en marcha la empresa; dichas instalaciones se encuentran en cuatro de las fábricas de la empresa, dos de ellas en la provincia de Jaén (Vilches y Jabalquinto) y otras dos en Sevilla (Dos Hermanas y La Roda de Andalucía), con una superficie de 30 000 metros cuadrados capaz de generar 3.654,70 MWh al año y proporcionar un 18 % estimado de autosuficiencia energética.
Cualquiera que haya buscado información sobre si merece la pena instalar placas solares en su tejado tarde o temprano se encuentra con el asunto de las sombras (y de si hay otras cosas que puedan generar electricidad en su lugar). Nosotros ya publicamos un artículo sobre ShadowCalculator, un sitio web gratuito que simula la sombra que proyecta un edificio sobre una zona de interés (y la versión original del artículo es de 2022). La diferencia radica en que, en este caso, no se trata de cuánta electricidad se pierde a causa de la sombra, sino de cuántas aceitunas se pierden; una cifra que no se cita en la nota de prensa.

articles.title: Le casse-tête des « dark GPU » : pourquoi Amazon empile des milliards de dollars en puces IA inutilisées — Frandroid
articles.text:
Business Insider a consulté en octobre des courriels internes d’Amazon Web Services (AWS), la branche d’Amazon qui loue de la puissance de calcul aux entreprises. On y apprend qu’AWS comptait recevoir environ 5 milliards de dollars d’armoires de serveurs Nvidia GB300 rien qu’en août, puis à peu près 3 milliards de plus chaque mois. Or une partie de ce matériel reste éteinte. Certains centres de données d’AWS aux États-Unis n’ont pas assez d’électricité pour l’installer, et les serveurs attendent la fin des travaux dans des entrepôts « intermédiaires ».
Les GB300 sont des armoires complètes vendues par Nvidia, remplies de GPU, ces processeurs graphiques qui font tourner les modèles d’intelligence artificielle. Avant la vague de l’IA, AWS ne devenait propriétaire d’une armoire qu’une fois celle-ci terminée et livrée dans un centre de données.
Désormais, l’entreprise fondée par Jeff Bezos paie des milliards d’avance pour réserver le matériel plus tôt. Et dans ces e-mails, une équipe d’Amazon se plaint de n’avoir aucune prévision claire sur la date où tous ces GPU seront vraiment installés dans leurs serveurs
Le phénomène des dark GPUs
Amazon n’est pas un cas isolé. Le site américain TechSpot, qui a détaillé l’affaire le 24 octobre, la range dans un phénomène appelé les « dark GPUs », ces GPU éteints faute d’alimentation. Les géants du cloud achètent tout le matériel qu’ils peuvent et en laissent une bonne partie prendre la poussière sur des étagères, pendant que le reste de l’industrie doit se contenter des restes. Pourtant, rejeter la faute sur le réseau électrique ou sur les permis de construire, c’est un peu facile. Même si le courant arrivait demain, un centre de données demande toujours du béton, de l’acier, du câble en cuivre, des électriciens et des techniciens pour assembler les serveurs.
Amazon ne pouvait pas l’ignorer au moment de commander. Un bâtiment de ce genre prend souvent plusieurs années à sortir de terre, et les blocages rencontrés depuis n’ont fait que le confirmer. Le groupe continue malgré tout d’acheter pour environ 3 milliards de dollars d’armoires Nvidia par mois, soit autour de 36 milliards de dollars sur un an.
Amazon parle de « meilleure pratique »
Chez Amazon, on ne voit pas où est le problème. Un porte-parole du groupe qualifie le stockage d’armoires finies en entrepôt de « meilleure pratique commerciale ». Andy Jassy, CEO d’Amazon, rappelle qu’AWS a déjà connu une situation comparable. Surtout, l’entreprise compte sur de gros retours financiers à terme, persuadée que l’IA est une occasion unique qu’aucun acteur de la tech ne peut se permettre de rater.
En attendant, la facture se voit déjà dans les comptes. Le flux de trésorerie disponible d’Amazon, c’est-à-dire l’argent qui reste une fois les investissements payés, est passé dans le rouge au deuxième trimestre sur douze mois glissants, une première depuis 2023. Le groupe prévoit environ 220 milliards de dollars de dépenses d’investissement cette année et s’attend à ce que ce flux reste négatif encore un moment.

articles.title: Han subastado objetos del Pazo de Meirás y, para sorpresa de nadie, los nostálgicos de Franco se han vuelto locos
articles.text:
Los herederos de Franco han empezado a vender los objetos que sacaron del Pazo de Meirás en una subasta de Magna Art Auctions, en Madrid. No hablamos de la querida biblioteca Salvat. La puja de esta feria de las vanidades, "espectáculo inmoral" que no inmortal, de 689 lotes con precios de salida de entre 20 y 5.000 euros, ha superado las expectativas y el valor inicial en todos y cada uno de los lotes vendidos.
La primera sesión, el martes 27, duró de las cinco de la tarde a las 23:30. Se adjudicaron 250 lotes por 247.500 euros, sin descontar la comisión de la casa. Al cierre de la segunda, la recaudación superaba los 460.000 y aún quedaban piezas por salir. Los recuerdos del militar y dictador español, desde el golpe de Estado de 1936 contra el Gobierno democrático de la Segunda República hasta su muerte en 1975, cotizan bien alto. Los fans de hurgar en el cubo de basura de la historia están de enhorabuena.
Qué se ha vendido y a cuánto. Casi todo lo que ha llamado la atención tenía a Franco en el catálogo o en la dedicatoria:
- Foto familiar coloreada de Franco, Carmen Polo y su hija: de 80 a 2.250 euros. Era el lote 228.
- Óleo del pazo dedicado a Carmen Franco por la condesa de Morata de Jalón: de 50 a 6.000, 120 veces su precio de salida.
- Tapiz con el escudo franquista: de 850 a 9.000 euros según elDiario.es y a 9.500 según El País. Se lo disputaron un comprador telefónico y otro desde fuera de España.
- Maletín de Franco, grabado con su título de caudillo y jefe de Falange: de 350 a 19.000 euros. Era el lote 465.
- Caja joyero de plata “Carmencita”: de 120 a 14.000.
- Jarra de Talavera: de 350 a 10.000.
- Dos “niños mártires” de madera: de 120 a 5.000.
- Placa del Cabildo Compostelano de 1937: de 180 a 1.900. La dedicó a Franco en plena Guerra Civil.
El pajarraco y otras rarezas. La subasta también ha tenido su parte absurda. Un ave de metal plateado de 20 centímetros pasó de 90 a 275 euros tras una puja reñida, y entre aves de rapiña los asistentes bromeaban con que "el pajarraco" se había resistido. Una cerámica india del siglo XVIII se fue por 550. Un asistente la tasaba en 3.000 como mínimo, y concluía que allí se compraba memorabilia, no antigüedades. En el catálogo había además una foto de la concentración de la Plaza de Oriente de 1975, tras los últimos fusilamientos del régimen, con 500 euros de salida.
Los precios ya venían inflados. Antes de la subasta, las ofertas anticipadas por internet ya habían disparado varios lotes. Según elDiario.es, la propia casa asumía que los precios finales serían muy superiores. El día de la puja, un empleado explicó que había diez veces más gente conectada de lo habitual. Hubo unas veinte líneas telefónicas, compradores desde plataformas internacionales y problemas en el servidor.
Quién pujaba. El perfil era variado. El personal de Magna admitió a elDiario.es que había franquistas declarados, y también coleccionistas e interesados en la historia de España. A la puerta, algunos asistentes evitaban a la prensa y otros se declaraban admiradores del dictador. Una mujer dijo que iba a por un recuerdo que todos los españoles deberían tener; otra, que buscaba cosas de pazo sin relación con Franco. En su crónica, El País describe un público de alta edad y a varios asistentes quejándose de que se tratase a la familia como si hubiera robado. Ah.
Qué dice la casa de subastas. El director, José Miguel Carrillo de Albornoz, defendió que es una puja normal, como cualquier otra. Antes de la subasta, aseguró que lo importante se había quedado en el pazo. El catálogo, sin mencionar la Guerra Civil ni el golpe criminal, defendía que el “marcado carácter histórico” de las piezas les da un valor superior al intrínseco. Una de las organizaciones memorialistas replica que la frase del catálogo según la cual el pazo “ha pertenecido” a los Franco durante décadas es falsa, algo que a su juicio ha quedado demostrado documental y judicialmente.
Cómo hemos llegado hasta aquí. Para intentar esclarecerlo un poco, aquí va un brevísimo resumen de hechos, para tener contexto:
- 1938: Franco recibe el pazo mediante una suscripción popular, como jefe del Estado.
- Septiembre de 2020: una sentencia obliga a los Franco a devolverlo al Estado.
- Septiembre de 2022: la Abogacía del Estado reclama 564 bienes que seguían dentro. Un juzgado acabó adjudicando unos 600 al Estado, y el resto quedó en manos de los herederos.
- Marzo de 2026: el Supremo pone fin al periplo judicial.
- Julio: los herederos trasladan sus bienes a Madrid y el pazo pasa definitivamente a ser del Estado.
- 14 de agosto: el Gobierno lo declara Lugar de Memoria Democrática.
- 7 y 8 de octubre: se exponen las piezas. La Xunta dice que estará atenta y la alcaldesa de A Coruña, Inés Rey, llama sinvergüenzas a los Franco.
- 10 de octubre: se publica el catálogo.
- 21 de octubre: la ARMH pide al Gobierno que frene la puja.
Lo que piden los memorialistas. La Asociación para la Recuperación de la Memoria Histórica pidió a Presidencia que, a través de la Fiscalía General, promoviera la suspensión cautelar hasta que la familia acredite la propiedad de cada pieza. La Comisión pola Recuperación da Memoria Histórica de A Coruña lleva semanas reclamando a la Xunta y al Gobierno que verifiquen si alguna pieza puede ser de dominio público.
Hay un precedente: las dos esculturas del Pórtico de la Gloria que acabaron en el pazo y que el Supremo ordenó devolver a Santiago. La subasta se ha celebrado según lo previsto pero, según la prensa, muchos de los objetos ya estaban en Meirás cuando era de Emilia Pardo Bazán.
Qué queda. Al cierre de la segunda sesión todavía faltaban lotes por salir. Los herederos defienden que venden lo que la justicia les ha dejado, y sus críticos que se enriquecen con la memoria de la dictadura. Medio siglo después de la muerte del dictador, la memorabilia franquista tiene un mercado que ha pagado 14.000 euros por una cajita de plata.
